summary: Ruth Edith Taylor Johnson, a retired Baltimore art teacher, died on Sunday 21 August 1988 at Good Samaritan Hospital, aged 87. A Baltimore native, she earned her teaching certificate from Coppin Normal School in 1919 and later a bachelor's degree from Morgan. summary: Waverly business men, led by their attorney Solomon Liss, asked the Off-Street Parking Commission (chairman William G. Ewald) to condemn the last four parcels needed for a 120-car lot in the 3200 block of Barclay street. They had spent three years buying property, but four of eleven owners refused to sell. Liss said the four pieces 'were all homes occupied by their owners' and that the business men sought condemnation reluctantly because it meant moving residents from their homes. Theodore Frank was president of the Waverly Business Men's Association. Liss, just elected to the City Council, said he would withdraw from the negotiations.

summary: The Off-Street Parking Commission gave preliminary approval to an open lot on Barclay street just west of the Waverly shopping district. 'The Waverly project involves clearing the entire 3200 block of Barclay street. There are eleven properties and the applicants for the city loan now control seven of them.' Owners of the other four were 'not willing even to discuss their sale' and condemnation was to be started. summary: 'The City Council approved and sent to the Mayor a precedent-setting ordinance providing for the condemnation of four houses to make way for an off-street parking project. summary: The Sun reported that the Waverly Merchants Parking Lot, Inc., had bought the Barclay street properties in October 1957 for roughly $88,500 with a $60,200 low-interest city loan, 'knocked the houses down and built the parking lot,' bought an additional piece 'at 32d street and Brentwood avenue for $20,000' in November 1960, paid off the loan in March 1973, and the same month sold the land to Luck Dome, Inc., the company of hotel developer Simantov S. summary: The Sun reported that developer Samintov Capon had abandoned the hotel and that 'the Waverly Merchants Parking Lot, at 32d and Barclay streets and Merrymans lane, will be auctioned to the highest bidder Thursday.' summary: The two court orders recorded as Exhibits A and B to the receiver's deed (X.A.C. 25999/390-405, MSA CE 164-35156; read on the scan, pages 6 to 13). Exhibit B, Order Ratifying Sale, entered February 17, 2023 (Judge Michael Studdard): the receiver terminated a prior contract of sale dated June 21, 2022 that failed to settle, resold the property at public auction on December 13, 2022, and filed a Report of Sale on or about January 9, 2023; no exceptions stood; the sale is ratified and the receiver is to convey. The receiver's deed followed on May 11, 2023 (see 714:25999-390).

summary: Superior Court block book index line for Block 3882 (MSA CE 9-321, p.83; read on the scan): Aug. 26, 1915, Griswold, Alice G. to Drischman, Mary M., Trustee, Deed, '1100-1102-1104 York Rd', Liber S.C.L. 2996, folio 308. 1100 and 1102 York Road are today's 3200 and 3202 Greenmount (one lot); 1104 was split off by 1916 (now 3204). This is the first line of what the block books show as the reversion line under the Samstag leasehold of 1911 (rent $120 a year): Griswold 1915, Title Guarantee and Trust Co. 1916 (S.C.L. 3073/433), Milligan and Pleasants 1920 (S.C.L. 3583/257), then the Samstags in 1924 (S.C.L. 4206/512). That the line is the reversion is an inference; no deed in it has been read. The nature of the trust is not shown. Update Oct. 16, 2026: S.C.L. 2996/308 read from the scan Jeff saved (MSA CE 168-3004). The instrument beginning at the foot of folio 308 is Alice Gerry Griswold of Atlantic City, New Jersey, deed of Aug. 23, 1915 to Mary M. Drischman, trustee, also of Atlantic City, for $1 and other considerations: all her real estate, real property, ground rents and leasehold interests, furniture, jewelry and property in Baltimore, New York and Atlantic City, in trust (the trust terms run onto folio 309, not saved). A blanket trust: it shows where Griswold's 3200 rent went in 1915, not how she took it, and names no lease or tract. The top of folio 308 is the end of an unrelated building-association mortgage by Harry G. and Gesine Thomas (Aug. 26, 1915).

summary: The root of title that 3117's deeds recite: its lot begins at a post at the northwest corner of 'the whole Coffield tract'. Deed of Assignment, Baltimore County Liber J.H.L. 43, folios 548 to 550 (MSA CE 62-43; read in full on the scan). Samuel H. Tagart (so spelled in the text and the signature; the 1988 deeds' 'Taggert' is a misreading), of the City of Baltimore, trustee, to George C. H. Coffield, dated January 31, 1865, acknowledged that day before Gideon Herbert, J.P., and recorded February 10, 1865 (Jno. H. Longnecker, clerk). It recites a decree of the Circuit Court for Baltimore County, sitting in equity, dated April 14, 1864, in William Tagart, complainant, against Elizabeth Baden and others, defendants, appointing Tagart trustee to sell the property; his sale of it to Coffield on July 5, 1864 for $1,525; and payment in full. For $5 recited, Tagart assigns 'all that lot or parcel of Ground' in Baltimore County on the east side of the York Turnpike Road: beginning at a stone on the east side of the road, north 1 degree west 12 perches along the road, south 88 degrees east 9 perches, south 7 1/2 degrees west 4 perches, south 15 degrees west 11 perches and thence to the beginning, containing 103 perches (about 28,000 square feet). No tract name is given. What passes is a LEASEHOLD, not the fee: 'for and during all the rest and residue of the term of ninety nine years originally granted and yet to come and unexpired therein with the benefit of renewal of said term from time to time for ever', freed of all claims of the parties to the suit, 'subject nevertheless to the payment of the yearly rent of one cent if demanded.' The original lease, its lessor and its date are not recited. Coffield's own lease of the northern part to George Vandyke Smith in 1868 (E.H.A. 59/86, $150 a year) was therefore a sub-lease. The 12 perches along the road measure 198 feet, against the 204 ft 6 in that the later deeds and the 1904 notice use from this tract's beginning to its northwest corner; the 6 ft 6 in difference is not explained. Page 548 opens with the end of the previous instrument (recorded February 9, 1865); a margin note, read with uncertainty, says 'Delivered to Jno R. Bedford Mar 22 1865'.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 71, folios 582 to 586 (MSA CE 66-121; read in full on the scan; page 582 opens with the end of an unrelated deed, Slater to Miller). James Edwards and Abraham Van Bibber, both of Baltimore County, gentlemen, to James Wilson, merchant, of the City of Baltimore, dated Sept. 3, 1802, for $3,000, each granting 'according to their estate right title and interest, jointly and respectively'. The land is 'parts of two tracts of Land called Huntington Resurveyed and Merriman's Lot': 10 1/4 acres with a dwelling house, with 30 3/4 perches (about 507 ft) of frontage on the York Turnpike, beginning at a stone on the northeast side of the road from the City of Baltimore to Abraham Van Bibber's Mill. The calls, as read: north 40 degrees east 1 1/2 perches; 'south' (interlined) 51 degrees east 16 1/2 perches; north 84 degrees east 40 3/4 perches to the York Turnpike Road; along the road north 30 3/4 perches; north 82 degrees west 30 perches; south 40 degrees west 26 1/4 perches; north 53 degrees west 11 1/4 perches; south 39 degrees west 11 3/4 perches until it meets the road to Van Bibber's Mill; and a straight line to the beginning, 'ten acres and one quarter of an acre'. So the turnpike is the lot's east side and the lot lies west of it, the side Lots 16 and 17 are on. Acknowledged before an associate justice, both wives examined and releasing dower; recorded Sept. 15, 1802. Edwards and Van Bibber had bought it as tenants in common in 1801: from Daniel Grant and Samuel Moale, trustees under John Hackett's trust deed of May 28, 1800 (W.G. 60 folios 349-352, now read: 776:mdlr-wg60-349-hackett-grant-moale-trust-1800), on Feb. 24 (W.G. 65 folio 444, now read: 776:mdlr-wg65-444-grant-moale-edwards-vanbibber-1801), from John Hackett the same day (W.G. 65 folio 442, a release of dower, Hackett &c to Edwards &c, per the Tract Index; not pulled; the instrument that ends at the top of page 444, acknowledged before Dorsey and Presbury with a wife's examination, is probably its end, but the page names no parties; this Wilson deed itself cites Hackett's instrument as 'Liber WG number 65 folio 4?28', the digits unclear, where the Tract Index and the 1802 Whitely deed give 442) and from James Barry on April 13 (cited as W.G. 69 folio 163, but that page is a June 1801 deed from Spicer to Scott, and the Tract Index lists no Barry to Edwards deed under Huntington or Merryman's Lot, so this citation is unplaced; Barry's indexed April 1801 sales are to Thompson, W.G. 66/150, to Carroll, 66/409, and to King, 68/102, none pulled). Of the three, only the Grant and Moale deed has been pulled (with Hackett's trust deed behind it); Hackett's release of dower and Barry's deed have not. The deed names the two tracts and gives the bounds from Van Bibber's Mill road; it does not mention Wilson Street, which did not exist yet. Why it is filed on 3326-3338: the 1871 Wilson trustees' deed to John Bolgiano (E.H.A. 70/115-118, mdlandrec-eha70-115) closes its recital 'For title see Liber W.G. 71 folio 582, W.G. 114 folio 437 and W.G. 114 folio 439', and this is the first of the three. The Bolgiano deed names no tract and does not say which of the three covers Lots 16 and 17 (100 ft on the turnpike at Wilson Street), and this deed does not measure its 10 1/4 acres against Wilson Street, so that Lots 16 and 17 lie within it is probable, not shown. Update Oct. 14, 2026: W.G. 66/150 was pulled for the Barry source and is Barry's Feb. 12, 1801 deed to Hugh Thompson of a half of 'Merrymans lott or Lilien dale' and Huntington (776:mdlr-wg66-150-barry-hugh-thompson-merrymans-lott-huntington-1801), not the Apr. 13, 1801 deed to Edwards and Van Bibber; W.G. 66 about folios 160 to 166 is the next try. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (night): a survey for James Wilson's heirs (776:msa-c2843-15-p28-heirs-james-wilson-merrymans-lane-surveys) begins 'on the N E side of Merryman's Lane at the beginning of the land conveyed by Jas. Edwards and Abraham Van Bibber', so the road to Van Bibber's Mill here is Merryman's Lane and the lot lay north-east of it; Job Merryman's deed to Wilson of Nov. 3, 1802 (W.G. 74/20) adjoins. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Barry deed found): the Barry deed this deed cites for its southern neighbour ground is found at W.G. 69 folio 163 (not 'unrelated'): 30 square perches, April 13, 1801, a corner between Merryman and Hall (776:mdlr-wg69-163-barry-edwards-vanbibber-30-perches-1801).

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 114, folios 437 to 439 (MSA CE 66-164; read in full on the scan, which holds pages 437 to 441). John Whitely (witnessed by Owen Dorsey and Tho. W. Griffith) to James Wilson, dated July 3, 1811, for $600, 'to his heirs and assigns forever': 1 1/4 acres, part of 'a tract of Land called Huntington', beginning at a stone on the north side of 'the road leading from Joseph Merrymans to the city of Baltimore', running north 84 1/2 degrees east 41 1/2 perches to the York Turnpike and south 9 3/4 perches along the turnpike; worked out on the ground the lot is a wedge at the turnpike end of that road. Recorded Aug. 17, 1811 (Wm. Gibson, clerk). It is the lot Whitely bought from James Edwards and Abraham Van Bibber around Jan. 2, 1802 (that deed's liber is not recited in what was read). Why it is filed on 3200: the calls put the lot at the turnpike end of Merryman's Lane, and worked out as a wedge it resembles the triangular 3200 lot; Hopkins' 1876 atlas shows the Estate of James Wilson on the 3200 block (hopkins1876-q-estate-of-james-wilson). The lot has not been placed on a plat, so this is a lead (possible), not a link. The 1871 Bolgiano deed (776, mdlandrec-eha70-115) also cites this deed as title for the Wilson trustees' holding, so it is not specific to Merryman's Lane. Update: Edwards and Van Bibber's own title is documented from three 1801 deeds recited in W.G. 71/582; the Grant and Moale deed (W.G. 65/444, 752:mdlr-wg65-444-grant-moale-edwards-vanbibber-1801) has been read, but which of the three, if any, is the source of this 1 1/4-acre lot is not shown. Update Oct. 12, 2026: the deed by which Whitely got these 1 1/4 acres, Edwards and Van Bibber to Whitely of Jan. 2, 1802 (W.G. 72/460-462, 752:mdlr-wg72-460-edwards-vanbibber-whitely-1802, now read), recites Grant and Moale's deed (W.G. 65/444) and Hackett's release of dower (65/442) and gives the same calls as the 1811 deed, so the lot was cut out of the Hackett ground and not out of ground Edwards and Van Bibber bought from Barry; where on 3200 it lies is still not shown by any deed. Update Oct. 15, 2026: 'John Whitely to James Wilson' is item 6 of the Survey Papers envelope 'York Road No. 3' (MSA CE71-281), not filmed in the public PDF (752:msa-ce71-281-283-york-road-envelopes-sweep-2026-10-15).

summary: Assignment of a ground lease, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 114, folios 439 to 441 (MSA CE 66-164; read in full on the scan, which holds pages 437 to 441). John Whitely to James Wilson, dated July 3, 1811, for $400, recorded Aug. 17, 1811 (Wm. Gibson, clerk): about one acre, part of 'a tract of Land called Huntington', that Henry D. Gough 'and others' leased to Jesse Brown by indenture of April 16, 1798, and that Brown assigned to Whitely on Oct. 20, 1801 (W.G. 72/454, see the Brown-to-Wheetley row). The term is renewable for ever at one penny a year, and the turnpike runs along the east side of the lot for 4 1/2 perches. What passed is a leasehold, not the fee: the reversion stayed with the lessors (Gough, his wife Prudence and Job Merryman, per W.G. 72/454) or their successors. The 1798 lease itself has not been seen. Why it is filed on 3200: the lot lies on the north side of Merryman's Lane at the turnpike, the 3200 to 3224 block; Hopkins' 1876 atlas shows the Estate of James Wilson on the 3200 block (hopkins1876-q-estate-of-james-wilson). The lot has not been placed on a plat, so this is a lead (possible), not a link; the same instrument is also filed on 3224 (768). The 1871 Bolgiano deed (776, mdlandrec-eha70-115) cites the 1811 assignment (W.G. 114/439) as title too. John Whitely to James Wilson, dated July 3, 1811, for $400, recorded Aug. 17, 1811 (Wm. Gibson, clerk): about one acre, part of 'a tract of Land called Huntington', that Henry D. Gough 'and others' leased to Jesse Brown by indenture of April 16, 1798, and that Brown assigned to Whitely on Oct. 20, 1801 (W.G. 72/454, see the Brown-to-Wheetley row). The term is renewable for ever at one penny a year, and the turnpike runs along the east side of the lot for 4 1/2 perches. What passed is a leasehold, not the fee: the reversion stayed with the lessors (Gough, his wife Prudence and Job Merryman, per W.G. 72/454) or their successors. The 1798 lease itself has not been seen. Why it is filed on 3224: a lead only. The Wilson trustees leased a Waverly lot to James E. Sinclair in 1872 (768:wp-1872-wilson-trustees-lease-waverly-lot-to-james-e-sinclair), the first link in 3224's chain, and 3224's 1884 deed recites title from Elizabeth Huff, 'Thomas J. Wilson and others' and Oliver P. Merryman (768:WMI141-407-deed); Thomas J. Wilson was one of the three trustees of James Wilson's estate, and the lessors of this lot were Gough, his wife and Job Merryman. No document yet connects this one-acre lease to 3224's ground; the same instrument is also filed on 3200 (752). Update Oct. 14, 2026: James Wilson's estate still held turnpike ground at Merryman's Lane in 1872 to 1873, the lot just north of 'Brown's lot', which it leased and then sold to Sinclair (768:mdlr-jb84-387-wilson-trustees-sinclair-reversion-1873); and the fork itself is 'part of a tract called Huntington' (768:mdlr-eha74-321-huff-sinclair-huntington-1872).

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 65, folios 444 to 446 (MSA CE 66-115; read in full on the scan, which holds pages 444 to 447; page 444 opens with the end of an earlier instrument, acknowledged that same day (Feb. 24, 1801) before the same two justices with a wife's separate examination, probably Hackett's release of dower (W.G. 65/442) though the page names no parties; the deed itself ends at the top of 446, and the rest of 446 and all of 447 are an unrelated mortgage, Lemmon to Mondel). Daniel Grant and Samuel Moale, of the City of Baltimore, trustees, to James Edwards and Abraham Van Bibber, of Baltimore County, dated Feb. 24, 1801, for $2,500 cash, 'as Tenants in common but not as joint Tenants'. Grant and Moale held under a trust deed from John Hackett dated May 28, 1800, made 'in Trust for the purposes therein mentioned' and recorded in Liber W.G. 60 folios 349 to 352 (now read: the trust deed is dated May 28, 1800 and received for recording May 31, 1800, as this deed says; the deed's text reads 'folio 369' with a pencil '349' above it, and 349 is right; the book places it between entries of Dec. 2, 1799 and Jan. 7, 1800, an unexplained sequence oddity); after advertising the property they sold it here. What passed: (1) 'all that part of a Tract of land ... called Huntington distinguished on a Plat thereof by the numbers Ninety Eight, ninety seven, ninety five and ninety six', 14 acres, 1 rood and 20 perches, more or less; (2) 'all that part of Merrymans lot', half an acre, beginning at a stone in the first line of the Huntington land, north 59 degrees west 11 perches, north 41 degrees east 8 perches 14 feet, south 54 degrees east 9 perches to the first line of 'Merryman's lot', then a straight line back to the beginning; (3) Hackett's household furniture and farming utensils, and three enslaved people, named in the deed as a man, Tom, and a woman, Beckey, with her child Sandy, all sold with the land. The deed also passes all the trustees' estate in law or equity. Acknowledged Feb. 24, 1801 before Owen Dorsey and Geo. Gould Presbury and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, clerk); the margin heading reads 'Daniel Grant &c Deed to James Edwards &c'. The deed ties its land to no road, turnpike or present street: its only anchors are the numbered Huntington plat and 'Merryman's lot'. The deed gives neither the date nor the maker of the numbered Huntington plat, which is not the 1871 Wilson plat of Lots 16 and 17. The half-acre is part of Merryman's Lot itself (the Tract Index files this deed under Merryman's Lot as 1/2 acre), the second tract name in the 1802 Wilson deed's 'Huntington Resurveyed and Merriman's Lot' (W.G. 71/582), so this deed carries both of that deed's tract names (here 'Huntington', there 'Huntington Resurveyed'). Why it is filed on 3326-3338: the 1802 deed to James Wilson (W.G. 71/582-586, 776:mdlr-wg71-582-edwards-vanbibber-wilson-1802) recites this deed (its W.G. 65 folio 444) as one of three 1801 sources of Edwards and Van Bibber's title, and the 1871 Bolgiano deed (mdlandrec-eha70-115) cites the Wilson deeds as the trustees' title. Each link is documented; the weak one is the last: this deed's ground is not measured against Wilson Street or the turnpike, its 14 acres 1 rood 20 perches plus a half acre are more than the 10 1/4 acres Wilson bought, and the Wilson deed drew on three sellers, so which part of this ground Wilson took, and whether Lots 16 and 17 fall in it, is not shown.

summary: Deed of trust, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 60, folios 349 to 352 (MSA CE 66-110; read in full on the scan, which holds pages 349 to 353; the top of 349 is the end of a Smythe to Ridgely deed and the foot of 352 starts an unrelated Goodwin to Waters lease). John Hackett, 'late Partner of Alexander Grant ... under the firm of Hackett and Grant', to Daniel Grant and Samuel Moale of the City of Baltimore, dated May 28, 'one thousand eight hundred', for five shillings; acknowledged that day before Ja. Calhoun and R. H. Moale, witnessed by Geo. Henry and R. H. Moale, received to be recorded May 31, 1800 (Wm. Gibson, clerk). Hackett conveys 'in Trust' to Grant and Moale and the survivor of them: (1) a Baltimore Town lot, part of the lot numbered Eighty five on a plat, 31 feet 6 inches on Gay Street and running to Frederick Street, which Nicholas Sluby had conveyed to Hackett in fee on or about March 11, 1795; (2) two tracts that Henry Wilmans had conveyed to Hackett on or about March 31, 1795, which the deed cites as recorded in 'Liber W.G. No. 22 folio 164' and 'folio 165' (resolved 2026-10-12 from the Land Records Index: 'No. 22' is the lettered book Q.Q. of 1794, whose folio 164 is Harry Dorsey Gough to Henry Wilmans, 'part of Huntington' 14-1-20, and whose folio 165 is Thomas Rutter Junior to Wilmans, 'part of Merryman's Lott' 1 1/2 acres, so these are Wilmans's own purchase deeds; the deed from Wilmans to Hackett is W.G. R.R. folios 127-129 (1795), now read (776:mdlr-wgrr-127-wilmans-hackett-1795) and the origin of this citation; the Gough and Rutter deeds (Q.Q. 164 and 165) have since been pulled and read, and the Rutter bounds are word for word the half acre here; the deed from Wilmans to Hackett (R.R. 127) has since been pulled and read; the earlier checks of book W page 164 (1785) and book R.R. page 164 (1795) were looking in the wrong place): part of 'a Tract of land ... called Huntington distinguished on a plat thereof by the numbers Ninety Eight, Ninety seven, Ninety five, and Ninety six', 14 acres 1 rood 20 perches, and part of 'Merryman's lot', one half acre, beginning at a stone in the first line of the Huntington land, north 59 degrees west 11 perches, north 41 degrees east 8 perches 14 feet, south 54 degrees east 9 perches to the first line of Merryman's lot, then straight to the beginning; and (3) the household furniture in the house Hackett occupies, the farming utensils on the lot where he lives, 'one Negro man Slave named Tom and one Mulatto woman Slave named Beckey with her Child a Slave named Sandy'. The trust: Grant and Moale are to sell it all at public or private sale and pay, first, Daniel Grant whatever he has advanced or may be bound to pay as security for Hackett and Grant; Moale is to take a commission on the money paid to Grant or other creditors of the firm (the rate is not clearly legible). This is the instrument Grant and Moale sold under in their deed of Feb. 24, 1801 to Edwards and Van Bibber (W.G. 65/444). The deed ties its Huntington and Merryman's lot ground to no road, turnpike or present street, only to the numbered plat and the Wilmans deed. A sequence oddity is unexplained: the deed is dated May 28 and received May 31, 1800, yet it stands in the book between a deed recorded Dec. 2, 1799 and a deed dated Jan. 7, 1800, and the Tract Index files it among the 1799 lines; whether the clerk entered it late or wrote the wrong year is not shown. Why it is filed on 3326-3338: it is the first link of a documented chain, Hackett (1795 from Wilmans) to Grant and Moale (this deed) to Edwards and Van Bibber (W.G. 65/444, 1801) to James Wilson (W.G. 71/582, 1802), and the 1871 Bolgiano deed (mdlandrec-eha70-115) cites that last deed as the Wilson trustees' title. Each link is documented; the weak one is still the last: nothing read so far measures this ground against Wilson Street, and the 1802 deed to Wilson took 10 1/4 acres, while Grant and Moale's 1801 deed alone passed 14 acres 1 rood 20 perches of Huntington and half an acre of Merryman's lot (the Tract Index gives that deed as 14 acres 3 roods 20 perches; the deed itself reads 1 rood).

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 179, folios 639 to 643 (MSA CE 66-229; read in full on the scan, which holds pages 639 to 646; the top of 639 is the end of a McKim deed acknowledged March 25, 1826, and the foot of 643 starts an unrelated Maxwell to Tilden deed). The President and Directors of The Union Bank of Maryland (Thomas Ellicott, President; Robert Mickle named attorney to acknowledge) to James Wilson and Thomas Wilson, both of the City and County of Baltimore, dated Feb. 4, 1826, for $6,293, to them as joint tenants. Acknowledged by Mickle on Feb. 4, 1826 before Fielder Israel and John F. Harris, justices of the peace; received to be recorded March 21, 1826 and recorded that day (Wm. Gibson, clerk). The Bank had acquired the ground, with other property, from John White and John Glenn, trustees, by an indenture of the same date (not recited by liber). Three parcels: (1) in fee, 216 acres 2 roods 20 square perches, 'part of a tract called Sheredine's Discovery, part of a tract called Gorsuch's Folly, a tract called Grant's Addition, part of a Tract called Merryman's Lot and part of a Tract called Huntington', beginning at a stone at the beginning of Gorsuch's Folly and Grant's Addition, running on lines of Grant's Addition and along the land of General Samuel Smith, extending across 'a road known by the name of the old York road', meeting the lines of 6 1/2 acres that Hugh Pannel conveyed to John Hollins on Sept. 10, 1804 and of a piece Job Merryman conveyed to Hollins on June 13, 1805, running along 'the Eastern boundary line of the Turnpike road, leading from the City of Baltimore towards the Town of York in Pennsylvania' for 52 1/2 perches to a lot Job Merryman sold James Naylor, and meeting the part of Huntington that Harry Dorsey Gough and Prudence his wife conveyed to Job Merryman on Feb. 26, 1805; (2) in fee, 'Prospect', 4 1/2 acres (laid out for 6 3/4), beginning at the beginning stone of Grant's Addition; and (3) a leasehold, part of Huntington, 3 acres 2 roods 20 square perches, beginning at a stone at the south east corner of Hopkin Hopkins's lot on the west side of the Old York road, north 82 degrees west 22 perches to the Turnpike road, along the turnpike south 1/2 degree east 30.2 perches, south 82 degrees east 17.1 perches to the Old York road, and north 9 degrees east 30.2 perches along it, held 'for and during all the rest and residue of the term of ninety nine years originally granted' with renewal forever, at a yearly rent of 21 pounds 15 shillings payable to whoever is authorised to receive it. The land lies on the EAST side of the York Turnpike: the 216-acre boundary follows the turnpike's eastern boundary, and the 3-acre parcel lies between the turnpike on its west and the Old York road on its east. Why it is filed on 3326-3338 (context, not a chain link): James Wilson died in 1848 and the 1871 Bolgiano deed (mdlandrec-eha70-115) recites a court division of his 'real and leasehold estate'; ground like this, fee and renewable leasehold, is what that estate held on the east side. It is NOT the source of Lots 16 and 17, which are on the west side of the turnpike (the Bolgiano deed starts 'on the west side of the York Turnpike Road'); the Tract Index's other Wilson deeds of 1820 and 1823 (W.G. 156/50 and 168/653) have not been read. The deed gives no street address, so where these parcels lie against today's streets is not shown. It names no lessor of the 3-acre leasehold, so it does not name the unknown lessor of the east-side 1865 Tagart to Coffield lease (742:mdlr-jhl43-548-tagart-coffield-1865) either; the two leases are renewable forever but their rents differ (21 pounds 15 shillings here, one cent there). Update Oct. 12, 2026: the Tract Index's 1820 'Jackson &c to Wilson' deed is at W.G. 156/50 (the folio was first misread as 30; a 200-dpi look reads 50, and pages 29 to 34 hold other deeds) and is now read: the Mechanics Bank and William Jackson to Thomas Wilson, merchant, April 21, 1820, 12a 2r 18 1/4p, being Jackson's 1803 lot less the piece sold to Elisha E. Russell in 1811 (726:mdlr-wg156-50-mechanics-bank-jackson-thomas-wilson-1820). The grantee is Thomas Wilson, not shown to be James Wilson, so it is not a source for the James Wilson estate's ground.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. Q.Q. (1794-95), folios 164 to 165 (MSA CE 66-91; read in full on the scan, which holds pages 164 to 167; the top of 164 is the end of an earlier Carroll of Carrollton deed to Wilmans, received for recording Feb. 3, 1795). Harry Dorsey Gough and Prudence Gough, of Baltimore County, to Henry Wilmans of Baltimore Town, dated Feb. 7, 1795, for 50 pounds current money (witnessed by Luther Martin and Nich. Brice; signed H. D. Gough and P. Gough; acknowledged before Geo. Salmon and Geo. G. Presbury, Prudence examined apart; received to be recorded Feb. 7, 1795 and recorded that day, Wm. Gibson, clerk; a margin note reads 'L. Martin', read with uncertainty, probably a delivery note): 'all that part of a Tract of Land called Huntingdon and Distinguished on a plat thereof by the numbers Ninety Eight, ninety Seven, ninety Six and ninety five containing by Estimation fourteen Acres One Rood and Twenty perches', to him and his heirs forever. No bounds, road or turnpike are given: the ground is described only by the plat numbers and the acreage. It is the ground John Hackett's trust deed of 1800 (W.G. 60/349-352) cites as 'Liber W.G. No. 22 folio 164' ('No. 22' being the lettered book Q.Q.), and Wilmans conveyed it to Hackett in 1795 (W.G. R.R. folios 127-129, now read: 776:mdlr-wgrr-127-wilmans-hackett-1795). Why it is filed on 3326-3338: it is the head of the documented chain Wilmans (this deed, Feb. 1795) to Hackett (R.R. 127, 1795) to Grant and Moale in trust (W.G. 60/349, 1800) to Edwards and Van Bibber (W.G. 65/444, 1801) to James Wilson (W.G. 71/582, 1802), the deed the 1871 Bolgiano deed cites. Nothing in it measures the ground against Wilson Street, so whether Lots 16 and 17 lie within it remains the weak link.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. Q.Q. (1794-95), folios 165 to 166 (MSA CE 66-91; read in full on the scan, which holds pages 164 to 167). Thomas Rutter Junior of Baltimore Town to Henry Wilmans of the same place, dated Feb. 7, 1795, for 500 pounds current money (ten times what Wilmans paid Gough the same day for fourteen acres): 'all that part of Merryman's Lot contained within the following Courses: Beginning at a stone standing on the first line of the said Land and running thence North fifty nine degrees West Eleven perches then North forty one degrees East Eight Perches fourteen feet then South fifty four degrees East nine perches until it Intersects the first line of Merryman's Lot, then with a straight line to the beginning containing and laid out for One half an acre more or Less'. Signed Tho. Rutter Jun. in the presence of L. Martin, Geo. Salmon and Geo. G. Presbury; acknowledged before the two justices, Mary Rutter his wife releasing dower; received to be recorded and recorded Feb. 7, 1795 (Wm. Gibson, clerk); a margin note reads 'L. Martin', read with uncertainty. These are word for word the bounds of the half acre of Merryman's lot in John Hackett's trust deed of 1800 (W.G. 60/349-352), which cites this deed as 'Liber W.G. No. 22 folio 165' ('No. 22' being the lettered book Q.Q.). The deed ties the half acre to no road, turnpike or present street. summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. R.R. (1795), folios 127 to 129 (MSA CE 66-92; read in full on the scan, which holds pages 127 to 130; the top of 127 is the end of an unrelated assignment, also received for recording April 13, 1795, and the foot of 129 opens Charles Rogers to William Sedden, which runs on into 130). Henry Wilmans, merchant, of Baltimore Town, to John Hackett, merchant, of the same town and county, dated March 31, 1795, for 665 pounds current money of Maryland. It recites that Harry Dorsey Gough and Prudence his wife, by indenture of about Feb. 7, 1795, sold Wilmans 'all that part of a tract of Land called Huntington distinguished on a plat thereof by the numbers Ninety Eight, Ninety Seven, Ninety Six and Ninety five and containing by Estimation fourteen Acres one Rood and Twenty perches', 'among the Records of Baltimore County Court in Liber W.G. No 22 folio 164 &c', and that Thomas Rutter Junior, by indenture also of Feb. 7, 1795, sold him 'all that part of Merryman's Lot' within bounds it repeats (beginning at a stone in the first line of the land, north 59 degrees west 11 perches, north 41 degrees east 8 perches 14 feet, south 54 degrees east 9 perches to the first line of Merryman's Lot, and a straight line back: one half an acre), cited as 'Liber W.G. No 22 folio 165 &c'; Wilmans 'hath agreed to sell and convey the two above described pieces or parcels of Land' to Hackett. He now grants them to Hackett and his heirs and assigns forever, with all buildings, ways, waters and appurtenances, covenanting that they are free of incumbrances made or suffered by him, with a special warranty (against claims 'by from or under him' only) and further assurance. Signed Henry Wilmans (seal; the deed's heading and opening spell it 'Willmans', and the grantee is 'John Hachet' throughout), in the presence of J. C. Niemeyer and James Alcock; Wilmans's receipt for the 665 pounds the same day, witnessed by James Alcock. Acknowledged April 1, 1795 before Abm. Van Bibber and Geo. Gould Presbury, justices of the peace for Baltimore County, Wilmans's wife (the name reads Catherine Solamans, the letters uncertain) examined apart and releasing dower; received to be recorded April 13, 1795 and recorded and examined that day, Wm. Gibson, clerk. Hackett paid 665 pounds for what Wilmans had bought less than eight weeks earlier for 50 pounds and 500 pounds (550 pounds). This is the source of the 'Liber W.G. No. 22 folio 164 / 165' citation in Hackett's own 1800 trust deed (W.G. 60/349-352): 'No. 22' is the lettered book Q.Q., and Hackett's trust deed copied the citation from this deed. The deed ties the two pieces to no road, turnpike or present street. The justice 'Abm. Van Bibber' who took the acknowledgment bears the name of the Abraham Van Bibber who, with James Edwards, bought this ground from Grant and Moale in 1801 (W.G. 65/444); the deeds do not say whether they are the same man. Why it is filed on 3326-3338: every link from Gough's 1795 deed to the 1802 deed to James Wilson has now been read: Gough and Rutter to Wilmans (W.G. Q.Q. 164-165, Feb. 7, 1795), Wilmans to Hackett (this deed), Hackett in trust to Grant and Moale (W.G. 60/349, 1800), Grant and Moale to Edwards and Van Bibber (W.G. 65/444, 1801), Edwards and Van Bibber to James Wilson (W.G. 71/582, 1802), which the 1871 Bolgiano deed cites as the Wilson trustees' title. The weak link is still the last: no deed read so far measures this ground against Wilson Street, and the 1802 deed took 10 1/4 acres, while Grant and Moale's 1801 deed alone passed 14 acres 1 rood 20 perches of Huntington and half an acre of Merryman's lot.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 72, folios 460 to 462 (MSA CE 66-122; read in full on the scan, which holds pages 460 to 463; the top of 460 is the end of an unrelated Stewart and Falls deed to William McCreery, and the foot of 462 opens Charles Carroll of Carrollton to Thomas Hillen). James Edwards and Abraham Van Bibber, of Baltimore County, to John Whitely, of the City of Baltimore, dated Jan. 2, 1802, for $333.33 current money of the United States. It recites Grant and Moale's deed to Edwards and Van Bibber 'recorded among the land records of Baltimore County Court in liber W.G. No. 65 folio 444 &c', conveying 'that part of a tract of Land situate in Baltimore County called Huntington that is distinguished on a plat thereof by the numbers ninety eight, ninety seven, ninety five and ninety six containing by estimation fourteen acres a quarter and twenty square perches', and John Hackett and Jane his wife's release of dower to them (W.G. No. 65 folio 442 &c). It then conveys to Whitely, in fee, 'all that part of the above mentioned part of a tract of Land called Huntington which is contained within the following metes and bounds': beginning at a stone on the north side of 'the road leading from Joseph Merryman's to the City of Baltimore', 'being the beginning of a lot of Ground part of said tract assigned by Jesse Brown to said Whitely', running from that stone north 84 1/2 degrees east 41 1/2 perches to 'the York Turnpike road', thence bounding on that road south 9 3/4 perches to 'the aforesaid part of said tract assigned by Jesse Brown to said Whitely', and thence bounding on that part to the beginning: one acre and one quarter more or less, with buildings and improvements, to Whitely, his heirs and assigns forever, with warranty and further assurance. Signed Jas. Edwards and Abm. Van Bibber (seals) in the presence of Geo. Gould Presbury and Thos. B. Hodgkin; receipt for $333.33 the same day; acknowledged Jan. 2, 1802 before Presbury and Hodgkin, Ruth wife of James Edwards and Mary wife of Abraham Van Bibber examined apart and releasing dower; received to be recorded Feb. 26, 1802 and recorded that day (Wm. Gibson, clerk), the same day as Jesse Brown's assignment to Whitely (W.G. 72/454, 752:mdlr-wg72-454-brown-wheetley-1801). What this settles: the 1 1/4 acres Whitely sold James Wilson in 1811 (W.G. 114/437) are the lot of this deed, with the same calls word for word, and they were cut out of the same 14 acres 1 rood 20 perches of Huntington (plat lots 95-98) that Hackett held in trust and Grant and Moale sold to Edwards and Van Bibber in 1801; they did not come from Barry. The lot touches Jesse Brown's one-acre leasehold at the turnpike end of the road from Joseph Merryman's. The deed gives no street name and does not say where the road from Joseph Merryman's meets the turnpike today. Why it is filed on 3200: the calls (a stone on the north side of the road from Joseph Merryman's, 41 1/2 perches to the York Turnpike, 9 3/4 perches along it) make a wedge at the turnpike end of that road, and the Hopkins atlas shows the Estate of James Wilson on the 3200 block (hopkins1876-q-estate-of-james-wilson); no deed read places the lot on a street, so this is a lead (possible), not a link. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the Huff deed of 1872 names the apex ground 'part of a tract called Huntington' (752:mdlr-eha74-321-huff-sinclair-huntington-1872), and the 1873 Wilson trustees' deed shows James Wilson's estate holding the lot just north of it on the turnpike (768:mdlr-jb84-387-wilson-trustees-sinclair-reversion-1873). (330 feet to the inch; Maryland State Archives; the plate as Jeff saved it on October 12, 2026, already in Corridor as an image on 3107, 3117, 3200 and 3224), read for the James Wilson estate. Wilson Street runs west from the York Road to Barclay Street, and the plate letters Bolgiano on the north side of Wilson Street at the road (the lettering reads 'Bolgiana'), where the 1871 deed puts Lots 16 and 17 (E.H.A. 70/115, mdlandrec-eha70-115). South of Wilson Street on the west side of the road the lots are lettered A. Henderson, Jas. Wilson Est., Jos. Cross, Jno. Volks, A. Volks and Jno. H. Hartman, then the public school and a lot lettered Sinclair at Merryman's Lane: the estate had sold lots from its plat and still held at least one in 1877 (compare the 1876 Plate Q rows, hopkins1876-q-*). West of Barclay Street 'Jas. Wilson Est.' runs along the street and two large tracts lettered 'Jas. Wilson Estate' lie on both sides of Merryman's Lane; another lies at the depot and toll gate, with 'Darcey Wilson' south-west of it. East of the turnpike, in the wedge between the turnpike (with its horse railway) and the Old York Road, a long parcel is lettered 'Jas. summary: Plat and descriptions, read from the Archives' public PDF of MSA C2843-15 (132 pages; Superior Court (Baltimore City) Survey Papers, the Bouldin surveyors' Envelope No. 15). The cover (p. 1) reads: 'Plat - Jackson - Walker - Biays and Smith, 13th Jan'y 18[..]. Cope's Plat and Descriptions of the several Lots, part of Huntington sold and conveyed by Henry Dorsey Gough and Prudence his wife to Wm Jackson, James Biays and John Smith. Lodged in the Office by James Carroll the Elder the 13th day of June 1823. York Rd and Rutter's Mill Road.' (The year after 'Jan'y' is torn; the catalogue's 'Hanes' is 'James'.) Cope's descriptions (pp. 113-114) say four parts of a tract were 'conveyed in Fee simple by Harry Dorsey Gough and Prudence his wife unto William Jackson, James Biay's and John Smith, on the Thirteenth day of January Eighteen hundred and three': to William Jackson one part, 14 3/4 acres (14a 3r 0p), beginning at a stone on the NW side of 'a Road laid out by the said Harry Dorsey Gough' at the NE corner of 'Stephen T. Wante's' lot (the initial reads T once and P once), N 40 E 16 3/4 perches along the road; to James Biays two parts, one of 1 acre 47 perches (1a 1r 7p) by 'a road leading from Joseph Merryman's House to the Turnpike Road leading from the City of Baltimore towards the Town of York in Pennsylvania', the other of 'Seven Acres two roods and thirty three perches' (7a 2r 33p) with its south line on 'a Road left open by the said Harry Dorsey Gough'; to John Smith one part, 3a 2r 8p, bounded by 'a road left open by William Jackson and James Biays'. A note signed by William Jackson, James Biays, C. Walker and John Smith before Wm Hollins says the parcel 'was sold originally in one body to William Jackson, Christopher Walker and James Byass' and was then parcelled out, and confirms the plat and certificate as binding on them. The plat Jeff holds is p. 73 of the same PDF. Where: Bouldin's survey of January 1844 (p. 82) shows the 3a 1r 12p that 'Carroll and others' conveyed to Philip G. Biays in 1823, next to 'the lot formerly Thornburgh's', at the YORK TURNPIKE and Gough's road, with 'the Gate House lot' (0a 0r 20p) and a School House lot excepted; which puts Gough's road at the toll gate, evidently the lane then called Gilmor's, now Vineyard, Lane, with these lots on its north-west side, along it. Corrects the earlier filings: the lots are Biays's (the plat letters 'Biay's'), not 'Bray'; the second lot is 7a 2r 33p, not the dossier's 2-2-33; the west neighbour is Stephen Wante, not 'Wyatt'; and the placement is the toll-gate corner, not the 33rd Street corner and not the Oriole Park wedge itself. Why it is filed on 401 E 30th St: the Old Oriole Park (V) dossier reads these as Colonel James Biays's holdings at the ballpark wedge; the plat's lots lie at the toll gate on the north-west side of Gough's road, next to the Biays ground the dossier describes, so this is neighbouring context, not the wedge itself. Update Oct. 12, 2026: the four Gough deeds of Jan. 13, 1803 (W.G. 74/327, 330, 334 and 337, MSA CE 66-124) are now read in full from the scan Jeff saved, and filed on 3028 (726:mdlr-wg74-327-gough-smith-1803, 726:mdlr-wg74-330-gough-biays-first-lot-1803, 726:mdlr-wg74-334-gough-biays-second-lot-1803, 726:mdlr-wg74-337-gough-jackson-1803). They confirm Cope's four figures (3a 2r 8p, 1 acre 47 perches, 7a 2r 33p, 14 3/4 acres), say who bought each lot and for how much ($710, $258.75, $1,541.25 and $2,950), and were all recorded Jan. 17, 1803; the Jackson deed reads 'Stephen P. Wante', settling the initial Cope's copy leaves doubtful.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 74, folios 327 to 330 (MSA CE 66-124; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 327 to 341; the top of 327 is the end of an unrelated Anne Arundel County acknowledgement, received for record Jan. 15, 1803). Harry Dorsey Gough, of Baltimore County, gentleman, and Prudence his wife, to John Smith, of the City of Baltimore, master mariner, dated Jan. 13, 1803, for $710, each granting 'according to their estate right title and interest, jointly and respectively'. The land is a 'lot or piece or parcel of land or grounds being part of a tract of land' called Huntington, 'contained within the following metes and bounds': beginning 'in the North easternmost boundary line of another part of the said tract of lands, sold unto a certain William Jackson', south 36 1/2 degrees east 8 1/2 perches from a stone at the most northerly corner of Jackson's part; thence north 39 3/4 degrees east 26 7/10 perches to 'a road leading from Joseph Merryman's house to the Turnpike Road leading from the City of Baltimore towards York Town in the State of Pennsylvania'; thence along that road south 58 degrees east 3 perches, south 54 degrees east 14 perches and south 48 degrees east 1 1/10 perches; thence south 44 degrees west 24 perches; south 35 1/2 degrees east 8 8/10 perches; south 51 1/2 degrees west 7 8/10 perches to the center of 'a Road left open by William Jackson and James Biays'; and along the center of that road, in a straight line, to the beginning: 'Three acres Two Quarters of an acre and eight square perches' (3a 2r 8p), more or less. The words 'and James Biays' were interlined, which the witnesses' note certifies. Title recited (the same words in all four deeds): the tract 'called Huntington' was, 'with other lands, granted by a certain Achsha [Achsah] Carnan, since deceased, unto certain Trustees and their heirs forever, in trust (amongst other things) to permit and suffer her daughter the said Prudence, and her lawful issue, to have hold and enjoy one moiety thereof forever, and in trust to permit and suffer her other daughter Elizabeth and her lawful issue to have hold and enjoy the other moiety', by indenture of Feb. 13, 1768 recorded in 'Liber B. Number Q. Folio 503 &c'; and 'the last mentioned moiety' (Elizabeth's) 'was granted and conveyed unto the said Harry Dorsey Gough by a certain Thomas Bond Onion and Elizabeth his wife' by indenture of Feb. 24, 1790, recorded in 'Liber W.G. Number E.E. Folio 157 &c'. Both are now read, see the update at the end of this note. Signed 'H. D. Gough' and 'P. Gough' (seals) in the presence of Thorowgood Smith and Wm Hollins, with the receipt of the full consideration signed the same day; acknowledged Jan. 13, 1803 before Thorowgood Smith and James Carroll, justices of the peace, Prudence examined apart and relinquishing dower; received to be recorded Jan. 17, 1803 and recorded and examined the same day (Wm Gibson, clerk). Why it is filed on 3028: Bouldin's 1844 survey (MSA C2843-15, 726:bouldin-1844-biays-gate-house-mumma-wilson) puts the Biays ground at the toll gate, on Gough's road beside the Gate House lot, and Cope's plat (726:cope-plat-gough-1803-jackson-biays-smith) draws these four lots along that road. The deeds name no street and reach the York Turnpike only through the road from Joseph Merryman's house, so the placement rests on Bouldin and is probable, not read here. Update Oct. 12, 2026: both instruments are now read (726:mdlr-bq-503-carnan-ridgely-release-1768; 726:mdlr-wgee-157-onion-gough-1790). The 1768 deed is a lease for a year and a release 'in trust' to John Ridgely and Charles Ridgely Junior, to uses: each daughter's moiety is limited to her 'and the heirs of her body', with remainders over, where this recital says 'her lawful issue ... forever'; whether those entails were barred is not shown. The 1790 deed is Thomas Bond Onion and Elizabeth to Gough, for 1,400 pounds, in fee.

The 1768 deed is a lease for a year and a release 'in trust' to John Ridgely and Charles Ridgely Junior, to uses: each daughter's moiety is limited to her 'and the heirs of her body', with remainders over, where this recital says 'her lawful issue ... forever'; whether those entails were barred is not shown. The 1790 deed is Thomas Bond Onion and Elizabeth to Gough, for 1,400 pounds, in fee.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 156, folios 50 to 54 (MSA CE 66-206; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 49 to 54; page 50 opens with the end of an unrelated deed, Williams and others, received for record June 5, 1820, and page 54 closes with the opening of another, Courtenay to Courtenay). The Tract Index (MSA CE 15-1, p. 519) lists it as 'Jackson &c to Wilson', 12 1/2 a. 18 1/4 Pr, at 156/50; the folio was first misread as 30, and pages 29 to 34 of this liber hold other deeds. Three parties, dated April 21, 1820: the President and Directors of the Mechanics Bank of Baltimore (the first part, signing by James Mosher, President, with the corporate seal); William Jackson, of the City of Baltimore, merchant (the second part); and Thomas Wilson, of the City of Baltimore, merchant (the third). It recites (1) Gough and Prudence's deed to Jackson 'on or about the thirteenth day of January 1803', 'recorded ... in Liber W.G. No. 74 folio 337', whose lot begins 'at a stone on the north west side of a road laid out by' Gough 'at the north east corner of a lot then or lately belonging to Stephen P. Wante' and was 'laid out for fourteen acres and three quarters of an acre' (the courses are those of row 726:mdlr-wg74-337-gough-jackson-1803); (2) Jackson's deed of March 18, 1819 to the Bank (Liber W.G. No. 150 folio 371), made to secure a $9,000 'accommodation' on paper drawn by Jackson and endorsed by John Brice, the Bank's cashier, with power for the Bank's president to sell after thirty days' public notice in two Baltimore daily papers; and (3) that Jackson had agreed to sell Wilson part of the lot. For $7,000 paid by Wilson to the Bank and $1 to Jackson, the Bank and Jackson convey to Wilson, in fee, 'all that part of the aforesaid tract ... called Huntington' beginning at the beginning of the whole lot Gough conveyed to Jackson; north 40 degrees east 16 3/10 perches to the end of the first line of the whole lot; then on its second line north 36 1/2 degrees west 51 perches 15 feet 8 1/10 inches to 'the piece or parcel of land conveyed by the said William Jackson to Elisha E. Russell'; thence on that parcel south 57 1/2 degrees west 9 6/10 perches and north 35 1/2 degrees west 35 2/10 perches to the third line of the whole lot, at 9 perches and a fraction from its beginning; then on that third line south 39 1/2 degrees west 27 9/10 perches to its end; and by a straight line to the beginning: 'twelve Acres two roods and Eighteen perches and one fourth of a perch' (12a 2r 18 1/4p), more or less, 'except the part thereof conveyed by the said William Jackson to Elisha Russell by deed ... on or about the thirteenth day of March one thousand eight hundred and eleven ... Liber W.G. No. 112 folio 467'. Jackson warrants against himself and his heirs. Signed 'James Mosher Prest.' and 'William Jackson' (seals) in the presence of Nath. Knight and Peter Galt; acknowledged April 21, 1820 before Knight and Galt, justices of the peace, by Mosher for the Bank and by Jackson, Mary Jackson his wife relinquishing dower; received to be recorded June 5, 1820 and recorded and examined the same day (Wm Gibson, clerk). What it settles: the Tract Index's 1820 'Jackson &c to Wilson' is William Jackson's lot of 1803, less the piece he sold Elisha E. Russell in 1811 (W.G. 112/467, the index's 'Jackson to Russell'), passing to Thomas Wilson through the Bank that held it in trust; the 14 3/4 acres less about 2 acres 21 3/4 perches is the 12a 2r 18 1/4p. As the courses read, the Russell piece is at the north-west end of the lot, away from Gough's road. What it does not settle: the grantee is Thomas Wilson, merchant, and nothing read here ties him to James Wilson (whose estate's trustees included a Thomas J. Wilson), so it is not shown to be a source for the James Wilson estate's ground; and the deed names no street. Why it is filed on 3028: it is the later history of Jackson's lot, one of the four 1803 lots filed on 3028 (726:mdlr-wg74-337-gough-jackson-1803), which Bouldin's 1844 survey puts at the toll gate; this deed does not itself place the lot on a street, so the placement stays probable.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber B No. Q, folios 502 to 507 (MSA CE 66-36; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 502 to 508; the top of 502 is the end of an unrelated deed acknowledged April 15, 1768, and the foot of 507 opens another, Bond and Fell to Christie, May 12, 1768). Two instruments, a pair: (1) A lease for a year, 'made the 12th day of February 1768', Achsah Carnan, of Baltimore County, widow of John Carnan deceased and daughter of Colonel Charles Ridgely, to John Ridgely and Charles Ridgely Junior, both of the Town of Baltimore, for five shillings sterling, of 'that part of a tract of land ... called Taylors Purchase' (600 acres, conveyed to her by her father), 'all that tract or parcel of land called Huntington ... containing four hundred and Seventy five Acres more or less as per the Certificate thereof returned into his Lordship's Land Office at Annapolis in the name of the aforesaid John Carnan deceased and the said Achsah Carnan on or about the twenty Ninth day of September Seventeen hundred and fifty Seven', and 'that part of a tract of land called Ridgely's whim' (500 acres, also from her father), for a term of one year at a pepper corn, so that the Ridgelys could take a release. Witnesses Benjamin Rogers and Wm Asquith; Lord Baltimore's alienation fine, 3 pounds 3 shillings on the 1,575 acres, received by John Boyd for the Agent; recorded May 30, 1768 (B. Bordley, clerk). (2) The release, headed 'Achsah Carnan to John & Charles Ridgely in Trust', 'made the 13th day of February 1768', for ten shillings sterling and 'the advancement and maintenance of her children and other relations and for the setting and establishment of the lands and tenements', to the Ridgelys and their heirs and assigns, of the same three tracts, to the uses declared: to Achsah for her natural life without impeachment of waste; then, as to Huntington and Ridgely's Whim, one full moiety to Prudence Carnan 'and the heirs of her body lawfully to be begotten' and, failing such issue, to Elizabeth Carnan, and the other moiety to Elizabeth 'and the heirs of her body' and, failing such issue, to Prudence; failing both, to Charles Ridgely Carnan her son and the heirs of his body; then to her sons and daughters born after a later marriage, in order; then to John Robert Holiday her son; then, for a moiety, to Achsah and Deborah Ridgely, daughters of John Ridgely, in turn; and failing all, to the right heirs of Achsah Carnan forever. Taylors Purchase is limited separately in much the same family order, ending with Elizabeth and Susannah Gooding and then the right heirs. Signed 'A Carnan' (seal) in the presence of Benjamin Rogers; receipt of ten shillings Feb. 13, 1768; acknowledged that day before Benjamin Rogers and Wm Asquith, two of his Lordship's justices; recorded June 4, 1768 (B. Bordley, clerk). What it settles: the recital in all four of Gough's 1803 deeds ('indenture ... the thirteenth day of February 1768 ... Liber B Number Q Folio 503') is this release. What differs: the recital says the trustees were to let the daughters and their lawful issue enjoy a moiety each 'forever'; the release limits each moiety to the daughter 'and the heirs of her body', with remainders over, so the daughters took estates in tail, not (on the face of the deed) in fee. Whether those entails were barred, or ended, before Gough's 1790 and 1803 deeds is not shown by anything read. Prudence Carnan is the Prudence who joins Gough's 1803 deeds. The deed names no street, house or lot; it conveys the whole 475-acre Huntington and two other tracts. Why it is filed on 3028: it is a link above Gough's four 1803 deeds (726:mdlr-wg74-327-gough-smith-1803, -330-, -334- and -337-), which Bouldin's 1844 survey puts at the toll gate; it conveys the whole tract and names no street, so the placement stays possible.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. E.E., folios 157 to 159 (MSA CE 66-80; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 156 to 161; the top of 157 is the end of a different deed, Thomas Bond Onion alone to Gough of the same day, for 700 pounds, whose first page is not pulled; the foot of 159 opens James Calhoun to Alexander Gallagher, Feb. 25, 1790). A margin note beside the deed's title reads 'See Liber W.G. No. 102 folio 33'. Thomas Bond Onion of Baltimore County and Elizabeth Onion his wife to Harry Dorsey Gough of the same county, dated Feb. 24, 1790, for 1,400 pounds, receipt acknowledged. They convey 'all that undivided Moiety of a Portion a part of a Tract of Land called Ridgelys Whim heretofore conveyed to a certain Achsah Holliday mother to the aforesaid Elizabeth Onion by a certain Charles Ridgely Grandfather to the said Elizabeth Onion for five hundred acres more or Less', one moiety of which Achsah Holliday 'by the name of Achsah Carnan' had conveyed 'to and for the use of the said Elizabeth Onion and the heirs of her Body with sundry remainders over'; and 'all that undivided Moiety of a Tract or Parcel of Land called and known by the name of Huntington ... containing four hundred and seventy six acres of Land more or Less as per Certificate and Patent thereof in the name of John Carnan and Achsah his wife', of which one moiety was likewise conveyed by Achsah Carnan 'to the use and behoof of the said Elizabeth Onion then Elizabeth Carnan and the heirs of her Body with sundry remainders over as will appear by a Reference to said Deed'. With it go all the Onions' rights 'to all Debts Contracted and yet unpaid heretofore arising on the sale of the said Lands with the Interest accruing thereon and all arrearages of Rent', to Gough, his heirs and assigns forever, with the Onions' covenants of further assurance and warranty. Signed Thomas Bond Onion and Eliza Onion (seals) in the presence of Standish Barry and Saml Vincent; receipt of 1,400 pounds the same day; acknowledged Feb. 24, 1790 before Jas. Calhoun and Geo. Gould Presbury, Elizabeth examined apart and out of her husband's hearing; received to be recorded and recorded that day (Wm Gibson, clerk). What it settles: the instrument every 1803 Gough deed cites as 'W.G. Number E.E. folio 157' is this one, and it is how Elizabeth's moiety of Huntington reached Gough, who already held Prudence's through his wife. It says Huntington was 476 acres where the 1768 settlement says 475, and it recites that deed's limitations to Elizabeth 'and the heirs of her body with sundry remainders over' while conveying in fee, so it does not itself show that the remainders were barred. The sale of 'the said Lands' for which debts were 'yet unpaid' is not explained on these pages. The same pages show a second Onion deed of the same day, Thomas Bond Onion alone to Gough for 700 pounds, covering 'the aforesaid Tracts or parcels of Land' and Onion's own 'Estate Right Title Interest and Demand' in them (the end of it, on 156 to 157, is read; its first page, probably W.G. E.E. 155, is not). The 1803 deeds do not cite it. Why it is filed on 3028: it is a link above Gough's four 1803 deeds (726:mdlr-wg74-327-gough-smith-1803, -330-, -334- and -337-), which Bouldin's 1844 survey puts at the toll gate; it conveys the whole tract and names no street, so the placement stays possible. Update Oct. 12, 2026: two more pages are read. (1) W.G. E.E. 155, the opening of the same-day Onion-alone deed (700 pounds), is on the scan Jeff saved (MSA CE 66-80, pages 153 to 155): it conveys Onion's right in 'two hundred acres of Land lying in Baltimore County being part of a Tract of Land Called Thompsons Choice' and in 'another Tract or Parcel of Land being part of a Tract of Land Called Heathcotes Cottage' (123 acres), neither of them Huntington; the note above that it covers 'the aforesaid Tracts' should be read as those tracts, not as Huntington and Ridgely's Whim. (2) W.G. 102/33 (June 6, 1809), the deed the margin note points to, is read: the Onions reconveyed the moiety in fee to Gough's executors because 'doubts are entertained' whether the 1790 deed passed the fee simple (726:mdlr-wg102-33-onion-carroll-gough-1809).

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber A.W.B. 354, folios 374 to 376 (MSA CE 66-404; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 373 to 377). The top of 373 is the end of a different instrument of the same day, signed by the same parties and by Mumma: a covenant to renew a lease, that the parties 'shall and will make, execute, acknowledge and deliver ... a Lease for the above described and hereby demised ground and premises for other ninety nine years ... subject to the same rent', 'renewable and renewed from time to time forever'; its first pages are the lease filed as 719:mdlr-awb354-371-biays-heirs-lease-mumma-1844 (a lease east of the turnpike at the Quaker Lane, not this lot). The foot of 376 opens Catherine Ferguson to N. Carroll Spence (July 10, 1845), unrelated. Indenture made Nov. 9, 1844 between Sarah Biays, Jacob Hoke and Nancy Hoke, Henry Hammond and Frances Hammond, Henry N. Bowerman and Elizabeth Bowerman, W. T. Allender and Hannah Jane Allender, John W. Stump and Philip G. Biays, of the one part, and David Mumma of Baltimore County, of the other, for $250. They convey 'all that piece or parcel of Land, Situate and lying in Baltimore County' beginning 'at Stone planted at the South West intersection of the York Turnpike Road, and the Road leading from said Yorke Turnpike Road towards the Lands of Mrs Gilmore and Mrs Biays'; thence on the west side of the turnpike south 3 1/4 degrees west 6 3/10 perches to a stone (about 104 feet of frontage); thence west 17 perches to a free stone 'standing on the East Side of the Lane or Road running between the Lands of Mrs Gilmore and Mrs Biays'; thence on the east side of that lane north 42 1/2 degrees east 9 6/10 perches and south 85 1/2 degrees east 11 perches to the beginning stone: 'Ninety four Square perches of Land more or less' (about 25,600 square feet). 'It being a part of the Ground Conveyed by John McFadon to John W. Stump and Philip G. Biays in trust by deed dated the Eleventh day of April Eighteen hundred and twenty two and Recorded among the Land records of Baltimore County Court in Liber W.G. No. [blank] folio [blank] &c.' Warranty and further assurance. Signed S. Biays, Jacob Hoke, Nancy Hoke, Henry Hammond, Fanny Hammond, H. N. Bowerman, E. Bowerman, Walter T. Allender, Hannah J. Allender, Jno. W. Stump, Philip G. Biays and David Mumma (seals), in the presence of T. Hanson Belt, O. P. Merryman, Robt. W. Willett and Geo. R. Braddock. Acknowledged Nov. 9, 1844 in the City of Baltimore before T. Hanson Belt and O. P. Merryman, the four wives examined apart; Philip G. Biays acknowledged May 29, 1845 in Montgomery County before Willett and Braddock, certified May 30, 1845 by Saml. T. Stonestreet, clerk of Montgomery County Court; received to be recorded July 10, 1845 at 11 A.M. and recorded the same day (A. W. Bradford, clerk). What it settles: Bouldin's abstract (MSA C2843-15, row 46060) was right, and Corridor's 'T.K. 354' (the 1912 turnpike deed's recital) is, on liber and year, this deed. The grantors are the family and trustees of the McFadon trust ground (four couples, Sarah Biays, and the two trustees), not an estate in fee from a patent; the deed names no tract (Bouldin's 'Ensor's Inspection' is his). The lot lies on the SOUTH side of the lane and on the west side of the turnpike, south of the toll-house lot (3026 to 3032) where 3010 to 3020 lie, and it fronts the lane that runs to the Gilmor and Biays lands; a second lane bounds it on the west. The 1846 and 1848 documents (Mumma to Nicoll; Nicoll to Leicht, 36 feet on the road from 'the corner of the York Turnpike Road and the Lane leading to Mr. Gilmor's') are a piece of this ground. What it does not settle: the 1822 McFadon deed, whose liber and folio are blank in this deed (the paired lease gives them as W.G. 165/492, a trust deed for Sarah Biays for life and then her children); whether the 1912 recital's stone 'eight feet' from the toll-house lot's corner is this beginning stone across the lane (the 1912 text should be re-read for the direction); and the width and name of either lane. Update Oct. 12, 2026: the McFadon deed of trust this deed recites is now read, W.G. 165/492 (719:mdlr-wg165-492-mcfadon-trust-stump-biays-1822): April 11, 1822, John McFadon to John W. Stump and Philip G. Biays in trust for Sarah Biays for life, then for Nancy, Frances J., Elizabeth and Hannah Jane Biays, the Ensor's Inspection ground 'at or near the gate'. The 1844 grantors are exactly those four daughters, their husbands and the trustees. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the Mumma lot's later history is read (719:mdlr-jb96-352-mumma-heirs-mott-1876, J.B. 96/352): Mumma kept the fee and leased the lot on Jan. 21, 1846 to Nicoll for 99 years renewable at $32 a year; his heirs sold the fee and rent to Abraham G. Mott on Apr. 10, 1876 for $533.33. The 94 perches are exactly 3020 plus 3010: 6.3 perches on the turnpike is 103 ft 11 2/5 in (36 ft plus 67 ft 11 2/5 in) and 17 perches the 280 1/2 ft depth of the 1896 deed. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1846 lease recites this deed as recorded July 10, 1845 (719:mdlr-awb372-23-mumma-nicoll-lease-1846). Fourteen months after paying $250, Mumma had leased the lot at $32 a year, redeemable at $533.33: a little over twice his price (an observation from the two documents).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber J.F.C. 1004, folios 488 to 489 (MSA CE 168-11322; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 487 to 491; the top of 487 is the end of an unrelated deed, Que Holding Corporation to the Olszewskis, recorded at 1004/486, and 490 opens a De Soto Apartment Company mortgage). A Title Guarantee Company form (T-2-O, App. H-32211). Guiseppe Palladi and Adele Palladi, his wife, of Baltimore County, to Jerome Silbiger and Lillian Silbiger, his wife, of Baltimore City, as tenants by the entireties, dated Dec. 30, 1960, for $5 and other valuable considerations: 'those two (2) lot(s) of ground situate in Baltimore City'. (1) The first lot begins on the west side of Greenmount Avenue (formerly the York Road) 402 feet 9 1/2 inches northerly from the northwest corner of Twenty-Ninth Street and Greenmount Avenue, at the center of a partition wall, runs 14 feet northerly on the avenue to the center of another partition wall, then 100 feet west, parallel with Twenty-Ninth Street, to the west side of a 10-foot alley, 14 feet back along the alley 'with the use thereof in common with others', and 100 feet east to the beginning; held 'for all the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein, with the benefit of renewal forever, subject to the payment of the annual rent aforesaid'. (2) The second lot begins 416 feet 9 1/2 inches northerly from the same corner, runs about 8 feet on the avenue to the south side of 'Thirtieth Street as now laid out', then 100 feet west along 30th Street to the alley, one foot back along the alley, and east through the partition wall 100 feet; conveyed 'in fee simple, forever'. 'The improvements thereon being known inclusively as No. 2958 Greenmount Avenue.' 'BEING the same lots of ground which, by Deed and Assignment dated March 13th, 1925 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber S.C.L. No. 4353, folio 212, were granted, assigned and conveyed by Albert C. Brandt and Alice E. Brandt, his wife, to the Grantors herein; the first lot of ground above described subject to the annual ground rent of Sixty-five Dollars ($65.00), payable in equal semi-annual installments on the first days of March and September, in each and every year, and the second lot of ground above described being conveyed in fee simple.' Signed Guiseppe Palladi and Adele Palladi (seals), witness Robert J. Neubauer, Notary Public; acknowledged Dec. 30, 1960; received for record Dec. 30, 1960 at 3 P.M. and recorded J.F.C. 1004/488 (James F. Carney, clerk); a stamp in the margin reads 'Jan. 24 1961 Grantee'. What it settles: the 1960 deed is the first instrument read for 2958 before 1982 and it carries the property's two-part structure: a 14-foot ground-rent leasehold ($65 a year, renewable forever, so not a one-cent rent) and an 8-foot fee corner at 30th Street, both the Palladis' since March 13, 1925 from Albert C. Brandt (J. Milton Brandt, the broker of the 1924 advertisement CR#5169, attested and notarized the 1925 deed). The deed gives the metes and bounds the earlier text said were unknown, and it names the house, so the identification is secure. Corrects 'parties not recited' and 'leasehold or fee unknown' in the earlier chain. What it does not settle: the lessor and the date of the lease behind the $65 rent (S.C.L. 4353/212, now read, repeats the rent but not the lease; its recital points to S.C.L. 3459/372 of 1919); who held the reversion in 1960; the 1961 'see also' deed (J.F.C. 1134/578), the Straw Man deeds of 1965 and 1969, or whether the ground rent was merged or redeemed before 1982. Update Oct. 12, 2026: the deed this one recites, Brandt to Palladi of March 13, 1925 (S.C.L. 4353/212 to 213), is now read (714:mdlr-scl4353-212-brandt-palladi-1925), with the Palladis' mortgage of the same day (714:mdlr-scl4353-213-palladi-first-mortgage-bond-1925): it repeats these two descriptions and the $65 rent word for word, says the lots were conveyed to the Brandts by Clara Butzler on October 9, 1919 (S.C.L. 3459/372), and was attested and notarized by J. Milton Brandt. Update Oct. 12, 2026: the 1919 deed behind the 1925 one (S.C.L. 3459/372, Butzler to the Brandts, 714:mdlr-scl3459-372-butzler-brandt-1919) is now read. It names the lessor and the date of the lease behind the $65 rent: a lease of Aug. 24, 1907 from James Keelty to James F. Bowersox (S.C.L. 2363/423), whose first line the second lot is tied to; the second lot's frontage reads 'six and forty four hundredths feet' there, 'eight feet more or less' here. Update Oct. 12, 2026: the lessor's side of the $65 rent is now read (714:mdlr-jfc1134-578-gerwig-heirs-silbiger-1961): on July 15, 1961 the Gerwig heirs deeded the Silbigers the fee and the rent of the 14-foot lot, six and a half months after this assignment, 'to the end and intent that the reversionary and leasehold estates be forever merged and the annual ground rent henceforth extinguished'. From July 1961 the lot is held in fee simple, free of ground rent.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber S.C.L. 4353, folios 212 to 213 (MSA CE 168-4361; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 211 to 215; the top of 212 is the end of an unrelated mortgage, The Homebuilders Organization Inc. to The Oakmont Realty Company). The index heading reads 'Albert C Brandt &c, Asst to, Giuseppe Palladi &c'. Albert C. Brandt and Alice E. Brandt, his wife, of Baltimore City, to Giuseppe Palladi and Adele Palladi, his wife, dated March 13, 1925, for five dollars and other good and valuable considerations: 'all those two lots of ground situate in Baltimore City'. (1) The first lot begins 'on the west side of the York Road at the distance of four hundred and two feet nine and one half inches northerly from the northwest corner of Twenty Ninth Street and the York Road and at the centre of a partition wall', runs 14 feet northerly on the road to the centre of another partition wall, then 100 feet west, parallel with Twenty-Ninth Street, to the west side of a 10-foot alley, 14 feet back along the alley 'with the use thereof in common with others', and 100 feet east to the beginning: to be held 'for all the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein with the benefit of renewal forever subject to the payment of the annual rent of Sixty Five ($65) Dollars payable half yearly on the first days of March and September'. (2) The second lot begins 416 feet 9 1/2 inches northerly from the same corner, runs 8 feet more or less to 'the south side of Thirtieth Street as now laid out', 100 feet west along it, one foot back along the alley, and east through the partition wall 100 feet: 'in fee simple'. It recites: 'Being the same two lots of ground which are described in a deed dated October 9th 1919 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber S C L No 3459 folio 372 &c were conveyed to the said Grantors by Clara Butzler'. Attested J. Milton Brandt; signed Albert C. Brandt and Alice E. Brandt (seals); acknowledged March 13, 1925 before J. Milton Brandt, Notary Public; received for record and recorded March 14, 1925 at 12.21 P.M. (Stephen C. Little, clerk). A revenue-stamp and index stamp ('Grantee, JUN 3 1925') appear in the margin. What it settles: the 1960 deed's recital is accurate word for word in its descriptions, and the Palladis got both lots on March 13, 1925, the first as a $65 leasehold renewable forever and the second in fee. The seller's source is Clara Butzler, by a deed of October 9, 1919 (S.C.L. 3459/372), now the earliest instrument cited for 2958. J. Milton Brandt, the broker whose 1924 advertisement of the house 'with ground rent' is CR#5169, attested this deed and took the Brandts' acknowledgment as notary: the 1924 advertisement was in all likelihood the Brandts' own listing, and the same family sold the house. What it does not settle: the date, lessor and term of the lease behind the $65 rent (the deed recites the rent, not the lease: the 1919 deed, or the lease it recites, should); when the Brandts or Clara Butzler held the fee of the first lot; and the price (the deed states five dollars; the mortgage on 213 to 215 says its $3,700 was 'part of the purchase price'). Update Oct. 12, 2026: the 1919 deed behind the 1925 one (S.C.L. 3459/372, Butzler to the Brandts, 714:mdlr-scl3459-372-butzler-brandt-1919) is now read. It names the lessor and the date of the lease behind the $65 rent: a lease of Aug. 24, 1907 from James Keelty to James F. Bowersox (S.C.L. 2363/423), whose first line the second lot is tied to; the second lot's frontage reads 'six and forty four hundredths feet' there, 'eight feet more or less' here.

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore City land records, Liber S.C.L. 4353, folios 213 to 215 (MSA CE 168-4361; read in full on the scan, pages 211 to 215). Giuseppe Palladi and Adele Palladi, his wife, of the City of Baltimore, to The First Mortgage Bond Homestead Association Incorporated, dated March 13, 1925, securing $3,700 current money, 'part of the purchase price of the hereinafter described property', the Palladis being members who had subscribed to 36 shares of Series 'A' stock: a principal note due two years after date with 6 percent interest, and eight further notes of $55.50 (the interest) payable at 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21 and 24 months, in gold coin. The mortgaged property is 'those two lots or parcels of ground ... located in block No 3855 and being now known as No 2958 Greenmount Avenue', 'the same two lots of ground described in an assignment of even date herewith and recorded or so intended to be immediately prior hereto ... conveyed to the said Mortgagors by Albert C Brandt and Alice E Brandt his wife': the first lot for the residue of the term, renewable forever, subject to the annual rent of $65, payable in half-yearly instalments on March 1 and September 1, the second in fee simple. A change of ownership of the equity of redemption matures the debt. O. Parker Baker, Esq., is named attorney and trustee for the foreclosure and confession of judgment. Signed Giuseppe Palladi and Adele Palladi, witness O. P. Baker; acknowledged March 13, 1925 before O. Parker Baker, Notary Public, Harry B. Gorrell, president of the association, making the consideration affidavit; received for record and recorded March 14, 1925 at 12.22 P.M. (Stephen C. Little, clerk). The foot of 215 carries the association's release, dated June 14, 1929, 'for value received', signed under its corporate seal by William H. Hudgins, president (attested John F. Steinmetz), recorded June 15, 1929 at 10.40 A.M. What it settles: the property is block 3855, 'now known as No 2958 Greenmount Avenue' in 1925, so the number is old; the Palladis bought with a $3,700 building-association loan, repaid by June 1929; and the two lots were sold together, as the 1960 deed says. What it does not settle: the purchase price (the deed says five dollars); and nothing here names the lessor of the $65 rent.
