summary: Lease, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber A.W.B. 354, folios 371 to 373 (MSA CE 66-404; read in full on the scans Jeff saved, pages 369 to 372, with 373 on the earlier scan; the top of 371 and all of 370 are the end of an unrelated deed, Maurice and Catharine Barrett of Galway to George Brown, recorded July 10, 1845). The index heading reads 'Sarah Biays and others, Lease to David Mumma'. It is the paired instrument of the deed of the same day, A.W.B. 354/374 (row 46070), and carries the 373 tail that ends in a covenant to renew. Made Nov. 9, 1844 between Sarah Biays, Henry N. Bowerman and Elizabeth Bowerman, Walter T. Allender and Hannah Jane Allender (of Baltimore City), Jacob Hoke and Nancy Hoke, Henry Hammond and Frances Hammond (of Harford County), of the first part; John W. Stump of Harford County and Philip G. Biays of Montgomery County, 'Trustees under the deed or Indenture hereinafter referred to', of the second part; and David Mumma of Baltimore County, of the third. They lease him, for 99 years from the day before the date (the term runs from Oct. 1, 1844) at a clear yearly rent of $15.75, payable on the first of October, 'to the said Sarah Biays for and during her natural life and after her death to the said Elizabeth Bowerman, Hannah Jane Allender, Nancy Hoke, and Frances Hammond', 'all that piece or parcel of Land or ground, Situate and lying in Baltimore County ... Beginning for the same on the East Side of the York Turnpike Road, at the Corner formed by the East side of the York Turnpike Road and the South Side of a Lane known as the Quaker Lane', then north 2 1/2 degrees east 66 feet 8 inches along the east side of the turnpike 'to the Lot of ground Leased by Sarah Biays and others to Abraham H. Becker', east 16 6/10 perches on that lot to the line of 'the Quaker Lot', south 16 1/4 degrees west 59 feet 'to Quaker Lane', and along the lane to the beginning. 'It being a part of the Land or ground which by Indenture bearing date the Eleventh day of April One thousand Eight hundred and twenty two, and recorded among the Land records of Baltimore County aforesaid in Liber W.G. No 165 folio 492 &c was granted and Conveyed by John McFadden to the above named John W. Stump and Philip G. Biays, In Trust for the said Sarah Biays Wife of James Biays now deceased, for and during the term of her natural life, and after her death, to be Conveyed to the aforesaid Elizabeth Bowerman, Hannah Jane Allender, Nancy Hoke, and Frances Hammond, (Children of the said James and Sarah Biays)'. The covenants (on 372 and 373): Mumma pays the rent and all taxes and assessments; the lessors may re-enter if the rent is 60 days unpaid and expel him if a year in arrears; they covenant quiet enjoyment; and, on 373, on payment of $10 and at the end of the term the parties 'shall and will' make him a lease 'for other ninety nine years', 'renewable and renewed from time to time forever'. Signed S. Biays, H. N. Bowerman, E. Bowerman, Walter T. Allender, Hannah J. Allender, J. Hoke, Nancy Hoke, Henry Hammond, Fanny Hammond, Jno. W. Stump, Philip G. Biays and David Mumma; acknowledged Nov. 9, 1844 (Baltimore City) and May 29, 1845 (Philip G. Biays, Montgomery County); recorded July 10, 1845 (A. W. Bradford, clerk). What it settles: the 1822 McFadden (McFadon) deed is Liber W.G. 165 folio 492, and it was a trust deed for Sarah Biays, widow of James Biays (d. 1822), for life and then for her four daughters, the same four couples who sell Mumma the south-west lot by the deed of the same day. Mumma took two parcels from them on Nov. 9, 1844: the 94 square perches in fee on the WEST side of the turnpike, at the south-west corner of the lane toward Gilmor's (354/374), and this lot on the EAST side, at the south-east corner by the Quaker Lane, as a 99-year lease at $15.75, renewable forever. Abraham H. Becker held an adjoining leased lot to the north, and the 'Quaker Lot' lay to the east. What it does not settle: which present parcel the east-side lot is (the 66 feet 8 inches of frontage and the 'Quaker Lane' are the clues; it is on the opposite side of the turnpike from 3010 to 3020, so it is not that chapter's ground); whether the Quaker Lane is the same lane as the one toward Gilmor's; and the later history of the lease. Update Oct. 12, 2026: the McFadon deed of trust is now read at W.G. 165/492 (719:mdlr-wg165-492-mcfadon-trust-stump-biays-1822), $7,700, April 11, 1822, in trust for Sarah Biays and then her four daughters.

Box 111, Cockeysville, Maryland), assignor, to AMJM Limited Partnership (the same P.O. box), assignee, for 'good and valuable consideration': all its rights in the promissory note dated Aug. 31, 2010 for $40,000.00 executed by Michael Williams and Kasheilia Vanessa Richardson (also Kasheilia Vanessa Williams) and the deed of trust of even date to Ronald J. Roberta, Jr., Trustee, and IRA Tax Certificates Limited Partnership, Beneficiary, 'filed of record on September 2, 2010, in Book 12903, folio 268'; 'Premises known as 2958 Greenmount Avenue, Baltimore, Maryland 21218-4121 ... Lot .042 acres, Ward 12, Section 17, Block 3855, Lot 017'. Without recourse, representation or warranty. Signed Ronald J. Roberta, Jr., General Partner, before Patricia W. Burgess, Notary Public, Harford County; received for record Aug. 29, 2011 at 1:43 P.M. (recording fee $20; imp. fd. surcharge $40). What it settles: the purchase-money deed of trust of Aug. 31, 2010 (row 45994, F.M.C. 12903/272) passed in 2011 from IRA Tax Certificates LP to AMJM LP: AMJM LP is the seller of the 2010 deed to Williams and Richardson (row 5046), the two partnerships share the P.O. box and the general partner, so the note went back to the seller's own entity. What it does not settle: its folio cite, 'Book 12903, folio 268', is the folio of the deed from AMJM to Williams and Richardson (row 5046), recorded the same day; the deed of trust itself is at 12903/272 (row 45994, and the 2014 substitute-trustee deed).

summary: Removal of Trustees and Appointment of Substitute Trustees, Baltimore City land records, Liber F.M.C. 16474, folios 221 to 223 (MSA CE 164-25629; read in full on the scan), headed '2958 Greenmount Avenue'. AMJM Limited Partnership, a Maryland limited partnership, recites that on Aug. 31, 2010 Michael Williams and Kasheilia Vanessa Richardson gave a Commercial Purchase Money Deed of Trust to Ronald J. Roberta, Jr., Trustee (Liber 12903, Folio 272) to secure a note held by IRA Tax Certificates Limited Partnership, that IRA assigned it to AMJM on Aug. 1, 2011 (Liber 13721, Folio 334), and that the deed of trust lets the note holder remove the trustee and appoint a successor; it removes Roberta and appoints Douglas L. Burgess as Substitute Trustee, effective Aug. 8, 2014. Signed by Ronald J. Roberta, Jr., General Partner, with a witness; received for record Aug. 18, 2014 at 2:22 P.M. What it settles: AMJM LP still held the Williams and Richardson note in August 2014 and moved to enforce it by a substitute trustee; the substitute trustee appointed here, Douglas L. Burgess, is the grantor of the foreclosure deed of April 2015 to 2958 Greenmount LLC (row 5047, L.G.A. 17087/58, case 24-O-14-002888, with the case papers in MSA CE 164-26243 p.63 to 86), so this was the deed of trust that was foreclosed (the 2015 deed's recital should confirm). It also fixes the deed of trust at 12903/272 and the assignment at 13721/334. What it does not settle: the default, the amount, or the sale.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber S.C.L. 3459, folios 372 to 373 (MSA CE 168-3467; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 371 to 375; the deed opens at the foot of 372 under the index heading 'Clara Butzler, Deed to Albert C Brandt &c'). The first of the five scanned pages, 371, and the top of 372 are the end of the deed that fed it (next row). Clara Butzler, unmarried, of Baltimore City, to Albert C. Brandt and Alice E. Brandt, his wife, 'as tenants by the entireties the survivor of them their assigns and the heirs personal representatives and assigns of the survivor', dated Oct. 9, 1919, for five dollars and other valuable considerations: 'all those two lots of ground situate in Baltimore City'. (1) The first begins on the west side of the York Road 402 feet 9 1/2 inches north of the northwest corner of Twenty-Ninth Street, at the centre of a partition wall, runs 14 feet north on the road to the centre of another wall, 100 feet west (parallel with Twenty-Ninth Street) to the west side of a ten-foot alley, 14 feet back along the alley 'with the use thereof in common with others', and 100 feet east: the lot 2958's 1925 and 1960 deeds describe word for word. (2) The second begins at 416 feet 9 1/2 inches 'at the end of the first line of the lot of ground described in a lease from James Keelty to James F. Bowersox dated August 24 1907 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber S C L No 2363 folio 423', runs north on the west side of the York Road 'six and forty four hundredths feet' (the later deeds say 'eight feet, more or less') to 'the northernmost outline of the land described in a deed from William T. Wilson and wife to the said James Keelty dated January 11 1907 and recorded ... in Liber R O No 2302 folio 43', 36 feet 7 inches west along that line to the south side of Thirtieth Street, 63 feet 5 inches farther west along the street to the west side of the alley, 10 1/2 inches south along it to the end of the second line of the Keelty lease, and 100 feet east to the beginning. The deed says it is 'the same property which by deed bearing even date herewith and recorded or intended to be recorded ... was granted conveyed and assigned by Alice E. Brandt, trustee et al, to the said party hereto of the first part'. The first lot is held for 'all the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein with the benefit of renewal thereof forever subject to the payment of the annual rent of Sixty five dollars payable semi annually on March and September first'; the second 'in fee simple'; the household furniture and utensils in the house pass with the buildings. Butzler covenants special warranty and further assurance. Witness J. Milton Brandt; signed Clara Butzler (seal); acknowledged Oct. 9, 1919 before J. Milton Brandt, Notary Public, Baltimore City; received for record Oct. 10, 1919 and recorded the same day ('Sent for Stephen C. Little, clerk'); a Grantee index stamp reads 'Dec. 13 1919'. What it settles: the $65 rent is the rent of the 1907 lease from James Keelty to James F. Bowersox (S.C.L. 2363/423), so Keelty was the original ground-rent lessor and the lease dates from August 24, 1907; the lot and its metes are the same in 1919, 1925 and 1960, except that the second lot's frontage reads six and forty-four hundredths feet here and eight feet more or less later. Butzler was a one-day link: she took the property from the Brandts' own family and trust and sold it to Alice and Albert Brandt as tenants by the entireties the same day, taking back a $1,700 mortgage (third row). J. Milton Brandt witnessed and notarized every instrument, and is the broker of the 1924 advertisement and the attorney in the mortgage. What it does not settle: the lease itself (S.C.L. 2363/423 is not pulled), who built the house and when (the 1907 lease is the earliest date for the lot as a leasehold; the row of about 1900 is the National Register's), the 1917 trust deed's terms, and the date of the 'long' rent's extinguishment. The ground behind the $65 rent, as these pages recite it: William T. Wilson and his wife to James Keelty, deed of Jan. 11, 1907 (Liber R.O. 2302 folio 43); James Keelty to James F. Bowersox, lease of Aug. 24, 1907 (Liber S.C.L. 2363 folio 423), the lease of the first lot, so Keelty was the ground-rent lessor; and James Keelty and wife to Alice E. Brandt (formerly Alice E. Bowersox), in trust for the lives of James F. Bowersox and Mary E. Bowersox his wife and the survivor, remainder to Alice E. Brandt, Archibald Bowersox and Clarence V. Bowersox in fee simple, deed of Oct. 3, 1917 (Liber S.C.L. 3159 folio 384), which the pages cite for the second lot. None of the three is pulled. Mary E. Bowersox had since died, 'all interests in the properties are now vested in the said parties of the first part'. Update Oct. 12, 2026: the instruments behind the $65 lease are now read: William T. Wilson to James Keelty, Jan. 11, 1907 (R.O. 2302/43), Keelty's 99-year lease to the Bowersoxes, Aug. 24, 1907 (S.C.L. 2363/423), their $1,300 building-association mortgage of the same day (S.C.L. 2363/425), and Keelty's Oct. 3, 1917 deed in trust of the second lot (S.C.L. 3159/384); see the 714:mdlr-ro2302, -scl2363 and -scl3159 rows.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber S.C.L. 3459, ending at folios 371 and 372 (MSA CE 168-3467; the scan Jeff saved opens mid-deed at 371, so the first page, with the consideration and the opening of the first lot's description, is not read; it begins on an earlier folio, probably 370). Read: the rest of the first-lot and all of the second-lot description, the recital, the habendum and the acknowledgment. The grantors, as signed and acknowledged on 371 and 372: Alice E. Brandt, trustee; James F. Bowersox; Alice E. Brandt and Albert C. Brandt, her husband; Archibald Bowersox and Inetta Bowersox, his wife; Clarence V. Bowersox and Inetta F. Bowersox, his wife; the grantee is Clara Butzler (the habendum says 'unto and to the proper use of the said Clara Butzler her personal representatives and assigns for all the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein with the benefit of renewal thereof forever subject to the payment of the aforesaid annual rent' for the first lot, and 'her heirs and assigns in fee simple' for the second). The second lot is described as 416 feet 9 1/2 inches north of the northwest corner of York Road and Twenty-Ninth Street, at the end of the first line of the lot in the Keelty to Bowersox lease of Aug. 24, 1907 (S.C.L. 2363/423), with the same metes the Butzler deed gives (row above). It recites: 'Being the same lot of ground which by deed dated October 3 1917 and recorded among the aforesaid Land Records in Liber S C L No 3159 folio 384 etc was granted and conveyed by James Keelty and wife to Alice E. Brandt (formerly Alice E. Bowersox) in trust during the lifetime of said James F. Bowersox and Mary E. Bowersox his wife or the survivor of them with remainder to Alice E. Brandt, Archibald Bowersox and Clarence V. Bowersox in fee simple. The said Mary E. Bowersox wife of James F. Bowersox having since died all interests in the properties are now vested in the said parties of the first part hereto.' Together with the buildings, 'and also the household furniture furnishings and utensils contained in the above described premises'. Tested by J. Milton Brandt; acknowledged Oct. 9, 1919 before J. Milton Brandt, Notary Public; received for record Oct. 10, 1919 at 10:15 A.M. and recorded the same day. What it settles: where the Brandts got title: the Bowersox family (James F. Bowersox, his children Alice, Archibald and Clarence, and their spouses), whose life and remainder interests were held in a trust made by Keelty's 1917 deed, with Alice E. Brandt, the Brandts' own Alice, as trustee, conveyed to Clara Butzler on Oct. 9, 1919, and Butzler conveyed to Alice and Albert Brandt the same day, so the 1919 pair converted the Bowersox trust into a tenancy by the entireties. What it does not settle: the consideration and the opening of the deed (the first page), whether the 1917 trust gave the Bowersoxes a leasehold or the fee in the first lot, and James F. Bowersox's own earlier chain. The ground behind the $65 rent, as these pages recite it: William T. Wilson and his wife to James Keelty, deed of Jan. 11, 1907 (Liber R.O. 2302 folio 43); James Keelty to James F. Bowersox, lease of Aug. 24, 1907 (Liber S.C.L. 2363 folio 423), the lease of the first lot, so Keelty was the ground-rent lessor; and James Keelty and wife to Alice E. Brandt (formerly Alice E. Bowersox), in trust for the lives of James F. Bowersox and Mary E. Bowersox his wife and the survivor, remainder to Alice E. Brandt, Archibald Bowersox and Clarence V. Bowersox in fee simple, deed of Oct. 3, 1917 (Liber S.C.L. 3159 folio 384), which the pages cite for the second lot. None of the three is pulled. Mary E. Bowersox had since died, 'all interests in the properties are now vested in the said parties of the first part'. Update Oct. 12, 2026: the 1917 deed it recites (S.C.L. 3159/384, Keelty and wife to Alice E. Brandt, trustee) is now read, with Keelty's 1907 lease and the Wilson deed behind it: see 714:mdlr-scl3159-384-keelty-brandt-trustee-1917. The trust was for the lives of James F. and Mary E. Bowersox, remainder in common to their children Alice, Archibald and Clarence. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the deed's FIRST page is now read: it begins on S.C.L. 3459/370 (MSA CE 168-3467, pages 366 to 370; 366 to 369 are unrelated instruments), under the index heading 'Alice E. Brandt Trustee &c Deed To Clara Butzler'. 'This Deed made this 9th day of October in the year nineteen hundred and nineteen by and between Alice E. Brandt (formerly Alice E. Bowersox) Trustee, James F. Bowersox, Alice E. Brandt and Albert C. Brandt her husband, Archibald Bowersox and Loretta Bowersox his wife, Clarence V. Bowersox and Loretta F. Bowersox his wife [the wives' name reads Loretta here and Inetta on 371: the hand is not clear] of Baltimore City, parties of the first part, and Clara Butzler unmarried of the same place, party of the second part. Witnesseth that in consideration of the sum of Five Dollars and other valuable considerations ... the said parties of the first part do hereby grant and assign unto the said party of the second part her personal representatives and assigns all those two lots of ground situate in Baltimore City.' The first lot (402 ft 9 1/2 in north of the corner of 29th Street, 14 ft by 100 ft on the west side of the York Road, from the centre of one partition wall to the centre of the next) is 'the same lot of ground which by deed dated August 1 1908 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber S.C.L. No 2445 folio 42 &c was granted and assigned by James F. Bowersox and wife to Alice E. Brandt (formerly Alice E. Bowersox) in trust during the lifetime of the said James F. Bowersox and Mary E. Bowersox his wife or the survivor of them with remainder to [Alice E. Brandt,] Archibald Bowersox and Clarence V. Bowersox subject to the annual rent of sixty-five dollars payable in equal semi-annual instalments on the first days of March and September in each and every year'; the second lot (416 ft 9 1/2 in) is the one the 1917 Keelty deed put in trust. So the family trust of the leasehold dates from Aug. 1, 1908, a year after Keelty's lease to the Bowersoxes (Aug. 24, 1907), and the 1917 deed added the second lot to it. The consideration, $5, is read; the row's status is raised to verified.

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore City land records, Liber S.C.L. 3459, folios 374 to 375 (MSA CE 168-3467; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 374 and 375: the acknowledgment, the recording stamp and any release are on 376 and after, not pulled). Index heading 'Albert C Brandt &c, Mtge to Clara Butzler'. Albert C. Brandt and Alice E. Brandt, his wife, of Baltimore City, mortgagors, to Clara Butzler, mortgagee, dated Oct. 9, 1919, securing $1,700.00 'for money this day loaned and advanced' by their negotiable promissory note of even date, payable to her order five years after date with interest at 6 percent a year, both payable semi-annually, 'in gold coin of the United States of the present standard of weight and fineness'. They grant and assign 'all those two lots of ground' with the same descriptions as the Butzler deed (first lot 402 ft 9 1/2 in north of Twenty-Ninth Street, 14 by 100 ft; second lot at 416 ft 9 1/2 in, 'six and forty four hundredths feet' on the York Road, bounded by the Wilson to Keelty deed of Jan. 11, 1907, R.O. 2302/43, and the Keelty to Bowersox lease of Aug. 24, 1907, S.C.L. 2363/423), 'subject however as to the first herein described lot to the annual rent of sixty five dollars payable in equal semi annual installments on the first days of March and September in each and every year' and the second 'in fee simple'. A default accelerates the debt; the mortgagors assent to a decree under Chapter 123 of the Laws of Maryland (Jan. 1898 session); and a sale may be made by Butzler, her representatives or assigns, or by J. Milton Brandt, her or their attorney, under Article LXVI of the Code of 1904. What it settles: the Brandts bought with a $1,700 loan from the seller of the day, Clara Butzler, five years at 6 percent, and J. Milton Brandt was the named foreclosure attorney. What it does not settle: the rest of the instrument (the covenant to insure, the signatures, the acknowledgment and the recording) and whether and when it was released (the 1925 deed, which sells the same lots to the Palladis, says nothing of it; nothing read shows it paid). The ground behind the $65 rent, as these pages recite it: William T. Wilson and his wife to James Keelty, deed of Jan. 11, 1907 (Liber R.O. 2302 folio 43); James Keelty to James F. Bowersox, lease of Aug. 24, 1907 (Liber S.C.L. 2363 folio 423), the lease of the first lot, so Keelty was the ground-rent lessor; and James Keelty and wife to Alice E. Brandt (formerly Alice E. Bowersox), in trust for the lives of James F. Bowersox and Mary E. Bowersox his wife and the survivor, remainder to Alice E. Brandt, Archibald Bowersox and Clarence V. Bowersox in fee simple, deed of Oct. 3, 1917 (Liber S.C.L. 3159 folio 384), which the pages cite for the second lot. None of the three is pulled. Mary E. Bowersox had since died, 'all interests in the properties are now vested in the said parties of the first part'.

The lot: 'Beginning for the same on the west side of the York Road at the end of the south forty six degrees east twenty two and four tenths perch line of the land described in a deed from Walter T. Allender Trustee et al to William T. Wilson senior dated January 19th 1848 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County now City in Liber A.W.B. No. 391 folio 169', then northeasterly on the west side of the York Road about 118 feet to 'the southernmost outline of the land described in a lease from William Thomas Wilson to Eleanor Cross dated April 16th 1874' (Baltimore County Liber J.B. 86 folio 487), westerly on that outline and on, 395 feet more or less in all, to the southeast side of Gilmore Lane, southwesterly on the lane about 82 feet 6 inches to the north 81 degrees west 27 perch line of the Allender deed, and southeasterly 450 feet more or less to the beginning. 'The lot of ground above described being and comprising the southernmost part of all those two lots of ground which were granted and conveyed to William T. Wilson senior in fee simple by the two following deeds viz one thereof from Jacob Hoke and wife et al dated June 10th 1847 ... in Liber A.W.B. No. 382 folio 30 &c and the other from Walter T. Allender Trustee et al dated January 19th 1848 ... Liber A.W.B. No. 391 folio 169' (the liber of the first reads 382 on the scan). The deed adds that those lots 'are also the same which by the Last Will and Testament of the said William T. Wilson senior were devised and bequeathed to his wife Henrietta D'Arcy Wilson for and during her natural life with power to her said wife to devise same as she by her last will and testament may direct' (Baltimore County Wills, Liber J.S. No. 1), and that Henrietta D'Arcy Wilson, 'in pursuance of the power conferred on her by the said will of her husband by the sixth clause of her last will and testament' (Wills, Liber J.S.R. No. 1), 'did devise and bequeath said lot of ground to her son the said William T. Wilson'. Special warranty and further assurance. Signed William T. Wilson and Eliza W. Wilson (seals), witness Wm. D. Poultney; acknowledged Jan. 11, 1907 before Wm. D. Poultney, Notary Public, Baltimore; received for record Jan. 12, 1907 at 11:30 A.M. and recorded the same day (Robt. Ogle, clerk). What it settles: the ground behind 2958's two lots came to James Keelty from William T. Wilson on Jan. 11, 1907, seven months before Keelty's lease of the 14-foot lot (S.C.L. 2363/423) and ten years before his deed in trust of the 8-foot lot (S.C.L. 3159/384); both of those cite this deed. The Wilson title runs William T. Wilson senior (deeds of June 10, 1847 from Jacob Hoke and wife et al. and Jan. 19, 1848 from Walter T. Allender, trustee, et al.), to his widow Henrietta D'Arcy Wilson for life with a power of appointment, then by her will to their son William T. Wilson, the grantor here. Jacob Hoke and Walter T. Allender are the names of two of the Biays sons-in-law in the 1844 Mumma deed (A.W.B. 354/374, row 46070), so the 1847 and 1848 deeds may come out of the same McFadon trust ground; these pages do not say so. What it does not settle: where this parcel lies on the modern grid (it is measured from the Allender line, not from a cross street, and whether the 'Gilmore Lane' of 1907 is the later Thirtieth Street is not shown, though Keelty's 1917 deed does bound his land by 'the south side of Thirtieth Street'); the Hoke and Allender deeds (A.W.B. 382/30, 391/169) and the two wills are not pulled; and the 1844 survey Edition 2 cites names a 'James Wilson' as grantee of lots 1 to 3, where this deed names William T. Wilson senior as grantee in 1847 and 1848: the two are not shown to be the same conveyances. Update Oct. 13, 2026: both deeds this lot recites are now read: A.W.B. 382/30, Hoke, Hammond, Bowerman and Allender with their wives to William T. Wilson, June 10, 1847, 3/4 acre 11 perches for $750 (714:mdlr-awb382-30-hoke-bowerman-allender-wilson-1847), and A.W.B. 391/169, Walter T. Allender, trustee, to William T. Wilson, Jan. 19, 1848, 1 acre 2 perches, a Chancery sale of May 1, 1847 for $300 (714:mdlr-awb391-169-allender-trustee-scott-wilson-1848). The 'south forty six degrees east twenty two and four tenths perch line' and the 'north 81 degrees west 27 perch line' named here are read in the Allender deed word for word. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the J.B. 86/487 carried for the Cross lease is a different lease of the same date: William Thomas Wilson to Margaret Hamilton, wife of Charles Hamilton, 100 ft just south of A. G. Mott's lot, $325 a year (714:mdlr-jb86-487-wilson-margaret-hamilton-lease-1874). The Cross lease is very probably the instrument recorded just before it (J.B. 86, folios before 487, recorded May 6, 1874 at 2 p.m.). Henrietta D. A. Wilson's will was probated Aug. 29, 1854. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the Cross lease is read (714:mdlr-jb86-483-wilson-elenor-cross-lease-1874): 35 ft on the turnpike immediately south of Margaret Hamilton's 100 ft, which is immediately south of A. G. Mott's lot. Keelty's ground begins at the Cross lot's south line. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (night): Keelty also created the 2936 rent, by a lease of Oct. 29, 1907 to Richard C. Jent et al. at $60 (R.O. 2380/251), and sold it with at least three other lots to Leopold A. Fischer on Dec. 30, 1907 (704:mdlr-scl4722-289-fischer-clarke-reversion-2936-keelty-lease-1927); 2936 is on the same 14-ft grid, eleven lots south of 2958, but south of this deed's 118 ft: Keelty held 2930 to 2940 from the Brady estate trustees, Richard H. Woollen et al., by deed of Mar. 28, 1907 (R.O. 2319/497; 704:mdlr-scl2394-467-keelty-fischer-six-rents-2930-2940-1907), so the Brady and Wilson grounds probably meet between 2942 and 2944 (inference). Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): the Brady trustees' deed of Mar. 28, 1907 (714:mdlr-ro2319-497-brady-trustees-keelty-seven-houses-1907) bounds north on 'the land belonging to the said James Keelty', so this Wilson parcel begins at the north end of 2942, about 301 to 305 ft north of 29th Street. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (south call re-read): the whole deed was read again from the scan (pp. 42 to 46; the deed runs from the foot of 43 to the signatures on 45, recorded Jan. 12, 1907 at 11:30 A.M., Robt. Ogle, Clerk), and the description above is right word for word. What the row did not say is what its last two calls are. The deed's own words: 'running thence southwesterly bounding on the southeast side of Gilmore Lane about eighty two feet and six inches more or less to the north eighty one degrees west twenty seven perch line of the land described in the deed from said Walter T. Allender Trustee et al to the said William T. Wilson senior above mentioned as said line is indicated on the ground by a partition fence there situate thence southeasterly bounding on said line reversely and on said fence four hundred and fifty feet more or less to the place of beginning.' In plain language: the SOUTH boundary of the lot is not a new line. It is the Allender deed's north 81 degrees west, 27-perch line (27 perches is 445.5 ft; the deed says 450 more or less) run backward, from the east side of Gilmore Lane (probably the old two-perch road, INFERRED) to the turnpike, and in January 1907 a partition fence stood on it. The deed names no owner, lot or street on the far side of it. The beginning is the turnpike end of that line (the end of the 22.4-perch line, on the west side of the York Road), so the south-east corner of the lot is the point where the Allender triangle of Jan. 19, 1848 touches the road (714:mdlr-awb391-169-allender-trustee-scott-wilson-1848). The Brady tract of Nov. 30, 1848 ends its north line the same way, 'south 81 degrees east 27 perches to the Baltimore and York Turnpike Road' (714:mdlr-awb404-533-allender-brady-1848), and the two were lots of one Chancery sale, so the Wilson/Keelty ground and the Brady ground meet along that one line from the turnpike west to Gilmore Lane, and the Wilson south-east corner and the Brady north-east corner are one point on the road (INFERRED from the same bearing and length and the one sale; the 1907 Brady trustees' deed bounds its north on 'the land belonging to the said James Keelty', row 46657). What it settles: (1) the deed confirms the structure of the 2942/2944 point: the Wilson and Brady grounds meet at the beginning on the turnpike, and the 118 feet of frontage that follows (the eight 14-foot lots of 2944 to 2958, 112 ft, plus the 6.44-foot wedge, 118.44 ft, row 46188) ends at the south line of the Cross lease; the Brady trustees' deed puts the north end of 2942 at about 301 ft 4 1/2 in (95 ft from 206 ft 4 1/2 in) and the built widths reach 304 ft 9 1/2 in, within its 'more or less'. It does not disagree with that point anywhere. (2) Gilmore Lane is the only street this deed names on the west; it names no Thirtieth Street. The deed in trust of Oct. 3, 1917 has the south side of Thirtieth Street meet the north outline of this ground 36 ft 7 in west of the turnpike and run along it (row 46087), so the street was named or cut between Jan. 11, 1907 and Oct. 3, 1917; this deed does not date it. What it does not settle: (1) the deed measures nothing from Twenty-ninth Street, so the corner's distance from 29th Street (the 2942/2944 line at about 304 ft 9 1/2 in) is still inferred from the lot widths and the Brady trustees' deed, not read from a measure on the Wilson side; (2) the closing line bears north 81 degrees west against a turnpike that runs about north 3 1/2 degrees east, so it is about 5 1/2 degrees off square to the road, and whether the lot lines of 2942 and 2944 follow it or are cut square (the leases say 'parallel with Twenty ninth Street') is a plat question; (3) where Thirtieth Street was cut, and whether Gilmore Lane became it. Next: a City plat or fire-insurance map of the block, 1901 to 1914, for the fence line and the lane, and the Brady trustees' 1906 deed to Harvey (R.O. 2290/225, already filed on 2332), which bounds the rest of the Brady tract on a lane that was Gilmor Lane.

summary: Lease, Baltimore City land records, Liber S.C.L. 2363, folios 423 to 425 (MSA CE 168-2371; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 422 to 426; the top of 423 is the end of an unrelated release; the lease opens under the index heading 'James Keelty Lease to James F. Bowersox &c'; the Bowersox mortgage of the same day follows it on 425, next row). James Keelty, bachelor, of Baltimore City, to James F. Bowersox and Mary E. Bowersox, his wife, 'in consideration of the sum of eighteen hundred and fifty dollars current money and in consideration of the rent hereinafter expressed': 'all that lot of ground ... Beginning for the same on the west side of York Road at the distance of four hundred and two feet nine and one half inches northerly from the northwest corner of Twenty ninth Street and the York Road and at the centre of a partition wall there situate', 14 feet north on the York Road to the centre of another partition wall, west through that wall and parallel with Twenty-Ninth Street 100 feet to the west side of a ten-foot alley, 14 feet south on the alley 'with the use thereof in common with others', and east 100 feet to the beginning. 'Being a part of the lot of ground which by deed dated January 11th 1907 and recorded ... in Liber R.O. No. 2302 folio 43 etc was conveyed by William T. Wilson and wife to said James Keelty.' The term is 99 years from the date, 'yielding and paying unto the said James Keelty his heirs or assigns the rent or yearly sum of sixty five dollars and that in even and equal half yearly instalments accounting from the first day of September one thousand nine hundred and seven over and above all deductions for taxes and assessments'; distress for arrears; re-entry if the rent is sixty days in arrear, and if six months in arrear Keelty may re-enter 'as if this Lease had never been made'; Keelty covenants that on payment of ten dollars as renewal fine he will give a new 99-year lease on the same rent and covenants 'so that the demise hereby created may be renewable and renewed from time to time forever'. Signed James Keelty, James F. Bowersox and Mary E. Bowersox (seals), witness Bernard A. Schmitz; acknowledged Aug. 24, 1907 before Bernard A. Schmitz, Notary Public; received for record Aug. 24, 1907 at 11:20 A.M. (as read) and recorded the same day (Robt. Ogle, clerk). What it settles: the $65 ground rent of 2958 was created on Aug. 24, 1907, by James Keelty as lessor, with a $1,850 fine paid up front (a sale of the building lot in lease form); the lines of the 14 by 100-foot lot run through the centres of partition walls 'there situate', which implies the row's walls stood by August 1907 (an inference from the wording, not a statement); the lease is renewable forever for a $10 fine, which is why the 1919, 1925 and 1960 deeds call the lot a leasehold with 'the benefit of renewal forever'. What it does not settle: who built the row, who held the reversion between Keelty and Henry Gerwig (the Gerwig heirs' 1961 deed cites an 1932 deed from Sarah Stanley Armour, S.C.L. 5289/183, not pulled), and the margin notes on the index line, which I cannot read. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the Bowersoxes put the leasehold into a family trust a year after the lease, by a deed of Aug. 1, 1908 (James F. Bowersox and wife to Alice E. Brandt, trustee, S.C.L. 2445/42), as the first page of the 1919 deed to Butzler recites (S.C.L. 3459/370). Update Oct. 13, 2026: the lease's afterlife is read: the Bowersoxes put the 14-foot leasehold into a family trust on Aug. 1, 1908 (714:mdlr-scl2445-42-bowersox-family-trust-1908, S.C.L. 2445/42), and the reversion and its $65 rent are traced in the Armour deed of Mar. 12, 1932 (714:mdlr-scl5289-183-armour-gerwig-1932, S.C.L. 5289/183): James G. Stanley, trustee, to Sallie H. Stanley (later Sarah Stanley Armour), Nov. 4, 1908 (S.C.L. 2460/398), then Armour to Henry Gerwig. The step from Keelty to Stanley is still not read. Update Oct. 14, 2026: Keelty sold the reversion of this lease a month later, on Sept. 26, 1907, to James G. Stanley, trustee (R.O. 2371/148, recited in 714:mdlr-scl2460-398-stanley-trustee-sallie-stanley-1908).

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore City land records, Liber S.C.L. 2363, folios 425 to 427 (MSA CE 168-2371; the scan Jeff saved ends on 426, so the acknowledgment, the recording stamp and any release are on 427 and after, not pulled; index heading 'James F. Bowersox &c, Mtge to Madison Square Permt Bldg Asso', with a margin note I cannot read). James F. Bowersox and Mary E. Bowersox, his wife, to The Madison Square Permanent Building Association of Baltimore City, dated Aug. 24, 1907: they have received 'an advance or loan of thirteen hundred dollars ($1300.00) on thirteen shares of its stock', and 'it was a condition precedent to said advance being made that this mortgage should be executed, said loan being for the balance of the purchase money of the hereinafter described lot of ground'. They grant and assign the lot: 'Beginning for the same on the west side of York Road four hundred and two feet nine and a half inches north from Twenty ninth Street fronting north on York Road fourteen feet with a depth west of even width of one hundred feet to a ten feet alley Being more fully described in a Lease of even date herewith and intended to be recorded prior hereto from James Keelty (bachelor) to said mortgagors', to hold 'for and during all the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein with the right and benefit of renewal from time to time forever'. They covenant to pay 25 cents a week as dues on each of the 13 shares plus a premium of 12 cents a week a share, 'making in all the weekly sum of four dollars and eighty one cents ($4.81)', until $100 a share has been paid back, and to pay all ground rents, taxes and assessments and keep the improvements insured. What it settles: the Bowersoxes bought on credit, putting up $550 of the $1,850 price and borrowing $1,300 from a building association on the same day (the sum of the mortgage and the $550 equals the fine; this is arithmetic, not a statement in the deed); the mortgage calls the first lot 'fronting north on York Road fourteen feet' with no mention of a building by name. What it does not settle: the rest of the instrument (the acknowledgment and recording) and when it was released.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber S.C.L. 3159, folio 384 (MSA CE 168-3167; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 383 to 387; index heading 'James Keelty &c, Deed to Alice E. Brandt, Trustee'; a margin note reads 'A. J. Jones, 11-7-17', which I take to be a clerk's check; the other instruments on the page are unrelated). James Keelty and Nora L. Keelty, his wife, of Baltimore City, to Alice E. Brandt, formerly Alice E. Bowersox, trustee, dated Oct. 3, 1917, for five dollars and other good and valuable consideration, in fee simple. The lot: 'Beginning for the same on the west side of the York Road at the distance of four hundred and sixteen feet nine and one half inches Northerly from the North west corner of York Road and Twenty ninth Street and at the end of the first line of the lot of ground described in a lease from the said James Keelty to James F. Bowersox dated August 24th 1907 and recorded ... in Liber S.C.L. No. 2363 folio 423 etc and running thence Northerly binding on the west side of York Road six and forty four one hundredths feet to the Northernmost outline of the land described in a deed from William T. Wilson and wife to the said James Keelty dated January 11th 1907 and recorded ... in Liber R.O. No. 2302 folio 43 etc and running thence with and bounding on said line westerly thirty six feet and seven inches to the South side of Thirtieth Street, thence still westerly and binding thereon sixty three feet and five inches to the west side of an alley ten feet wide there situate, thence Southerly binding thereon with the use thereof in common ten and one half inches to the end of the second line of the land described in the lease from the said James Keelty to the said James F. Bowersox above referred to and thence easterly binding thereon one hundred feet to the place of beginning. Being a part of the lot of ground which by deed bearing date January 11th 1907 ... R.O. No. 2302 folio 43 etc was granted and conveyed by William T. Wilson and wife unto the said James Keelty in fee simple.' (The four-hundred-and-sixteen-foot figure is the 402 feet 9 1/2 inches of the lease plus its 14-foot frontage.) The deed is to Alice E. Brandt 'in fee simple, in trust and confidence nevertheless', for the life of James F. Bowersox and Mary E. Bowersox, his wife, or the survivor, 'for the use and benefit of the family as now constituted', named as James F. Bowersox, Mary E. Bowersox, Alice E. Brandt (formerly Alice E. Bowersox), Archibald Bowersox and Clarence V. Bowersox, and after both parents' deaths 'to the use and benefit of the said children absolutely free clear and discharged from this trust as tenants in common share and share alike'. Special warranty. Signed James Keelty and Nora L. Keelty (seals), witness Alfred T. Edel; acknowledged Oct. 3, 1917 before Alfred T. Edel, Notary Public, Baltimore; received for record Oct. 8, 1917 at 11:45 A.M. and recorded the same day (Stephen C. Little, clerk). What it settles: where the second, thin lot of 2958 (6.44 feet on the York Road, running to Thirtieth Street) came from: Keelty's own deed in trust of Oct. 3, 1917, to Alice Brandt, with life interests for her parents and remainders to the three children (the 1919 Bowersox deed to Clara Butzler, S.C.L. 3459/371, recites exactly this); that the Bowersoxes paid nothing on this lot ('five dollars and other good and valuable consideration') and held it by a trust, not by lease, so it was always fee simple; and that by 1917 Thirtieth Street was the northern boundary of Keelty's land. What it does not settle: why Keelty gave it (nothing in the deed says), and the lot's frontage, which later deeds call 'eight feet, more or less' where this one measures 6.44. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the first lot (the $65 leasehold) had been in the same Bowersox family trust since Aug. 1, 1908 (S.C.L. 2445/42), so this 1917 deed added the second lot to a trust that already existed (S.C.L. 3459/370).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber J.F.C. 1134, folios 578 to 581 (MSA CE 168-11452; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 577 to 581; 577 is the end of a different instrument, a Raczkowski mortgage to Sun Life Insurance Company of America received Sept. 1961; a left-margin stamp on 578 reads 'GRANTEE SEP 27 1961'). The grantors, presumably Henry Gerwig's heirs (the deed does not label them): Jacob F. Gerwig, widower; Annie Marie Gerwig, 'sometimes known as Annie Marie Harris', unmarried; Janet Kelly and John Kelly; Mary Loftus and Howard Loftus; Charles and Thelma C. Gerwig; John B. and Eunice Gerwig; William and Helen M. Gerwig; William Charles and Margaret Gerwig; Frank H. and Dorothy G. Gerwig; Phillip Gerwig, unmarried; Mary Latham and Joseph Latham Jr.; Peggy Gerwig, unmarried; Evelyn G. Beales and John L. Beales; Lucille G. Hughes and Felton L. Hughes; Mabel J. Felkner and John Felkner, the last two couples 'of the State of Florida'; 'Florida' is struck in the second acknowledgment), to Jerome Silbiger and Lillian Silbiger, his wife, 'as tenants by the entireties', dated July 15, 1961, 'five dollars and other valuable considerations'. The lot is the 14-foot lot of 2958: 'BEGINNING for the same on the West side of Greenmount Avenue (formerly known as the York Road) at the distance of 402 feet 9 1/2 inches Northerly from the Northwest corner of Twenty-Ninth Street and Greenmount Avenue and at the center of a partition wall there situate, and running thence Northerly binding on the West side of Greenmount Avenue 14 feet to the center of another partition wall ... 100 feet to the West side of an alley 10 feet wide ... Southerly ... 14 feet ... Easterly through the center of said first mentioned partition wall ... 100 feet to the place of beginning. The improvements thereon being known as No. 2958 Greenmount Avenue.' It is 'the same lot of ground which, by Lease dated August 24th, 1907 and recorded ... in Liber R.O. No. 2363, folio 423 [sic: S.C.L.], was demised and leased by James Keelty, unmarried, to James F. Bowersox and wife whereby was reserved ... the annual ground rent of Sixty-five Dollars ($65.00), payable in equal semi-annual installments on the first days of March and September'; and it is 'one of the lots of ground described in a Deed dated March 12th, 1932 ... Liber S.C.L. No. 5289, folio 183, from Sarah Stanley Armour and husband to Henry Gerwig. The said Henry Gerwig having departed this life intestate on or about November 18th, 1960. SEE ALSO Administration proceedings in the matter of the estate of the said Henry Gerwig, deceased, in the Orphans' Court for Baltimore City Estate Docket No. 88, folio 435.' 'The leasehold interest in the above described lot of ground was acquired by the Grantees herein by Assignment from Guiseppe Palladi and wife dated December 30th, 1960 and recorded as aforesaid in Liber J.F.C. No. 1004, folio 488.' Together with the improvements 'and particularly the aforesaid rent, issuing and payable thereout, and the reversion thereto'; to hold 'unto and to the use of the said Grantees, as tenants by the entireties ... in fee simple, forever, to the end and intent that the reversionary and leasehold estates be forever merged and the annual ground rent henceforth extinguished'. Special warranty and further assurance. Signed by all the grantors, S. Leonard Rottman witnessing 'as to all'; acknowledged July 15, 1961 (most) and July 17, 1961 (Lucille G. and Felton L. Hughes) before S. Leonard Rottman, Notary Public, Baltimore City. What it settles: who held the $65 ground rent in 1961 (the heirs of Henry Gerwig, who bought 2958's reversion with other lots from Sarah Stanley Armour and her husband on March 12, 1932) and that the rent ended that year: the Silbigers bought the leasehold from Giuseppe Palladi on Dec. 30, 1960 (row 46072) and the reversion from the Gerwig heirs six and a half months later, and the deed says in terms that the two estates are merged and the rent extinguished. From July 1961 the 14-foot lot is held in fee simple, free of ground rent. What it does not settle: the clerk's recording date; the 1932 Armour deed (S.C.L. 5289/183, not pulled), which would show how Armour came to hold the reversion Keelty created (and what 'one of the lots' means: it was a package of lots); Henry Gerwig's estate (Orphans' Court docket 88/435, not pulled); and the price (the deed recites $5; the stamps are not on the pages pulled). This deed covers the 14-foot lot only: the 8-foot fee lot needs no merger and is not mentioned. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the Gerwig heirs are presumably Henry Gerwig's: the reversion of the $65 rent was bought for Henry Gerwig, a lunatic, by his committee William F. Gerwig on Mar. 12, 1932 from Sarah Stanley Armour (714:mdlr-scl5289-183-armour-gerwig-1932, $4,516.67 for four ground-rent lots, 2958 York Road first). The Silbigers' own 1965 deed recites this merger in Lot 7 ('Jacob F. Gerwig, widower, et al ... extinquishing said ground rent', 714:mdlr-jfc2008-87-lot-list-silbiger-straw-man-1965).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber S.C.L. 5263, folio 428 (MSA CE 168-5271; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 427 to 431; the other instruments on 427, 430 and 431 are unrelated: the end of a Barry mortgage, Agata Lewonas's mortgage to the Sterling Permanent Building and Loan Association, and an Ida E. Mills assignment). Index heading 'William H Wolfe &c, Deed to Lula Smith'. William H. Wolfe and Charles T. Leight to Lula Smith, spinster, Oct. 31, 1931, five dollars and other valuable considerations: the lot 'which by deed bearing date the 18th day of November 1927 and recorded ... in Liber S.C.L. No. 4815 folio 438 etc was granted and assigned by Lula B. Dietrich widow to the said William H. Wolfe and Charles T. Leight as tenants in common subject to an annual ground rent of One hundred and eighty dollars ($180.00) payable in equal quarterly installments on the first days of February, May, August and November in each and every year', to hold 'for all the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein with the benefit of renewal forever subject to the payment of the annual rent aforesaid'. Special warranty. Signed William H. Wolfe and Charles T. Leight; witness C. L. Albright; acknowledged Oct. 31, 1931 before Clayton L. Albright, Notary Public; received for record Nov. 6, 1931 at 11:00 A.M. and recorded the same day (Stephen C. Little, clerk). The grantee index stamp reads 'Jan 11 1932'. What it settles: the two men took the $180-rent leasehold of the lot just south of 3020 (the lot that M.L.P. 8259/53 calls 3010) from Lula B. Dietrich, widow, by an assignment of Nov. 18, 1927 (S.C.L. 4815/438), as tenants in common, and on Oct. 31, 1931 passed it to Lula Smith, a third party, apparently to change how they held it (the deed does not say why): the next row. What it does not settle: the 1927 deed (not pulled; who Lula B. Dietrich was is not shown; the 1901 lessee of the lot was Allen K. Wood, R.O. 1928/77) and the price (the stamps are not on the page pulled). Update Oct. 13, 2026: the 1927 deed this recites is read (719:mdlr-scl4815-438-lulu-dietrich-wolfe-leight-3010-1927, S.C.L. 4815/438): the grantor is 'Lulu S. Dietrich', widow, not 'Lula B. Dietrich' as the recital here has it; dated Nov. 18, 1927, recorded Nov. 19 at 11:41 a.m.; she and her husband John Harmon Dietrich had taken the lease by assignment from C. Reese Dietrich on May 6, 1927 (S.C.L. 4735/61).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber S.C.L. 5263, folios 428 to 430 (MSA CE 168-5271; read on the scan Jeff saved; index heading 'Lula Smith, Deed to William H Wolfe &c', immediately under the Wolfe and Leight deed to her). Lula Smith, spinster, to William H. Wolfe and Carrie Wolfe, his wife, 'as tenants by the entireties', an undivided one-half interest, and to Charles T. Leight and Ella B. Leight, his wife, 'as tenants by the entireties', the other undivided half, Oct. 31, 1931, five dollars and other valuable considerations, in the lot she had just taken from Wolfe and Leight, to hold 'for all the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein with the benefit of renewal forever subject to the payment of the annual rent' of $180. The lot: 'BEGINNING for the same on the line of the west side of Greenmount Avenue (formerly the York Turnpike Road) at the distance of thirty-six feet south three and one-fourth degrees west from a stone planted at the southwest intersection of Greenmount Avenue and Gilmore Lane and running thence binding on the west side of Greenmount Avenue south three and one-fourth degrees west sixty-seven feet eleven and two-fifths inches more or less to a boundary stone and southernmost outline of the whole land formerly belonging to Mary Clemens, thence westerly bounding on said southernmost outline two hundred and fifteen feet more or less, thence northerly parallel with Greenmount Avenue eighty-two feet more or less to the southeast side of Gilmore Lane, thence bounding on said Lane north forty-two and one-half degrees east fifty-three feet, thence south eighty-five degrees east one hundred and five feet six inches to the end of the third line of the lot described in the Sub-Lease from John D. Nicholl to Lorenz Leight, recorded ... in Liber A.W.B. No. 394 folio 156 &c, thence bounding on said third line reversely and parallel with Greenmount Avenue southerly thirty-eight feet to the end of the second line of the lot described in said Sub-lease, and thence easterly bounding on said second line reversely seventy-six feet four inches to the place of beginning', 'subject to the payment of an annual ground rent of One hundred and eighty dollars ($180.00)'. Signed Lula Smith (seal); acknowledged Oct. 31, 1931 before Clayton L. Albright, Notary Public; received for record Nov. 6, 1931 at 11:01 A.M. and recorded the same day. The grantee index stamp reads 'Jan 11 1932'. What it settles: the lot (67 feet 11 2/5 inches on Greenmount, the next south of the 36-foot corner lot at 3020, which begins at the Vineyard Lane corner) is bounded south by 'the whole land formerly belonging to Mary Clemens', and is the lot M.L.P. 7491/449 and 8259/53 later divide and merge; the ground lies partly within a sub-lease from John D. Nicholl to Lorenz Leight (A.W.B. 394/156, a Leight family lease of the 1840s or 1850s, not pulled). By this pair of deeds the Wolfes and the Leights held the leasehold in equal undivided halves from Nov. 1931 until Wolfe's June 1948 deed (M.L.P. 7491/449). What it does not settle: why the conveyance went through Lula Smith (it has the form of a change from a tenancy in common to two tenancies by the entireties, but the deed does not say so).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber S.C.L. 5328, folios 110 to 111 (MSA CE 168-5336; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 110 to 114; the instruments on 110, 112, 113 and 114 are unrelated: a Waverly Building Association release, a West North Avenue Savings and Loan assignment to Welsh Construction, a Sterling Realty assignment and an Albert E. Pohmer mortgage; a left-margin stamp reads 'GRANTEE MAR 22 1935'). Index heading 'Charles T Leight &c, Deed to William H Flayhart Jr &c'. Charles T. Leight and Ella B. Leight, his wife, to William H. Flayhart Jr. and Catherine B. Flayhart, his wife, 'as tenants by the entireties', Oct. 5, 1932, five dollars and other valuable considerations: 'BEGINNING for the same at a stone planted at the corner formed by the intersection of the west side of Greenmount Avenue formerly called York Turnpike Road and the south side of Vineyard Lane formerly called Gilmor Lane and running thence southerly on the west side of Greenmount Avenue thirty-six feet thence westerly seventy-six feet four inches thence northerly parallel with Greenmount Avenue thirty-eight feet to the south side of Vineyard Lane and thence easterly seventy-six feet six inches on said lane to the place of beginning, the improvements thereon being known as No. 3020 Greenmount Avenue'. The recital: 'BEING one of the lots of ground which by assignment dated May 1st 1919 and recorded ... in Liber S.C.L. No. 3561 folio 216 was conveyed by W. Harry Holmes to Susan Leight and Charles T. Leight as joint tenants and being the same lot of ground which by deed of reversion dated June 9th 1924 and recorded ... in Liber S.C.L. No. 4210 folio 380 was conveyed by Mary Clemens to the said Susan Leight and Charles T. Leight as joint tenants, the said Susan Leight having since departed this life the title to the above described lot is now vested in the said Charles T. Leight.' Special warranty. Signed Charles T. Leight and Ella B. Leight (seals); acknowledged Oct. 5, 1932 before Lennox B. Clemens, Notary Public; recorded Oct. 7, 1932 at 2:40 P.M. (Stephen C. Little, clerk). Corridor has Susan Leight, widow of Henry, dying Sept. 1, 1932 (row 41912) and Catherine B. Leight Flayhart, Charles T.'s daughter, married to William H. Flayhart Jr. (rows 41913, 41949): the deed's 'Flayhart' is the spelling the death notices use. What it settles: that 3020 (the Vineyard Lane corner, 36 feet on Greenmount) was a leasehold the Leights bought on May 1, 1919 from W. Harry Holmes and whose reversion they bought from Mary Clemens on June 9, 1924, so a fee-simple lot from 1924; that Susan Leight was a joint tenant until her death in 1932, when the title vested in her son Charles T.; and that on Oct. 5, 1932 Charles T. and Ella B. Leight deeded the lot to William H. Flayhart Jr. and Catherine B. Flayhart and the Flayharts deeded it straight back, the first recorded at 2:40 and the second at 2:41 P.M. on Oct. 7 (second row, S.C.L. 5328/111 to 112), 'unto ... Charles T. Leight and Ella B. Leight his wife as tenants by the entireties': a pass-through that turns Charles's sole title into a tenancy by the entireties with his wife (the deed does not say that was the purpose). The Flayharts never held the lot beyond that moment. Correction, Oct. 13, 2026: an earlier version of this row said the corner was given to Charles's daughter and son-in-law and stayed with them; that was wrong. What it does not settle: the 1919 Holmes assignment and the 1924 Clemens deed are not pulled, nor is the purpose of the pass-through.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber M.L.P. 7491, folios 449 to 451 (MSA CE 168-7499; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 448 to 452; 448 is the end of a Jesse S. Weinberg mortgage to the Great American Building and Loan Association, released Feb. 4, 1953; 452 opens an unrelated Goldberg to Linden Holding Company deed for 508 West Preston Street; a left-margin stamp on 449 reads 'GRANTEE FEB 10 1953'). William H. Wolfe and Carrie Wolfe, his wife, to Charles T. Leight and Ella B. Leight, his wife, 'as tenants by the entireties', an undivided one-half interest and estate in the lot of S.C.L. 5263/428, June 21, 1948, 'five dollars and other valuable considerations'; the lot 'BEGINNING for the same on the line of the west side of Greenmount Avenue (formerly the York Turnpike Road), at the distance of thirty-six feet south three and one-fourth degrees from a stone planted at the southwest intersection of Greenmount Avenue and Vineyard Lane (formerly Gilmore Lane)' and running with the same lines as in the 1931 deed (67 feet 11 2/5 inches on Greenmount, 215 feet west along 'the whole land formerly belonging to Mary Clemens', 82 feet north to the lane, 'the Sub-Lease from John D. Nicholl to Lorenz Leight, recorded ... in Liber A.W.B. No. 394, folio 156'), to hold 'for all the residue of the terms of years yet to come and unexpired therein, with the benefit of renewal forever; subject to the payment of the annual rent of one hundred and eighty ($180.00) dollars, payable in equal quarterly installments on the first days of February, May, August and November in each and every year'. 'BEING the same lot of ground which by Deed, dated October 31st, 1931, and recorded ... in Liber S.C.L. No. 5263, folio 428, was conveyed by Lula Smith in two undivided interests, one thereof to the said William H. Wolfe and Carrie Wolfe, his wife, and the other to the said Charles T. Leight and Ella B. Leight, his wife.' Special warranty. Signed William H. Wolfe and Mrs. Carrie Wolfe (seals), witness Pearl M. Thompson; acknowledged June 21, 1948 before Lennox B. Clemens, Notary Public; received for record June 24, 1948 at 1:30 P.M. (M. Luther Pittman, clerk). What it settles: by June 1948 the Wolfes had sold their half of the leasehold to the Leights (the Leights now held it all, but still as lessees: the reversion and the $180 rent were another estate, held by the Wolfes, next row); What it does not settle: the price (stamps are not legible in the scan); who owned the reversion in 1948 (the next row says the Wolfes, by a Dec. 16, 1930 deed from Mary L. Swormstedt et al.).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber M.L.P. 8259, folios 53 to 54 (MSA CE 168-8267; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 52 to 56; 52 is an Anderson Enterprises assignment of a mortgage, 55 and 56 are an unrelated Fugmann to Etner deed for 2804 Evergreen Avenue; a left-margin stamp on 53 reads 'GRANTEE FEB 10 1953'). William H. Wolfe and Carrie Wolfe, his wife, to Charles T. Leight, widower, Oct. 24, 1950, 'three thousand ($3,000.00) dollars, together with accrued rent to the date hereof': the lot 36 feet 3 1/4 degrees south of the southwest intersection of Greenmount Avenue and Vineyard Lane, with the lines of the 1931 deed, 'the improvement thereon being known as No. 3010 Greenmount Avenue'. 'BEING the same lot of ground which by Lease, dated October 31st, 1901 and recorded ... in Liber R.O. No. 1928, folio 77, was demised and leased by Mary Clemens and husband to Allen K. Wood, for the renewable term of ninety-nine years, at and under the annual rent of one hundred and eighty dollars, payable in quarterly installments on the first days of February, May, August and November in each and every year. AND BEING the same lot of ground which by Deed, dated December 16th, 1930 and recorded ... in Liber S.C.L. No. 5182, folio 192, was conveyed by Mary L. Swormstedt et al. to the herein Grantors. BEING ALSO the same lot of ground which was conveyed to the said Charles T. Leight and Ella B. Leight, his wife, (the said Ella B. Leight having since departed this life) by Assignment from Lula Smith, dated October 31st, 1931 ... S.C.L. No. 5263, folio 428, and Assignment from William H. Wolfe and wife, dated June 21st, 1948 ... M.L.P. No. 7491, folio 449.' Together with the buildings and improvements, 'and especially the reversion therein and the clear yearly rent of one hundred and eighty dollars issuing thereout by virtue of the Lease aforesaid', to hold in fee simple 'to the end and intent that the leasehold estate created by the lease aforesaid shall be merged with the fee and the annual rent issuing thereout shall be forever extinguished'. Special warranty. Signed William H. Wolfe and Carrie Wolfe, witness Lennox B. Clemens; acknowledged Oct. 24, 1950 before Lennox B. Clemens, Notary Public; recorded Oct. 26, 1950 (M. Luther Pittman, clerk). What it settles: 3010 is the Leight family's lot immediately south of 3020 and is the lot of the 1901 Clemens-to-Wood lease (R.O. 1928/77, $180 a year, 99 years renewable forever); that Mary L. Swormstedt et al. (presumably the Clemens heirs; the deed does not say) sold the reversion and the rent to the Wolfes on Dec. 16, 1930, a year before the two Wolfe-and-Leight halves of the leasehold were put in the entireties; and that on Oct. 24, 1950, seven months after Ella Leight's death, Charles T. Leight bought the Wolfes out and merged the lease into the fee: from 1950 3010 was his in fee simple, with no ground rent. Charles T. Leight died Aug. 12, 1953 (row 41915); the 1953 deed to the Rashbaums (row 42211) is the sale of this lot with 3020. What it does not settle: the 1901 lease itself (R.O. 1928/77 is loaded in Jeff's browser, not yet downloaded), the Dec. 16, 1930 deed (S.C.L. 5182/192), and the Dietrich 1927 assignment (S.C.L. 4815/438) that put the leasehold in the Wolfe-Leight hands. Correction/pointer, Oct. 13, 2026: the 1901 lease it recites is now read: R.O. 1928/77 to 79, Mary Clemens and her husband to Allen K. Wood, Oct. 31, 1901, 99 years at $180 quarterly (719:mdlr-ro1928-77-mary-clemens-wood-lease-1901); the lessor was Mary Clemens herself. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the Swormstedt deed this recites is read (719:mdlr-scl5182-192-swormstedt-wolfe-reversion-3010-1930, S.C.L. 5182/192): Mary L. and Martha Swormstedt, both unmarried, to William H. and Carrie Wolfe as tenants by the entirety, Dec. 16, 1930, the reversion and the $180 rent; the Swormstedts had it of Robert N. Baer by a deed of Mar. 30, 1927 (S.C.L. 4728/211, not read), so the grantors are not Clemens heirs.

summary: Deed of trust, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 165, folios 492 to 493 (MSA CE 66-215; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 491 to 496: 491 is the end of a Dolen and Dwyer lease, and 494 to 496 are other deeds of the same September 1822 recording). Index heading 'John McFadon, Deed of Trust to John W. Stump & Philip G. Biays'. John McFadon of the City of Baltimore to John W. Stump and Philip G. Biays, both of the same city, April 11, 1822, 'for and in consideration of the sum of seven thousand seven hundred dollars current money': 'all that part of a tract of land situate lying and being in Baltimore County ... commonly called or known by the name of Ensors Inspection', 'Beginning for the same at a stone standing on the north east side of a road leading from the land of Hugh Thompson into the York Turnpike road at or near the gate the said stone being marked with the letter B and running thence on the said road north forty degrees and one half of a degree east to the Turnpike road and north the same course across the said road to the distance of ninety four perches and three quarters of a perch from the beginning and to a stone standing at the end of the north forty two degrees east one hundred and seventeen perch line mentioned in a deed from John Foster to Christopher Walker' (and on, in lines I have not copied, with a reference to Indentures from Samuel Moale to John McFadon 'recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County Court'). The grant is in trust 'for the use of Sarah Biays wife of James Biays of Baltimore County ... for and during her lifetime without impeachment of or for any manner of waste, and upon this further trust that they the said John W. Stump and Philip G. Biays or the survivor of them shall at the decease of the said Sarah Biays convey and assure all and singular the hereby granted premises ... unto Nancy Biays, Frances J. Biays, Elizabeth Biays and Hannah Jane Biays, daughters of the said James Biays and Sarah Biays, their heirs and assigns forever'. Acknowledged April 11, 1822 before two justices of the peace (Mrs. McFadon released her dower); received to be recorded Sept. 30, 1822 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, clerk). What it settles: this is the deed the 1844 Mumma deed recites as 'the Ground Conveyed by John McFadon to John W. Stump and Philip G. Biays in trust by deed dated the Eleventh day of April Eighteen hundred and twenty two ... Liber W.G. No. [blank] folio [blank]' (A.W.B. 354/374, row 46070): the liber and folio are W.G. 165/492. It names the tract (Bouldin's 'Ensor's Inspection' is the deed's own name, not only his), puts the ground 'at or near the gate' on the York Turnpike, and gives the trust: Sarah Biays for life, then Nancy, Frances J., Elizabeth and Hannah Jane Biays. The 1844 grantors, Sarah Biays with Jacob and Nancy Hoke, Henry and Frances Hammond, Henry N. and Elizabeth Bowerman, W. T. and Hannah Jane Allender, and the trustees Stump and Philip G. Biays, are exactly the trust's beneficiaries and trustees. What it does not settle: where the 'whole' trust ground lies relative to 3010 to 3020 (the Mumma lot is a 94-perch corner cut from it; the full courses of the trust ground are on 492 and 493 and I have copied only the first lines), how McFadon bought it from Samuel Moale (those indentures are not named by date or liber on the pages read), and what the $7,700 bought and who paid it. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the two Moale deeds the trust deed recites are read (W.G. 160/580 and 582, 719:mdlr-wg160-580-moale-biays-mcfadon-lot1-1821 and 719:mdlr-wg160-582-moale-mcfadon-lots2-5-1821): Moale, trustee in the Chancery suit Bolte et al. v. Biays, sold McFadon the five lots of the ground Biays had mortgaged to John Bolte in 1813, on April 26, 1821; and the trust was executed on Oct. 28, 1845 (A.W.B. 359/136, 719:mdlr-awb359-136-stump-biays-daughters-1845). Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): part of this trust land at the turnpike and Gilmor's Lane went from the four daughters to James Wilson in 1847 (725:mdlr-awb382-43-hoke-biays-daughters-james-wilson-toll-gate-triangle-1847), later the First Toll Gate House lot (3026 to 3032). Update Oct. 15, 2026: the lane it starts from, 'from the Land of Hugh Thompson unto the York Turnpike Road at or near the Gate', is probably the 'private road laid out by said Harry Dorsey Gough leading from the York Turnpike to the grounds of Hugh Thompson' of Gough's 1805 lease to John Neale (726:mdlr-wg84-302-gough-neale-lease-huntingdon-private-road-1805).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber M.L.P. 9546, folios 140 to 142 (MSA CE 168-9554; the scan Jeff saved opens on 142, the last page, so the grantee's name, the consideration and the description are on 140 and 141, not pulled; the recording stamp at the foot of 142 reads 'AUG 2 1954 ... LIBER M.L.P. 9546 PAGE 140'). What 142 shows: the recital 'Being the same lot which by lease bearing even date herewith and recorded or intended to be recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City immediately prior hereto was demised and leased by Henry John Weber and Lillian F. Weber, Adam H. Weber and Virginia Weber, and Raymond H. Plack and Doris E. Plack, his wife, unto Elizabeth McC. West for the term of ninety-nine years and for the annual rent of Sixty-Six Dollars, payable in semi-annual installments on the 2nd day of February and August in each and every year' (two typed lines struck through); 'Together with the improvements thereon ... and especially the reversion therein with the right to collect the annual rent aforesaid'; 'To Have and To Hold the above granted property and particularly the aforesaid rent payable out of said lot and the reversion thereto, unto the said Grantee, her heirs and assigns forever, in fee simple; subject to the estate, terms and interest of the said lessee, her personal representatives and assigns under said lease'; special warranty. Signed Henry John Weber, Lillian F. Weber, Adam H. Weber, Virginia Weber, Raymond H. Plack and Doris E. Plack, witness Dennis P. Murphy; acknowledged Aug. 2, 1954 before Dennis P. Murphy, Notary Public, Baltimore County. What it settles: on Aug. 2, 1954 the Weber and Plack families, who owned 3011 Greenmount in fee and had mortgaged it on June 19, 1954 (the release, below), created a 99-year leasehold at $66 a year in favour of Elizabeth McC. West and sold the reversion and the rent to a woman, 'the said Grantee'; the next instrument, West's assignment to Max Silen of the same day, calls this a 'Deed from [the Webers and Placks] to the said Elizabeth McC. West, whereby the within leasehold was created'. What it does not settle: whether the Grantee of the reversion and rent is West herself or another person (the name is on the unpulled opening page), the price, and the description of the lot (on 140 and 141). Elizabeth McC. West also appears as witness and notary on the same-day release (9546/146), so she is the lessee, the assignor and a notary on one day. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the Weber deeds of June 19, 1954 are read (720:mdlr-mlp9513-58-weber-west-3011-1954 and 720:mdlr-mlp9513-61-west-weber-plack-3011-1954): the Webers and Placks bought 3011 from four Sinclairs, put Elizabeth McC. West in the chain as a straw the same day, and took it back from her as tenants in common. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (SDAT registration): the State's Ground Rent Registry shows a registration filed Apr. 6, 2012 citing Liber 9546, folio 140, of 1954, this deed of the reversion and the rent (720:sdat-ground-rent-registration-3011-greenmount-2012). The $66 rent registered for 3011 is therefore the 1954 rent, not an older one.

summary: Deed in the 'Assignment' printed form, Baltimore City land records, Liber M.L.P. 9546, folios 143 to 145 (MSA CE 168-9554; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 142 to 146: 142 is the end of the Weber and Plack deed, the row above; 146 is the release, below). Elizabeth McC. West, of Baltimore City, to Max Silen, of the same city, Aug. 2, 1954, 'five dollars and other good and valuable considerations': 'all that lot or parcel of ground situate in the City of Baltimore' described by courses on the east side of Greenmount Avenue, beginning 'at the end of the first line of the firstly described lot of ground in the deed from J. Holliday Riepe (Single) to James M. Sinclair and Ena M. Sinclair his wife dated March 1, 1927 and recorded ... in Liber S.C.L. No. 4707, folio 12', at 'the point formed by the intersection of the East Side of said Greenmount Avenue sixty-six feet wide as established by the City of Baltimore Topographical Survey Commission as directed by Section 2 of Ordinance No. 129 of the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore approved December 3, 1898 and the North West Side of Old York Road', 58 feet 4 inches north along Greenmount and back by three lines (the Sinclair lot's fourth, third and second lines reversed) to the beginning; 'The improvements thereon being known as No. 3011 Greenmount Avenue. The courses in the above description are all referred to the True Meridian established by the City of Baltimore Topographical Survey Commission.' 'Being the same lot of ground described in a Deed from Henry John Weber and wife and Raymond H. Plack and wife, to the said Elizabeth McC. West, whereby the within leasehold was created, bearing even date herewith.' To hold to Max Silen, his personal representatives and assigns, 'for all the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein, with the benefit of renewal forever; subject to the payment of the annual rent of Sixty-Six ($66.00) Dollars, payable in equal semi-annual installments on the second days of February and August in each and every year'. Special warranty. Signed Elizabeth McC. West; witness Phyllis J. Smith; acknowledged Aug. 2, 1954 before Phyllis J. Smith, Notary Public, Baltimore County; recorded Aug. 2, 1954 at about 1:02 P.M. (M. Luther Pittman, clerk). What it settles: the lot's lines are tied to the 1927 Sinclair deed (S.C.L. 4707/12, Riepe to Sinclair, March 1, 1927, loaded in Jeff's browser and not yet downloaded); the improvements are 'No. 3011 Greenmount Avenue'; Max Silen (d. 1971, row 42365) took the leasehold; and the ground rent was $66 a year, owed to whoever held the reversion after the 1954 Weber and Plack deed. What it does not settle: who held the reversion and the $66 rent from Aug. 2, 1954 (the Silen family later held both lots in fee, but when the rent was merged is not shown), and the price.

John E. Minor, of Baltimore County, to Max Silen, of Baltimore City, Aug. 25, 1954, 'five dollars and other good and valuable consideration': the lot 'Beginning for the same on the east side of Greenmount Avenue (formerly the York Turnpike Road) at a point distant 190 feet 7 inches southerly from the 2 mile stone located on the east side of Greenmount Avenue in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot, said point of beginning being also 267 feet 2 inches southerly from the north side of a 4 foot alley-way called Bateman's Alley, and running thence southerly bounding on the east side of Greenmount Avenue 14 feet, thence easterly at right angles to Greenmount Avenue 42 feet 4 inches to the westernmost side of the Old York Road, thence northeasterly bounding on the westernmost side of the Old York Road 15 feet 2 1/2 inches and thence westerly by a straight line 48 feet 3 inches to the place of beginning. The improvements thereon being known as No. 3013 Greenmount Avenue.' 'BEING the same lot of ground and premises which were transferred and conveyed to the said John E. Minor from Charles F. Obrecht and wife, by Lease dated 20th December, 1943 ... Liber M.L.P. No. 6544, folio 521, creating a one cent ground rent, if demanded, bearing date of December 20th, 1943', to hold 'for all the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein, with the benefit of renewal forever; subject to the payment of the annual rent of One Cent ($.01), if demanded'. Special warranty. Signed John E. Minor (seal), witness Charles F. Obrecht; acknowledged Aug. 25, 1954 before Charles F. Obrecht, Notary Public, Baltimore County; recorded Aug. 25, 1954 (M. Luther Pittman, clerk). What it settles: 3013 Greenmount (the 14-foot lot a few feet north of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot, measured from the two-mile stone and from Bateman's Alley) came to Max Silen in two steps three weeks after he took 3011 (Aug. 2, 1954): the leasehold from John E. Minor on Aug. 25 (this row) and, the day before, the fee and the penny rent from the Obrechts to Samuel G. Silen (next row). John E. Minor's leasehold dated from Dec. 20, 1943, when he deeded the fee to the Obrechts and took back a 99-year lease at one cent, a sale-leaseback; Charles F. Obrecht witnessed and notarised this deed; he was the grantor of the reversion to Samuel G. Silen the day before. What it does not settle: the 1943 deed and lease (M.L.P. 6544/521, not pulled), why Minor sold the fee in 1943 and kept the lease, and the price. Update Oct. 15, 2026: a month after this deed the one-story store at 3013 was razed (permit 169771, Sept. 23, 1954; 720:bca-brg48-permit-card-3013-greenmount-1954-1957).
