summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 102, folios 33 to 35 (MSA CE 66-152; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 32 to 36; 32 is the end of a Howard to Cross lease and 36 opens a Pierpoint deed; the margin note beside the 1790 deed in W.G. E.E. 157 reads 'See Liber W.G. No. 102 folio 33', which is how this page was found). Index heading 'Thomas B. Onion & wife, Deed to James Carroll & Prudence Gough'. The recitals: Charles Ridgely, on or about Dec. 27, 1753, conveyed to his daughter Achsah Holliday and her heirs Huntington and a part of Ridgely's Whim (Liber B.B. No. 1 folio 210); Achsah married John Carnan, survived him, and by lease and release of Feb. 12 and 13, 1768 conveyed an undivided moiety of Huntington and of that part of Ridgely's Whim to John Ridgely and Charles Ridgely the younger, to her use for life and then to her daughter Elizabeth Carnan 'and to the heirs of her Body and for default of such heirs to the use of sundry other persons in remainder' (the release is read as B Q 503, filed on this property); Elizabeth married Thomas Bond Onion, and by their joint indenture of Feb. 24, 1790, for 1,400 pounds, assigned to Harry Dorsey Gough 'all the said Elizabeth's undivided half part of the said Tracts of land and all the Estate right and title of her and her said Husband therein and thereto' (W.G. E.E. 157); Gough then died, having by his will devised 'the said two moieties of Ridgelys Whim and Huntington to his Executors James Carroll and Prudence Gough of Baltimore County and their heirs in trust to sell and convey the same or such parts thereof as they should deem proper and to hold all such parts thereof as they should not so sell and convey in trust for Sophia Carroll daughter of the said Harry Dorsey Gough during her life and after her death in trust for such Children as she should leave living at the time of her death and their heirs in equal portions' (with the issue of a dead child taking its parent's share). Then: 'And whereas doubts are entertained whether the said Indenture from the said Thomas Bond Onion and Elizabeth his wife be sufficient and operative in law to pass the fee simple Estate of and in the Lands aforesaid and therein mentioned to the said Harry Dorsey Gough and the said Thomas Bond Onion and Elizabeth have therefore agreed to execute these presents for the purpose of conveying to the said James Carroll and Prudence Gough and their heirs a good and indefeasible Estate in fee simple of and in the said lands to and upon the trusts herein before and in the said Will recited and expressed.' 'Now This Indenture made on this sixth day of June in the year of our Lord one thousand eight hundred and nine' between Thomas Bond Onion and Elizabeth his wife of the one part and James Carroll and Prudence Gough of the other, for one dollar, they 'grant bargain sell release and confirm' to Carroll and Prudence Gough and their heirs 'all the said above described premises' with the reversion and remainders, to hold in trust 'to sell and convey in fee simple all such parts thereof as they or the survivor of them may think proper, and to receive the Purchase money therefor and to apply and dispose of it as in the said Will is directed', and for Sophia Carroll and her children as the will provides. Signed Tho. B. Onion and Eliza Onion (seals); acknowledged June 6, 1809 before Geo. Gould Presbury and Saml. Vincent, Elizabeth examined apart from her husband; received to be recorded June 10, 1809 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, clerk). What it settles: the question the 1768 release and the 1790 deed left open (whether Elizabeth Carnan's moiety, limited to 'the heirs of her body' with remainders over, passed to Gough in fee) was raised in 1809 in terms: 'doubts are entertained', and the Onions, the only grantors to the deed, gave a confirmatory deed in fee to Gough's executors to remove them; the Carnan moiety therefore reached Gough's executors by a second route in June 1809. What it does not settle: whether the sundry remaindermen under the 1768 limitation joined or were barred (the deed names no one but the Onions), and whether the 1809 deed cured the title of buyers who had already bought from Gough and Prudence under the 1803 deeds (Jackson, Biays, Smith: W.G. 74/327, 330, 334, 337): it does not mention them, and its trust is for the unsold remainder.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 112, folios 467 to 469 (MSA CE 66-162; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 466 to 471; 466 and the top of 467 are the end of Michael Warner's deed to the Vestry of St. Peter's Church, Oct. 27, 1810, unrelated; the instruments of 469 to 471 are the next two rows and Russell's deed of trust). Index heading 'William Jackson, deed to Elisha E. Russell'. William Jackson 'of the City of Baltimore in Baltimore county and State of Maryland Merchant' to Elisha E. Russell 'of the City County and state aforesaid Master Mariner', March 13, 1811, for 'four thousand Dollars lawful money of the United States': 'all that part of a tract of Land situate and lying in Baltimore County aforesaid and near to the said City of Baltimore called Huntington', 'Begining for the same part at a stone placed at the End of the north thirty six and a quarter degrees West ninety and one quarter perches line of that part of said tract which was on the thirteenth day of January Eighteen hundred and three conveyed by Harry D. Gough and wife to the said William Jackson', running 'bounding on said line reversely South thirty six and one quarter of a degree East thirty Eight perches and three tenths of a perch' (about 632 feet), then south 57 1/2 degrees west 9.6 perches, north 35 1/2 degrees west 35.2 perches 'until it intersects the second line of that part of said tract conveyed by Harry Dorsey Gough and wife to the said William Jackson at the distance of nine perches and sixtenths of a perch from the beginning stone', and on that line to the beginning, 'containing' a blank (the acreage was left unfilled in the record). With the buildings and improvements, 'the reversion and reversions remainder and remainders rents issues and profits', to Russell, his heirs and assigns forever; special warranty and further assurance. Signed Wm. Jackson (seal); acknowledged March 13, 1811 before two justices of the peace (Sam. H. Gatchell and Matthew Bennet), Mary Jackson, his wife, relinquishing dower; received to be recorded April 5, 1811 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, clerk). What it settles: that William Jackson's 1803 lot (W.G. 74/337, 14a 3r) was already being cut by 1811, to a master mariner, for $4,000 (roughly 2 acres by the courses, 38.3 by 9.6 perches, my estimate; the sum is large for that, and the 'buildings' words are boilerplate); that Jackson was described as a merchant of the City while the 'tract of Land called Huntington' was still in Baltimore County; and that the beginning stone is the end of the 90 1/4-perch first line of Gough's deed to Jackson, so Jackson's 1803 courses are the frame for this strip. What it does not settle: where on the ground (the courses are tied to Jackson's deed, not to a road or a street), the area (blank), and whether the strip was ever built on. Russell borrowed against it the next day (a deed of trust to George I. Brown and William S. Hollins, March 14, 1811, $4,735 owed on account, opening on 471; not filed). Update Oct. 14, 2026: Russell put both lots in trust with Brown & Hollins the next day to secure $4,735 (726:mdlr-wg112-471-russell-trust-brown-hollins-1811). Update Oct. 14, 2026: this lot reached James Wilson on July 4, 1823, through the City Bank and James McCormick Jr. (726:mdlr-wg168-653-mccormick-james-wilson-russell-lots-1823).

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 112, folios 469 to 471 (MSA CE 66-162; read on the scan Jeff saved; index heading 'James Biays, deed to Elisha E. Russell'; 471 then opens Russell's deed of trust to Brown and Hollins, not filed). James Biays 'of the City of Baltimore in Baltimore county and State of Maryland Merchant' to Elisha E. Russell, master mariner, March 13, 1811, for 'five hundred dollars lawful Money of the United States': 'all that piece or parcel of Land part of a tract of Land called Huntington', 'Beginning for the same part at a stone standing at the north East Corner of William Jacksons lot part of said tract and running thence and bounding on said Jacksons Lot South thirty six and an half degrees East eight and a half perches thence north thirty nine and three quarter degrees East twenty six perches and seven tenths of a perch to a road leading to Joseph Merryman's [the surname is written cramped, 'Meeryman's' or 'Moorymans'] thence bounding on said road north fifty eight and a half degrees West Eight and a half perches to the End of the north thirty nine and a half degrees East twenty four perches line of said James Biays's part of said tract and thence bounding on said line to the place of begining containing one Acre and forty seven perches of Land more or less'. With the buildings and improvements, the reversion and remainders, to Russell and his heirs; Biays's special warranty and further assurance. Signed Jas. Biays (seal), witness Matthew Bennet; acknowledged March 13, 1811 before two justices (Sam. H. Gatchell and Matthew Bennet), Sarah Biays, his wife, relinquishing dower; received to be recorded April 5, 1811 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, clerk). What it settles: James Biays sold a small piece (1 acre 47 perches) of his Huntington ground to the same buyer, on the same day and recording, as William Jackson's strip, so Russell assembled roughly 3 1/2 acres of Huntington in March 1811 (my estimate from the courses) on the common line between the two men's lots; the Biays piece touches the north-east corner of Jackson's lot and a road 'leading to Joseph Merryman's', so the ground lies along a lane to the Merryman house (the lane's name is not given: this is the 'Merryman's Lane' question in the Edition 2 open list, and it fits a lane running from the turnpike toward the Merryman farm, not necessarily 33rd Street); and that Biays described himself in 1811 as 'of the City of Baltimore'. What it does not settle: which of Biays's 1803 lots (W.G. 74/330, the first lot of 1a 1r 7p; or W.G. 74/334, the second, 7a 2r 33p) the piece came from, the position on the ground, and whether the 1811 road is the lane that later became Vineyard Lane, Gilmor Lane or Merryman's Lane. Update Oct. 14, 2026: Russell's deed of trust of the next day is read in full (726:mdlr-wg112-471-russell-trust-brown-hollins-1811): this lot runs to 'a road leading to Joseph Merryman's'. Update Oct. 14, 2026: this lot reached James Wilson on July 4, 1823 (726:mdlr-wg168-653-mccormick-james-wilson-russell-lots-1823); the 1823 deed calls the road 'a road leading from Joseph Merrymans house to the turnpike road leading from the City of Baltimore towards York town'.

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 141, folios 46 to 47 (MSA CE 66-191; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 45 to 50; 45 is the end of an Adam Waltemeyer to Dr. Allen Thomas deed, 47 below the mortgage and 48 to 50 are other deeds: Bryson to Dorsey, 1815, and a Carrere mortgage to the Bank of the United States). Index heading 'James Biays, Mortgage to John W. Stump'. James Biays of the City of Baltimore to John W. Stump of the same place, Dec. 23, 1816, 'for and in consideration of the sum of thirty four hundred dollars current money of this State due and owing by the said James Biays to the said John W. Stump and for the better securing the payment thereof': 'All the following lots or parcels of land situate on or near the York Turnpike road in Baltimore County': (1) 'all that part of a tract of land called Ensors Inspection which was conveyed by James Edwards of Baltimore County to the said James Biays by deed bearing date on or about the third day of November ... one thousand eight hundred and four ... Liber W.G. No. 83 folio 371'; (2) 'all that part of one other tract of land called Huntington containing seven acres two roods and thirty three perches more or less which was conveyed to the said James Biays by Harry Dorsey Gough and Prudence his wife by deed bearing date on or about the thirteenth day of January ... eighteen hundred and three ... Liber W.G. No. 74 folio 334'; and (3) 'all that lot or part of the aforesaid tract of land called Huntington which was conveyed by Dorathy Brown executrix of Jesse Brown [containing two acres and fifteen sixteenths of an acre] to the said James Biays by deed of assignment bearing date on or about the second day of September Eighteen hundred and nine ... Liber W.G. No. 104 folio 48'. To hold to Stump, his heirs and assigns, 'in the same right and estate as he the said James Biays held and enjoyed the same provided nevertheless that if the said James Biays shall on or before the twenty third day of December Eighteen hundred and eighteen well and truly pay or cause to be paid unto the said John W. Stump his heirs executors administrators or assigns the aforesaid sum of thirty four hundred dollars and Interest thereon then this deed and every thing therein contained shall cease and be null and void'. Signed Jas. Biays (seal), witnesses John Hanna and S. H. Gatchell; acknowledged Dec. 23, 1816 before S. H. Gatchell and Matthew Bennet; received to be recorded May 21, 1817 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, clerk). What it settles: that the 7a 2r 33p Huntington lot Gough sold Biays in 1803 (W.G. 74/334, row 726:mdlr-wg74-334-gough-biays-second-lot-1803) was whole and in his hands in December 1816, as security for $3,400 owed to John W. Stump (a John W. Stump is a trustee of the McFadon trust in 1822 and a grantor in the 1844 Mumma deed: the same name, probably the same man, so Stump would be a long-time Biays creditor and co-trustee); that Biays then also held an Ensor's Inspection lot from James Edwards (1804, W.G. 83/371, a new hop) and a 2-acre-and-fifteen-sixteenths Huntington lot bought from Jesse Brown's executrix on Sept. 2, 1809 (W.G. 104/48, a second new hop). The mortgage does not list the 1a 1r 7p 'first lot' (W.G. 74/330) or any piece of the 1811 Russell sale (W.G. 112/469), so those had left his hands by 1816 (an inference from what the mortgage lists). What it does not settle: whether Biays paid in 1818 (no release is among the pages read) and where the three parcels lie on the ground. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the third parcel, 'two acres and fifteen sixteenths of an acre ... deed of assignment ... Liber W.G. No 104 folio 48', is read in its 1847 sale: Walter T. Allender, trustee, to John Leitzinger, June 10, 1847, a leasehold under Gough's lease to Jesse Brown (W.G. 54/156), bounded by the York Turnpike on the west and the Old York Road on the east, 35 perches long (A.W.B. 381/475, 720:mdlr-awb381-475-allender-trustee-leitzinger-huntington-leasehold-1847). It lies EAST of the turnpike, between it and the Old York Road. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the Edwards deed this mortgage cites is read (714:mdlr-wg83-371-edwards-biays-1804, W.G. 83/371, Nov. 3, 1804).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber S.C.L. 5328, folios 111 to 112 (MSA CE 168-5336; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 111 and 112: it opens at the foot of 111 under the index heading 'William H Flayhart Jr &c, Deed to' with the number 100, and ends on 112 above an unrelated assignment of mortgage, West North Avenue Savings and Loan to Welsh Construction Company; the first lines on 111 after the heading are cut off in the scan, so the grantee names and the consideration are read from the habendum and the recital). William H. Flayhart Jr. and Catherine B. Flayhart, his wife, of Baltimore City, dated Oct. 5, 1932: the 3020 corner lot with the same description as the deed of the same day to them (36 feet on the west side of Greenmount Avenue from the south side of Vineyard Lane, formerly Gilmor Lane, 76 feet 4 inches west, 38 feet north, 76 feet 6 inches east, 'the improvements thereon being known as No 3020 Greenmount Avenue'). 'BEING the same lot of ground which by deed of even date herewith and intended to be recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City immediately prior hereto was conveyed by the said Charles T Leight and wife to the said Grantors.' To hold 'unto and to the proper use and benefit of the said Charles T Leight and Ella B Leight his wife as tenants by the entireties their assigns the survivor of them and the survivors heirs and assigns in fee simple'. Special warranty and further assurance. Signed William H. Flayhart Jr. and Catherine B. Flayhart (seals), witness Lennox B. Clemens; acknowledged Oct. 5, 1932 before Lennox B. Clemens, Notary Public; recorded Oct. 7, 1932 at 2:41 P.M. (Stephen C. Little, clerk), one minute after the deed to the Flayharts (2:40 P.M.). A grantee-index stamp on the facing page reads 'MAR 22 1935'. What it settles: the two deeds of Oct. 5, 1932 are one transaction: Charles T. Leight, who held 3020 alone after his mother Susan's death, conveyed it with his wife Ella to Charles's daughter Catherine and her husband, and they conveyed it straight back to Charles and Ella as tenants by the entireties; the Flayharts held title for the minute between the two recordings. That is why the 1953 deed to the Rashbaums (row 42211) recites 3020 as 'conveyed by William H. Flayhart, Jr. and wife to Charles T. Leight and Ella B. Leight ... S.C.L. 5328, folio 111', and why Charles T. Leight, widower, could sell it in 1953. It is the same device as the 3010 lot's pass through Lula Smith the year before (rows 46089 and 46090). What it does not settle: the consideration, and why the pass-through was made (the deeds do not say). Update Oct. 13, 2026: the two 3020 parents recited in S.C.L. 5328/110 are read: W. Harry Holmes to Susan and Charles T. Leight, May 1, 1919, a straw round trip (S.C.L. 3361/216, 719:mdlr-scl3361-216-holmes-susan-charles-leight-1919), and Mary Clemens, widow, to them, June 9, 1924, merging the $9 rent (S.C.L. 4210/380, 719:mdlr-scl4210-380-mary-clemens-leight-3020-merger-1924).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber J.F.C. 2008, folios 87 to 89 (MSA CE 168-12326; the scan Jeff saved opens on 89, the last page of this deed, so the parties' opening, the consideration and the list of lots are on 87 and 88, not pulled; pages 90 to 92 are the next deed, the row below, and 93 is an unrelated cancellation of a lease). Read on 89: the habendum, 'unto and to the proper use and benefit of the said Straw Man, Inc., it's successors and assigns ... in fee simple'; the special-warranty covenants; signed Jerome Silbiger and Lillian Silbiger (seals), witnessed by Melvin C. Paul; acknowledged Dec. 28, 1965 before Melvin C. Paul, Notary Public, whose address is typed under his signature as 2958 Greenmount Avenue; recorded Dec. 28, 1965 at 2:10 P.M., Liber J.F.C. 2008 page 87 (James F. Carney, clerk). That it conveys 2958 and the other ten lots is read from the next deed, whose last line recites 'a Deed of even date herewith and recorded or intended to be recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City immediately prior hereto was granted and conveyed by Jerome Silbiger and Lillian Silbiger, his wife unto Straw Man, Inc.' What it settles: the Silbigers, who held 2958 by the 1960 and 1961 deeds as tenants by the entireties, deeded it with ten other lots to a corporation named Straw Man, Inc. (a 1938 Maryland corporation, by its seal) at 2:10 P.M. on Dec. 28, 1965, and the corporation deeded all eleven lots to Jerome Silbiger alone at 2:11 P.M. (next row): a straw round trip that moved title from the couple jointly to the husband alone. It also puts Melvin C. Paul, notary and witness on both deeds, at 2958 Greenmount Avenue in December 1965, which supports the lawyer's-office reading of row 39485. What it does not settle: the consideration, the lot list as drafted, and why the couple moved title into Jerome's sole name (the 1969 deed, third row, moves it back). Update Oct. 13, 2026: the deed's lot list (pages 87 and 88) is read (714:mdlr-jfc2008-87-lot-list-silbiger-straw-man-1965): 'Lot #7 ... The improvements thereon being now known as 2958 Greenmount Avenue', citing J.F.C. 1004/488 (Dec. 30, 1960) and J.F.C. 1134/578 (July 15, 1961, 'extinquishing said ground rent'). So this deed does convey 2958: the status is raised from probable to verified. Page 85 of the same pull is Straw Man, Inc.'s assignment of a Falls Road leasehold back to Jerome Silbiger, recorded Dec. 28, 1965 at 2:11 p.m.

Russell); (6) 1765 Abbottston Street (M.L.P. 9404/216, Feb. 10, 1954, the Baltimore Transit Company); (7) 2958 Greenmount Avenue; (8) six concrete garages in the rear of Paine Street (J.F.C. 1241/379, Feb. 23, 1962, Guarantee Title Holding Corporation; stamped 'UNLOCATED'); (9) 4667 Falls Road (J.F.C. 1447/153, March 6, 1963, Roland and Evelyn Scott); (10) 4705 Falls Road (J.F.C. 1478/225, May 2, 1963, Herbert Kaufman); (11) 2700 Harford Road (J.F.C. 1673/184, April 13, 1964, Maryland National Bank, trustee). Lot 7 reads: 'Being the same lot of ground described in a Deed dated December 30, 1960 and recorded ... Liber JFC 1004, Folio 488 was granted and conveyed by Guiseppe Palladin, wife unto the said Jerome Silbiger and Lillian Silbiger, his wife. See also Deed dated July 15, 1961 and recorded ... Liber JFC 1134, Folio 578 was granted and conveyed by Jacob F. Gerwig, widower, et al to the said Jerome Silbiger and Lillian Silbiger, his wife, extinguishing said ground rent. The improvements thereon being now known as 2958 Greenmount Avenue.' A hand-written '3855' beside it is the City block number. Lots 5, 9 and 11 are 'subject to existing mortgages with The Equitable Trust Company of Baltimore' and lot 10 to a mortgage to Yorkridge Federal Savings and Loan Association. The deed ends: 'Being the same lots of ground in a Deed of even date herewith and recorded or intended to be recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City immediately prior hereto was granted and conveyed by Jerome Silbiger and Lillian Silbiger, his wife unto Straw Man, Inc.' Signed for Straw Man, Inc. by Theodore Denick, Vice-President (corporate seal, 'Incorporated 1938 Maryland'), witnessed by Melvin C. Paul; acknowledged Dec. 28, 1965 before Melvin C. Paul, Notary Public, Baltimore County, 'Melvin C. Paul, 2958 Greenmount Avenue'; recorded Dec. 28, 1965 at 2:11 P.M., Liber J.F.C. 2008 page 90 (James F. Carney, clerk); a grantee-index stamp reads 'Mar 18 1966'. What it settles: the Dec. 28, 1965 deed Corridor knew only by recital (S.E.B. 2747/219, row 5043) is read; it is a one-minute-later reconveyance of the lots the Silbigers had just deeded to Straw Man, Inc., so Jerome Silbiger held 2958 alone from Dec. 28, 1965; the 1961 deed (J.F.C. 1134/578) is described here as 'extinguishing said ground rent', which agrees with the merger clause read on that deed (row 46088); and the 1960 and 1961 deeds are cited by their libers, so the Silbigers' title to 2958 is the Palladi assignment and the Gerwig reversion. What it does not settle: why the pair was made (the deed says only 'no title search, no consideration necessary').

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber R.H.B. 2499, folios 294 to 296 (MSA CE 168-12817; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 293 to 297: 293 is the end of a Jo-Ann I. Campbell deed recorded at 2499/292, and 297 an unrelated substitution of trustees by Reynolds Aluminum Credit Corporation for 3731 Falls Road). A fee-simple deed form headed 'No title search - no consideration', with a 'Transfer tax not required' stamp numbered 35225. Jerome Silbiger to himself and Lillian Silbiger, his wife, 'as tenants by the entireties, their heirs and assigns, in fee simple', dated March 31, 1969, five dollars and other good and valuable considerations, thirteen lots, each described as the same lot conveyed to him by Straw Man, Inc. in the deed of Dec. 28, 1965 (J.F.C. 2008, folios 90 and 91), with the earlier deed named for the detailed description. Lot 7: 'BEING the same lot of ground described seventh in a Deed dated December 28, 1965, and recorded ... in Liber JFC 2008, folio 91 ... For detailed description see Deed dated December 30, 1960, and recorded among the Land Records in Liber JFC 1004, folio 488. See also deed dated July 15, 1961, and recorded in Liber JFC 1134, folio 578. The improvements thereon being known as 2958 Greenmount Avenue.' (the lot paragraph is on page 295; the City block, 3855, is hand-numbered beside it). The other twelve lots are those of the 1965 deed plus 4665 Falls Road (lot 12, 'See deed dated April 19, 1966, whereby Columbus P. Harris and Mary M. Harriss conveyed the existing ground rent unto Jerome Silbiger, and the leasehold was merged with the fee, and the aforesaid ground rent was forever extinguished') and 4643-45 Falls Road (lot 13, J.F.C. 2043/609, March 21, 1966, Wallace and Adeline Hall); lots 5, 9, 11 and 12 are 'subject to existing mortgages with The Equitable Trust Company' and lot 10 to Yorkridge Federal Savings and Loan Association. Signed Jerome Silbiger, witnessed by Roselin C. Raxter; acknowledged March 31, 1969 before Roselin C. Raxter, Notary Public, Baltimore City; recorded April 8, 1969 at 2:55 P.M., Liber R.H.B. 2499 page 294 (Robert H. Bouse, clerk). What it settles: the 1969 deed behind the 1982 deed (C.W.M. Jr. 4185/89, row 5042) and the 1990 personal representative's deed (S.E.B. 2747/219) is read, and its liber is R.H.B. 2499, not 'J.F.C. 2499': the clerk's series changed in 1969 (the stamp names Robert H. Bouse as clerk, where the 1965 stamps name James F. Carney), and 2958 is 'described seventh' on page 295, the folio the 1982 deed cites. It also confirms the 1960 and 1961 deeds as the Silbigers' source and that the clerk's drafter treated the 1961 deed as extinguishing the ground rent. What it does not settle: why the Silbigers moved all thirteen lots from the husband alone back into the entireties three years after the straw round trip (the deed says only 'no consideration').

summary: Lease, Baltimore City land records, Liber R.O. 1928, folios 77 to 79 (MSA CE 168-1936; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 76 to 80: the top of 77 is the acknowledgment (Oct. 29, 1901) of a release by the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County, Henry W. Fox its attorney, of a 1899 mortgage by Mary Clemens and her husband, received for record the same Oct. 31, 1901 around noon (whether the mortgaged land includes this lot is not read); the lease opens under the index heading 'Mary Clemens &c Lease to Allen K. Wood'; the foot of 79 opens an unrelated Central Real Estate and Trust Company deed to Josephine S. Channell). Mary Clemens and Augustus D. Clemens Junior, her husband, of Baltimore County, to Allen K. Wood of the same county, dated Oct. 31, 1901, 'in consideration of the rent hereinafter expressed': 'all that lot of ground ... Beginning for the same on the line of the west side of the York Turnpike Road at the distance of thirty six feet south three and one quarter degrees west from a stone planted at the southwest intersection of the York Turnpike Road and Gilmor Lane as now opened (said lane having been known as the road running between the lands of Mrs Gilmor and Mrs Biays and also called a road leading from the lands of Hugh Thompson into the York Turnpike Road)', south 3 1/4 degrees west 67 feet 11 2/5 inches to a boundary stone 'and the southernmost outline of the whole land belonging to Mary Clemens', west 215 feet along that outline, north parallel with the turnpike 82 feet 'to the southeast side of Gilmor Lane', north 42 1/2 degrees east 53 feet, south 85 degrees east 105 feet 6 inches 'to the end of the third line of the lot described in the sub lease from John D. Nicoll to Lorentz Leicht (A.W.B. No 374 fol 156 &c)', south 38 feet to the end of that sub-lease's second line, and east 76 feet 4 inches to the beginning. 'Being part of the land which by deed dated the 23rd day of April A.D. 1896 and recorded ... in Liber A.Q. No 1115 folio 24[?] was conveyed by Richard S. Dodson et al unto said Mary Clemens in fee simple.' To Wood, his executors, administrators and assigns, 'for the term of ninety nine years beginning on the day of the date of these presents', rent $180 'in even and equal quarter yearly instalments accounting from the first day of November one thousand nine hundred and one over and above all deductions for taxes and assessments', with distress, re-entry if sixty days in arrear and, after a year in arrear, as if the lease 'had never been made'. Acknowledged before Chas. J. Fox, Notary Public, Baltimore County; received for record Oct. 31, 1901 at 12:30 P.M. and recorded the same day (Robert Ogle, clerk). What it settles: the lessor of the $180 rent of 3010 was Mary Clemens herself, with her husband joining, from land in her own name (so 'Mary Clemens' of the 1931 to 1950 deeds is the wife of A. D. Clemens Jr. and the whole tract south of 3010 was hers); the lease is Oct. 31, 1901, 99 years, $180 a year, quarterly from Nov. 1, 1901, as the 1950 deed (M.L.P. 8259/53) recites; the lot is the same 67 ft 11 2/5 in lot of the 1931, 1948 and 1950 deeds; and her source is a deed of April 23, 1896 from Richard S. Dodson et al. (new hop; the clerk's liber 'A.Q. 1115' does not match a City liber of 1896, which would be near R.O. 16xx, so the cite is probably misread or mis-copied). It also describes Gilmor Lane as 'a road leading from the lands of Hugh Thompson into the York Turnpike Road', the same road McFadon's 1822 deed of trust begins on (W.G. 165/492, row 46094), so McFadon's ground and this lot lie along the same lane. What it does not settle: the renewal covenant (on the lower half of page 78, not read here; the 1950 deed calls the term 'renewable') and who Dodson et al. were (Abram G. Mott died in Oct. 1895, which may be the link). Update Oct. 13, 2026: the lease's two sides are traced forward in two deeds now read: the reversion and the $180 rent went from Robert N. Baer (deed not read) to Mary L. and Martha Swormstedt (Mar. 30, 1927, S.C.L. 4728/211, not read) and to William H. and Carrie Wolfe on Dec. 16, 1930 (719:mdlr-scl5182-192-swormstedt-wolfe-reversion-3010-1930); the lessee's term went by an assignment from C. Reese Dietrich to John Harmon and Lulu S. Dietrich on May 6, 1927 (S.C.L. 4735/61, not read) and from Lulu S. Dietrich, widow, to William H. Wolfe and Charles T. Leight on Nov. 18, 1927 (719:mdlr-scl4815-438-lulu-dietrich-wolfe-leight-3010-1927). The 1930 deed types the lessee 'Alan K Wood'. Update Oct. 13, 2026: Mary Clemens's source, read here as 'A.Q. 1115', is R.O. 1615/24, now read (719:mdlr-ro1615-24-dodson-griffith-mary-clemens-1896): Richard S. Dodson and John M. and Rose J. Griffith to Mary Clemens, Apr. 23, 1896, $5,000, from Abraham G. Mott's deed of Dec. 6, 1892 (J.B. 1422/568). The scan of this lease reads 'R.O. No 1615 folio 24'. Update Oct. 14, 2026: by 1927 the reversion of this lease was the Swormstedt family's (719:mdlr-scl4728-211-baer-swormstedt-1927) and the lessee's term the Dietrichs' (719:mdlr-scl4735-61-c-reese-dietrich-dietrichs-1927); the steps from Mary Clemens and from Allen K. Wood to them are not read. Update Oct. 14, 2026: by Dec. 16, 1903 the reversion and $180 rent were sold by John P. Clarke, executor (whose estate is not stated), to Richard and Barbara C. Swormstedt (R.O. 2050/46, recited in 719:mdlr-scl4728-194-swormstedts-baer-3010-reversion-1927). Mary Clemens also leased Wood the Vineyard Lane lot behind it on Apr. 17, 1902 at $54 (R.O. 1952/245). Update Oct. 14, 2026: Mary Clemens sold the $180 rent the same day to Francis P. Duggan (R.O. 1928/238, recited in 719:mdlr-ro2050-46-duggan-executors-swormstedt-3010-rent-1903); the 1902 Vineyard Lane lease to Wood is read, and that rent too was sold the same day, to Mary L. Conway for $900 (719:mdlr-ro1952-245-mary-clemens-wood-lease-conway-rent-vineyard-lane-1902).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber R.O. 1729, folios 241 to 242 (MSA CE 168-1737; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 240 to 244: 240 is the end of another instrument, the foot of 242 below this deed's acknowledgment opens a City of Baltimore Permanent Building Association release to John Bauer, and the rest of the scan holds other instruments). Index heading 'Augustus D Clemens Jr &c Deed to William L Fink'. Augustus D. Clemens Junior and Mary Clemens, his wife, of Baltimore County, to William L. Fink of Baltimore City, 'this eighteenth day of April ... eighteen hundred and ninety eight', 'five hundred dollars', in fee simple: 'all that lot of ground situate and lying in said Baltimore City in the Village of Waverly', 'Beginning for the same on the east side of the York Turnpike Road at a point distant one hundred and ninety feet and seven inches southerly from the two mile stone located on the east side of the York Turnpike Road in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot said point of beginning being also two hundred and sixty seven feet and two inches southerly from the north side of a four foot alleyway called Bateman's alley and running thence southerly bounding on the east side of the York Turnpike Road fourteen feet thence easterly at right angles ... forty two feet and four inches to the westernmost side of the Old York Road thence northeasterly bounding on the westernmost side of the Old York Road fifteen feet and two and one half inches and thence westerly by a straight line forty eight feet and three inches to the place of beginning'. 'Being a part of the ground conveyed by Shepard G Miller (widower) to said Augustus D Clemens Jr by deed in fee dated December 20th 1897 and recorded among the Land Records of said Baltimore City in Liber R O No 1710 folio 153 &c.' Special warranty. Signed Augustus D. Clemens Junior and Mary Clemens (seals), witness Wm. D. Wright; acknowledged April 18, 1898 before Wm. D. Wright, Justice of the Peace; received for record April 20, 1898 at 11 A.M. and recorded the same day (Robert Ogle, clerk). What it settles: the 3013 lot is the Fink lot, 14 ft on the turnpike, bought for $500 in fee, so the 1898 deed is a plain fee conveyance (the one-cent rent of 3013 comes from the 1943 sale-leaseback recited in M.L.P. 9566/459 and 461, rows 46098 and 46099, not from 1898). Three corrections: the deed is dated April 18, 1898 and recorded April 20 (later deeds recite April 19; row 42086 had April 12); the 1897 grantor of the parent ground is Shepard G. Miller, a widower, not 'Keller'; and his deed is R.O. 1710/153, not 1710/105 (the folio the 1902 and later recitals give, which the Oct. 12 pull found to be other deeds). What it does not settle: the Miller deed itself (R.O. 1710/153 is a new hop) and how the lot passed from Fink to W. Harry Holmes, from whom James M. Sinclair took a deed in 1919 (S.C.L. 3311/260, as read in the 1927 deed, rows below). Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Fink deeds S.C.L. 2559/393 and 3126/290 read): this lot is the first of the four lots William L. Fink left at his death (the 1910 deed, S.C.L. 2559/393, 720:mdlr-scl2559-393-frederick-fink-mary-catherine-bertha-estella-four-lots-3013-1910: 'died seized and possessed', so he died after April 18, 1898), and the 1917 deed (S.C.L. 3126/290, 720:mdlr-scl3126-290-mary-catherine-fink-himmelmann-3013-and-five-limond-place-lots-1917) calls it '3013 York Road (formerly 1005)', the first deed to tie the lot to the street numbers. His will of Feb. 2, 1893 (Wills S.R.M. 82/278, not read) left the residue to his wife Louisa for life or widowhood and then to his four children as tenants in common; the 1910 deed treats the 1898 lot as part of that residue.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber S.C.L. 4707, folios 12 to 14 (MSA CE 168-4715; read on the scan Jeff saved: it opens on 12 under the index heading 'J Holliday Riepe Deed To James M Sinclair &c', directly under the Sinclairs' deed to Riepe, and ends on 14 above the Peppler mortgage). J. Holliday Riepe, unmarried, of Baltimore County, to James M. Sinclair and Ena M. Sinclair, his wife, of Baltimore City, 'this first day of March' 1927 as typed, 'Five Dollars and other valuable considerations': the same three lots by the same descriptions as the deed to him (the first, the 3011 tip lot, 204 ft 7 in south of the two mile stone, 58 ft 4 in on the turnpike; the second, the 14-foot lot 190 ft 7 in south of the stone; the third, the leasehold at the eight-foot alley), to hold 'unto the use of the said James M Sinclair and Ena M Sinclair his wife as tenants by the entireties their assigns the survivor of them and the survivor's heirs and assigns in fee simple' as to the first and second lots, and the third for the residue of the term with renewal forever at one cent a year if demanded. Special warranty. Signed J. Holliday Riepe, witness Lennox B. Clemens; the notarial certificate, by Lennox B. Clemens, reads 'on this first day of' a month that ends in '-ary' (February, as I read it) 1927; recorded March 7, 1927 at 2:01 P.M. (Stephen C. Little, clerk), one minute after the Sinclairs' deed to Riepe. What it settles: the deed Corridor and the 3011 descriptions of 1954, 1974 and 2007 call 'Riepe (Reipe) to James M. and Edna M. Sinclair, March 1, 1927' is read: it is the return half of a pass-through in which James M. Sinclair, the only buyer the recitals name, conveyed three lots to Riepe on March 5 and Riepe conveyed them to James and his wife as tenants by the entireties, both recorded March 7, 1927 (the purpose is not stated; the Sinclairs' deed is dated four days later than Riepe's, and the certificate's month reads February, so the typed dates are unreliable and the recording stamps, 2:00 and 2:01 P.M. on March 7, are the safe dates). 3011 and 3013 were fee simple in 1927; the $66 rent on 3011 does not come from a lease older than 1954. What it does not settle: the amounts and the third lot's location. Update Oct. 13, 2026: both Sinclair sales of the two tip lots recite this deed: the 3013 lot in the Sinclair to Moser deed of Nov. 23, 1938 ('the same lot of ground which by Deed dated March 1st 1927 was granted and conveyed by J. Holliday Riepe to the said Grantors', 720:mdlr-mlp5874-532-sinclair-moser-3013-1938) and the 3011 lot in the Sinclair children's deed to Adam H. Weber of June 19, 1954 ('the firstly described lot of ground in the deed from J. Holliday Riepe (Single) to James M. Sinclair and Ena M. Sinclair his wife dated March 1, 1927', 720:mdlr-mlp9513-54-sinclairs-weber-3011-1954). So Riepe's 1927 deed carried both lots, the first of them (3011) in the 'firstly described' position.

Lillie Norris, single, of Baltimore, to Fletcher L. Vinson, Dec. 18, 1934, 'in consideration of the rent hereinafter expressed': the 15-foot lot of 3015, 175 feet 7 inches south of the two mile stone and 252 feet 2 inches south of the north side of 'Boteman's Alley', running south 15 feet to the northwest corner of the Fink lot (R.O. 1729/241, which the lease dates April 19, 1898), east 48 feet 3 inches, north 15 feet 2 inches and west 53 feet; 'BEING the same lot of ground which by deed dated December 18 1934 and recorded ... immediately prior hereto' was conveyed by the Vinsons to Norris. For 99 years 'beginning on the day of the date of these presents', rent $120 in half-yearly instalments from Dec. 18, 1934 (the 1944 deed and the mortgage below say June 18 and December 18), over and above taxes; distress; re-entry if the rent is sixty days in arrear and, at six months, 'as if this lease had never been made'; the lessor to execute, on ten dollars as a renewal fine, a new 99-year lease 'so that the demise hereby created may be renewable and renewed from time to time forever'. Signed Fletcher L. Vinson, lessee, and Lillie Norris, lessor, witness E. Gardner Ziegler; acknowledged Dec. 18, 1934 before E. Gardner Ziegler, Notary Public, Lillie Norris being described as 'single'; received for record Dec. 19, 1934 at 2:46 P.M. and recorded the same day (Stephen C. Little, clerk); a grantee-index stamp reads 'Jun 19 1941'. What it settles: the lease is at S.C.L. 5497/146, recorded one minute after the Vinsons' deed to Norris and one minute before her deed of the rent (next row); its terms (99 years, $120, $10 renewal fine, renewable forever) are the ones the 1944 deed recites. Row 42029 had it from a recital only.

Benson Phelps of the same city, Dec. 18, 1934, 'five dollars and other good and valuable considerations': the 15-foot lot of 3015 with the same description as the lease, 'BEING the same lot of ground described in a deed from Fletcher L Vinson and Margaret C Vinson his wife to the said Lillie Norris dated December 18 1934 and recorded ... immediately prior hereto', and 'being the same lot of ground which by lease dated the 18th day of December 1934 and recorded ... immediately prior hereto was demised and leased by Lillie Norris single unto Fletcher L Vinson for the term of ninety nine years at and for the annual rent of one hundred and twenty dollars ($120.00) payable in semi-annual instalments on the 18th day of June and December'. 'TO HAVE AND TO HOLD the above granted property and particularly the aforesaid rent payable out of said lot and the reversion thereto unto the said R Benson Phelps his assigns forever in fee simple subject however to the estate terms and interest of the said lessee his representatives and assigns under the said lease.' Special warranty. Signed Lillie Norris, witness E. Gardner Ziegler; acknowledged Dec. 18, 1934 before E. Gardner Ziegler; recorded Dec. 19, 1934 at 2:47 P.M. (Stephen C. Little, clerk). What it settles: the 'Norris to Phelps deed of the rent, liber not found' of rows 42029 and the Edition 2 hop list is S.C.L. 5497/147 to 148, recorded in a run of three instruments at 2:45, 2:46 and 2:47 P.M. on Dec. 19, 1934: Vinson to Norris, Norris's lease back, Norris's deed of the rent and reversion to Phelps. Phelps held the reversion and the $120 rent until his deed of July 8, 1944 (M.L.P. 6619/477, row 42030). What it does not settle: who Lillie Norris was (an acknowledged 'single' woman, with E. Gardner Ziegler notarizing every instrument of the day, so very probably a conveyancing nominee, which the deeds do not say).

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore City land records, Liber S.C.L. 5497, folios 148 to 149 (MSA CE 168-5505; read on the scan Jeff saved to the foot of 149: the end of the mortgage, its acknowledgment and its recording stamp are on 150 and after, not pulled; index heading 'Fletcher L Vinson Mtge To R Benson Phelps', with a margin note 'Order filed 3/13/35' in a later hand). Fletcher L. Vinson of Baltimore, mortgagor, to R. Benson Phelps, mortgagee, dated Dec. 18, 1934, securing $1,000.00 'for money this day loaned and advanced', repayable $350.00 at four years, $350.00 at five and $350.00 at six, 'with interest on all of said payments at the rate of 6% per annum payable semi-annually', anticipation permitted on interest days. He grants and assigns the 15-foot lot of 3015 'for all the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein with the benefit of renewal thereof from time to time forever subject to the payment of the annual rent of one hundred and twenty ($120.00) dollars', with a power of sale under Chapter 123 of the Laws of Maryland of the January session of 1898 and Article LXVI of the Code of 1904, E. Gardner Ziegler named attorney to sell. What it settles: on Dec. 18, 1934 the Vinsons turned 3015 into a leasehold at $120 a year (deed to Norris, lease back, deed of the rent to Phelps) and Vinson borrowed $1,000 from Phelps on the leasehold the same day, so the ground rent and the loan went to the same man: row 42029's reading, that the owner 'probably raised money on the ground and kept the building', is borne out by the three instruments. The 1944 buy-back (row 42030, about $2,000 by stamps) paid Phelps for the rent. What it does not settle: the rest of the mortgage, when it was released, and the $1,000's relation to the 1934 price of the lot ($3,600 on Sept. 18, 1934, S.C.L. 5481/414).

Calvin Carney et al., Receivers to the said Fletcher L. Vinson and Kathryn R. Vinson, his wife.' Together with the buildings and 'especially the clear yearly rent of Fifty-four dollars issuing out of said lot of ground by virtue of the lease aforesaid', to hold in fee simple 'to the end and intent that the leasehold estate created by the lease aforesaid shall be merged with the fee, and the annual rent issuing thereout shall be forever extinguished'. Special warranty. Signed Harry R. Sinclair and Alice M. Sinclair, witness John M. Biesecker; acknowledged Dec. 20, 1951 before Philip Schwartzman, Notary Public, Baltimore City; recorded Dec. 26, 1951, Liber M.L.P. 8666 page 310 (M. Luther Pittman, clerk). What it settles: the reversion and $54 rent of 3017 were held by Leopold Lehman (will W.J.P. 16/78; his widow Mary C. Lehman for life, remainder to their son Ernest George, who died about Jan. 13, 1924 intestate and unmarried, so the whole passed to his mother), then Mary C. Lehmann, widow, who sold them on Dec. 21, 1946 to the Sinclairs (M.L.P. 7060/156), who sold the Vinsons, then lessees, the reversion on Dec. 20, 1951, extinguishing the $54 rent by merger: Corridor's 'who held the fee before Sinclair is not known' (row 42033) is answered, and the merger it inferred is read. Willis (R.O. 2037/211, a new hop), which fits the trustee's deed of Dec. 1908 to Clemens Jr. and his assignment to Mason in 1909 as the end of Willis's term. A caution: the 1951 deed says 3017 was 'formerly known as No. 3013', so the old York Road number 1005 that Polk gives Joseph J. Willis, carpenter, may belong to this lot and not to the 14-foot lot now numbered 3013; that is not resolved. What it does not settle: the 1946 deed, the Lehman will and why Leopold Lehman held the reversion (he may have bought it from the Clemens estate). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the two instruments this deed recites are read: the 1903 Willis lease (721:mdlr-ro2037-211-clemens-willis-lease-3017-1903) and Mary C. Lehmann's 1946 deed to the Sinclairs (721:mdlr-mlp7060-156-lehmann-sinclair-3017-rent-1946), four ground rents in one deed, with 3017 typed 'No. 3013 Greenmount Avenue'. The rent's owners before Lehmann: Mary K. Fink (1903 to 1907).

summary: Lease, Baltimore City land records, Liber R.O. 1728, folios 284 to 286 (MSA CE 168-1736; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 283 to 287: 283 is the end of a Maryland Building and Loan Association deed of two Milton Avenue lots; 287 is Jane C. Rowe's assignment to William L. Batchelor). Index heading 'Augustus D Clemens Jr &c Lease to Jacob H Aull'. Augustus D. Clemens Junior and Mary Clemens, his wife, of Baltimore County, to Jacob H. Aull of Baltimore City, April 14, 1898, 'in consideration of the rent hereinafter expressed': the lot 'on the east side of the York Turnpike Road at a point distant one hundred and twenty three feet and five inches southerly from the two mile stone located on the east side of the York Turnpike Road in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot said point of beginning being also two hundred feet southerly from the north side of a four foot alley way called Bateman's alley', south 33 feet on the turnpike, east 58 feet 1 inch to the Old York Road, northeast 34 feet 4 inches, and west by a straight line 67 feet 7 inches to the beginning, 'Being a portion of the ground described in a deed from Shepard G Miller to said Augustus D Clemens Junior dated December 20th 1897 and recorded ... Liber R O No 1710 folio 153 &c'. For 99 years from the date, rent sixty dollars 'in even and equal half yearly instalments accounting from the fifteenth day of April' 1898, over and above taxes; distress; re-entry if the rent is sixty days in arrear and, at six months or a year, as if the lease 'had never been made'; on ten dollars as a renewal fine the lessors to give a new 99-year lease on the same rent 'so that the demise hereby created may be renewable and renewed from time to time forever'. Signed Augustus D. Clemens Junior, Mary Clemens and Jacob H. Aull, witness John J. Dunn; acknowledged April 14, 1898 before John J. Dunn, Justice of the Peace; recorded the same day (Robert Ogle, clerk). What it settles: the lot 123 ft 5 in to 156 ft 5 in south of the two-mile stone, 33 ft on the avenue, is the lot of 3019, and the lease the 3017 description bounds itself on ('the southwest corner of the lot leased by Augustus D. Clemens, Jr. and wife to Jacob H. Aull', 1909, 1951, 1961 and later) is this one: it was made April 14, 1898, four days before the Fink deed for the 14-foot lot to the south of 3015. Clemens Jr. leased the 3019 ground at $60 a year and deeded Henry D. Konig the rent the same day (next row, R.O. 1728/286); the whole is cut from Shepard G. Miller's ground of Dec. 20, 1897 (R.O. 1710/153). What it does not settle: Aull's later holdings and how the rent ended.

Rowe to William L. Batchelor, begins). Index heading 'Augustus D Clemens Jr &c Deed to Henry D Konig'. Augustus D. Clemens Jr. and Mary Clemens, his wife, of Baltimore County, to Henry D. Konig of Baltimore City, April 14, 1898, 'in consideration of one thousand dollars', in fee simple: the same 33-foot lot of the Aull lease, 123 feet 5 inches south of the two mile stone, 'Being a part of the ground described in a deed from Shepard G Miller to said Augustus D Clemens Jr dated December 20th 1897 and recorded ... Liber R O No 1710 folio 153 &c', 'Together with the improvements thereon ... and especially the clear yearly rent of sixty dollars issuing out of said lot by virtue of a lease thereof from said Augustus D Clemens Jr and wife to Jacob H Aull of even date herewith and intended to be recorded prior hereto', to hold 'in fee simple subject to the leasehold interest created by the above mentioned lease but with the right to collect' the rent, payable half-yearly on the 15th of April and October. Special warranty. Signed Augustus D. Clemens Junior and Mary Clemens, witness John J. Dunn; acknowledged April 14, 1898 before John J. Dunn, Justice of the Peace; recorded the same day (Robert Ogle, clerk). What it settles: Clemens Jr. leased the lot at $60 and sold the right to the $60 for $1,000 (6 percent) to Henry D. Konig on the same day, so the reversion of 3019 was Konig's from April 14, 1898. This is the common Baltimore pattern (lease out, sell the rent) and it is what the 1934 Vinson and Norris deeds do again at 3015. What it does not settle: how the rent ended, and what became of Konig's reversion.

Miller Deed to Augustus D. Clemens Jr' and ends at the top of 154; 154 and 155 are Clemens's mortgage, next row). Sheppard G. Miller, unmarried, of Baltimore City, to Augustus D. Clemens Jr. of Baltimore County, Dec. 20, 1897, 'fifty three hundred dollars', his heirs and assigns forever in fee simple: 'all that lot of ground situate in Baltimore city', 'Beginning for the same on the East side of the York Turnpike Road at the Southwest corner of a lot of ground formerly belonging to William Baden and running thence bounding on said York Turnpike Road South six degrees west two hundred and fourteen feet' [the next words are cut at the page edge in the scan], north 89 degrees east 8 feet 6 inches to the northwest side of the Old York Road, 'thence bounding on the Northwest side of the Old York Road two courses and distances viz North thirty one and one half degrees East ninety nine feet and North twenty one and one half degrees East ninety five feet to a post at the Southeast corner of the lot formerly belonging to William Baden and thence bounding thereto North sixty one degrees West eighty two feet to the place of beginning. Being the same lot described in a deed from William H Bayless trustee to said Shepard G. Miller dated September 2nd 1896 and recorded ... Liber R.O. No 1637 folio 49 &c'. With the improvements; special warranty. Signed Shepard G. Miller (seal), witness John J. Dunn; acknowledged Dec. 20, 1897 before John J. Dunn, Justice of the Peace; received for record Dec. 20, 1897 at 3:50 P.M. and recorded the same day (Robt. Ogle, clerk). What it settles: the 'Keller' of the 1902 Rahe deed and of Corridor's earlier rows is Shepard G. Miller (spelled Sheppard on the page), and his deed is at R.O. 1710/153, not 1710/105; it is the parent ground of the 1898 Fink deed (3013), the Aull lease and Konig deed (3019), and the Rahe deed of 1902 (3015) and the 3017 lot, each of which says it is 'a part of the ground conveyed by Shepard G. Miller ... Liber R.O. No. 1710 folio 153'. It is a wedge between the turnpike and the Old York Road, 214 feet on the turnpike, bounded north by William Baden's former lot, and its first line is about 75 feet longer than the 139 feet 6 inches from the north line of 3019 to the fork (arithmetic from the stone-measured distances of the 1898 deeds, so the Miller ground probably ran about 75 feet north of the Aull lot, taking in the lots now numbered above 3019: an inference). Miller is 'unmarried' here and 'widower' in the 1898 recitals. Clemens paid $5,300 and mortgaged the same ground the same afternoon (next row). It also names the first source back: William H. Bayless, trustee, to Miller, Sept. 2, 1896 (R.O. 1637/49), a new hop. What it does not settle: whose trust Bayless executed (William Baden's former lot adjoins it on the north and the 1889 plat letters the tip 'Miss Tredway, Jno. T. Ensor Guardian'), and how much of the ground north of 3019 Clemens kept. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the 'Bayless, trustee' source it recites is read (720:mdlr-ro1637-49-bayless-miller-1896, R.O. 1637/49): a trustee's deed under the Circuit Court decree of June 25, 1896 in Miller v. Harrison (Alice M. Harrison and N. Waldo Harrison, defendants), the sale of July 27, 1896 at $4,950. It recites no earlier deed and no County instrument.

Clemens Jr. and Mary Clemens, his wife, of Baltimore County, to the Loyola Perpetual Building Association of Baltimore City, Dec. 20, 1897: Clemens, a member, has received 'an advance of Four thousand dollars on thirty two shares of stock standing in his name being the full par value' of them 'when fully paid up and completed'; they grant 'all that lot of ground' beginning on the east side of the York Turnpike Road at the southwest corner of the former William Baden lot, south 6 degrees west 214 feet 'with irregular depth to the Old York Road', 'Being the same lot described in a deed from Shepard G. Walsh, the Association's President, swearing the consideration; recorded Dec. 20, 1897 at 3:50 P.M. (as read; the Miller deed carries the same time) and the same day (Robt. Ogle, clerk). What it does not settle: how the mortgage was released or divided as the lots were sold (none of the 1898 deeds mentions it).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City land records, Liber R.O. 1637, folios 49 to 50 (MSA CE 168-1645; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 47 to 51: 47 and 48 are other instruments, a Herring mortgage and Slonaker's assignment to Kendall; the deed opens on 49 under the index heading 'William H. Bayless Trustee Deed to Shepard G. Miller', a later hand noting 'grantee 11-10-96', and ends on 50, where a Safe Deposit and Trust Company release to Frank W. Trimble follows). William H. Bayless of Baltimore City, trustee, to Shepard G. Miller of the same city, Sept. 2, 1896. It recites a decree of the Circuit Court of Baltimore City dated June 25, 1896, passed in a cause between Shepard G. Miller, complainant, and Alice M. Harrison and N. Waldo Harrison, defendants, appointing Bayless trustee with authority to sell 'the real estate in the proceedings in said cause mentioned'; that he sold it, 'after complying with all the previous requisites of the decree', on or about July 27, 1896 to Miller 'for the sum of forty nine hundred and fifty dollars'; that the sale was reported to, ratified and confirmed by the court and the purchase money paid; and that the decree authorizes him to execute the deed. The property: 'Beginning for the same on the east side of the York Turnpike Road at the southwest corner of the lot belonging to William Baden', south 6 degrees west 214 feet on the turnpike, north 89 degrees east 8 1/2 feet to the west side of the Old York Road, north 31 1/2 degrees east 99 feet 'to a post', north 21 1/2 degrees east 95 feet 'to a post at the southeast corner of Wm Badens lot', and north 61 degrees west 82 feet to the beginning (the courses of the Miller to Clemens deed of Dec. 20, 1897, which was written from this one). For $5 Bayless grants Miller, his heirs and assigns, the property 'and all the right title interest and estate of the parties to the aforesaid decree both at Law and in equity in and to the same'. Signed William H. Bayless, trustee (seal), witness Robert C. Rhodes; acknowledged Sept. 2, 1896 before Robert C. Rhodes, Justice of the Peace; received for record Sept. 2, 1896 at 2 o'clock P.M. and recorded the same day (Robt. Ogle, clerk). What it settles: Miller did not buy the ground at arm's length from an owner; he was the complainant in a suit against Alice M. Harrison and N. Waldo Harrison and bought the property at the trustee's sale the court ordered (in a suit where the complainant takes the property, the usual shape is a foreclosure or a creditor's bill, but the deed does not say which, and it does not say what the Harrisons' interest was). The $4,950 sale price is $350 below the $5,300 Miller took from Clemens fifteen months later, and the deed names no earlier owner, no earlier deed and no County instrument: the Miller to Clemens deed's 'R.O. 1637/49' is a trustee's deed, not a chain of title. The tract's County-era title therefore has to be reached through the Harrisons (how Alice M. and N. Waldo Harrison came to hold it) or through William Baden's adjoining lot (the northern neighbour, named in both deeds as 'the lot belonging to William Baden'), not through this deed. What it does not settle: the Harrisons' source, the nature of the suit (the equity papers and docket), and whether Miller held a mortgage on the ground; the grantee-index stamp 'grantee 11-10-96' is a later indexing note, not a second recording. The 1889 plat's 'Miss Tredway, Jno. T. Ensor Guardian' is not mentioned here, so the Tredway link (row 42366) is not supported by this deed.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 160, folios 580 to 581 (MSA CE 66-210; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 580 to 584: the foot of 580 is the end of a Rogers, Donaldson and Emory deed to Richard Caton, acknowledged Aug. 8, 1821; this deed opens in the lower half of 580 under the index heading 'Samuel Moale & James Biays Deed to John McFadon' and ends on 581; the next deed, row below, follows it on 582). Samuel Moale, trustee for the sale of the property in a Chancery decree of Feb. 2, 1819 (John Bolte, J. and E. Schultze, Rudolph Wagler and others, complainants, against James Biays, defendant), and James Biays, of Baltimore City, to John McFadon, April 26, 1821. The decree ordered a sale of the ground Biays had mortgaged to Bolte on Feb. 4, 1813; Moale sold it at public auction at Patrick Allison's auction room on July 28, 1819, in lots shown on a plat made for the sale. This deed conveys Lot No. 1, 'part of a tract of Land called Ensors Inspection': 'Beginning for the same at a Stone marked B it being the beginning of the Ground mortgaged by the said James Biays to John Bolte', running north 40 1/2 degrees east 27 perches 'to the York Turnpike Road', then southerly on the turnpike about 34 perches (the figure reads thirty-four and a half) until it meets a line the clerk wrote as 'the Green line' of the whole mortgaged ground, and back along that line to the stone, 'Containing one acre three quarters and thirty Square perches'. Biays was the highest bidder for it at $1,450, subject to the dower of his wife Sarah Biays, and directed Moale to convey it to McFadon, which Biays joins in doing. Signed Saml Moale, trustee, and Jas. Biays (seals), witnesses R. H. Moale and John F. Harris; acknowledged April 26, 1821 before two justices; received to be recorded Aug. 14, 1821 (Wm. Gibson, clerk). What it settles: McFadon's first source for the ground his 1822 deed of trust describes is read. The lot-1 beginning stone 'B' is the beginning stone of McFadon's 1822 trust ground (W.G. 165/492, row 46094), so Lot No. 1 and the 1822 ground start at the same stone and the same first line (north 40 1/2 degrees east to the York Turnpike), which crosses the road. The courses (from the stone on the south-east side of the lane, 27 perches north-east to the turnpike, then south along it) suggest Lot 1 lies on the west side of the turnpike, south of the toll-gate lane, where the 1844 Mumma lot (A.W.B. 354/374, row 46070) is; that is an inference from the courses, not a statement in the deed. Why the five lots came to McFadon: James Biays bought Lot 1 at the sale of his own mortgaged ground and assigned the bid; the other lots are in the next deed. What it does not settle: where on the modern grid any lot lies; the figure after 'thirty four and a half perches' is not certain. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the mortgaged ground is read (719:mdlr-wg122-133-biays-bolte-mortgage-1813): stone B stands 'on the south east side of a road leading from the land of Hugh Thompson into the york turnpike road at or near the gate', the road later called Gilmor Lane; the ground was the 'Walker's Tavern' parcel, conveyed to Biays by Christopher Walker about July 14, 1809 (W.G. 104/46). Update Oct. 17, 2026 (archive lead): the Archives' chancery index lists the Bolte suit as S512-1-501 (Aug. 30, 1816, John Bolte, John E. Schultz, Rudulph Vogelar v. James Biays, 'Mortgage foreclosure on Ensors Inspection', accession 17,898-450-1/3, 1/35/5, Chancery Record 109 p. 354); an outside addendum's 'S512-501' is a truncation of that ID. Not read (719:msa-leads-ensors-inspection-s512-1-501-c295-3272-2026-10-17).

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 160, folios 582 to 584 (MSA CE 66-210; read on the scan Jeff saved: it opens on 582 under the index heading 'Samuel Moale Deed to John McFadon' and ends on 584, where an Isaac Green mortgage to John Cugle follows). Samuel Moale, trustee in Bolte et al. v. Biays, to John McFadon, April 26, 1821, the second of the pair (the first, Lot No. 1, is the row above). Lot No. 2, 'part of a tract of Land called Ensors Inspection' and so numbered on the trustee's plat: 'Beginning for the same at a Stone standing at the end of the north sixty nine degrees west thirty five perches line of the Land mortgaged by James Biays to John Bolte ... and for the corner of a Lot of Ground belonging to the Quaker Society and running south fifteen degrees west twenty two perches and nine tenths of a perch to Henry Starrs lane thence bounding on said lane south eighty four degrees west fifteen and a half perches to the York Turnpike Road thence northerly bounding on said road' [to the stone, the line continued across the page edge], 'Containing three acres and twenty Square perches of Land more or less with the Tavern and other improvements thereon erected', sold to McFadon, by the bid of Edward Perine, for $3,000, 'subject to the right of Dower of Sarah Biays' and 'to a County road that runs as it is said through a corner of this Lot to intersect the York Turnpike road'. Lot No. 3 ('Beginning ... north sixty nine degrees west two perches from the Stone the beginning of Lot number Two', north 32 degrees east 12 perches, north 67 degrees west 21 perches to a lot owned by Captain Chaytor, and so back along the first line of the mortgaged ground to the turnpike, 8 perches 'to Lot number Two'): 'one acre two quarters and sixteen Square perches ... with the brick building and two frame buildings on the road which are subject to a lease of twenty-two years (as read) from the twenty sixth day of May eighteen hundred and nineteen and at thirty two dollars each per annum', sold by the bid of William Bromwell Junior for $1,400, subject to dower, to that lease and 'to a County road that runs as it is supposed through the front of this Lot to intersect the York Turnpike road'. Lot No. 4 (six acres two quarters and thirty-four perches, bounded by Captain Chaytor's lot, a 'Grant's addition', Lot 3 and the first line of the mortgaged ground) and a further parcel of Lot 4 and Lot 5 (nine acres one quarter and twenty perches, with 'a claim set up to Lot number five by Robert Gorsuch Esq.') were sold to McFadon 'subject to the several claims and supposed incumbrances before particularly mentioned', the prices not certain on the page; the deed then conveys 'all those aforegoing Lots pieces and parcels of Land numbers Two, Three, Four and Five' together to McFadon, his heirs and assigns forever. Signed Saml Moale (Trustee); acknowledged April 26, 1821 before two justices; received to be recorded Aug. 14, 1821. What it settles: the five parcels McFadon's 1822 trust deed says Moale conveyed to him in two deeds of April 26, 1821 are Lots 1 to 5 of the ground Biays mortgaged to Bolte, sold at a Chancery sale on July 28, 1819; they lie in Ensor's Inspection, the east-side lots (2 to 5) bounded by the Quaker Society's lot, Henry Starr's lane, Captain Chaytor's lot, 'Grant's addition' and a County road that crosses the turnpike frontage, with a Tavern on Lot 2 and a brick building and two frame buildings on the road on Lot 3. That is a lead for the east-side lots at the fork, not a placement: the deeds name no street, no modern lot and no number, and the 1897 and 1896 deeds of the Miller ground (R.O. 1710/153, 1637/49) do not cite them. What it does not settle: whether the 'County road' of Lots 2 and 3 is the Old York Road, where Henry Starr's lane and the Quaker lot were, and the prices and exact bounds of Lots 4 and 5. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the 'Quaker Society' lot that bounds Lot 2 also appears in 1847 as 'the Quaker Lot' on the south-east of Jacob Aull's 2 a 29 P bought from the four Biays couples (A.W.B. 381/479, 720:mdlr-awb381-479-bowerman-aull-bond-1847), beside the Vestry's lot and Leitzinger's 77 1/2 perches (A.W.B. 381/477, 720:mdlr-awb381-477-bowerman-leitzinger-1847): the same name on the same Biays ground. Same lot, not proved. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (archive lead): the case is S512-1-501 in the Archives' chancery index (Chancery Record 109 p. 354); Moale's sale plat of July 28, 1819 may be in that file. Not read (719:msa-leads-ensors-inspection-s512-1-501-c295-3272-2026-10-17).

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber A.W.B. 359, folios 136 to 137 (MSA CE 66-409; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 136 to 140: the top of 136 is the end of a different instrument; it opens under the index heading 'John W. Stump Trustee Deed To Nancy Hoke &c' and ends on 137 above Samuel Griscom's grant of a right of way to Thomas Galloway; 138 to 140 are other instruments). John W. Stump, surviving trustee, 'of Harford County' [struck, 'now of the City of Baltimore' interlined], to Nancy Biays (now the wife of Jacob Hoke), Frances J. Biays (now the wife of Henry Hammond), Elizabeth Biays (now the wife of Henry N. Bowerman) and Hannah Jane Biays (now the wife of Doctor Walter T. Allender), Oct. 28, 1845. It recites McFadon's deed of trust of April 11, 1822 (W.G. 165/492) to Stump and Philip G. Biays, for Sarah Biays for life and then for her four daughters; that Philip G. Biays and Sarah Biays are both dead; and that Stump executes the deed 'for the more fully and completing the object and intent of the trust'. For $5 he conveys to the four daughters, their heirs and assigns, 'all that part of a tract of Land situate lying and being in Baltimore County ... commonly called or known by the name of Ensors Inspection', by the same metes as the 1822 deed ('Beginning ... at a Stone standing on the South East side of a road leading from the land of Hugh Thompson into the York Turnpike near the gate the said stone being marked with the letter B', north 40 1/2 degrees east to the turnpike 'and with the same course across the said road to the distance of ninety four perches and three quarters of a perch from the beginning', the Foster to Walker line of 'on or about the fourth March 1800', south 59 east 41 perches, south 19 west 9 1/4, and so on to the Quaker Society's lot and Henry Starr's lane and James Biays's lot), 'being the same land which was by two several Indentures bearing date respectively on the twenty sixth day of April in the year Eighteen hundred and twenty one Conveyed in five several parcels by Samuel Moale to the said John McFadon' (W.G. 160/580 and 582). Signed Jno. W. Stump; acknowledged Oct. 28, 1845 before G. D. Spencer and T. Hanson Belt, justices of the peace of the City; received Nov. 5, 1845 at 10 minutes before 10 A.M. and recorded the same day (Wm. A. W. Bradford, clerk). A later margin note beside the index heading ('W. T. Allender, 6 [?] May 184[?]') is not read. What it settles: the trust of 1822 was executed on Oct. 28, 1845, after Sarah Biays's death (after the 1844 Mumma deed, which she signed) and Philip G. Biays's: the four daughters took the whole ground in fee. The partitions that follow in the Tract Index (Hoke, Hammond, Bowerman and Allender to Wilson, Leitzinger, Heavey and Brady, A.W.B. 381 to 404, 1847 to 1848) are their sales, so the Biays-heirs ground passes to the people on the 1844 to 1849 plats and in the deeds on file (Wilson, Mumma, Allender to Brady) from here. What it does not settle: where any of the later lots lie. Update Oct. 13, 2026: Allender, one of the four sons-in-law who took under this deed, sold Samuel Brady 19 a 38 P of Ensor's Inspection on Nov. 30, 1848 (A.W.B. 404/533), by a trustee's deed under his own 1847 Chancery suit against William Jackson and others; it recites the 1801 to 1804 Biays deeds (714:mdlr-awb404-533-allender-brady-1848). Update Oct. 13, 2026: the four couples' first small sales under this deed are read: John Leitzinger, 8 1/2 and 77 1/2 square perches, June 10, 1847, $500 (A.W.B. 381/477, 720:mdlr-awb381-477-bowerman-leitzinger-1847), and Jacob Aull, 2 a 29 P by bond of conveyance of May 1, 1847 (381/479, 720:mdlr-awb381-479-bowerman-aull-bond-1847); both recite this deed (A.W.B. 359/136). Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): the daughters sold James Wilson the 85-perch triangle at the turnpike and Gilmor's Lane in 1847 (725:mdlr-awb382-43-hoke-biays-daughters-james-wilson-toll-gate-triangle-1847).

Realty Corporation', and 'the same lot of ground as described in a Lease dated July 13, 1956 from The R. C. Realty Corporation to Royal Crown Bottling Company of Baltimore, Inc.' Realty's stockholders when it dissolved in 1962; William Franklin held 80 of 106 parts and put them in a family trust in 1972. Special warranty deed made July 3, 2010 by Beverage Capital Corporation, a Pennsylvania corporation, to Bevco Realty LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, 'in consideration of the sum of ONE DOLLAR ($1.00)', of all its 'right, title and interest' in the lot at 401 East 30th Street, 'subject to all matters of record'. The grantor certifies that the conveyance is not part of a transaction in which there is a sale, lease, exchange or other transfer of all or substantially all of its assets. Exhibit A is the 1.6250-acre description. It recites the root: 'BEING the same premises which Mary Marshall Franklin, James Henry Franklin, IV, Judith Franklin Campbell and First National Bank of Maryland, Trustees under Trust Agreement of William C. Franklin dated December 26, 1972, and James Henry Franklin, IV, individually, by Deed dated February 25, 1986 and recorded among the Land Records of the City of Baltimore in Liber 0803, Page 420, granted and conveyed unto Royal Crown Bottling Company of Baltimore, Inc., ... in fee. AND by Certificate of Merger filed ... April 19, 1993 in Liber 3947, Page 102, the said Royal Crown Bottling Company of Baltimore, Inc. merged with and into and became known as Beverage Capital Corporation.' Signed by Walter Wilkinson, Secretary of Beverage Capital Corporation, before Sharon K. Boddy, Notary Public, Camden County, New Jersey, July 3, 2010; recorded Dec. 16, 2010 at 11:42 A.M. with a City transfer tax stamp of $4,500 (cash slip 215814, dated 12/16/2010). The intake sheet lists the deed as 'Not an arms-length sale', purchase price and full cash value $300,000, grantee c/o The Honickman Group, 8275 N. Crescent Boulevard, Pennsauken, New Jersey, instrument submitted by David Feldman, First American Title Insurance Company. What it settles: the exact date (July 3, 2010, recorded Dec. 16, 2010, so the earlier whitepaper row's 'sold in 2010' is right), the parties (a Pennsylvania corporation that was the Royal Crown bottler after its 1993 merger, to a Honickman-family entity) and the chain behind it: Franklin trustees to Royal Crown Bottling Co. of Baltimore, Inc. in 1986 (Liber 0803/420, folio digits as printed), then Beverage Capital by merger in 1993. What it does not settle: the intra-family transfers inside the Honickman group, why a $300,000 transfer was stamped on a $1 deed, or the 1986 deed's price (not pulled).
