summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber A.W.B. 404, folios 533 to 535 (MSA CE 66-454; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 533 to 537: the top of 533 is the end of another instrument; the deed opens on 533 under the index heading 'Walter T. Allender, Trustee, Deed to Samuel Brady' and ends on 535, where a lease follows and runs on to 536; 537 holds a second lease). Walter T. Allender, of the City of Baltimore, trustee, to Samuel Brady of Baltimore County, dated Nov. 30, 1848. It recites a cause 'lately depending in Baltimore County Court sitting as a Court of Equity wherein Walter T. Allender the above named trustee and wife were Complainants and William Jackson and others were defendants', in which it was 'on or about the Second day of April ... eighteen hundred and forty seven' decreed that the property be sold and Allender appointed trustee; that on May 1, 1847 he sold at public auction the land described, Samuel Brady the highest bidder at $6,700; and that the sale was reported to and ratified by the Court of Chancery. For $1 Allender conveys 'all that piece or parcel of land being part of the tract of land called Ensors Inspection': 'Beginning for the same at a Stone heretofore planted on the West side of the Baltimore and York Turnpike road marked J.B. on one side and E. on the other which said Stone stands on the Second line of the land conveyed by James Edwards to James Biays on the third day of November ... eighteen hundred and four', north 86 degrees west 36 4/10 perches to another stone marked J.B. and E., south 35 1/2 degrees west 17 1/10 perches to a white oak, south 53 degrees west 5 1/2 perches, north 45 degrees west 29 1/2 perches to a stone on the east side of a road two perches wide, 'being the beginning of the land conveyed by Samuel Smith and others to James Biays' on May 30, 1801, then on that road north 42 3/4 degrees east 72 perches, south 81 degrees east 27 perches to the Baltimore and York Turnpike Road, and 'running and bounding on said road south three and one half degrees west fifty three and one half perches to the beginning, Containing Nineteen acres and thirty eight square perches'. It is 'the land conveyed by Samuel Smith and others to James Biays' (May 30, 1801, W.G. 67/447), 'also the land conveyed by James Maydwell to James Biays' (Sept. 26, 1801, W.G. 67/63 as read; the Tract Index has 67/62), 'also the land conveyed by John Gorsuch to William Jackson and others in trust' (May 10, 1803, W.G. 76/243), 'also the land conveyed by James Edwards to James Biays' (Nov. 3, 1804, W.G. 83/371, the folio written 381 and corrected above), 'and also a part of the land conveyed by Christopher Walker to James Biays' (March 9, 1801, W.G. 66/519), 'the greater portion of the above described land being also the land conveyed by James Biays to William Jackson and others in trust by deed dated the fourth day of February ... eighteen hundred and two' (W.G. 72/319), with the buildings and improvements, to Brady, his heirs and assigns forever. Signed Walter T. Allender, trustee (seal), witnessed by two men whose names read as Henry F. Friese and John J. Snyder; acknowledged Nov. 30, 1848 before two justices of the City, who are the same two names that witness it; received to be recorded Dec. 1, 1848 at about 12:07 P.M. (as read) and recorded the same day (Wm. A. W. Bradford, clerk). What it settles: the Tract Index entry 'Allender to Brady, 19 a. 38 Pr., A.W.B. 404/533' is this deed, and it is the first County instrument that puts a Brady on a named tract west of the turnpike: Samuel Brady bought, at a Chancery sale in 1847 brought by Walter T. Allender and his wife (presumably Hannah Jane Biays Allender, one of the four Biays daughters of the 1822 trust, though the deed does not name her) against William Jackson and others, 19 acres 38 perches of Ensor's Inspection which James Biays had assembled between 1801 and 1804 (five County deeds, all named by liber and folio) and put in trust for Jackson in 1802. The ground has 53 1/2 perches (about 882 feet) of frontage on the west side of the turnpike. Why it is filed on 2958 as probable and not verified: the deed names no street, no lot and no neighbour on the turnpike; the placement rests on the west side of the turnpike, the frontage, and the 1877 plan's 'Saml. Brady Est.' on the west side south of the toll gate (Edition 2, ch. 04), and the identity of this Samuel Brady with the mayor (1789 to 1871, the Brady Mansion at 2900 Greenmount) is not stated in the deed ('of the County'). What it does not settle: the 1801 to 1804 deeds themselves (not pulled; W.G. 66/519 is the Walker to Biays deed Bouldin abstracts), where the beginning stone lies, and how Brady's 19 acres became the 'about 8 acres on the York road' of his will. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the Chancery suit that produced this sale (Allender and wife v. William Jackson and others, decree April 2, 1847, sale May 1, 1847) also sold John Leitzinger the Huntington leasehold east of the turnpike, between it and the Old York Road, for $587.50 (A.W.B. 381/475, 720:mdlr-awb381-475-allender-trustee-leitzinger-huntington-leasehold-1847). Update Oct. 13, 2026: this deed (A.W.B. 404/533) is one of four title deeds recited in the Brady trustees' deed of Nov. 22, 1906 (R.O. 2290/225, 2332:mdlr-ro2290-225-brady-trustees-harvey-1906), which sold the whole remaining Brady tract, between the York Road and a lane that was Gilmor Lane, to James W. Harvey for $200,000, excepting the seven brick houses on the York Road immediately north. Update Oct. 13, 2026: published sources make 'this Samuel Brady is the mayor' probable (714:research-brady-estate-published-sources): the Archives' biography has the mayor retire to Baltimore County, and the estate's court trust of 1899 and its 1906 sale (R.O. 2290/225) fit his will. Update Oct. 13, 2026: two other Allender trustee's deeds of Jan. 19, 1848 (one to James Wilson, A.W.B. 391/168, the Gough ground of 1803; one to William T. Wilson, A.W.B. 391/169, 714:mdlr-awb391-169-allender-trustee-scott-wilson-1848) recite the same Chancery cause as this one (Allender and wife v. William Jackson and others; decree on or about Apr. 2, 1847; auction May 1, 1847): the Brady tract and the Wilson piece were lots of one sale. And Brady's other title deed, from William Gilmor, is read (2332:mdlr-awb412-283-gilmor-brady-1849): Huntington, 12 a 2 r 19 1/5 p, $3,500, Apr. 24, 1849. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the Edwards deed is read (714:mdlr-wg83-371-edwards-biays-1804): its second line runs north 88 west 36.4 perches between two stones 'marked J.B. upon one side and E upon the other', the line this deed begins on and runs (north 86 west 36 4/10 perches). Update Oct. 14, 2026: three of the Biays deeds this recites are read: the 1802 trust (W.G. 72/319: Spear's 9 7/8, Walker's 3 3/8 and Maidwell's 2 1/4 acres, trustees William Jackson, Levin Jones and John Smith), Gosuch's 1803 conveyance of Harkin's Rest into the same trust (W.G. 76/243) and the end of Maidwell's 1800 deed (W.G. 67/63; it begins on 62). summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber A.W.B. 381, folios 477 to 479 (MSA CE 66-431; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 477 to 481: the top of 477 is the end of another instrument, see below; this deed opens on 477 under the index heading 'Henry N. Bowerman, wife & others, deed to John Letzinger' and ends on 479, where the second instrument, the Aull bond, begins). Dated June 10, 1847; acknowledged the same day before John W. Stump and J. Hanson Bell, two Justices of the Peace for the City, each wife examined apart from her husband; the $500 receipted on p. 478 and the deed received to be recorded June 14, 1847 at 2 p.m. (P. A. W. Bradford, Clerk). Grantors: Henry N. Bowerman and Elizabeth his wife, Walter T. Allender and Hannah Jane his wife (both of Baltimore), Jacob Hoke and Nancy his wife and Henry Hammond and Frances his wife (both of Harford County): the four couples who took the Biays ground under the trustee's deed of Oct. 28, 1845 (A.W.B. 359/136, row 46130), which the deed recites twice by liber and folio. Grantee: John Leitzinger (the clerk writes Letzinger; the Tract Index has Leitzinger). Price $500. The deed conveys 'all that part of Ensor's Inspection' within two parcels. First parcel: begins on the east side of the York Turnpike Road at the south-west corner of a parcel 'now owned by the said Letzinger', runs along the turnpike south 5 1/2 perches, then 3/10 of a perch to the west side of the Old York Road, up the west side of the Old York Road (north 30 1/2 degrees east, distance not legible) and closes on a 3 1/10-perch line (the record writes East for that last course; it must be West to close): 8 1/2 square perches, a wedge between the two roads. Second parcel: begins at the north-west corner of the lot the same parties conveyed to the Vestry of St. John's Church by a deed of Sept. 27, 1844, runs on the east side of the road north 32 1/2 degrees east 8.2 perches, south 81 1/4 degrees east 10.4, south 17 degrees west 6.3 to the corner of the Church Lot, and back along it north 87 1/2 degrees west about 12 perches: 77 1/2 square perches. Together 86 square perches, which is the Tract Index's 'Bowerman to Leitzinger, 8 1/2 Pr. + 77 1/2 Pr., 381/477' (row 46123). What it settles: the Tract Index entry is this deed; the four couples were selling the Biays ground in small lots by June 1847; the deed puts a wedge between the turnpike and the Old York Road inside Ensor's Inspection. At the wedge's south end the two roads are 3/10 of a perch (about 5 feet) apart, and its turnpike side is 5 1/2 perches (90 ft 9 in), with an area of 2,314 square feet: the shape and place of the fork's tip. Thompson's 1889 ward plat gives the tip lot at the fork 88 ft on the York Road (chapter 06), the same order, which is suggestive and nothing more. Leitzinger already owned ground that touches the wedge's north-west corner; the instrument that ends at the top of p. 477 is a $1 conveyance from Walter T. Allender, trustee, to Leitzinger with rent or tax language ('over and above all deductions for taxes and assessments'), whose opening is on p. 476 or earlier and is not pulled. What it does not settle: which lots today are these. The deed names no street, no lot number and no neighbour that can be tied to the 1889 plat; nothing read links the wedge to 3011 or 3013, or the second parcel to any property, and whether the Vestry's 'Church Lot' of 1844 is the ground of 3009 (property 718, where the church's cornerstone was laid April 22, 1847) is not shown. Next: the beginning of the Allender-to-Leitzinger instrument (A.W.B. 381/476, or earlier), the Vestry's deed of Sept. 27, 1844, and the chain from Leitzinger forward (City or County grantor index under Leitzinger, 1847 to 1888). Update Oct. 13, 2026: Leitzinger's other ground of the same day is read: Walter T. Allender, trustee, assigned him the 2 a 15/16 Huntington leasehold between the turnpike and the Old York Road on June 10, 1847, after a Chancery sale of May 1, 1847 ($587.50; A.W.B. 381/475, 720:mdlr-awb381-475-allender-trustee-leitzinger-huntington-leasehold-1847). It is 11.7 perches wide at its foot and the wedge 3.1 perches at its top, so it is not shown to be the 'parcel now owned by the said Letzinger' at the wedge's corner. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the Vestry's deed of Sept. 27, 1844 is located in the Grantor Index: Bowerman and wife &c to the Vestry of St. John's Church, Huntingdon, 'lot of ground on the York Road', T.K. (A.W.B.) 349 folio 45, entered January 1845 (718:mdlr-ce33-15-p50-bowerman-vestry-st-johns-tk349-45); the deed (MSA CE 66-399, pages 45 to 49) is loaded for Jeff and not read. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the Church Lot is read (718:mdlr-awb349-45-biays-couples-vestry-st-johns-1844): 209 ft east-west by 208 ft along the turnpike, so this deed's second parcel (77 1/2 perches) lies directly north of it and the roads part at its north-west corner (720:analysis-fork-apex-at-church-lot-corner-3009-3011). Update Oct. 13, 2026: the same four Biays couples' deed to William T. Wilson of the same day, June 10, 1847, is read (714:mdlr-awb382-30-hoke-bowerman-allender-wilson-1847, A.W.B. 382/30, $750): on June 10, 1847 the four couples sold Leitzinger his two parts and Wilson his 3/4 acre 11 perches. Wilson's lot begins on the turnpike at the end of the first line of David Mumma's 1844 lot (A.W.B. 354/374). Update Oct. 14, 2026 (night): Bouldin's survey for this deed, Apr. 19, 1847 (720:msa-c2843-15-p106-bouldin-field-notes-1847-04-19), gives the illegible distance on the old York Road as 6 6/10 perches, shortens the turnpike line from 6 to 5 1/2 perches, and notes 'on this lot is a two Story Brick House'. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (Litzinger deeds): the 'parcel now owned by the said Letzinger' is the land John W. Stump and others deeded him on Oct. 25, 1841 (T.K. 315/188, recited, not read): Litzinger's 1864 deed to John W. Treadway (G.H.C. 39/499, 720:mdlr-ghc39-499-litzinger-treadway-1864) conveys this deed's first parcel (the wedge) and the 1841 land together as one 214-ft lot, by the courses of the 1896 sale and the 1897 Miller deed of 3011 to 3019. So the wedge is the tip, 3011 and 3013. The second parcel went to Abraham H. Bucher in 1853 (H.M.F. 7/347, 720:mdlr-hmf7-347-litzinger-bucher-ensors-inspection-77-perches-1853), beside St. John's Church lot, east of the Old York Road.

summary: Bond of conveyance, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber A.W.B. 381, folios 479 to 481 (MSA CE 66-431; read in full on the scan Jeff saved: the bond begins at the foot of 479 under the index heading 'Henry N. Bowerman, wife & others, Bond of Conv. to Jacob Aull' and ends on 481, where an unrelated instrument, George L. Melleman's assignment to George Phelan dated June 14, 1847, begins and is not read). It is not a deed. The four couples of the Leitzinger deed (Bowerman, Allender, Hoke, Hammond, with wives) bind themselves to Jacob Aull for $1,500, dated May 1, 1847, to convey him 2 acres 29 square perches 'part of the Land which was conveyed by John W. Stump Surviving trustee to Elizabeth Bowerman and others' on Oct. 28, 1845 (A.W.B. 359/136, row 46130). The price was $750: Aull paid $250 on delivery of the bond (receipted May 1, witnessed by J. Hanson Bell) and gave two $250 notes at nine and eighteen months, 'the amount of purchase money yet due'; the $1,500 penalty is twice the price. Until the deed is made he takes the rents and profits. Acknowledged June 10, 1847 before Stump and Bell with the wives examined apart, and received to be recorded June 14, 1847 at 2 p.m., the same time as the Leitzinger deed. The lot begins on the east side of the Old York Road at the end of the 8.2-perch line of the lot 'purchased from the parties by a certain John Letzinger' (the second parcel of the Leitzinger deed, so Aull's ground is immediately north of it), runs along the road north 21 1/4 degrees east about 10 perches, south 77 1/4 degrees east about 27 perches to 'the outline of the Land belonging to the heirs of James Biays' (the four daughters, as heirs of James and Sarah Biays), south 28 1/4 degrees west 16.9 perches to 'the Quaker Lot', along the north line of the Quaker Lot north 66 1/4 degrees west about 5 perches to its north-west corner, north 81 1/4 degrees west about 9 perches to the north-east corner of the Vestry's lot, and by Leitzinger's lot north 17 degrees east 6.3 perches and north 81 1/4 degrees west to the beginning (the tenths of several perch distances are hard to read in the scan and are not given here). What it settles: the County side of the ground east of the Old York Road in June 1847, in order from the south: the Vestry's lot (deed of Sept. 27, 1844), Leitzinger's 77 1/2 perches, Aull's 2 acres 29 perches; the Biays heirs' ground on the east; and 'the Quaker Lot', the Quaker Society's lot that the 1821 Moale deeds also name on the east boundary of Lot 2 beside Henry Starr's lane (row 46129): the same name on the same ground, so the 1847 parcels lie in or beside the ground of Moale's Lots 2 to 5 (Tavern, brick building), which the chapter for 3011 and 3013 carries as an unproven lead. What it does not settle: where any of this lies on today's grid, or whether it touches 3011. The Tract Index lines read (row 46123) list no Aull deed, so the deed that completed the bond was either not entered under this tract's name or not found. Next: the Aull deed (grantor index under Bowerman, Allender, Hoke or Hammond, 1847 to 1849), the Vestry's 1844 deed, and a plat. Update Oct. 13, 2026: Leitzinger's lot 'purchased from the parties herein first above mentioned' is the second parcel of the Bowerman deed (720:mdlr-awb381-477-bowerman-leitzinger-1847); his other ground, the 2 a 15/16 Huntington leasehold between the turnpike and the Old York Road (whether it adjoins these parcels is not shown), came from Allender as Chancery trustee on the same day (A.W.B. 381/475, 720:mdlr-awb381-475-allender-trustee-leitzinger-huntington-leasehold-1847). Update Oct. 13, 2026: the deed completing this bond is found and read: Nov. 4, 1848, $750, recorded March 7, 1849 (A.W.B. 409/275, 720:mdlr-awb409-275-bowerman-aull-deed-1848), with the courses this row left unread: north 21 1/2 degrees east 10.7 perches, south 77 1/4 degrees east 27.2, south 28 1/4 degrees west 16.9, north 66 1/2 degrees west 5.8, north 81 1/4 degrees west 8.9, north 17 degrees east 6.3, north 81 1/4 degrees west 10.4. The Grantee Index 1848-49 (CE 32-17 p. 24) lists it as 'Aull, Jacob from Henry N. Bowerman &c, lot on York road 2a 29P'.

Allender, Trustee, Assignt to John Letzinger', fills 476 and ends at the top of 477, where the Bowerman deed to Leitzinger follows). Dated June 10, 1847; acknowledged the same day before John W. Stump and J. Hanson Bell; received to be recorded June 14, 1847 at 2 p.m. (P. A. W. Bradford, Clerk). Allender, appointed trustee by the Baltimore County Court sitting in equity (decree of April 2, 1847, in the suit Walter T. Allender and Hannah Jane his wife v. William Jackson and others, the suit that also sold Samuel Brady 19 a 38 P west of the turnpike, row 46149), advertised and sold at auction on the premises on May 1, 1847; John Leitzinger was the highest bidder at $587.50 with interest, paid it in full, and the sale was ratified in June (the day is blank). The trustee assigns Leitzinger 'all that part of a tract of Land called Huntingdon', 2 acres and 15/16 of an acre: it begins in the middle of the York Turnpike where the first line of the parcel named first in 'a Lease from Harry Dorsey Gough and Prudence his wife [and] Job Merryman to Jesse Brown', recorded W.G. 54/156, crosses the road; runs along that line south 82 degrees east 15.9 perches to a stone on the west side of the Old York Road; down the old road south 7 3/4 degrees west 30.7 perches; south 79 1/2 degrees west 11.7 perches to the middle of the York Road; and straight back to the beginning. It is a leasehold: the unexpired term of Gough's lease, renewable forever, which Dorothy Brown, executrix of Jesse Brown, assigned to James Biays on Sept. 2, 1809 (W.G. 104/48), at a yearly rent of 4 pounds 8 shillings 1 penny currency (about $11.75), over and above taxes and assessments. The Biays heirs' side (the four daughters, who are the Bowerman, Allender, Hoke and Hammond couples of the Leitzinger deed) is cleared of all claim by the decree. What it settles: (1) the 'W.G. 104/48' that Biays's 1816 mortgage to John W. Stump recites as the third parcel (row 46103; 'two acres and fifteen sixteenths of an acre') is this lot, and W.G. 54/156, which the Tract Index carried as an unread instrument, is the Gough lease behind it (Gough and Prudence with Job Merryman to Jesse Brown): the County chain of the ground between the turnpike and the Old York Road is Gough's lease (W.G. 54/156; its date is not recited), Jesse Brown, Brown's executrix to James Biays in 1809, the Chancery sale of 1847 in the suit Biays's daughters and their husbands brought, Leitzinger. (2) Where it lies: a strip between the York Turnpike (west, the middle of the road) and the Old York Road (east), 15.9 perches wide at its north line and 11.7 at its foot, and some 35 perches (about 570 ft) long: the ground between the two roads, in Huntington, east of the turnpike. The same-day Bowerman deed to Leitzinger (row 46151) puts an 8 1/2-perch Ensor's Inspection wedge at the very tip of the fork (the roads 3/10 of a perch apart at its south end, 3.1 perches apart at its top) 'at the south west corner of a parcel of land now owned by the said Letzinger'. Whether that parcel is this leasehold is not shown, and the widths argue against it unless the old road bends: this lot is 11.7 perches wide at its foot, the wedge only 3.1 at its top, so some ground lies between them (about 24 perches at a 20 degree opening, my estimate from the courses). All the ground is Leitzinger's by June 1847 either way, in three pieces: the tip, the lot above it that he already owned, and this leasehold. What it does not settle: which of today's lots (3011, 3013, 3015, 3017 or others) lie in either piece, because the deed names no street or neighbour that reaches the 1889 plat; the lengths along the turnpike (about 570 ft for this lot and 91 ft for the wedge) and the widths are the evidence to hold against the lot frontages in the City chains. Next: Leitzinger's own deeds out (grantor index CE 33 for 1847 to 1849 and the County sales after), the Biays heirs' 1845 deed (A.W.B. 359/136), the original lease (W.G. 54/156) and the Chancery file Allender v. Jackson (the plat and the report of sale). Update Oct. 13, 2026: the Vestry's deed of Sept. 27, 1844, the head of the Church Lot, is T.K. (A.W.B.) 349 folio 45, entered January 1845 in the Grantor Index (718:mdlr-ce33-15-p50-bowerman-vestry-st-johns-tk349-45). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1809 assignment is read (720:mdlr-wg104-48-dorothy-brown-biays-huntington-leasehold-1809): 2 15/16 acres between the centre of the turnpike and the west side of the Old York Road, 30.7 perches along the old road, under Gough and Job Merryman's 1798 lease to Jesse Brown, £4 8s 1d. Update Oct. 14, 2026: Litzinger bought the fee and rent of this leasehold from Oliver P. and Araminta Merryman in 1865 (720:mdlr-jhl46-149-oliver-merryman-litzinger-brown-lease-fee-1865). Update Oct. 16, 2026 (Litzinger deeds): the parcel the wedge deed starts from is not this leasehold: it is Litzinger's 1841 land from John W. Stump and others (T.K. 315/188), recited with the wedge in his 1864 deed to John W. Treadway (G.H.C. 39/499), the 214-ft parent lot of 3011 to 3019. This leasehold lies north of it: Litzinger cut it into the Blum half-acre (J.H.L. 45/362, 1865; fee 1871, E.H.A. 70/80), John H. White's half-acre (J.H.L. 48/502, 1866) and Jacob Aull's north 260 ft (J.H.L. 46/520, 1865), all read.

summary: Index entry, Baltimore County Land Records, Grantor Index 1844 to 1845 (MSA CE 33-15, page 50, 'Bo cont'd', read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 50 to 59; the grantor index lists every deed by the first-named grantor, with the grantee, the kind of instrument, a one-line description and the liber and folio). Under January 1845: 'Bowerman, H. N.; Bowerman, Elizabeth &c' to 'Vestry of St. John's Church, Huntingdon, Balto. County', 'Deed', 'Lot of ground on the York Road', folio 45; the liber is a ditto mark under the 349 of the line above, so T.K. 349 folio 45 (the T.K. and A.W.B. books are one series: the Mumma deed that the 1912 turnpike deed cites as 'T.K. 354' is A.W.B. 354/374). The 1847 deed of the same four couples to John Leitzinger names 'the Lot of Ground conveyed ... to the Vestry of St Johns Church by deed bearing date the 27th September 1844' as the Church Lot at the head of his 77 1/2-perch parcel and at the foot of Jacob Aull's 2 a 29 P (rows 46151 and 46152 on 3011): this entry is that deed, dated Sept. 27, 1844 and entered in January 1845, so the Vestry's own title comes from the Biays couples, the grantors of the Stump trustee's deed of Oct. 28, 1845 (A.W.B. 359/136, row 46130); the order is odd (the lot was conveyed a year before the trustee executed the 1822 trust) and is what the deed itself should explain. What it settles: the Church Lot is a private deed of a lot on the York Road to the Vestry from the Biays couples (the 1844 federal sale of the Barracks to the Gibsons, which the National Register form describes, is a separate conveyance). What it does not settle: whether the lot is the present ground of St. John's at 3009 (the parish's first services were in 1843 to 1844 and the cornerstone was laid April 22, 1847, which fits), and which road 'the York Road' is. The deed, T.K. 349 folios 45 to 49 (MSA CE 66-399), is loaded in Chrome for Jeff to save and is not read. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the deed is read (718:mdlr-awb349-45-biays-couples-vestry-st-johns-1844): Sept. 27, 1844, $1,200, one acre, 209 by 208 ft on the east side of the York Turnpike, from the McFadon trust ground, recorded Jan. 31, 1845.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber T.K. (A.W.B.) 349, folios 45 to 47 (MSA CE 66-399; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 45 to 49: the deed opens at the foot of 45 under the index heading 'Sarah Biays & others, deed to The Vestry of St. John's Church, Huntingdon, Baltimore County', fills 46 and ends with its acknowledgments on 47, where Benjamin Hart's deed to Lemuel Wetherell follows; 48 and 49 are other instruments). Dated Sept. 27, 1844. Grantors: Sarah Biays, Henry N. Bowerman and Elizabeth, Walter T. Allender and Hannah Jane, Jacob Hoke and Nancy, Henry Hammond and Frances and John W. Stump (all of Harford County), and Philip G. Biays of Montgomery County: the life tenant, her four daughters and their husbands, and both trustees of the McFadon trust, so the whole interest is conveying. Grantee: the Vestry of St. John's Church, Huntingdon, Baltimore County. Price $1,200. The lot: begins 200 feet from the north side of 'a lane known as the [Gerker?] Lane' (the name is hard to read), runs east at right angles with the York Turnpike 209 feet, north parallel with the turnpike 208 feet, west at right angles 209 feet and south binding on the turnpike 208 feet to the beginning: 'one acre more or less' (209 by 208 feet is 43,472 square feet, 0.998 acre), 'part of the ground conveyed by John McFadon to John W. Stump and Philip G. Biays in trust' on April 11, 1822 (W.G. 165/492, row 46094). To the Vestry and their successors 'to be for ever kept and used as and for the site of a Protestant Episcopal Church', with covenants of further assurance. Acknowledged in Baltimore on Sept. 27, 1844 before J. Hanson Bell and O. P. Merryman, two Justices of the Peace (the wives examined apart); Philip G. Biays acknowledged in Montgomery County on Oct. 9, 1844 before Richard Ricketts and Wm. S. Beckwith, certified by John A. Carter, clerk of that court; received to be recorded Jan. 31, 1845 at 10 minutes before 5 p.m. and recorded the same day. What it settles: the church ground is a one-acre lot that fronts the York Turnpike on its east side, cut from the McFadon trust ground that the 1822 deed names Ensor's Inspection, for $1,200 (the sum Scharf gives; the $12,000 in the National Register form and the Gibson family's purchase belong to the Barracks, the old federal building, which this deed does not mention). It is the 'Church Lot' of the 1847 Leitzinger deed and Aull bond (rows 46151, 46152): their parcels begin at its corners. Its west side binds on the turnpike for 208 feet, its north line is 209 feet (12.6 perches), and a lane lies 200 feet south of its south-west corner. What it does not settle: the lane's name and place on today's grid, and whether the present ground of 3009 is exactly this acre (the parish held the church, cemetery and rectory as separate pieces in 2023). Update Oct. 14, 2026 (night): the Bouldin papers hold a St. John's vestry list folded with a June 1844 survey of 20,000 sq ft by the eastern gate post (718:msa-c2843-15-p77-st-johns-huntingdon-vestry-list-gate-post-lot-1844), and Bouldin's notes of Apr. 19, 1847 give the church lot as '208 feet square' beside the Leitzinger wedge (718:msa-c2843-15-p106-bouldin-field-notes-1847-04-19).

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber A.W.B. 409, folios 275 to 277 (MSA CE 66-459; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 275 to 279; found through the Grantee Index 1848-49, CE 32-17 page 24: 'Mar 1849, Aull, Jacob, from Henry N. Bowerman &c, Deed, lot on York road 2a 29P, 409/275'; the deed opens at the foot of 275 under the index heading 'Henry N. Bowerman, wife &c, deed to Jacob Aull', fills 276 and has its acknowledgments at the foot of 276; 277 is the start of an unrelated mortgage). Dated Nov. 4, 1848 and acknowledged the same day before two Justices of the Peace for the City; received to be recorded March 7, 1849 at 20 minutes before 1 p.m. and recorded the same day. The four Biays couples (Bowerman, Allender, Hoke, Hammond, with wives) convey Jacob Aull, for $750, the 2 acres 29 square perches of the bond of May 1, 1847 (A.W.B. 381/479, row 46152), which the deed recites: beginning on the east side of the Old York Road at the end of the 8.2-perch line of the lot sold to John Leitzinger (the second parcel of the Bowerman deed, row 46151), north 21 1/2 degrees east 10.7 perches up the east side of the road, south 77 1/4 degrees east 27.2 perches to the line of 'the land belonging to the heirs of James Biays', south 28 1/4 degrees west 16.9 perches to 'the Quaker lot', along its north line north 66 1/2 degrees west 5.8 perches to its north-west corner, north 81 1/4 degrees west 8.9 perches to the north-east corner of the lot the grantors conveyed to the Vestry of St. John's Church, then by Leitzinger's lot north 17 degrees east 6.3 perches and north 81 1/4 degrees west 10.4 perches to the beginning. Title recited: McFadon's trust deed of April 11, 1822 (W.G. 165/492), Stump's deed of Oct. 28, 1845 to the four daughters (A.W.B. 359/136, row 46130) and the bond of 1847. What it settles: the bond of 1847 was completed, 21 months after it was signed, at the same $750, and the 'Tract Index lines read list no Aull deed' remark on rows 46152 and 46123 is closed: the deed is indexed by the grantors' first name and the lot's acreage, not by the tract name. It gives the tenths of the perch courses the bond's scan left unread, and confirms in the grantors' own words that the Church Lot is the Vestry's and that the Quaker lot lies to the south-east. What it does not settle: where the lot lies today; no street or lot number is named. Next: Aull's own deeds out and the Quaker lot's owner. Update Oct. 15, 2026: a pencil working plat of this lot is in the Survey Papers, 'York Road No. 5' (720:msa-ce71-283-p59-aull-lot-plat-old-york-road): the same courses, closing within 0.3 perch, with a corner building, lots in feet and a 40-ft street.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 3692, folios 300 to 301 (MSA CE 168-3700; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 300 to 305: the deed opens at the head of 300 under the index heading 'Lulie H. Wallace, deed to James M. Sinclair' and ends at the top of 301; the instruments after it on 301 to 305, Parks to Levy, Levy's mortgage, Ripple to Ripple and Bachmann's mortgage, are unrelated). Dated Jan. 6, 1921 and acknowledged the same day in Washington before the notary Alfred H. Mori; received for record Jan. 18, 1921 and recorded the same day (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Grantor: Lulie H. Wallace, a widow of Washington. Grantee: James M. Sinclair. Price $1,250. The lot: begins on the east side of the York Turnpike 204 ft 7 in south of the two-mile stone in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot (281 ft 2 in south of the north side of Bateman's Alley, a four-foot alley), runs south along the turnpike 58 ft 4 in to the south-west corner of the whole ground of which it is a part, north 89 degrees east 8 ft 6 in to the north-west side of the Old York Road, up that side north 31 1/2 degrees east 66 ft, and west 42 ft 4 in to the beginning. It is, word for word in its measurements, the 'firstly described' 3011 lot of the 1995 deed (S.E.B. 4810/135) and the 1954 mortgage (M.L.P. 9513/64). 'Being the same lot of ground which by lease dated April 18th 1898 and recorded ... in Liber R.O. No. 1730 folio 92 &c. was demised by Augustus D. Clemens Jr. and wife to Jacob H. Aull for the renewable term of ninety nine years', rent $75 a year in half-yearly installments on May 1 and November 1; Wallace's title is the deed of William Hall Wallace to her dated April 1, 1907 (R.O. 2320/441). She conveys 'especially the right to collect the rent', in fee, to Sinclair 'to the end and intent that the leasehold interest created by the lease aforesaid shall be forever merged and extinguished': the leasehold was already Sinclair's, so the sale of the reversion ended the ground rent in 1921. What it settles: the chain behind the Sinclair holdings of the tip: Clemens Jr. leased the 3011 lot to Jacob H. Aull on April 18, 1898 (the day of the Clemens-to-Fink deed of the 3013 lot, R.O. 1729/241); the leasehold passed to Sinclair by Clemens's 1906 assignment (R.O. 2292/410, loaded for Jeff, not read) and the reversion, by way of William Hall Wallace and Lulie H. Wallace, in 1921: the 'Lulie H. Wallace's deed of the 3011 reversion' of the chapter's hop list. It also shows the lessee of 1898, Jacob H. Aull, bore the name of the Jacob Aull who bought the 2 a 29 P north of Leitzinger from the Biays couples in 1847 and 1848 (rows 46152 and the 1848 deed): a son or grandson is likely and no document read says so. The $75 rent of 1898 ended with this merger. The $66 rent on 3011 that every deed from 1954 to 2017 carries is a different, later lease (made Aug. 2, 1954, row 46095), and the 1927 deeds treat 3011 as fee simple (row 46110). What it does not settle: how the ground came to Clemens Jr. (the Miller deed of 1897 and the Baden, Tredway and Ensor lines remain the route above him) and where the rent of 1921 to 1927 went after the Sinclairs' 1927 pass-through (rows 46110, 46111). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the reversion's earlier holders are read: Clemens to Lulie H. Wallace (Apr. 18, 1898, the end of the deed on R.O. 1730/92, probable), Lulie to William Hall Wallace (Aug. 11, 1898, R.O. 1748/566), and back to Lulie (Apr. 1, 1907, 720:mdlr-ro2320-441-william-hall-wallace-lulie-wallace-3011-reversion-1907). The 1898 Aull lease is read (720:mdlr-ro1730-92-clemens-aull-lease-3011-1898): $75, May and November.

'Being the secondly described lot of ground which by Deed of even herewith ... was conveyed by Bertha F. Keil and others to the said W. Harry Holmes': Holmes bought a two-lot parcel from the Keils on the day he sold this lot to Sinclair, so the Keil deed is the straw deed or the true source of 3013 before 1919 (folios not on file, probably the pages just before 260). What it settles: the 3013 hop 'W. Harry Holmes's deed of 3013' is read, and the 3013 line now runs Clemens Jr. to William L. Fink (1898, R.O. 1729/241, row 46109) to ... Bertha F. Keil and others, to Holmes, to Sinclair (1919); the Fink-to-Keil step and the Keil deed's folios are the open links. Together with the 1921 Wallace deed (720:mdlr-scl3692-300-wallace-sinclair-3011-reversion-1921) it shows James M. Sinclair assembled both tip lots in two years, and the 3011 lot (204 ft 7 in from the stone) begins exactly where 3013 (190 ft 7 in plus 14 ft) ends: the two lots adjoin along the turnpike. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Fink deeds S.C.L. 2559/393 and 3126/290 read): the open links on this row are read. The 'Keil deed' of Feb. 7, 1919 is S.C.L. 3311/297 (row 47367); William L. Fink's heirs took 3013 under his will (Wills S.R.M. 82/278, recited), Frederick Fink's share went to his sisters on Feb. 9, 1910 (S.C.L. 2559/393, 720:mdlr-scl2559-393-frederick-fink-mary-catherine-bertha-estella-four-lots-3013-1910), and Mary Catherine Fink's third went to Estella and Sigmund Himmelmann on May 1, 1917 (S.C.L. 3126/290, 720:mdlr-scl3126-290-mary-catherine-fink-himmelmann-3013-and-five-limond-place-lots-1917). The 3013 line is now Clemens Jr. (1898), Fink, his four children, the three sisters (1910), the Kiels and Himmelmanns (1917 and 1919), Holmes and Sinclair (1919).

summary: Three instruments and a release, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. 6544, folios 521 to 525 (MSA CE 168-6552; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 521 to 526; page 521 opens with the acknowledgment of the Moser deed, which begins on an earlier page, and 525 to 526 end with the release and then an unrelated deed, Rogers to Pelikan, 101 and 103 N. Bradford St.). All dated Dec. 20, 1943 and recorded Dec. 27, 1943 at 1:20 to 1:23 p.m. (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk). (1) Deed: John E. Minor and Edythe D. Minor convey Charles F. Obrecht in fee, for $5, the 3013 lot, which Minor had taken from Simon Moser and wife by a deed 'of even date recorded immediately prior'. (2) Lease: Charles F. Obrecht and Alice F. Obrecht lease the same lot back to Minor for 99 years from Dec. 20, 1943 at one cent a year if demanded, renewable forever for a $10 fine, with taxes on the lessee only while he holds the title ('the Lessee ... shall be liable for and shall pay the taxes ... only during the period of time when he the said lessee is vested with title'). (3) Purchase-money mortgage: Minor to the Obrechts, $1,000 borrowed 'as part of the purchase money', $250 every six months at 4 percent. (4) Release: the Obrechts release 'the within mortgage' Feb. 18, 1946, recorded Feb. 19, 1946. What it settles: the 'Minor to Obrecht sale-leaseback of 3013' of the hop list is read, and how the one-cent leasehold of the 1974 deeds arose: Obrecht kept the fee (the 'reversion' he deeded to Samuel G. Silen on Aug. 24, 1954, M.L.P. 9566/461, row 46099) and Minor held a 99-year renewable lease at one cent, which he assigned to Max Silen in 1954 (row 46098). The effect: Obrecht holds the fee and a $1,000 mortgage, Minor a renewable leasehold at one cent; the instruments do not say why this form was used. The Moser deed itself and Moser's own source are not read. What it does not settle: why the structure was used; who Simon Moser was; whether the one-cent rent was ever demanded. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the Moser deed that begins this sale-leaseback is read (720:mdlr-mlp6544-520-moser-minor-3013-1943): Simon and Helena J. Moser to John E. Minor, Dec. 20, 1943, from James M. Sinclair and wife's deed of Nov. 23, 1938 (M.L.P. 5874/532).

summary: Corporation mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. 9513, folios 64 to 66 (MSA CE 168-9521; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 64 to 69: 64 to 66 are this mortgage, 67 to 69 an unrelated release to J. Louis and Augusta M. Frindt). Dated June 19, 1954; the Webers and Placks are the three buyers of 3011 from Elizabeth McC. West by a deed of the same date ('recorded immediately prior', folio not on file), and borrow $10,000 from the Belair Road Building and Loan Association as 'balance of the purchase money'; recorded June 24, 1954 (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk). It describes 3011 by the courses of the 1927 Sinclair deed (S.C.L. 4707/12): the apex of the fork, where the east side of Greenmount Avenue, 66 ft wide under Ordinance 129 of 1898, meets the north-west side of the Old York Road, then north 58 ft 4 in along the avenue, east 42 ft 4 in, south-west 66 ft along the old road and 8 ft 6 in back to the beginning (the same measurements as the 1921 and 1995 deeds, now on the 1898 street line). The habendum clause's printed leasehold wording ('during the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein, with the right and benefit of renewal') is typed over with 'in fee simple' and a row of X's, so the Webers and Placks mortgaged a FEE SIMPLE estate on June 19, 1954; the $66 leasehold of 3011 was created six weeks later by their lease to Elizabeth McC. West of Aug. 2, 1954 (row 46095). The mortgage requires weekly payments of $6.65 for taxes, water rent, ground rent and insurance (a printed clause). What it settles: the June 19, 1954 mortgage that the Belair Road Association released on Aug. 2, 1954 (M.L.P. 9546/146, row 46097) is read, so the sequence of 1954 is closed: June 19 West to the Webers and Placks (deed not on file) and this mortgage (recorded June 24); Aug. 2 the Webers and Placks lease it to West, West assigns Max Silen the leasehold and the Association releases (rows 46095 to 46097). What it does not settle: the West deed of June 19, 1954 and how Elizabeth McC. West came to hold 3011 (from the Sinclair estate, OLD48532, or the Riepe line of 1927; the Register of Wills file would say).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Circuit Court land records, Liber S.E.B. 4810, folios 135 to 137 and the deed of trust that follows on 140 (MSA CE 164-4810; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 135 to 140: the deed is 135 to 136, Exhibit A is 137, 138 is the recording stamps, 139 the State intake sheet and 140 the first page of the deed of trust). Dated April 4, 1995; recorded April 7, 1995 per the clerk's stamp and SDAT (the stamp is hard to read). Grantors: Irvin Silen and Samuel G. Silen. Grantee: the People's Community Health Center, Inc. Price $68,000. Two lots: the firstly described is 3011 (the tip lot at the fork, 58 ft 4 in on the avenue), a leasehold (the lease of Aug. 2, 1954, row 46095), 'with the benefit of renewal forever, subject to the payment of the annual rent of Sixty-Six Dollars ($66.00) payable half-yearly on the second days of February and August'; the secondly described is 3013, whose leasehold and reversion the grantors hold and convey together 'in fee simple', the reversion having come to Samuel G. Silen from the Obrechts on Aug. 24, 1954 (M.L.P. 9566/461, row 46099). Both leaseholds were acquired by the Silens by deed of June 6, 1974 from the personal representatives of the estate of Reba Silen (R.H.B. 3133/39, row 39579). The deed says 3011 and 3013 are 'not single family dwellings' under Article XIII of the City Code. Exhibit A gives both lots by their present courses: 3011 from the apex of the fork north 58 ft 4 in along the avenue (66 ft wide under Ordinance 129 of 1898), east 42 ft 4 in, south-west 66 ft along the old road and 8 ft 6 in back; 3013 from 190 ft 7 in south of the two-mile stone (267 ft 2 in south of Bateman's Alley), 14 ft, 42 ft 4 in, 15 ft 2 1/2 in and 48 ft 3 in. The State intake sheet shows a second document, the purchaser's $40,000 deed of trust (indexed under Robert A. Williams and Deborah A. Epps, with Harbor Federal Savings Bank), whose first page is 140. What it settles: the 1995 sale that Corridor knew only from SDAT (rows 7410, 720:sdat-09034076A001-s2) is read, on the real date: the puzzle of 'the Silen deed of even date' in the 2007 Provident deed of trust (F.M.C. 9050/264) most likely carries this deed forward in a misdated recital: the People's Community Health Center bought in 1995, so a second Silen deed to it in 2007 is not expected. It also settles the estate conveyed in 3013: fee simple, by the 1995 merger of the leasehold and reversion in one grant. What it does not settle: where the 1995 deed of trust was released (no release is in Corridor), and whether the two 1974 leaseholds of R.H.B. 3133/39 are the leasehold of 3011 at $66 and the one-cent lease of 3013 (the deed says 'both leaseholds').

The property: 3011-3013 Greenmount Avenue, Ward 09 Section 03 Block 4076A Lot 001, 'one being leasehold and the other being in fee simple', the 1995 lots, with the $66 rent on the firstly described (3011) lot. summary: Trustees' deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 2290, folios 225 to 227 (MSA CE 168-2298; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 225 to 230: the deed is 225 to 227, where Harvey's mortgage to the trustees begins and runs on through 230 and beyond, not pulled beyond 230). Dated Nov. 22, 1906; acknowledged the same day before the notary Harry L. Drake; received for record Nov. 22, 1906 at 1:35 p.m. and recorded the same day (Robt. Ogle, Clerk). Grantors: Richard H. Woollen, Howard P. Sadtler and S. Procter Brady, trustees; grantee James W. Harvey. Price $200,000: the deed recites the sale of Oct. 17, 1906, its ratification by the Circuit Court, and $30,000 paid, the $170,000 balance being secured by Harvey's mortgage of the same day. The decree it recites is NOT the Feb. 21, 1895 decree in Brady v. Sadtler that Corridor carries: it is a decree of May 23, 1899 in a cause between 'Martha A. Woollen et al., plaintiffs, and Nannie H. Stump et al., defendants' (Docket A 51-1899), by which the Court 'assumed jurisdiction of the trust created by the twelfth clause of the will of Samuel Brady, deceased' and appointed these three trustees to sell. The tract: bounded by Hunter Alley (west), the centre line of 28th Street, the centre line of Guilford Avenue, the centre line of 29th Street, the road formerly Gilmor Lane (the present Vineyard Lane) and an irregular line along the outline of the Brady land on W. H. Shipley's plat of March 1889 (the 1877 plan's 'Saml. Brady Est.') to 26th Street, a block of land between York Road and the lane, with the York Road frontage from 29th Street to 51 feet south of 28th Street among its edges. It excepts 'the seven brick houses on the York road' (built by John W. S. Brady on the land immediately adjoining the tract on the north, facing the York Road, with their land) and 'the lot at the northwest corner of York road and Twenty-ninth Street fronting fifty feet on York road'. Title: Gilmor to Samuel Brady, Apr. 24, 1849 (A.W.B. 412/283); Walter T. Allender, trustee, to Samuel Brady, Nov. 30, 1848 (A.W.B. 404/533, the Chancery sale read as row 46149: so the County deed the 2958 chapter reads is the root of this tract); Francis E. Yewell and wife to John W. S. Brady, trustee, Nov. 11, 1896 (R.O. 1647/561); and the Peabody Heights Company to the trustees, Feb. 24, 1906 (R.O. 2212/510). What it settles: (1) the 1906 sale of the Brady tract is the deed the Old Oriole Park dossier listed as an open item; it is to James W. Harvey, not 'Harvey & Son', and the price is $200,000. (2) The Brady estate sold in 1906 was in the hands of Woollen, Howard P. Sadtler and S. Procter Brady under the 1899 decree: Charles Herbert Sadtler and the 1895 decree are not named. (3) The ground behind the Allender-to-Brady deed (A.W.B. 404/533) was still the Brady estate's in 1906, with the 'seven brick houses on the York road' just north of it: the row of about 1900 that the 2958 chapter carries as an inference. (4) 'Gilmor lane' is the old name of Vineyard Lane, the lane at the corner of 3026. What it does not settle: which of the seven brick houses are today's 2900 block lots (the deed gives no numbers); the 1895 decree itself (Brady v. Sadtler), which is not recited; the 1899 decree's papers (Docket A 51-1899, Baltimore City Superior Court equity). Update Oct. 13, 2026: the first of the four title deeds recited here is read (2332:mdlr-awb412-283-gilmor-brady-1849): William Gilmor and wife Louisa A. to Samuel Brady, Apr. 24, 1849, A.W.B. 412/283, part of Huntington beginning at the large red oak, 12 acres 2 roods 19 1/5 perches, $3,500, recorded Apr. 28, 1849. The recital's date, book and folio are right. Update Oct. 14, 2026: both deeds it recites are read: Yewell to John W. S. Brady, 1896 (half the bed of Gilmor's Lane north of 29th, formerly Holmes, Street; 714:mdlr-ro1647-561-yewell-brady-trustee-gilmor-lane-bed-1896) and the 1906 exchange with the Peabody Heights Company between Calvert Street and Guilford Avenue (714:mdlr-ro2212-510-brady-trustees-peabody-heights-exchange-1906), which names the cause as Martha A. W. Woollen et al. v. Nannie H. Stump et al. Neither touches the Greenmount frontage.

summary: Purchase-money mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 2290, opening at folio 227 and running through 230 (MSA CE 168-2298, pages 225 to 230; the mortgage continues past 230, so its acknowledgment, recording stamp and any release are not read). James W. Harvey, the buyer, mortgages the whole tract back to the three trustees for the $170,000 balance of the price: two notes, $10,000 due Oct. 17, 1907 without interest, and $160,000 due Oct. 17, 1909 at 5 percent from Oct. 17, 1908. He may prepay and have land released at the capitalization of $3.50 a front foot until 2,000 front feet are paid for and $3.00 after that, the front measured along Guilford Avenue, Barclay Street and the York Road to the centre lines of the blocks on 'said plat' (the W. H. Shipley plat of March 1889); the $10,000 note does not count toward the releases. The mortgage names the sale 'ratified on or about the 22nd day of November 1906'. What it settles: how the Brady estate was sold in lots: Harvey paid $30,000 down and bought the whole $200,000 tract on credit, with a release schedule by front foot, so that lots sold on from Harvey (such as Hanlon's, the same day, R.O. 2290/355) could be freed from the trustees' lien by paying the per-foot price; this is the mechanism behind 'Hanlon is sole owner' and the Harvey resales of 1907. What it does not settle: the release of Hanlon's lot (no release is on the pages pulled), the mortgage's later folios and the sale of the remainder of the tract.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 2290, folios 355 to 356 (MSA CE 168-2298 p.355 to 360; the deed opens at 355 under the index heading 'James W. Harvey &c, deed to Edward Hanlon' and ends on 356, where the next instrument, Goldstein to Stockdale, begins; 357 to 360 are other deeds and mortgages of Nov. 22, 1906). Dated Nov. 22, 1906; acknowledged the same day before a notary; received for record Nov. 22, 1906 at 3:40 p.m. (two hours after the trustees' deed to Harvey, recorded at 1:35 p.m.) and recorded the same day (Robt. Ogle, Clerk). Grantors: James W. Harvey and his wife Maude T. Harvey; grantee: Edward Hanlon; price: 'five dollars and other valuable considerations', no sum. The lot: begins where the west side of the York Road meets the centre line of 29th Street, runs west along that centre line 390 ft 9 in to the east side of Barclay Street and 33 ft more to Barclay's centre, south along Barclay's centre line 541 ft to a point 40 ft 10 in south of the south side of 28th Street, east by a straight line 423 ft 9 in to the west side of the York Road, and north along the York Road 549 ft 3 in to the beginning: a block of ground of about 549 ft by 424 ft (roughly 5.3 acres by my count of the courses). It is 'part of the whole tract' the trustees sold Harvey the same day. What it settles: Ned Hanlon took the ballpark lot on Nov. 22, 1906, the same day as Harvey's purchase, not on Nov. 27 as the dossier and Corridor row 11603 have it, and the deed states no price (the roughly $50,000 is the newspapers' figure); the grantee is 'Edward Hanlon'. The Brady-Sadtler-Hanlon chain of the Old Oriole Park dossier is therefore closed at the deed: Brady estate trustees (R.O. 2290/225) to Harvey to Hanlon, all Nov. 22, 1906, and the lot lies south of the centre line of 29th Street, running down the York Road past 28th Street to 40 ft 10 in beyond it; the Harvey mortgage's release schedule at $3.50 a front foot (row on this property) is how Hanlon's lot would have been freed. What it does not settle: which ball ground this is on the ground (the 1901 American League Park, Oriole Park IV, or the grounds of the later park): the deed names only streets, York Road, Barclay Street, 28th and 29th Streets; the release of Hanlon's lot from the trustees' mortgage; and Hanlon's 1908 and 1909 transactions with the White syndicate and the Sadtler estate.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. 9513, folios 58 to 60 (MSA CE 168-9521; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 58 to 63: 58 to 60 this deed, 61 to 63 the next one, West to the Webers and Placks; the Belair Road mortgage that follows begins at 64). Dated June 19, 1954; acknowledged the same day before Dennis P. Murphy, notary; received for record June 24, 1954 and recorded the same day (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk). Adam H. Weber and Virginia Weber, his wife, of Baltimore City, convey Elizabeth McC. West, for $5 and other considerations, in fee simple, the 3011 lot described by the 1927 courses (S.C.L. 4707/12: from the apex of the fork north 58 ft 4 in along the avenue at its 66-foot line of 1898, east 42 ft 4 in, south-west 66 ft along the Old York Road and 8 ft 6 in back). The deed recites that the lot is the one conveyed to the grantor by Ena Gambrill Sinclair, unmarried, Dorothy Melville Sinclair, unmarried, and James Edward Sinclair and Pauline S. Sinclair, his wife, by a deed of the same date recorded immediately before (folios 55 to 57, not pulled). What it settles: where the Webers and Placks got 3011: from four Sinclairs, named by their given names (presumably the children of James M. and Ena M. Sinclair, who held both tip lots from 1919 to 1927 and in fee, though no instrument read says the relationship) by a deed of June 19, 1954 to Adam H. Weber alone; and the pass-through that followed on the same day: Weber to West (this deed), West to Henry John Weber, Adam H. Weber and Raymond H. Plack (next row), then their Belair Road mortgage (row 46163). The device converts the title of one buyer, Adam Weber, into co-ownership with two others as tenants in common, using West as the straw. What it does not settle: the Sinclair-to-Weber deed itself (price and date of death of the Sinclairs' parents), and whether the Sinclairs held 3011 in fee after 1927 or under the Aull 'rent' arrangements that ended in 1921. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the deed before this one is read (720:mdlr-mlp9513-54-sinclairs-weber-3011-1954, M.L.P. 9513/54): Ena Gambrill and Dorothy Melville Sinclair and James Edward and Pauline S. Sinclair (of Carmel Valley, California) to Adam H. Weber, June 19, 1954, $5 and other considerations, recorded June 24. And Elizabeth McC. West, the grantee here, is a notary public on page 52 of the same volume (the Holmes mortgage to the Belair Road Building and Loan Association, J. Calvin Carney agent, recorded June 24, 1954 at M.L.P. 9513/50): she is notary and witness on a mortgage J. Calvin Carney handled, so the 'straw' in the pass-through was probably someone in the lawyer's office (an inference).

Dated June 19, 1954, acknowledged the same day, recorded June 24, 1954 (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk). Elizabeth McC. West conveys Henry John Weber (of Baltimore County), Adam H. Weber and Raymond H. Plack (of Baltimore City), as tenants in common, in fee simple, the same 3011 lot by the same courses. These three are the mortgagors of the $10,000 Belair Road mortgage that follows at folio 64 (row 46163, whose description says the lot is 'the same ... described in a Deed from Elizabeth McC. West to Henry John Weber, Adam H. Weber and Raymond H. Plack bearing even date herewith'). What it settles: the straw. Elizabeth McC. West took 3011 from Adam H. Weber and gave it to him and two others on the same day: she is the pass-through and never owned it for more than a moment, which answers the chapter's question of how West came to hold the lot in the August 2, 1954 sale (rows 46095 and 46096): she held it as lessor of the 99-year lease and assignor to Max Silen only because the three buyers had put her in the chain. The Webers and Placks bought from the Sinclairs and mortgaged for $10,000 the same day. What it does not settle: why the title went through West and why the buyers leased the lot to her on Aug. 2, 1954 (row 46095).

It is 'the same lot of ground described in a deed dated November 23, 1938 ... in Liber M.L.P. No. 5874 folio 532', granted by James M. Sinclair and wife to the Mosers. What it settles: the missing first step of the 1943 sale-leaseback: the Mosers owned 3013 from Nov. 23, 1938 to Dec. 20, 1943, and they bought it from James M. Sinclair and wife (so the Sinclairs sold the 3013 lot in 1938 and kept 3011 until their heirs sold it to the Webers in 1954). Dated Dec. 8, 2006; the City transfer-tax stamp is dated Dec. 20, 2006 ($150); the recording stamp is not legible on the pages saved. John T. Spellman III, 'surviving joint tenant', conveys John M. Watkins, for $50,000, the 3026 corner house: 15 feet on the west side of Greenmount Avenue at the north side of Vineyard Lane ('formerly Gilmor Lane'), 82 feet deep to a four-foot alley, with 10 ft 7 in on the alley. Title: Jon F. Oster to Helen P. Spellman and John T. Spellman III as joint tenants, Jan. 13, 1967 (J.F.C. 2173/9); Helen P. died on or about Aug. 4, 1981, leaving the survivor the whole. What it settles: the deed behind the 2007 Watkins-to-Clerge sale (row 39540, F.M.C. 9256/107, which recites it as 'FMC 8778, folio 605'), and the end of the Spellman family's ownership (about ninety years by the Sun's report of the 1917 purchase from Jacob H. Aull, rows 42218 and 42227): the Spellmans held 3026 from 1917; the house passed from John T. Spellman Jr. (the plumber) to the pair of Helen P. and John T. Spellman III in 1967 by Oster, so the 1967 deed is a buy-in by the family, not an inheritance, and the house was sold for $50,000 in 2006, then for $140,000 three months later (Watkins to Clerge, Mar. 23, 2007) and $145,000 in 2010. A name to carry: Jacob H. Aull sold the corner house to John T. Spellman Jr. in 1917 (Sun, Feb. 18, 1917, subject to the $72 ground rent) and is the lessee of 3011 under Clemens Jr.'s 1898 lease (row 46160): no document read says they are the same man. What it does not settle: the Oster deed of 1967, the date of the 2006 recording, and the 1912 ground rent's end. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1967 deed this recites is read (725:mdlr-jfc2173-9-oster-spellman-joint-tenants-1967): a straw round trip from Helen P. Spellman, widow, through Jon F. summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber A.W.B. 382, folios 30 to 32 (MSA CE 66-432; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 30 to 34: the deed opens at the top of 30 under the index heading 'Jacob Hoke & wife & others, Deed to William T. Wilson' and ends on 32, where an unrelated deed follows, Columbus O'Donnell and Richard S. Stewart, trustees, to the Mayor and City Council of a Fells Point strip). Dated June 10, 1847, acknowledged the same day before Jno. W. Stump and Windham Spurrier, Justices of the Peace for Baltimore City, with the four wives examined apart from their husbands; received for record June 17, 1847 at 2 p.m. and recorded the same day (A. W. Bradford, Clerk). Grantors: Jacob Hoke and Nancy, Henry Hammond and Frances I. (Fanny), Henry N. Bowerman and Elizabeth, Walter T. Allender and Hannah Jane, the four Biays daughters and their husbands, the Hoke and Hammond couples of Harford County; grantee William T. Wilson; price $750, receipted by all eight. The parcel: part of 'Ensor's Inspection', beginning on the west side of the York Turnpike 'at a stone planted at the end of the first line of the land conveyed by Sarah Biays and others to David Mumma' on Nov. 9, 1844 (A.W.B. 354/374, the Mumma lot read earlier); west 17 perches along Mumma's second line to a free stone, 'the end of said line and the beginning of the land lately sold to the said William T. Wilson by Walter T. Allender Trustee'; then along that land's first line south 46 degrees east 22.4 perches to the west side of the Turnpike; then north 3 1/2 degrees east along the road 15 1/2 perches to the beginning; 3/4 acre and 11 square perches (the three sides, 17, 22.4 and 15.5 perches, close as a triangle of about 131 square perches, which agrees with the stated area). Title: the 1822 McFadon deed to Stump and Philip G. Biays in trust for Sarah Biays (W.G. 165/492), which the trustee carried out by his deed of Oct. 28, 1845 to the four daughters (A.W.B. 359/136). What it settles: (1) this is the first of the two deeds the Keelty deed of 1907 calls 'the two following deeds' by which William T. Wilson senior took his lots (row 46084, R.O. 2302/43, whose 'south forty six degrees east twenty two and four tenths perch line' is this deed's second line): the other is the Allender trustee's deed of Jan. 19, 1848 (A.W.B. 391/169, next row). (2) The same four Biays couples sold John Leitzinger two parts of Ensor's Inspection on the same day, June 10, 1847 (rows 46151 and 46153, A.W.B. 381/477 and 475), and bound themselves to convey Jacob Aull 2 a 29 P east of the turnpike on May 1, 1847 (46152): the same four couples sold Wilson and Leitzinger on one day. (3) The land is the McFadon trust ground of Ensor's Inspection that the four daughters took in 1845, the same source as the Leitzinger deed (row 46151). (4) The 1847 parcel lies along the turnpike, beginning at the end of the first line of the Mumma lot and running 15 1/2 perches (about 256 ft) of frontage south-southwest from it (the bearing along the road is north 3 1/2 degrees east, read from the far end back to the beginning), and its third line is the first line of the 1848 purchase (next row). What it does not settle: where on the avenue today the 1847 triangle sits (that needs the Mumma lot of 1844, A.W.B. 354/374, placed on the ground, and is a measurement, not a reading); who the 'Harford County' Hoke and Hammond couples were beyond what the deed says; and the lane (the later Gilmor Lane) that the 1907 deed measures to.

summary: Trustee's deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber A.W.B. 391, folios 169 to 171 (MSA CE 66-441; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 169 to 173). The top of 169 is the end of the deed just before it, folio 168 and on (not pulled), a second deed of the same day by the same trustee: it reads 'Walter T. Allender and Townsend Scott ... unto the said James Wilson', for land 'being the same land which by Indenture dated the thirteenth day of January eighteen hundred and three ... in Liber W.G. No. 74 folio 334 was granted and conveyed by Harry Dorsey Gough and wife to James Biays', 4 acres 2 roods 33 perches; this deed begins at the foot of 169 under the index heading 'Walter T. Allender, Trustee &c, Deed to William T. Wilson'. Dated Jan. 19, 1848; acknowledged the same day before J. Hanson Bell and Jno. W. Stump; received Jan. 20, 1848 at a quarter before 3 p.m. and recorded the same day (A. W. Bradford, Clerk); the margin shows it delivered to the grantee on Mar. 21, 1848; 171 then opens an Archibald Stirling deed to Thomas J. Gott (Jan. 19, 1848, $250). The Chancery cause: Walter T. Allender and wife, complainants, against William Jackson and others; decree on or about Apr. 2, 1847 ordering a sale and naming Allender trustee; public auction May 1, 1847, where Townsend Scott, bidding for William T. Wilson, bought this piece for $300 (Wilson paid it, with interest); sale ratified by the County Court. The parcel, part of Ensor's Inspection: beginning at a stone on the east side of a road two perches wide, at the end of the first line of Christopher Walker's 1801 deed to James Biays (W.G. 66/519, read in the next row); south 46 degrees east 22.4 perches along Walker's second line to the west side of the York Turnpike; north 81 degrees west 27 perches to the east side of the two-perch road; north 42 3/4 degrees east 14 perches along it to the beginning; 1 acre and 2 square perches, a part of Walker's land. The three sides, 22.4, 27 and 14 perches, close as a triangle of about 157 square perches, which agrees with the stated area. What it settles: (1) the second of the two Wilson deeds that Keelty's lease-origin deed of 1907 recites (row 46084 begins 'at the end of the south forty six degrees east twenty two and four tenths perch line of the land described in a deed from Walter T. Allender Trustee et al to William T. Wilson senior dated January 19th 1848 ... A.W.B. No. 391 folio 169', and refers to 'the north 81 degrees west 27 perch line of the Allender deed'): both lines are read here word for word, so the 2958 lot's County title is now two deeds on the page rather than a recital. (2) The piece is 'lately sold' to Wilson in the 1847 deed (previous row): the May 1, 1847 auction came before the June 10, 1847 deed, and the Allender deed was only delivered in January 1848. The 1848 land and the 1847 land share their line of south 46 degrees east, 22.4 perches, ending on the turnpike. (3) Allender, as trustee under the one decree of about Apr. 2, 1847, sold more than this piece on May 1, 1847: the Brady deed of Nov. 30, 1848 (A.W.B. 404/533, rows 46124 and 46149) recites the same decree and the same auction day, with Samuel Brady the bidder at $6,700, so the Brady tract and the Wilson piece were two lots of one Chancery sale, deeded ten months apart. What it does not settle: the cause papers (Allender v. Jackson, not online), which would say what was being divided; the first deed on 168 (to James Wilson, the Gough ground of 1803), which is not read; and why Scott, not Wilson, bid. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the defendant 'William Jackson' is very probably the trustee (or his heirs) of James Biays's 1802 trust for Sarah Biays and her children (W.G. 72/319, read: 714:mdlr-wg72-319-biays-trust-sarah-biays-1802), which held Walker's 3 3/8 acres; the four Biays daughters were the children who took the remainder at Sarah's death, so the Chancery sale cleared the trustee's legal title (inference).

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 66, folios 519 to 521 (MSA CE 66-116; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 519 to 523: the deed opens at the foot of 519 under the index heading 'Christopher Walker, Deed to James Biays', after the end of George Foss's assignment of a leasehold to Benjamin Mason, and ends on 521, where Leah Knysly's deed to Peter Frank begins). Dated Mar. 9, 1801, acknowledged the same day before Abraham Van Bibber and Richard Britton, with Patience Walker, the grantor's wife, releasing her dower; received for record May 4, 1801 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). Christopher Walker, of Baltimore County, sells James Biays, of Fells Point, 'all that part of a Tract of land ... called Ensors inspection' for $900 current money. The bounds: beginning at a stone north 43 3/4 degrees east 62 perches from 'a bounded red oak tree said to be the Beginning tree of a Tract of land called Huntington'; north 43 3/4 degrees east 24 perches along 'a Road leading to intersect the York Turnpike Road'; south 47 1/4 degrees east 22.4 perches 'to a stone standing in the York Road'; along the road south 1 degree west 30 perches; south 75 degrees west 3.7 perches; north 28 degrees west 1 perch to a stone; north 9 1/2 degrees west 27.2 perches; south 75 1/2 degrees west 18.3 perches; and by a straight line to the beginning; 3 3/8 acres. No ground rent, no lease: an outright sale in fee, no prior title recited. What it settles: (1) the 1848 Allender deed to Wilson (previous rows) names this deed as the source of its land ('a part of the land conveyed by Christopher Walker to James Biays by the deed above referred to') and its second line, south 46 degrees east 22.4 perches to the turnpike, is the second line of this one (south 47 1/4 degrees east 22 4/10 perches 'to a stone standing in the York Road': the same line, the bearing read 47 1/4 degrees in 1801 and 46 in 1848). So the Wilson-Keelty-2958 lots are ground James Biays bought of Walker in 1801. (2) This is the Biays purchase the Spear deed of May 30, 1801 (next row) adjoins: the Spear land ends 'at the end of the last line of a parcel of land conveyed by Christopher Walker to the said James Biays'. (3) The land is fixed to the tree each deed calls the beginning tree of Huntington (a 'bounded red oak' here and in the Spear deed, a 'large red oak' in Gilmor's deed to Samuel Brady, A.W.B. 412/283): very probably one tree, so Ensor's Inspection and Huntington are tied together here. What it does not settle: how Walker got the 3 3/8 acres (no title is recited), where the red oak stood in terms of a present street, and what the 'Road leading to intersect the York Turnpike Road' became (Gilmor Lane, the later Vineyard Lane, is a candidate, not a reading). Update Oct. 13, 2026: Walker's own deed is read (719:mdlr-wg63-161-foster-walker-1800): John Foster to Christopher Walker, Mar. 4, 1800, 29 acres from a stone 62 1/2 perches north 42 east of the Huntington red oak; the 1801 parcel begins at that stone and closes on Foster's last two courses, so it is the south-western corner of Walker's 29 acres. Update Oct. 14, 2026: within a year Biays put this land into a trust for his wife Sarah for life, then their children (Feb. 4, 1802, W.G. 72/319, read: 714:mdlr-wg72-319-biays-trust-sarah-biays-1802), with William Jackson, Levin Jones and John Smith as trustees. The 1847 Chancery case that sold part of it to Wilson was against 'William Jackson and others'.

Ensors Inspection' beginning 'at a Bounded Red oak tree (the Beginning of a tract ... called Huntington)'; south 47 degrees east 29 1/2 perches; north 50 degrees east 5.6 perches to a bounded white oak; north 33 3/4 degrees east 38 perches; north 70 degrees east 0.7 perch to the southwest corner of 'a Lot of ground which formerly belonged to John Gorsuch now the property of the said James Biays'; along that lot north 5 degrees 6 minutes west 27.1 perches 'to a stone standing at the end of the last line of a parcel of Land conveyed by Christopher Walker to the said James Biays'; along Walker's land north 52 1/2 degrees west 7.1 perches to the southeast side of a road, and along the road to the beginning; 9 7/8 acres. The title of the Spear daughters is not recited. What it settles: (1) James Biays had, by June 1801, assembled three adjoining pieces east of the Huntington red oak: the Gorsuch lot (not read here), Walker's 3 3/8 acres (previous row, bought Mar. 9, 1801) and these 9 7/8 acres of the Spear estate (May 30, 1801), all of Ensor's Inspection. (2) The Spear parcel starts at the very tree the Walker parcel is measured from (Walker's beginning stone is 62 perches north 43 3/4 east of it), and it closes on the end of Walker's last line, so the two fit together along a stone. (3) This is the Biays deed of the 'Brady route' of the next-hops list (W.G. 67/447); the others, 67/63, 76/243, 83/371 and 72/319, are not read. What it does not settle: how the Spear daughters took the land (William Spear's will or estate, not recited); the Gorsuch lot; and how the ground passed from Biays to Brady (the Brady title instead runs Gilmor 1849, A.W.B. 412/283, Huntington, and Allender 1848, A.W.B. 404/533, Ensor's Inspection). Update Oct. 14, 2026: William Spear also sold John Foster ground about Oct. 4, 1786, the source of Foster's 1800 sale to Walker and of the Walker's Tavern ground Biays bought in 1809 (719:mdlr-wg104-46-walker-biays-tavern-1809): both the Spear-heirs land and the tavern ground at the gate descend from William Spear. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 9 7/8 acres went into James Biays's trust for Sarah Biays and their children on Feb. 4, 1802 (714:mdlr-wg72-319-biays-trust-sarah-biays-1802). Update Oct. 14, 2026 (night): the Spear title is probably Job Garretson's deed to William Spear of Feb. 3, 1781, 46 acres of Ensor's Inspection from a Huntington tree (714:msa-c2843-15-p68-garretson-spear-ensors-inspection-1781). Update Oct. 15, 2026: the grandchild's share followed on Oct. 24, 1801 (714:mdlr-wg72-226-nicholas-spear-heir-biays-ensors-inspection-1801): Philip N. and Mary Nicholas, John Spear's only child, for $20, the same courses; 'N 5.6 W' is 5 degrees 6 minutes.

summary: Deed in trust, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 2445, folios 42 to 43 (MSA CE 168-2453; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 42 to 46: the deed opens at the foot of 42 under the index heading 'James F. Bowersox &c, Deed to Alice E. Bowersox, Trustee' and ends on 43, after the end of a deed of the same date, John Novak and wife to Shepherd and Eliza D. Owens, a Hoffman Street leasehold). Dated Aug. 1, 1908, acknowledged the same day before Robert H. Carr, a Justice of the Peace (as read); received for record Aug. 25, 1908 at about half past three in the afternoon and recorded the same day (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). The grantors, James F. and Mary E. Bowersox, who took the lease of the 14-foot lot from James Keelty on Aug. 24, 1907 (R.O. 2363/423, row 46085), convey it for $1 to Alice E. Bowersox as trustee (she is also one of the five beneficiaries named), 'the owners of a certain lot of ground ... which is occupied by them and their children as a home', so that 'no interest therein can be conveyed by those having interests therein during the lifetime of said grantors except by joint consent'. The lot is described by the 1907 courses (402 ft 9 1/2 in north of the northwest corner of 29th Street and the York Road, 14 ft on the avenue, 100 ft to a ten-foot alley) and named 'the same lot of ground described in a lease from James Keelty, bachelor, ... dated August 24th 1907 ... R.O. No. 2363 folio 423'; it is held 'subject to the payment of the annual ground rent of sixty-five dollars payable on the first day of March and September'. The use: during the lifetime of James F. and Mary E. or the survivor, 'for the use and benefit of the family now constituted', named as James F., Mary E., Alice E., Archibald and Clarence V. Bowersox; after both parents' deaths, to the children absolutely, 'as tenants in common share and share alike'. Special warranty only. What it settles: the missing 1908 step of the Edition 2 chain, which had only the recital in the Butzler deed of 1919 (S.C.L. 3459/370, row 46082): the Bowersoxes put the leasehold into a family trust less than a year after Keelty's lease, with the trustee being the Alice who appears as 'Alice E. Brandt (formerly Bowersox)' in the 1917 and 1919 deeds (rows 46087 and 46082). It also settles who the beneficiaries were: five named family members, of whom the three children are Alice, Archibald and Clarence V. The restraint on alienation ('except by joint consent') is consistent with the 1919 deed to Clara Butzler being signed by the whole family (trustee, father, the children and their spouses). What it does not settle: to whom the $65 rent was owed (the deed holds the lot 'subject to' it and says no more; the Armour deed of 1932, S.C.L. 5289/183, next row, shows the reversion was by then Sarah Stanley Armour's); and the exact minute of recording.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5289, folios 183 to 186 (MSA CE 168-5297; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 183 to 187: the deed opens in the middle of 183 under the index heading 'Sarah Stanley Armour &c, Deed to Henry Gerwig', after the end of a mortgage, and ends at the top of 186 with the acknowledgment taken at Cobourg, Ontario, and the recording stamp; 186 and 187 hold two later instruments, Cook and Jones, administrators of Marian J. M. Sims, to William L. Carter for a Vine Street leasehold, and Carter's mortgage back to the Adonis Building and Loan Association). Dated Mar. 12, 1932; acknowledged at Cobourg, County of Northumberland, Province of Ontario before T. K. Creighton, notary public; received for record Mar. 14, 1932 at 1:20 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Grantors: Sarah Stanley Armour (formerly Sallie H. Stanley) and her husband George Armour, of Cobourg; grantee Henry Gerwig, of Baltimore City, 'heretofore adjudged a lunatic', with William F. Gerwig as his committee ('Ex Parte in the matter of Henry Gerwig', Circuit Court No. 2 of Baltimore City, Docket 28 A folio 308), who by the Court's order of Mar. 10, 1932 was authorized to invest $4,516.67 of his funds in 'the four lots of ground hereinafter described together with the four annual ground rents issuing and payable thereout'. The four lots, all leasehold reversions: (1) 'No 2958 York Road', 14 by 100 ft, 402 ft 9 1/2 in north of the northwest corner of 29th Street, 'the same lot of ground described in a Lease from James Keelty to James F Bowersox and wife dated August 24th 1907 ... R O No 2363 folio 423', rent $65 a year, March and September, 'and BEING ALSO the same lot of ground described in a Deed from James G Stanley Trustee to the said Sarah Stanley Armour (she being therein named as Sallie H Stanley ...) dated November 4th 1908 ... SCL No 2460 folio 398'; (2) 4418 Wrenwood Avenue, $65 (Baltimore County lease of 1914); (3) 3624 Parkdale Avenue, $75 (1927 lease); (4) 502 East Lynn Street, $66 (1926 lease). The deed conveys each lot 'in fee simple ... subject however to the respective leasehold estates and terms of years' and the right to the four rents. What it settles: (1) who held the reversion, and so the $65 ground rent, of 2958 from late 1908 until 1961, as far as this deed goes: Sallie H. Stanley, by a trustee's deed of Nov. 4, 1908 (S.C.L. 2460/398), three months after the Bowersox trust and fourteen months after Keelty's lease; then Sarah Stanley Armour (the same woman, married, living at Cobourg, Ontario) until Mar. 1932; then Henry Gerwig, bought by his committee for his estate. (2) The fifteen grantors of the merger deed of July 15, 1961 (J.F.C. 1134/578, row 46088, which does not say who they were) are presumably Henry Gerwig's heirs: the 1965 lot list (next row) names the first grantor as Jacob F. Gerwig, widower, 'et al'. On that reading the reversion ran Keelty (before 1908) to a trustee, James G. Stanley, to Sallie H. Stanley (Armour), to Gerwig, to Gerwig's heirs, to the Silbigers, where it merged with the leasehold. (3) 2958 York Road is the first of four ground-rent lots bought together by a committee for a lunatic's estate, a purchase of four rents, not of four houses. What it does not settle: how the reversion went from James Keelty to James G. Stanley, trustee, before 1908 (S.C.L. 2460/398, not yet read); and who Henry Gerwig's heirs were beyond the names in the 1961 deed. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the gap is closed (714:mdlr-scl2460-398-stanley-trustee-sallie-stanley-1908): James Keelty sold the reversion to James G. Stanley, trustee, on Sept. 26, 1907 (R.O. 2371/148), and the trustee conveyed it to Sallie H. Stanley by court order on Nov. 4, 1908.
