summary: The opening pages of the Silbigers' deed to Straw Man, Inc., Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.F.C. 2008, folios 87 to 89 (MSA CE 168-12326, pages 85 to 88 on the scan Jeff saved: 85 and 86 are a different instrument, Straw Man, Inc.'s assignment of a Falls Road leasehold back to Jerome Silbiger, dated and recorded Dec. 28, 1965 at 2:11 p.m. (J.F.C. 2008/85); 87 and 88 are the deed's first two pages; 89 and the next deed were read earlier, rows 46105 and 46106). The deed, a printed fee-simple form stamped 'No title search performed, No consideration necessary' and 'Transfer tax not required', is dated Dec. 28, 1965; the grantee index is stamped Mar. 18, 1966. Jerome and Lillian Silbiger convey Straw Man, Inc., 'its successors and assigns', in fee simple, eleven lots 'described as follows' by their title deeds: Abbotston Street (three houses, one lot), 515 and 514 East 25th Street, 1762 Carswell Street, 2702-04 Harford Road, 1765 Abbottston Street, 2958 Greenmount Avenue, six concrete garages in the rear of Paine Street (marked 'unlocated' in the margin), two Falls Road lots and 2700 Harford Road. 'Lot #7' reads: 'the same lot of ground described in a Deed dated December 30, 1960 ... JFC 1004, Folio 488 ... granted and conveyed by Guiseppe Palladin ... unto the said Jerome Silbiger and Lillian Silbiger. See also Deed dated July 15, 1961 ... JFC 1134, Folio 578 ... granted and conveyed by Jacob F. Gerwig, widower, et al ... extinquishing said ground rent. The improvements thereon being now known as 2958 Greenmount Avenue.' Lots 5, 9 and 11 are subject to Equitable Trust Company mortgages and lot 10 to a Yorkridge Federal Savings and Loan mortgage; 2958 has no mortgage recited. What it settles: (1) row 46105 was 'probable' because the deed's lot list had not been read: Lot 7 now names 2958 Greenmount by number, so the Silbiger-to-Straw-Man deed of 2:10 p.m. does convey 2958 and is verified. (2) The deed repeats, in 1965, the two instruments that built the Silbigers' title: the 1960 purchase of the leasehold from Guiseppe Palladin (spelled here 'Palladin', 'wife', so the typed word after the name may be a slip for 'and wife'; the 1960 deed itself, row 46072, names Guiseppe and Adele Palladi) and the 1961 purchase of the reversion from Jacob F. Gerwig, widower, 'et al', 'extinquishing said ground rent': the merger of the ground rent is stated in the Silbigers' own deed. (3) Jacob F. Gerwig, widower, is the first-named grantor of the 1961 deed; the surname matches Henry Gerwig's, who bought the reversion in 1932 (S.C.L. 5289/183, previous row), which is the reason to read the 1961 grantors as his heirs. What it does not settle: why the Silbigers, whose eleven lots were not all mortgaged, put them through a corporation for a minute (the 2:10 and 2:11 p.m. stamps; a 'straw man' deed of this kind presumably turned the husband and wife's tenancy by the entireties into Jerome's sole ownership, and row 46107 puts the lots back into the entireties in 1969: an inference from the pattern, not a statement in the deeds); and the incorporation of Straw Man, Inc. Update Oct. 14, 2026: Straw Man, Inc. also appears in 1954, conveying 3014 Vineyard Lane to Harry W. and Bertha J. Hoover (M.L.P. 9509/244, recited in 1117:mdlr-jfc877-28-hoover-bordley-lease-1960): a conveyancing straw company used across Waverly, not the Silbigers' own (an inference).

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber A.W.B. 412, folios 283 to 285 (MSA CE 66-462; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 283 to 287: the deed opens at the foot of 283 under the index heading 'William Gilmor & Wife, Deed to Samuel Brady', after the end of a trust deed of John Glenn, trustee, and William Broadbent; it ends on 285, where William F. Johnson and others' deed to Walter T. Allender, for two Baltimore City lots at Chester and Pratt Streets and Duncan Alley, begins; 286 and 287 are later pages of that deed and others). Dated Apr. 24, 1849, acknowledged the same day before Henry F. Friese and John I. Snyder, Justices of the Peace, Louisa A. Gilmor examined apart from her husband; received Apr. 28, 1849 at 10 a.m. and recorded the same day (A. W. Bradford, Clerk). William Gilmor and his wife sell Samuel Brady, of Baltimore County, for $3,500, part of 'a tract of land called Huntington': beginning at 'a large red Oak tree, being the beginning tree of a resurvey called Huntington Surveyed the Sixteenth day of May Seventeen hundred and Ninety four'; south 47 1/4 degrees east 50 perches; south 15 3/4 degrees west 9 perches 17 links; south 41 1/4 degrees west 21 perches; north 80 1/4 degrees west 16 perches; north 48 3/4 degrees west 40 perches 10 links 'until it intersects a thirty foot road'; north 40 1/2 degrees east along that road 39 perches 5 links to the beginning; 12 acres 2 roods 19 1/5 perches. Title: John I. and Samuel I. Donaldson, trustees, and Eliza H. Emory, to Gilmor by a deed of June 9, 1845 (A.W.B. 355/275). What it settles: (1) the first of the four title deeds the Brady trustees' deed of 1906 names (row 46168: 'a deed from William Gilmor and wife to Samuel Brady dated April 24th 1849 and recorded ... A.W.B. No 412 folio 283'): the date, the book and the folio of the 1906 recital are right. (2) Samuel Brady's Huntington purchase of 1849 ($3,500, 12.6 acres) and his Ensor's Inspection purchase of Nov. 30, 1848 from the trustee Allender (A.W.B. 404/533, 19 a 38 P, $6,700, row 46149) were two separate tracts; they are two of the four title deeds of the 1906 sale, and the Huntington part came from Gilmor, not Allender. (3) A possible origin of the name of 'Gilmor Lane' (the later Vineyard Lane, called Gilmor's in the 1906 and 2006 deeds): Gilmor owned land on a thirty-foot road from 1845; the deed itself names no lane, so this is an inference, not a reading. (4) The 'large red oak ... beginning tree of a resurvey called Huntington' here is, very probably, the 'bounded red oak' that Walker's and the Spear heirs' parcels of 1801 are measured from (W.G. 66/519, 67/447), so Brady's 1849 land and the 1801 Biays land hang from one tree; the deeds do not say it is the same tree. What it does not settle: what Donaldson and Emory held (A.W.B. 355/275, not read), whether the 'thirty foot road' is the York Road-to-lane road of the 1801 and 1848 deeds, and which parts of Gilmor's twelve acres lie in the ball ground of 1906 (the 1906 deed says it covers 'all of the land belonging to the estate of Samuel Brady').

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. 5874, folios 532 to 533 (MSA CE 168-5882; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 532 to 536: 532 holds the partial release that precedes the deed and the deed's opening, 533 the rest of the deed and the Mosers' mortgage, 534 to 536 the mortgage's later pages and the next instruments). Dated Nov. 23, 1938, acknowledged the same day before a notary (Gershil Moss); recorded Nov. 25, 1938 at 12:02 p.m. (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk). James M. Sinclair and Ena M. Sinclair, his wife, convey Simon Moser and Helena J. Moser, his wife, 'as tenants by the entireties', in fee simple, for $5 and other considerations, 'No 3013 Greenmount Avenue': 190 ft 7 in southerly from the two-mile stone in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot, 267 ft 2 in southerly from Bateman's Alley, 14 ft on the avenue, 42 ft 4 in east, 15 ft 2 1/2 in northeast along the Old York Road, and 48 ft 3 in west, the courses of every later deed; it is 'the same lot of ground which by Deed dated March 1st 1927 was granted and conveyed by J. Holliday Riepe to the said Grantors ... S.C.L. 4707 folio 12'. Special warranty only. On the same page and recorded one minute before: The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County's partial release of Nov. 10, 1938 (signed by its vice-president, Henry Joesting Jr.) frees 'that lot of ground and premises secondly described' in the Sinclairs' mortgage of Apr. 15, 1930 (S.C.L. 5109/220) and 'thirdly described' in their mortgage of Apr. 7, 1934 (S.C.L. 5419), 'the property hereby intended to be released being known as No 3013 Greenmount Avenue', reserving the association's lien on the other lots in the mortgages. After the deed (533): the Mosers' $2,000 purchase-money mortgage of the same lot to Sara K. Sykes, Nov. 23, 1938, six percent, in ten notes (three of $250 at 18, 24 and 30 months, one of $1,250 at three years, and six interest notes). What it settles: (1) the 1938 deed behind the Moser deed of 1943 (row 46173, 'M.L.P. 5874/532') is read: Sinclair sold 3013 to the Mosers on Nov. 23, 1938, with Sinclair's title being the Riepe deed of 1927 (row 46111). (2) The Sinclairs had mortgaged the lots to the Waverly Building Association three times, May 1929, Apr. 15, 1930 and Apr. 7, 1934, and the 1938 release freed 3013 from the last two while the association kept its lien on the other lots (presumably 3011 among them): the full release of all three mortgages was not given until June 21, 1954, two days after the Sinclair children's deed to Weber (M.L.P. 9513/53 and 54, 3011, row 'Sinclairs to Weber'). (3) The Mosers' purchase was financed: a $2,000 purchase-money mortgage of the same day, then a $5 sale to Minor in Dec. 1943 and the sale-leaseback that followed (rows 46173, 46162). (4) The Sinclairs held 3013 from Feb. 7, 1919 (Holmes to Sinclair, row 46161) through the Riepe round trip of March 1927 (rows 46110 and 46111) until this sale in 1938, and kept 3011 until their heirs sold it in 1954. What it does not settle: the price (stated only as $5 and other considerations; the Mosers' mortgage calls its $2,000 'part of the purchase price'); who Simon Moser was (the 1943 deed, row 46173, is his sale to John E. Minor); and the folio of the 1934 mortgage (the 1938 and 1954 releases print it differently). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1930 and 1934 Sinclair mortgages are read (720:mdlr-scl5109-220-sinclair-waverly-bldg-mortgage-3011-3013-1930, 720:mdlr-scl5419-571-sinclair-waverly-bldg-mortgage-four-lots-1934); the 1930 one carries a margin note pointing to this liber and folio. The cited 1929 mortgage is not at S.C.L. 5005/541 (720:negative-scl5005-541-545-no-sinclair-1929-mortgage).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. 9513, folios 54 to 57 (MSA CE 168-9521; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 52 to 57: 52 is the end of a Holmes mortgage to the Belair Road Building and Loan Association, acknowledged before Elizabeth McC. West, notary public, J. Calvin Carney appearing for the association (recorded June 24, 1954, M.L.P. 9513/50); 53 is a release of mortgages; 54 to 57 the deed; the deed carries federal documentary stamps and Maryland recordation-tax stamps). Dated June 19, 1954; the two Baltimore grantors acknowledged it that day before Marguerite E. Wolf, notary public, and the two Californian grantors the same day at Carmel Valley before Irene I. Baldwin, notary public of Monterey County; witness Julius G. Maurer; received for record June 24, 1954 and recorded the same day (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk; block no. 4076). The firm on the form is J. Calvin Carney's, 3 East Lexington Street. The grantors: Ena Gambrill Sinclair and Dorothy Melville Sinclair, unmarried, of Baltimore, and James Edward Sinclair and Pauline S. Sinclair, his wife, of Monterey County, California; grantee: Adam H. Weber, of Baltimore City, for $5 and other considerations, in fee simple, the 3011 lot (from the end of the first line of the 'firstly described' lot of the 1927 deed J. Holliday Riepe to James M. and Ena M. Sinclair, S.C.L. 4707/12: 58 ft 4 in north along the east side of Greenmount Avenue at its 66-foot line of 1898), with special warranty only. Page 53, recorded the same day (M.L.P. 9513/53): The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County (Arthur C. Hershfeld, president; Lennox B. Clemens, notary) releases to James M. and Ena M. Sinclair, dated June 21, 1954, 'all those lots of ground described in three mortgages' of May 1929 (S.C.L. 5005), Apr. 15, 1930 (S.C.L. 5109/220) and Apr. 7, 1934 (S.C.L. 5419/571), the covenants performed and the whole sums paid. What it settles: (1) the first deed of the 3011 pass-through (rows 46171, 46172 and the Belair Road mortgage 46163 are the rest): Adam H. Weber bought 3011 from four Sinclairs, two unmarried Sinclairs of Baltimore and a married couple of Monterey County, California, presumably the children of James M. and Ena M. Sinclair (the deed gives the names and no relationship, and cites no estate record). The two Californian grantors acknowledged the same day in California, so the deed was signed at a distance and delivered in time for the same-day deeds. (2) The Waverly Building Association's three mortgages on the Sinclairs' lots (May 1929, Apr. 1930, Apr. 1934) were released as paid on June 21, 1954, two days after this deed, and the release was recorded the same day as the deed (June 24, 1954); the deed recites no mortgage on the lot. (3) Elizabeth McC. West, the straw woman of the same-day deeds (rows 46171 and 46172), appears on 52 as witness and notary public on a mortgage handled by J. Calvin Carney, whose office (3 East Lexington Street) is printed on this deed's form: the 'straw' was probably someone in that office (an inference). What it does not settle: the price; why Weber took title alone and then put the lot through West into three names; the relationship of these four to James M. and Ena M. Sinclair (an estate record would say); and the dates of death of the parents. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1930 and 1934 Sinclair mortgages it clears are read (720:mdlr-scl5109-220-sinclair-waverly-bldg-mortgage-3011-3013-1930, 720:mdlr-scl5419-571-sinclair-waverly-bldg-mortgage-four-lots-1934). Update Oct. 16, 2026: the Register of Wills online index has James M. Sinclair, Baltimore City estate OLD48532, died Jan. 6, 1948, no will (so the four Sinclair grantors of 1954 take as his heirs at law with Ena M.), and William L. Fink, OLD45631, died July 8, 1946, no will; both files are papers in folder only, with no images online.

Leight, of Baltimore City, as tenants in common, for $5 and other considerations, the lot on the west side of the York Turnpike Road 'now Greenmount Avenue', 36 ft south of the stone at the southwest corner of the Turnpike and Gilmore Lane, 67 ft 11 2/5 in on the road to the southern outline of 'the whole land formerly belonging to Mary Clemens', 215 ft west, 82 ft north to the southeast side of Gilmore Lane, 53 ft along the lane, 105 ft 6 in east to 'the end of the third line of the lot described in the sub lease from John D Nicholl to Lorenz Leight' (A.W.B. 394/156), and back by the sub-lease's third and second lines (38 ft and 76 ft 4 in): the 3010 lot, wrapped round the 3020 corner lot of Nicoll's sub-lease. It is 'the same lot of ground and premises firstly described in an assignment from C. Reese Dietrich to John Harmon Dietrich and Lulu S. Dietrich his wife dated May 6th 1927 ... S.C.L. No. 4735 folio 61', held for the residue of the term 'with the benefit of renewal ... forever', subject to the annual ground rent of $180 payable quarterly (Feb., May, Aug., Nov.); 'the said John Harmon Dietrich being now deceased'. Special warranty only. The mortgage that follows (439 to 441, recorded Nov. 19, 1927 at 11:42 a.m.): Wolfe and Leight to the York Road Building Association of Baltimore City, $6,500 advanced on fifty shares, 'part purchase money', the lot 'BEING the same ... described in a deed of even date from Lulu S Dietrich to the above named mortgagors', Louis M. Augustine, vice-president, making the consideration oath; a margin note reads 'For release of mtge. Date 4/24/31, Liber 5212 Folio 569'. What it settles: (1) the 1927 step that S.C.L. 5263/428 (rows 46089 and 46090) and the later Wolfe deeds only recite is read, and it corrects its spelling: the grantor is 'Lulu S. Dietrich', not 'Lula B. Dietrich' as the 1931 recital has it, and she is the widow of John Harmon Dietrich, with whom she had taken the lease by assignment from C. Reese Dietrich on May 6, 1927 (S.C.L. 4735/61, not read): so the Dietrichs held the lessee's side for about six months before Wolfe and Leight bought it. (2) The buyers financed it: $6,500 from the York Road Building Association, released about Apr. 24, 1931 (the margin note), six months before Wolfe and Leight passed the leasehold to Lula Smith and she to the two couples (Oct. 31, 1931, rows 46089 and 46090). (3) The deed is explicit that the 3010 lot's northern line is the third line of Nicoll's sub-lease to Leicht, so the 3010 lot was cut out of Mumma's lease ground around the 3020 corner. What it does not settle: how the lessee's term reached C. Reese Dietrich from Allen K. Wood (the 1901 lease, row 46108; no assignment between them is read); who C. Reese Dietrich and John Harmon Dietrich were (a relationship is not stated); the price (the deed's $5 is nominal; the mortgage was $6,500 on a 'part purchase money' basis); and the Montebello release above it (S.C.L. 4646/313), which names John H. Dietrich but no lot. Update Oct. 14, 2026: S.C.L. 4735/61 is read (719:mdlr-scl4735-61-c-reese-dietrich-dietrichs-1927): a straw round trip of May 6, 1927 (the Dietrichs to C. Reese Dietrich and straight back by the entireties), so the Dietrichs were already the lessees of 3010 before May 1927; the lot was then 'now known as No 3010 to 3016 Greenmount Avenue'.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5182, folio 192 (MSA CE 168-5190; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 192 to 196: the deed opens on 192 under the index heading 'Mary L Swormstedt &c, Deed to William H Wolfe &c', after the recording stamp of a previous instrument (Dec. 17, 1930 at 2:15 p.m.), and fills the page; 193 to 196 hold an unrelated Louis Earl Rice mortgage of Dec. 16, 1930 to the Real Estate and Improvement Company of Baltimore City, for a Mulberry Street lot, released Oct. 17, 1942). Dated Dec. 16, 1930; acknowledged the same day before Kathleen Meehan, notary public; witness Webster Bell; received for record Dec. 18, 1930 at 2:30 p.m. and recorded the same day (Stephen C. Little, Clerk); the grantee-index margin reads 'Jan. 21, 1931'. Mary L. Swormstedt and Martha Swormstedt, both unmarried, of Baltimore, convey William H. Wolfe and Carrie Wolfe, his wife, as tenants by the entirety, for $5 and other considerations, the 3010 lot (the courses of the 1927 deed, row above: 36 ft south of the Gilmor Lane corner, 67 ft 11 2/5 in on the avenue, 215 ft west, 82 ft north to the lane, 53 ft, 105 ft 6 in, and back by the third and second lines of Nicoll's sub-lease, A.W.B. 394/156), 'BEING the same lot of ground which by lease dated the 31st October 1901 ... R O No 1928 folio 77 was demised and leased by Mary Clemens and Augustus D Clemens Jr her husband unto Alan K Wood for the term of ninety-nine years at ... the annual rent of One hundred and eighty Dollars payable in quarterly installments on the first days of February May August and November', 'and being also the same lot which by deed dated the 30th of March 1927 ... SCL No 4728 folio 211 was granted and conveyed by Robert N Baer unto Mary L Swormstedt and Martha Swormstedt subject to the term of years aforesaid'. To hold 'the aforesaid rent payable out of said lot and the reversion thereto' in fee simple, 'subject however to the estate terms and interest of the said lessee'. Special warranty only. What it settles: (1) the deed Edition 2 listed as 'Deed of the reversion of the $180 rent to the Wolfes, presumably the Clemens heirs (the deed does not say)' is read, and the grantors are not Clemens heirs: Mary L. and Martha Swormstedt, two unmarried women of Baltimore, held the reversion by a deed of Mar. 30, 1927 from Robert N. Baer (S.C.L. 4728/211, not read), nine months before they sold it. (2) The reversion's chain is now: Mary and Augustus D. Clemens Jr., lessors in 1901 (row 46108); then Robert N. Baer, by a deed not read; then the Swormstedts (Mar. 30, 1927); then the Wolfes, as tenants by the entirety (Dec. 16, 1930); then Charles T. Leight, who bought the reversion on Oct. 24, 1950 for $3,000 and accrued rent (M.L.P. 8259/53, row 46093, which recites this deed). (3) While William H. Wolfe held the reversion with his wife from December 1930, he and Leight still held the leasehold by the 1927 assignment: on Oct. 31, 1931 they passed it through Lula Smith to the two couples (rows 46089 and 46090), so from late 1931 the Wolfes held both the reversion and half the leasehold. What it does not settle: how the reversion passed from the Clemens family to Baer (S.C.L. 4728/211 or an earlier deed would say); the price (nominal, $5); and the spelling of the 1901 lessee's first name (this deed types 'Alan K Wood'; the 1901 lease, row 46108, and the 1950 deed read 'Allen'). Update Oct. 14, 2026: S.C.L. 4728/211 is read (719:mdlr-scl4728-211-baer-swormstedt-1927): Baer was a straw; Richard Swormstedt et al. deeded him the $180 rent on Mar. 29, 1927 and he deeded it to Mary L. and Martha Swormstedt the next day, so the reversion was the Swormstedt family's before 1927. Update Oct. 14, 2026: how the Swormstedts held the rent is read (719:mdlr-scl4728-194-swormstedts-baer-3010-reversion-1927): Richard and Barbara C. Swormstedt bought it from John P. Clarke, executor, Dec. 16, 1903 (R.O. 2050/46), and their daughters took it in the 1927 partition.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 63, folios 161 to 163 (MSA CE 66-113; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 161 to 165: the top of 161 is the end of a deed of the same day from John Foster to Nicholas Foster, also for five pounds, with a certificate of Feb. 17, 1800 that its year was altered before signing; this deed opens at the foot of 161 under the index heading 'John Foster Deed To Christopher Walker' and ends at the top of 163, where William Aisquith's lease to Mabury Parks of a Coles Harbour lot follows). Dated and acknowledged Mar. 4, 1800 before Alexis Lemmon and John Garrett, justices, Ellenor Foster releasing dower; received July 21, 1800 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). John Foster sells Christopher Walker 'all that part of tract of Land called ... Ensors Inspection', 29 acres, for five pounds sterling: beginning at a stone north 42 degrees east 62 1/2 perches 'from a bounded red oak standing in an old field being a bounded tree of Huntington'; north 42 east 117 perches to a stone in a line of 'Grants Addition'; south 59 east 41 perches; south 27 west 13 perches to 'Loveless Addition'; along it north 58 west 3, south 52 west 38, south 58 east 20 and south 7 west 7 perches to the tract 'Darby'; along it north 66 west 36 perches to a bounded tree; south 15 west 53, south 26 1/2 west 16, north 8 west 27 1/2 and south 75 1/2 west 18 1/2 perches; and straight to the beginning. No earlier title is recited. What it settles: (1) the source of Walker's ground, which the 1801 deed to Biays (row 46179) and the 1813 Bolte mortgage (row below) both cut from: the Walker-to-Biays 3 3/8 acres of 1801 begin 62 perches north 43 3/4 east of the same red oak and close on two courses that are this deed's last two (north 9 1/2 west 27.2 and south 75 1/2 west 18.3 perches in 1801, north 8 west 27 1/2 and south 75 1/2 west 18 1/2 here), so the 1801 parcel is the south-western corner of these 29 acres; and the Bolte mortgage of 1813 runs to 'the end of the north forty two degrees east one hundred and seventeen perch line mentioned in the deed from said Foster to said Walker'. (2) Ensor's Inspection here adjoins Grants Addition, Loveless Addition and Darby (Darley Hall), the neighbours the 1754 certificate and the Hopkins plates name. What it does not settle: Foster's own title (none recited) and the Nicholas Foster deed above it (its land is on page 160, not pulled). Update Oct. 14, 2026: Foster's title, which this deed does not recite, is named in Walker's 1809 deed to Biays: 'by the said Foster purchased from William Spear by Deed on or about the fourth day of October' 1786 (719:mdlr-wg104-46-walker-biays-tavern-1809).

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 122, folios 133 to 136 (MSA CE 66-172; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 133 to 137: the top of 133 is the end of a Frederick County deed of John Dudderar to Conrod Dudderar, recorded the same day; the mortgage opens at the foot of 133 under the index heading 'James Biays Mortgage To John Bolte', ends on 136 with the list of notes, and is followed by an Ann Carson and Peter Green assignment to Henry Harrod of a Fells Point lot). Dated Feb. 4, 1813, acknowledged the same day before Saml. H. Gatchell and Matthew Bennet, witnessed by John Hanna; recorded Feb. 9, 1813 (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). James Biays, merchant, owes John Bolte, merchant, $13,930.73 on eighteen notes of Jan. 1, 1813 drawn in favour of and endorsed by John Hanna (at 7, 9 and 11 months, the amounts listed on 136), and mortgages him 'All that part ... of the tract ... called "Ensors Inspection" on which is situated the tenement called "Walker's Tavern"', part of Foster's land sold to Christopher Walker: beginning at 'a stone standing on the south east side of a road leading from the land of Hugh Thompson into the york turnpike road at or near the gate', marked B; north 40 1/2 east along that road to the turnpike and on across it, 94 3/4 perches in all, to the stone at the end of the 117-perch line of the Foster deed; then south 59 east 41, south 19 west 9 1/4 to a stone on the east side of a branch, [south] 59 west 3, south 51 west 38, south 59 east 20, south 6 west 17 3/4 and north 69 west 35 perches to a stone at the corner of a lot of 'the quakers society'; south 15 west 22.9 perches to Henry Starr's lane; south 84 west 19 1/2 perches to 'a lot now owned by said Biays'; and along that lot to stone B. Biays had it of Walker by a deed of about July 14, 1809 (W.G. 104/46, not read). What it settles: (1) the mortgage that the Chancery decree of Feb. 2, 1819 in Bolte et al. v. Biays foreclosed and Samuel Moale sold in lots in 1819 (rows 46128 and 46129): Moale's Lot 1 begins 'at a Stone marked B it being the beginning of the Ground mortgaged by the said James Biays to John Bolte', and Lot 2 at 'the end of the north sixty nine degrees west thirty five perches line', with the Tavern; every course of those two deeds is here. (2) The road from Hugh Thompson's land is Gilmor Lane: the 1901 Wood lease and the 1896 Dodson deed call Gilmor Lane 'also called a road leading from the lands of Hugh Thompson into the York Turnpike Road', so stone B stands on the south-east side of the lane, and by its courses the mortgaged ground takes in the south-west corner of the turnpike and the lane (the later 3010 to 3020, Moale's Lot 1 of 1821) and runs across the road to the east. (3) The Walker's Tavern ground came to Biays from Walker in 1809 (W.G. 104/46), out of Foster's 29 acres of 1800 (row above). What it does not settle: the 1809 Walker deed itself; the Chancery papers and the trustee's plat of the five lots; and who John Hanna and the other complainants (the Schultzes and Rudolph Wagler) were. Update Oct. 14, 2026: Walker's 1809 deed is read (719:mdlr-wg104-46-walker-biays-tavern-1809): $6,000, the same courses; Walker was an innkeeper in possession of the tavern; Foster had bought of William Spear about Oct. 4, 1786.

summary: Assignment, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 149, folios 635 to 636 (MSA CE 66-199; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 635 to 639: the top of 635 is the end of the McElderry lease to John Young, acknowledged June 7, 1819; this deed opens in the lower half of 635 under the index heading 'William Gray Trustee Deed To John McFadon' and ends on 636, where McFadon's own lease to Patrick Carroll of two Prince Street lots on the east side of Jones Falls begins). Dated and acknowledged Jan. 12, 1819 before Charles Gwinn and Saml. Farnandis, justices; received July 10, 1819 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). The deed recites that by an agreement of July 9, 1814 James Biays had agreed to give Benjamin Collins of Baltimore County a lease for 99 years renewable forever of 'a certain lot of Ground part of a tract of land called Ensors Inspection lying and being on the east side of the old York Road, running and bounding on said Road two hundred feet running thence Easterly to the line on the plat called Gorsuchs regulation', and that Collins conveyed his interest to William Gray as trustee on Sept. 13, 1817. Gray, as trustee, assigns McFadon for $60 the lot and the residue of the term 'Granted or to be Granted by the said James Biays with the benefit of renewment forever', subject to the yearly rent (not stated) and the agreement's covenants. What it settles: (1) the Tract Index's '1819, Gray to McFadon, 149/635' (row 46122) is not a sale of fee: it is the assignment of a promised Biays lease of a 200-ft lot on the EAST side of the old York Road, bounded east by a line on a plat called 'Gorsuch's regulation'; so the McFadon trust ground of 1822 (W.G. 165/492, 'at or near the gate' and across the turnpike) was not the Gray lot, and the trust's two named sources remain the Moale deeds of 1821. (2) McFadon was buying into the Biays ground at the gate even before the Chancery sale of July 1819 (Lot 1 and Lots 2 to 5, rows 46128 and 46129). What it does not settle: where the 'old York Road' frontage lies against today's streets (the 'old York Road' is presumably the later Old York Road, east of the turnpike at the 3011 fork, but no distance from a known point is given); the rent; and whether the promised lease was ever executed by Biays.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 83, folios 371 to 372 (MSA CE 66-133; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 371 to 375: the top of 371 is the end of John Eager Howard's lease to Solomon Heims, recorded the same day; this deed opens in the lower half of 371 under the index heading 'James Edwards Deed To James Biays' and ends on 372; 373 opens John Latour's assignment to Ebenezer Finley of a Paca Street lot). Dated Nov. 3, 1804; acknowledged Dec. 3, 1804 before Geo. Gouldsmith Presbury and Sam W. Lee; received Jan. 24, 1805 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). James Edwards sells James Biays, for $1,000 (the receipt below the signature names 'five shillings current money' as the full consideration, a discrepancy on the page), part of Ensor's Inspection: beginning on the west side of the York Turnpike in the first line of the part Joseph Ensor conveyed to Richard Dick, 'now owned by the said James Edwards'; south 1 degree west along the road 22.8 perches 'until it intersects a line drawn south eighty eight degrees east from a stone marked J.B. upon one side and E upon the other'; north 88 west 36.4 perches 'to another stone marked J.B. upon one side and E upon the other'; north 34 east 4 perches 2 ft 7 in to the part James Maydwell conveyed Biays; north 83 east 33 perches to the second line of Dick's part; along it 'reversely along the old main road' north 1 east 17 perches; and back along Dick's first line. No acreage is stated. What it settles: (1) the 'stone marked J.B. on one side and E. on the other' at which Samuel Brady's 1848 deed begins (A.W.B. 404/533, row 46149: 'which said Stone stands on the Second line of the land conveyed by James Edwards to James Biays on the third day of November ... eighteen hundred and four', then 'north 86 degrees west 36 4/10 perches to another stone marked J.B. and E.') is this deed's: the second line runs 36.4 perches west between the two J.B. and E. stones, so Brady's tract of 1848 begins on the Biays-Edwards line and its first course is that line. (2) It is the Edwards deed Biays's 1816 mortgage to Stump cites (row 46103, on 3028) and one of the six Biays deeds the Brady deed recites. (3) The parcel fronts the turnpike for 22.8 perches (about 376 ft) and also bounds 'along the old main road', so two roads ran here in 1804. What it does not settle: the Ensor-to-Dick deed (not recited by liber); where the J.B. and E. stones stand against today's grid; and the Maydwell lot (W.G. 67/63, not read). Update Oct. 17, 2026 (County grantor index, Dick and Gorsuch): the County grantor index runs for Di (CE 33-1 pp. 87-88 for 1655-1769, CE 33-2 p. 84 for 1770-86, CE 33-3 pp. 97-98 for 1787-97, CE 33-4 p. 99 for 1799-1803, the first Di page of that volume, p. 98, not held) show no Richard Dick as grantor in any form, and no Dick deed of Ensor's Inspection or of any land on the York road; the Dicks indexed (Thomas, James, Christian) are other men on other ground. No deed from Dick to Edwards is indexed before 1804, so how Edwards came by Dick's part is open: a will or descent, a deed entered under another first-named grantor or a variant spelling, an unrecorded deed, or a Dick deed of 1804 or later (CE 33-5 not held). Ensor's own deed to Dick was not among the Ensor lines found in CE 33-1 pp. 105-107 either. Next: the Grantee Index (MSA CE 32) under Dick, 1655-1769, for Ensor's deed to Richard Dick; and the Maydwell-to-Edwards deeds, W.G. 66/123 (1801) and 82/206 (1804), whose liber and folio are already known (row 46122). (714:index-ce33-1-p87-dick-richard-1765-1769 and its three siblings.) Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Maidwell to Edwards read): Edwards held 5 1/2 acres of Maidwell's nine by Sept. 15, 1804, the south 2 1/2 acres (W.G. 66/123, Mar. 25, 1801, $875) and the middle 3 acres (W.G. 82/206, Sept. 11, 1804, $2,000, with buildings), and the 1804 deed already calls 'another parcel of land belonging to said James Edwards' on its east, so Edwards had Richard Dick's part (probably, INFERRED) before Nov. 3, 1804 (rows 714:mdlr-wg66-123-maidwell-edwards-2-5-acres-1801 and 714:mdlr-wg82-206-maidwell-edwards-3-acres-1804).

S. Dodson et al., Deed to Mary Clemens' and ends on 25, where Augustus D. Clemens Jr. and Mary Clemens's deed to Charles Coll of a Hampden Avenue and 27th Street lot ($10,000, Apr. 20, 1896) begins; 26 to 28 not about this land). Dated, acknowledged (before S. Magruder Tubman, J.P.) and recorded Apr. 23, 1896 at 1:50 p.m. (Robt. Ogle, Clerk); the margin notes delivery to A. D. Clemens Jr. on Dec. 17, 1896. Richard S. Dodson, John M. Griffith and Rose J. Griffith sell Mary Clemens, 'the wife of Augustus D. Clemens Jr. of Baltimore County', in fee, for $5,000: from 36 ft south of the stone at the south-west corner of the York Turnpike and 'Gilmor Lane as now opened (said lane having been known as the road running between the lands of Mrs Gilmor and Mrs Biays and also called a road leading from the lands of Hugh Thompson into the York Turnpike Road)', south 3 1/4 west 67 ft 11 2/5 in to a boundary stone, west 17 perches to a free stone on the south-east side of Gilmor Lane, along the lane north 42 1/2 east 9.6 perches, south 85 east 105 ft 6 in to the end of the third line of Nicoll's sub-lease to Leicht (A.W.B. 394/156), south 38 ft and east 76 ft 4 in along that lot to the beginning. Title: Abraham G. Mott and wife to Dodson and Griffith, Dec. 6, 1892 (J.B. 1422/568), 'saving and excepting therefrom the reversion of Nine dollars issuing out of the part of said ground leased ... to Lorentz Leicht'; see also J.B. 1542/97. What it settles: (1) Mary Clemens's source, recited in the 1901 Wood lease (row 46108) and read there as 'A.Q. 1115': it is R.O. 1615/24, Apr. 23, 1896, $5,000, and the 1901 Wood lot (67 ft 11 2/5 in on the turnpike, 215 ft deep, the later 3010) is 'part of' this land, which runs 17 perches (280 1/2 ft) back to the lane. (2) The Mott-to-Clemens link: Abraham G. Mott (d. Oct. 3, 1895) and his wife sold in December 1892 to Dodson and Griffith, who sold to Mary Clemens three years later; so the Bromley 'Mott Est.' label of 1896 was already out of date, and the 1906 'A. D. Clemens Jr.' label is right. (3) The Nicoll-Leicht corner (3020) was carved out, and its $9 rent went separately (next row). What it does not settle: the 1892 Mott deed and J.B. 1542/97 (not pulled), and Dodson's and Griffith's place in the chain (buyers for resale, as the three-year hold suggests, is an inference). summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 1619, folios 244 to 245 (MSA CE 168-1627; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 244 to 248: the top of 244 is the end of a John E. Cullimore deed to Ella M. L. Brooks of a Ducatel Street lot, recorded May 15, 1896 at 1:55 p.m.; this deed opens in the lower half of 244 under the index heading 'Richard S Dodson &c, Deed to Mary Clemens' and ends on 245, where C. Hopewell Warner's executor's deed to George C. Thomas begins). Dated and acknowledged May 7, 1896 (Peter Sahm, J.P., for the Griffiths; W. B. Hammond, J.P., for Dodson); recorded May 15, 1896 at 2:15 p.m. (Robt. Ogle, Clerk). Dodson and the Griffiths sell Mary Clemens, wife of Augustus D. Clemens Jr., for $250, in fee, the 3020 corner lot (36 ft on the turnpike from the stone at the south side of Gilmor Lane, 76 ft 4 in west, 38 ft north, 76 ft 6 in on the lane), 'the same lot ... described in a sub-lease from John D Nicoll to Lorentz Leicht dated February 29th 1848 ... A W B No 394 folio 156', 'subject to the leasehold interest in said lot but with the right to collect' the clear yearly rent of $9, payable on Feb. 1. The deed explains the rent: 'the original rent on the whole lot of which the above described is a part was bought out by Abraham G Mott see land records of Baltimore County Liber J B No 96 folio 352 &c and the annual sub rent reserved under said sub-lease became an original rent and as such was conveyed to said Griffith and Dodson together with the balance of the original lot by deed dated December 6th 1892 ... J B No 1422 folio 568'. What it settles: (1) the 1924 deed's 'R.O. 1619 folio 244 ... dated May 7th 1896' (row below) is right, and is a second Dodson deed, not a miscite of R.O. 1615/24. (2) How the Leight corner's $9 rent became a fee rent: Mott bought out Mumma's original rent on the whole lot (Baltimore County J.B. 96/352, not read; the deed that should recite the Mumma-to-Nicoll lease of 1846, which A.W.B. 372/234 does not hold), so Nicoll's $9 sub-rent of 1848 became the original rent; Mott sold it with the rest to Dodson and Griffith in 1892; they sold it to Mary Clemens in 1896; and she merged it into the Leights' leasehold in 1924. What it does not settle: J.B. 96/352 itself (date, Mumma's or his assigns' grantor, price) and J.B. 1422/568. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 'buy-out' (J.B. 96/352) and the 1892 deed (J.B. 1422/568) are read: the Mumma heirs sold Mott the fee and $32 rent on Apr. 10, 1876 for $533.33 (719:mdlr-jb96-352-mumma-heirs-mott-1876), and Mott sold the 94 perches with 'the sub-annuity of nine dollars' to Dodson and Griffith on Dec. 6, 1892 for $1,500 subject to a $1,500 mortgage (719:mdlr-jb1422-568-mott-dodson-griffith-1892).

summary: Assignment, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 3361, folios 216 to 217 (MSA CE 168-3369; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 216 to 220: 216 holds the end of Susan Leight's deed to W. Harry Holmes, which begins on 215, not pulled, and this deed's opening; it ends on 217, where Bartus C. Dorsey Jr.'s assignment to Amelia C. Ziegenhein of a Linwood Avenue lot begins). Both deeds are dated May 1, 1919, witnessed and acknowledged before Louis W. Rahe, notary public, and recorded May 13, 1919 at 12:20 and 12:21 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk); Susan Leight signs by her mark, with Belle Archer also witnessing. The end of Susan's deed (216) shows its second lot: 20 ft on the east side of Barclay Street at the north side of Waverly Avenue, 110 ft deep, which Charles T. Leight, executor, conveyed her on June 29, 1904 (R.O. 2083/14), subject to $40 a year. Holmes's deed back conveys Susan Leight and Charles T. Leight 'as joint tenants and not as tenants in common' the 'same two lots' Susan had deeded him that day, for the residue of the terms renewable forever, 'subject to the payment of the annual rent of Nine Dollars on the firstly described lot and the annual rent of Forty Dollars on the secondly described lot'. What it settles: (1) the recited 1919 'assignment from W Harry Holmes dated May 1st 1919 ... S C L No 3361 folio 216' (S.C.L. 4210/380, row below) is read, at 3361, not the '3561' of the Edition 2 hop list (S.C.L. 3561/216 was pulled and holds 1920 Bartlett Avenue instruments: row '719:negative-scl3561-216'). (2) It was a straw round trip: Susan Leight (the widow of Henry Leight, d. 1904) put the two Leight leaseholds through Holmes so that she and Charles T. Leight would hold them as joint tenants with survivorship; the $9 rent on the first lot is the Nicoll-Leicht rent, so the first lot is the 3020 corner. (3) W. Harry Holmes did the same service for James M. Sinclair on Feb. 7, 1919 for 3013 (row 720:mdlr-scl3311-260-holmes-sinclair-3013-1919): a straw man of the Waverly conveyancers in 1919. Louis W. Rahe, notary, shares a surname with Charles M. Rahe, who married Johannah C. Leicht (row 41950); no document read says they are related. What it does not settle: the opening of Susan's deed (215), and how the 3020 leasehold passed from Lawrence Leight (d. 1892) and Wilhelmina (d. 1902) to Susan. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the opening of Susan Leight's deed to Holmes is read (719:mdlr-scl3361-215-susan-leight-holmes-1919): the corner, 'Known as No 3020 Greenmount Avenue', came to Henry and Susan Leight from Louis W. Leicht et al. on Feb. 2, 1903 (R.O. 1999/329). Update Oct. 14, 2026: Louis W. Rahe, the notary of these deeds, is one of Lawrence Leight's heirs who sold the corner to Henry and Susan Leight in 1903 (719:mdlr-ro1999-329-leicht-heirs-henry-susan-leight-1903), with Sophia Rahe: the family connection is now documented.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 4210, folio 380 (MSA CE 168-4218; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 380 to 384: the deed fills the top of 380 under the index heading 'Mary Clemens, Deed to Susan Leight &c'; below it, the Waverly Building Association's release to Kate D. Clubb of June 7, 1924, and on 381 to 384 unrelated instruments). Dated June 9, 1924; witnessed and acknowledged before Lennox B. Clemens, notary public; recorded June 10, 1924 at 1:30 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk); one 50-cent federal documentary stamp, which at 50 cents per $500 implies a price of $500 or less (an inference). Mary Clemens, widow, conveys Susan Leight and Charles T. Leight, as joint tenants, in fee, the 3020 corner lot (36 ft on Greenmount Avenue 'formerly called York Turnpike Road' from the stone at the south side of 'Vineyard Lane formerly called Gilmor Lane'), 'and especially the clear yearly rent of nine dollars', 'to the end and intent that the leasehold estate created by the lease aforesaid and the annual rent issuing thereout shall be forever merged and extinguished'. Recitals: R.O. 1619/244 (Dodson et al. to Mary Clemens, May 7, 1896); A.W.B. 394/156 (Nicoll to Leicht, Feb. 29, 1848); S.C.L. 3361/216 (Holmes's assignment to the Leights, May 1, 1919). What it settles: the 3020 corner's own parents, the hop the 1932 deed (S.C.L. 5328/110, rows 46091 and 46104) only recites: the Leights' leasehold of 1848 lasted 76 years as a leasehold under a $9 rent, and in 1924 the fee and the rent were bought in from Mary Clemens, widow of Augustus D. Clemens Jr., who held them by the 1896 Dodson deed; Augustus D. Clemens Jr. had died by June 1924. Lennox B. Clemens, the notary, also attests the Wolfe-to-Leight deed of 1953 and the release of the Rashbaum mortgage. What it does not settle: the price (stated as $5; the stamp suggests a small sum).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. 9085, folios 398 to 399 (MSA CE 168-9093; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 397 to 401; found by the Grantee Index 1953 H-O, MSA CE 166-390 p.271, which lists on Mar. 3, 1953 'Leight, Charles T. / William H. Wolfe &c / deed / S.E.S. Vineyard Lane / 9085 / 398' and, the same day, 'Same / Jacob Rashbaum &c / mtge / 3 Lots / 9085 / 395'). The typed form was prepared as of 'November ... fifty-two' and corrected by hand to Feb. 4, 1953 in both the deed and the acknowledgment; witnessed and acknowledged before Lennox B. Clemens, notary public; recorded Mar. 3, 1953 at 1 p.m. (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk). William H. and Carrie Wolfe convey Charles T. Leight, in fee, the lot on the south-east side of Vineyard Lane ('formerly known as Gilmor Lane'): from a point 2 ft north of the second line of the 1896 Dodson deed (R.O. 1615/24), 75 ft east parallel to it, 80 ft north along the west side of the 1901 Wood lot to the lane, and 123 ft south-west along the lane; the Wolfes reserve the 2-ft strip along the south side. Their title: an assignment from John E. Wyman, Jan. 14, 1928 (S.C.L. 4836/513), and a deed of the reversion from Rose I. Harding, widow, July 14 (the year is unclear on the typed copy; S.C.L. 5742 is a book of the late 1930s) (S.C.L. 5742/413). The Rashbaums' mortgage to Leight recorded the same day: page 397 is its last page, with Jacob and Rheba Rashbaum's acknowledgment in March 1953, recording on Mar. 3, 1953 and a release endorsed 'as executrix under the will of Charles T Leight deceased' by Catherine B. Flayhart, Lennox B. Clemens testing, in September 1953, recorded Sept. 14, 1953 at noon; the amount is on pages 395 and 396, not pulled. Page 400 opens the Leight-to-Rashbaum deed (row 42211). What it settles: (1) the Edition 2 'liber not stated' row: the Vineyard Lane lot came to Leight by M.L.P. 9085/398, recorded on Mar. 3, 1953 two folios before his March 2, 1953 deed of the three lots to the Rashbaums (M.L.P. 9085/400), which describes it as the third lot word for word: Leight took in the lane lot to sell it with the other two (an inference from the dates and the folios). (2) The Rashbaums gave Leight a mortgage back on the three lots, recorded with the deeds, and his daughter Catherine B. Flayhart released it as his executrix in September 1953, a month after his death on Aug. 12, 1953: so part of the price was carried by Leight. (3) The lane lot was itself a ground-rent lot: Wyman assigned the Wolfes the lease in 1928 and Rose I. Harding sold them the reversion in the 1930s. What it does not settle: the mortgage amount (pages 395 and 396), the Wyman and Harding deeds, and what the reserved 2-ft strip served. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the Wolfes' title is read: Wyman's 1928 assignment of the $54 leasehold (719:mdlr-scl4836-513-wyman-wolfe-vineyard-lane-lot-1928) and Rose I. Harding's 1937 deed of the reversion, merged (719:mdlr-scl5742-413-harding-wolfe-vineyard-lane-reversion-1937). The rent came from Mary Clemens's lease to Allen K. Wood of Apr. 17, 1902 (R.O. 1952/245).

Dated June 1, 1960 (typed 'May', corrected by hand); acknowledged before Cary D. Hall Jr., notary public; recorded June 2, 1960 at 10:18 a.m. (James F. Carney, Clerk). Clayton W. Bordley, Inc. assigns Henry Barnes and Madeline Barnes, his wife, as tenants by the entireties, the 3014 Vineyard Lane lot (18 ft on the north-west side of the lane, 156 ft north-east of Cat Bird Lane, 75 ft back to a ten-foot alley, and bounded on the west by 'the lot of ground thirty-thirdly described in a lease from William H. Brune, Jr. to Jacob H. Aull, dated April 20, 1887 ... J.W.S. No. 163, folio 9'), 'intending to convey hereby the entire lot of ground described in the lease from Harry W. Hoover to the said Clayton W. Bordley, Inc., for the term of ninety-nine years renewable forever, at and under the annual rent of Ninety Dollars ($90.00), payable ... on the eighteenth day of May and of November ... dated of even date herewith', recorded immediately before. The Barnes mortgage that follows (877/33): $3,640 on 35 shares from The Harewood Permanent Building and Loan Association of Baltimore City, 'part of the purchase money'. What it settles: (1) the $90 ground rent on 3014 Vineyard Lane, which the 2016 and 2020 deeds carry and the Edition 2 hop list asked about, was created on June 1, 1960 by a 99-year lease from Harry W. Hoover, the owner of the fee, to Clayton W. Bordley, Inc., which assigned the leasehold the same day to the Barneses: a ground rent made for a sale, not an old rent. (2) The 1887 Brune-to-Aull lease is only an adjoiner: the 33rd lot of that lease lies west of 3014, and 3014 is bounded 'on the northeasternmost side of said last mentioned lot'. Rows 41855 and 41856, which read the 2020 deed as making 3014 the 33rd lot, are corrected by pointer. What it does not settle: Hoover's lease itself (the folio just before 31) and his title to the fee; who held the $90 reversion after 1960. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the Hoover lease is read (1117:mdlr-jfc877-28-hoover-bordley-lease-1960): June 1, 1960, recorded 10:11 a.m.; Hoover leased as life tenant with power of sale under Marjorie C. Gamble's 1959 deed (J.F.C. 551/90); his leasehold came from Straw Man, Inc. in 1954 (M.L.P. 9509/244) and an older rent was merged in 1956 (M.L.P. 10304/216).

summary: Deed, Baltimore County land records, Liber J.B. 96, folios 352 to 355 (MSA CE 62-96, the Circuit Court series; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 352 to 356: the top of 352 is the end of Patrick H. and Rosa B. Walker's deed to Isaac H. Matthews, recorded May 8, 1876 at 4 p.m.; this deed opens at the foot of 352 under the heading 'David T Mumma and others, Deed To Abraham G Mott' and ends on 355 to 356 with acknowledgments; 356 then opens a Martinet and Chesapeake Bank release to John Moul). Dated Apr. 10, 1876; acknowledged in Baltimore City Apr. 10, 1876 before John T. Gorsuch, J.P., and in Adams County, Pennsylvania on Apr. 3, 1876; recorded May 8, 1876 (Jno. Bacon, Clerk). The grantors are the heirs of David Mumma, late of Baltimore County: his children Sarah Pennington (wife of Ross T.), David T. Mumma (and Georgia), Eugenia L. Gabler (and Lewis), Margaret Mumma Matthews, John J. Mumma, Edward W. Mumma (and Sarah, of Adams County, Pa.) and Julia Clowes (and Norris A., of Pittsburgh). By his will of May 31, 1857 (filed June 1857), Mumma left the parcel and 'the yearly rent of thirty two dollars issuing there out' to his wife Julia Ann for life, then to the children; she has died. For $533.33 they convey Abraham G. Mott in fee the parcel 'at the south west intersection of the York Turnpike Road and the Road leading ... towards the Lands of Mrs Gilmor and Mrs Biays': south 3 1/4 west 6.3 perches along the turnpike, west 17 perches to a free stone on the east side of the lane, north 42 1/2 east 9.6 perches and south 85 1/2 east 11 perches to the beginning, 94 square perches. It is the ground Mumma leased on Jan. 21, 1846 'to Jo[seph] D. Nicoll for the renewable term of ninety nine years' at $32 a year (Feb. 1 and Aug. 1), recorded, the deed says, 'in Liber A.W.B. no 372 folio 23[4]'; Mott already held the leasehold, by a deed from Samuel Hamilton Caughy of Oct. 4, 1860 (Baltimore County Liber G.H.C. No. 30 folio 473). The rent is conveyed 'to the end and intent that the said yearly rent of thirty two dollars ... shall henceforth be merged and extinguished'. What it settles: (1) the 'bought out' original rent of R.O. 1619/244 (row 46196): Mott bought the Mumma reversion and the $32 rent in 1876 for $533.33, which is the rent capitalized at 6 percent, and so held the 94 perches in fee, subject only to Nicoll's 1848 sub-lease of the corner to Leicht at $9. (2) The 1846 lease's terms, never read because the cited folio is empty (rows 46071 and 46201): 99 years renewable, $32 a year, to a lessee written here as 'Jo[seph] D. Nicoll' (the 1848 sub-lease names John D. Nicoll). The 1876 deed repeats the citation 'A.W.B. 372 folio 23[4]', so two independent recitals agree on a folio that does not hold the lease. (3) The 94 perches are exactly the two lots of the later deeds: 6.3 perches on the turnpike is 103 ft 11 2/5 in, the 36 ft of the corner lot (3020) plus the 67 ft 11 2/5 in of the 3010 lot; 17 perches west is the 280 1/2 ft depth of the 1896 Dodson deed. So the 1844 Mumma deed (A.W.B. 354/374, row 46070) is the 3010-3020 ground and nothing more. (4) The Mumma family: David Mumma's will of 1857 and the seven children, two in Pennsylvania. What it does not settle: the Caughy deed of 1860 (G.H.C. 30/473) and the leasehold's path from Nicoll to Caughy; the will itself. Update Oct. 14, 2026: Mott's leasehold is read (719:mdlr-ghc30-473-caughy-mott-1860, G.H.C. 30/473): Caughy assigned it to him on Oct. 4, 1860 for $3,300; Caughy had it from Frederick Gabler (Aug. 14, 1854), and Nicoll had cut two sub-leases from it, to Franklin Wilson (Feb. 7, 1847, $7, A.W.B. 378/206) and to Lorentz Leicht (1848, $9); Caughy bought Wilson's back in 1855. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the $533.33 is the buyout price written into the 1846 lease itself (719:mdlr-awb372-23-mumma-nicoll-lease-1846): the $32 rent capitalized at 6 percent, raised from $500 by words inserted before signing. Mott was exercising the lessee's redemption right, not paying a market price. Correction to the pointer above: Nicoll's sub-lease to Franklin Wilson is dated Feb. 27, 1847 (A.W.B. 378/206), not Feb. 7.

Clemens Jr. of a lot in his and Mary Clemens's mortgage of June 10, 1892 (J.B. 1398/170), recorded Dec. 6, 1892 at 1:25 p.m.; this deed opens below it under the heading 'Abraham G Mott & Wife, Deed to Richard S Dodson &c' and ends on 570, where Mollie E. Glück's mortgage to James S. Calwell begins). Dated Dec. 6, 1892; acknowledged the same day before G. Evett Reardon, J.P.; received Dec. 7, 1892 at 11:55 a.m. and recorded the same day (Jas. Bond, Clerk). Abraham G. and Mary E. Mott sell Richard S. Dodson and John M. Griffith, as tenants in common, for $1,500, the 94 square perches at the south-west corner of the turnpike and the road toward 'the lands of Mrs Gilmor and Mrs Biays' (the courses of the 1876 deed), 'the same lot ... conveyed to the said Abraham G Mott by Samuel Hamilton Caughy by a deed of assignment dated October 4th 1860 ... Liber G H C No 30 folio 473', with the 1876 merger of the $32 rent (J.B. 96/352), subject to Nicoll's 1848 sub-lease of a portion to Leicht at $9, 'and especially with the right to collect the sub-annuity of nine dollars', and subject to the Motts' mortgage of Mar. 24, 1890 to the Savings Bank of Baltimore, $1,500 at 5 percent (J.B. 1284/503). What it settles: the 1892 deed that both 1896 Dodson deeds recite (rows 46195 and 46196) is read: Mott sold the whole 94 perches, the 3010 land and the 3020 corner's $9 rent, for $1,500 over a $1,500 mortgage, so the buyers took on the bank debt (an inference from the two equal sums; the deed does not say how the price was paid). The leasehold title Mott had held since 1860 came from Samuel Hamilton Caughy; the 1876 merger made it a fee. What it does not settle: why the Loyola release to Augustus D. Clemens Jr. sits directly above on the same day (no connection is stated; the Clemens purchase from Dodson and Griffith came in 1896); and the Caughy deed itself.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 104, folios 46 to 47 (MSA CE 66-154; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 46 to 50: the top of 46 is the end of John Tessier's lease to Stephen Farall, acknowledged Sept. 16, 1809; this deed opens in the lower half of 46 under the heading 'Christopher Walker Deed To James Biays' and ends on 47). Dated and acknowledged July 14, 1809 before Sam. H. Gatchell and Thos. Cole, Patience Walker examined apart; received Sept. 16, 1809 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk); the margin is marked 'paid'. Christopher Walker, 'of Baltimore County Innkeeper', sells James Biays, merchant, for $6,000, the part of Ensor's Inspection 'which Land said Walker is now in the actual possession of and on which is situated the Tenement called Walkers Tavern', part of the land Foster sold Walker about Mar. 4, 1800, which, by an interlined clause, Foster 'purchased from William Spear by Deed on or about the fourth day of October in the year Seventeen hundred and eighty six'. The courses are word for word those of Biays's 1813 mortgage to Bolte (row 46192): from stone B on the south-east side of the road from Hugh Thompson's land (Gilmor Lane) 'at or near the Gate', north 40 1/2 east across the turnpike 94 3/4 perches to the end of Foster's 117-perch line, around to the Quaker lot, Henry Starr's lane and a lot already Biays's, and back to B. What it settles: (1) the Walker's Tavern deed the 1813 mortgage recites is read, at $6,000: the biggest single purchase in the Biays assembly at the gate, and the ground that Moale sold in lots in 1821 (Lot 1 at stone B, Lot 2 with 'the Tavern'), part of which became the McFadon trust ground and in 1844 the Mumma lot (3010 and 3020). (2) Foster's title came from William Spear, about Oct. 4, 1786: the same Spear whose four daughters sold Biays the 9 7/8 acres in 1801 (row 46180), so both the Walker ground and the Spear-heirs ground at the gate descend from William Spear. (3) Walker was an innkeeper in possession: the tavern at the gate was his before 1809. What it does not settle: the Spear-to-Foster deed of 1786 (no liber given); 'a Lot at present owned by said Biays' on the west, probably the 1801 Walker lot or the Spear lot (an inference).

Simpson, recorded May 13, 1919 at 11:15 a.m., and below it the opening of this deed under the heading 'Susan Leight, Asst to W Harry Holmes'; 211 to 214 are earlier instruments, not read for this row; the deed's end and Holmes's deed back are on 216, row 46197). Dated May 1, 1919, recorded May 13, 1919 at 12:20 p.m. Susan Leight, of Baltimore, conveys W. Harry Holmes two leasehold lots: the first 'at the corner of the York Turnpike Road now called Greenmount Avenue and the lane leading to Mr Gilmore's', 36 ft by 76 ft 4 in, 'Known as No 3020 Greenmount Avenue', 'the same lot of ground which by Deed bearing date the 2nd day of February 1903 ... R.O. No 1999 folio 329 ... was conveyed by Louis W Leicht et al to Henry Leight and Susan Leight his wife, the said Henry Leight having since departed this life', subject to $9 a year; the second on the east side of Barclay Street, 366 ft 8 1/2 in north of the corner, at $40. What it settles: (1) how the corner came to Susan Leight: Lawrence Leight's heirs (Louis W. Leicht et al.) conveyed it on Feb. 2, 1903 to Henry and Susan Leight, eleven years after Lawrence's death and a year after his widow Wilhelmina's; Henry died in 1904, and Susan held it as the survivor; the straw round trip of May 1, 1919 then put it in Susan and Charles T. Leight as joint tenants. (2) The house number 3020 is in use by 1919. What it does not settle: R.O. 1999/329 itself (who the 'et al.' were) and Henry Leight's estate. Update Oct. 14, 2026: R.O. 1999/329 is read (719:mdlr-ro1999-329-leicht-heirs-henry-susan-leight-1903): Lawrence Leight's heirs sold Henry and Susan Leight the corner leasehold on Feb. 2, 1903 for $1,500.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 4728, folios 211 to 212 (MSA CE 168-4736; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 211 to 215: the top of 211 is the acknowledgment and recording (2:36 p.m.) of the instrument before, which by Baer's acknowledgment is the deed to him; this deed opens under the heading 'Robert N Baer, Deed to Mary L Swormstedt &c' and ends on 212, where a Securities Company of Baltimore extension of mortgage to Wirt W. Pendleton follows). Dated and acknowledged Mar. 30, 1927 before Chas. H. Taylor, notary; recorded Apr. 27, 1927 at 2:37 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Robert N. Baer, bachelor, of Baltimore County, conveys Mary L. Swormstedt and Martha Swormstedt 'as joint tenants and not as tenants in common', in fee, three lots 'and the annual rents issuing therefrom', subject to the leaseholds: 2845 North Calvert Street ($120 a year); the 3010 lot by the 1901 courses ($180 a year, quarterly), 'the same lots ... sixthly and seventhly described in a deed from Richard Swormstedt et al unto the grantor herein dated March 29th 1927 and recorded ... prior hereto'; and a Baltimore Street lot ($75). What it settles: the step the 1930 deed (row 46190) recites as 'Robert N Baer unto Mary L Swormstedt and Martha Swormstedt' was a straw: the day before, Richard Swormstedt and others had deeded Baer the same rents, and Baer passed them to the two women as joint tenants. So the $180 reversion on 3010 belonged to the Swormstedt family before 1927 (Richard Swormstedt and others, presumably heirs; the deed does not say how they held it), not to Baer and not to the Clemens heirs. What it does not settle: the Swormstedt-to-Baer deed (the folios before 211, not pulled), and how the reversion passed from Mary Clemens (the 1901 lessor) to the Swormstedts. Update Oct. 14, 2026: Baer's two other deeds of Mar. 30, 1927 are read (719:research-scl4728-202-210-baer-swormstedt-family-partition-1927): he divided the Swormstedt family's ground rents between Richard Swormstedt and Martha and Mary L. Swormstedt, a partition through a straw; the deeds to him (Mar. 28 and 29) are on folios before 202. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the deed into Baer is read (719:mdlr-scl4728-194-swormstedts-baer-3010-reversion-1927): the 3010 rent was Barbara C. and Richard Swormstedt's by the entireties, bought from John P. Clarke, executor, on Dec. 16, 1903 (R.O. 2050/46); Richard senior died about Aug. 28, 1913, Barbara about Oct. 13, 1926.

Calvert's mortgage to the Commercial Permanent Savings and Loan Association begins). Dated and acknowledged May 6, 1927 before J. Lindamore Pennington, notary, witness Leo H. Fait; recorded May 12, 1927 at 10:16 a.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). C. Reese Dietrich, unmarried, conveys John Harmon Dietrich and Lulu S. Dietrich, his wife, as tenants by the entireties, three leaseholds 'which by deed of even date herewith ... was granted and conveyed from John Harmon Dietrich and Lulu S Dietrich his wife to C Reese Dietrich': (1) the 3010 lot by the 1901 courses, 'Being now known as No 3010 to 3016 Greenmount Avenue' (the words 'to 3016' interlined), at $180 a year quarterly; (2) 409 East 31st Street (formerly Waverly Avenue), at $61.25; (3) a lot 'on the east side of the York Turnpike Road' 204 ft 6 in north of the north-west corner of the ground Samuel H. Tagard, trustee, assigned George C. H. Coffield on Jan. 31, 1865 (Baltimore County J.H.L. 43/548), 35 ft on the turnpike and running 126 to 140 1/2 ft east 'to the west side of the Old York Road', at $175 a year. What it settles: the deed the 1927 Wolfe and Leight deed recites as 'an assignment from C. Reese Dietrich to John Harmon Dietrich and Lulu S. Dietrich his wife dated May 6th 1927 ... S.C.L. No. 4735 folio 61' (row 46189) is read, and it is a straw: the Dietrichs deeded the three leaseholds to C. Reese Dietrich and took them straight back as tenants by the entireties, the same device as the Leight and Holmes deeds of 1919. The Dietrichs were already the lessees of 3010 before May 1927, so the leasehold's step from Allen K. Wood (1901) to them is still unread. In 1927 the 3010 lot's buildings were numbered 3010 to 3016. What it does not settle: the Dietrichs' own title to the 3010 leasehold; and where the third lot lies (a lot between the turnpike and the Old York Road, 126 to 140 ft deep, so somewhat north of the fork; the Coffield tract of 1865 is not placed). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the third lot can be placed by arithmetic: it begins 204 ft 6 in north of the Coffield tract's beginning, which the 1904 and 1974 deeds put about 319 ft 9 in south of 32nd Street (738:mdlr-ro2062-398-bateman-provident-bank-lot-1904-read), so the lot runs from about 115 ft to 80 ft south of 32nd Street on the east side (an inference).

summary: Lease, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.F.C. 877, folios 28 to 30 (MSA CE 168-11195, pages 26 to 30 on the scan Jeff saved: 26 and 27 are earlier instruments, not read for this row; the lease is a printed 'Lease for Ninety-Nine Years' form on 28 to 30; the assignment to the Barneses follows at 31, row 46202). Dated June 1, 1960; acknowledged before Cary D. Hall Jr., notary public; recorded June 2, 1960 at 10:11 a.m. (James F. Carney, Clerk), seven minutes before the assignment at 31. Harry W. Hoover (divorced), 'in exercise of the power to sell and lease contained in the deed from Marjorie C. Gamble to the said Harry W. Hoover, et al., dated January 19, 1959' (J.F.C. 551/90), leases Clayton W. Bordley, Inc. the 3014 Vineyard Lane lot for 99 years renewable forever at $90 a year in half-yearly payments from May 18, 1960, renewal fine $10. Title recitals: the lot joins in one perimeter 'the entire two lots of ground' the Safe Deposit and Trust Company, substituted trustee, conveyed Levi A. and Helen A. Barnett on Feb. 27, 1953 (M.L.P. 9083/422); and 'the entire lot of ground which was conveyed by Straw Man, Inc. to the said Harry W. Hoover and Bertha J. Hoover, his wife', June 18, 1954 (M.L.P. 9509/244); the Barnetts deeded the Hoovers 'the reversion and the said rent' on Dec. 18, 1956 (M.L.P. 10,304/216), 'whereupon the said rent became merged and extinguished'; and Marjorie C. Gamble's deed of Jan. 19, 1959 gave Hoover a life estate with power of sale. What it settles: (1) the lease that created the $90 rent on 3014 Vineyard Lane (rows 46202 and 41855) is read: June 1, 1960, Hoover to Bordley, recorded just before Bordley's assignment to the Barneses: a sale by way of a new ground rent. (2) There was an earlier rent on the lot, held by the Barnetts as reversioners after 1953 and merged into the Hoovers' leasehold in 1956. (3) The Hoovers' leasehold came in 1954 from Straw Man, Inc., the same corporate straw used by the Silbigers for 2958 in 1965 (rows 46105 and 46106): Straw Man, Inc. was evidently a conveyancing company used across Waverly, not a family vehicle (an inference). What it does not settle: the Gamble deed (why Marjorie C. Gamble held the fee in 1959), the 1953 Barnett deed and its substituted trustee's sale, and the 1954 Straw Man deed. Update Oct. 14, 2026: both deeds behind it are read: Straw Man, Inc. to the Hoovers, June 18, 1954, under a $90 lease from Levi A. and Helen A. Barnett to Straw Man of the same day (1117:mdlr-mlp9509-244-straw-man-hoover-3014-vineyard-1954), and Marjorie C. Gamble's 1959 straw deed giving Harry W. Hoover a life estate with powers, remainder to Roma Vernelle Hoover (1117:mdlr-jfc551-90-gamble-hoover-life-estate-3014-vineyard-1959).

Levy, notary; recorded Nov. 6, 1908 at 2:30 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). James G. Stanley, trustee, under a decree of May 19, 1890 in the Circuit Court No. 2 cause James G. Stanley et al. v. Joseph Cox, executor of Caroline C. Hooper (Docket 1 folio 176), and by the Court's order of Oct. 19, 1908 directing him to convey to Sallie H. Stanley, conveys her in fee for $1 the 14-ft lot 402 ft 9 1/2 in north of 29th Street on the west side of the York Road, 'and particularly the rent or reversion reserved on and payable out of the said lot'. It is 'the same lot ... which by deed dated the 26th day of September 1907 ... R.O. No 2371 folio 148 ... was conveyed by James Keelty (unmarried) to James G Stanley Trustee'. What it settles: the one gap in the 2958 reversion's chain (row 46182) is closed: James Keelty sold the reversion of the $65 rent to James G. Stanley as trustee on Sept. 26, 1907 (R.O. 2371/148, recited), a month after leasing the lot to the Bowersoxes (Aug. 24, 1907, row 46085): Keelty built and leased the house and sold the rent at once, the usual Baltimore builder's sequence. The trustee held trust funds under the 1890 decree in a Hooper estate case and, by court order in 1908, conveyed the rent to Sallie H. Stanley (presumably a beneficiary; the deed does not say), who as Sarah Stanley Armour sold it to Henry Gerwig in 1932. The full reversion chain is now: Keelty (1907), Stanley trustee (1907), Sallie H. Stanley (1908), Gerwig (1932), the Gerwig heirs (1961, merged). What it does not settle: the price Stanley paid Keelty (R.O. 2371/148, not pulled) and the Hooper case papers. Update Oct. 14, 2026: Keelty's deed to the trustee is read (714:mdlr-ro2371-148-keelty-stanley-trustee-1907): Sept. 26, 1907, $1,130.43, recorded at noon.

summary: Assignment, Baltimore County land records, Liber G.H.C. 30, folios 473 to 474 (MSA CE 62-30, the Circuit Court series; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 473 to 477: the top of 473 is the acknowledgment of a William and Sarah D. B. Pole indenture, recorded Oct. 20, 1860; this deed opens below under the heading 'Samuel Hamilton Caughy, Assignment to Abraham G. Mott' and ends on 474). Dated and acknowledged Oct. 4, 1860 before Wm. H. Hayward, J.P. of Baltimore City (certified by Geo. E. Sangston, Clerk of the Superior Court); recorded Oct. 22, 1860 (Geo. H. Carman, Clerk). Samuel Hamilton Caughy, of Baltimore, assigns Abraham G. Mott, for $3,300, the 94 square perches at the south-west corner of the York Turnpike and 'the Road leading therefrom towards the lands of Mrs. Gilmore and Mrs. Biays' (the courses of the 1844 Mumma deed and the 1876 deed), held for the rest of the term renewable forever, subject to the clear yearly rent of $32 and to Lorentz Leicht's sub-lease, with the right to collect its rent. Caughy's title: Frederick Gabler assigned him the leasehold on Aug. 14, 1854 (H.M.F. 9/447, a folio of the book before its 1866 re-recording; row 719:negative-hmf9-447-reconstituted-volume), subject to the $32 rent and to two sub-leases by 'John D. Nicholl': one of Feb. 7, 1847 to Franklin Wilson at $7 a year (A.W.B. 378/206) and one of Feb. 29, 1848 to Lorentz Leicht at $9 (A.W.B. 394/156); Franklin Wilson assigned his sub-lease to Caughy on Apr. 5, 1855 (H.M.F. 11/305). What it settles: (1) the lessee's side of the 1846 Mumma lease from Nicoll to Mott: Nicoll, then Frederick Gabler (by 1854; the step from Nicoll to Gabler is not recited), then Caughy (1854), then Mott (1860), who bought the fee and the $32 rent from Mumma's heirs in 1876 (row 46204). (2) Nicoll had cut TWO sub-leases out of the 94 perches: the corner to Leicht (36 ft, the later 3020) and a second parcel to Franklin Wilson at $7 a year in February 1847, a year earlier. Caughy bought Wilson's sub-lease back in 1855, so in 1860 only the Leicht sub-lease was outstanding, which is why every later deed knows only the $9 rent. The Franklin Wilson parcel is presumably part of the later 3010 lot (an inference; its description is in A.W.B. 378/206, loaded for Jeff). (3) A Gabler held the leasehold in 1854, and Eugenia L. Gabler, wife of Lewis Gabler, was one of Mumma's heirs in 1876: no document read says Frederick and Lewis Gabler are related. What it does not settle: Nicoll to Gabler, the Franklin Wilson sub-lease's metes, and the Gabler deed at its re-recorded folio. Update Oct. 14, 2026: both Nicoll instruments this deed recites are read: the 1846 lease (719:mdlr-awb372-23-mumma-nicoll-lease-1846) and the Franklin Wilson sub-lease (719:mdlr-awb378-206-nicoll-franklin-wilson-sublease-1847), which is dated Feb. 27, 1847: this deed's 'seventh day of February' drops the 'twenty'. Wilson's lot was the back end of the Mumma lot, on the lane at the Biays line.

summary: Assignment, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 1999, folios 329 to 331 (MSA CE 168-2007; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 329 to 333: the top of 329 is the end of Henry Leicht's deed to George E. Leicht of the same corner, dated Feb. 2, 1903, acknowledged before Wilmer Emory, J.P., and recorded Feb. 12, 1903 at 10:51 a.m.; this deed opens at the foot of 329 under the heading 'Louis W. Leicht &c, Asst to Henry Leight & wife' and runs to 331 with its New Jersey acknowledgments; its recording stamp is lower on 331, not read). Dated Feb. 2, 1903. The grantors, Louis W. Leicht, George E. Leicht, Louisa Katto, Louis W. Rahe, Sophia Rahe, Frank Maurer, Lawrence Maurer and Evelina Anderson, convey Henry Leight and Susan Leight his wife, by the entireties, for $1,500, the corner lot of Nicoll's 1848 sub-lease (A.W.B. 394/156: 36 ft on the turnpike at 'the lane leading to Mr. Gilmore's', 76 ft 4 in, 38 ft, 76 ft 6 in), for the residue of the term renewable forever, subject to the $9 rent. Their title: an administrator's deed of Feb. 22, 1893 from Louis W. Leicht, administrator (of Lawrence, d. 1892), to Louis W. Leicht et al. (J.B. 1434/417); another of Feb. 2, 1903 from him as administrator of Wilhelmina Leicht (d. 1902) and Chas. G. Leicht to the same; and Henry Leicht's deed of his share to George E. Leicht the same day. Louis W. Leicht, George E. Leicht, Louis W. Rahe and Sophia Rahe acknowledged in Baltimore before Wilmer Emory, J.P.; Frank Maurer, Lawrence Maurer and Evelina Anderson in Hudson County, New Jersey, on Feb. 10, 1903; Louisa Katto there the same day; Charles T. Leight witnessed her signature. What it settles: (1) the 1903 deed that the 1919 deed recites (rows 46207 and 46197) is read: after Lawrence Leight (d. 1892) and Wilhelmina (d. 1902), the corner leasehold was held by their heirs in shares, and on Feb. 2, 1903 Henry Leight bought out the others for $1,500, taking it with his wife Susan by the entireties; Susan, his widow from 1904, held it by survivorship. (2) The heirs name the family: three Leicht sons (Louis W., George E., Henry; Charles G. had a share administered), Louisa Katto of Hudson County, New Jersey, and grandchildren presumably through daughters, the Rahes (Louis W. and Sophia; Johannah C. Leicht married Charles M. Rahe in 1862, row 41950) and the Maurers and Evelina Anderson of New Jersey. Louis W. Rahe, the notary of the 1919 Leight deeds, is one of the heirs, so the earlier 'no document read says they are related' (row 46197) is answered. 'Mrs. Louisa Kotta' of Jersey City visiting 922 York Road in 1907 (row 41969) is very probably this Louisa Katto. What it does not settle: the family relationships themselves (the deed gives none), the 1893 administrator's deed (J.B. 1434/417), and the recording stamp. Update Oct. 14, 2026: a notary named Louis W. Rahe also witnessed and took the acknowledgment of Jacob H. Aull's 1917 deed of 3026, across Vineyard Lane, to the Spellmans (725:mdlr-scl3109-316-aull-spellman-1917): very probably the same man.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 2371, folios 148 to 149 (MSA CE 168-2379; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 148 to 152: the top of 148 is the acknowledgment of Catherine E. Robb's mortgage, recorded Sept. 26, 1907 at 11:55 a.m.; this deed opens under the heading 'James Keelty, Deed to James G Stanley Trustee' and ends on 149, where Solomon Adler's mortgage to Alphonso L. Smithson begins). Dated, acknowledged (before Geo. A. Foos, notary) and recorded Sept. 26, 1907 at noon (Robt. Ogle, Clerk). James Keelty, unmarried, sells James G. Stanley, trustee in the Circuit Court No. 2 cause James G. Stanley et al. v. Joseph Cox, executor of Caroline C. Hooper (Docket 1 folio 176), for $1,130.43, the 2958 lot 'and particularly the aforesaid rent payable out of the said lot and the reversion thereto', subject to the Bowersox lease of Aug. 24, 1907 (99 years renewable, $65 a year). The lot is 'a part of' Keelty's purchase from William T. and Eliza W. Wilson of Jan. 11, 1907, cited here as 'Liber RO No 2303 folio 43' (Corridor carries it as R.O. 2302/43, row 46084, from the scan's header). What it settles: the price of the 2958 reversion: $1,130.43, the $65 rent capitalized at about 5.75 percent (an inference from the two figures). Keelty bought the ground in January 1907, leased the house in August and sold the rent in September: the builder's ground-rent sequence, with the trust fund of the Hooper estate case as the buyer. The reversion chain is now read at every step from Keelty to the 1961 merger. What it does not settle: the Hooper case papers and why the trustee conveyed the rent to Sallie H. Stanley in 1908.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.F.C. 2173, folios 9 to 11 (MSA CE 168-12491; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 9 to 13: 9 to 11 this deed; 12 and 13 an unrelated deed of Houck executors to Samuel B. Rochkind). Dated Jan. 13, 1967; acknowledged before a notary; recorded Jan. 16, 1967 (James F. Carney, Clerk); witness Carl L. Wannen Jr.; 'prepared without benefit of title examination'. Jon F. Oster, not married, conveys Helen P. Spellman, 'mother', and John T. Spellman III, 'son', as joint tenants, in fee, 3026 Greenmount Avenue (15 ft at the corner of Vineyard Lane, formerly Gilmor Lane, 82 ft deep to a four-foot alley). Oster had the lot from 'Helen P. Spellman, widow' by a deed of the same day recorded just before. The deed recites the whole Spellman title: the lot was leased by Jacob H. Aull and wife to Alice M. Chapman on Dec. 6, 1912 for 99 years renewable at $72 (S.C.L. 2787/374, June and December); the reversion vested in the Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore by a deed of Dec. 7, 1917 (S.C.L. 3177/132); Chapman assigned the leasehold back to Aull on Aug. 27, 1916; Aull sold it to John T. Spellman Jr. and Helen P. Spellman, his wife, by the entireties, on Feb. 14, 1917 (S.C.L. 3109/316); and the Mercantile Trust Company deeded them the reversion by a 'Deed of Redemption' of June 13, 1950 (M.L.P. 8123/414), ending the $72 rent. What it settles: the two gaps in the 3026 chapter. (1) The $72 rent: redeemed June 13, 1950 by the Spellmans from the Mercantile Trust Company, the Hooper estate's trustee (M.L.P. 8123/414), so the house was fee from 1950. (2) The joint tenancy that made John T. Spellman III 'surviving joint tenant' in 2006 (row 46175): after John T. Jr. died (May 1966), his widow Helen P. put the house through Jon F. Oster, a straw, on Jan. 13, 1967, and took it back jointly with her son. With the 1917 Aull deed (S.C.L. 3109/316, loaded for Jeff), the Spellman ninety years are now read end to end except the 1917 page itself. What it does not settle: the widow's deed to Oster (the folio before 9), the 1950 redemption deed itself, and who Jon F. Oster was. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1917 deed it recites is read (725:mdlr-scl3109-316-aull-spellman-1917): Aull to John T. Jr. and Helen P. Spellman by the entireties, Feb. 14, 1917, recorded Feb. 17, the first lot of Aull's Dec. 6, 1912 lease to Alice M. Chapman (S.C.L. 2787/374) at $72 a year. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1950 redemption (M.L.P. 8123/414) and the 1917 Hooper division (S.C.L. 3177/132) it recites are both read (725:mdlr-mlp8123-414-mercantile-spellman-redemption-3026-1950, 726:mdlr-scl3177-132-hooper-division-1917).
