summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.F.C. 1800, folios 528 to 530 (MSA CE 168-12118; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 528 to 532: 528 to 530 this deed; 531 and 532 an unrelated Mercantile-Safe Deposit deed of a Madeira Street rent under the will of Louis Kahler). Dated Nov. 13, 1964; signed for the company by a vice-president; acknowledged before S. Howard Oler Jr., notary; recorded Nov. 30, 1964 (James F. Carney, Clerk). Mercantile-Safe Deposit and Trust Company, surviving trustee under the will of Francis X. Hooper, sells David Siegel, for $825, the 3032 lot (14 ft on the west side of Greenmount Avenue, 43 ft north of Vineyard Lane, 'formerly Gilmor Lane', to the northern outline of the turnpike company's 1912 deed to Jacob H. Aull, 82 ft to a four-foot alley) 'and especially the aforesaid yearly rent of Sixty-six Dollars', subject to the lessee's estate. Recitals: Hooper's will (Baltimore County W.H.B. 19/182; City J.H.B. 217/204) left a third to his widow Florence W. Hooper and two-thirds in trust to the company and William Jenkins, since deceased; the widow and trustees divided the real estate by a deed of Dec. 7, 1917 (S.C.L. 3177/132; the second recital types 122); the lot is 'the fourthly described lot' of Aull's lease to Alice M. Chapman of Dec. 6, 1912 (S.C.L. 2787/374) at $66. What it settles: the 3032 reversion's step from the Hooper trust to Siegel (row 39459 had it by recital): $825 for a $66 rent, about 8 percent; Siegel deeded it to the clinic in 1975, merging it. With the 3026 deed of 1967 (row on 725), the same division deed of Dec. 7, 1917 put the four 1912 Aull rents (3026 to 3032) in the Hooper trust. What it does not settle: the 1917 division deed itself and the other two rents (3028, 3030).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.H.B. 3139, folios 15 to 17 (MSA CE 168-13459; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 15 to 19: 15 to 17 this deed; 18 and 19 an unrelated Schuman to Carey deed of 202 Montgomery Street). Dated in June 1974 (the day is handwritten and not legible on the copy); recorded June 24, 1974 (Robert H. Bouse, Clerk). Jack O. Chertkof, 'Surviving Trustee under a Revocable Trust Agreement dated 2/9/1968 made by David W. Chertkof', conveys Sample Stores of Baltimore, Inc. two lots in fee. The first, 'known as No. 3105, 3107 and 3109 Greenmount Avenue': from the end of the first line of the Bateman-to-Provident lot (R.O. 2062/398), at the north wall of the northernmost building, 218 ft 3 in south of the south-east corner of Greenmount Avenue and 32nd Street, south 46 ft 2 1/2 in to the north-west corner of the lot of William Hammel's sub-lease to 'Edward Mallalieu and others, Trustees' of Aug. 31, 1872 (Baltimore County E.H.A. 77/296), east 101 ft 9 1/2 in to Old York Road, north 47 ft 11 in, and west 114 ft 6 1/4 in along the bank lot; it is the first lot of a deed of Nov. 17, 1971 (R.H.B. 2860/136) from the directors and trustees of Ruth Realty, Inc. (Ethel Posnick, Helen Gimbel, Howard Chertkof and Jack O. Chertkof) to the executors of Annie Chertkof and the trustee of David W. Chertkof's trust. The second is a strip 9 1/4 in wide, 264 ft 5 1/2 in south of 32nd Street, to the centre of a 13-inch party wall, beginning at the end of the first line of M. Lillian Slade's 1935 deed to David W. Chertkof and wife (S.C.L. 5580/582); the strip itself came to the Chertkofs from Beulah Bruehl on Mar. 10, 1954 (M.L.P. 9424/40, recited in J.F.C. 969/476), and Sample Stores had deeded it to the trustee on Mar. 5, 1974 (R.H.B. 3106/316). What it settles: the 1974 row's 'trust unnamed' (rows 39759 and 10396): it is David W. Chertkof's revocable trust of Feb. 9, 1968, the 'DWC Trust' of the tax case, with Jack O. Chertkof surviving trustee; the lot came through Ruth Realty, Inc., a Chertkof family company liquidated in 1971; and the lot's lines tie to the Bateman bank lot of 1904 on the north and the Methodist trustees' sub-lease of 1872 on the south (the Waverly M.E. Church lot, by the chapter's reading). What it does not settle: Ruth Realty's own title (how the Chertkofs took the Bateman ground after M. Estelle Bateman's death in 1920), and the March 1974 strip deed's purpose (a party-wall adjustment, presumably). Update Oct. 14, 2026: R.H.B. 2860/136 was not reached: the tab used unit 13180, which is R.H.B. 2862 (737:negative-rhb2862-136-wrong-book-for-rhb2860); the right unit is 13178. The Coffield-Hammel and church deeds behind the lot are read. Update Oct. 14, 2026: R.H.B. 2860/136 is read (737:mdlr-rhb2860-136-ruth-realty-dissolution-chertkof-trustee-1971): Ruth Realty was dissolved in 1969 and its land distributed to the DWC trust; Ruth Realty had 3105 to 3109 from David W. Chertkof and wife, Nov. 1, 1960 (J.F.C. 969/476).

Estelle Bateman on Oct. 28, 1902 (R.O. 1984/398), held for the rest of the term renewable forever at one cent a year if demanded, with her interest in the alley. What it settles: the bank lot's own deed, which row 42263 and the 3107 chapter knew only from recitals: $2,000, a one-cent leasehold (so the 2002 deed's 'assignment at $0.01' goes back to this), cut from the Coffield tract of 1865 and the Bateman holding, with a two-story house on it in 1904. By arithmetic from the 1974 deed (218 ft 3 in south of 32nd Street at this lot's south end), the Coffield tract begins about 319 ft 9 in south of 32nd Street on the east side (an inference). What it does not settle: George Vandy L. Smith's 1868 sub-lease and the one-cent rent's reversioner.

Walter I. Dawkins, administrator of the personal estate of Clara V. Bateman, late of Baltimore City, under an Orphans' Court order of Oct. 23, 1902 and a sale ratified Oct. 27, assigns M. Estelle Bateman, feme sole, for $3,050, two leaseholds: (1) a lot on the west side of the Old York Road, 40 ft on it and about 81 to 85 ft deep, from a stone marked '2' of a lease from John Litzinger and wife to John H. White of May 5, 1866 (Baltimore County liber 48 folio 503), next to a 1870 sub-lease from White to Christian [Hinteman] (E.H.A. 65/502), at $58 a year; (2) the ground on the east side of the York Turnpike that George C. H. Coffield assigned William Hammel on May 15, 1869 (E.H.A. 62/390), less the part Hammel sub-leased to 'Edward Mallalieu and others trustees' on Aug. 31, 1872 (E.H.A. 77/296): 70 ft 6 in on the turnpike, 140 ft deep to the fourth line of the Tagart-to-Coffield tract of 1865 (J.H.L. 43/548), the whole Coffield tract being subject to one cent a year. Clara V. Bateman had the first lot from Dawkins as administrator of James S. Bateman and the second from him as administrator of Mary A. Bateman, both on Apr. 17, 1901 (R.O. 1896/419 and 421). What it settles: (1) the Edition 2 'City transfer' row of 1902 (newspaper only, 'Walter I. Dawkins to Clara V. Bateman ... name or date is wrong'): the deed is from Dawkins as administrator OF Clara V. Bateman (d. Feb. 1902) to M. Estelle Bateman, $3,050, so the newspaper named the decedent as grantee. (2) The Bateman ground on the turnpike was 70 ft 6 in of the Coffield tract, held from Coffield through William Hammel (1869), at a one-cent rent, with the Methodist trustees' sub-lease of 1872 cut from its south end; in 1904 M. Estelle sold 24 ft to the Provident Savings Bank (3111) and kept 46 ft 6 in (3105 to 3109; the 1913 plat's 'M. Estelle Bateman, 44.8 ft'). (3) A second Bateman lot fronted the Old York Road under a lease from John Litzinger of 1866: Litzinger is very probably the John Leitzinger of the 1847 Biays-heirs deeds at the fork (rows on 720), so this is a first deed out of the Leitzinger ground after 1847 (an inference from the name and the Old York Road frontage; the 1866 lease is not read and the lot is not placed). What it does not settle: the 1901 administrator's deeds, Hammel's title and the Litzinger-White lease (Baltimore County liber 48/503, prefix not written, presumably J.H.L.). Update Oct. 14, 2026: everything it recites is read: Coffield to Hammel 1869 (737:mdlr-eha62-390-coffield-hammel-1869), Hammel's 1872 church sub-lease (737:mdlr-eha77-296-hammel-methodist-trustees-church-lot-1872) and the two 1901 administrator's deeds to Clara V. Bateman (737:mdlr-ro1896-419-421-dawkins-administrator-clara-bateman-1901). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1866 lease is at J.H.L. 48/502 (read: 737:mdlr-jhl48-502-litzinger-white-lease-1866), and the Hunteman sub-lease at E.H.A. 65/502 (read: 737:mdlr-eha65-502-taylor-white-hunteman-sublease-1870). Litzinger's title was a 1865 Merryman deed (J.H.L. 46/149).

summary: Lease, Baltimore County land records, Liber A.W.B. 372, folios 23 to 26 (MSA CE 66-422; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 23 to 27: the top of 23 is the end of a Peter Rose to Enoch Holl lease, acknowledged Nov. 2, 1846 and recorded Nov. 3; this lease opens at the foot of 23 under the heading 'David Mumma, Lease to John D. Nicoll' and ends on 26 with its recording line). Dated and acknowledged Jan. 21, 1846, before R. Middleton and a second justice whose name reads like Wm. McTilton; recorded Nov. 3, 1846 at 11 a.m. (A. W. Bradford, Clerk), more than nine months after signing. David Mumma leases John D. Nicoll, both of Baltimore County, the 94 square perches at the south-west corner of the York Turnpike and the road toward Mrs. Gilmore's and Mrs. Biays's lands (the courses of the 1844 deed, A.W.B. 354/374, which the lease says was recorded July 10, 1845), for 99 years from Jan. 20, 1846, renewable forever on a $5 fine, at $32 a year from Feb. 1, 1846, paid $16 each Feb. 1 and Aug. 1. Two covenants matter: Nicoll must build 'a good and sufficient dwelling house' on the lot within one year, at his own cost; and Mumma must release the rent and convey the fee whenever Nicoll or his assigns pay $533.33 plus arrears. The clerk notes that the words 'and thirty three' and 'thirty three cents' were inserted before the lease was signed, so the buyout was first written as $500. What it settles: (1) the head lease that the 1847 and 1848 sub-leases, the 1860 Caughy deed and the 1876 Mott deed all rest on is found and read, at folio 23. The earlier search at '372/234' (folios 233 to 242, two negative pulls) was looking at a bad citation: the 1847 sub-lease cites it correctly as 'Liber A.W.B. 372 folio 23 &c.', and the 1848 '234' is probably '23 &c.' misread or miscopied (an inference). (2) The 1876 price is the lease's own buyout figure: $533.33 is the $32 rent capitalized at 6 percent, and Mott paid exactly that to Mumma's heirs (row 46204). He was exercising the redemption right written in 1846, not paying a market price. (3) The building covenant gives the first documented plan for a house on the lot: Nicoll was bound to have a dwelling up by January 1847 (a promise in the lease, not proof that it was built). (4) The arithmetic of the deal: Mumma paid $250 for the 94 perches in November 1844 (row 46070) and fourteen months later had a rent whose buyout value was $533.33, a little over twice his price (an observation from the two documents). What it does not settle: whether the house was built, and the step from Nicoll to Frederick Gabler, who held the lease by 1854.

summary: Sub-lease, Baltimore County land records, Liber A.W.B. 378, folios 206 to 209 (MSA CE 66-428; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 206 to 210: the top of 206 is the end of a Samuel Bentze to Gerard Stonebraker deed from Washington County, recorded Apr. 6, 1847; this sub-lease opens lower on 206 under the heading 'John D. Nicoll, Sublease to Franklin Wilson' and ends at the top of 209). Dated Feb. 27, 1847; acknowledged Apr. 1, 1847 before J. Hanson Bell and Jno. W. Stump, justices of the peace of Baltimore City, who also witnessed it; recorded Apr. 6, 1847 at 10:30 a.m. (A. W. Bradford, Clerk). John D. Nicoll, of Baltimore County, sub-leases Franklin Wilson, of Baltimore City, for $2 and $7 a year from Dec. 1, 1846, a lot beginning at a free stone on the east side of the lane between Mrs. Biays's and Mrs. Gilmore's lands and running 92 feet north along the lane, then 8 feet, 67 feet and 66 feet back to the start, touching Mrs. Biays's line; part of the Mumma lease, which it cites as 'Liber A.W.B. 372 folio 23 &c.' The term is the rest of the 99 years less one year, renewable forever. A rider lets Wilson cut the rent to one cent a year by paying Nicoll $116.67 with arrears. What it settles: (1) the date: the sub-lease is dated Feb. 27, 1847; the 1860 Caughy deed's 'seventh day of February' (row 46213) dropped the 'twenty'. (2) The citation: it is the document that gives the Mumma lease's true folio, 372/23, which is how the lease was found. (3) Where Wilson's lot was: it begins at the free stone the Mumma lease puts at the lot's far (west) corner on the lane, runs north along the lane and touches the Biays land, so it is the back end of the 94 perches, on the lane, not on the turnpike (an inference from the description; the courses as recorded do not close, so its shape is uncertain). (4) The same 6 percent arithmetic as the head lease: $116.67 is the $7 rent capitalized at 6 percent, as $533.33 is for the $32. (5) Jno. W. Stump, a witness and justice here, is the John W. Stump who held the McFadden ground in trust with Philip Biays before the 1844 sale to Mumma (row 46070). Caughy bought this sub-lease back in 1855 (H.M.F. 11/305, recited in row 46213), so it was gone by 1860. What it does not settle: the lot's true shape, and whether it lay inside the later 3010 lot.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 3109, folios 316 to 317 (MSA CE 168-3117; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 316 to 320: the top of 316 is the end of a partial release by the York Road Building Association of Baltimore City, by its president Geo. C. Earp, acknowledged before Catherine Gossman, notary, on Feb. 14, 1917 and recorded Feb. 17 at 10:45 a.m., whose start on 315 was not read; the Spellman deed follows under the heading 'Jacob H. Aull, Deed to John T. Spellman Jr.' and their mortgage begins on 317). Dated Feb. 14, 1917; witnessed and acknowledged before Louis W. Rahe, notary public; recorded Feb. 17, 1917 at 10:45 a.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Jacob H. Aull, of Baltimore County, conveys John T. Spellman Jr. and Helen P. Spellman his wife, by the entireties, for $5 and other consideration, with special warranty, the lot at the north-west corner of Greenmount Avenue 'formerly the York Turnpike Road' and Vineyard Lane 'formerly Gilmor Lane': 15 feet on Greenmount to the centre of the party wall with the house on the north, 82 feet deep to a 4-foot alley, 10 feet 7 inches on the alley, and 82 feet 1 inch on Vineyard Lane. It is the first lot of Aull's lease of Dec. 6, 1912 to Alice M. Chapman (S.C.L. 2787/374) at $72 a year, which Chapman assigned back to Aull on Aug. 27, 1916; the Spellmans take it for the rest of the term, renewable forever, subject to the $72 rent. The same day they mortgaged it to the York Road Building Association for an advance of $1,430 on eleven shares, 'part purchase money' (folio 317 on). What it settles: (1) the start of the Spellman tenure that the 1967 deed recites (row 46218) is read: Feb. 14, 1917, recorded Feb. 17. (2) The house: the description already runs through 'the house erected on the lot now being described' and its party wall, so the corner house stood by February 1917, as the 1912 lease's 'four new houses' implies (row 42192). (3) The street names: Vineyard Lane was Gilmor Lane, the same 'road leading toward the lands of Mrs. Gilmore' that bounds the 1844 Mumma lot across the lane on the south, so 3026 and 3020 face each other across it. (4) The price is hidden: $5 nominal, but the building-association advance of $1,430 was only part of the purchase money. (5) Louis W. Rahe, the notary, is the name of one of Lawrence Leight's heirs in the 1903 deed of the 3020 corner across the lane (row 46214) and of the notary of the 1919 Leight deeds: very probably the same man. What it does not settle: the 1916 Chapman assignment (the 1912 lease itself, S.C.L. 2787/374, is read, row 42192), the partial release on 315 to 316, and the mortgage's release (a margin stamp beside it appears to read Jan. 22, 1929; reading uncertain). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1950 redemption is read (725:mdlr-mlp8123-414-mercantile-spellman-redemption-3026-1950): $1,200. Update Oct. 14, 2026: Aull's title to the 3026 leasehold was Alice M. Chapman's assignment of Aug. 27, 1916 (725:mdlr-scl3109-328-chapman-aull-four-leaseholds-1916), recorded a few folios later in the same book; the corner rent was $72.

summary: Lease, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 2037, folios 211 to 213 (MSA CE 168-2045; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 211 to 215: the top of 211 is the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County's release, Oct. 5, 1903, of the mortgage Clemens Jr. and his wife gave it on Jan. 9, 1903 (R.O. 1995/142), signed by Henry C. Huff, president, witnessed by Geo. C. Earp; the lease follows under the heading 'Augustus D. Clemens Jr. &c, Lease to Joseph J. Willis', and the Fink deed begins on 213). Dated and acknowledged Oct. 1, 1903 before Chas. J. Fox, notary of Baltimore County, who witnessed it; recorded Oct. 6, 1903 at 1 p.m. (Robert Ogle, Clerk), with the release and the Fink deed. Augustus D. Clemens Jr. and Mary, of Baltimore County, lease Joseph J. Willis, of Baltimore City, the lot 156 ft 5 in south of the two-mile stone in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church, at the south-west corner of the 1898 Aull lease (R.O. 1728/284): 19 ft 2 in on the turnpike to Charles M. Rahe's lot, 53 ft to Old York Road, 20 ft 4 in on Old York Road, 58 ft 1 in back along Aull's line. Title: Shepherd G. Miller's deed in fee of Dec. 20, 1897 (R.O. 1710/153, read). Term 99 years from the date, renewable forever on a $10 fine; $54 a year, half-yearly from Oct. 1, 1903, clear of taxes; re-entry after 60 days, forfeiture after six months. What it settles: (1) the 3017 lease recited in M.L.P. 8666/310 is read: Oct. 1, 1903, at $54, as recited. (2) The parent title is Miller's 1897 deed, the same as 3015's and the Aull lot's. (3) Four days later Clemens sold the rent (row 721:mdlr-ro2037-213-clemens-fink-3017-rent-1903), so from October 1903 the 3017 ground rent and the leasehold were in different hands, which is the split the 1909 to 1951 deeds show. Henry C. Huff, president of the Waverly Building Association, signs the release on the same page. What it does not settle: how Willis's leasehold reached Clemens Jr. again by 1909 (the 1908 Lennox B. Clemens trustee's deed, not at S.C.L. 2497/333).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 2037, folios 213 to 215 (MSA CE 168-2045; read on the scan Jeff saved). Dated and acknowledged Oct. 5, 1903 before Chas. J. Fox, notary of Baltimore County; recorded Oct. 6, 1903 at 1 p.m. (Robert Ogle, Clerk). Augustus D. Clemens Jr. and Mary Clemens, of Baltimore County, convey Mary K. Fink, of Baltimore City, in fee, for $1,733, two lots 'in the Village of Waverly': first, the 3017 lot (the courses of the Willis lease), part of Shepard G. Miller's 1897 deed (R.O. 1710/153), 'especially the clear yearly rent of fifty-four dollars' under the Willis lease of Oct. 1, 1903, subject to the leasehold; second, a lot on the east side of the turnpike 23 ft 7 in wide, between a lot Clemens leased Joseph J. Willis on Jan. 9, 1903 (R.O. 1995/231) and one he leased Leonard P. Eisinger and wife on May 4, 1903 (R.O. 2011/211), running 160 ft to Old York Road, which Henry W. Fox, trustee, had conveyed Clemens in fee on Jan. 9, 1903 (R.O. 1995/230). Special warranty. What it settles: (1) who bought the 3017 ground rent: Mary K. Fink, four days after the lease, recorded the same hour. From her it went to Leopold Lehmann (deed of Sept. 17, 1907, R.O. 2369/13, recited in M.L.P. 7060/156), then by his will to Mary C. Lehmann, to the Sinclairs in 1946 and the Vinsons in 1951, where it merged. (2) Clemens was creating rents and selling them: a lease, then the rent sold the same week. (3) Joseph J. Willis took a second Clemens lease in January 1903, elsewhere on the turnpike, where the gap to Old York Road is about 160 ft. The second lot's place on the avenue is not fixed by this deed. Mary K. Fink may be of the family of William L. Fink, who bought 3013 from Clemens in 1898 (R.O. 1729/241): the deed does not say. What it does not settle: the price split between the two lots (at 6 percent the $54 rent is worth $900, an inference) and where the second lot lies. Fink's title as recited includes a deed from Estella Fink of July 31, 1907 (R.O. 2358/421).

Dated and acknowledged Dec. 21, 1946 before Jennie E. Weil, notary of Baltimore County, who witnessed it; Mary C. Lehmann signs by her mark; recorded Dec. 24, 1946 at 11:15 a.m. (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk). Mary C. Lehmann, widow, of Baltimore County, conveys Harry R. and Alice M. Sinclair, by the entireties, for $5 and other consideration, four ground rents and their reversions: 3426 Old York Road ($60, from Philip Silbert, 1916), 4412 Old York Road at Cold Spring Lane ($60, her own lease of 1923), a Springfield Avenue lot in Baltimore County ($36, from Charles L'Allemand, 1907), and the 3017 lot, typed 'Known as number 3013 Greenmount Avenue', under the Willis lease of Oct. 1, 1903 at $54. Her title to 3017: Leopold Lehmann's will (Baltimore County Wills W.J.P. 16/78), and Mary K. Fink's deed to Leopold Lehmann of Sept. 17, 1907 (R.O. 2369/13). What it settles: (1) the 1946 deed recited in M.L.P. 8666/310 is read, and it closes the 3017 ground-rent chain: Clemens Jr. to Mary K. Fink (1903), Fink to Leopold Lehmann (1907), his will to Mary C. Lehmann, Lehmann to the Sinclairs (1946), the Sinclairs to the Vinsons (1951, merged). (2) The 3017 rent was one of a small portfolio of north Baltimore ground rents the Lehmanns built up from 1907 and sold together. (3) The deed numbers the lot '3013 Greenmount Avenue', a scrivener's or old-numbering slip: the courses are 3017's, and 3013 is the Fink lot two doors south (R.O. 1729/241). What it does not settle: the real price (only $5 is stated), Leopold Lehmann's dates, and the 1907 Fink deed itself (R.O. 2369/13, not pulled). Rubenstein, personal representative of the estate of Delmond F. Shields as the chapter inferred: Alva held the house to 1960 and deeded it to Delmond, very probably her son (the 1950 census shows her widowed at 3032 with a son, 33; an inference, the deed gives no relationship). summary: Sub-lease, Baltimore County land records, Liber E.H.A. 59, folios 86 to 88 (MSA CE 62-59; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 86 to 90; Edwin Eachus and wife's deed to Joseph F. Snyder follows on 88). Dated and acknowledged Mar. 2, 1868 before Wm. H. Bayzand, J.P. of Baltimore City, who witnessed it (certified by George Robinson, Clerk of the Superior Court, the same day); recorded Aug. 6, 1868 (Edward H. Ady, Clerk). The margin heading reads 'Sub Lease to'. George C. H. Coffield leases George Vandyke Smith, both of Baltimore County, the 79-ft lot at the north end of the Coffield tract: beginning on the turnpike 125 ft 6 in north of the tract's beginning (J.H.L. 43/548), a point four feet north of 'the two story house erected on the lot next adjoining on the south', then N 2 E 79 ft to the tract's north-west corner post, S 85 1/2 E 140 ft 6 in to Old York Road, S 19 1/2 W 78 ft 6 in, N 86 1/4 W 119 ft. Term: 'all the rest and residue save one year' of Coffield's own term, renewable forever on a $10 fine by a new sub-lease 'reserving ... a reversion of one day'; rent $150 a year from Mar. 1, 1868, clear of taxes; re-entry after 60 days, forfeiture after one year. Buyout: only 'within thirty days after the expiration of ten years' (March 1878), on $2,500 and arrears, Coffield to assign the lot free of the rent and subject 'to the yearly rent of one cent only'. What it settles: (1) the 1868 instrument is read and it is a SUB-lease: Coffield held the tract under a 99-year renewable lease at one cent a year (the 1865 Tagart deed), so the $150 rent was a sub-rent, carved under a one-cent ground rent whose lessor is still unknown. Every later 'fee' and 'reversion' of the $150 rent (the Schaeffer trust 1936, Crittenton, the 1988 merger) is Coffield's position: the one-cent leasehold plus the $150 sub-rent (an inference from the two deeds; no later deed read mentions the one cent). (2) The buyout was a single 30-day window in 1878 at $2,500 (the $150 at 6 percent) and was evidently not used, which is why the rent lived to 1988. (3) A two-storey house stood on the lot south of the 79 ft in 1868, the Bateman ground (3111). What it does not settle: how the sub-leasehold passed from Smith to Charles Hamilton by 1889, and the original one-cent lease. Update Oct. 14, 2026: confirmed in words by the 1887 assignment (742:mdlr-jws160-431-stump-peirce-150-subrent-1887), which calls this 'a certain sub-lease (the original rent being one cent)'. The $150 sub-rent was held by Mary J. Stump by 1886 and John H. Stump, who assigned it to Mary Louisa and William Edward Peirce in 1887. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 4): the passage from Smith toward Hamilton is now read in outline. Martin Kratt's assignment to Charles Hamilton of July 2, 1870 (E.H.A. 67/41, $500; 742:mdlr-eha67-41-kratt-hamilton-79ft-leasehold-1870) recites that Kratt held the term jointly with Joseph M. Cone by a deed of about May 8, 1869 (E.H.A. 62/262, grantor not named) and took Cone's interest by a deed of about July 30, 1869 (E.H.A. 63/71). Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 5): E.H.A. 62/262 is read (742:mdlr-eha62-262-treadway-bruns-heise-cone-kratt-1869). Its grantors were John W. Treadway, John Bruns and William Heise, for $800 on May 6, 1869, and they held by an assignment of Oct. 14, 1868 from 'John C Smith' (E.H.A. 59/471, not read), seven months after this sub-lease; whether that is George Vandyke Smith miscopied or a second holder is open. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 6): E.H.A. 59/471 is read (742:mdlr-eha59-471-george-vandyke-smith-treadway-bruns-heise-1868). George Vandyke Smith himself assigned this sub-lease to John W. Treadway, John Bruns and William Heise on Oct. 14, 1868 for $325, reciting it ('leased or subleased to the said George Vandyke Smith by George C. H. Coffield'); the 'John C Smith' of the 1869 recital is a miscopy, very probably of the index heading 'John V. Smith' (inference). The leasehold side now runs deed by deed from Coffield to Hamilton.

summary: Trustees' deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5349, folios 127 to 128 (MSA CE 168-5357; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 127 to 131: the top of 127 is the end of a Mortgage Guarantee Company assignment, recorded Feb. 24, 1933; this deed follows under the heading 'James L. Hennegan &c Trustees, Deed to The Eyring Realty Corp'). Dated and acknowledged Feb. 23, 1933 before Antoinette S. Gray, notary, who witnessed it; recorded Mar. 7, 1933 at 2:30 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk); $19 in federal stamps, which fits $19,000. Under a decree of the Circuit Court of Baltimore City of Oct. 21, 1932 in Erhard Eyring et al. v. The Miller Brothers Furniture Company, Incorporated, et al. (Docket 72-C folio 663), the trustees sold the leasehold on or about Nov. 21, 1932 to The Eyring Realty Corporation for $19,000; the sale was ratified and the money paid. The lot: 35 ft on Greenmount Avenue beginning 114.7 ft south of the south curb of 32nd Street, which is the north-west corner post of the Coffield tract, 204 ft 6 in north of its beginning (J.H.L. 43/548), 126 ft to Old York Road. It passes for the residue of the term, renewable, 'subject however to the payment of the annual rent of twelve hundred dollars'. What it settles: (1) the folio: 127, as the Hong-side papers say; the 1988 Crittenton deed's 'folio 727' is wrong (there is no folio 727 in this liber). (2) The date, Feb. 23, 1933, and the leasehold: Eyring bought the sub-leasehold under the $1,200 sub-rent, not the fee. (3) The suit behind the sale was brought by Erhard Eyring, of E. Eyring and Sons, the builders of the 1928 showroom, against Miller Brothers; the Eyring company then bought the building at the sale. That this was a builder's claim for an unpaid contract is an inference: the deed does not say what the suit was for. What it does not settle: the equity file (Docket 72-C/663).

summary: Trustee's deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5669, folios 442 to 443 (MSA CE 168-5677; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 442 to 446: the top of 442 is the end of Rhoda M. Weant's deed, recorded Oct. 30, 1936 at 10:30 a.m.; this deed follows, and John L. Long's deed to Home Friendly Insurance Co. begins on 443). Dated and acknowledged Oct. 28, 1936 (W. R. Hubner, vice president, before Chas. C. Reinhardt, notary); recorded Oct. 30, 1936 at 10:40 a.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). The Safe Deposit and Trust Company of Baltimore, trustee under the will of Ellen M. Schaeffer of Baltimore City (will dated Sept. 20, 1926, Wills E.R.D. 158/519, with power of sale), conveys Florence Crittenton Mission, Incorporated, 'in fee simple', for $4,137.93, the $150 annual rent and reversion of the whole 79-ft lot, then 3113, 3115 and 3117 Greenmount Avenue and 3100 and 3102 Old York Road (the 1868 courses), 'which said annual rent is the special subject of this conveyance', subject to the leasehold. Title: Coffield's lease to Smith (E.H.A. 59/86) and Henry Bradley and wife's deed to Ellen M. Schaeffer of Oct. 27, 1908 (S.C.L. 2459/514). What it settles: (1) the fee-side hop before 1936 is named: Henry Bradley and his wife sold Ellen M. Schaeffer the $150 rent in October 1908, so the 71-year gap (Coffield 1865 to 1936) is now 1868 to 1908, Coffield to Bradley. (2) Ellen M. Schaeffer's will is dated 1926 and her trustee was the Safe Deposit and Trust Co., which sold under its power of sale. (3) The price, $4,137.93, is not the 6 percent figure ($2,500); it is about 27.6 years' purchase, a 3.6 percent yield (arithmetic). (4) The house south of the lot is a 'two story brick house' by 1936; the 1868 lease just says 'two story house'. What it does not settle: Coffield to Bradley (1868 to 1908), and the one-cent lease above Coffield's term, which this deed does not mention. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1908 deed is read (742:mdlr-scl2459-514-bradley-schaeffer-150-rent-1908): Bradley held the rent three days, from Edward S. Peirce, trustee (Oct. 24, 1908), and cites older title at R.O. 1888/54 (City) and J.W.S. 160/431 (County); the lot lay 'immediately to the south of No 4 Baltimore City Engine House'.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5686, folios 215 to 216 (MSA CE 168-5694; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 215 to 219: the top of 215 is the end of a Real Estate Investment and Finance Company deed recorded Dec. 30, 1936 at 2:45 p.m.; this deed follows, and the Eyring company's mortgage to the Eyring trustees begins on 216). Dated and acknowledged Dec. 30, 1936 before Raymond L. Henry, notary, who witnessed it; recorded the same day at 2:45 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Dorothy Dietrich, Wilhelmina Dietrich and Helen Dietrich Butler, of Baltimore City, convey The Eyring Realty Corporation, for $5 and other consideration ($19 in federal stamps), the $1,200 sub-ground rent and sub-reversion of 3117 (the 35-ft lot at the Coffield tract's north-west corner, 409 ft south of Gorsuch Avenue), 'to the end and intent' that it be merged in Eyring's leasehold, subject to the $150 rent. The sub-rent was created by 'a sub-lease from Lula S. Dietrich, widow, to Miller Brothers Furniture Company Incorporated dated March 3, 1928' (S.C.L. 4854/321), $1,200 a year quarterly; the grantors had it by 'a Deed from Wilhelmina Dietrich, Administratrix' of Apr. 27, 1931 (S.C.L. 5213/440). The same day Eyring Realty mortgaged the lot for $15,000 to Edward and Richard Eyring, surviving trustees under Erhard Eyring's will (Wills J.H.B. 181/6). What it settles: (1) the 1928 sub-lease is named: S.C.L. 4854/321, dated Mar. 3, 1928, made by Lula S. Dietrich as a widow, so John H. Dietrich was dead by March 1928. (2) The three grantors took through an administratrix's deed of 1931, very probably from Lula's estate, and are very probably her daughters (inference: the deed states no relationship and does not say whose estate Wilhelmina administered). (3) Erhard Eyring, the complainant of 1932, was dead by December 1936, and his estate financed the purchase. (4) It confirms the 1933 folio, 5349/127. What it does not settle: how the Dietrichs took the leasehold (the 1904 decree sale, Hamilton or Zoll), and the administratrix deed (S.C.L. 5213/440).

summary: Corporate deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. 7523, folios 422 to 424 (MSA CE 168-7531; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 422 to 426). Dated May 3, 1948 and acknowledged that day by Edward Eyring, president, with Richard Eyring, secretary, who swore that the board (May 1, 1948) and the stockholders approved it; recorded July 28, 1948 at 10:50 a.m. (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk), with a sheet of federal documentary stamps. Under 'a plan of reorganization', The Eyring Realty Corporation conveys Eyring Realty Enterprises, Inc., for $5 and other consideration, 'all and singular the lands ... fee simple and leasehold properties, ground rents, reversionary estates' it owned in Baltimore City and Baltimore County, except stocks, bonds and notes: leaseholds subject to their rents, fee lots in fee. No lot is described, and the clerk marked it 'UNLOCATED'. What it settles: (1) the 1948 transfer is a blanket deed: it passes 3117 only because the company owned it, and it names no lot, no liber and no rent, so it cannot settle fee against leasehold for 3117 (the 1933 and 1936 deeds do: leasehold under the $150 rent until 1988). The 1988 Hong-side papers' 'fee simple' does not come from this deed. (2) Edward and Richard Eyring ran the company; Erhard Eyring had died by 1936. What it does not settle: the stamp total (not counted) and what else the company owned.

summary: Trustees' deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.F.C. 2079, folios 102 to 105 (MSA CE 168-12397; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 102 to 106, which also hold the start of the purchase-money mortgage at 106). Dated June 1, 1966; acknowledged June 1 (the individual trustees, before Dorothy S. Weintraub) and June 6 (Maryland National Bank by J. Edward Macatee Jr., vice president, before Frances Elizabeth Brown); recorded June 7, 1966 at 1 p.m. (James F. Carney, Clerk). Janet E. C. Wurtzburger and Moses W. Rosenfeld, successor trustees, and Maryland National Bank, successor corporate trustee, under Tillie M. Wurtzburger's deed of trust of Dec. 13, 1940 (M.L.P. 6111/293), convey Harry B. Gorfine, surviving trustee under two deeds of trust of Dec. 30, 1948 from Myles Katz and wife (M.L.P. 7669/44 and /56), an undivided half under each, in fee simple, for $35,500, the apex lot: 36 ft 1/2 in on York Road north from Merryman's Lane, 42 ft back to the lane, 55 ft on the lane; 'known as 3200 and 3202 Greenmount Avenue'. Recited title: Elizabeth Ruth Samstag to Alan and Tillie M. Wurtzburger, joint tenants, Dec. 2, 1936 (S.C.L. 5678/406); Tillie's half into the 1940 trust; her resignation and Janet E. C. Wurtzburger's appointment (Dec. 13, 1941, M.L.P. 6254/433); Alan's half into the trust (Aug. 1, 1962, J.F.C. 1326/16); Alan's death about Feb. 20, 1963; Rosenfeld named successor (Apr. 26, 1961, J.F.C. 1696/562); Maryland National Bank named (Dec. 10, 1965, J.F.C. 2014/51); and the 1926 party-wall agreement with J. Alan Fledderman (S.C.L. 4603/330). The same day Gorfine mortgaged it to the Union Trust Company of Maryland for $48,000 'for part of the purchase price', 5 3/4 percent over ten years (J.F.C. 2079/106), released July 7, 1976 (margin, Liber 3368 folio 324). What it settles: (1) the Katz trusts took the corner in June 1966 by purchase, $35,500, as the 1976 deed recites (row 42333's reading is right). (2) The Samstag name question: the 1936 grantor is 'Elizabeth Ruth Samstag', so the 1924 'Ruth E.' and the 1926 and 1936 'Elizabeth R.' are one woman, Frederick H. Samstag's wife. (3) The Wurtzburger tenure is now read step by step, 1936 to 1966, with the trust's successor trustees. (4) The mortgage was larger than the price because it also covered a second lot (on Frederick Road at Warwick Avenue, from an 1890 deed, J.B. 1283/277). What it does not settle: what the Katz trusts were for (the 1972 papers name the beneficiaries) and the S.C.L. 5678/406 deed itself.

summary: Two trust instruments, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.H.B. 2927, folios 593 to 595 (resignation) and 596 to 598 (designation) (MSA CE 168-13245; read in full on the scan Jeff saved). Both executed July 5, 1972 by Harry B. Gorfine and acknowledged that day before Dotti Claire Liberles, notary; recorded July 13, 1972 at 11:00 and 11:01 a.m. (Robert H. Bouse, Clerk). They recite that Myles and Betty Katz made two deeds of trust on Dec. 30, 1948, one for the primary benefit of Alan R. Katz (M.L.P. 7669/56) and one for Barbara E. Katz, now Barbara K. Gerstley (7669/44), naming Joseph Smelkinson and Harry B. Gorfine trustees, and quote paragraph 7 (trustees may name successors; any trustee may resign in writing). Smelkinson had died without naming a successor. Gorfine designates Arthur H. Katz as successor and, failing him, Morris Fiddle, and resigns; Alan R. Katz and Barbara K. Gerstley, 'the only descendants of Myles Katz and Betty Katz who are ... sui juris', acknowledge and release him; Arthur H. Katz and Morris Fiddle accept on July 6, 1972 and declare themselves satisfied with Gorfine's accounts. What it settles: (1) the trusts' beneficiaries (Alan R. Katz; Barbara K. Gerstley) and why Arthur H. Katz could deed the corner as 'successor trustee' in 1976 (R.H.B. 3415/175). (2) Gorfine was still the owner of record on the 1977 DHCD roster after he had resigned, a stale roster entry. (3) The papers do not describe 3200: the margin indexes other property (Block 107, 1900 Edmondson Avenue, and Block 4163), so the trusts held several Baltimore properties. What it does not settle: the 1948 deeds of trust themselves (M.L.P. 7669/44 and /56) and how Arthur H. Katz is related to Myles Katz (not stated).

Dated and acknowledged Mar. 6, 1872 before Frank Lewis, J.P. of Baltimore County, who also witnessed it; recorded Mar. 22, 1872 (Edward H. Ady, Clerk). Elizabeth D. Huff assigns James E. Sinclair, both of Baltimore County, for $2,500, 'part of a tract called Huntington': beginning at the intersection of the York Turnpike 'agreeable to Baker's survey' and 'the road now called Merryman's Lane leading to Van Bibber's Mill', ten perches (165 feet) up the York Road, then square across to the lane, which closes the lot. It is the land Andrew Brown assigned her on Apr. 9, 1866 (J.H.L. 48/236), and passes for the rest of 'the original Lease', subject to its yearly rent (neither lease nor rent is named). What it settles: (1) the first of the three sources the 1884 Sinclair-to-Harris deed cites (W.M.I. 141/407, row 23723) is read, and it names the TRACT: Huntington, the first tract name reached for the 3200 block. (2) The lot is a triangle at the fork of the York Road and Merryman's Lane, 165 feet on the road, which is the 3200 apex and the frontage north of it (an inference from the description; 3200-3202 is the 36-foot apex lot). (3) It was a leasehold: Sinclair bought a term under an older ground lease, through Andrew Brown (1866). The 1873 Wilson deed (J.B. 84/387) bounds its own lot on 'the old division fence between Brown's lot and said Wilson's land', which is this lot's north line (an inference). (4) Huff is the family of 'Residence late A. J. Huff, 1815, west side York Road, near Merryman's Lane' (Aull, Old Land Marks no. 21): probable. What it does not settle: the original lease (its lessor, date and rent), the Brown deed of 1866, and how the fee was cleared before Sinclair sold to Harris in 1884. summary: Deed, Baltimore County land records, Liber J.B. 84, folios 387 to 389 (MSA CE 62-84; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 387 to 391: the top of 387 is the end of another indenture, recorded Dec. 31, 1873; this deed follows under the heading 'Thomas J. Wilson, Trustee, Henry R. Wilson, Trustee, Deed to James E. Sinclair', and Margaret Slater and others' deed to John Daniel Ahles of part of 'Lukes Adventure' begins on 389). Dated and acknowledged Oct. 24, 1873 before John P. Maddox, J.P. of Baltimore City, who witnessed it (certified Dec. 30, 1873 by George Robinson, Clerk of the Superior Court); recorded Dec. 31, 1873 (John Bacon, Clerk). The Wilsons, with David S. Wilson, as trustees under James Wilson's will, leased Sinclair the lot for 99 years on Oct. 1, 1872 (E.H.A. 77/361). Sinclair paid $800 and the arrears and so was entitled to have the rent extinguished; David S. Wilson being absent from the county, the Circuit Court of Baltimore City (William C. Wilson and others v. David S. Wilson and others) ordered on Oct. 23, 1873 that Thomas J. and Henry R. Wilson deed the reversion alone. The lot, 'adjacent to the village of Waverly': on the west side of the turnpike, 150 ft south of the line of the north end wall of a stone house on a lot lately leased to J. H. Hartman and 475 ft south of Wilson Street, at the south-east corner of Lot No. 7 conveyed to P. P. Pendleton; west 200 ft to the centre of a 20-ft alley; south 22 1/2 ft to the north-east side of Merryman's Lane; south-east 30 ft along the lane 'to the place where the old division fence between Brown's Lot and said Wilson's Land formerly stood'; along that line south-east 175 ft to the turnpike; north 44 1/2 ft to the start. What it settles: (1) the second of the three sources the 1884 deed cites is read: the Wilson-estate lot is the one leased Sinclair in October 1872 (the Towson News item, row 5208) and bought outright in 1873 for $800 ($800 is $48 a year at 6 percent, an inference about the rent). (2) It lies just north of 'Brown's lot', the Huff lot (Andrew Brown to Huff 1866, Huff to Sinclair 1872), so Sinclair held the fork from the apex north: Brown's lot for 10 perches (165 ft), then the Wilson lot for 44 1/2 ft. (3) 3224, 181 to 196 ft north of the lane, falls inside the Wilson lot (165 to about 209 ft) if Brown's 10 perches are measured along the turnpike from the fork (probable, from the measurements; the 1884 lease's second lot begins 164 ft 8 in north of the lane, almost exactly 10 perches). If so, 3224's fee comes from the James Wilson estate, whose Huntington holding at the turnpike dates from 1802 and 1811. What it does not settle: the 1872 lease itself (E.H.A. 77/361), the Merryman deed, and the Wilson estate's title to this exact lot. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): the lease this deed ends is indexed: David S. Wilson and others, trustees, to James E. Sinclair, lease recorded Oct. 2, 1872, E.H.A. 77/361 (776:index-ce256-287-p143-wilson-trustees-1867-1872). Update Oct. 16, 2026 (J.B. 84/381 read): on Oct. 31, 1873, a week after this deed, Sinclair sold the north 30 ft of the Wilson lot to Mary F. Ridgely, $600, from the south-east corner of Pendleton's Lot 7 (J.B. 84/381, 768:mdlr-jb84-381-sinclair-ridgely-north-30-ft-of-wilson-lot-1873), recorded Dec. 31 just ahead of this deed at 387. Sinclair still owned 132 ft 8 in to 197 ft north of the lane in 1884, so the Ridgely strip lies at or north of 197 ft, the Brown-Wilson line met the road at or north of about 182 1/2 ft rather than at 165 ft, and the 165-to-209 ft placement above cannot stand; 3224 (181 ft 4 in to 197 ft) is probably the south 14 1/2 ft Sinclair kept (inference; no plat).

summary: Assignment, Baltimore County land records, Liber J.H.L. 48, folios 236 to 237 (MSA CE 62-48; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 236 to 240; Warfield T. Browning, trustee of the Walnut Hill Copper Mining Company, to Wm. H. Keener follows on 237). Dated and acknowledged Apr. 9, 1866 before John W. Irwin, J.P. of Baltimore County, who witnessed it with R. W. Dougherty; Andrew Brown signs by his mark; recorded Apr. 11, 1866 (Jno. H. Longnecker, Clerk); a margin note records delivery to the grantee on July 11, 1866. Andrew Brown assigns Elizabeth D. Huff, both of Baltimore County, for $1,900, 'part of a tract of land called Huntington ... about two miles on the Baltimore and York Turnpike': beginning at the intersection of the turnpike and 'the road leading to Van Bibbers Mill now called Paradise Mill', ten perches up the road, then square across to the mill road. John Litzinger sold Brown the lot by an assignment of May 17, 1834 (T.K. 237/457). It passes for the rest of the term of 'the original Lease', renewable forever, 'subject to the payment of the yearly rent of one cent'. What it settles: (1) the date: Apr. 9, 1866, not 1856. The 1872 Huff deed's recital was first transcribed as 'fifty six'; this deed, in an 1866 volume, fixes the year. (2) The ground rent is one cent a year: the fork lot sat under a nominal-rent renewable lease, the form of the Gough-era leases of the 1790s (an observation; the original lease is not named). (3) The chain now runs Litzinger (by 1834), Andrew Brown (1834 to 1866), Elizabeth D. Huff (1866 to 1872), James E. Sinclair (1872). (4) The lane was 'the road leading to Van Bibbers Mill now called Paradise Mill' in 1866 and 'Merryman's Lane' by 1872. (5) Huff paid $1,900 in 1866 and sold for $2,500 in 1872. John Litzinger has the name of John Leitzinger, who bought a Huntington leasehold near the 3011 fork in 1847 (row 46153): possibly the same man, not shown. What it does not settle: the original lease and Litzinger's title (T.K. 237/457 should recite them). summary: Assignment, Baltimore County land records, Liber J.H.L. 48, folios 236 to 237 (MSA CE 62-48; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 236 to 240; Warfield T. Browning, trustee of the Walnut Hill Copper Mining Company, to Wm. H. Keener follows on 237). Dated and acknowledged Apr. 9, 1866 before John W. Irwin, J.P. of Baltimore County, who witnessed it with R. W. Dougherty; Andrew Brown signs by his mark; recorded Apr. 11, 1866 (Jno. H. Longnecker, Clerk); a margin note records delivery to the grantee on July 11, 1866. Andrew Brown assigns Elizabeth D. Huff, both of Baltimore County, for $1,900, 'part of a tract of land called Huntington ... about two miles on the Baltimore and York Turnpike': beginning at the intersection of the turnpike and 'the road leading to Van Bibbers Mill now called Paradise Mill', ten perches up the road, then square across to the mill road. John Litzinger sold Brown the lot by an assignment of May 17, 1834 (T.K. 237/457). It passes for the rest of the term of 'the original Lease', renewable forever, 'subject to the payment of the yearly rent of one cent'. What it settles: (1) the date: Apr. 9, 1866, not 1856. The 1872 Huff deed's recital was first transcribed as 'fifty six'; this deed, in an 1866 volume, fixes the year. (2) The ground rent is one cent a year: the fork lot sat under a nominal-rent renewable lease, the form of the Gough-era leases of the 1790s (an observation; the original lease is not named). (3) The chain now runs Litzinger (by 1834), Andrew Brown (1834 to 1866), Elizabeth D. Huff (1866 to 1872), James E. Sinclair (1872). (4) The lane was 'the road leading to Van Bibbers Mill now called Paradise Mill' in 1866 and 'Merryman's Lane' by 1872. (5) Huff paid $1,900 in 1866 and sold for $2,500 in 1872. John Litzinger has the name of John Leitzinger, who bought a Huntington leasehold near the 3011 fork in 1847 (row 46153): possibly the same man, not shown. What it does not settle: the original lease and Litzinger's title (T.K. 237/457 should recite them). summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 2459, folios 514 to 516 (MSA CE 168-2467; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 514 to 518: the top of 514 is Frank F. Knecht and wife's deed to Carlos E. Twitchell of a Carey Street lot; this deed opens at the foot of 514 under the heading 'Henry Bradley &c, Deed to Ellen M. Schaeffer'; J. Frank Dorney's deed to Mary McEvers Tucker follows on 516). Dated and acknowledged Oct. 27, 1908 before R. Legare Webb, notary, who witnessed it with Wm. E. Ferguson; Carrie Bradley signs by her mark; recorded Nov. 2, 1908 shortly after noon (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Henry Bradley and Carrie, his wife, of Baltimore City, convey Ellen M. Schaeffer, for $5 and other consideration, in fee, the 79-ft lot 'on the east side of the York Turnpike Road in the Annex of Baltimore City and immediately to the south of No 4 Baltimore City Engine House' (the 1868 courses), 'and particularly the aforesaid rent' of $150 (March and September), subject to 'the original lease thereof to George Vandyke Smith'. Bradley's title: a deed of Oct. 24, 1908 from 'Edward S. Peirce, Trustee et al', not yet recorded; 'see also for title' R.O. 1888/54 (City) and J.W.S. 160/431 (Baltimore County). What it settles: (1) the 1908 hop is read, and Bradley held the rent for three days: it came from a trustee's sale (Edward S. Peirce, trustee) on Oct. 24, 1908, so Bradley was a buyer for resale or a straw for Schaeffer (an inference). (2) Two older title links are named: J.W.S. 160/431, a Baltimore County deed of about 1887, and R.O. 1888/54, a City deed of 1901 (dates estimated from the liber series), which should reach back toward Coffield. (3) The lot lay immediately south of a city engine house (No. 4 in the Annex numbering, as the deed calls it) in 1908. What it does not settle: the Peirce trust, and the hops from Coffield (1868) to the 1880s. Update Oct. 14, 2026: both cited deeds are read: J.W.S. 160/431 (John H. Stump to Mary Louisa and William Edward Peirce, 1887, 742:mdlr-jws160-431-stump-peirce-150-subrent-1887) and R.O. 1888/54 (Mary Louisa Peirce's 1901 marriage settlement with Edward S. Peirce as trustee, 742:mdlr-ro1888-54-mary-louisa-peirce-marriage-trust-1901).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.F.C. 873, folio 14 (MSA CE 168-11191; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 14 to 18). Dated, acknowledged and recorded May 25, 1960 (recorded 12:30 p.m., James F. Carney, Clerk). Alva M. Shields, of Baltimore City, conveys Delmond F. Shields, 'a single person', 'in consideration of the love and affection existing between them, and of the loving and devoted care and support extended to her by the said Delmond F. Shields for many years', the 3032 leasehold (14 ft beginning 43 ft north of Vineyard Lane 'formerly Gilmore Lane', 82 ft to the alley), subject to the $66 rent. Her title: Allan Eli Cohan's deed of June 30, 1930 (S.C.L. 5137/195). What it settles: (1) the 1960 hop is read: a gift, from Alva to the man who had cared for her for years. The deed does not say he was her son; the 1950 census son, 33, makes it very probable (an inference). (2) Alva's own title is named: Allan Eli Cohan, June 30, 1930. The Shields household was at 3032 from 1919 (directories), so either they rented before 1930 or the 1930 deed is a straw round trip (not shown). What it does not settle: S.C.L. 5137/195 and how Cohan held it. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1930 deeds are read (726:mdlr-scl5137-195-alva-shields-cohan-straw-life-estate-1930): Cohan was a straw; they gave Alva a life estate with full power of sale, remainder to Delmond F. and Charles R. Shields, and recite Aull's 1918 deed to Charles D. and Alva M. Shields (S.C.L. 3281/596). The 1960 gift used that power.

John Litzinger, of Baltimore County, assigns Andrew Brown, for $500, 'a part of a tract of Land called Huntington ... about 2 Miles on the Baltimore and York turnpike': beginning at the intersection of the turnpike and 'the road leading to Van Bibbers Mill', ten perches up the road, then square across to the mill road (the courses of the 1866 and 1872 deeds). Huff (1866 to 1872), James E. Sinclair (1872). (2) Brown bought for $500 in 1834 and sold for $1,900 in 1866, and Huff for $2,500 in 1872: the lot gained buildings in between (the 1866 and 1872 deeds pass 'buildings and improvements'; an inference that the rise is building value). Fielding, recorded June 3, 1887 at 12:30 p.m.; this assignment follows, and William Heinekamp's deed to August Meinicks begins on 433). Dated and acknowledged June 3, 1887 before Geo. McCaffray, J.P. of Baltimore City, who witnessed it (certified by James Bond, Clerk of the Superior Court); recorded the same day at 3 p.m. (John W. Shanklin, Clerk). John H. Stump, of Baltimore City, assigns Mary Louisa Peerce and William Edward Peerce, of Baltimore County, for $5, the lot 'described in a certain sub-lease (the original rent being one cent) from George C. H. Coffield to George Vandyke Smith' of Mar. 2, 1868 (E.H.A. 59/86), 'and especially the subreversion or annual rent of $150 reserved out of said lot by said sublease', subject to one cent a year, 'with the right to all the benefits of renewal in sub-original lease and said sub-lease'. Stump's title: Mary J. Stump's deed of Mar. 10, 1886 (J.W.S. 151/9). What it settles: (1) the reading of the 1868 instrument as a sub-lease under a one-cent lease is confirmed in so many words: 'the original rent being one cent'. (2) The $150 rent's holders now run Coffield (1868), Mary J. Stump (by 1886), John H. Stump (1886 to 1887), Mary Louisa and William Edward Peirce (1887), the Peirce trust (Mary Louisa's share from 1901), Henry Bradley (Oct. 24 to 27, 1908), Ellen M. Schaeffer and her trust (1908 to 1936), Crittenton (1936). (3) The deed spells the grantees 'Peerce'; the 1901 and 1908 deeds 'Peirce'. The Stumps are not shown to be related to John W. Stump, the 1822 trustee by 3010 (a surname only). What it does not settle: Coffield to Mary J. Stump (1868 to 1886) and J.W.S. 151/9.

summary: Deed of trust, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 1888, folios 54 to 56 (MSA CE 168-1896; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 51 to 55, which end mid-acknowledgment on 55: folios 51 to 54 above it hold the Kendall assignment and mortgage of 1900 and 1901 and an Uncle Sam Loan and Savings Company release, recorded Feb. 18, 1901). Dated and acknowledged Feb. 18, 1901 before Thos. C. Bailey, J.P., who witnessed it; Edward S. Peirce made oath the same day (the rest of the oath and the recording stamp are on folio 56). Mary Louisa Peerce, of Baltimore County, 'about to be married', conveys Edward S. Peerce, trustee, all her estate and property, real, personal and mixed, wherever situated: income to her for life for her sole and separate use, whether married or not, without power to anticipate it; then to her children or their descendants per stirpes, held in trust for any under 21; failing issue, as she appoints by will, else to her intestate heirs; the trustee and his successors may sell and reinvest at discretion. What it settles: (1) the 'Edward S. Peirce, Trustee, et al.' who sold the 3117 rent to Henry Bradley on Oct. 24, 1908 is this marriage-settlement trustee: Mary Louisa's half of the rent (with William Edward Peirce's, the 'et al.') passed through it (an inference: the deed names no property). (2) The 1908 deed's citation is 'Liber R.O. No 1888 folio 54', as written; it was misread as 'folio 51' when that deed was filed, and rows 46244 and 46232 are corrected. What it does not settle: her married name, the trustee's relation to her, and the Oct. 24, 1908 trustee's deed to Bradley.

summary: Two deeds, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5137, folios 194 to 196 (MSA CE 168-5145; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 195 to 199: the first deed begins on 194, not on the scan, and ends on 195; the Donohue Hilton Company's deeds to Anna M. and C. Frederick Grebe follow on 196). Both dated June 30, 1930 and acknowledged before David Friedman, notary, who witnessed both; recorded July 11, 1930 at 1:46 and 1:47 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). First, Alva M. Shields conveys the 3032 leasehold (14 ft, 43 ft north of Vineyard Lane 'formerly known as Gilmore Lane', 82 ft to the alley; $66 rent, June and December) to Allan Eli Cohan; it recites Jacob H. Aull's deed of Nov. 6, 1918 to 'Charles D. Shields & Alva M. Shields his wife' (S.C.L. 3281/596), 'the said Charles D. Shields having since departed this life'. Second, Cohan conveys it back to Alva M. Shields for her life, with full power to collect the income, lease, mortgage, sell 'the absolute estate' and consume the proceeds, and on her death whatever is left to Delmond F. Shields and Charles R. Shields equally, the survivor taking all if one dies before her without issue. The second deed types the 1912 grantee as 'Isaac H Aull', a slip for Jacob. What it settles: (1) the 3032 leasehold chain is now complete from 1912: Aull (1912), Charles D. and Alva M. Shields by the entireties (Nov. 6, 1918, the Sun's 1918 sale line), Alva as survivor, the 1930 straw that gave her a life estate with power of sale and named Delmond F. and Charles R. Shields as remaindermen (very probably her sons, an inference: the deed gives no relationship), her 1960 gift to Delmond using that power, and Delmond's estate to the clinic (1972). (2) Charles D. Shields died between 1918 and 1930. (3) Cohan was a straw (the two deeds were recorded a minute apart). What it does not settle: S.C.L. 3281/596 itself, and what became of Charles R. Shields's remainder (the 1960 gift used Alva's power to dispose of the whole). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1918 Aull deed is read (726:mdlr-scl3281-596-aull-shields-3032-1918): Nov. 6, 1918, the fourth lot of Chapman's 1916 assignment, with a building-association mortgage the same day.

summary: Deed of trust, Baltimore County land records, Liber W.G. 72, folios 319 to 324 (MSA CE 66-122; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 319 to 323: the top of 319 is the end of William Brookes's assignment to John Shaw, acknowledged Oct. 12, 1801 and recorded Feb. 4, 1802; this deed opens lower on 319 and runs past 323, so its acknowledgment and recording stamp are not on the scan). Dated Feb. 4, 1802. James Biays, merchant of Baltimore City, for love and affection for his wife Sarah and their children and $1 from each trustee, conveys William Jackson, block maker, and Levin Jones and John Smith, master mariners, all of Baltimore City, three parts of Ensor's Inspection: (1) 9 7/8 acres beginning at 'a bounded red Oak tree (the beginning of a tract of land ... Called Huntington)', which runs to the south-west corner of 'a lot of Ground which formerly belonged to John Gosuch now the property of the said James Biays' and to the end of Walker's last line, from William Spear's representatives (May 30, 1801); (2) Walker's 3 3/8 acres beginning 62 perches north 40 3/4 east of the red oak, with a line south 47 1/4 east 22.4 perches to a stone in the York Road (Mar. 9, 1801, W.G. 66/519); (3) 2 1/4 acres at the northern end of a tract adjoining Biays's land, beginning near the second corner of James Maidwell's land, east 25 perches 'to the main road', south 10 east along it 14 perches 10 ft 4 in, then west 'through the Northern part of the orchard' (from Maidwell, Sept. 26, 1800, W.G. 67/62). The trustees are to let Sarah take the rents and profits for her own use for life, 'notwithstanding her Coverture', and at her death convey in fee to the children of James and Sarah then living, the issue of any dead child taking the parent's share, as tenants in common; failing children, to Biays's heirs. Biays covenants that he holds the land in fee simple without condition. What it settles: (1) both 1801 purchases behind 2958 (Walker's and the Spear heirs', rows 46179 and 46180) went into this trust within a year. (2) It explains the 1840s sellers: the four Biays daughters and their husbands were the children who took the remainder when Sarah died (she was dead by October 1845, row 46130). (3) It names the defendant of the 1847 Chancery case: the 1848 deeds out of the Walker land (to Wilson, row 46178) and to Samuel Brady (row 46149) were made under Allender and wife v. 'William Jackson and others', and William Jackson is the trustee named here (very probably the same man or his heirs; the 1848 deeds do not say). So the 2958 ground passed from Walker (1801) to Biays, into this trust (1802), out of it by the 1847 Chancery sale, and to William T. Wilson (1848) (the trust link is probable). (4) A lot 'formerly ... John Gosuch's' was already Biays's in February 1802; its conveyance into the same trust is W.G. 76/243 (row 714:mdlr-wg76-243-gosuch-trust-harkins-rest-1803). What it does not settle: the recording date (folio 324), and the 1847 Chancery papers.

summary: Deed of trust, Baltimore County land records, Liber W.G. 76, folios 243 to 246 (MSA CE 66-126; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 243 to 247: the top of 243 is the end of Thomas Rutter Jr.'s deed to Solomon Rutter, $6,000, acknowledged May 27, 1803; Henry Alexander's deed to Charles Conaway of part of 'Monzie' follows on 246). Dated and acknowledged May 10, 1803 before Rob. Gosuch and Geo. Gouldsmith Presbury, justices of the peace; John Gosuch signs by his mark; recorded June 7, 1803 (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). John Gosuch, son of Thomas, gentleman, conveys the three Biays trustees, for $1,200, a lot of Ensor's Inspection 'heretofore sold by a certain Job Garretson unto a certain John Harkin': beginning at a stone marked 'I.H. 1765' on the west side of 'the old main road', at or near where the given line of Ensor's Inspection crosses it, north 7 west 26 1/2 perches along the road to stone No. 2, south 26 west 18 perches 2 ft to No. 3, south 7 east 26 1/2 perches to No. 4, then straight back: 3 acres 'called by the Name of Harkin's rest'. Harkin conveyed it to Gosuch on Mar. 4, 1771 (Liber A.L. C, folio 231 as read; the letters are uncertain). It is held on the trusts of the 1802 deed: Sarah Biays's separate use for life, then the children of James and Sarah living at her death. What it settles: (1) the 'lot ... which formerly belonged to John Gosuch now the property of the said James Biays' in the 1802 deed is Harkin's Rest, and it joined the trust in 1803 (Biays had evidently bought it before February 1802; Gosuch conveyed straight to the trustees). (2) It gives the oldest dated mark found on this ground: a stone 'I.H. 1765', very probably John Harkin's initials (an inference), on the old main road where the Ensor's Inspection line crossed it. (3) The Biays holding west of the York Road in the 1802 to 1803 trust was four pieces: Spear's 9 7/8 acres, Walker's 3 3/8, Maidwell's 2 1/4 and Harkin's Rest, 3. Whether the 2958 lot lies in Walker's land (as the 1848 deed says) or reaches Harkin's Rest is not shown. What it does not settle: the Garretson-to-Harkin deed and the 1771 citation. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (County grantor index, Dick and Gorsuch): the County grantor index for Gorsuch finds no deed or mortgage by John Gorsuch of Thomas in 1778 to 1786 (CE 33-2 pp. 134-138, the whole Go run: only an estray notice, W.G. B/290; 714:index-ce33-2-p133-gorsuch-john-1778-1786). From 1787 to 1803 (CE 33-3 and 33-4) his only conveyances of Ensor's Inspection are A.A. 205 (1787, to James Edwards, index p. 151, recorded twelve folios after Maidwell's mortgage, A.A. 193; not read), the 1795 release to Maidwell (S.S. 231) and the 1803 deed of trust (76/243, 3 acres, which is Harkin's Rest, bought from Harkin in 1771, and not this lot). There is no Gorsuch deed to Biays, Walker, Maidwell or Dick in the index, and none between W.G. 53/197 (1798) and 73/72 (1802). So the 5 1/4 acres Gorsuch took from the Speagles in 1778 are not shown sold before the 1787 mortgage, and A.A. 205 is the best candidate for where they went (INFERRED: the index gives no acreage or road, and it could instead be another part of Ensor's Inspection, for example Richard Dick's part, which Edwards held by 1804). The lot that 'formerly belonged to John Gorsuch now the property of the said James Biays' in 1801 (rows 46180, 46685) therefore rests on a deed or contract not indexed under Gorsuch, or on A.A. 205 through Edwards. Next: W.G. A.A. 205 itself (MSA CE 66-76 p. 205; the scan on disk stops at p. 197), read against the 1778 courses (row 47038) and the Edwards deeds. summary: Lease, Baltimore County land records, Liber J.B. 86, folios 487 to 490 (MSA CE 62-86; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 487 to 491: the top of 487 is the end of another instrument certified by the Clerk of the Superior Court of Baltimore City and recorded May 6, 1874 at 2 p.m.; Henry Bowerman and wife's deed to Eliza Bowerman of a St. Denis lot follows on 490). Dated Apr. 16, 1874; Margaret Hamilton acknowledged that day before Frank Lewis, J.P. of Baltimore County, and William Thomas Wilson before H. W. Snowden, J.P. of Baltimore City; recorded May 6, 1874 at 3:40 p.m. (John Bacon, Clerk). William Thomas Wilson, of Baltimore City, leases Margaret Hamilton, wife of Charles Hamilton, of Baltimore County, a lot on the west side of the York Turnpike beginning at the south-east corner of 'a lot of ground belonging, or supposed to, ... A. G. Mott' at a stone, 282 ft west along Mott's lot to a marked stone, 100 ft south to a stake, about 282 ft east to the turnpike, 100 ft north along it. His title: the will of his mother, Henrietta D. A. Wilson, probated by the Baltimore County Orphans' Court on Aug. 29, 1854 (the third digit of the year is faint). Term 99 years from the day before, renewable forever on a $10 fine; $325 a year from June 1, 1874, half-yearly; re-entry after 60 days, forfeiture after six months. Within five years she may buy the fee for $4,642.86 (the $325 at 7 percent), free of the rent but still bound by covenants against liquor saloons, houses of public entertainment, bone, glue and hair factories, butchers, public stables, tanneries, blacksmith shops and any nuisance. What it settles: (1) the citation carried for 'the lease from William Thomas Wilson to Eleanor Cross dated April 16th 1874' (the outline that bounds Keelty's 1907 ground on the north, row 46084) leads to a different lease of the same date: to Margaret Hamilton, of the 100 ft immediately south of Mott's lot (3010 to 3020; that lot began at Gilmor Lane). Wilson very probably made two leases that day, Hamilton's adjoining Mott and Cross's south of it, adjoining the later Keelty ground (an inference; the 1877 plan letters 'Chas. Hamilton' and 'Jno. C. Cross' together north of 30th Street with 'A. Mott', row 714:1877 plan). The instrument that ends at the top of folio 487, recorded at 2 p.m. the same day, is the first candidate for the Cross lease. (2) Henrietta D'Arcy Wilson's will was probated in 1854, so the life estate and power of appointment the Keelty deed describes had passed to William Thomas Wilson by then. (3) Wilson was creating rents at 7 percent with nuisance covenants in 1874. What it does not settle: the Cross lease itself and where on the avenue the two lots end. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the Cross lease is on folios 483 to 487, just before this one (714:mdlr-jb86-483-wilson-elenor-cross-lease-1874); the 2 p.m. instrument is a Myers deed to John C. Cross of a Western Homestead lot. The 1854 probate date is confirmed on that copy. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 6): Charles and Margaret Hamilton mortgaged this lease, with the 79 ft lot at 3113 to 3117 Greenmount, to John T. Ensor on Apr. 21, 1886 for $1,000 (Balt. Co. mortgage J.W.S. 121/373, read; 742:mdlr-jws121-373-hamilton-ensor-mortgage-1000-1886), where it is called a deed of assignment.

summary: Exchange deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 2212, folios 510 to 512 (MSA CE 168-2220; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 510 to 514, a heavily speckled film; the Ninth West Columbia Building Association's release to John G. Delrick follows on 512). Dated and acknowledged Feb. 24, 1906 before T. Bayard Williams, notary; recorded Feb. 26, 1906 at 3 p.m. (Robert Ogle, Clerk). Richard H. Woollen, Howard P. Sadtler and S. Procter Brady, trustees of Samuel Brady's estate, and the Peabody Heights Company (Eugene Levering, president; J. Appleton Wilson, secretary) own adjoining tracts whose division line is 'the Southeast side of a former lane or road now called Gilmor Lane'. To make both more marketable they exchange four irregular lots so the line follows the city blocks: the trustees give Peabody Heights two lots at Calvert and 27th Streets and at Guilford Avenue and 28th Street; Peabody Heights gives the trustees two at Calvert and 28th Streets and at Guilford Avenue and 29th Street. The agreement was reported to the Circuit Court of Baltimore City in the cause administering the trust, 'Martha A. W. Woollen et al. vs Nannie H. Stump et al.' (docket and folio read as '59 A folio 512', uncertain on this film), and ratified. What it settles: (1) the 1906 Peabody Heights deed recited in R.O. 2290/225 is read: a boundary exchange west of the York Road, between Calvert Street and Guilford Avenue, nowhere near the Greenmount frontage. (2) The Brady trust case is Martha A. W. Woollen et al. v. Nannie H. Stump et al., and the trustees in 1906 were Woollen, Sadtler and S. Procter Brady. (3) In 1906 the old Gilmor Lane was the line between the Brady estate (south-east) and Peabody Heights (north-west). It adds nothing on whether 2958 was ever Brady land.

The fee title is a chain of four: Henry L. Rocklin's assignment of the leasehold to J. Paul Rocklin and wife (May 12, 1953, M.L.P. 9152/237); Henry Lewis Rosenthal and wife's deed to them (Sept. 14, 1953, M.L.P. 9274/275), very probably the reversion, so the rent merged in 1953 (an inference: the deed does not say); their 1959 lease to Arthur L. Rocklin (J.F.C. 774/114); and a 1960 trustee's deed from Norman P. Rocklin to Arthur (J.F.C. 798/457), a round trip that left the fee in the family before the sale. What it settles: (1) 2936 was a ground-rent leasehold until 1953, the reversion held by Henry Lewis Rosenthal. (2) It is measured from the same base as 2958: 248 ft 9 1/2 in here, 402 ft 9 1/2 in for 2958 (rows 46073, 46088), exactly eleven 14-ft lots apart. It names no common seller or original lessor before 1953. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1953 deed is read (704:mdlr-mlp9274-275-rosenthal-rocklin-2936-1953): the $75 rent was created by Earl Hoffmaster in 1944 and sold to the Rosenthals the same day; Hoffmaster held 2936 in fee before.

summary: Deeds, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 4728, folios 193 to 201 (MSA CE 168-4736; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 192 to 201: 192 is the end of a Hahn and Coleman mortgage on Riggs Avenue). Three Swormstedt instruments, all recorded Apr. 27, 1927 at 2:30 and 2:35 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). (1) Folio 193: Martha and Mary L. Swormstedt assign their brother Richard a mortgage of their father's estate (Mar. 30, 1927); it recites that Richard Swormstedt senior died on or about Aug. 28, 1913 (the day as read), will H.W.J. 116/331, leaving all to his wife Barbara C. Swormstedt for life, then their three children, and that Barbara died about Oct. 13, 1926. (2) Folios 194 to 198: the deed of Mar. 29, 1927 from Richard Swormstedt, of Douglas, Wyoming, and Martha and Mary L. Swormstedt, all unmarried, to Robert N. Baer, so that Baer might reconvey by the dividing deeds of Mar. 30, 1927, of eleven ground-rent lots. Six were Barbara's own (her will dated Apr. 7, 1924, probated Oct. 26, 1926, E.R.D. 156/455); the seventh was held by Barbara and Richard 'as tenants by the entireties'; four more were bought by her as trustee with his estate's money. The seventh is the 3010 lot: on the west side of the turnpike 36 ft south of a stone at the south-west corner of the turnpike and Gilmor Lane ('known as the road running between the lands of Mrs Gilmore and Mrs Biays and also called a road leading from the lands of Hugh Thompsons' into the York Turnpike Road'), 67 ft 11 2/5 in on the turnpike to Mary Clemens's south line, 215 ft west, 82 ft north to the lane, 53 ft on the lane, then around the Nicoll-to-Leicht sub-lease (cited 'A.W.B. 374/156', a slip for 394); its rent is $180 a year quarterly, February, May, August and November. Its source: 'a deed from John P. Clarke Executor &c to Richard Swormstedt and Barbara C. Swormstedt dated December 16th 1903' (R.O. 2050/46). Richard junior acknowledged in Converse County, Wyoming on Apr. 22, 1927; his sisters in Baltimore on Mar. 30 before Chas. H. Taylor. (3) Folios 198 to 201: a second deed of the same date to Baer of the lots devised by Richard senior's will (dated June 15, 1909): York Road at 23rd Street, Baltimore Street and Bouldin Street. What it settles: (1) how the Swormstedts held the $180 reversion on 3010: Richard and Barbara C. Swormstedt bought it from John P. Clarke, executor, on Dec. 16, 1903, two years after Mary Clemens created the rent; Barbara held it as survivor from 1913 and died in October 1926; her three children divided her estate through Baer in March 1927, and the 3010 rent went to Martha and Mary L. (row 46208). (2) Mary Clemens therefore sold the reversion to someone, or it passed through an estate, between October 1901 and December 1903: whose executor John P. Clarke was is the next question (R.O. 2050/46). What it does not settle: R.O. 2050/46 itself. Update Oct. 14, 2026: R.O. 2050/46 is read (719:mdlr-ro2050-46-duggan-executors-swormstedt-3010-rent-1903): John P. Clark and James B. Kailer were executors of Francis P. Duggan, who bought the $180 rent from Mary Clemens on Oct. 31, 1901 (R.O. 1928/238); the Swormstedts paid $3,000, the rent at 6 percent.

summary: Assignment, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 4836, folios 513 to 514 (MSA CE 168-4844; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 513 to 517). Dated and acknowledged Jan. 14, 1928 before Emma Roberts, notary, who witnessed it; recorded Jan. 17, 1928 at 10:51 a.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk), a minute after the Waverly Building Association's release of Wyman's 1927 mortgage (George E. Leight, president; Lennox B. Clemens, attorney) and a minute before the Wolfes' own mortgage. John E. Wyman, of Baltimore City, conveys William H. and Carrie Wolfe, for $5 and other consideration, the lot on the south-east side of Gilmor Lane: from the end of the second line of the 1896 Dodson-to-Mary Clemens deed (R.O. 1615/24), 75 ft east to the south-west corner of the Wood lot (the 1901 lease, R.O. 1928/77), 82 ft north along it to the lane, 125 ft back along the lane. It passes for the rest of the term, renewable forever, subject to $54 a year (April 15 and October 15). Wyman's title: Mary Clemens's deed of Apr. 21, 1919 (S.C.L. 3348/167). The same day the Wolfes mortgaged it to the Kennedy Hill Permanent Building and Loan Association for $910 on seven shares, 'part of the purchase price'. What it settles: (1) how the Wolfes held the Vineyard Lane lot behind 3010 that they deeded to Charles T. Leight in 1953 (row 46199): as a $54 leasehold from Wyman (1928), whose rent they bought out in 1937 (719:mdlr-scl5742-413-harding-wolfe-vineyard-lane-reversion-1937). (2) The Wolfes bought this lot two months after buying the 3010 leasehold with the Leights (Nov. 1927). What it does not settle: S.C.L. 3348/167 (how Mary Clemens conveyed a leasehold she had created, presumably her lessee Wood's interest come back to her; an open question). Update Oct. 14, 2026: S.C.L. 3348/167 is read (719:mdlr-scl3348-167-mary-clemens-wyman-vineyard-lane-1919): Mary Clemens to Wyman, Apr. 21, 1919, from Wood's 1903 assignment back to her.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5742, folios 413 to 415 (MSA CE 168-5750; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 413 to 417: Rudolph M. Winterling's deed of 2335 Druid Hill Avenue is above it on 413, and Adolph H. Schlag's deed of a Harford Road lot to David W. Chertkof follows on 415). Dated July 14, 1937 and acknowledged that day in Northumberland County, Virginia before W. C. Blackwell, notary; witnessed by T. M. Spangler; recorded July 21, 1937 at noon (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Rose I. Harding, widow, of Northumberland County, Virginia, conveys William H. and Carrie Wolfe, by the entireties, for $5 and other consideration, the Vineyard Lane lot (the courses of the 1928 Wyman deed) 'and particularly the aforesaid rent', 'to the end and intent that the reversion and aforesaid annual ground rent ... be forever merged and extinguished'. The rent was reserved by Mary Clemens and her husband's lease to Allen K. Wood of Apr. 17, 1902 (R.O. 1952/245), $54 a year, April and October; the reversion was among the lots James B. Guyton conveyed to Rose I. Conway (now Harding) and Mary L. Conway as joint tenants on July 30, 1910 (S.C.L. 2599/429); Mary L. Conway died about Oct. 5, 1916. What it settles: (1) the Vineyard Lane lot's two estates: Mary Clemens leased it to Allen K. Wood on Apr. 17, 1902 at $54, six months after leasing him the 3010 lot at $180; the leasehold reached Wyman (1919) and the Wolfes (1928); the reversion went from Mary Clemens to James B. Guyton (how and when not shown) and to the Conways (1910), and merged in the Wolfes in 1937. (2) Allen K. Wood was the Clemenses' lessee for both lots behind the corner. What it does not settle: R.O. 1952/245 itself, how Guyton took the reversion, and S.C.L. 3348/167. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1902 lease is read and the rent went straight to Mary L. Conway for $900 the same day (719:mdlr-ro1952-245-mary-clemens-wood-lease-conway-rent-vineyard-lane-1902), so Guyton's 1910 deed to Rose I. and Mary L. Conway was very probably a straw for a joint tenancy (inference).

summary: Assignment, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. 9509, folios 244 to 245 (MSA CE 168-9517; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 244 to 248, with the start of the mortgage on 246). Dated and acknowledged June 18, 1954 (Edward F. Lastner, vice president of Straw Man, Inc., before Mary Louise Willeke, notary); recorded June 21, 1954 (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk). Straw Man, Inc. assigns Harry W. and Bertha J. Hoover, by the entireties, for $5 and other consideration, 3014 Vineyard Lane: on the north-west side of Vineyard Lane 'formerly called Gilmor Lane', 156 ft north-east of Cat Bird Lane 'formerly Wilson Lane', 18 ft on the lane, 75 ft back to a 10-ft alley, 70 ft west along it to the north-east corner of the thirty-third lot of the 1887 Brune-to-Aull lease (J.W.S. 163/9), then 82 ft 6 in and 7 ft 6 in back to the lane. It is 'the entire lot of ground described in the lease from Levi A. Barnett and Helen A. Barnett, his wife, to the said Straw Man, Inc.', 99 years renewable forever at $90 a year (June 18 and December 18), dated the same day and recorded just before. The Hoovers gave William H. Logue and Margaret M. Davies a $4,500 purchase-money mortgage the same day (folio 246). What it settles: (1) Hoover's 1954 leasehold (row 46210) came through a straw: the Barnetts, as owners, leased 3014 to Straw Man, Inc. at $90 and Straw Man assigned the leasehold to the Hoovers, so the Barnetts kept a $90 rent and the Hoovers paid a capital price (the standard Baltimore way of selling a house while creating a ground rent). (2) Straw Man, Inc. is the same straw company of the Silbigers' 1965 deeds of 2958 (row 46183). (3) This first $90 rent is not the 1960 $90 rent: per row 46210 an older rent was merged in 1956, and Hoover created the new $90 rent by his 1960 lease to Bordley (inference connecting the two rows). What it does not settle: the Barnett lease itself, how the Barnetts held 3014, and the 1956 merger.
