Dated and acknowledged Jan. 19, 1959 before Jacqueline M. Campbell, notary, who witnessed it; recorded Jan. 30, 1959 (James F. Carney, Clerk). Marjorie C. Gamble, unmarried, of Baltimore County, conveys 3014 Vineyard Lane (the 1954 courses) to Harry W. Hoover for life, with full power to sell, lease, mortgage or convey the whole except by will and to use the proceeds, and at his death, if the powers are unused, to his daughter Roma Vernelle Hoover in fee. Her title: a deed of the same day from 'Hardy W. Hoover, also known as Harry W. Hoover, and Bertha J. Hoover, his wife', recorded just before. What it settles: (1) the 1959 deed behind Hoover's 1960 lease to Bordley (row 46210) is read: a straw round trip through Marjorie C. Gamble that ended Bertha J. Hoover's share and gave Harry a life estate with power of sale, remainder to Roma Vernelle Hoover. (2) It describes the lot without a ground rent and calls the grant fee simple, consistent with the 1956 merger of the 1954 $90 rent (row 46210). What it does not settle: why Bertha joined in giving up her share (not stated).

summary: Lease, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 1730, folios 92 to 94 (MSA CE 168-1738; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 92 to 96; the Maryland Building and Loan Association's deed of 1310 Milton Avenue to Ella Virginia Vander Horst follows on 94). Dated and acknowledged Apr. 18, 1898 before John J. Dunn, J.P., who witnessed it; recorded Apr. 25, 1898 (Robert Ogle, Clerk). Augustus D. Clemens Jr. and Mary, of Baltimore County, lease Jacob H. Aull, of Baltimore City, the tip lot at the fork: from a point on the east side of the turnpike 204 ft 7 in south of the two-mile stone in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot (281 ft 2 in south of the north side of Bateman's Alley), 58 ft 4 in south to the south-west corner of the whole ground, N 89 E about 8 ft 6 in to the north-west side of Old York Road, N 31 1/2 E 66 ft along it, then 42 ft 4 in straight back; part of Shepard G. Miller's 1897 deed (R.O. 1710/153). Term 99 years from the date, renewable forever on a $10 fine; $75 a year from May 1, 1898, half-yearly (May and November); re-entry after 60 days, forfeiture after a year. Directly above it, ending at the top of folio 92, is a deed by the same Clemenses, the same day, conveying a lot 'unto the said Lulie H Wallace ... in fee simple subject however to the leasehold estate aforesaid'. What it settles: (1) the 1898 lease of 3011 is read, with its terms ($75, May and November, $10 fine). (2) The reversion: Clemens sold Lulie H. Wallace the fee of this lot subject to the Aull lease the same day (the end of that deed is on this folio; its start, on folio 91, was not saved: probable), so the $75 rent and the leasehold split at once, as at 3017 in 1903. The 1907 Wallace deed (720:mdlr-ro2320-441-william-hall-wallace-lulie-wallace-3011-reversion-1907) carries the rent from Lulie through William Hall Wallace and back. (3) Jacob H. Aull, the developer of 3026 to 3032 in 1912, took the 3011 leasehold in 1898. What it does not settle: folio 91, and how Aull's leasehold reached Sinclair (the 1906 assignment). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the start of the Wallace deed is read (720:mdlr-ro1730-91-clemens-lulie-wallace-3011-rent-1898): $1,250 for the fee and $75 rent, the rent at 6 percent; the probable reading is confirmed.

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5419, folios 571 to 573 (MSA CE 168-5427; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 571 to 575; the recording stamp is not on the pages read). Dated and acknowledged Apr. 7, 1934 before Lennox B. Clemens, notary; John G. Maier, president of the association, made oath. The Sinclairs owe the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County $1,913.29, repaid monthly at 6 percent, with the right to have the first lot released for $1,000, and mortgage it four lots: (1) 202 Homewood Terrace (from the Baltimore Discount Company, 1925, S.C.L. 4502/519), a leasehold at $180, also under a Home Owners Loan Corporation mortgage of the same day; (2) 3011 and (3) 3013, in fee; (4) a lot beginning on 'the fourth line of description in an Assignment from M. Estelle Bateman to The Provident Savings Bank', the centre line of an 8-ft alley, 28 ft 6 1/4 in east of Greenmount Avenue at the west side of a frame building, 24 ft south along it, 86 ft 6 in east to Old York Road, 24 ft 11 in north-east to the alley centre, 92 ft 8 in back: a one-cent leasehold ('the annual rent of one cent if demanded'). Lots 2 to 4 are the three of Riepe's 1927 deed (S.C.L. 4707/12). What it settles: (1) the 1934 Sinclair mortgage is read; with the 1930 one it accounts for the releases of 1938 and 1954. (2) The Sinclairs' third Riepe lot, the one-cent leasehold, lies behind a frame building on the Greenmount-to-Old York Road block, measured from an alley line named in the 1904 Bateman-to-Provident deed (R.O. 2062/398, row on 3111): it is Coffield-tract ground near 3105 to 3111, held at the tract's one cent (an inference about which lot; the deed gives no house number). What it does not settle: the exact place of the fourth lot and the recording date. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the fourth lot is placed: Provident Savings Bank assigned it to Sinclair on Mar. 26, 1920 and he assigned it back on July 9, 1934 (737:mdlr-scl5455-522-sinclair-provident-one-cent-lot-1934): ground behind the bank, from M. Estelle Bateman's 1904 assignment.

summary: Executors' deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 2050, folios 46 to 48 (MSA CE 168-2058; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 46 to 50; the Assurance Permanent Loan and Savings Association's release to Edmund T. Horner follows on 48). Dated and acknowledged Dec. 16, 1903 before Wilmer Emory, J.P., who witnessed it; recorded the same day about noon (Robert Ogle, Clerk). John P. Clark (written 'Clarke' in the 1927 recital) and James B. Kailer, executors of Francis P. Duggan of Baltimore City (will dated June 8, 1901, Wills S.R.M. 91/446, with power to sell this property), sold at private sale about Nov. 10, 1903, ratified by the Orphans' Court, to Richard and Barbara C. Swormstedt by the entireties, for $3,000, the $180 rent and reversion of the 3010 lot (the courses of the 1927 deeds). Duggan's title: Mary Clemens and husband's deed of Oct. 31, 1901 (R.O. 1928/238), 'being the Reversion or Ground Rent of $180.00', the same day as the lease to Allen K. Wood (R.O. 1928/77). What it settles: (1) whose estate John P. Clark served: Francis P. Duggan's. (2) Mary Clemens created the $180 rent and sold it the same day, as she did at 3017 (1903) and 3011 (1898): a builder's pattern of leasing a lot and selling the rent at once. (3) The executors' price is the rent at exactly 6 percent ($180 / 0.06 = $3,000). The 3010 rent chain is now read from its creation: Clemens (Oct. 31, 1901), Duggan (same day), his executors to the Swormstedts (1903), the 1927 partition, the Wolfes (1930), Leight (1950, merged). What it does not settle: R.O. 1928/238 itself (the rent deed of 1901, its price) and Duggan's dates. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1901 deed to Duggan is read (719:mdlr-ro1928-238-mary-clemens-duggan-3010-rent-1901): $3,000, the same 6 percent price.

West's deed to Mary E. Sauerwein is above it on 245). (1) The lease, dated and acknowledged Apr. 17, 1902 before Chas. J. Fox, notary of Baltimore County, recorded the same day at noon (Robert Ogle, Clerk): Mary Clemens and her husband Augustus D. Clemens Jr. lease Allen K. Wood the lot on the south-east side of Gilmor Lane behind his 1901 lot (75 ft from the end of the Dodson deed's second line to Wood's south-west corner, 82 ft north to the lane, 125 ft back along it), for 99 years from the date, renewable forever on a $10 fine, at $54 a year from Apr. 15, 1902. (2) The deed, folio 247, the same day: the Clemenses convey Mary L. Conway the same lot for $900, that is the $54 rent at 6 percent (the deed continues on 248, not saved). What it settles: (1) the 1902 lease the 1937 Harding deed recites is read. (2) The rent was sold at once to Mary L. Conway, not first to James B. Guyton: so the 1910 deed from Guyton to Rose I. and Mary L. Conway as joint tenants (S.C.L. 2599/429) was very probably a straw to make the sisters joint tenants (an inference). summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 1730, folios 91 to 92 (MSA CE 168-1738; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 88 to 92). Dated and acknowledged Apr. 18, 1898 before Wm. D. Wright, J.P., who witnessed it; recorded Apr. 25, 1898 (Robert Ogle, Clerk), just before the Aull lease on 92. The Clemenses convey Lulie H. Wallace, of Baltimore City, in fee, for $1,250, the 3011 lot 'in the Village of Waverly', subject to the Aull lease of the same day ($75 from May 1, 1898), 'and especially the clear yearly rent of seventy five dollars'. On folio 90 the Loyola Perpetual Building Association, two days earlier, released from Clemens's December 1897 mortgage (R.O. 1710/154) the reversion of the Aull lot, a lot Clemens held under a lease from Henry C. Huff and wife, and the lot Clemens sold William L. Fink in fee (3013), leaving the mortgage on the rest. What it settles: (1) the start of the Wallace deed, whose end was read on folio 92: the 3011 rent's first sale, $1,250, the rent at 6 percent, so the chain of the 3011 rent is read from creation to Sinclair's merger in 1921. (2) Henry C. Huff (later president of the Waverly Building Association, 1903) had leased Clemens a lot near the fork before April 1898, so Clemens held part of the Miller ground as a Huff lessee (inference from the release; the Huff lease is not read). What it does not settle: the Huff lease.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 2369, folios 13 to 14 (MSA CE 168-2377; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 13 to 17; Monro Smith's assignment to Albert Ottilber follows on 14). Dated, acknowledged before Wm. H. Watson, J.P., and recorded Sept. 17, 1907 (Robert Ogle, Clerk). Mary K. Fink conveys Leopold Lehmann, in fee, for $5, the 3017 lot (156 ft 5 in south of the two-mile stone in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot, at the south-west corner of the 1898 Aull lease, R.O. 1728/284) 'and particularly the rent or reversion', subject to the Willis lease of Oct. 1, 1903 (R.O. 2037/211, $54). Her title as recited: 'a deed dated July 31st 1907 ... Liber R O No 2358 folio 421 ... from Estella Fink to said Mary K Fink'. What it settles: (1) the one unpulled deed in the 3017 rent chain is read: Fink to Lehmann, September 1907. (2) A second Fink, Estella, held the rent for a time between 1903 and July 1907 (how she took it from Mary K. is not recited: perhaps a straw or a family transfer, not shown). The chain now reads Clemens (1903), Mary K. Fink (1903), Estella Fink (to July 1907), Mary K. Fink, Leopold Lehmann (1907), Mary C. Lehmann, the Sinclairs (1946), the Vinsons (1951). What it does not settle: R.O. 2358/421 and the Finks' relationship to William L. Fink of 3013. Update Oct. 14, 2026: R.O. 2358/421 is read (721:mdlr-ro2358-421-mary-estella-fink-straw-3017-rent-1907): Estella Fink was a same-day straw, Mary K. to Estella and back, July 31, 1907. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Fink deeds S.C.L. 2559/393 and 3126/290 read): Mary K. Fink is Mary Catherine Fink and Estella Fink her sister, two of the four children of William L. Fink of 3013 (will of Feb. 2, 1893; deed S.C.L. 2559/393, Feb. 9, 1910). The Finks' relationship to William L. Fink, left open above, is answered by the family's own recitals: the 3017 rent holder of 1903 to 1907 is his daughter, who co-owned 3013 from 1910.

summary: Lease, Baltimore County land records, Liber J.B. 86, folios 483 to 487 (MSA CE 62-86; read in full on the scan Jeff saved, pages 481 to 486, the stamp on 487 read earlier). Dated Apr. 16, 1874, acknowledged the same day by Elenor Cross before Frank Lewis, J.P. of Baltimore County, and by William Thomas Wilson before H. W. Snowden, J.P. of Baltimore City; recorded May 6, 1874. William Thomas Wilson leases Elenor Cross, wife of John C. Cross, of Baltimore County, a lot on the west side of the York Turnpike beginning at the south-east corner of 'the lot of ground leased by Indenture of even date herewith to Margaret Hamilton', 282 ft west along it, 35 ft south, about 282 ft east to the turnpike, 35 ft north along it; title from his mother Henrietta D. A. Wilson's will, probated Aug. 29, 1854 (the year is clear on this copy). Term 99 years renewable forever on a $10 fine; $113.75 a year from June 1, 1874 (June and December); buyout within five years at $1,625, the rent at 7 percent, as in the Hamilton lease; the same nuisance covenants. Above it (folios 482 to 483), recorded at 2 p.m. the same day, is Thomas and Sarah Ann Myers's deed to John C. Cross of a lot on Jefferson Street in the Western Homestead, part of 'Ensors Inspection', merging a $45 rent (Fox to Cross lease of 1867, E.H.A. 57/219): another Cross holding, not this lot. What it settles: (1) the Cross lease the Keelty deed bounds on is read: 35 ft directly south of the Hamilton lot, which is 100 ft directly south of A. G. Mott's lot. So from Mott's south-east corner on the turnpike the frontage runs Hamilton 100 ft, Cross 35 ft, then Keelty's ground (about 118 ft) and the 2944 to 2958 row (arithmetic from the three instruments; where 30th Street was cut through is not stated in any of them). (2) Henrietta D. A. Wilson's will was probated Aug. 29, 1854: confirmed. (3) The 1874 leases of the Wilson frontage at Waverly all carry the same 7 percent buyouts and nuisance covenants. What it does not settle: whether the Cross lot became fee, and where 30th Street falls in these lines.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County land records, Liber W.G. 67, folio 62 (MSA CE 66-117; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 60 to 62; the end is on 63, read earlier, row 46254). John O'Donnell's lease to Peter Ealer of a Water Street lot in the city is on 60 to 62 above it. Dated Sept. 26, 1800. James Maidwell, of Baltimore City, sells James Biays, of the same place, for 450 Spanish milled dollars or £168 15s Maryland currency, 2 1/4 acres 'in the northern extremity of a tract of land lying in Baltimore County adjoining the land of the said James Biays being part of a tract of land called Ensors inspection': from near a stone at the second corner of Maidwell's land, N 76 1/2 E 25 perches 'to the main Road, or as near to it as elder surveys will permit', S 10 E along the main road 14 perches 10 ft 4 in, then S 88 W 'thro the northern part of the Orchard' to the tract's first line and along it to the start, 'no more nor no less'; with general warranty. No source of Maidwell's title is recited. What it settles: (1) the Maidwell deed is now read in full: the land was the north end of Maidwell's own tract of Ensor's Inspection, fronting the main road (the York Road), with an orchard; Biays already owned the land next to it in September 1800, before the 1801 Walker and Spear purchases (so Biays had an earlier holding, not identified). (2) The 'moiety' of folio 63 is this 2 1/4-acre part. What it does not settle: Maidwell's title and Biays's earlier land. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): a lead for Maidwell's title: John Gorsuch (son of Thomas) to James Maidwell, a release dated Feb. 14, 1795 of part of Ensor's Inspection, reciting Maidwell's deed to Gorsuch of Feb. 26, 1787, begins at the foot of W.G. S.S. 231 (seen on the scan of the 1795 Merryman lease). Its N 76 1/2 E 25-perch line 'to the main road' and S 10 E course along the road are courses of this 1800 deed, so it is very probably Maidwell's title (inference); folios 231 to 235 are loaded for Jeff. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (later): the 1795 release is read (714:mdlr-wgss231-gorsuch-maidwell-release-ensors-inspection-1795): Maidwell held nine acres of Ensor's Inspection on the main road, mortgaged to John Gorsuch in 1787 (W.G. AA/193) and cleared in 1795; this 1800 deed's 2 1/4 acres were their northern tip, from stone M on the Garretson line. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Maidwell to Edwards read): the rest of Maidwell's nine acres went to James Edwards, 2 1/2 acres on Mar. 25, 1801 (W.G. 66/123) and 3 acres on Sept. 11, 1804 (W.G. 82/206), the latter beginning at the J B stone at the south-east corner of this 2 1/4 acres (rows 714:mdlr-wg66-123-maidwell-edwards-2-5-acres-1801 and 714:mdlr-wg82-206-maidwell-edwards-3-acres-1804).

Rocklin, by the entireties, in fee, 2936 Greenmount Avenue (248 ft 9 1/2 in north of 29th Street, 14 ft, 100 ft to the alley) 'and especially the annual ground rent and reversionary interest', so that the rent be merged. The rent: Earl Hoffmaster and wife's lease of Mar. 7, 1944 to Christina Caparrola, $75 a year (March 7 and September 7, M.L.P. 6570/338); the same day the Hoffmasters sold the Rosenthals the reversion (M.L.P. 6570/339). The Rocklins held the leasehold by Henry L. Rocklin's assignment of May 12, 1953 (M.L.P. 9152/237). What it settles: (1) the 2936 ground rent was a 1944 creation, not an original row rent: Earl Hoffmaster held 2936 in fee before March 1944, leased it and sold the rent at once. (2) So 2936 names no row-era lessor; the next step back is Hoffmaster's own deed. What it does not settle: how Hoffmaster took 2936. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1944 instruments are read (704:mdlr-mlp6570-338-hoffmaster-lease-rosenthal-rent-posner-2936-1944): Caparrola was a straw lessee and Victor Posner bought the leasehold; the Hoffmasters had 2936 from the Clarkes and Oehrls, Jan. 8, 1943 (M.L.P. 6413/203).

Milton Brandt, notary, who witnessed it; recorded Nov. 10, 1953 (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk). G. Agatha Riordan, unmarried, conveys 2934 Greenmount Avenue to Ann B. Lyons for life, with full power to sell, mortgage or lease the whole (not by will) and to consume the proceeds, remainder to Daniel J. Lyons; she had it the same day from Ann B. Lyons, widow, so she was a straw. No earlier title is recited. What it settles: (1) the 1953 2934 deed is a straw round trip that set up the life estate used in the 1966 sale (row 46259). (2) J. Milton Brandt, the broker and notary of the 1924 and 1925 2958 sales (rows on 714), also handled 2934 in 1953. It does not reach the row's builder; the next step is Ann B. Lyons's own title (not recited). Update Oct. 14, 2026 (night): the start of the Lyons title is read (703:mdlr-scl2390-425-keelty-lyons-lease-2934-1907): James Keelty's 99-year lease to Frank A. and Catherine Lyons, Dec. 6, 1907, $60 a year; the rent went to the Fischers that month (S.C.L. 2394/467). The step to Ann B. Lyons and the end of the rent are not yet found.

summary: Opening page of a trustees' deed, Baltimore County land records, Liber E.H.A. 65, folio 404 (MSA CE 62-65; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 401 to 404; the deed continues on 405 to 407, on disk since September and filed in Corridor). Dated Feb. 3, 1870. David S., Thomas J. and Henry R. Wilson, all of Baltimore County, trustees, to the President, Managers and Company of the Baltimore and Yorktown Turnpike Road. It recites that 'a certain lot of ground on the west side of the York Turnpike Road known or formerly known as the gate house lot ... has been for sixty years or more in the possession under claim of title' of the company, and that by an indenture of May 14, 1844 (T.K. 341/328) 'the late Alexander Contee Magruder conveyed or intended to convey in fee to the late James Wilson of the City of Baltimore a certain' [tract, continued on 405]. The margin notes delivery on June 18, 1871 to J. Fox. What it settles: (1) the missing opening of the 1870 deed: the company had held the gate-house lot by possession since about 1810 or before, without a deed, and the Wilson trustees, heirs to Magruder's 1844 conveyance to James Wilson, gave it one (with folio 405's memorandum that Wilson held title for the company). (2) A new County hop above the toll-gate corner: Magruder to James Wilson, May 14, 1844 (T.K. 341/328). The gate-house lot is the corner at Gilmor Lane that the company sold Aull in 1912 for 3026 to 3032 (the 1912 deed recites a Wilson-trustee deed of July 5, 187-, E.H.A. 70/92, for 'all that property'; whether that is this deed's lot or a second lot is open). What it does not settle: T.K. 341/328 itself and E.H.A. 70/92. Update Oct. 14, 2026: Magruder's 1844 deed is read (725:mdlr-tk341-328-magruder-trustee-james-wilson-huntington-1844): $1,025 for 3 a 1 r 12 p of Huntington between Gough's road and the turnpike, sold as trustee under Philip G. Biays's 1826 deed of trust (W.G. 184/618). Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): the gate-house lot itself went to the company by a separate deed of July 5, 1871 (725:mdlr-eha80-97-wilson-trustees-turnpike-first-toll-gate-house-lot-4-1871), Lot 4 of the Huntingdon plat, 57 ft at Gilmor's Lane; this 1870 deed's 50 ft lies north of the gate.

summary: Deed of redemption, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. 8123, folios 414 to 416 (MSA CE 168-8131; read on the scan Jeff saved). Dated June 13, 1950, acknowledged that day in Baltimore County before Howard F. Sieber, notary, for the trustee by A. F. Dempsey, vice president; recorded June 15, 1950 at 11:30 a.m. (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk). Francis X. Hooper's will (Baltimore County Wills W.J.R. 19/182; City J.H.B. 217/204) left a third to his widow Florence W. Hooper and two-thirds in trust to the Mercantile Trust and Deposit Company and William Jenkins; the 1917 division deed (S.C.L. 3177/132) gave the trustees this lot; Jenkins died. The Spellmans, leaseholders since 1917 (S.C.L. 3109/316), gave notice to redeem, and for $1,200 (the $72 at 6 percent) the trustee conveys them the reversion and rent of 3026 so that the lease 'be merged in the fee'. What it settles: (1) the 1950 redemption the 1967 deed recites is read: $1,200, on the Spellmans' statutory notice. (2) It fixes the Hooper trust's documents: the will's two citations and the 1917 division. What it does not settle: nothing new upstream.

summary: Division deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 3177, folios 132 to 136 and following (MSA CE 168-3185; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 132 to 136, which end before the deed does; the Geiler mortgage ends at the top of 132). Dated Dec. 7, 1917. Francis X. Hooper, late of Baltimore County, left his estate a third to his widow Florence W. Hooper and two-thirds to the Mercantile Trust and Deposit Company of Baltimore and William Jenkins in trust; the widow and the trustees divide the real estate, the widow taking lots in Beaumont Park, Idlewylde and elsewhere in Baltimore County, the trustees taking, among others, 'all those four lots' on the west side of Greenmount Avenue 'formerly the York Turnpike Road' at Vineyard Lane 'formerly Gilmor Lane', beginning at the corner and at 15, 29 and 43 ft north of it (3026, 3028, 3030 and 3032). What it settles: (1) the Hooper division deed recited in the 1950, 1964 and 1967 deeds is read: the four Aull rents bought by Hooper in December 1912 ($4,500) went to his testamentary trust in 1917, which sold them one by one (3028 in 1945, 3026 in 1950, 3032 in 1964; 3030's rent was elsewhere by 1944, see 726:mdlr-mlp8386-70-interrante-podlich-3030-1951). What it does not settle: the folios after 136 and the recording date. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (late): the 3030 rent the Interrantes bought in 1944 (M.L.P. 6549/594, read) was a 1935 rent created by the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County, which then held 3030 in fee; how the trust's 1912 rent on 3030 ended is not read. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (1935 read): the 1935 instruments are read (S.C.L. 5518/171 to 175, rows 47394 to 47396). The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County took the 3030 leasehold by assignment from David McCoy and wife, July 8, 1932 (S.C.L. 5312/27), and the reversion by a deed from 'the Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore et al Trustees', Feb. 18, 1935 (folio not given; very probably the Hooper trust selling the 1912 $66 rent, an inference), so the 1912 lease and rent met in the Association. On Feb. 25, 1935 it leased 3030 to Helen M. Bordley at $66, sold that new rent to Charles T. and Ella B. Leight for $1,100, and took the lease back from Bordley the same day (a straw, inference). Bordley's 1943 assignment to the Interrantes is M.L.P. 6513/139 (row 47397). Update Oct. 16, 2026 (5313/27 read): the McCoy assignment that the 1935 instruments cite as 'Liber S C L No 5312 folio 27' is recorded at S.C.L. 5313/27 (MSA CE 168-5321; Grantor Index 1932, row 47520), on a folio whose typed header reads '5312', corrected by hand to 5313. It is read (726:mdlr-scl5313-27-mccoy-waverly-bldg-assignment-3030-1932): David and Mary E. McCoy assigned the 3030 leasehold to The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County on July 8, 1932 (recorded July 12) for $5 and other valuable considerations, subject to the 1912 rent of $66 due June 1 and Dec. 1; they held it by Mary A. J. Aull's assignment of Dec. 20, 1929 (S.C.L. 5076/70). No mortgage or default is recited. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (1929 and 1935 read): S.C.L. 5517/92 (MSA CE 168-5525, read; 726:mdlr-scl5517-92-hooper-trustees-waverly-bldg-redemption-3030-1935) is the deed of Feb. 18, 1935 by which Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore and William Jenkins, trustees under Francis X. Hooper's will, on the Waverly Building Association's statutory notice to redeem, conveyed it the 1912 $66 reversion on 3030 for $1,100, 'to the end and intent that the leasehold estate created by the lease aforesaid shall be merged with the fee'. So the trustees of the 1935 recitals are Hooper's, and the 1912 lease and rent on 3030 merged in the Association by that deed, not by inference. S.C.L. 5076/70 and /71 (MSA CE 168-5084, read) show how the leasehold reached the McCoys: Jacob H. Aull's executors deeded it to his widow Mary A. J. Aull on Oct. 11, 1922 (S.C.L. 3918/495, recited), she assigned it to David and Mary E. McCoy on Dec. 20, 1929, and they mortgaged it the same day to the Waverly Building Association for a $3,120 purchase-money advance on 24 shares, released only on Mar. 15, 1951 (M.L.P. 8386/69). Their 1932 assignment to that lender was very probably in lieu of foreclosure [inference].

summary: Deed and lease, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. 8386, folios 70 to 72 (MSA CE 168-8394; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 70 to 74). Dated and acknowledged Mar. 14, 1951 before Catherine W. McCann, notary, who witnessed it; recorded Mar. 15, 1951 at 2:32 p.m. (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk). Nicholas Interrante, widower, conveys Robert F. Podlich, of Anne Arundel County, 3030 Greenmount Avenue in fee (29 ft north of Vineyard Lane, 14 ft, 82 ft). The leasehold came to Nicholas and Ida H. Interrante, by the entireties, from Helen M. Bordley (Sept. 30, 1943, M.L.P. 6513/139), and the reversion from Charles T. and Ella B. Leight (Jan. 7, 1944, M.L.P. 6549/554); Ida died, leaving Nicholas the fee. On folio 72, the same day, Podlich leases 3030 to Marie B. Pipitone for 99 years at $90 from Mar. 15, 1951: the lease recorded just before the deed of the rent (row 42198). What it settles: (1) the 3030 dark run is partly lit: by 1943 the leasehold was Helen M. Bordley's and the 1912 reversion was held by Charles T. and Ella B. Leight, the 3010 and 3020 family across the lane, who sold it in January 1944 (how the Leights took it from the Hooper trust is not shown). (2) Dr. Nicholas Interrante owned 3030 from 1943 to 1951 (rows 39349, 42015 to 42017 put him there). (3) The 1951 $90 rent is Podlich's creation. What it does not settle: M.L.P. 6549/554 (the Leights' title) and 6513/139 (Bordley's). Update Oct. 14, 2026: M.L.P. 6549/554, the cite this deed gives for the Leights' 1944 deed to the Interrantes, was pulled and holds other deeds recorded Jan. 12, 1944 (726:negative-mlp6549-554-not-leight-interrante-1944); the folio is probably miscopied. The $90 rent this deed created is still in the 2016 deed (726:mdlr-lga18376-272-bloom-substitute-trustee-3028-greenmount-llc-2016). Update Oct. 16, 2026: the 1944 Grantee Index (MSA CE 166-315, p.151) gives the Leight-to-Interrante deed of Jan. 11, 1944 as M.L.P. 6549 folio 594, not 554 (the 1951 recital miscopied it); M.L.P. 6549/594 is the next pull. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (late): M.L.P. 6549/594 is read (726:mdlr-mlp6549-594-leight-interrante-3030-rent-1944). It is a deed of reversion dated Jan. 7, 1944, for $1,100 and accrued rent, and the rent it conveys is not the 1912 Aull rent: it recites a new 99-year lease at $66 from the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County to Helen M. Bordley of Feb. 25, 1935 (S.C.L. 5518/171), the Association's deed of the reversion to the Leights the same day (S.C.L. 5518/173), and Bordley's assignment to the Interrantes (M.L.P. 6513/139). How the Association came to hold 3030, and how the 1912 Aull leasehold and the Hooper trust's 3030 rent ended, are not read. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (1935 read): the 1935 instruments are read (S.C.L. 5518/171 to 175, rows 47394 to 47396). The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County took the 3030 leasehold by assignment from David McCoy and wife, July 8, 1932 (S.C.L. 5312/27), and the reversion by a deed from 'the Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore et al Trustees', Feb. 18, 1935 (folio not given; very probably the Hooper trust selling the 1912 $66 rent, an inference), so the 1912 lease and rent met in the Association. On Feb. 25, 1935 it leased 3030 to Helen M. Bordley at $66, sold that new rent to Charles T. and Ella B. Leight for $1,100, and took the lease back from Bordley the same day (a straw, inference). Bordley's 1943 assignment to the Interrantes is M.L.P. 6513/139 (row 47397). Update Oct. 16, 2026 (5313/27 read): the McCoy assignment that the 1935 instruments cite as 'Liber S C L No 5312 folio 27' is recorded at S.C.L. 5313/27 (MSA CE 168-5321; Grantor Index 1932, row 47520), on a folio whose typed header reads '5312', corrected by hand to 5313. It is read (726:mdlr-scl5313-27-mccoy-waverly-bldg-assignment-3030-1932): David and Mary E. McCoy assigned the 3030 leasehold to The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County on July 8, 1932 (recorded July 12) for $5 and other valuable considerations, subject to the 1912 rent of $66 due June 1 and Dec. 1; they held it by Mary A. J. Aull's assignment of Dec. 20, 1929 (S.C.L. 5076/70). No mortgage or default is recited. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (1929 and 1935 read): S.C.L. 5517/92 (MSA CE 168-5525, read; 726:mdlr-scl5517-92-hooper-trustees-waverly-bldg-redemption-3030-1935) is the deed of Feb. 18, 1935 by which Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore and William Jenkins, trustees under Francis X. Hooper's will, on the Waverly Building Association's statutory notice to redeem, conveyed it the 1912 $66 reversion on 3030 for $1,100, 'to the end and intent that the leasehold estate created by the lease aforesaid shall be merged with the fee'. So the trustees of the 1935 recitals are Hooper's, and the 1912 lease and rent on 3030 merged in the Association by that deed, not by inference. S.C.L. 5076/70 and /71 (MSA CE 168-5084, read) show how the leasehold reached the McCoys: Jacob H. Aull's executors deeded it to his widow Mary A. J. Aull on Oct. 11, 1922 (S.C.L. 3918/495, recited), she assigned it to David and Mary E. McCoy on Dec. 20, 1929, and they mortgaged it the same day to the Waverly Building Association for a $3,120 purchase-money advance on 24 shares, released only on Mar. 15, 1951 (M.L.P. 8386/69). Their 1932 assignment to that lender was very probably in lieu of foreclosure [inference].

summary: Assignment, Baltimore County land records, Liber E.H.A. 62, folios 390 to 391 (MSA CE 62-62; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 390 to 394; John P. and Mary Meyer's deed to Caroline Sutton follows on 391). Dated and acknowledged May 15, 1869 before Geo. McCaffray, J.P. of Baltimore City (certified by George Robinson, Clerk of the Superior Court); recorded May 18, 1869 (Edward H. Ady, Clerk). George C. H. Coffield assigns William Hammel, of Baltimore City, for $600, the south part of the Coffield tract on the east side of the turnpike: from a stone on the road 125 ft 6 in along it to the south line of the 1868 Smith lot (E.H.A. 59/86), about due east 140 ft to the tract's fourth line (J.H.L. 43/548), S 15 W along it, then straight back to the start; for the rest of the term, renewable, 'subject however to the payment of the yearly rent of one cent if demanded'. What it settles: (1) the Bateman ground's County source is read: Coffield split his tract in 1868 and 1869, the north 79 ft to Smith under a $150 sub-rent and the south 125 ft 6 in to Hammel outright at the tract's one cent, so 3105 to 3111 never carried a sub-rent. (2) From Hammel the ground went in two parts: the south end to the Methodist trustees by the 1872 sub-lease (737:mdlr-eha77-296-hammel-methodist-trustees-church-lot-1872) and the rest, 70 ft 6 in, to the Batemans. What it does not settle: how the Batemans took Hammel's part (the 1901 deed recites only this deed).

summary: Sub-lease, Baltimore County land records, Liber E.H.A. 77, folios 296 to 299 (MSA CE 62-77; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 296 to 300; the recording stamp is on a later folio, not read). Dated Aug. 31, 1872. William Hammel sub-leases nine trustees (Edward Mallalieu, Samuel Corby, Joseph J. Wheeler, John Prince, Edward P. Standiford, John T. Dellahunt, Joseph A. Bolgiano, John H. Brown and Robert H. Heyde; some names as read) the south end of his Coffield ground: from a stake on the east side of the turnpike 3 1/2 ft from the beginning stone of the Coffield-to-Hammel deed, 55 ft north along the road, 101 ft east to the fence on the west side of the Old York Road and 13 ft more to the deed's fourth line, 99 ft south-west along it in the old road's bed, then back about 97 ft. Term: the rest of Hammel's term less a year, renewable on a $1 fine; rent $165 a year (February and August) from Aug. 1, 1872; buyout $2,750 (the rent at 6 percent). In trust: the ground and 'the Church and Parsonage to be erected thereon' for divine worship of the Methodist Episcopal Church and a residence for its preachers stationed there. What it settles: (1) the 'Methodist trustees' 1872 sub-lease' named in the 1901 and 1902 Bateman deeds is read: a church lot of 55 ft at the south end of the Coffield tract, with a $165 sub-rent to Hammel. (2) The church and parsonage were still to be built in August 1872. This is very probably the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot in front of which the two-mile stone stood, the stone every 3011 to 3017 description measures from (probable: the deed names no congregation, and Joseph A. Bolgiano is a Waverly name). (3) Of Hammel's 125 ft 6 in, 55 ft went to the church; 70 ft 6 in remained, the Bateman ground. What it does not settle: the congregation's name, the recording date, and whether the $165 rent was ever redeemed.

Both dated Apr. 17, 1901 under an Orphans' Court of Baltimore City order of Apr. 12, 1901, acknowledged before Robert C. Rhodes, J.P.; the first recorded Apr. 18, 1901 at 11 a.m. (Robert Ogle, Clerk). (1) As administrator of James S. Bateman, Walter I. Dawkins sells Clara V. Bateman, feme sole, for $250, a 40-ft lot on the west side of the Old York Road, from a stone marked '2' in a lease from John Litzinger and wife to John H. White of May 5, 1866 (Baltimore County, liber '48' folio 502, the letters not written), 81 ft 8 in west to the corner of White's sub-lease to Christian Hunteman of Feb. 17, 1870 (E.H.A. 65/502), 40 ft north, 85 ft east to the old road; a leasehold at $58 a year (May and November). (2) As administrator of Mary A. Bateman, he sells Clara, for $3,000, the Coffield ground Coffield assigned Hammel in 1869 (E.H.A. 62/390) less the 1872 Methodist sub-lease (E.H.A. 77/296), 70 ft 6 in on the turnpike. What it settles: (1) the two 1901 deeds behind M. Estelle Bateman's 1902 purchase (R.O. 1984/398, row 46222) are read: Clara bought both lots from the estates of James S. and Mary A. Bateman for $3,250 and her administrator sold them to M. Estelle for $3,050 in 1902. (2) The Bateman turnpike ground is exactly Hammel's 1869 ground less the church lot, so 3105 to 3111 descend Tagart (1865), Coffield, Hammel (1869), the Batemans (by 1877), Clara (1901), M. Estelle (1902). (3) The Old York Road lot comes from a lease by John Litzinger in 1866, the name of the man who sold the Huntington fork lot at 3200 to Andrew Brown in 1834 (same man probable, not shown). What it does not settle: how James S. and Mary A. Bateman took the Hammel ground, and folio 422. Update Oct. 14, 2026: both cited instruments are read: the 1866 Litzinger lease to John H. White (737:mdlr-jhl48-502-litzinger-white-lease-1866: half an acre and 20 perches between the turnpike and the Old York Road at $120, from a P. Merryman's 1865 deed, J.H.L. 46/149) and White's 1870 sub-lease to Christian Hunteman, 22 by 82 ft on the turnpike at $55 (737:mdlr-eha65-502-taylor-white-hunteman-sublease-1870).

summary: Assignment, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5455, folios 522 to 523 (MSA CE 168-5463; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 522 to 526; Emil Budnitz, trustee, and Essie K. Hohlbein's assignment to The Afro-American Company is above it). Dated, acknowledged before Harry Kuszmaul, notary, and recorded July 9, 1934 at 2:55 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). James M. and Ena M. Sinclair assign the Provident Savings Bank of Baltimore, for $5 and other consideration, the lot behind the bank: from the centre line of an 8-ft alley (the fourth line of M. Estelle Bateman's assignment to the bank), 28 ft 6 1/4 in east of the turnpike at the west side of a frame building, 24 ft south along the building, 86 ft 6 in east to the Old York Road, 24 ft 11 in north-east along it, 92 ft 8 in back along the alley; subject to one cent a year if demanded. Sinclair's title: 'an assignment from Provident Savings Bank of Baltimore to James M Sinclair dated March 26th 1920' (S.C.L. 3552/81 as read). What it settles: (1) how James M. Sinclair came by the ground behind the bank: the Provident Savings Bank, which had bought it as part of M. Estelle Bateman's land in 1904, assigned it to him in March 1920, and he assigned it back in July 1934, three months after mortgaging it (row 46269). (2) It is Coffield-Hammel ground at the tract's one cent, cut from the Bateman lot, which fits the shrinking Bateman frontage (69 ft in 1889, 44.8 ft about 1913). What it does not settle: S.C.L. 3552/81 (reading to check) and why the bank sold and bought it back.

Eichelberger follows on 330). Dated May 14, 1844; acknowledged that day in Anne Arundel County before Wm. Glover and J. M. Hunter, justices; recorded May 16, 1844 (Thomas Kell, Clerk). Alexander Contee Magruder, of Annapolis, trustee under a deed of trust of Nov. 7, 1826 from Philip G. Biays (W.G. 184/618) of two parts of 'Huntington' (3 a 1 r 12 p and 3 a 3 p) with power to sell, sells James Wilson, of Baltimore City, for $1,025, the first: 'part of a tract called Huntington', beginning at a stone at the end of the S 43 3/4 E line of the part Harry D. Gough and Prudence sold James Biays, 'which stone stands on the northwest side of a road laid out by the said Harry D. Gough'; S 40 3/4 W 41 1/2 perches along the Biays lot, N 38 1/4 W 10 perches to Joseph Thornburg's lot, N 49 1/2 E about 39 perches along it to the York Turnpike, S 3.7 perches along the turnpike to Gough's road, and along the road to the start: 3 acres 1 rood 12 perches, with buildings. What it settles: (1) the Magruder deed recited in the 1870 gate-house deed is read: James Wilson bought this Huntington parcel in 1844 from a trust Philip G. Biays had created in 1826, so the Wilson estate's ground at the toll gate comes from the Biays family through Philip G. Biays. (2) It is Huntington, bounded by Gough's road (the lane, later Gilmor and Vineyard Lane), the turnpike (only 3.7 perches, about 61 ft), a Biays lot (Gough to James Biays) and Joseph Thornburg's lot: a wedge running back from the turnpike at the mouth of the lane on its north side, which is where 3026 to 3032 and the toll-gate lot stand (an inference from the bounds; no deed ties a house to it). (3) The parcel came with buildings in 1844. (4) A new hop above it: Philip G. Biays's 1826 trust (W.G. 184/618). What it does not settle: the 1826 trust itself and who its beneficiaries were. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1826 trust is read (725:mdlr-wg184-618-philip-biays-trust-magruder-1826): Philip G. Biays bought both Huntington parcels from James Carroll the Elder and his sons on July 7, 1823 (W.G. 169/672) and put them in trust for his wife and children. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): James Wilson gave the Trustees of Huntingdon Chapel part of this ground, beside the Gate House lot, in 1849 (725:mdlr-awb423-290-james-wilson-huntingdon-chapel-church-lot-1849).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 1928, folios 238 to 239 (MSA CE 168-1936; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 238 to 242: Oliver H. Ebbert's assignment is above it on 238, and Howard W. Patton's deed to Willard F. Gore follows on 239). Dated, acknowledged before Chas. J. Fox, notary, and recorded Oct. 31, 1901 at noon (Robert Ogle, Clerk), the same hour as the lease. Mary Clemens and her husband sell Francis P. Duggan, of Baltimore City, for $3,000, the 3010 lot in fee 'and particularly the aforesaid rent ... and the reversion', subject to Allen K. Wood's 99-year lease of the same day at $180 (quarterly, February, May, August and November); part of the Dodson deed of 1896 (R.O. 1615/24). What it settles: the 1901 rent deed is read: $3,000, the $180 at exactly 6 percent, the same price Duggan's executors got from the Swormstedts two years later (row 46272). Duggan was a ground-rent investor who paid full value, not a lender. The 3010 rent chain is now read at every step from creation to merger.

summary: Distribution deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.H.B. 2860, folios 136 to 138 (MSA CE 168-13178; read on the scan Jeff saved). Dated Nov. 17, 1971; acknowledged Nov. 8 in Broward County, Florida, and Nov. 12, 1971 in Baltimore; recorded Dec. 2, 1971 at 11:35 a.m. (Robert H. Bouse, Clerk); the margin reads 'Unlocated'. Ruth Realty, Inc. was dissolved on Aug. 1, 1969; at dissolution David W. Chertkof's revocable trust of Feb. 9, 1968 held half its stock and Annie Chertkof the other half; Annie died Sept. 13, 1969 and her estate took cash, the trust took the real estate. So the corporation's directors and trustees (Ethel Posnick, Helen Gimbel, Howard Chertkof, Jack O. Chertkof) and Annie's executors (Jack O. Chertkof, Ethel Posnick, Charles F. Stein Jr.) convey Jack O. Chertkof, surviving trustee, 'all that property described in a Deed from David W. Chertkof and wife dated November 1, 1960' (J.F.C. 969/476), and any other Ruth Realty property. What it settles: (1) the 1971 deed the 1974 sale recites is read: a family corporation unwinding, not a purchase. (2) The Chertkofs held 3105 to 3109 before 1960 in David W. Chertkof's own name and put it into Ruth Realty on Nov. 1, 1960, so the gap behind 3107 is now the Bateman heirs (after 1920) to David W. Chertkof (before 1960). What it does not settle: J.F.C. 969/476 (it should recite how Chertkof bought) and the Bateman-heirs sale. Update Oct. 14, 2026: J.F.C. 969/476 is read (737:mdlr-jfc969-476-chertkof-ruth-realty-1960): the Chertkofs bought 3105 to 3109 from M. Lillian and Charles A. Slade on Nov. 25, 1935 (S.C.L. 5580/582).

summary: Deed of trust, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 184, folios 618 to 620 (MSA CE 66-234; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 618 to 622: Charles Worthington's lease to John Brooks ends on 618 above it; Isaiah Mankin's deeds to Henry Mankin follow). Dated and acknowledged Nov. 7, 1826 before Saml. Young and Tho. W. Griffith, justices of Baltimore City; recorded Feb. 27, 1827 (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). Philip G. Biays, gentleman, conveys Alexander Contee Magruder, counsellor at law of Annapolis, two parts of 'Huntington' (3 a 1 r 12 p and 3 a 3 p), as described in a deed of July 7, 1823 from James Carroll the Elder and his three sons, James Carroll Jr., Harry Dorsey Gough Carroll and Charles Ridgely Carroll, to Philip G. Biays (W.G. 169/672), in trust for his wife Jane Catharine Thomas Biays and their son Alexander Magruder Biays and any other children of the marriage, share alike for life, remainder to the survivor, with power to sell and apply the proceeds to them. What it settles: (1) the 1826 trust behind Magruder's 1844 sale to James Wilson is read, and it names the source: the Carrolls, heirs of Harry Dorsey Gough's estate (James Carroll was Gough's son-in-law and executor; Harry Dorsey Gough Carroll and Charles Ridgely Carroll his sons), sold Philip G. Biays both parcels in July 1823, after the 1818 to 1819 Carroll allotment of Gough's lands. So the toll-gate corner's chain runs Huntington, Gough (1790 to 1808), the Carroll heirs, Philip G. Biays (1823), the Magruder trust (1826), James Wilson (1844), the Wilson trustees and the turnpike company (1870s), Aull (1912), 3026 to 3032 (the first parcel's place at the corner is an inference from the 1844 bounds). (2) Magruder was evidently a family connection: the Biays son was named Alexander Magruder Biays. What it does not settle: W.G. 169/672 (the 1823 Carroll deed and its description) and where the 3 a 3 p second parcel lay. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1823 Carroll deed is read (725:mdlr-wg169-672-carroll-heirs-philip-biays-toll-gate-wedge-school-house-1823): lot 1 is the toll-gate wedge, bought by Christopher Walker under Gough's 1803 bond and plat, with a school-house lot excepted.

summary: Deed of trust, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 112, folios 471 to 473 (MSA CE 66-162; the first page was on disk, the rest saved by Jeff October 14, pages 472 to 474; John Armagost's deed of 'Stoddars Delight' follows on 473). Dated and acknowledged Mar. 14, 1811 before Edwd. Woodyear and Edwd. Aisquith, justices, with Elizabeth Russell's release of dower; recorded Apr. 5, 1811 (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). Elisha E. Russell, master mariner of Baltimore, conveys George I. Brown and William S. Hollins, merchants trading as Brown & Hollins, as joint tenants, both of the Huntington lots he had bought the day before, to secure $4,735 owed the firm: the strip from William Jackson's 1803 Gough lot (W.G. 112/467) and the 1 a 47 p from James Biays (W.G. 112/469), the latter bounded by Jackson's lot, 'a road leading to Joseph Merryman's' and James Biays's part of the tract. If Russell defaulted for twelve months the trustees could sell at auction. What it settles: (1) Russell's deed of trust is read in full: a merchant's security, not a sale. (2) The second lot runs to 'a road leading to Joseph Merryman's', the 'Merryman[s] Road' drawn dashed on Cope's plat of Gough's 1803 lots (MSA C2843-15); the 1802 Whitely deed has 'the road leading from Joseph Merryman's to the City of Baltimore'. Whether that road is the later Merryman's Lane (33rd Street) or another track near the toll gate is not shown, so the lots are not yet placed. What it does not settle: whether Russell defaulted, and where on the road the lots lay. Update Oct. 14, 2026: both Russell lots reached James Wilson: McCormick's deed of July 4, 1823 (726:mdlr-wg168-653-mccormick-james-wilson-russell-lots-1823) conveys them course for course with a third parcel, from the City Bank of Baltimore (1820, W.G. 155/345); the Tract Index has Brown to the City Bank in 1817 (W.G. 141/81). Update Oct. 14, 2026: Russell then conveyed both lots outright to Brown and Hollins by a deed of about May 4, 1811 (W.G. 113/638), as Brown's 1817 deed to the City Bank recites (726:mdlr-wg141-81-brown-city-bank-bouldin-plat-1817), with Jehu Bouldin's plat of the three lots. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): the May 4, 1811 deed is read (726:mdlr-wg113-638-russell-brown-hollins-release-1811): Russell released his equity of redemption and conveyed both lots outright to Brown and Hollins for a $4,500 credit on the $4,735 debt; there was no trustees' sale.

summary: Assignment, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 104, folios 48 to 49 (MSA CE 66-154; on disk since October 13 in the Walker-to-Biays scan, pages 46 to 50, and read October 14). Dated and acknowledged Sept. 2, 1809 before J. Smith and Saml. H. Gatchell, justices; recorded Sept. 16, 1809 (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). Harry Dorsey Gough, Prudence Gough and Job Merryman leased Jesse Brown two lots of 'Huntington' on Apr. 16, 1798 (W.G. 54/156); Brown agreed to sell part to Christopher Walker, who sold his right to James Biays and witnessed this deed; Brown's widow and executrix Dorothy assigns Biays, for $1, 2 15/16 acres: from the centre of the York Turnpike where the lease's first line crosses it, S 82 E 15.9 perches to a stone on the west side of the Old York Road, S 7 3/4 W 30.7 perches along it, S 79 1/2 W 11.7 perches to the centre of the turnpike, and straight back; for the rest of the term, renewable forever, at £4 8s 1d a year on April 16. What it settles: (1) the 1809 assignment recited in Allender's 1847 sale to Leitzinger (row 46153) is read: the 2 15/16-acre Huntington leasehold lies between the York Turnpike and the Old York Road, about 506 ft along the old road, 15.9 perches (262 ft) across at the north line and 11.7 perches (193 ft) at the south: ground where the two roads run about 190 to 260 ft apart, which fits the stretch from about the 3100 block north rather than the fork tip at 3011, where they are under 50 ft apart (an inference from the widths; no house or street of the later city is named). (2) Job Merryman joined the 1798 lease as the lessee of a defective 1795 lease that he surrendered for GBP 100 paid by Jesse Brown (W.G. 54/156, read October 14), not as an owner. (3) Christopher Walker, who sold Biays the Ensor's Inspection lot in 1801, was also the go-between here. What it does not settle: where the 1798 lease's 11 acres lie and how the leasehold passed from Biays to Allender's 1847 sale. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the parcel's fee went to the leaseholder Litzinger in 1865 (720:mdlr-jhl46-149-oliver-merryman-litzinger-brown-lease-fee-1865): Gough's heirs to Charles R. Carroll, to Oliver P. Merryman (1859), to Litzinger, with the £4 8s 1d rent. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): the Jesse Brown lease cited in this chain was surrendered and re-granted in corrected form on Jan. 9, 1802 (720:mdlr-wg72-124-gough-jesse-brown-corrected-lease-1802), so by 1809 Brown held under the 1802 lease (inference).

Dated and acknowledged Aug. 11, 1898 before Wm. D. Wright, J.P.; recorded Aug. 27, 1898 at 10 a.m. (Robert Ogle, Clerk). Lulie H. Wallace, widow, conveys William Hall Wallace, for $1,250, 'in pursuance of an order of the Orphans Court of Baltimore City passed on the 22nd day of July 1898 in the matter of the estate of William Hall Wallace an Infant', the 3011 lot in the Village of Waverly 'and especially the clear yearly rent of Seventy five dollars', subject to the Aull lease. What it settles: (1) the 1898 hop is read: four months after buying the rent, Lulie H. Wallace sold it at cost to William Hall Wallace, a minor, under a court order in his estate, so the rent was an investment of a ward's money (she was presumably his mother and guardian; the deed does not say). In 1907, of age, he deeded it back to her for $1 and love and affection (row 46267). What it does not settle: the relationship and the guardianship papers.

summary: Two deeds, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 2358, folios 420 to 422 (MSA CE 168-2366; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 421 to 425; the first begins on 420, not on the scan). Both dated and acknowledged July 31, 1907 before Wm. H. Watson, J.P.; both recorded Aug. 3, 1907 at 10 a.m. (Robert Ogle, Clerk). Mary K. Fink, single, conveys Estella Fink, single, the 3017 lot and its $54 rent (first lot of the 1903 Clemens deed, R.O. 2037/213); Estella conveys it straight back to Mary K. 'by Deed of even date herewith'. What it settles: Estella Fink was a straw, not an owner: the 1907 Lehmann deed's recital of 'a deed ... from Estella Fink' is this round trip, made seven weeks before Mary K. Fink sold to Leopold Lehmann, very probably to separate the 3017 rent from the second lot of the 1903 deed for the sale (an inference: the deeds give no reason). The 3017 rent chain is now read at every step: Clemens 1903, Mary K. Fink 1903 to 1907, Lehmann 1907, Mary C. Lehmann, the Sinclairs 1946, the Vinsons 1951. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Fink deeds S.C.L. 2559/393 and 3126/290 read): Mary K. and Estella Fink, the 1907 straws, are two of William L. Fink's four children and co-owners of 3013 from 1910 (S.C.L. 2559/393; S.C.L. 3126/290): sisters passing the 3017 rent between themselves before the sale, not strangers.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 2599, folios 429 to 430 (MSA CE 168-2607; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 429 to 433; the Hendersons' mortgage to the Ashland Building Association follows). Dated and acknowledged July 30, 1910 before Wm. S. Gould, J.P.; recorded Aug. 4, 1910 at 1 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). James B. Guyton, bachelor, conveys Rose I. and Mary L. Conway, as joint tenants, two ground rents and reversions: $30 on a lot on the north side of St. Joseph Street and $54 on the Vineyard Lane lot behind 3010 (the 1902 Wood lease courses), the same two lots Rose I. Conway had deeded him that day. What it settles: the inference in row 46273 is confirmed: Guyton was a straw, used so that Rose I. Conway could hold the rents jointly with Mary L. Conway (the $54 rent came to Mary L. Conway in 1902 and evidently passed to Rose before 1910; how is not shown). Mary L. Conway died about Oct. 5, 1916, leaving Rose (later Harding) as survivor (row 46263). What it does not settle: how Rose took the rent from Mary L. Conway, and the sisters' relationship.

summary: Assignment, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 3348, folios 167 to 168 (MSA CE 168-3356; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 167 to 171; Michael G. Kilchenstein's deed to Fred A. Rahe follows on 168). Dated Apr. 21, 1919, witnessed and acknowledged before Lennox B. Clemens, notary; recorded Apr. 24, 1919 at 10 a.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Mary Clemens conveys John E. Wyman the Vineyard Lane leasehold (the 1902 lease courses), subject to $54 a year; her title is Allen K. Wood's deed to her of Apr. 11, 1903 (R.O. 2027/364). What it settles: how the Vineyard Lane leasehold came back to Mary Clemens: Wood assigned it to her in April 1903, a year after taking it, so she held the leasehold while Mary L. Conway held the rent, until she sold the leasehold to Wyman in 1919. The Clemens pattern again: lease, sell the rent, take the lease back. What it does not settle: R.O. 2027/364 (why Wood gave up the lot).

summary: Four instruments, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. 6570, folios 338 to 342 (MSA CE 168-6578; read on the scan Jeff saved). All dated Mar. 7, 1944, acknowledged before John A. Helldorfer, notary, and recorded Mar. 13, 1944 between 10:31 and 10:33 a.m. (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk). (1) Earl and Katherine Hoffmaster lease Christina Caparrola the lot 248 ft 9 1/2 in north of 29th Street, 14 ft by 100 ft, for 99 years renewable at $75 (March 7 and September 7); the lease types the house as 'No 2930 Greenmount Avenue (formerly York Road)', a slip for 2936 (the courses and the next three instruments say 2936). (2) The Hoffmasters convey the rent and reversion to Henry Lewis and Glen Marie Rosenthal. (3) Caparrola assigns the leasehold to Victor Posner. (4) Posner mortgages it to the Vermont Federal Savings and Loan Association for $1,800, 'part of the purchase money'. The Hoffmasters' title: Harry M. and Isabel A. Clarke and Evelyn E. and John F. Oehrl, Jan. 8, 1943 (M.L.P. 6413/203). What it settles: (1) the 1944 creation of the 2936 rent: a same-day package in which Caparrola was a straw lessee and Victor Posner the real buyer of the leasehold. A Victor Posner was a young Baltimore real-estate buyer in the 1940s; whether this is the later financier is not shown. (2) The next step back is the Clarke and Oehrl deed of 1943 (M.L.P. 6413/203). (3) No old York Road number is given ('formerly York Road' refers only to the street name). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the Hoffmasters' 1943 deed is read (704:mdlr-mlp6413-203-clarke-oehrl-hoffmaster-2936-fee-1943): they bought 2936 in fee with no ground rent, so this lease created the $75 rent new; their $2,500 Parkwood mortgage was released at Liber 6570, folio 337, just before this lease. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (evening): Katherine Hoffmaster was a daughter of Martin J. and Jane E. Clarke, who held 2936 from 1919 and merged its old rent in 1927 (704:mdlr-mlp5912-77-clarke-heirs-napfel-straw-2936-1938).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.F.C. 969, folios 476 to 478 (MSA CE 168-11287; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 476 to 480; the Hildebrand executor's deed of 2200 W. Lafayette Avenue follows on 479). Dated Nov. 1, 1960, acknowledged in Carroll County before Edna M. Arnold, notary; recorded Nov. 3, 1960 at 10:30 a.m. (James F. Carney, Clerk). David W. and Annie Chertkof convey Ruth Realty, Inc., in fee, three lots: (1) 3127-31 Greenmount, from Walter A. Hense (Oct. 3, 1939, M.L.P. 5964/215); (2) 'Nos. 3105, 3107 and 3109', from the end of the first line of the 1904 Bateman-to-Provident deed (218 ft 3 in south of 32nd Street), 46 ft 2 1/2 in south to the north-west corner of the 1872 Hammel-to-Mallalieu sub-lease, 101 ft 9 1/2 in east to the Old York Road, 47 ft 11 in north, 114 ft 6 1/4 in back, by an S. J. Martinet survey of Nov. 20, 1935, from M. Lillian Slade and her husband Charles A. Slade (Nov. 25, 1935, S.C.L. 5580/582); (3) a 9 1/4-in strip beginning 264 ft 5 1/2 in south of 32nd Street at the end of the Slade lot's first line, from Beulah Bruehl (Mar. 10, 1954, M.L.P. 9424/40). The first lot's courses run along a deed from the Franklin Realty and Finance Company to the Read Drug and Chemical Company of Baltimore City of Aug. 23, 1932, so the 1929 store lessor was conveying ground on this block in 1932. What it settles: (1) the Chertkofs bought 3105 to 3109 in November 1935 from M. Lillian Slade (the surveyed lot of 1935), so the gap behind 3107 is now 1920 (M. Estelle Bateman's death) to 1935, Bateman heirs to the Slades. (2) The lot is exactly the Bateman remainder of the Hammel ground between the church sub-lease and the bank. What it does not settle: S.C.L. 5580/582 (it should recite the Slades' title from the Bateman heirs or Franklin Realty). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1935 Slade deed is read (737:mdlr-scl5580-582-slade-chertkof-3105-3109-1935): fee, from Edna L. Rainey, widow, Oct. 11, 1921 (S.C.L. 3787/503).

summary: Lease, Baltimore County land records, Liber J.H.L. 48, folios 502 to 504 (MSA CE 62-48; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 502 to 506: the top of 502 is the end of John H. White's deed to Henry Taylor, acknowledged May 9 and recorded May 14, 1866, conveying a lot subject to $120 a year, very probably this leasehold; Thomas A. Mellon's deed of a St. Denis lot follows on 505). Dated May 5, 1866, acknowledged by the Litzingers before Edward B. Freeland, J.P., and by White before W. H. Hayward, J.P.; recorded May 14, 1866. John and Elizabeth Litzinger lease John H. White for 99 years, renewable forever, at $120 a year (half-yearly, from March 1), redeemable after ten years for $2,000: from stone '1' on the east side of the Baltimore and Yorktown turnpike, S 84 1/2 E 9 21/25 perches (about 162 ft) to stone '2' on the west side of the Old York Road, N 10 3/4 E 10 17/25 perches (about 176 ft) along the old road to stone '3' at a corner of John O'Brian's lot, N 80 1/2 W 11 16/25 perches (about 192 ft) along it to stone '4' on the turnpike, and straight back; half an acre and 20 perches, part of the land a P. Merryman and wife deeded Litzinger on June 27, 1865 (J.H.L. 46/149). The first name is cramped at the line end and reads like 'Olivr': probably Oliver P. Merryman, the name 3224's 1884 deed recites as one of its sources (row 23723). What it settles: (1) the 1866 lease that the 1901 and 1902 Bateman deeds cite (rows 46289, 46222) is read: the Bateman Old York Road lot (40 ft on the old road from stone '2') is the south-east part of this half-acre. (2) Litzinger's title is a Merryman deed of 1865, not Huntington ground from Brown or Parks, so the ground between the two roads here came from the Merrymans (Merryman's Lot is the tract that lies north of Huntington: an inference, no tract named). (3) White assigned the leasehold to Henry Taylor within days (May 9, 1866), and Taylor gave it back in 1870 (E.H.A. 65/502). What it does not settle: J.H.L. 46/149 (the Merryman deed and its tract), and where O'Brian's lot and this half-acre sit against 3107 to 3117. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the Merryman deed is read (737:mdlr-jhl46-149-oliver-merryman-litzinger-brown-lease-fee-1865): Oliver P. Merryman, the 2 15/16-acre Jesse Brown lease parcel, from Charles R. Carroll (1859); White's half-acre was cut from it.

summary: Two instruments, Baltimore County land records, Liber E.H.A. 65, folios 502 to 504 (MSA CE 62-65; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 502 to 506; Franz Henry Boklage's deed of a Bear Creek farm to Christian Schorr follows on 505). (1) The end of Henry Taylor's deed back to John H. White of the leasehold White had assigned him in 1866 (J.H.L. 48/501), subject to the $120 rent; acknowledged Mar. 8, 1870 before Thos. H. Robinson, J.P.; recorded Mar. 24, 1870 (Edward H. Ady, Clerk). (2) Sub-lease dated Feb. 17, 1870, acknowledged that day before John B. O'Donnell, J.P., recorded Mar. 24, 1870: White sub-leases Christian Hunteman, for the residue of the term less one year, renewable forever, at $55 a year from Mar. 1, 1870, redeemable for $916.66 (the rent at 6 percent), a lot from stone '1' on the east side of the turnpike, 82 ft east, 22 ft north parallel with the turnpike, 82 ft west to the turnpike and 22 ft south along it; part of the 1866 Litzinger lease (J.H.L. 48/502), the whole subject to $120. A margin note records delivery to J. Fox on July 19, 1871. What it settles: the Hunteman sub-lease the 1901 and 1902 Bateman deeds name as their west neighbour is read: Hunteman had the turnpike front (22 ft) at the south-west corner of White's half-acre, and the Bateman Old York Road lot lay behind it, from stone '2' 81 ft 8 in west to Hunteman's corner. The sub-rent pattern ($120 on the whole, $55 on a 22-ft piece) is the 1870s Waverly ground-rent ladder. What it does not settle: who held the rest of White's half-acre and where it lies against the modern lots.

summary: Assignment and mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 3552, folios 81 to 83 (MSA CE 168-3560; read on the scan Jeff saved, pages 81 to 85). Both dated Mar. 26, 1920; the assignment acknowledged that day before Otto V. [Yursik], notary, and recorded Mar. 26, 1920 at 3 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). The Provident Savings Bank of Baltimore, by Elisha H. Perkins, president, assigns James M. Sinclair, for $5 and other considerations, the easternmost part of the lot M. Estelle Bateman assigned the bank on Mar. 18, 1904 (R.O. 2062/398): from the centre line of an 8-ft alley (the bank lot's fourth line), 28 ft 6 1/4 in east of the turnpike and in line with the west side of the frame building on the lot, 24 ft south along that building, 86 ft 6 in east to the Old York Road, 24 ft 11 in north-east along it to the alley, and 92 ft 8 in west along the alley's centre line; for the rest of the term, renewable forever, at one cent. Sinclair is to remove the eaves of the house that overhang the bank's eastern line on 30 days' notice and claim no easement. The same day James M. and Ena M. Sinclair mortgage the lot to the bank for $1,000 at $10 a month and 6 percent. What it settles: the 1920 sale behind row 46290 is read in its own words: a frame house stood on the back of the bank lot, the bank kept the front, and the line between them ran along the house's west wall, with a one-cent rent carried down from the Coffield tract. What it does not settle: who built the frame house (the Bateman house of the 1877 atlas sat on the turnpike front, not here).

summary: Substitute trustee's deed and assignment, Baltimore City Circuit Court land records, Liber L.G.A. 18376, folios 272 to 276 (MSA CE 164-27533; read on the scan Jeff saved, all five pages: deed, signature page, Exhibit A, Exhibit A-1 and the clerk's receipt of Aug. 17, 2016). Dated and acknowledged Aug. 8, 2016 in Montgomery County; prepared by Henry I. Louis. People's Community Health Centers, Inc. had given Jeannine Jacokes, trustee, a deed of trust on May 7, 2010 (F.M.C. 12614/394); Edward A. Bloom was substituted as trustee on Aug. 22, 2014 (F.M.C. 16527/263) and sold the property at public auction on Feb. 16, 2016 to Andrew M. Woods, who assigned his bid to 3028 Greenmount Avenue, LLC on Mar. 14, 2016; the Circuit Court for Baltimore City ratified the sale on July 12, 2016 (Case 24-O-14-002930 FC). For $275,000 Bloom conveys the LLC 3028 and 3032 in fee and 3030 as a leasehold, renewable forever, at $90 a year (Mar. 15 and Sept. 15). Exhibit A gives the three 14-ft lots 15, 29 and 43 ft north of Vineyard Lane, 82 ft to a 4-ft alley, the third tied to the north line of the turnpike company's 1912 deed to Jacob H. Aull (S.C.L. 2727/29); Exhibit A-1 consolidates them as 42 by 82 ft, 3,444 sq ft, from the clinic's two deeds of Feb. 14, 1975 (Charles C. Freitag, R.H.B. 3207/657; David Siegel, R.H.B. 3207/655). What it settles: (1) the present owner's root deed is read: the sale date is Feb. 16, 2016 by the deed itself (row 39467 has a Dec. 4, 2014 auction; that may have been an earlier sale date that did not close). (2) The $90 rent on 3030 survived into the present title, confirming the 1951 Interrante lease (row 46286) as its origin. (3) The SDAT segment s1 cite (L.G.A. 18376/272) is the deed.

Potomac Street follows on 262). Dated Jan. 17, 1972 (the acknowledgments are Jan. 3, before Stewart R. Brown, notary); recorded Jan. 18, 1972 at 1:10 p.m. (Robert H. Bouse, Clerk); Title Guarantee application H-75628. Mercantile-Safe Deposit and Trust Company, as trustee under two deeds of trust of Dec. 28, 1935, from Mary Mildred and Joseph T. Hazen (S.C.L. 5589/232) and from Jane Collison and Frederick A. Weiss (S.C.L. 5589/227), conveys The Miller Realty Corporation, for $2,105, Lots 16 and 17 (200 by 100 ft at the north-west corner of the York Turnpike and Wilson Street, with 10 ft left open as half of a 20-ft alley along the rear) and 'especially' the $200 ground rent, 'to the end and intent that the Leasehold estate be merged in the fee and the aforesaid annual ground rent ... be forever merged and extinguished'. Recitals: the fee came to Mary Mildred Hazen and Jane Collison Weiss from Safe Deposit and Trust Company, substituted trustee under the will of Joseph A. Bolgiano, by deed of Dec. 27, 1935 (S.C.L. 5589/225); the rent was reserved by the lease of John Bolgiano and wife to 'Bernard Bestling' of Sept. 21, 1876, recorded in Baltimore County 'Liber JB No. 971, folio 584' (no County liber 971 existed in 1876, so this is J.B. 97, folio 584); Miller Realty held the leasehold by William John Lacey's executor's deed of June 17, 1969 (R.H.B. 2529/79). What it settles: (1) the 1972 deed is read in its own words: the $200 rent created in 1876 was merged and extinguished on Jan. 18, 1972, so 3326 to 3338's Lots 16-17 ground has been one fee since then. (2) The rent's path is now Bolgiano (1876), Joseph A. Bolgiano's will and trustee, the Hazen and Weiss sisters (1935, each putting her half in trust the next day), Mercantile-Safe Deposit (1972). (3) The lease's folio is 584, not 57 (J.B. 97/57, pulled October 14, holds June 1876 deeds). The sale price, $2,105, is about ten years' rent. What it does not settle: how the reversion passed from John Bolgiano to Joseph A. Bolgiano (no will date or probate cite is given). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the sisters were Joseph A. Bolgiano's granddaughters, daughters of Flora B. Joyce (776:mdlr-scl5589-225-bolgiano-trust-flora-joyce-hazen-weiss-1935); each had put her half in trust for the other.

Mix's Curley Street deed and the Wisterwitz mortgage follow). Dated and acknowledged Nov. 15, 1910 before Louis H. Rahe, J.P., who witnessed it; recorded Nov. 16, 1910 at 12:10 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). James D. Lacey, unmarried, conveys John P. and Mary E. Lacey, as tenants by the entireties, in fee, for $5 and other considerations, TWO lots: (1) the 25-ft lot on the west side of the York Turnpike 100 ft north of Wilson Street, 120 ft deep to a 10-ft alley; (2) a 25 by 60 ft lot on the east side of Talbot Street. Both had come to William and Elizabeth Lacey as tenants by the entireties by two deeds, from Henry W. Fox, trustee, Oct. 25, 1898 (R.O. 1758/40) and from Wilhelmina McLaughlin and husband, July 25, 1904 (R.O. 2087/487), the recital not saying which brought which; William died first, and Elizabeth died intestate about May 30, 1910 'leaving as her only child and sole heir at law the said James D Lacey'. What it settles: (1) the 1910 deed behind chain B is read (row 42280 had it from recitals only): the 25-ft lot was fee, with no ground rent, in 1910. (2) No Gutman appears: the lot came to the Laceys in 1898 or 1904, and a trustee's sale (Fox, 1898) is the likelier route from William Gutman, owner on the 1889 plat (an inference). (3) James D. was Eliza's only child, while John P. Lacey's death record names his mother as Margaret Lambert (row 41831), so the two were probably half-brothers, sons of William Lacey by two wives (an inference that reconciles the deed with the 1920 'brother' notice). What it does not settle: R.O. 1758/40 and 2087/487, and which is the 25-ft lot. Update Oct. 14, 2026: both recited deeds are read: the 25-ft lot came by the Fox trustee's deed of Oct. 25, 1898 (778:mdlr-ro1758-40-fox-trustee-lacey-25ft-lot-waverly-building-assn-henry-1898: Waverly Building Association v. summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 168, folios 653 to 657 (MSA CE 66-218; read on the scan Jeff saved: the Mayor and City Council's deed to Edward Denison ends above it on 653, and Henry Lenhart's assignment of a John Street lot follows on 657). Dated and acknowledged July 4, 1823 in Baltimore City before Fielder Israel and John T. Harris, justices, Elizabeth McCormick releasing dower; recorded Aug. 7, 1823 (Wm. Gibson, Clerk); the margin records delivery to 'Wm C Wilson' on Dec. 13, 1848, the year of James Wilson's will. James McCormick Jr. conveys James Wilson, for $7,000, three parcels of 'Huntington' (7 a 0 r 2 p in all, the Tract Index's '7 a 2 p'): (1) 2 a 27 p from the end of the N 36 1/4 W 90 1/4-perch line of the lot Harry Dorsey Gough sold William Jackson on Jan. 13, 1803, back along it 38.3 perches and round to his second line; (2) 1 a 47 p from the north-east corner of Jackson's lot, N 39 3/4 E 26.7 perches 'to a road leading to Joseph Merryman's'; (3) 3 a 2 r 8 p beside it, running to 'a road leading from Joseph Merrymans house to the turnpike road leading from the City of Baltimore towards York town' and along that road. All three came to McCormick from the City Bank of Baltimore on Mar. 15, 1820 (W.G. 155/345). What it settles: (1) parcels 1 and 2 are, course for course, Elisha E. Russell's two lots of 1811 (from William Jackson, W.G. 112/467, and from James Biays, W.G. 112/469), which Russell put in trust with George I. Brown and William S. Hollins (W.G. 112/471); the Tract Index has Brown to the City Bank in 1817 (W.G. 141/81), so the path is Russell, the Brown & Hollins trust, the City Bank, McCormick (1820), James Wilson (1823): James Wilson's estate held the Russell ground (the Brown-to-bank step and the trust sale are not yet read). (2) The road on which the Russell lots front runs from Joseph Merryman's house to the York Turnpike, so it is a cross road meeting the turnpike, not the turnpike itself. (3) The 1823 purchase is Huntington at the north corner of Jackson's 1803 lot; nothing in it names Wilson Street or Lots 16 and 17, so it is not yet shown to be the Lots 16-17 ground. What it does not settle: where Jackson's lot lies against the modern blocks (plotting W.G. 74/327 to 341 would place all three parcels). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the bank's deed to McCormick is read (726:mdlr-wg155-345-city-bank-mccormick-russell-lots-1820): $6,000 in 1820; George I. Brown had deeded the bank the lots in 1817 'in satisfaction of a debt' (W.G. 141/81, with a plat).

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 66, folios 150 to 153 (MSA CE 66-116; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved and checked: Linkefelter to Bixler ends on 150; James Hicks's market-yard lease and Joseph Swan's deed of a 'Hale Folly' partition follow). Dated and acknowledged Feb. 12, 1801 in Prince George's County before Amariah Frost and Robert Brent, Joanna Barry releasing dower; recorded Apr. 3, 1801 (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). James Barry, merchant of Washington, sells Hugh Thompson, merchant of Baltimore, for $1,000, an undivided half of two parcels: 2 a 1 r 35 p of 'Merrymans lott or Lilien dale', from the second boundary of Merryman's Lot (stones marked H.T.), and 12 a 2 r 19 1/5 p of 'Huntington' from 'a large Red Oak Tree being the beginning Tree of a Resurvey Called Huntington surveyed the sixteenth day of May' 1794, ending on 'a thirty foot Road'. Barry held a half of what Henry Wilmans had sold Stephen Casenave and James Walker in 1795 (W.G. R.R. 190), by Walker's deed of 1798 (W.G. 54/448). What it settles: (1) the hop is a negative for its purpose: W.G. 66/150 is Barry's deed to Thompson, not the Apr. 13, 1801 Barry deed to Edwards and Van Bibber that the 1802 Wilson deed cites (at 'W.G. 69/163', an unrelated deed); W.G. 66 was being recorded in early April 1801, so the April 13 deed may be a few folios on (66/160 to 166 is the next try; inference). (2) It is still a direct link: Barry's title runs to Henry Wilmans, who bought Gough's Huntington lots and pieces of Merryman's Lot in 1795, and it pairs the same two tracts, Huntington Resurveyed and Merryman's Lot, that James Wilson's 1802 purchase names; 'Lilien dale' (or Liliendale) is a new alias for part of Merryman's Lot. (3) The red oak is the Huntington resurvey's beginning tree, the same tree the Biays deeds of 1801 call. What it does not settle: where these parcels lie, and the April 1801 deed. Update Oct. 14, 2026: W.G. 66/158 to 167 is negative for the April 1801 Barry deed too (776:negative-wg66-158-167-no-barry-april-1801-deed); try later in W.G. 66 or early W.G. 67. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Barry deed found): the 'James Barry of Washington' of this deed is 'James Barry of the Territory of Columbia' in his April 13, 1801 deed to Edwards and Van Bibber for 30 square perches in Merryman's Lot, a corner between Merryman and Hall (W.G. 69/163, row 776:mdlr-wg69-163-barry-edwards-vanbibber-30-perches-1801; same grantor by name and residence, INFERRED). So Barry sold two lots of Merryman's ground within two months, a half of two parcels to Thompson in February and a 30-perch strip to Edwards and Van Bibber in April.

The York Road Building Association releases the Sanners' two mortgages (Oct. 30, 1918, S.C.L. 3281/603; Mar. 18, 1921, S.C.L. 3713/177). Lawrence W. and Mary E. Sanner assign Charles E. and Lilly M. Morris, as tenants by the entireties, the lot 15 ft north of Vineyard Lane (formerly Gilmor Lane), 14 by 82 ft to a 4-ft alley, between partition walls: 3028. The Morrises' mortgage to the York Road Building Association, recorded two minutes later, recites the lot as subject to a $66 ground rent (June 1 and December 1) and conveys the residue of the renewable term, so 3028 was a leasehold under the 1912 Aull rent. The image MSA serves for folio 256 is a second exposure of folio 258 (same folio number, text and margin note), so the end of the deed (its recital of the Aull-to-Sanner deed, signatures and recording line) and the start of the mortgage are missing from the scan. What it settles: the 1921 step in 3028's leasehold chain is read: Aull (1918), the Sanners (1918 to 1921), the Morrises (1921), Masbach (1925, row 46285). The stamps ($4.50) suggest a price near $4,000 to $4,500 (inference). What it does not settle: the Aull-to-Sanner deed (the Sanners' Oct. 30, 1918 mortgage is at S.C.L. 3281/603 and Aull's deed to the Shieldses at 3281/596, so it is very probably between them) and folio 256 itself, which needs a re-request from MSA. Shorey; Virginia died about July 4, 1924, leaving everything by will (Wills E.R.D. 149/438) to her daughter Lillian K. Winbigler. Winbigler took as Virginia's daughter and devisee (whether she was George's daughter too is not said). (3) The stamps ($20) suggest about $20,000 (inference). (4) Schwaab's holding was the 1921 corner lot plus this lot, through to Starr Lane; this lot lies south of the building on the lot to the north, so its fit to 3313 (the 1926 permit's number) against 3303 (Schwaab's ads) is a placement question for the chapter. All dated Feb. 23, 1926, acknowledged before George C. Wiedersum, notary, and recorded Feb. 24, 1926 between 11:01 and 11:03 a.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Carter and Sarah Williams lease Abraham H. Levine and Jesse Rosenstein, for 99 years renewable at $3 a year and redeemable for $50, a lot on the west side of Starr Lane 'formerly the Old York Road', north of Gorsuch Avenue: from the north-east corner of the 1866 Barrenger-to-Bucher lot (J.H.L. 52/250), 30 ft south to the centre of a 6-ft alley, 121 ft west to the east line of Hooper's 1872 sub-lease to Thomas Johnson (E.H.A. 76/578), and back; the Williamses had it from Minnie Gordon Gorter et al. (Oct. 30, 1919, S.C.L. 3478/514). The same day they deed the $3 rent and reversion to Edwin T. Dickerson, and Levine, Rosenstein and Dickerson mortgage the lot to the Maryland Title Guarantee Company for $2,000 of purchase money (released 1929). What it settles: (1) the 1926 lease is a lease of the Starr Lane lot itself (parcel FOURTH, 3312 to 3314 Old York Road, about 30 by 121 ft), not a lease under the Venable corner; the nominal $3 rent was a financing device. (2) It ties parcel FOURTH to the County chain: it is the north-east 30 ft of George W. Bucher's 1866 lot, and Hooper's 1872 Johnson sub-lease is its west neighbour. What it does not settle: S.C.L. 3478/514 (the Gorter title) and whether the $3 rent was redeemed or merged before Irvin or Franklin Realty. Update Oct. 14, 2026: Franklin Realty bought out Jessie Rosenstein and Edwin T. Dickerson on Oct. 20, 1941 (M.L.P. 6229/141, /142) and took a trustee's deed in 1944 (M.L.P. 6605/526), as recited in 773:mdlr-mlp6660-512-franklin-realty-hudson-realty-starr-lane-1944.
