Bucher, for 99 years renewable at $150 a year ($121.50 to Lewis, $28.50 to Barbara), redeemable for $2,500, a lot 'near the first Toll Gate on the York Turnpike road': 100 ft on the east side of the turnpike, from about 31 ft north of the south-west corner of the land of Augustus Dawes (or Danes), deceased, at Thomas A. Hart's lot, about 240 ft east to the west side of the Old York Road (98 2/3 ft on it), and back along Hart's lot; no building until a dwelling fronts the Old York Road. The ground is part of lots 6, 7 and 8 of the partition of Dawes's land among his children by the Circuit Court for Baltimore County (decree Sept. 25, 1866, John P. Dawes et al. v. Lewis L. Barrenger et al.): lot 6 allotted to William Dawes and conveyed to Barrenger, lot 7 to Lewis, lot 8 to Barbara (probably a Dawes daughter). What it settles: the root of 3313 to 3319's Starr Lane and turnpike ground is reached at 1866: the Bucher lease of a through lot from the turnpike to the Old York Road, out of Augustus Dawes's partitioned land. No tract is named; the Dawes partition papers and Dawes's own deed are where one would appear. 'Near the first Toll Gate' is a location phrase only and is not shown to be the Gilmor Lane gate. What it does not settle: how Bucher's lease passed to George G. Hooper before 1872, and the rent's later holders to Minnie Gordon Gorter (1919).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 4853, folios 457 to 459 (MSA CE 168-4861; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved; Adams's $7,500 mortgage ends on 457 above it, assigned in 1931 to Maryland Title Securities). Dated and acknowledged Mar. 1, 1928 before Harry Kuszmaul, notary; recorded Mar. 3, 1928 at 12:15 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Samuel H. Adams, unmarried, conveys the Title Holding Company an eight-sided tract: 101 ft 7 1/4 in on Greenmount from the north end of Schwaab's 1925 lot, east 247 ft 4 in along the third lot of the 1922 Wamsley deed (S.C.L. 3869/529) and a Frederick-to-Esselman lot (cited 'S.C.L. 2905/14', a liber out of sequence for 1922) to Old York Road, then round the Hooper-to-Johnson sub-lease of 1872 and the Rich trustees' lot of 1922 (on the centre of a 6-ft alley) and back along Schwaab's north line. Adams had it from 'Maude E. Shorey widow et al' by a deed of Feb. 27, 1928 recorded just before; the deed does not call them heirs, but the tract is described entirely by Esselman's own 1922 deeds. What it settles: the Esselman land passed from his heirs to Adams (Feb. 27, 1928) and at once to the Title Holding Company (a lender's title company), so Adams was a conduit. The tract is parcels FIRST, SECOND and THIRD of the 1979 deed plus the 1935 Siwinski corner, and leaves out a 30 ft 4 in by 121 ft strip on Old York Road, which is parcel FOURTH (the 1926 Starr Lane lease lot). What it does not settle: the Feb. 27, 1928 deed (who 'et al.' were), the Frederick deed's true liber, and the Rich trustees' deed (here 'S.C.L. 3904 folio 258'; the 1925 deed has 358).

summary: Deed and mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5368, folios 38 to 42 (MSA CE 168-5376; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved). Dated, acknowledged (before Bessie R. Burns, notary) and recorded July 21, 1933 at 2:56 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). The Title Holding Company conveys Alvin J. and Alma R. Irvin and Irving J. and Carolyn W. Orem, each couple an undivided half by the entireties, the Greenmount front from the north line of Schwaab's 1925 lot (101 ft 9 in north of 33rd Street) 101 ft 7 1/4 in north to 'Venable Street (formerly Crawford Street)', 103 ft 11 in deep to an iron pipe, its east line ending 15 ft east of the south-east corner of 'a brick garage there erected'; part of Adams's 1928 deed. The gasoline tanks, pumps and equipment pass only as the grantor's interest, and the grant is subject to existing leases. The buyers give back a $25,000 purchase-money mortgage (payable over five years at 6 percent), assigned the same day to Maryland Title Securities and released July 21, 1936; a second mortgage of even date follows. A margin note cites a partial release at S.C.L. 5576/59, the folio before the 1935 Siwinski deed. What it settles: (1) 'Irvin et al.' are the Irvins and the Orems (the partners of Irvin's Auto Service, row 39742), buying Esselman's garage front in 1933 with a filling station on it. (2) Venable Street was formerly Crawford Street. (3) The stamps ($40) suggest about $40,000 (inference). The 32-ft north corner went to George W. Siwinski in 1935 (S.C.L. 5576/60), leaving the 69 ft 7 1/4 in that is parcel FIRST. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): the 1935 Siwinski package is read (773:mdlr-scl5576-60-irvin-orem-siwinski-venable-corner-1935): the 32-ft Venable corner was released from the $25,000 and $13,841.84 purchase-money mortgages (S.C.L. 5368/39, /42) and deeded to Siwinski, and the brick garage stood at the south end of this tract.

Dated, acknowledged (before Harry G. Bayley, notary) and recorded July 17, 1941 at 2:50 p.m. (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk). The Irvins and Orems convey the Franklin Realty & Finance Co., Inc. two lots: the 69 ft 7 1/4 in Greenmount front by 103 ft 11 in (part of their 1933 deed) and an irregular Old York Road piece south of the alley (from the Title Holding Company, June 10, 1936, S.C.L. 5635/18), with a 6-ft right of way north to Venable Avenue, subject to their Aug. 22, 1940 mortgage to the Metropolitan Savings Bank (M.L.P. 6071/98), which the grantee assumes. What it settles: the 1941 hop: 'et al.' are Alma R. Irvin and the Orems, and the lots are parcels FIRST and SECOND of the 1979 deed. Franklin Realty & Finance (the Chertkof family company, row 42239 on 3107) held them from July 1941; by Nov. 24, 1941 David W. and Annie Chertkof deeded FIRST to THIRD to the Hudson Realty Company (M.L.P. 6244/524, recited in 1979), so a step from Franklin to the Chertkofs, and THIRD's route from Title Holding, are unread. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): the Irvins and Orems had borrowed $4,000 from George W. Siwinski on parcel FIRST in 1935 (773:mdlr-scl5576-60-irvin-orem-siwinski-venable-corner-1935), released Dec. 12, 1939. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (late): both open steps are read. Franklin Realty & Finance Co. deeded FIRST and SECOND to David W. Chertkof and wife on July 17, 1941 (M.L.P. 6193/218; Chertkof signed as Franklin's president), subject to the Irvins' 1940 Metropolitan Savings Bank mortgage (M.L.P. 6071/98), which the grantees 'do not assume'; and the Title Holding Company deeded THIRD to David W. and Annie Chertkof on Sept. 30, 1941 (M.L.P. 6222/14). No release of the 1940 mortgage has been found.

summary: Deed and two mortgages, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber W.A. 3747, folios 332 to 341 (MSA CE 168-14067; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved; the second mortgage runs past 341). All dated Apr. 18, 1979 and recorded Apr. 19, 1979 from 10 a.m. (William Allen, Clerk). The Hudson Realty Company, by Jack O. Chertkof as president, conveys Henry Y. C. Lee four parcels in fee for $200,000: FIRST, the 69 ft 7 1/4 in Greenmount front; SECOND, the Old York Road piece south of the alley; THIRD, the Venable and Old York Road corner, bounded by the 1926 Williams-to-Levine lease lot; FOURTH, the 30 by 121 ft Starr Lane lot, the north-east corner of the 1866 Barrenger-to-Bucher lot, bounded by Hooper's 1872 Johnson sub-lease. No ground rent is mentioned. Hudson had FIRST to THIRD from David W. and Annie Chertkof (Nov. 24, 1941, M.L.P. 6244/524) and FOURTH from the Franklin Realty & Finance Company (Sept. 5, 1944, M.L.P. 6660/512). Lee gives back $120,000 to the David and Annie Chertkof Mitzvah Fund, Inc. (10 percent, $1,500 a month; transfer to a company allowed) and a second mortgage of $30,000 to the Chertkof Foundation, Inc.; both were assigned on Oct. 4, 1983 (Liber 0118/295 and /296) and released in 1986 (917/433) and 1990 (2684/491). What it settles: (1) how Hudson acquired each parcel (the chapter's open question). (2) The Chertkof family (Franklin Realty & Finance; Hudson Realty; the 1977 owner 'Chertkoff' in row 39664) held 3313 to 3319 from 1941 to 1979 and financed the sale through its charities. (3) 'No releases found' is corrected: both Chertkof mortgages were released. summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 169, folios 672 to 674 (MSA CE 66-219; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved and checked; an assignment from William A. Ridgely ends above it and a sheriff's deed of 'Shillings Meadows' follows). Dated and acknowledged July 7, 1823 before Fielder Israel and Jas. B. Latimer, justices of Baltimore City; recorded Dec. 9, 1823 (W. Gibson, Clerk). James Carroll the Elder (Gough's executor, who had married Sophia, Gough's only child) and his three surviving sons convey Philip G. Biays, for $1, two Huntington lots whose price had long been paid but never deeded: (1) 3 a 1 r 12 p, under Harry Dorsey Gough's bond of about Jan. 15, 1803 to Christopher Walker and a plat of Jan. 13, 1803 'signed by William Jackson Jas Biays C Walker & John Smith' and lodged by Carroll in the County Court office: from the end of the S 40 3/4 E line of James Biays's lot, on the north-west side of 'a road laid out by the said Harry D Gough', along Biays's lot to Joseph Thornburgh's lot, along it about 39 perches to the York Turnpike, 3.7 perches down the turnpike to Gough's road and back along the road, excepting 'a School house' lot that Gough and Prudence had conveyed to trustees; (2) 3 a 3 p, sold by Carroll as executor to Walker on Mar. 8, 1809 at $200 an acre: from the point where the N 45 W line of 'Old Huntington' meets the Old York Road (a line run from a stone at the beginning of 'New Huntington' to two stones where a boundary stone once stood, shown to James Baker by Joseph Merryman and John Gorsuch), N 40 1/4 E 45 perches, N 82 1/2 W 24.7 perches to the Old York Road and back along it, subject to an old lease by Gough, Prudence Gough and Thomas B. and Elizabeth Onion to 'Charles Carline' (reading uncertain). Walker's rights passed to James Biays, then to John W. Stump, then to Philip G. Biays. The Carrolls' title is the wills of Harry Dorsey Gough and of Prudence Gough, 'who held in her own right an undivided moiety' of Huntington. What it settles: (1) the 1823 deed behind Philip G. Biays's 1826 trust and Magruder's 1844 sale is read: lot 1 is the toll-gate wedge (the same courses as 1844), bought by Christopher Walker under Gough's 1803 bond and plat, which is Cope's plat of Gough's 1803 lots (MSA C2843-15), signed by the buyers. (2) A school house stood on the wedge by 1823, on a lot Gough and his wife gave trustees; whether it is the later toll-house lot is not shown. (3) Prudence Gough's own half of Huntington is the Carnan daughters' share of the 1768 settlement, and the Carrolls are the heirs by both wills. (4) Lot 2 lies on the Old York Road at the 'Old Huntington' line, under an Onion-era lease. What it does not settle: the Gough deed to the school trustees, the 1803 bond itself, and the lease to Carline. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): the County grantor index under Gough, 1787 to 1809, is read (725:index-ce33-3-p151-gough-1787-1797, 725:index-ce33-4-p163-gough-1798-1803, 725:index-ce33-5-p181-gough-1804-1809) and has no deed to school trustees, so the school-house lot was conveyed after 1809 or is indexed under another name. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (night): the Bouldin papers hold the 1821 draft of this deed (725:msa-c2843-15-p15-carroll-philip-biays-lot-74-draft-1821): the second lot, 3 a 3 p, is 'Lot No. 74 on a plat of Huntington', drafted at $2,000; a part of Lot 74 on the old York Road had been assigned by Margaret Burke to William Goodwin in 1800 (W.G. 50/586). Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Gough school house, 1810-1823 index): the three County grantor volumes that follow are read as far as the scans go (725:index-ce33-6-p164-gough-none-1811-1813, 725:index-ce33-7-p193-gough-prudence-ridgelys-whim-1816-1818 and 725:index-ce33-8-p209-gough-prudence-jenkins-huntington-1820-1823 (also filed on 726)). They hold nine Gough lines in all, every one entered 'Gough Prudence &c': eight deeds of Pt Ridgely's Whim in 1818 (W.G. 147/140 to 578) and one deed of 'Pt Huntington 5 3/4 a 11 P' to William Jenkins in 1822 (W.G. 163/674). None is to trustees and no line in the Go pages names a school or a school house. The scans do not hold the first Go pages of any of the three volumes (W.G. 105 to 115/28, 126 to 137/594 and 148 to 155/206, about 1810 to mid-1811, 1814 to 1816 and 1819 to early 1820), so the 'after 1809' reading is narrowed, not closed. 'Gough and Prudence' in the 1823 deed reads most naturally as Harry Dorsey Gough and his wife (INFERRED), which would put the deed in the 1787 to 1808 runs already read, with no such deed; the other branch, 'indexed under another name' (for example under Carroll, the first-named executor, or never recorded), gains weight. The Go run of CE 33-8 stops at W.G. 169/294, before this deed (169/672, recorded Dec. 9, 1823), so this deed and anything after 169/294 sit in the next index volume. What it still does not settle: the Gough deed to the school trustees.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County land records, Liber J.H.L. 46, folios 149 to 151 (MSA CE 62-46; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved and checked against the 1809 and 1847 courses). Dated and acknowledged June 27, 1865 before Saml. Spicer, J.P.; recorded Oct. 4, 1865 (Jno. H. Longnecker, Clerk). Oliver P. and Araminta Merryman convey John Litzinger, for $200, in fee, the 2 15/16 acres between the centre of the York Turnpike and the west side of the Old York Road on the first line of Gough, Prudence Gough and Job Merryman's 1798 lease to Jesse Brown (W.G. 54/156): S 82 E 15.9 perches, S 7 3/4 W 30.7 perches along the old road, S 79 1/2 W 11.7 perches to the turnpike's centre: the same courses as Dorothy Brown's 1809 assignment to James Biays (W.G. 104/48) and Allender's 1847 sale of the leasehold to Litzinger (A.W.B. 381/475), 'and to have and to hold specially the clear yearly rent of four pounds eight shillings & one penny'. The Merrymans had the fee from Charles R. Carroll (Gough's grandson) by a deed of Aug. 18, 1859 (G.H.C. 27/45). No tract is named. What it settles: (1) the reversion of the 1798 Brown lease went from Gough to the Carroll heirs and, in 1859, to Oliver P. Merryman, who sold it to the leaseholder Litzinger in 1865, merging rent and lease. (2) Litzinger's 1866 lease to John H. White (row 46310) cut half an acre and 20 perches out of this parcel, so the Bateman Old York Road lot and Hunteman's 1870 sub-lease lie inside the 2 15/16 acres. (3) The parcel's width, 190 to 260 ft between the roads, fits the stretch from about the 3100 block north rather than the fork tip at 3011 (an inference from the widths). (4) 3224's 1884 deed recites a separate, later Merryman deed; this one shows Oliver P. Merryman held Carroll reversions. What it does not settle: G.H.C. 27/45 and the exact place of the parcel on the modern blocks. Update Oct. 14, 2026: both steps behind it are read: the 1798 lease (720:mdlr-wg54-156-gough-job-merryman-jesse-brown-lease-1798) and Carroll's 1859 deed of the reversion of the whole 11 acres to Merryman for $736 (720:mdlr-ghc27-45-charles-carroll-oliver-merryman-brown-lease-reversion-1859). Dated and acknowledged Sept. 21, 1876. John and Hannah Bolgiano lease Bernard Bertling Lots 16 and 17 (200 by 100 ft at the north-west corner of the York Turnpike and Wilson Street, half of a 20-ft alley left open on the rear line) for 99 years renewable forever at $200 a year from Jan. 1, 1877 (January and July). Bertling could buy the rent out for $2,500 before Jan. 1, 1878, or for $3,333 1/3 before Jan. 1, 1881 (the rent at 8 and then 6 percent). No building covenant appears. Bolgiano's title: the Wilson trustees' deed of Jan. 14, 1871 (E.H.A. 70/115). Delivered Jan. 19, 1877. What it settles: the lease behind the $200 rent on 3326 to 3338 is read at its true folio (584, as the 1972 deed gives it; 57 was negative): the rent was redeemable for four years and, not redeemed, became 'now irredeemable' (the 1935 deed's words) until the 1972 merger. What it does not settle: the recording date (on the missing folios).

summary: Three instruments, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5589, folios 225 to 234 (MSA CE 168-5597; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved; the third runs past 234). (1) Dec. 27, 1935: Safe Deposit and Trust Company, substituted trustee under the will of Joseph A. Bolgiano, conveys his granddaughters Mary Mildred Hazen and Jane Collison Weiss, as tenants in common, four ground rents with their reversions (1115 Ashland Avenue, 1715 Jefferson Street, the Greenmount and Venable corner, 1224 Aisquith Street). Joseph A. Bolgiano's will left a trust for his daughter Flora for life with remainder to her issue; Flora (Mrs. J. Burch Joyce) died in August 1935, leaving the two sisters; the Circuit Court of Baltimore City (Frank W. Bolgiano et al., trustees, v. Flora B. Joyce, Docket 53A/107) awarded them the fund on Nov. 13 and ratified the division on Dec. 6, 1935. The four rents were Flora's share ('Division A') in the partition of Joseph A. Bolgiano's estate (Charles J. Bolgiano et al. v. Flora B. Joyce, Docket 1913 A/159). The Greenmount rent is 'the annual now irredeemable ground rent of two hundred dollars' under the 1876 lease to Bertling (J.B. 97/584). Recorded Jan. 2, 1936 at 10:45 a.m. (2) and (3) Dec. 28, 1935: each sister deeds her half to the trust company in trust for the OTHER sister for life and then her family (the Weiss half for the Hazens, the Hazen half for the Weisses). What it settles: the rent's path from 1913 to 1972 is now read: John Bolgiano's ground to Joseph A. Bolgiano's estate, partitioned in 1913 with Flora's share in trust, to her daughters in 1935, and through their cross-trusts with the trust company (later Mercantile-Safe Deposit) to the 1972 merger. What it does not settle: how John Bolgiano's 1876 reversion reached Joseph A. Bolgiano (not recited), the will's date, and the equity papers.

summary: Trustee's deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 1758, folios 40 to 41 (MSA CE 168-1766; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved). Dated, acknowledged (before Wm. Merriken, J.P.) and recorded Oct. 25, 1898 (Robert Ogle, Clerk). Henry W. Fox, trustee under a decree of Circuit Court No. 2 of Baltimore City of Aug. 29, 1898 in Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County v. John B. Henry and others, sells William and Elizabeth Lacey, for $675 (sale of Sept. 20, 1898), in fee, the 25 by 120 ft lot on the west side of the York Turnpike 100 ft north of Wilson Street: Lot 1 and part of Lot 2 on the plat filed with William H. Brune Jr.'s lease to Augustus D. Clemens Jr. of May 1, 1886 (J.W.S. 153/55), mortgaged by John B. Henry and others to the association on Feb. 27, 1895 (J.B. 1546/108). What it settles: (1) the 25-ft lot of chain B came to the Laceys in 1898 (not 1895, as first read from the 1910 recital) by a building-association foreclosure against John B. Henry, the Waverly blacksmith (J. B. Henry & Sons, 1204 York Road), not from Gutman directly. (2) The lot lies in the Brune ground leased to A. D. Clemens Jr. in 1886, so chain B joins the Clemens subdivisions north of Lots 16-17. What it does not settle: how Henry took the lot from Clemens or Gutman (J.B. 1546/108 and J.W.S. 153/55 are next), and whether the 1886 lease's rent was ever redeemed (the 1898 deed conveys fee simple). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1895 mortgage is read (778:mdlr-jb1546-108-henry-waverly-building-assn-mortgage-1895): John B. Henry and his sons William R. and Charles D. had the lot in fee from A. D. Clemens Jr. (Nov. 23, 1886, J.W.S. 157/35); the 1886 Brune lease is cited only for its plat (778:mdlr-jws153-55-brune-clemens-lease-calvin-avenue-lots-1886). Dated, acknowledged (before B. C. Chesney, notary) and recorded Nov. 25, 1935 at 2:46 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). M. Lillian and Charles A. Slade sell David W. and Annie Chertkof, in fee, 'Nos 3105 3107 and 3109 Greenmount Avenue' by the Martinet survey of Nov. 20, 1935; no ground rent is mentioned. The Slades' title: Edna L. Rainey, widow, to M. Lillian Slade, Oct. 11, 1921 (S.C.L. 3787/503). The stamps ($21) suggest about $21,000 (inference). The Chertkofs gave the Equitable Trust Company a $15,000 purchase-money mortgage, released May 1, 1936. What it settles: the Slades' seller was Edna L. Rainey, widow; the Raineys were neighbours (Robert Rainey, plumber, 1015 York Road; his 47.8-ft lot south of the church on the c. 1913 plat, row 42264). The Raineys' title is answered by S.C.L. 3787/503 (read October 14): M. Estelle Bateman sold to Robert and Edna L. Rainey herself on July 18, 1918 (S.C.L. 3236/149), so there was no heirs' step. Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 1921 Rainey deed is read (737:mdlr-scl3787-503-rainey-slade-3105-3109-1921).

Levine's half, sold in Martin Levine, infant, v. Stella M. Levine) completed the title; the Chertkof company then moved the lot to Hudson Realty, the 1979 seller. The stamps suggest about $3,300 to $3,400 (inference).

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 141, folios 81 to 85 (MSA CE 66-191; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved, the date and plat checked). Dated and acknowledged Mar. 12, 1817 before Geo. Gouldth Presbury and Baltzer Schaeffer, justices (Esther Brown releasing dower); recorded May 23, 1817 (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). George I. Brown, merchant, sells the City Bank of Baltimore, for $12,000, three lots of 'Huntington' (7 a 0 r 2 p): Lot 1 (Jackson's strip of 1811) and Lot 2 (1 a 47 p, Biays's lot of 1811), which Elisha E. Russell conveyed Brown and William S. Hollins by a deed of about May 4, 1811 (W.G. 113/638), Brown holding by survivorship after Hollins's death; and Lot 3 (3 a 2 r 8 p), John Smith's lot from Gough of Jan. 13, 1803, which Dennis A. Smith conveyed Mary Allison in 1811 (W.G. 116/404) and Allison conveyed Brown on Feb. 26, 1817; Lot 3 runs to 'a road leading from Joseph Merrymans house to the Turnpike road' and to the centre of 'a road left open by William Jackson and James Biays'. Copied into the record is Jehu Bouldin's plat of Apr. 1, 1817, 'Three lots part of Huntington', at 10 perches to the inch, with 'Merryman's Road' along the north-east and 'Jackson & Biays's Road' running south-south-east from the lots; no turnpike, neighbours or north arrow are drawn. What it settles: (1) Russell's lots left him by an outright conveyance to his creditors Brown and Hollins in May 1811, two months after his deed of trust; the bank's 1820 deed calls the 1817 sale a settlement of Brown's debt, while this deed states $12,000. (2) The 1817 plat is the oldest drawing found of any of these lots, and it names two roads: Merryman's Road and the road Jackson and Biays left open. (3) The three lots, with the Smith lot, went bank (1817) to McCormick (1820) to James Wilson (1823). What it does not settle: W.G. 113/638 itself, and where the plat sits on the modern blocks (the Jackson-Biays road is the key). Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): both deeds it recites are read: Russell to Brown and Hollins, May 4, 1811 (726:mdlr-wg113-638-russell-brown-hollins-release-1811), and Dennis A. Smith to Mary Allison, Nov. 21, 1811 (726:mdlr-wg116-404-dennis-smith-mary-allison-huntington-lot-1811); Allison's lot starts at the second corner of Russell's Biays lot and shares its N 39 3/4 E line.

summary: Lease, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 54, folios 156 to 160 and on (MSA CE 66-104; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved; the renewal clause, signatures and recording are past folio 160). Dated Apr. 16, 1798. A three-party lease: Harry Dorsey Gough and Prudence Gough, Job Merryman, farmer, and Jesse Brown, tailor of Baltimore. The Goughs had leased Job Merryman two parcels of 'Huntingdon' on Aug. 6, 1795 (W.G. S.S. 227) for 99 years renewable at £16 11s 3d; that lease was defective (an unattested interlineation and obliterations), and Job, needing £100, surrendered it for that sum paid by Brown, and the Goughs re-granted it to Brown on the same terms. Parcel 1, 6 a 3 q 15 p: from a point 16 perches 6 ft S 46 1/2 E of a large stone at the corner of Joseph Merryman's land, S 82 E 59 3/4 perches to the York road, S 8 W 37 perches along it to 'a road left by the said Harry Dorsey Gough and wife', and along that road back. Parcel 2, 4 a 32 p, a quadrilateral off the end of the first lot's second course, also bounded by the Goughs' road. 11 a 7 p in all; rent £16 11s 3d on April 6. What it settles: (1) the 1798 lease behind the 1809 Brown-to-Biays assignment, the 1847 Allender sale and the 1865 Merryman deed is read: it is Job Merryman's 1795 lease re-granted, so Job was the outgoing lessee, not an owner. (2) The 1809 parcel (2 15/16 acres) starts where parcel 1's S 82 E line 'crosses' the later York Turnpike and runs to its end at the 'York road' of 1798, which is the Old York Road: so the turnpike, built after 1798, was cut across the lease, leaving most of parcel 1 west of it and the 2 15/16 acres between the two roads. (3) Joseph Merryman's land (Merryman's Lot) lay at its north-west corner. What it does not settle: where on the modern blocks (the 1801 Brown-to-Wheetley assignment and Whitely's to James Wilson, rows 46012 to 46014, are parts of the same lease, at 3200 to 3224 by the chapter's reading). Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): the 1795 original (720:mdlr-wgss227-gough-job-merryman-lease-1795), this lease's end with Job Merryman's GBP 100 receipt (720:mdlr-wg54-160-jesse-brown-lease-1798-end-receipt) and the corrected 1802 re-grant (720:mdlr-wg72-124-gough-jesse-brown-corrected-lease-1802) are read: parcel 2's N 30 W, copied from 1795 into this lease, was corrected to N 50 W in 1802.

What it does not settle: where on the modern blocks (the 1801 Brown-to-Wheetley assignment and Whitely's to James Wilson, rows 46012 to 46014, are parts of the same lease, at 3200 to 3224 by the chapter's reading). summary: Lease, Baltimore County land records, Liber J.W.S. 153, folios 55 to 59 (MSA CE 62-153; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved; the lease runs past folio 59, so its term, rent, Brune's title recital and recording are not seen). Dated May 1, 1886 (entry 905; mailed to Clemens July 17, 1886). William H. Brune Jr. leases Augustus D. Clemens Jr. 21 lots in Baltimore County 'as designated on the plat of the property of Augustus D Clemens Junior herewith filed', the plat being in 'Plats' at the Circuit Court clerk's office (the margin's '1/14' is probably Plat Book 1, folio 14). The lots read are 25 by 90 ft on the south side of Calvin Avenue (laid out 50 ft wide at right angles to Barclay Street and the York Turnpike) from Barclay Street east, plat Lots 11 onward, each to a 10-ft alley. What it settles: the plat cited by the Laceys' 1898 deed and the Henrys' 1895 mortgage for 'lot no 1 and a part of lot no 2' is the plat of Clemens's own property filed with this lease; the lease itself does not include Lot 1, so it is cited only for the plat, and Brune's title was Clemens's own deed of the same day, so the lease is a sale and lease-back (folio 61, read October 14; 778:mdlr-jws153-60-brune-clemens-lease-end-sale-leaseback-1886). What it does not settle: the plat itself (Baltimore County plats, apparently 1/14), which would place Lot 1 on the turnpike.

Aull the four leaseholds of the 1912 row north of Vineyard Lane: the corner lot (15 ft, 3026) subject to $72 a year, and 3028, 3030 and 3032 (14 ft each) subject to $66 each, June and December, which Aull and his wife had leased her on Dec. 6, 1912 (S.C.L. 2787/374). The same day Aull mortgages all four to the York Road Building Association for $5,330 (41 shares), released in 1924. What it settles: Chapman was Aull's straw: he leased her the four new houses in December 1912, sold the four rents to F. X. Hooper ten days later (S.C.L. 2787/376), took the leaseholds back in 1916, and sold them one by one: 3026 to the Spellmans (1917), 3028 to the Sanners and 3032 to the Shieldses (1918). The corner rent was $72, not $66. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (S.C.L. 3918/495 read): the executors' deed is read (726:mdlr-scl3918-495-aull-executors-widow-3030-1922). summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 113, folios 638 to 641 (MSA CE 66-163; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved, the trust clause checked). Dated and acknowledged May 4, 1811 before Edwd. Woodyear and Edwd. Aisquith, justices, Elizabeth Russell releasing dower; recorded June 21, 1811 (Wm. Gibson, Clerk); delivered to Geo. I. Brown. Elisha E. Russell, master mariner, grants George I. Brown and William S. Hollins, merchants, in fee, for $4,500, the two Huntington lots he had bought on Mar. 13, 1811. Lot 1 starts at a stone at the end of the N 36 1/4 W 90 1/4-perch line of William Jackson's 1803 Gough lot and runs back along that line S 36 1/4 E 38.3 perches, then S 57 1/2 W 9.6 perches and N 35 1/2 W 35.2 perches to Jackson's second line, and along it to the start; the acreage is left blank (about 2 1/8 acres by the courses). Lot 2, 1 a 47 p, starts at the stone at the north-east corner of Jackson's lot and runs S 36 1/2 E 8 1/2 perches along it, N 39 3/4 E 26.7 perches 'to a road leading to Joseph Merryman's', N 58 1/2 W 8 1/2 perches along the road to the end of James Biays's N 29 1/2 E 24-perch line, and along it back. The deed recites Russell's trust of Mar. 14, 1811 to secure his debt to Brown and Hollins, and says the conveyance and release are made 'by way of satisfying and extinguish[ing] four thousand five hundred dollars part' of that debt. What it settles: (1) Russell's lots left him by a deed in lieu of foreclosure, not by a trustees' sale: he released his equity of redemption to his creditors for a $4,500 credit against the $4,735 secured (so about $235 still owing, inference); Brown later held alone by survivorship after Hollins's death (W.G. 141/81). (2) Lot 1 bounds on the N 36 1/4 W line of Jackson's lot and Lot 2 starts at Jackson's north-east corner; Mary Allison's 1811 lot (W.G. 116/404) starts at Lot 2's second corner and shares its N 39 3/4 E line, so the three lots of Bouldin's 1817 plat lie together along Jackson's line and Merryman's road (inference from the courses). What it does not settle: where Jackson's lot and Merryman's road fall on the modern blocks.

Elisha E. Russell, master mariner, grants George I. Brown and William S. Hollins, merchants, in fee, for $4,500, the two Huntington lots he had bought on Mar. 13, 1811. Lot 1 starts at a stone at the end of the N 36 1/4 W 90 1/4-perch line of William Jackson's 1803 Gough lot and runs back along that line S 36 1/4 E 38.3 perches, then S 57 1/2 W 9.6 perches and N 35 1/2 W 35.2 perches to Jackson's second line, and along it to the start; the acreage is left blank (about 2 1/8 acres by the courses). Lot 2, 1 a 47 p, starts at the stone at the north-east corner of Jackson's lot and runs S 36 1/2 E 8 1/2 perches along it, N 39 3/4 E 26.7 perches 'to a road leading to Joseph Merryman's', N 58 1/2 W 8 1/2 perches along the road to the end of James Biays's N 29 1/2 E 24-perch line, and along it back. The deed recites Russell's trust of Mar. 14, 1811 to secure his debt to Brown and Hollins, and says the conveyance and release are made 'by way of satisfying and extinguish[ing] four thousand five hundred dollars part' of that debt. What it settles: (1) Russell's lots left him by a deed in lieu of foreclosure, not by a trustees' sale: he released his equity of redemption to his creditors for a $4,500 credit against the $4,735 secured (so about $235 still owing, inference); Brown later held alone by survivorship after Hollins's death (W.G. 141/81). (2) Lot 1 bounds on the N 36 1/4 W line of Jackson's lot and Lot 2 starts at Jackson's north-east corner; Mary Allison's 1811 lot (W.G. 116/404) starts at Lot 2's second corner and shares its N 39 3/4 E line, so the three lots of Bouldin's 1817 plat lie together along Jackson's line and Merryman's road (inference from the courses). What it does not settle: where Jackson's lot and Merryman's road fall on the modern blocks.

Smith, Esquire, of Baltimore sells Mary Allison of the same city, in fee, for $1,065, the Huntington lot that Harry Dorsey Gough and Prudence his wife conveyed John Smith on Jan. 13, 1803: from a point in the north-east line of William Jackson's part, S 36 1/2 E 8 1/2 perches from the stone at Jackson's most northerly corner, N 39 3/4 E 26.7 perches 'to a road leading from Joseph Merrymans house to the Turnpike road leading from the City of Baltimore towards York Town', along that road S 58 E 3, S 54 E 14 and S 48 E 1.1 perches, then S 44 W 24 perches, S 35 1/2 E 8.8 perches and S 51 1/2 W 7.8 perches 'to the center of a road let open by William Jackson and James Biays', and along the centre of that road straight back: 3 a 2 r 8 p (the courses close, about 563 square perches against 568 stated). Title: John Smith's deed to Dennis A. Smith of Apr. 28, 1809 (W.G. 104/352); no relationship between them is stated. What it settles: (1) Lot 3 of Bouldin's 1817 plat is read at its source: it starts at the second corner of Russell's Biays lot and shares that lot's N 39 3/4 E line, so it lay next to the Biays lot on its south-east (inference from the courses). (3) The road left open by Jackson and Biays, 'Jackson & Biays's Road' on the 1817 plat, is its south-west boundary. W.G. 104/352 (1809) and the 1803 Gough deed to John Smith (W.G. 74/327) are both read. Dated and acknowledged Aug. 6, 1795 before Geo. Salmon and Geo. Gouldsmith Presbury, Prudence Gough privately examined; witness Nicholas Brice; recorded Aug. 7, 1795 (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). Harry D. Gough and Prudence his wife lease Job Merryman of Baltimore County, for the rents and covenants only (no money paid), two parcels of Huntington: parcel 1, 6 a 3 q 15 p, from 16 perches 6 ft S 46 1/2 E of a large stone at the corner of Joseph Merryman's land, S 82 E 59 3/4 perches to the York Road, S 8 W 37 perches along it to 'a road left by the said Harry D Gough and wife', and along that road back; parcel 2, 4 a 32 p, from 3 perches 5 ft on a S 18 1/2 W line from the end of parcel 1's second course, S 38 W 16 perches, N 30 W 42 perches, N 38 E 16 perches to the Goughs' road, and along it back; 11 a 7 p in all. Term 99 years from Apr. 1, 1795, 'Renewable forever' at Job's option on paying a year's rent as a fine; rent £16 11s 3d current money a year, clear of taxes; re-entry at 60 days' arrears and forfeiture at two years'. No building covenant. What it settles: (1) the lease behind the 1798 Jesse Brown lease is read: an ordinary 99-year renewable ground lease to Job Merryman, which he surrendered in 1798 for £100 paid by Brown (W.G. 54/156 and 160). (2) The recorded copy reads N 30 W for parcel 2's second course, and the 1798 lease copies it; with 30 degrees the parcel holds only about 3 a 3 r 23 p, with 50 degrees exactly the stated 4 a 32 p, and the 1802 corrected lease (W.G. 72/124) changes it to N 50 W. (3) The 1798 lease called this one defective for an interlineation and obliterations, which this clean record copy does not show (they were on the original).

Dated and acknowledged Jan. 9, 1802 before Geo. Gouldsmith Presbury and James Carroll, justices, Prudence Gough privately examined; recorded Jan. 15, 1802 (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). Harry Dorsey Gough and Prudence Gough lease Jesse Brown, tailor of Baltimore, the two Huntington parcels of the 1798 lease. The recital: the Goughs leased Brown the parcels on about Apr. 16, 1798; 'it hath been discovered that there was a mistake made in describing the extent of one of the lines or courses of one of said lots'; Brown has that day assigned and surrendered the lease 'with intent that a new lease of said property by an accurate description be made to him ... under the like covenants and on the same rent'. Parcel 1 is unchanged (S 82 E 59 3/4 perches to the York road, S 8 W 37 perches along it); parcel 2 now runs S 38 W 16 perches, N 50 W 42 perches and N 38 E 16 perches to the Goughs' road; 11 a 7 p in all. Term 99 years from Jan. 8, 1802; rent £16 11s 3d on April 6 each year, clear of taxes; renewable forever on a fine of a year's rent; the same default clauses. The only road named is 'the York road'. Brown's assignment and surrender of the same date begins on folio 128 (read only to its opening). What it settles: (1) the 1802 lease the 1859 Carroll deed cites is read: a corrected re-grant, not a renewal or a division, and the error was parcel 2's bearing (N 30 W in 1795 and 1798, N 50 W here), which makes the stated acreage close. (2) The reversion of this lease is what the 1819 Chancery decree allotted Charles R. Carroll and he sold Oliver P. Merryman in 1859. (3) Brown's Oct. 20, 1801 assignment of one acre to John Wheetley (W.G. 72/454) was made under the 1798 lease and recorded on Feb. 26, 1802, after this re-grant; how the surrender dealt with Wheetley's acre is not stated (open question). What it does not settle: folio 128 on, the surrender's own terms. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (later): Brown's surrender of the same day is read (720:mdlr-wg72-128-jesse-brown-surrender-gough-1802): it names 'a mistake in one of the lines or courses' without saying which, and does not mention Wheetley.

Title: 'Deed from Walter I. Dawkins Administrator to M. Estelle Bateman dated October 28th 1902', R.O. 1984/398. (2) Entry 97: the Raineys mortgage the lot back to Bateman for $2,000, 'part of the purchase price', at 5 1/2 percent for three years, W. What it settles: the deed the 1921 Rainey-to-Slade deed recites is read: Bateman sold the Raineys a leasehold (the one-cent Coffield lease) for about $2,500, not the fee; by 1921 the one-cent rent had not been demanded for thirty years, and Edna Rainey sold M. Lillian Slade in fee for about $9,000 by the stamps. Lennox B. Clemens, notary and witness here and in 1921, may be of the Clemens family of the 3010 chain (unconfirmed).

Entry 366; dated Apr. 20, 1944, acknowledged in Philadelphia before E. S. Garrison, notary; recorded May 4, 1944 at 2:15 p.m. (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk); no revenue stamps. John Kaplan and Mary Kaplan his wife, of Philadelphia, grant and assign Stella M. Levine, widow, Martin Levine and Ruth Levine, all of Philadelphia, as tenants in common in equal shares, for one dollar 'and Natural Love and affection', their undivided half of the Starr Lane lot: from the west side of Starr Lane (now the Old York Road) at the north-east corner of the 1866 Barrenger-to-Bucher lot (J.H.L. 52/250), 30 ft south to the centre of a 6-ft alley, 121 ft west to the line of the 1872 Hooper-to-Johnson lot (E.H.A. 76/578), 30 ft north and 121 ft back, 'now known by the Street numbers as Nos 3312 and 3314 Old York Road'. The Kaplans had the half from 'Stella M Levine Administratrix' by a deed of July 30, 1941 (M.L.P. 6193/222), 'subject to a ground rent of one cent if demanded'. What it settles: (1) the 'Stella Levine widow et al' of the 1944 trustee's deed are Stella, Martin and Ruth Levine; the half went out of Abraham H. Levine's estate to the Kaplans in 1941 and came back as a family gift in 1944, which fits a straw or family arrangement (inference: the deed states no relationship and names no decedent). Six weeks later the court's trustee sold the half to Franklin Realty (M.L.P. 6605/526). (2) This deed states a one-cent rent where the 1926 lease and the 1944 trustee's deed state $3 (S.C.L. 4533/216): not reconciled. What it does not settle: M.L.P. 6193/222 and the estate. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (later): the 1941 deed it recites is read (773:mdlr-mlp6193-222-levine-administratrix-john-kaplan-starr-lane-1941): Stella M. Levine, administratrix, sold to John Kaplan alone for $500 under an Orphans' Court of Baltimore City order, subject to $3, so this deed's 'John Kaplan and wife' and 'one cent' are loose recitals.

(2) Entry 50: Alvin J. and Alma R. Irvin and Irving J. and Carolyn W. Orem grant George W. Siwinski that corner for his life, with power to sell, lease or mortgage the whole fee, remainder at his death to Arthur George Siwinski, Marjorie A. Michniewicz and Gertrude V. Porter (no relationships stated), for $5 and other considerations (stamps $12, about $11,500 to $12,000); special warranty; acknowledged before Vera C. Bushong, notary. Title: the 1933 Title Holding deed (S.C.L. 5368/38). (3) Entry 51: the Irvins and Orems, with Frank Gottschalk and B. Holly Porter as guarantors, mortgage Siwinski the rest of their tract for $4,000 at 6 percent, $250 a quarter; waived in 1936 and 1937 and released Dec. 12, 1939 (S.C.L. 5986/155 or 153). Its description of the whole tract: from a point 101 ft 9 in north of the north side of Thirty-third Street (the end of the first line of the 1925 Shorey-to-Schwaab lot, S.C.L. 4507/266), 101 ft 7 1/4 in north to 'Venable Street formerly Crawford Street', 103 ft 11 in east, 100 ft 4 1/2 in south to the Schwaab line at a point '15 feet easterly from the southeast corner of a brick garage there erected', and 103 ft 11 in back, saving the Siwinski corner. What it settles: (1) the 1935 Siwinski deed that ends parcel FIRST on the north is read: the Irvins and Orems cut the 32-ft Venable corner out of their 101 ft 7 1/4 in, leaving the 69 ft 7 1/4 in of parcel FIRST, and the same day borrowed $4,000 from Siwinski on what they kept. (2) The brick garage stood at the south (Schwaab) end of the tract, on parcel FIRST, not on the Siwinski corner. (3) From Thirty-third Street north: Schwaab's lot 101 ft 9 in, parcel FIRST 69 ft 7 1/4 in, Siwinski's corner 32 ft, then Venable: about 203 ft 4 1/4 in in all (arithmetic, assuming a straight frontage). What it does not settle: Siwinski's later dispositions and S.C.L. 4507/266.

The 15th lot is plat Lot 25; the 16th, plat Lot 26, is the corner of Calvin Avenue and the York Turnpike: 25 ft on the south side of Calvin Avenue, 375 ft east of Barclay Street, by 90 ft on the west side of the turnpike to the north side of a 10-ft alley. Brune's title: 'deed from said Clemens and wife to said Brune dated May 1st A D 1886 and recorded or intended to be recorded prior hereto'. Term 99 years, renewable forever on a $10 fine; rent $50 a year on each lot and $62.50 on the 16th, $1,062.50 in all, May 1 and November 1, each lot liable only for its own rent; distress or re-entry at 60 days, forfeiture at six months; redeemable after May 1, 1901 at 4 percent, written $1,200 a lot (4 percent of $50 is $1,250, so probably miscopied) and $1,562.50 for the 16th. Signed by Brune and Clemens before Geo. McCaffray, J.P., acknowledged May 1, 1886 in Baltimore City; recorded the same day (John W. Shanklin, Clerk); no plat is copied in. What it settles: (1) Clemens sold Brune the fee of 21 Calvin Avenue lots and leased them back the same day, creating $1,062.50 a year of ground rent; the earlier reading of all 21 as south-side lots is corrected (16 south, 5 north). (2) The only turnpike lot in the lease is the 90-ft corner lot 26, north of the 10-ft alley 90 ft south of Calvin Avenue: the 3360 lot (just south of that alley, parts of plat Lots 3 and 4) and the 25-ft Henry lot (Lot 1 and part of Lot 2, the north part of 3334-3338) stayed in Clemens's fee, and he sold or leased them himself in 1886 and 1887. What it does not settle: the plat (County plats, apparently 1/14) and the Clemens-to-Brune deed (not on J.W.S. 153/50 to 55, read October 14; still to be found). Update Oct. 14, 2026 (later): the Wilson trustees' deed to Clemens is read (778:mdlr-jws153-52-wilson-trustees-clemens-lots-18-28-1886); Calvin Avenue was laid out through Lots 18 to 28 of the 1871 Wilson plat.

Term 99 years, renewable forever on a $10 fine; rent $50 a year on each lot and $62.50 on the 16th, $1,062.50 in all, May 1 and November 1, each lot liable only for its own rent; distress or re-entry at 60 days, forfeiture at six months; redeemable after May 1, 1901 at 4 percent, written $1,200 a lot (4 percent of $50 is $1,250, so probably miscopied) and $1,562.50 for the 16th. Signed by Brune and Clemens before Geo. McCaffray, J.P., acknowledged May 1, 1886 in Baltimore City; recorded the same day (John W. Shanklin, Clerk); no plat is copied in. What it settles: (1) Clemens sold Brune the fee of 21 Calvin Avenue lots and leased them back the same day, creating $1,062.50 a year of ground rent; the earlier reading of all 21 as south-side lots is corrected (16 south, 5 north). (2) The only turnpike lot in the lease is the 90-ft corner lot 26, north of the 10-ft alley 90 ft south of Calvin Avenue: the 3360 lot (just south of that alley, parts of plat Lots 3 and 4) and the 25-ft Henry lot (Lot 1 and part of Lot 2, the north part of 3334-3338) stayed in Clemens's fee, and he sold or leased them himself in 1886 and 1887. What it does not settle: the plat (County plats, apparently 1/14) and the Clemens-to-Brune deed (not on J.W.S. 153/50 to 55, read October 14; still to be found).

Entry 3663; dated and acknowledged June 20, 1887 before Wm. D. Wright, J.P., who also witnessed; recorded June 21, 1887 at 8:30 a.m. (John W. Shanklin, Clerk); delivered Jan. 21, 1889. Augustus D. Clemens Jr. and Mary Clemens his wife, of Baltimore County, grant Charlotte B. Fuller of Baltimore City, in fee, for $886.95, the lot on the west side of the York Turnpike Road 100 ft south of the south side of Calvin Avenue, at the south-west corner of the turnpike and a 10-ft alley: 17 ft south on the turnpike and 120 ft west, parallel with Calvin Avenue, to the east side of a second 10-ft alley, with the use of both alleys. It is 'the first describe[d] lot' of the Feb. 7, 1887 lease to William H. Oliver (J.W.S. 158/447); the fee came to Clemens 'by deed from Thomas [J., written G.?] Wilson et al, Trustees dated May 1st 1886', J.W.S. 153/52; the habendum carries the fee 'especially with the right to collect and receive the yearly rent of Fifty-one dollars ($51.00)'; special warranty. Only this lot: the second Oliver lot ($48, 16 ft at 117 ft south of Calvin Avenue) is not in the deed. What it settles: (1) the 1908 Kimball deed's 'See also' is read: Clemens sold the new $51 rent and the reversion of 3360 four months after creating it, for $886.95 (about 17 1/2 years' rent, roughly 5 3/4 percent), so Charlotte B. Fuller held the rent in her own name from June 1887. (2) Clemens's fee came from the Wilson trustees by J.W.S. 153/52, not J.W.S. 152/527. What it does not settle: where the $48 rent went, and how the $51 rent passed from Charlotte B. Fuller to Richard F. Kimball (her will, R.T.B. 59/91, is the likely path). Update Oct. 14, 2026 (later): the deed it cites for Clemens's title (J.W.S. 153/52) is read (785:mdlr-jws153-52-wilson-trustees-clemens-lots-18-28-1886); the trustee is Thomas J. Wilson.

Entry 70; dated July 16, 1890 and acknowledged that day at Cape May, New Jersey, before Joseph H. Hughes, notary; recorded July 18, 1890 at 11:55 a.m. (Jas. Bond, Clerk). Florence Fuller, unmarried, of Baltimore City, 'now temporarily residing in the State of New Jersey', grants and assigns Richard F. Kimball, for $5 and other considerations, 'All and every the right title and interest both at law and in equity in and to the estate which was devised and bequeathed to her by and under the said Last Will and Testament of her father the said Richard Fuller' (will J.H.B. 43/143, which let her dispose of her portion absolutely). No lot, rent or lease is named; Charlotte B. Fuller and her will are not mentioned; special warranty. What it settles: the 1890 deed in the 1908 Kimball recital is read: a blanket assignment of Florence's share of her father Richard Fuller's estate. It does not name the 3360 rent, and Charlotte B. Fuller bought that rent in her own name in 1887 (J.W.S. 162/110), so this deed alone does not carry it to Kimball unless Charlotte's rent fell into Richard Fuller's estate; the path is more likely Charlotte's will (R.T.B. 59/91), Florence's will (T.W.M. 77/51) or the 1891 partition (inference). Kimball's relationship to Florence is not stated.

summary: Release, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. S.S., folios 231 to 233 (MSA CE 66-93; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved, the mortgage clause checked). Dated and acknowledged Feb. 14, 1795 before Jas. Calhoun and Geo. Gouldsmith Presbury; recorded Aug. 8, 1795 (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). John Gorsuch, son of Thomas, signing by mark, releases James Maidwell, for five shillings and because Maidwell has paid him £76 3s 6d, the land Maidwell had deeded him on Feb. 26, 1787 (W.G. AA/193) as security, with a power to sell at auction if the debt was not paid by Feb. 24, 1788: a mortgage. The land is 'part of a Tract of Land Called Ensors Inspection', nine acres: from a bounded white oak, the second tree of the part Joseph Ensor sold Thomas Cole Speagle, N 36 1/2 E 35 perches to a stone marked M on the line of the part Ensor sold Job Garretson, N 76 1/2 E 25 perches 'to the main road', then with the road and Richard Dick's part S 10 E 30 perches and S 35 W 14 perches to Speagle's beginning, a black oak by the road side, and straight back; with two lots in Baltimore Town east of Jones Falls, Nos. 28 and 29. What it settles: (1) Maidwell's title to the 2958 ground is read in outline: he held nine acres of Ensor's Inspection on the main road by 1787 and cleared the mortgage in 1795. (2) The 1800 Maidwell-to-Biays deed (W.G. 67/62) starts at stone M and repeats the N 76 1/2 E 25-perch line to the main road and the first 14.6 perches of the S 10 E road line, so the 2 1/4 acres were the northern tip of these nine acres (computed: the 1800 piece about 2.15 acres, the whole about 8.2 against 9 stated; the closing line, Speagle's first line, about N 80 1/2 W 42.9 perches). What it does not settle: how Maidwell acquired the nine acres before 1787, and what became of the six or seven acres he kept. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (evening): the 1787 mortgage is read (714:mdlr-wgaa193-maidwell-gorsuch-mortgage-ensors-inspection-1787): the same nine acres and lots, £76 3s 6d due Feb. 24, 1788; it recites no source for Maidwell's title. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (County grantor index, Dick and Gorsuch): the County grantor index for Gorsuch finds no deed or mortgage by John Gorsuch of Thomas in 1778 to 1786 (CE 33-2 pp. 134-138, the whole Go run: only an estray notice, W.G. B/290; 714:index-ce33-2-p133-gorsuch-john-1778-1786). From 1787 to 1803 (CE 33-3 and 33-4) his only conveyances of Ensor's Inspection are A.A. 205 (1787, to James Edwards, index p. 151, recorded twelve folios after Maidwell's mortgage, A.A. 193; not read), the 1795 release to Maidwell (S.S. 231) and the 1803 deed of trust (76/243, 3 acres, which is Harkin's Rest, bought from Harkin in 1771, and not this lot). There is no Gorsuch deed to Biays, Walker, Maidwell or Dick in the index, and none between W.G. 53/197 (1798) and 73/72 (1802). So the 5 1/4 acres Gorsuch took from the Speagles in 1778 are not shown sold before the 1787 mortgage, and A.A. 205 is the best candidate for where they went (INFERRED: the index gives no acreage or road, and it could instead be another part of Ensor's Inspection, for example Richard Dick's part, which Edwards held by 1804). The lot that 'formerly belonged to John Gorsuch now the property of the said James Biays' in 1801 (rows 46180, 46685) therefore rests on a deed or contract not indexed under Gorsuch, or on A.A. 205 through Edwards. Next: W.G. A.A. 205 itself (MSA CE 66-76 p. 205; the scan on disk stops at p. 197), read against the 1778 courses (row 47038) and the Edwards deeds. summary: Surrender, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 72, folios 128 to 130 (MSA CE 66-122; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved). Dated and acknowledged Jan. 9, 1802 before James Carroll and Geo. Gouldsmith Presbury; recorded Jan. 15, 1802 (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). Jesse Brown, tailor of Baltimore, for five shillings, surrenders to Harry Dorsey Gough and Prudence Gough of Perry Hall both parcels of the Apr. 16, 1798 lease (cited as W.G. 54/156), made 'with the consent approbation and at the request of the said Job Merryman', because 'a mistake in one of the lines or courses of one of the said parcels of land hath been discovered', which the Goughs will rectify by a new lease (W.G. 72/124, recorded just before). It surrenders 'all and singular' of both parcels, buildings and improvements included. What it settles: the surrender behind the corrected 1802 lease is read; it names the mistake but not the line, so the N 30 W to N 50 W correction is seen only by comparing the 1795, 1798 and 1802 leases. It does not mention John Wheetley, to whom Brown had assigned an acre of the lease on Oct. 20, 1801 (W.G. 72/454, recorded Feb. 26, 1802): how his acre fared is still open.

Entry 903; dated, acknowledged (before Geo. McCaffray, J.P., Baltimore City) and recorded May 1, 1886 (John W. Shanklin, Clerk); mailed to Clemens July 17, 1886. Thomas J. Wilson and Henry R. Wilson, surviving trustees under the will of James Wilson of Baltimore dated Jan. 22, 1848 (Baltimore County wills D.M.P. 24/154; trustees David S. Wilson, since dead, Thomas J. Wilson, and Henry R. Wilson in place of Robert P. Brown, who declined), sell Augustus D. Clemens Jr., for $16,000, in fee, one tract: from the west side of the York Turnpike Road 100 ft north of its north-west corner with Wilson Street, 339 ft north along the turnpike to the land of A. S. Abell, 408 ft 6 in north-westerly along Abell's land to the east side of Barclay Street, 396 ft south along Barclay Street to a point 100 ft north of Wilson Street, and 400 ft east, parallel with Wilson Street, back to the turnpike, with half the bed of Barclay Street: 'Lots Nos. Eighteen ... and twenty eight as laid out on the plat filed in said cause in the Circuit Court of Baltimore City on June 20th 1871'. The decree of Oct. 7, 1869 in William C. Wilson et al. v. David S. Wilson et al. appointed three men (George W. L[uges?], Francis T. King and John J. Jackson) to divide and value the estate; the parties declined to select lots, so the trustees sold under the will's power and reported the sale to the court. No tract name. The initial is J in all seven places. What it settles: (1) Clemens's whole Waverly tract is read: Lots 18 to 28 of the 1871 Wilson estate plat, 339 ft on the turnpike from 100 ft north of Wilson Street (now Venable Avenue) to A. S. Abell's land, back to Barclay Street, about 3.4 acres. He laid out Calvin Avenue through it, sold and leased back 21 lots to Brune the same day, and sold the 25-ft Henry lot (the north part of 3334-3338, at its south end) and the 3360 lot himself. (2) The 100-ft strip north of Wilson Street that the deed leaves out is where Bolgiano's Lots 16 and 17 (1871, the 3326-3338 corner) lie, so 3326, 3334-3338 and 3360 all come from the one James Wilson estate division of 1869 to 1871 (the lot fit is inference from the shared plat and the 100 ft). (3) The Clemens-to-Brune deed is not on folios 50 to 55: Brune's lease (entry 905) follows this deed directly. What it does not settle: the 1871 plat itself (Liber J.R.B. 18 [?], folio 536, in the equity proceedings) and where the Clemens-to-Brune deed was recorded.

Entry 903; dated, acknowledged (before Geo. McCaffray, J.P., Baltimore City) and recorded May 1, 1886 (John W. Shanklin, Clerk); mailed to Clemens July 17, 1886. Thomas J. Wilson and Henry R. Wilson, surviving trustees under the will of James Wilson of Baltimore dated Jan. 22, 1848 (Baltimore County wills D.M.P. 24/154; trustees David S. Wilson, since dead, Thomas J. Wilson, and Henry R. Wilson in place of Robert P. Brown, who declined), sell Augustus D. Clemens Jr., for $16,000, in fee, one tract: from the west side of the York Turnpike Road 100 ft north of its north-west corner with Wilson Street, 339 ft north along the turnpike to the land of A. S. Abell, 408 ft 6 in north-westerly along Abell's land to the east side of Barclay Street, 396 ft south along Barclay Street to a point 100 ft north of Wilson Street, and 400 ft east, parallel with Wilson Street, back to the turnpike, with half the bed of Barclay Street: 'Lots Nos. Eighteen ... and twenty eight as laid out on the plat filed in said cause in the Circuit Court of Baltimore City on June 20th 1871'. The decree of Oct. 7, 1869 in William C. Wilson et al. v. David S. Wilson et al. appointed three men (George W. L[uges?], Francis T. King and John J. Jackson) to divide and value the estate; the parties declined to select lots, so the trustees sold under the will's power and reported the sale to the court. No tract name. The initial is J in all seven places. What it settles: (1) Clemens's whole Waverly tract is read: Lots 18 to 28 of the 1871 Wilson estate plat, 339 ft on the turnpike from 100 ft north of Wilson Street (now Venable Avenue) to A. S. Abell's land, back to Barclay Street, about 3.4 acres. He laid out Calvin Avenue through it, sold and leased back 21 lots to Brune the same day, and sold the 25-ft Henry lot (the north part of 3334-3338, at its south end) and the 3360 lot himself. (2) The 100-ft strip north of Wilson Street that the deed leaves out is where Bolgiano's Lots 16 and 17 (1871, the 3326-3338 corner) lie, so 3326, 3334-3338 and 3360 all come from the one James Wilson estate division of 1869 to 1871 (the lot fit is inference from the shared plat and the 100 ft). (3) The Clemens-to-Brune deed is not on folios 50 to 55: Brune's lease (entry 905) follows this deed directly. What it does not settle: the 1871 plat itself (Liber J.R.B. 18 [?], folio 536, in the equity proceedings) and where the Clemens-to-Brune deed was recorded.

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. AA, folios 193 to 196 (MSA CE 66-76; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved, the date checked). Dated and acknowledged Feb. 26, 1787 before Lyde Goodwin and Tho. Russell, justices, with Temperance Maidwell's release of dower; witnesses Robt. Gorsuch and Tho. Russell; recorded May 16, 1787 (W. Gibson, Clerk). To secure a promissory note of £76 3s 6d due Feb. 24, 1788, James Maidwell (signing 'Maydwell') conveys John Gorsuch, son of Thomas, in trust with a power to sell at public vendue on default, nine acres of 'Ensors Inspection' (the same courses the 1795 release recites: from Speagle's second tree, a white oak, N 36 1/2 E 35 perches to stone M on Job Garretson's line, N 76 1/2 E 25 perches to the main road, with the road and Richard Dick's part S 10 E 30 and S 35 W 14 perches to Speagle's black oak, and straight back) and lots 28 and 29 in Baltimore Town east of Jones Falls. No recital of how Maidwell held, no closing course, no buildings or orchard named. The next instrument (folios 196 to 197) is Loveless and Nathan Gorsuch's 1787 deed to Robert Gorsuch of 'Ensors Choice' and 'Loveless's Addition', the Gorsuch family's land devised by Thomas Gorsuch. What it settles: the 1787 side of the 1795 release is read: an ordinary mortgage, paid off late (released 1795). What it does not settle: Maidwell's own title, which has to come from the grantee index (Maidwell, 1765 to 1787) or Joseph Ensor's grantor entries. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (County grantor index, Dick and Gorsuch): the County grantor index for Gorsuch finds no deed or mortgage by John Gorsuch of Thomas in 1778 to 1786 (CE 33-2 pp. 134-138, the whole Go run: only an estray notice, W.G. B/290; 714:index-ce33-2-p133-gorsuch-john-1778-1786). From 1787 to 1803 (CE 33-3 and 33-4) his only conveyances of Ensor's Inspection are A.A. 205 (1787, to James Edwards, index p. 151, recorded twelve folios after Maidwell's mortgage, A.A. 193; not read), the 1795 release to Maidwell (S.S. 231) and the 1803 deed of trust (76/243, 3 acres, which is Harkin's Rest, bought from Harkin in 1771, and not this lot). There is no Gorsuch deed to Biays, Walker, Maidwell or Dick in the index, and none between W.G. 53/197 (1798) and 73/72 (1802). So the 5 1/4 acres Gorsuch took from the Speagles in 1778 are not shown sold before the 1787 mortgage, and A.A. 205 is the best candidate for where they went (INFERRED: the index gives no acreage or road, and it could instead be another part of Ensor's Inspection, for example Richard Dick's part, which Edwards held by 1804). The lot that 'formerly belonged to John Gorsuch now the property of the said James Biays' in 1801 (rows 46180, 46685) therefore rests on a deed or contract not indexed under Gorsuch, or on A.A. 205 through Edwards. Next: W.G. A.A. 205 itself (MSA CE 66-76 p. 205; the scan on disk stops at p. 197), read against the 1778 courses (row 47038) and the Edwards deeds. summary: Two deeds, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. 5912, folios 76 to 78 (MSA CE 168-5920; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved, the heirs' recital checked; folio 76, the first page of the heirs' deed, is not in the scan). Both dated Oct. 28, 1938 (the De Grattas acknowledged in Queens, New York, on Oct. 27) and recorded Apr. 19, 1939 at 11:15 and 11:16 a.m. (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk). (1) The five children and heirs at law of Martin J. Clarke (died about Apr. 6, 1933) and Jane E. Clarke (died about July 10, 1938), Harry M. Clarke, Evelyn E. Oehrl, Isabel Glaser, Katherine Hoffmaster and Ethel M. DeGratta, with their spouses, deed 2936 to Agnes L. Napfel in fee. Their title: Frank A. and Catherine Lyons's assignment of the leasehold to Martin J. and Jane E. Clarke, Oct. 11, 1919 (S.C.L. 3463/70), and Leopold A. Fischer's deed of the reversion, Apr. 12, 1927 (S.C.L. 4722/289), which merged the ground rent. (2) Napfel, unmarried, deeds it the same day to Harry M. Clarke and Evelyn E. Oehrl as joint tenants, for $1: the west-side lot 14 ft by 100 ft, 248 ft 9 1/2 in north of 29th Street, 'now known as No 2936 Greenmount Avenue (formerly York Road)'. Witness and notary Frank J. Pintner. What it settles: (1) 2936 was the Clarke family home from 1919; the rent was bought out in 1927, so the house was held in fee from then until the Hoffmasters created a new $75 rent in 1944. (2) Napfel was a straw to put the house in two of the five heirs; the 1943 sale to Earl and Katherine Hoffmaster was a sale to a third Clarke child and her husband. The 1943 deed recites this deed as dated Nov. 28, 1938; it is dated Oct. 28. (3) The 1919 assignors, Frank A. and Catherine Lyons, may be kin of Ann B. Lyons of 2934 (not shown). What it does not settle: S.C.L. 3463/70 and 4722/289, the original lease and its rent. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (night): both deeds the 1938 heirs' deed recites are read: Lyons to the Clarkes, 1919 (704:mdlr-scl3463-70-lyons-clarke-2936-leasehold-1919), and Fischer's reversion deed, 1927 (704:mdlr-scl4722-289-fischer-clarke-reversion-2936-keelty-lease-1927), which names the original lease, James Keelty's of Oct. 29, 1907 (R.O. 2380/251), at $60.

Lyons and Catherine Lyons his wife assign Martin J. and Jane E. Clarke, as tenants by the entireties, for $5 and other considerations (one $2 revenue stamp, so about $1,501 to $2,000), the lot on the west side of the York Turnpike Road 248 ft 9 1/2 in north of the north-west corner of 29th Street, 14 ft between partition walls, 100 ft to the west side of a 10-ft alley, 'known as No 2936 Greenmount Avenue', for the residue of the renewable term, subject to $60 a year, May 1 and Nov. 1; the Lyonses had it by assignment from Richard C. Gent (Jent in 1927) and Florence A. Anderson of Nov. 26, 1912 (S.C.L. 2713/51). The original lease is not recited here. On Oct. 14, 1919 the Clarkes mortgaged it to the Baltic Perpetual Building and Loan Association for $1,560 on twelve shares, 'part of the purchase price', released Apr. 13, 1927 (S.C.L. 4722/300). What it settles: the Clarkes' purchase is read: they bought the house as a $60 ground-rent leasehold in 1919. No tie to Ann B. Lyons of 2934 appears. What it does not settle: the 1912 assignment and the original lease (recited in 1927 as R.O. 2380/251). Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): S.C.L. 2713/51, this deed's cite for the 1912 assignment, holds other January 1912 deeds (704:negative-scl2713-51-not-gent-anderson-lyons-1912); and the Lyonses had leased the house next door, 2934, from Keelty in December 1907 (S.C.L. 2390/425). summary: Deed of reversion and mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 4722, folios 289 to 292 (MSA CE 168-4730; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved, the lease recital checked). Dated and acknowledged Apr. 12, 1927 before William J. Jackson, notary; recorded Apr. 13, 1927 at 2:41 p.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Leopold A. Fischer, widower, deeds Martin J. and Jane E. Clarke, in fee, for $5 and other considerations, the reversion and $60 ground rent of the 2936 lot, 'to the end and an intent that the lease hold and reversionary estates ... shall be come merged and the annual ground rent ... forever extinguished'. The deed recites the lease: James Keelty to Richard C. Jent et al., Oct. 29, 1907 (R.O. 2380/251), $60 a year, May and November; and the reversion: Keelty's deed to Fischer of Dec. 30, 1907 (S.C.L. 23[9?]4/467; probably 2394), 'it being the fourth lot in said deed'. The same day the Clarkes borrowed $1,170 from the Baltic Perpetual Building and Loan Association toward the price (and the 1919 loan was released). What it settles: (1) 2936's rent was created by James Keelty in October 1907, the year he bought the Wilson ground behind 2958 (R.O. 2302/43, January 1907) and leased 2958 (August 1907); 2936 lies on the same 14-ft lot grid, 154 ft south of the 2958 lease's beginning (248 ft 9 1/2 in plus eleven 14-ft lots is 402 ft 9 1/2 in). Keelty sold the 2936 rent within two months, as he did the 2958 rent, and Fischer's deed held at least four lots, very probably reversions on the same row (inference). (2) The Clarkes bought out the $60 rent in 1927, so 2936 was held in fee from then until the Hoffmasters created a new $75 rent in 1944. What it does not settle: Keelty's own title to the 2936 ground (the 1907 Wilson deed's 118 ft is the 2944 to 2958 row, north of it), R.O. 2380/251 and the Keelty-to-Fischer deed. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): the lease (704:mdlr-ro2380-251-keelty-gent-anderson-lease-2936-1907) and Keelty's deed to the Fischers (704:mdlr-scl2394-467-keelty-fischer-six-rents-2930-2940-1907, six rents, 2930 to 2940, liber 2394) are read; Keelty's title was the Brady estate trustees' deed of Mar. 28, 1907 (R.O. 2319/497), not the Wilson deed.

Wilson, trustees under James Wilson's will, convey the Baltimore and Yorktown Turnpike Road Company, in fee, the lot they had sold it on May 26, 1870 for $3,000 (a sale reported to and ratified by the Circuit Court of Baltimore City): part of 'Ensors Inspection', beginning at the west side of the York Turnpike and the north side of 'a road one perch and seven tenths of a perch wide running from the York road by the residence of Mrs Gilmor and others' (Gilmor's Lane, now Vineyard Lane), 1.7 perches north of the stone that begins David Mumma's 1844 lot (A.W.B. 354/374); 57 ft north on the turnpike, 100 ft west, 53 ft south to the lane and back along it; 'lot four (4) on the Plat of a portion of the Huntingdon Estate' filed with the trustees' report; 'Together with the improvements thereon and particularly the house thereon known as the First Toll gate House'. Title: Jacob Hoke and others to James Wilson, June 10, 1847 (A.W.B. 382/43). No reservation or reverter. What it settles: (1) the deed the 1912 turnpike-company deed to Jacob H. Aull recites ('July 5, 187[ ]', S.C.L. 2727/29) is found and read: July 5, 1871, E.H.A. 80/97, after the 1870 pulls at folio 92 of E.H.A. 70, 76 and 78 came up negative. (3) The toll-gate ground came to James Wilson from the Hoke group (the Biays heirs) in 1847, the same day they sold William T. Wilson the 2958 side (A.W.B. 382/30). summary: Two deeds, Baltimore County Circuit Court land records, Liber E.H.A. 80, folios 269 to 273 (MSA CE 62-80; found in the County Grantor Index, CE 256-287 p.144, and read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved; the seven courses of the old lot close within about 3 ft and give 56.46 square perches against the stated 56.49). Both dated and acknowledged Feb. 27, 1873 before Jno. T. Maddox, J.P.; recorded Apr. 14, 1873 (Edw. H. Ady, Clerk); delivered to Thos. J. Wilson Oct. 22, 1873. Under the seventeenth clause of James Wilson's will (Jan. 22, 1848), and with the exchange ratified in William C. Wilson et al. v. the trustees, the trustees give the Trustees of Huntingdon Chapel an 80 by 150 ft lot at the north-east corner of Waverly Avenue and Barclay Street, 'the same lot on which the new Huntingdon Chapel has recently been built', and the chapel gives back the church lot James Wilson had given it on Nov. 17, 1849 (A.W.B. 423/290): about three-eighths of an acre, beginning 'at a stone planted on the West side of the York Turnpike road at the Southeast corner of the Gate House lot', a 20-ft-3-in strip running back some 150 ft beside the Gate House lot to a block about 107 by 115 ft behind it. Thomas J. Wilson signed for both sides (as trustee and as the chapel's president). No denomination is named. What it settles: (1) from 1849 to 1873 Huntingdon Chapel's church lot lay directly south of the toll-gate house lot, with a 20-ft frontage on the turnpike: at or beside the later Gilmor's (Vineyard) Lane, the south line of 3026 (whether the strip became the lane is not shown). (2) The chapel moved to Waverly Avenue and Barclay Street by 1873. What it does not settle: the 1849 deed (pages loaded for Jeff), the chapel's denomination (its articles, Chattel Records A.W.B. 75/5) and where Waverly Avenue was. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): the 1849 gift is read (725:mdlr-awb423-290-james-wilson-huntingdon-chapel-church-lot-1849): $1, no conditions, from Magruder's 1844 Huntingdon deed (T.K. 341/328); the chapel stood on the lot by 1849.

summary: Lease, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 2380, folios 251 to 252 (MSA CE 168-2388; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved). Dated and acknowledged Oct. 29, 1907 before Matthew J. Dunn, notary; recorded Oct. 30, 1907 (Robt. Ogle, Clerk). James Keelty, unmarried, leases Richard C. Gent and Florence A. Anderson, wife of Hugh B. Anderson, as joint tenants, 'the property known as No 2936 York Road', 14 ft between partition walls (the houses stood already), 248 ft 9 1/2 in north of 29th Street, 100 ft to a 10-ft alley, for 99 years renewable forever on a $10 fine, at $60 a year from Nov. 1, 1907; distress, re-entry at 60 days and forfeiture at six months; no redemption clause and no building covenant. Keelty's title: 'a Deed from Richard H. Woolen et al Trustees ... dated March 2[5], 1907' (R.O. 2319/497; the Fischer deed dates it Mar. 28). Gent also took the 2938 lease (with Ada A. Biggs, R.O. 2380/219) and the 2940 lease (with Howard E. Gent, R.O. 2380/249) the same day. What it settles: the lease that created 2936's $60 rent is read; the row 2930 to 2942 was already built when Keelty leased it in October 1907, and its ground came to him from the Brady estate trustees, not from William T. Wilson. What it does not settle: R.O. 2319/497 and how Gent, Anderson and Biggs were related.

Dated Dec. 30, 1907; recorded Jan. 2, 1908 (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). James Keelty, unmarried, sells Leopold A. and Marie Fischer, as tenants by the entireties, for $6,127.66, the reversions and six $60 ground rents of six contiguous lots on the west side of the York Road, measured from the north-west corner of 29th Street ('formerly Tenth Street') as laid out by the Brady trustees (fixed by their 1889 lease to John Seiglein [?], J.B. 1233/108): 2930 (206 ft 4 1/2 in, 14 ft 5 in, the south end of a row of seven) and 2932 under George W. Turner's lease of Nov. 7, 1907 (R.O. 2382/388 [?]); 2934 under the lease to 'Frank A. Lyons and wife' of Dec. 6, 1907 (S.C.L. 2390/425); 2936 under the Gent and Anderson lease (R.O. 2380/251), 'the fourth lot'; 2938 (Gent and Ada A. Biggs, R.O. 2380/219) and 2940 (Gent and Howard E. Gent, R.O. 2380/249). All are part of the ground Richard H. Woollen et al., trustees, conveyed Keelty in fee on Mar. 28, 1907 (R.O. 2319/497). What it settles: (1) Keelty built or bought the row 2930 to 2942 on Brady estate ground (the Woollen trustees sold the Brady land under the 1899 decree), leased six of the houses in October to December 1907 and sold their rents to the Fischers within weeks, as he did with 2958's. (2) The Lyons family took 2934 in December 1907, five years before they bought 2936: the Ann B. Lyons of 2934 is very probably of that family (inference). (3) The 14-ft grid runs unbroken from 2930 to 2958 (290 ft 9 1/2 in to 402 ft 9 1/2 in is eight lots, 2942 to 2956), so the Brady and Wilson grounds probably meet between 2942 and 2944 (inference until R.O. 2319/497 is read). What it does not settle: R.O. 2319/497, the Turner and Lyons leases, and 2942. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (late): Keelty's title deed is read (704:mdlr-ro2319-497-brady-trustees-keelty-seven-houses-1907): the Brady trustees sold him the seven houses already standing, 95 ft north to his own Wilson ground, for $10,350 on Feb. 13, 1907; so the Brady and Wilson grounds meet at 2942/2944. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (night): the 2934 lease it recites is read (704:mdlr-scl2390-425-keelty-lyons-lease-2934-1907).

Dated, acknowledged (before T. Bayard Williams, notary) and recorded Mar. 28, 1907 (Robt. Ogle, Clerk). Richard H. Woollen, Howard P. Sadtler and S. Procter Brady, trustees under the twelfth clause of Samuel Brady's will (the Circuit Court of Baltimore City took the trust under a decree of May 23, 1899 in Martha A. Woollen et al. v. Nannie H. summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber A.W.B. 423, folios 290 to 291 (MSA CE 66-473; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved; the courses close within about 3 ft). Dated, acknowledged (before John I. Snyder and Henry F. Friese, justices) and recorded Nov. 17, 1849 (A.W. Bradford, Clerk). James Wilson of Baltimore gives the Trustees of Huntingdon Chapel, a corporation under the 1846 general incorporation act (articles in Chattel Records A.W.B. 75/5), for $1, in fee and without conditions, the lot 'on part of which is built the Chapel known as Huntingdon Chapel', about two miles from the city: 'Beginning ... at a Stone now planted on the West side of the York Turnpike Road at the South East Corner of the Gate house Lot', a 20-ft-3-in strip running back some 150 ft to a block about 107 by 115 ft, 56.49 square perches in all; part of the Huntingdon land Alexander Contee Magruder, trustee, sold Wilson on May 14, 1844 (T.K. 341/328). No trustees or denomination are named. Plotted against the 1847 Hoke triangle, the chapel's turnpike frontage sits in the mouth of Gilmor's Lane, the strip roughly following the lane, the block west of the triangle. What it settles: (1) the 'Gate house Lot' is named in a deed by 1849, at the turnpike just north of the chapel strip, which the 1871 deed makes Lot 4 of the Huntingdon plat. (2) Huntingdon Chapel stood on the York Turnpike at the toll gate from 1849 (or before) until the 1873 exchange moved it to Waverly Avenue and Barclay Street. (3) The lane by Mrs. Gilmor's was probably the chapel's approach from the turnpike (inference: the two deeds' surveys differ by a wedge up to about 16 ft). What it does not settle: the chapel's denomination and trustees (the articles, A.W.B. 75/5) and when it was built. summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber A.W.B. 423, folios 290 to 291 (MSA CE 66-473; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved; the courses close within about 3 ft). Dated, acknowledged (before John I. Snyder and Henry F. Friese, justices) and recorded Nov. 17, 1849 (A.W. Bradford, Clerk). James Wilson of Baltimore gives the Trustees of Huntingdon Chapel, a corporation under the 1846 general incorporation act (articles in Chattel Records A.W.B. 75/5), for $1, in fee and without conditions, the lot 'on part of which is built the Chapel known as Huntingdon Chapel', about two miles from the city: 'Beginning ... at a Stone now planted on the West side of the York Turnpike Road at the South East Corner of the Gate house Lot', a 20-ft-3-in strip running back some 150 ft to a block about 107 by 115 ft, 56.49 square perches in all; part of the Huntingdon land Alexander Contee Magruder, trustee, sold Wilson on May 14, 1844 (T.K. 341/328). No trustees or denomination are named. Plotted against the 1847 Hoke triangle, the chapel's turnpike frontage sits in the mouth of Gilmor's Lane, the strip roughly following the lane, the block west of the triangle. What it settles: (1) the 'Gate house Lot' is named in a deed by 1849, at the turnpike just north of the chapel strip, which the 1871 deed makes Lot 4 of the Huntingdon plat. (2) Huntingdon Chapel stood on the York Turnpike at the toll gate from 1849 (or before) until the 1873 exchange moved it to Waverly Avenue and Barclay Street. (3) The lane by Mrs. Gilmor's was probably the chapel's approach from the turnpike (inference: the two deeds' surveys differ by a wedge up to about 16 ft). What it does not settle: the chapel's denomination and trustees (the articles, A.W.B. 75/5) and when it was built. Update Oct. 14, 2026 (night): the chapel was probably the old stone barn of 1844 (726:msa-c2843-15-p84-old-stone-barn-huntingdon-chapel-1844-1849).
