summary: Lease and mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 2390, folios 425 to 428 (MSA CE 168-2398; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved, the description, names and the Cook recital checked). Lease dated and acknowledged Dec. 6, 1907 before Calvin G. Chesnut, notary; recorded Dec. 7, 1907 (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). James Keelty leases Frank A. Lyons and Catherine Lyons, his wife, for 99 years renewable forever (renewal fine $10), at $60 a year in half-yearly payments counted from Nov. 1, 1907, the lot on the west side of the York Turnpike beginning 234 ft 9 1/2 in north of the south-east corner of the house at the north-west corner of the turnpike and 29th Street, 14 ft front by 100 ft deep: today 2934 Greenmount Avenue (the 1966 deed's same 234 ft 9 1/2 in). The lease names no house number, no alley, no building covenant and no redemption right, and recites no title (Keelty held the ground from the Brady trustees, R.O. 2319/497). The same day the Lyonses mortgaged the leasehold to the Merchants and Manufacturers Permanent Building and Loan Association for a $520 advance on four shares (folios 426 to 428; delivery note dated about Apr. 22, 1912); that mortgage recites the lot as 'conveyed by Henry E. Cook to Frank A. Lyons Et. Al.' by a deed of even date, a name the lease does not mention. What it settles: (1) 2934 began as the Lyons family's house: Frank A. Lyons (the stonemason and contractor of the 1915 and 1928 directories) and Catherine Lyons took it from Keelty on Dec. 6, 1907, five weeks after the Gent and Anderson lease of 2936; the Lyonses' line ran to Ann B. Lyons, whose 1953 and 1966 deeds are already read. (2) It is the 2934 lease the 1907 Keelty-to-Fischer rent sale recites (S.C.L. 2394/467): that cite is S.C.L., not R.O. (3) The mortgage's Henry E. Cook recital is unexplained: either Cook sold them the house (Keelty leasing the ground) or the clerk copied a form; it is an open question, not a finding. What it does not settle: how the $60 rent was redeemed or merged before 1953, and how the leasehold passed from Frank A. and Catherine to Ann B. Lyons. Update Oct. 15, 2026: the 1907 City grantor index shows no deed from Henry E. Cook to the Lyonses (703:negative-ce167-131-p264-no-cook-to-lyons-deed-1907); Cook's Dec. 7 assignment to Ida A. Bozman is at S.C.L. 2390/404, the same book, so the mortgage's Cook recital is probably carried over from another form.

summary: Draft deed, in the Bouldin surveyors' Envelope 15 (MSA C2843-15, pages 15 and 16 of the public PDF; found in the full page-by-page sweep of Oct. 14, 2026 and checked on the page). An unsigned, undated draft 'made the __ day of __' 1821: James Carroll of Baltimore County to Philip G. Biays, for $2,000, the lot 'known and distinguished on a plat of Huntington by the number Seventy four', 3 acres 3 perches, beginning where the N 45 W line of 'Old Huntington' meets the Old York Road (the line run from a stone at the beginning of 'New Huntington' to two stones where a boundary stone, shown to James Baker by Joseph Merryman and John Gorsuch and 'planted under a Land Commission', once stood), N 40 1/4 E 45 perches, N 82 1/2 W 24.7 perches to the Old York Road and back along it. The facing sheet, in the same hand and headed 'pt of Huntington', is an 'And Also' parcel whose courses are, call for call, those of James Biays's Second Lot of Jan. 13, 1803 (7a 2r 33p, W.G. 74/334), to 'a Road left open by' Gough; the sheet ends there. The page is stamped '12th Ward, Envelope No. 1, Plat No. 23' by a later office. What it settles: (1) the 3a 3p parcel that the executed deed of July 7, 1823 (W.G. 169/672) conveys as its second lot, sold to Christopher Walker in 1809, was Lot No. 74 on a numbered plat of Huntington: the plat whose Nos. 95 to 98 Gough sold Henry Wilmans in 1794 (Q.Q. 164). (2) The Carrolls first drew the conveyance in 1821 at $2,000; the deed they executed in 1823 recites the price as long paid and takes $1. What it does not settle: why the Second Lot's courses were attached (James Biays held it in fee from 1803, so a confirmation is a guess), and where the numbered Huntington plat is.

summary: Plats and field notes, in the Bouldin surveyors' Envelope 15 (MSA C2843-15, pages 69, 75, 81 to 85 and 99 of the public PDF; pages 69, 75, 84 and 99 found in the full page-by-page sweep of Oct. 14, 2026, the plats checked on the page). (1) An unsigned sketch in Bouldin's hand, captioned 'John Gibsons Property' (page 69, with its pencil field note on page 75), draws the 1823 Carroll-to-Philip G. Biays ground at the York Road and Gough's road: the 'Gate House Lot', a strip 3 perches on the road and 6 3/4 perches deep at N 77 W, and, 5.3 perches N 82 W beyond its inner end, an 'Old Stone Barn' 2.6 by 1.6 perches (about 43 by 26 ft), its long side S 41 1/2 W. Bouldin's January 1844 plat of the same ground, docketed 'for John Gibson Esqr' (pages 81 to 82), hatches a 'Stone House' in that place. (2) Bouldin's Nov. 10, 1849 plat for James Wilson's gift to the chapel trustees (pages 83 to 85; the deed is A.W.B. 423/290) draws the 'Gate House Lot' along the chapel's entrance strip and a hatched 'Church' 43 ft 3 in by 27 ft 3 in, its long side on the S 42 W line, with the lot drawn around it at 40, 40, 40 and 32 ft. (3) Bouldin's field notes of June 10, 1846 (page 99) pass 'the N W Corner of the Stone Barn' 19.7 perches along the lane and note that 'The Lane is between Mumma's Stone and the gate House 1 7/10 p wide at the Turnpike road'. What it suggests: Huntingdon Chapel was the old stone barn, converted, or was built on its exact footing: the 1844 barn and the 1849 church are the same size within a foot, face the same way, and, plotted from the Gate House lot, fall within a few feet of each other (an inference from the drawings; no paper says the barn became the chapel). It also shows the gate house standing at the turnpike on the north side of the 1.7-perch lane by Mrs. Gilmor's, and a John Gibson (second on the St. John's, Huntingdon, vestry list in the same envelope, page 77) interested in the Carroll-to-Biays ground in January 1844, four months before Magruder, trustee, sold it to James Wilson (T.K. 341/328). What it does not settle: whether the barn ever served as St. John's 'temporary place of worship' of November 1843 (not shown), Gibson's interest, and the school-house lot's size and place.

summary: Certified copy of the 1757 Huntington resurvey certificate, with its plat, and an abstract booklet, in the Bouldin surveyors' Envelope 15 (MSA C2843-15, pages 92 to 102 and 119 to 129 of the public PDF; found in the full page-by-page sweep of Oct. 14, 2026, the patent endorsement and the Huntington courses checked on the page). The Western Shore Land Office's true copy of Mar. 6, 1810 (John Brewer, register; cost $5.75 with the plat) of the certificate of Nicholas Ruxton Gay, deputy surveyor: under a special warrant of renewment of Apr. 11, 1757, Huntington was resurveyed on Sept. 29, 1757 for John Carnan and Achsah his wife, taking in Huntington (granted to John Edwards for 135 acres; the copy's year reads 1748, apparently written over), Wilkinson's Folly (William Wilkinson, May 6, 1689, 89 acres), part of Edwards Lot (Moses Edwards, Oct. 13, 1704) and part of Edwards Enlargement (Moses Edwards, May 10, 1707), with 90 acres of vacant land: 475 acres in all, 'to be held of the mannor of Baltimore by the name of Huntington'. Huntington's own lines begin at its original beginning tree, 'also a bounded tree of the land called Merryman's lot', S 42 3/4 W 199 perches, SE 88, N 48 3/4 E 190, NE 60, NW 90 (155 acres); the whole runs on Ensor's Inspection, Darley Hall, Sheredine's Discovery, Merryman's Lot, Mount Royal and Jones Falls. Disallowed Aug. 1, 1758 for an unclear sixth course, amended and passed Mar. 3, 1760, approved by Governor Sharpe Feb. 10, 1761: 'Patent the 29th of September 1761 ... Recorded in Liber B C & G S No. 14 fol 295', rent 19 shillings sterling. A small booklet in the same envelope (pages 93 to 99) abstracts the same certificate with the patents of Ensor's Choice (1702), Ensor's Inspection (1734 or 1754 in that copy), Lovelace's Addition (1734), Gorsuch's Regulation (Nov. 9, 1759, bounding on 'Huntingdon as lately resurveyed for John and Achsah Carnan'), Grant's Addition (1722) and Gorsuch's Folly (1720), and Bouldin's notebook (pages 100 to 102) copies the resurvey's courses. What it settles: (1) the Huntington of every corridor deed is the Carnans' 475-acre resurvey of 1757, patented Sept. 29, 1761. The copy's 'Recorded in Liber B C & G S No. 14 fol 295' is where the certificate was recorded: the Land Office index cards give certificate B.C. & G.S. 14/295 and patent B.C. & G.S. 15/219, so 15/219 remains the patent to pull. The certificate itself was already read from the Archives (MSA S1190-2564, Edition 2 ch. 05); this is an 1810 copy of it, lodged with the Biays papers, and it agrees on the courses and the acreage. (2) It is the land Achsah Carnan settled in 1768 (B.Q. 503) on her daughters Prudence (Gough) and Elizabeth (Onion), a moiety each. (3) Huntington's first tree is also a Merryman's Lot tree: the two tracts met there, and the 1802 Wilson deeds name them together. What it does not settle: where the resurvey's lines fall on today's grid. The copy's 1748 for the original Huntington grant is a copyist's slip: the Archives' certificate reads 1688.

An unsigned, undated plat of James Biays's whole holding at the York Turnpike, each purchase washed yellow and lettered with its deed: on the south-east side of a 'Road 2 ps wide' (S 42 3/4 W 86 perches from the turnpike), the Ensor's Inspection pieces, John Gorsuch's lot ('Surveyed Septr 17th 1799'), Maidwell's (W.G. 67/62), Christopher Walker's (Mar. 9, 1801), the Spear heirs' 9 7/8 acres (May 30, 1801) and Edwards's (1804, with the 'J.B' and 'E' stones); on its north-west side, in Huntington, William Jackson's lot, 'James Biays Lot 7 A. 2 R. 33 P.', 'Philip G Biays Lot 3 A. 1 R. 12 P.' and Joseph Thornburgh's lot, up to 'Merrymans Road'; east of the turnpike, the Old York Road. Later additions at the turnpike (a lane between a lot marked 'D M', David Mumma's of 1844, and a small piece whose figures are those of the April 1847 survey) date its use to the 1840s; two small buildings stand on the 2-perch road. What it settles: (1) it is the one map of the Biays ground as a whole: the 1799 to 1804 Ensor's Inspection purchases and the 1803 Gough lots lie on the two sides of one road, the 2-perch road 'leading to intersect the York Turnpike Road' of the Walker deed, with the Huntington lots between it and Merryman's Road. (2) Philip G. Biays's 3a 1r 12p (the 1823 Carroll lot, the toll-gate wedge) is drawn between James Biays's Second Lot and Thornburgh's lot, fronting the turnpike, where the 1823 deed puts it. What it does not settle: its date and maker (Bouldin's additions are in pencil and ink over an older plat), and which of the drawn buildings is the stone barn of 1844.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 72, folios 226 to 230 (MSA CE 66-122; read by a helper agent on the scan Jeff saved, the grant and courses checked; the scan stops in the Virginia governor's certificate, so the recording entry on folio 231 is not read; the Jarman mortgage above it was recorded Jan. 26, 1802). Dated Oct. 24, 1801. Philip Norborne Nicholas, attorney at law of Henrico County, Virginia, and Mary his wife, 'the only surviving Child of John Spear late of Baltimore County ... Merchant deceased, who was the only surviving son of William Spear', sell James Biays, for $20, their 'undivided part share' (the fraction is not stated) of 9 7/8 acres of Ensor's Inspection: from the bounded red oak at the beginning of Huntington, S 47 E 29 1/2, N 50 E 5.6 to a white oak, N 33 3/4 E 38, N 70 E 0.7 perches to the south-west corner of the lot 'which formerly belonged to John Gorsuch now the property of the said James Biays', N 5 degrees 6 minutes W 27.1 perches along it to the stone at the end of the last line of Christopher Walker's parcel to Biays, N 52 1/2 W 7.1 perches along Walker's land to the south-east side of a road, and along the road to the beginning: the same courses, call for call, as the Spear daughters' deed of May 30, 1801 (W.G. 67/447). Special warranty only. Mary was examined privately before Spencer Roane, a judge of Virginia's Supreme Court, at Richmond, and Philip gave a power of attorney to James A. Buchanan and John Hollins of Baltimore to acknowledge and record it, with Governor James Monroe's certificate. What it settles: (1) the 9 7/8 acres came to Biays from both lines of William Spear's family: the four daughters in May 1801 ($790) and, in October, his son John's only child for a share ($20), so Biays's title to the Spear piece was complete. (2) 'N 5.6 W' in the May deed is 5 degrees 6 minutes. (3) By October 1801 Biays already held the Gorsuch lot (Harkin's Rest, deeded to his trustees in 1803, W.G. 76/243) and Walker's parcel (Mar. 9, 1801, W.G. 66/519), and the Spear piece closes on both. What it does not settle: the size of the share (one fifth if William Spear died intestate with four daughters and a son, an inference), William Spear's own title (probably Job Garretson's 1781 deed of 46 acres, abstracted in the Bouldin papers; not recited here), and the recording date.

Harry Dorsey Gough and Prudence lease John Neale of Baltimore, for 99 years renewable forever (renewal fine one year's rent), at 59 pounds 14 shillings current money a year, due Mar. 1, tenant paying all taxes, 9 a 3 r 32 p of 'Huntingdon resurveyed': beginning on the south-west side of 'a private road laid out by said Harry Dorsey Gough leading from the York Turnpike to the grounds of Hugh Thompson and others for the accomodation of said lots', N 50 W and N 60 W 8 perches each along it to Samuel Vincent's lot, S 38 W 48.6 perches along Vincent's, S 50 E 43.6 perches to 'the road leading to Rutters Mill', N 40 E 28 perches along that road, N 50 W 28.6 perches and back (an L-shaped lot; the courses close within about 1 percent). Neale may buy the fee at any time for 995 pounds, the rent capitalized at 6 percent (100 pounds an acre). No title is recited and no building is required. What it settles: (1) the 'Gough to Neale lease' of Bouldin's abstract is read: the '59.14' is pounds and shillings, 6 pounds an acre, a redeemable ground rent. (2) By 1805 Gough was leasing Huntington in lots along a private road he had laid out from the York Turnpike to Hugh Thompson's, with Samuel Vincent already holding the next lot: the same road the McFadon trust deed of 1822 calls the road 'from the Land of Hugh Thompson unto the York Turnpike Road at or near the Gate', the lane at the first toll gate (probable: Bouldin filed the lease with the toll-gate papers; the lease itself names no gate). (3) The road to Rutter's Mill ran at right angles to it (Cope's plat envelope is docketed 'York Rd and Rutters Mill Road'). What it does not settle: where the lot lies along the lane (no distance from the turnpike), the later steps (Neale to John Mycroft, Mycroft to Philip B. Sadtler, Nov. 1815, per Bouldin), and whether the fee was ever bought.

summary: Plat, in the Baltimore City Superior Court Survey Papers, envelope 'York Road No. 5' (MSA CE71-283, legacy C2843-283, pages 58 to 60 of the Archives' public PDF; item 1 of the envelope's index, 'A[u]lls Lot York Rd & Old York Rd'; found in the page-by-page sweep of Oct. 15, 2026, the courses checked on the page). An unsigned, undated pencil working plat of Jacob Aull's lot east of the Old York Road, at 30 feet to the inch: its seven courses are those of the 1848 Bowerman-to-Aull deed (A.W.B. 409/275: N 21 1/2 E 10.7, S 77 1/4 E 27.2, S 28 1/4 W 16.9, N 66 1/2 W 5.8, N 81 1/4 W 8.9, N 17 E 6.3, N 81 1/4 W 10.4 perches), with the Old York Road front re-measured at 10 9/20 perches (172 ft) and the long side converted to 448.8 ft; they close within 0.3 perch at 2 a 30 p, against the deed's 2 a 29 p. Inside the lot the surveyor drew a building at the corner on the Old York Road, strips measured in feet and a 'Street ... 40 feet', and beside it a sketch of a lot on the 'Old road' with a stable. What it suggests: the Aull lot was being laid off for building, with a new 40-ft street through it, at some date after 1848 (the docket's box number, 350, sits among the 1830s to 1880s papers of the same series). It is the first drawing of the Aull ground found. What it does not settle: the date, the surveyor, the client, and which present street (if any) the 40-ft street became; that is the handle for placing the 1848 lot on today's grid.

summary: Lot description, in the Baltimore City Superior Court Survey Papers, envelope 'York Road No. 4' (MSA CE71-282, legacy C2843-282, pages 11 and 12 of the Archives' public PDF; item 10 of the envelope's index; found in the page-by-page sweep of Oct. 15, 2026 and checked on the page). Docketed 'Jno. W. Beall Lot, Bo't of Dd Mumma, York Road, County, 2 and 3 mile s[tones]': a lot bought by John W. Beall from David Mumma, beginning at a stone marked 'DM' and 'LH' on the EAST side of the York Turnpike, a corner of the part of the tract conveyed to Ludwig Herring, north 17.7 perches (292 ft) along the turnpike, S 82 E 17.1 perches to the west side of the Old York Road, S 4 1/2 W 17.2 perches along it to the end of Herring's second line, and back along that line (about S 83 E, computed): 1 a 3 r 2 p, closing within about 1 percent. The tract is not named and the paper is undated. What it suggests: David Mumma, who bought the Biays heirs' lot at the lane in 1844 (A.W.B. 354/374), also held ground in the wedge between the turnpike and the Old York Road, and sold it in lots: Ludwig Herring's to the south and Beall's north of it, each running the full width between the roads (260 to 280 ft here). 'County' dates it before the 1888 annexation, and 'between the 2 and 3 mile stones' puts it north of the 2-mile stone, which the 3013 and 3015 deeds place on the east side in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot, about 190 ft north of 3013: so in the wedge between the two roads north of the 3000 block's fork (probable from the milestone; the lot is not placed exactly). What it does not settle: Mumma's title to the wedge (not the 1844 deed, which is west of the turnpike), the dates and libers of the Mumma-to-Herring and Mumma-to-Beall deeds, and which modern lots they are.

summary: Building-permit index card for 3011-3013 Greenmount Avenue (Block 4076A, Lots 1-2), owner Max Silen of 4351 Park Heights Avenue, 1945 to 1961. (2) The 1847 'two Story Brick House' on the Leitzinger wedge did not survive past 1954 (inference: it was probably the brick and frame store razed). What it does not settle: the savings and loan's full name. summary: Mortgage, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber T.K. No. 280, folios 186 to 188 (MSA CE 66-330; read 2026-10-16 from the scans Jeff saved). Dated and acknowledged June 16, 1838 (Culver's 1915 article prints 1836). Eleanor Merryman, widow, and Nelson Merryman and Sarah his wife, Charles Merryman and Mary Ann his wife, Lewis, Eleanora, Joseph, George and Oliver P. Merryman mortgage to Samuel Brady of Baltimore City, to secure $2,000 lent that day for two years with interest half-yearly, "All that farm called Clover Hill" in Baltimore County near the City, about 200 acres, "on which Joseph Merryman late of said County deceased formerly resided and of which he died seized", descended to the widow and the seven children as his heirs at law. Witnesses Thomas W. Bond and William W. Waite. What it settles: Oliver P. Merryman, grantor of the 3224 ground to Sinclair about 1884, is one of Joseph Merryman's heirs to Clover Hill. What it does not settle: the deed gives no tract name and no bounds, so it cannot show whether Merryman land reached the York Road.

summary: Folio 406 of an 1884 deed, Baltimore County land records, Liber W.M.I. No. 141 (MSA CE 62-141; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved). Not the first page: the parties, date and consideration are on earlier folios (403 to 405 opened, not yet read). Wilson, Thomas J. Wilson and Henry R. Wilson, trustees (three, not two), lease to James E. Sinclair for 99 years renewable forever, at $72 a year payable April 16 and October 16, a lot "adjacent to the village of Waverly": beginning on the west side of the York Turnpike 150 ft south of a line along the north wall of a stone house on a lot lately leased by the trustees to J. H. Hallman [?], and 475 ft south of the south side of Wilson Street, at the southeast corner of "lot number Seven as conveyed by the said parties ... to P. P. Pendleton"; west 200 ft along Pendleton's south line to the centre of a 20-ft alley kept open for all the trustees' lots; south 22 1/2 ft along the alley to the northeast side of Merryman's lane; southeast along the lane 30 ft more or less to where "the old division fence between Brown's [?] lot and said Wilsons land formerly stood"; southeast 175 ft along that line to the turnpike; north 44 1/2 ft to the beginning. Sinclair could redeem the rent for $800 within the year (then at 6 percent, $1,200), or pay $300 by Feb. 1, 1873 for a reduced rent; failing that he must build a house of at least $1,250 within six months. What it settles: the 3224 lot was Wilson-estate ground let by the trustees, next to Pendleton's Lot No. 7 of a numbered trustees' division, and its south line was the old fence between the Wilson land and Brown's [?] lot. No tract name, no plat cited. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (batch 3): the Pendleton deed read (E.H.A. 72/153, 768:mdlr-eha72-153-wilson-trustees-pendleton-lots-7-8-1871). 'Lot number Seven as conveyed ... to P. P. Pendleton' is one of Lots 7 and 8 on the Wilson sales plat filed in Wilson against Wilson and others (Circuit Court of Baltimore City), 50 ft by 200 ft each, together 375 to 475 ft south of Wilson Street; this lease's beginning at 475 ft south of Wilson Street makes Lot 7 the southern lot [inference]. The trustees conveyed Pendleton's lots in fee under James Wilson's 1848 will (N.H. 26/354), which fits their holding the fee of this lot too and selling Sinclair the reversion for $800 in 1873 (J.B. 84/387).

Dated June 11, 1884. James E. Sinclair and Sarah C. Sinclair his wife, for $5,180.67, grant Alice P. Harris, wife of W. Hall Harris, in fee simple, three lots on the westernmost side of the York turnpike road north of Merryman's Lane, each about 100 ft deep to an alley three feet wide communicating with Merryman's lane: the first beginning 164 ft 8 in north of the corner formed by the northeasternmost side of Merryman's Lane and the westernmost side of the turnpike; the others along the turnpike by division walls between houses; the third beginning 36 ft 1/2 in north of that corner and running west 42 ft to the lane and northwest 76 ft 7 in along it, the lot just north of the apex. The apex triangle (36 ft 1/2 in on the road, 42 ft back to the lane) is not conveyed, so Sinclair kept it; his 1887 deed of a "lot on York turnpike, corner of Merryman's lane" to Robert Riddell Brown is probably the apex (inference). Recorded the same day as the Merryman release to Sinclair (folio 404), which put the fee of the apex in Sinclair first. No tract name on folios 405 to 406. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (R.O. 1661, R.O. 1715 and S.C.L. 2610/548 read): the third lot of this deed, from 36 ft 1/2 in to 96 ft 1/2 in north of the lane, was leased back to Sinclair at $150 a year (W.M.I. 141/407) and its fee stayed with the Harrises until Jan. 18, 1898, when they sold it to Alice Gerry Stewart for $2,500 (752:mdlr-ro1715-35-harris-alice-gerry-stewart-third-lot-1898). The apex, kept by Sinclair, went by his 1887 sale to Brown and the later deeds read on this property.

summary: Deed of sale, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber B No. Q, folios 740 to 741 (MSA CE 66-36; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved). Found in the Baltimore County Court Grantor Index 1655-1769 (MSA CE 33-1, p.107, 'En cont'd', Joseph Ensor's sales), pulled Oct. 16, 2026. The index dates it 1767; the deed is dated July 7, 1768. Joseph Ensor of Baltimore County, for 18 pounds current money, sells James Madewell (written also Madowell; the James Maidwell of the 1787 mortgage), of the same county, wheelwright, 'All that part of a Tract or Parcel of Land called Ensor's Inspection': beginning at a bounded white oak marked with three notches, being the second bounded tree of the part of Ensor's Inspection heretofore sold to Thomas Cole Speagle; N 36 1/2 E 35 perches to a stone marked M standing in the given line of the part sold by Ensor to Job Garrison; N 76 1/2 E 25 perches to the main Road; then bounding on and with the main Road and the part of Ensor's Inspection sold to Richard Dick, S 10 E 30 perches and S 35 W 14 perches to the beginning tree of Thomas Cole's part, a black oak standing by the road side marked with six notches; then a straight line to the beginning; nine acres more or less. General warranty. Witnesses Mark Alexander and Wm. Aisquith; receipt of 18 pounds the same day; alienation fine of 4 1/2 pence sterling received by Dan. Bowly for Lord Baltimore by order of Daniel of St. Thomas Jenifer; acknowledged July 7, 1768 before Wm. Aisquith and Benjamin Rogers, justices, with Mary Ensor's release of dower; recorded Jan. 2, 1769, examined by B. Bordley, Clerk. What it settles: the source of Maidwell's nine acres. The courses are those of his 1787 mortgage (W.G. AA/193) and 1795 release (W.G. S.S. 231); computed, the unstated closing line runs N 80 1/2 W 42.9 perches, as the chapter had computed from the mortgage, and the figure closes on about 8.2 acres. With the 1800 Maidwell deed to Biays (W.G. 67/62), the 2958 ground's chain now reaches Joseph Ensor, for whom Ensor's Inspection was surveyed in 1754 (S1190-1698) (the Biays-to-Wilson-to-Keelty link stays marked probable). The lot lies on the main road (the York Road) between Speagle's part, Garretson's line and Richard Dick's part. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (County grantor index, Dick and Gorsuch): the County grantor index runs for Di (CE 33-1 pp. 87-88 for 1655-1769, CE 33-2 p. 84 for 1770-86, CE 33-3 pp. 97-98 for 1787-97, CE 33-4 p. 99 for 1799-1803, the first Di page of that volume, p. 98, not held) show no Richard Dick as grantor in any form, and no Dick deed of Ensor's Inspection or of any land on the York road; the Dicks indexed (Thomas, James, Christian) are other men on other ground. No deed from Dick to Edwards is indexed before 1804, so how Edwards came by Dick's part is open: a will or descent, a deed entered under another first-named grantor or a variant spelling, an unrecorded deed, or a Dick deed of 1804 or later (CE 33-5 not held). Ensor's own deed to Dick was not among the Ensor lines found in CE 33-1 pp. 105-107 either. Next: the Grantee Index (MSA CE 32) under Dick, 1655-1769, for Ensor's deed to Richard Dick; and the Maydwell-to-Edwards deeds, W.G. 66/123 (1801) and 82/206 (1804), whose liber and folio are already known (row 46122). (714:index-ce33-1-p87-dick-richard-1765-1769 and its three siblings.)

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber B No. P, folios 470 to 473 (MSA CE 66-35; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, passages zoom-checked). Found in the Baltimore County Court Grantor Index 1655-1769 (MSA CE 33-1, p.107, 'En cont'd', Joseph Ensor's sales), pulled Oct. 16, 2026. The index dates it 1766; the deed is dated Jan. 16, 1767 (the clerk wrote 'seven Hundred Hundred and sixty seven'). Joseph Ensor of Baltimore County, for 10 pounds current money, conveys Thomas Cole Speigle (also Speagle), Rachel Cole Speagle and William Carter Junior, planters (the two added names interlined before signing), part of 'Ensors Inspection lying on the West Side of the main Road that leads from Baltimore Town to George Hailes': beginning at a bounded black oak of Mrs. Achsah Carnan's, with her land S 52 E 22 perches to the main Road; up the road N 14 E 29 1/2 perches to a black oak marked with six notches; on the road N 41 E 6 perches to a red oak marked with six notches; N 81 1/2 W 39 perches to a forked white oak marked with six notches; S 50 W 4 perches to Achsah Carnan's line, and with it to the beginning; 5 1/4 acres (the alienation-fine note says 5 1/2). No recital of Ensor's title. Witnesses Job Gar[r]son and Willm. Aisquith; acknowledged Jan. 16, 1767 before Aisquith and Benjamin Rogers, with Mary Ensor's release of dower; alienation fine received March 6, 1767 by John Boyd by order of Edward Lloyd; recorded March 6, 1767 (Bordley, Clerk). What it settles: Ensor's Inspection here lies on the WEST side of the main road from Baltimore Town (the York Road) and is bounded on its south and west by Mrs. Achsah Carnan's land, which is Huntington (patented 1761 to John and Achsah Carnan). Maidwell's 1768 nine acres begin at a Speagle tree, so the 2958 ground lies in this west-side strip against Huntington. The trees named in the two deeds do not match exactly (Maidwell's deed calls a three-notch white oak and a six-notch black oak 'by the road side'; this deed marks all three trees with six notches), so how the two lots join is not settled.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber B No. K, folios 84 to 86 (MSA CE 66-30; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 81 to 85; folio 86, with the justices, the alienation fine and the recording, was not saved). Found in the Baltimore County Court Grantor Index 1655-1769 (MSA CE 33-1, p.107, 'En cont'd', Joseph Ensor's sales), pulled Oct. 16, 2026. The index cites folio 81; the deed opens on 84 (81 to 84 hold the end of Thomas Harrison's lease to John Sligh, recorded May 5, 1762). Dated May 5, 1762. Joseph Ensor of Baltimore County, for 66 pounds current money of Maryland, conveys Job Garison (Garretson in the clerk's margin and the index) 'all that Part of a Tract of Land Called and known by the Name of Ensors Inspection', 'Beginning for the same at a Bounded Red Oak Standing in an Old Field being a Bounded Tree of a Tract of Land Called Huntington', thence North East 276 perches, S 27 W 140 perches, S 7 W 37 perches, then a direct line to the beginning; fifty-five acres (the index and margin say 50; plotted, the calls enclose about 51 acres and the closing line runs about S 75 W 131 1/2 perches). Special warranty; receipt of 66 pounds; witnesses Walt. Tolley and John Hall. No recital of Ensor's title. What it settles: (1) the root of William Spear's land. The Bouldin abstract of Job Garretson's 1781 deed to Spear (46 acres, MSA C2843-15 p.68) begins at the same 'bounded oak in an old field, a bounded tree of Huntingdon' and repeats this deed's S 27 W and S 7 W courses, so Spear bought the south-west part of these 55 acres from Garretson, who had it from Joseph Ensor in 1762. Through Spear the ground runs to his heirs' 1801 sale to Biays (W.G. 67/447, beside 2958) and to John Foster about 1786 and on to Christopher Walker (1800) and Biays (1809), the 3010 corner. (2) The 276-perch north-east line has the length of the long north-east line of the 1754 Ensor's Inspection certificate (S1190-1698, surveyed for Joseph Ensor), so Garretson's land very probably runs along that line from a Huntington boundary tree (inference: the certificate's line starts 27 perches along Darley Hall's north line, and the deed names no Darley Hall). Maidwell's 1768 lot calls 'the given line' of this part. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (later): folio 86 read (MSA CE 66-30 p.00086, saved by Jeff). It completes the acknowledgment before Walt. Tolley and John Hall (of Swan Town [?]), justices; the alienation fine of two shillings sterling was received May 5, 1762 by B. Bordley by order of Lord Baltimore's agent Edward Lloyd; recorded May 5, 1762, B. Bordley, Clerk. Two shillings is the fine on 50 acres at the usual four shillings per hundred (the 1768 Maidwell fine, 4 1/2 pence, fits nine acres the same way), so the fine supports the index's 50 acres against the body's 'fifty five'.

C, folios 18 to 20 (MSA CE 66-20; read 2026-10-16 from the scans Jeff saved, filed in Deeds and Title Chain/_Historic plats and maps). Dated Aug. 28, 1742. Charles Merryman and Millicent his wife, and Richard Miller Cole and Sabina his wife, convey John Boring Junior (with John Boring Senior and Sarah for their lives), in exchange for 100 acres of 'Borings Gift', 'Hales Folley' on the north side of Jones Falls: beginning at a bounded white oak on the north side of the road from Hale's plantation to the common wading place of the Falls, N 72 E 72 perches, S 50 E 156 perches, S 20 W 114 perches, then to the beginning; 100 acres. What it settles: computed, the figure closes on 102.2 acres and its unstated closing line runs N 38.8 W, within half a degree of the 1757 Huntington certificate's 'given line of Hailes Folly ... N 39 15 W' (MSA S1190-2564). So the smudged Huntington course 25, 'the second line of Hailes Folly', is S 50 E (59 perches), and Huntington computes to 468.5 acres against the certificate's 475 (Edition 3 of the title paper plots it so). With the 1818 Carroll allotment on the certificate, drawn along the York Turnpike and beginning 18 perches from the beginning of Hales Folly, that corner of the Huntington outline stood near the turnpike. Culver (MHM 10, 1915) cites the deed as TB-C f.18.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber A.L. No. L, folios 307 to 311 (MSA CE 66-47; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved). Found in the Baltimore County Court Grantor Index 1770-1786 (MSA CE 33-2, p.103: 'Ensor, Joseph to Griffith and Gist, Hailes Folley 100 Acres Land', A.L. L 307). Dated May 24, 1774. Joseph Ensor, now of Cecil County, for 500 pounds current money of Pennsylvania, conveys Benjamin Griffith and Mordecai Gist of Baltimore County, as tenants in common, 'all that undivided Moiety or half part of a Tract of Land ... called or known by the Name of Hales Folly containing and laid out for one hundred Acres ... originally Surveyed for a Certain Nicholas Hale long Since Deceased', with houses and improvements. No courses and no recital of how Ensor held it. The warranty excepts any part found 'to lie within the Bounds of a Tract of Land called Salisbury Plains' (Salisbury Plains is, with Hailes Folly, a named bound of the 1757 Huntington resurvey). Witnesses George McCall and Owen Allen; acknowledged May 24, 1774 before Isaac Van Bibber and Wm. Spear, justices of Baltimore County; Mary Ensor released dower in 'the within mentioned fifty Acres' in Cecil County on Sept. 30, 1774, before John Veazey Jr. and Stephen Hyland, certified Oct. 3, 1774; no recording clause on these folios. What it settles: by 1774 the Ensor family that surveyed Ensor's Inspection (1754) held at least half of Hailes Folly, the tract whose 1742 courses fix Huntington's course 25; so Ensor's Inspection, Hailes Folly and Huntington were neighbouring holdings near the York Road. summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. C, folios 19 to 22 (MSA CE 66-53; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved). Found in the Grantor Index 1770-1786 (MSA CE 33-2, p.338). Dated Sept. 13, 1778. Thomas Cole Speigle, Rachel Cole Speigle and William Carter Junior, planters, for 75 pounds current money, convey John Gorsuch, son of Thomas, part of 'Ensors Inspection lying on the west side of the main Road that leads from Baltimore Town to George Hailes', by the same courses as Joseph Ensor's 1767 deed to them (B P/470): from a bounded black oak of Mrs. Achsah Carnan's S 52 E 22 perches to the main Road, N 14 E 29 1/2 and N 41 E 6 perches bounding on the road, N 81 1/2 W 39 perches, S 50 W 4 perches to Carnan's line and with it to the beginning; 5 1/4 acres. No recital of title and no buildings named. Witnesses Richd. Lemmon and Benja. Griffith [?]; acknowledged Sept. 18, 1778 before Geo. Lindenberger and Jas. Calhoun, Rachel (wife of Thomas Cole Speigle) and Elinor (wife of William Carter Junior) releasing dower; recorded Oct. 22, 1778 (William Gibson, Clerk). What it settles: the Speagle 5 1/4 acres on the west side of the York Road, next to Huntington, passed in 1778 to John Gorsuch, son of Thomas, the same man who in 1787 took James Maidwell's mortgage of the adjoining nine acres (W.G. AA/193). So by 1787 Gorsuch held the lot south of Maidwell's and lent on Maidwell's. Where the Gorsuch 5 1/4 acres went next is not read. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (County grantor index, Dick and Gorsuch): the County grantor index for Gorsuch finds no deed or mortgage by John Gorsuch of Thomas in 1778 to 1786 (CE 33-2 pp. 134-138, the whole Go run: only an estray notice, W.G. B/290; 714:index-ce33-2-p133-gorsuch-john-1778-1786). From 1787 to 1803 (CE 33-3 and 33-4) his only conveyances of Ensor's Inspection are A.A. 205 (1787, to James Edwards, index p. 151, recorded twelve folios after Maidwell's mortgage, A.A. 193; not read), the 1795 release to Maidwell (S.S. 231) and the 1803 deed of trust (76/243, 3 acres, which is Harkin's Rest, bought from Harkin in 1771, and not this lot). There is no Gorsuch deed to Biays, Walker, Maidwell or Dick in the index, and none between W.G. 53/197 (1798) and 73/72 (1802). So the 5 1/4 acres Gorsuch took from the Speagles in 1778 are not shown sold before the 1787 mortgage, and A.A. 205 is the best candidate for where they went (INFERRED: the index gives no acreage or road, and it could instead be another part of Ensor's Inspection, for example Richard Dick's part, which Edwards held by 1804). The lot that 'formerly belonged to John Gorsuch now the property of the said James Biays' in 1801 (rows 46180, 46685) therefore rests on a deed or contract not indexed under Gorsuch, or on A.A. 205 through Edwards. Next: W.G. A.A. 205 itself (MSA CE 66-76 p. 205; the scan on disk stops at p. 197), read against the 1778 courses (row 47038) and the Edwards deeds. (714:index-ce33-3-p151-gorsuch-john-1787-1797 and -ce33-4-p163-gorsuch-john-1798-1803.) Update Oct. 17, 2026 (A.A. 205 read): the lot went to James Edwards on May 16, 1787 for 50 pounds, on word-for-word the same courses and acreage as this deed (W.G. A.A. 205 to 206, row 714:mdlr-waa205-gorsuch-edwards-speagle-5-quarter-acres-1787). Gorsuch held it nine years, 1778 to 1787.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. Z, folios 386 to 388 (MSA CE 66-75; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 386 to 390). Found in the Grantor Index 1770-1786 (MSA CE 33-2, p.339: 'Spear William, John Foster, pt of Ensors Inspection 29 a', folio 386 under a ditto of W.G. Z; W.G. Y/386 was pulled first and is not it). Dated Oct. 4, 1786. William Spear of Baltimore County, gentleman, for 400 pounds, conveys John Foster of the same county 'all that part of a Tract of Land Called and known by the Name of Ensors Inspection': 'begining for the same at a Stone standing North forty two degrees East Sixty two and a half perches from a bounded Red Oak standing in an old field being a Bounded tree of Huntington', thence N 42 E 117 perches to a stone in a line of 'Grants Addition'; with that land S 59 E 41 perches to a stone; S 27 W 13 perches until it intersects 'Loveless Addition'; with that land N 58 W 3 perches to the end of its line, S 52 W 38 perches, S 58 E 20 perches, S 7 W 7 perches until it intersects 'Daly [Darley] Hall'; with that land N 66 W 36 perches to a bounded tree of it; S 15 W 53 perches to a stone; S 76 1/2 W 16 perches to a stone; N 8 W 27 1/2 perches to a stone; S 75 1/2 W 18 1/2 perches to a stone; then a straight line to the beginning; twenty-nine acres more or less. Special warranty. Witnesses William Richardson and Christopher Walker; receipt of 400 pounds the same day, witness Lyde Goodwin; acknowledged Oct. 4, 1786 before Lyde Goodwin and Thos. Bailey, justices; recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). No recital of Spear's title. What it settles: (1) the 'about 1786' Spear deed that the 1809 Walker-to-Biays deed recites for Foster's 29 acres, the 3010 corner ground, is read, and its beginning, 62 1/2 perches N 42 E of the Huntington red oak, is the one the later deeds give. (2) It is the north-east part of Spear's 46 acres of 1781 (Bouldin abstract: from the same old-field oak N 42 E 178 perches to Grant's Addition and S 59 E 41 perches, the same second line), and the Huntington oak is the beginning tree of Joseph Ensor's 1762 deed to Job Garretson (B K/84), so the 3010 corner now runs, deed by deed, from Ensor (1762) to Garretson, Spear (1781, abstract), Foster (1786), Walker (1800) and Biays (1809). Spear kept the south-west 62 1/2 perches of the line, the part his heirs sold Biays in 1801 beside 2958 (W.G. 67/447; inference from the courses). (3) Christopher Walker, Foster's buyer of 1800 and the tavern keeper of 'Walker's Tavern', witnessed this deed. The rest of folio 388 to 390 holds James Morgan's 1786 assignment to Patrick and Susannah Kelly of part of lot 206 in the South East Addition of Baltimore Town; the top of 386 is the end of John Hoss to Henry Beckley (recorded Oct. 4, 1786).

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5005, folios 341 to 343 (MSA CE 168-5013; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 341 to 345). Found in the City Grantor Index 1929, Jan.-June, P-Z (MSA CE 167-232, p.294: 'May 22, Sinclair James M, Ena M, to Waverly Bldg Asso Balto Co, Mtge, E S York Tp Rd, 5005/341'); the '5005/541' cited before was a misreading (folios 541 to 545 were pulled and are other deeds). Dated May 21, 1929, recorded May 22, 1929 (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). James M. Sinclair and Ena M. Sinclair his wife, of Baltimore City, members of the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County, mortgage it the lot beginning on the east side of the York Turnpike Road 204 ft 7 in south of the two-mile stone in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot, also 281 ft 2 in south of the north side of 'a four foot alleyway called Bateman's Alley', 58 ft 4 in on the turnpike to the south-west corner of the whole ground, N 89 E 8 ft 6 in on its second line to the north-west side of the Old York Road, N 31 1/2 E 66 ft along that road, and west 42 ft 4 in to the beginning, 'known as No 3011 Greenmount Ave', being the firstly described lot of J. Holiday Riepe's deed to them in fee simple of March 1, 1927 (S.C.L. 4707/12); for an advance of $2,860 on 22 shares, dues 25 cents and interest 15 cents a share weekly; assent to a decree of sale. Margin: 'For release of mtge. Date 6/24/54 Liber 9513 fol. 53' (the association's 1954 release, read earlier). The release on folio 341 just above it, the same day, frees the Sinclairs from two earlier Waverly mortgages of March 29, 1923 (S.C.L. 3988/541) and June 11, 1926 (S.C.L. 4588/253), on a lot it does not describe: the source of the stray '541'. Lennox B. Clemens is the association's attorney for that release and witnesses the mortgage. What it settles: the 1929 mortgage the 1954 release names is read; 3011 was fee simple in the Sinclairs in 1929, with the two-mile stone and Bateman's Alley as its calls.

summary: Deed of a leasehold, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 2292, folios 510 to 511, with a mortgage at 511 to 513 (MSA CE 168-2300; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 510 to 514). Found in the City Grantee Index 1906, P-Z (MSA CE 166-124, p.222); R.O. 2292/410, pulled earlier, was a misreading of 510. Dated Nov. 30, 1906, acknowledged that day before Howard D. Adams, notary; recorded Dec. 3, 1906 at 2 P.M. (Robt. Ogle, Clerk). Augustus D. Clemens Junior, of Baltimore County, for $1,000, grants James M. Sinclair, of Baltimore City, the lot beginning on the east side of the York Turnpike road 204 ft 7 in south of the two-mile stone in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot, also 281 ft 2 in south of the north side of 'a four foot alleyway called Bateman's alley', 58 ft 4 in south along the turnpike to the south-west corner of the whole ground, N 89 E 8 ft 6 in to the north-west side of the Old York road, N 31 1/2 E 66 ft along it, and west 42 ft 4 in to the beginning (3011 Greenmount); 'Being the second described lot of ground in a deed from Jacob H Aull to Augustus D Clemens Junior dated the fourth day of May one thousand eight hundred and ninety eight ... Liber R O No 1739 folio 295'; for the residue of the term, renewable forever, subject to the annual rent of $75, May 1 and November 1. Special warranty. The same day Sinclair mortgaged the leasehold to the York Road Building Association of Baltimore City for an advance of $910 on seven shares, 'part purchase money', dues 25 cents and interest 15 cents a share weekly, Harry E. Parkhurst attorney to sell. What it settles: how Aull's 1898 leasehold reached Sinclair. Clemens leased the lot to Jacob H. Aull at $75 on April 18, 1898 (R.O. 1730/92) and sold the rent to Lulie H. Wallace the same day (R.O. 1730/91); Aull deeded the leasehold back to Clemens on May 4, 1898 (R.O. 1739/295, not yet read), and Clemens sold it to Sinclair in 1906; Sinclair bought the rent from Wallace in 1921 (S.C.L. 3692/300), merging it. The lease-and-sell-the-rent pattern Clemens used on 3017 and the Gilmor Lane lot (chapter 07) is the same here.

Dated Feb. 3, 1781. Job Garretson of Baltimore County, gentleman, for 350 pounds ('and fifty' interlined; receipt the same day), conveys William Spear of the same county, gentleman, 'all that part of a tract of Land called and known by the Name of Ensors Inspection', 'Begining at a bounded Red oak Standing in an old field being a bounded tree of Huntington', N 42 E 178 perches until it intersects Grants Addition, with it S 59 E 41 perches until it intersects Ensors Choice, with it S 27 W 49 perches, S 7 [W, cut at the gutter] 10 perches until it intersects Darley Hall, with it N 66 W 38 perches, S 15 W 53 perches, S 76 1/2 W 33 perches, S 54 W 62 perches, then a straight line to the first tree; forty-six acres. No recital of title. Witnesses John Spear and David Sterrett; acknowledged March 30, 1781 before Geo. Goldsmith Presbury and Geo. Lindenberger, with Mary Garretson's release of dower; recorded May 10, 1781 (W. Gibson, Clerk). What it settles: the deed behind Bouldin's 1781 abstract is read and agrees with it course for course. With Joseph Ensor's 1762 deed to Garretson (B K/84, the same red oak), Spear's 1786 deed of the north-east 29 acres to John Foster (W.G. Z/386), Foster to Walker (1800, W.G. 63/161) and Walker to Biays (1809, W.G. 104/46), the 3010 corner ground now runs deed by deed from Joseph Ensor, every link read; the south-west part Spear kept went from his heirs to Biays in 1801 (W.G. 67/447) beside the 2958 ground.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 1739, folios 295 to 297 (MSA CE 168-1747; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 295 to 299). Cited by the 1906 Clemens-to-Sinclair deed (R.O. 2292/510). Dated and acknowledged May 4, 1898 before Thos. C. Bailey, J.P.; recorded June 22, 1898 at 1:30 P.M. (Robt. Ogle, Clerk). Jacob H. Aull of Baltimore City, for $5, grants Augustus D. Clemens Junior of Baltimore County two lots on the east side of the York Turnpike Road, both measured from the two-mile stone in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot and from the north side of 'a four foot alley way called Batemans alley': (1) beginning 123 ft 5 in south of the stone (200 ft from the alley's north side), 33 ft on the turnpike, east at right angles 58 ft 1 in to the west side of the Old York Road, 34 ft 4 in along it and 67 ft 7 in back, held under Clemens and wife's 99-year lease to Aull of April 14, 1898 (R.O. 1728/284) at $60, April 15 and October 15 (the 3019 lot, north of 3015-3017); (2) beginning 204 ft 7 in south of the stone (281 ft 2 in from the alley), 58 ft 4 in on the turnpike, N 89 E 8 ft 6 in to the Old York Road, N 31 1/2 E 66 ft and back 42 ft 4 in, held under their lease to Aull of April 18, 1898 (R.O. 1730/92) at $75, May 1 and November 1 (3011 Greenmount); for the residue of each term, renewable forever. Special warranty; witness Thos. C. Bailey. The deed just above it (ending on folio 295) is another Aull deed to Clemens, of a Barclay Street lot at $50 from James R. Brewer's 1895 deed to Aull (J.B. 1580/209), acknowledged May 20, 1898. What it settles: Aull was a straw for the 1898 Clemens leases. Clemens leased the 3019 lot (April 14) and the 3011 lot (April 18) to Aull, sold the $60 rent to Henry D. Konig and the $75 rent to Lulie H. Wallace, and took both leaseholds back from Aull on May 4. Clemens held the 3011 leasehold until he sold it to James M. Sinclair in 1906 (R.O. 2292/510), who bought the Wallace rent in 1921 and merged it. The 3011 leasehold side is now read without a gap from the 1898 lease to the 1927 fee.

Given under the hands and seals of Thos. Boone, Henry Stevenson son of Edwd. and Nichs. Merryman son of Saml., May 30, 1768 (the clerk wrote '1760'; the March 1768 court and the qualifications fix 1768); filed August Term 1770, enrolled and examined by A. Lawson, Clerk. Huntington'), Garrison's 1781 deed to William Spear and Spear's 1786 deed to John Foster is a sworn, marked corner on the ground in 1768, in a level old field once settled by Moses Edwards. Huntington was first granted to the Edwards family (a John Edwards, 1688), so the 'Edwards' field fits the deeds' calling the oak a Huntington tree (inference). It gives no distance to a road, so it does not by itself fix the oak on a modern map.

summary: Sub-lease, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 4854, folios 321 to 323 (MSA CE 168-4862; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 321 to 325, at 130 and 300 dpi; the companion construction mortgage follows from folio 323 and is filed separately). Dated March 3, 1928. Lula S. Dietrich, widow, of Baltimore City, sub-lessor, sub-leases to Miller Brothers Furniture Company, Incorporated, a Maryland corporation, for all the rest of her term of years save one day (no 99-year term is stated), a lot on the east side of Greenmount Avenue (formerly York Turnpike Road) beginning 204 ft 6 in north of the beginning of the land Samuel H. Tagart, trustee, assigned to George C. H. Coffield by deed of January 31, 1865 (Balt. Co. J.H.L. 43/548), and 409 ft south of Gorsuch Avenue, at a post at the north-west corner of that whole tract; S 2 W 35 ft along the avenue, S 85 1/2 E 126 ft more or less to the west side of the Old York Road, N 19 1/2 E 35 ft more or less to a post at the north-east corner of the whole lot, N 85 1/2 W 140 ft 6 in to the beginning; the improvements known as No. 3117 Greenmount Avenue. Title recited: the same lot described in a deed of May 6, 1927 from C. Reese Dietrich to John Harmon Dietrich and Lula S. Dietrich (S.C.L. 4735/61); see also a confirmatory deed of March 2, 1928 from Lula S. Dietrich, executrix, to Lula S. Dietrich, survivor; and part of the whole lot conveyed by a deed of assignment from Augustus D. Clemens Jr. to John H. Dietrich dated December 9, 1907 (S.C.L. 2390/331), the whole lot subject to the original ground rent of $150 a year, half-yearly on March 1 and September 1. Rent $1,200 a year in equal quarterly instalments from March 1, 1928, over and above all taxes and assessments; distress for arrears; re-entry until paid after 60 days in arrear, and re-entry as though no sub-lease had been made after six months. Renewable forever: on a $10 renewal fine the sub-lessor gives a new sub-lease at the same rent reserving one day. The sub-lessee may pay the $150 original rent ($75 half-yearly) directly to its holder and deduct it from the $1,200. After five years the sub-lessee may redeem the $1,200 rent for $18,892.58 in gold coin, with rent accrued and a pro rata share. The sub-lease has no building covenant, no valuation and no builder. Signed Lula S. Dietrich and the company by Adolph Miller, President, under the seal 'Miller Bros Furniture Co Inc 1928'; witness and notary R. E. Lee Hall; acknowledged March 3, 1928; recorded March 7, 1928 at 9:50 A.M. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). What it settles: the $1,200 sub-rent is carved out of Lula Dietrich's own leasehold of the whole 79 ft lot under the $150 rent, and that leasehold came to John H. Dietrich by assignment from Augustus D. Clemens Jr. in December 1907 (S.C.L. 2390/331), not about 1920 as the undated City plat suggested. John Harmon Dietrich was Lula's husband (S.C.L. 5213/440 calls the 1927 grantees 'John Harmon Dietrich and Lulu S. Dietrich his wife'), and he had died by March 2, 1928, when Lula as executrix confirmed the lot to herself as survivor. What it does not settle: how Clemens Jr. came to hold the leasehold (possibly at the 1904 Hershey trustee's sale, an inference), what part C. Reese Dietrich played in 1927 (very probably a straw deed to create a tenancy by the entirety, an inference), and the basis of the $18,892.58 redemption price, which is not the 6 percent figure for $1,200.

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 4854, folios 323 to 325 and on (MSA CE 168-4862; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, which stops at folio 325 in the middle of the third lot's description, so the signatures, acknowledgment, recording and any release are not read). Dated March 3, 1928, the day of the Dietrich sub-lease, and entered next after it. Miller Brothers Furniture Company, Incorporated, Adolph Miller and Anna J. Miller his wife, and Jacob Miller, all of Baltimore City, mortgage to Erhard Eyring of Baltimore City, for $1 and to secure a loan of $20,000 'to be used ... in the construction and improvement upon the lot of ground hereinafter firstly described', under plans and specifications signed by Adolph Miller, President, and Eyring. The advances: $5,000 when the roof is on, $7,000 when plastered, $5,000 when all trim is on, and $3,000 within thirty days after completion, each only on a certificate of John F. Eyring, architect, of Baltimore; if the mortgage is assigned to The Eyring Realty Company Incorporated, it may make the advances in Eyring's place. A condition of the loan is that Eyring, the party of the second part, will begin the construction within ten days and fully complete the building within four months of the date. No further encumbrance before the last advance, and the debt advanced falls due at once on a transfer without consent, insolvency, bankruptcy or receivership. The whole $20,000 is due on or before March 1, 1933 at 6 percent, payable half-yearly and charged only from each advance, with a joint and several note for each advance, $1,000 to be repaid at three years and another $1,000 at four. Security: first (Block 4076), the 3117 Greenmount Avenue lot, beginning 114 7/10 ft south of the south curb line of Thirty-second Street, which is 204 ft 6 in north of the beginning of the Coffield land of 1865 (J.H.L. 43/548), with the courses of the sub-lease, being the lot Lula S. Dietrich demised to the company by lease of even date at $1,200 a year (written here as half-yearly; the sub-lease says quarterly); second (Block 1688), Adolph and Jacob Miller's interest in 242 N. Patterson Park Avenue, 14 by 80 ft, 14 ft south of Orleans Street, conveyed by Daniel F. Ludlow to Adolph Miller, Jacob L. Miller and Katherine Miller (now deceased) by deed of June 9, 1921 (S.C.L. 3748 [?] folio 219), subject to $60 rent; third, their interest in the lot at the south-west corner of Orleans Street and Patterson Park Avenue (the description runs on past folio 325). What it settles: this mortgage, not the sub-lease, is the construction instrument for the 1928 store at 3117. Erhard Eyring lent the $20,000 and undertook to build it within four months to John F. Eyring's plans, which fits the newspaper reports that E. Eyring and Sons would build (CR#4925, 4926) and the City permit of July 21, 1928. It very probably explains the equity case Erhard Eyring et al. v. The Miller Brothers Furniture Company et al. (decree of Oct. 21, 1932) and the 1933 trustees' deed of the leasehold to The Eyring Realty Corporation (S.C.L. 5349/127): the Eyrings enforcing this loan after the company's insolvency (an inference). What it does not settle: the recording date, the end of the third description and any release, which are on folios not saved.

summary: Administratrix's deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 5213, folios 440 to 441 (MSA CE 168-5221; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 440 to 444, at 130 and 300 dpi; folio 440 opens with the end of an unrelated Canton National Bank deed, and folios 442 to 444 hold unrelated instruments). Dated April 27, 1931. Wilhelmina Dietrich of Baltimore City, administratrix of the estate of Lula S. Dietrich, late of Baltimore City, deceased, authorized and directed by an order of the Orphans' Court of Baltimore City passed April 27, 1931 to convey under Article 93, Section 144 of the Code of Public General Laws, for $5 grants to Dorothy Dietrich, Wilhelmina Dietrich and Helen Dietrich Butler (nee Dietrich), as tenants in common, their personal representatives and assigns, two lots. First (Block 4076): the 3117 Greenmount Avenue lot, by the description of the 1928 sub-lease (beginning 204 ft 6 in north of the beginning of the land Samuel H. Tagart, trustee, assigned to George C. H. Coffield in 1865, J.H.L. 43/548, and 409 ft more or less south of Gorsuch Avenue; 35 ft on the avenue, about 126 ft to the Old York Road, 140 ft 6 in on the north line), 'and especially' the right to collect 'the annual sub rent of twelve hundred dollars' reserved by the sub-lease from Lula S. Dietrich, widow, to Miller Brothers Furniture Company, Incorporated, dated March 3, 1928 (S.C.L. 4854/321), payable quarterly from March 1, 1928; being the lot thirdly described in the deed of May 6, 1927 from C. Reese Dietrich to John Harmon Dietrich and Lulu S. Dietrich his wife (S.C.L. 4735/61), with the confirmatory deed of March 2, 1928 from Lula S. Dietrich, executrix, to Lula S. Dietrich (S.C.L. 4853/235); the whole lot subject to the original $150 ground rent, half-yearly on March 1 and September 1. Second (Block 3856): 409 East Thirty-first Street (formerly Waverly Avenue), 24 ft 6 in on the south side of the street beginning 97 ft 6 in east of Barclay Street, 100 ft deep to a 10 ft alley, the lot secondly described in the same 1927 deed to John H. Dietrich and Lula S. Dietrich his wife, subject to $61.25 ground rent half-yearly on April 15 and October 15. Both pass for the rest of the term with the benefit of renewal forever. Witness and notary R. Irving Hall; acknowledged April 27, 1931; recorded April 27, 1931 at 12:30 P.M. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). What it settles: the estate behind the 1936 merger deed (S.C.L. 5686/215) is Lula S. Dietrich's, not Wilhelmina's. Wilhelmina was Lula's administratrix, so Lula died between March 3, 1928 and April 27, 1931, apparently without a will (an administratrix, not an executrix; an inference). The three grantees took the $1,200 sub-rent and the sub-reversion of 3117 as tenants in common by this deed, and that is the title they deeded to The Eyring Realty Corporation in 1936. It also confirms that John Harmon Dietrich, also written John H. Dietrich, was Lula's husband, so the earlier reading of J. Harmon Dietrich as a son is wrong. What it does not settle: the grantees' kinship to Lula is still not stated (a conveyance in kind by order of the Orphans' Court points to her distributees, very probably her daughters; an inference), nor the dates of John Harmon's and Lula's deaths (the Register of Wills index is the route).

The folio order is odd: Holmes's deed of the 3013 lot to Sinclair, cited in Corridor as S.C.L. 3311/260, stands 37 folios before the Keil deed that gave him title, so either the deed out was recorded first or the 260 citation needs checking. summary: Sub-lease, Baltimore County land records, Liber J.W.S. No. 167, folio 405 (MSA CE 62-167; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, at 130 and 260 dpi). The instrument begins on folio 402 (folios 402 to 404 read earlier: David Stewart, assignee of the 1884 Harris lease, sub-leases four lots on the west side of the York Turnpike to Sarah E. Sinclair, the fourth lot beginning 181 ft north of Merryman's Lane, 16 by 100 ft, now 3224) and runs on to folio 406, which was not saved. Folio 405 holds the habendum and the rents. The term is ninety-nine years 'or for all the residue of the term created by the aforesaid lease', beginning on the date of the instrument (Feb. 1, 1888), to Sarah and her executors, administrators and assigns. The clerk writes her 'Sarah C. Sinclair' three times, but his capital E and C are alike and he gives her husband James the same letter, so E is the probable reading. The yearly rents, payable to David Stewart, his heirs, personal representatives or assigns, are $36 on the lot first described, $87 on the second, $81 on the third and $48 on the fourth (3224), $252 in all. They are paid in equal half-yearly instalments accruing from Feb. 1, 1888, clear of all taxes and assessments, 'each of said lots however being liable only for its own rent precisely as if each of said lots had been leased by a separate instrument'. Remedies: distress for any arrears; re-entry after sixty days until the arrears and costs are paid; and after six months, re-entry to hold the lot 'as if this lease had never been made'. Sarah and James E. Sinclair her husband covenant to pay the rent, taxes and assessments. The lessor's covenant for quiet enjoyment begins at the foot of the folio and runs onto folio 406. No signatures, acknowledgment or recording entry are on this folio. What it settles: the sub-rent on the 3224 lot was $48 a year from Feb. 1, 1888, the same sum John N. C. (or H. C.) Legg reserved on the same 16-ft lot in his lease to George T. Drechsler of Apr. 24, 1890 (J.B. 1299/406, $48, payable May 1 and Nov. 1), the rent that ran until the 1926 merger. The 1890 lease appears to restate the 1888 sub-rent on the same lot, though on different rent days [inference]. Each of the four lots was charged separately, so the 3224 rent could be dealt with on its own. What it does not settle: the signatures, acknowledgment and recording date (folio 406, not saved), and how the sub-lease was cleared before Legg's fresh lease of 1890. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (later): folios 406 and 407 read (MSA CE 62-167 p.00406 to p.00407, the scan Jeff saved; read by a helper agent). The instrument ends on folio 407. Folio 406 finishes the lessor's covenants: Stewart warrants the lots against claims by, from or under him; on payment of a $10 renewal fine and costs he will give Sarah C. Sinclair a new lease of all or any of the lots for another 99 years at the same rent, 'so that the demise hereby created may be renewable and renewed from time to time forever'; and any rent may be redeemed after five years at 5 percent and after fifteen years at 6 percent, in gold coin of the United States or its equivalent, with rent accrued and a pro-rata part of the current half-year's rent. A rent not redeemed by Feb. 1, 1904 runs as if the lease were dated that day and is not redeemable at 6 percent for fifteen years more. Folio 407: signed David Stewart (witness Robert A. Thursby [?]), Sarah C. Sinclair and Jas. E. Sinclair (witness Wm. D. Wright [?]). Stewart acknowledged on Feb. 1, 1888 before Thursby, a Baltimore City justice, with the certificate of Jas. Bond, Clerk of the Superior Court of Baltimore City; Sarah C. and James E. Sinclair acknowledged the same day before Wright, a Baltimore County justice. 'Recorded Feby 2nd 1888 at 8:30 AM' (John W. Shanklin, Clerk); a margin note reads 'Delivered ... 5064, Oct 13/88' [?]. Her initial is C in her signature, in the County clerk's hand of 1888 and in the City clerk's hand of 1890 (J.B. 1289/297 and 299); the 1923 deeds write E. The same day the Sinclairs mortgaged to Stewart (J.W.S. 135/275, recorded Feb. 9, 1888), and the foreclosure of that mortgage in April 1890 ended this sub-lease (J.B. 1289/297).

summary: Deed of assignment (indexed 'Asst to'), Baltimore City land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 3965, folio 93 (MSA CE 168-3973; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 93 to 96, at 130 and 260 dpi). Dated Feb. 1, 1923. Gee Qu Ying of Baltimore City, for $5 'and other good and valuable considerations', grants and conveys to Gee Quong, his personal representatives and assigns, 'all his right title and interest in all that lot of ground in Baltimore City known as 3224 Greenmount Avenue'. The lot begins on the west side of the York Turnpike Road 181 ft north of its intersection with the northeast side of Merryman's Lane and runs west at right angles along the north line of the lot thirdly described in the Feb. 1, 1888 sub-lease from David Stewart to Sarah E. Sinclair (Baltimore County J.W.S. 167/402) 100 ft to a three-foot alley leading to Merryman's Lane, laid out for use in common with others; then north along the alley 16 ft, east 100 ft to the road, and south along the road 16 ft to the beginning. Recital: the lot described in a deed from William F. Ludwig and Mary L. Ludwig his wife 'to the said Grantor' dated June 1, 1918 (S.C.L. 3217/44). Habendum for all the residue of the term with the benefit of renewal forever, subject to the annual ground rent of $48 payable half-yearly on May 1 and November 1. Special warranty and further assurances. Signed 'Gee Qu Ying', his mark; witness and notary James F. Johnson; acknowledged Feb. 1, 1923; recorded Feb. 2, 1923 at 9:55 a.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Federal revenue stamps '2-$1 USS cancelled' ($2), which at the 1923 rate of 50 cents per $500 points to a real price over $1,500 and not over $2,000 [inference]. A pencilled margin note reads 'Plat Book 8-17-23' [?]. What it settles: the instrument is read. Gee Qu Ying released his share of the 1918 Ludwig purchase to Gee Quong for a real sum, on the same day Gee Quong and Gee Ott mortgaged the lot (S.C.L. 3965/93 to 95), and the ground rent was still $48, due May 1 and November 1. It is also the first of the 1923 instruments to give the street number. What it does not settle: how Gee Qu Ying was related to Gee Quong, and why the deed calls the 1918 purchaser 'the said Grantor' alone when the 1918 deed ran to both men.

Tufts). Dated Feb. 1, 1923. Gee Quong and Gee Ott of Baltimore City, mortgagors, being members of the American National Building and Loan Association, a body corporate, have received from it an advance of $1,500 on fifteen shares of its stock. Gee Ott joins 'for the purpose of better securing the repayment of said loan' and holds himself personally liable. For the premises and $1 they grant the Association the lot 'at present known as No 3224 Greenmount Avenue', described as in the deed just before it (west side of the York Turnpike Road, 181 ft north of Merryman's Lane, 16 by 100 ft, off the north line of the third lot of the 1888 sub-lease, J.W.S. 167/402). Recital: the lot in the deed of even date from Gee Qu Ying to Gee Quong 'intended to be recorded ... immediately prior hereto'. Habendum for the residue of the term with the right of renewal forever, subject to the yearly rent of $48. Terms: weekly dues of 25 cents a share until the dues reach $100 a share; weekly interest and premium of 12 cents a share until the shares are paid up; and $3.25 a week toward taxes, water rent, ground rent and insurance. Fire insurance for the Association; the whole debt due on any sale of the lot; possession until default; and assent to a decree for sale after four weeks' default under sections 720 to 732 of Chapter 123 of the Acts of 1898. Witness and notary James F. Johnson; acknowledged Feb. 1, 1923, when Clemens H. Lears [?] Jr., the Association's president, made the consideration oath; recorded Feb. 2, 1923 at 9:56 a.m. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). No release is noted in the margins of folios 93 to 95. What it settles: the building and loan mortgage is read: $1,500 on the 3224 leasehold, with Gee Ott as co-obligor. The block book's February to April span fits: Gee Quong sold on Apr. 19, 1923 (S.C.L. 3998/78, recorded Apr. 20), so a release at S.C.L. 3998/621 would fall within days of the sale, which supports reading the index's '3898/621' as 3998/621 [inference]. What it does not settle: the release itself (not pulled) and who Gee Ott was. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (later): S.C.L. 3998/621 to 623 read (MSA CE 168-4006, the scan Jeff saved; read by a helper agent), and it is not the release. Folio 621 holds the end of a deed acknowledged before Ethel Miller, notary (recorded Apr. 21, 1923 at 9:05 a.m.); a release by The Sound Building and Loan Association to Philip B. and Mary Bessie Cashmeyer (Apr. 18, 1923; mortgage S.C.L. 3984/280; recorded Apr. 21 at 9:30 a.m.); and a release by the Washington Loan and Savings Association No. 1 to Thomas J. and Bernardine Flaherty (Apr. 17, 1923; mortgage S.C.L. 3354/364; recorded Apr. 21 at 10:50 a.m.). Folios 622 and 623 hold the Flahertys' $1,200 mortgage to the Parkwood Building and Loan Association on 10 S. Hare Street (Apr. 17, 1923). The edge of folio 620 shows a building and loan release and a deed from Samuel and Dora Corman [?], neither for 3224. No line names Gee or the American National Building and Loan Association. These folios were recorded two days after Gee Quong's sale, so a release recorded with the sale would fall in nearby libers, but the index's '3898/621' is not 3998/621, and the release remains unlocated; the 1923 grantor index under American National Building and Loan Association is the next place to look.

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore City land records, Liber M.L.P. No. 6140, folios 545 to 549, continuing onto folio 550, which was not saved (MSA CE 168-6148; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, at 130 and 300 dpi). Dated Apr. 4, 1941; acknowledged Apr. 7, 1941. The mortgagors are Lester S. Levy, Henry E. Wyman, and Reuben Oppenheimer, Selma L. Oppenheimer and Lester S. Levy, trustees under an Indenture and Declaration of Trust from Clara Oppenheimer and Martha Oppenheimer dated Aug. 17, 1935 and 'recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City prior hereto'. Eleanor K. Levy, Lester's wife, and Carrie K. Wyman, Henry's wife, join only to release dower. Dea Bing Young is not a party. The mortgagee is The Penn Mutual Life Insurance Company, a Pennsylvania corporation, with tax receipts to go to its office in Philadelphia. The debt is $18,000 lent that day on a negotiable note at 4 percent, payable in 180 monthly instalments of $133.15 from June 1, 1941 through Apr. 1, 1956, with the balance on May 1, 1956, and 6 percent on overdue instalments. The lot, 'according to survey made by Howard C Sutton Surveyor and Civil Engineer on March 25 1941', begins on the west side of Greenmount Avenue '(formerly known as York Turnpike Road)' 181 ft 4 3/8 in north of the northeast side of Merrymans Lane and runs west along the north line of the lot thirdly described in the 1888 sub-lease from David Stewart to Sarah E. Sinclair (J.W.S. 167/402) 100 ft to the three-foot alley, north 16 ft 1/4 in, east 100 ft, and south 16 ft 1/4 in; 'The improvements thereon being known as No 3224 Greenmount Avenue'. Recital: the same lot granted in fee simple to the mortgagors by Dea Bing Young, unmarried, by deed dated Feb. 17, 1941 (M.L.P. 6129/439). Covenants of seisin in fee simple and against encumbrances; insurance, taxes and acceleration clauses; assent to a decree under sections 720 to 732 of Chapter 123 of the Acts of 1898, and a power of sale to Joseph Addison, attorney, under Article 66 of the 1904 Code, with a $900 counsel fee; a receivership clause. Witness Harry G. Bayley. Maryland documentary stamps of $18 (three at $5, one at $1, one at $2) cancelled; grantee-index stamp June 14, 1941. The notary's name and the recording entry are on folio 550. No release is noted in the margins of folios 545 to 549; a typed 'O P' and an unreadable pencil mark beside the caption are not a release entry. What it settles: the Penn Mutual mortgage is read. The 1941 owners, not Dea Bing Young, borrowed $18,000 at 4 percent for fifteen years on 3224 about seven weeks after buying it in fee, which fits the new store front and one-story brick store addition permitted in February 1941 ($7,000 in all) [inference]. The Sutton survey puts the lot 181 ft 4 3/8 in from the lane and 16 ft 1/4 in wide, and the recital dates the Dea Bing Young deed Feb. 17, 1941 (the chain row has Feb. 15). What it does not settle: the release, and the recording date (folio 550). The loan was scheduled to run to May 1, 1956 and the owners sold to Theodore and Sylvia Lee Frank on Aug. 4, 1955 (M.L.P. 9873/248), so a release of about 1955 is the likely place to look [inference]. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (later): folio 550 read (MSA CE 168-6148 p.00550, the scan Jeff saved; read by a helper agent). It completes the acknowledgments: James Piper Jr., agent of The Penn Mutual Life Insurance Company, made the consideration oath; Eleanor K. Levy and Carrie K. Wyman acknowledged on Apr. 7, 1941; notary Harry G. Bayley; 'Recd for Record Recorded & exd April 7 1941 at 2.46 O'Clk P M' (M. Luther Pittman, Clerk). A typed release follows on the record: 'May 6 1946 FOR VALUE RECEIVED the THE PENN MUTUAL LIFE INSURANCE COMPANY doe[s] hereby release the within mortgage and the debt secured thereby', signed for the company by George S. Moffett, Assistant to the President, attested by Howard T. Maag, Assistant Secretary, under the corporate seal, and recorded May 8, 1946 at 2:30 P.M. ('Note Attached'). The margin stamps beside the next caption (an assignment of mortgage dated 5/7/41 and a grantee stamp of June 14, 1941) belong to that instrument, John G. and Annabella Buchanan to The Moss-Rouse Company, Mar. 29, 1941. So the $18,000 loan on 3224 was released on May 6, 1946, ten years before maturity, and the 1941 mortgage is not open of record.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 3869, folios 529 to 530 (MSA CE 168-3877; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 529 to 533, at 130, 260 and 400 dpi; folios 530 to 533 then hold a Lake Drive Building and Loan release, a Sacks mortgage on Eutaw Street and a Pressman Street assignment, none about 3313). Dated June 9, 1922. Porter G. Wamsley and Katherine M. Wamsley his wife, Morton Franklin and Anna Franklin his wife, and Harry Franklin, unmarried, all of Baltimore City, to George Esselmann of the same city, for $5 and other valuable considerations (two $10 revenue stamps, about $20,000, which matches the Sun's $20,000), 'all those four lots of ground' in fee simple, with special warranty. All four lie on the east side of the York Turnpike Road (Greenmount Avenue). First: beginning on the turnpike about 31 ft north of the south-westernmost corner of the whole ground formerly of Augustus 'Dames' (Dawes) deceased, at the north-west corner of a lot leased to and in the possession of Thomas Hart; north 30 ft; east at right angles about 119 ft 6 in to a fence; south with the fence to Hart's lot; west on it 119 ft to the beginning. Second: on the turnpike about 61 ft north of the same corner; north 30 ft; east 120 ft to the fence; south 30 ft to the lot George W. Bucher sub-leased to Anna M. Brown on June 18, 1869; west on that lot 119 ft 6 in to the beginning. Third: beginning at the south-west corner of lot 4 B allotted to Thomas A. 'Dames' (Dawes); east along that lot 122 ft; south at right angles 46 ft 8 in to a 3-ft alley 'it is intended shall be left running the depth of the lot from the York Turnpike Road'; west, parallel with and 3 ft from the southern boundary of 'said lot No 5' [or 6?], 120 ft to the turnpike; north along it 47 ft to the beginning; with the use of the 3-ft alley, 120 ft deep, and free ingress and egress for Jacob A. Aull, his heirs and assigns, with carts, carriages, horses or cattle if Aull should widen it, in common with Elizabeth '..ames' (Dawes [?]), her heirs and assigns. Fourth: on the east side of the turnpike at the north-west corner of the whole lot which by lease of Oct. 1 [?], 1866 (Balt. Co. J.H.L. 52/250) Lewis L. 'Barringer' and wife leased to George 'M.' [W.] Bucher; south along the turnpike, 'now known as the York Road', 40 ft; east 121 ft; north 40 ft to the north line of the whole lot; west along it 121 ft to the beginning. Title: the same four lots Henry Dubois and wife deeded to Porter G. Wamsley on Apr. 3, 1919 (S.C.L. 3337/102), in which Morton and 'Annie' Franklin took an undivided quarter and Harry Franklin another undivided quarter from the Wamsleys by deed of May 29, 1921 (S.C.L. 3753/103). No ground rent is reserved or recited, and no title company is a party. Witness George C. Wiedersum; acknowledged June 9, 1922 by all five grantors before George C. Wiedersum, notary (the notary of the Title Holding deeds of 1936); recorded June 10, 1922 at 11:01 A.M., Stephen C. Little, Clerk. Pencilled margin notes read 'Blck 4049'. What it settles: Esselmann's Greenmount front came from the Wamsleys and the Franklins, not from Sara H. Kohn; it was four lots, not three; the deed was recorded June 10, not June 11; the 'lot thirdly described' of the 1928 Adams mortgages is the 47-ft lot whose first line is the south line of Dawes lot 4 B, the line the 1933 and 1935 deeds call Venable Street [inference]; the fourth lot is the north-west 40 by 121 ft of the 1866 Bucher lot, the size and place of Hooper's 1872 sub-lease to Johnson [inference]; and lots one, two and four (30, 30 and 40 ft) add up to the 100-ft turnpike front of the Bucher lot, which began at Hart's lot [inference]. The land is part of the Dawes partition (lot 4 B, and lot 5 [?]), and the Aull family held a way in the 3-ft alley. What it does not settle: the Dubois title (S.C.L. 3337/102) and how the 1866 Bucher lease and the 1869 Brown sub-lease became a fee; the Old York Road half of the block, which came by the Rich and Frederick deeds.
