summary: Trustees' deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 3904, folios 358 to 359 (MSA CE 168-3912; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 358 to 362, at 130 and 260 dpi; folio 358 opens with the end of an unrelated New-to-Gruber ground-rent deed, and folio 362 goes on to a Ciurca assignment on Third Street). Dated June 30, 1922. Charles S. Rich and Edward N. Rich, trustees, of Baltimore City, to George Esselmann of the same city. Recitals: Edward L. Raborg, late of Baltimore City, died seized of fee simple property of which this lot is part on or about May 2, 1920, leaving a will probated and recorded in the Orphans' Court of Baltimore City, Wills H.W.J. No. 135 folio 27, which left the residue of his estate to Charles S. Rich and Edward N. Rich or the survivor in trust; acting under the will's powers they sold the lot to Esselmann for $8,000. For $8,000 they grant it in fee simple: beginning on the west side of Old York Road at the south-east corner of the whole lot Lewis L. Barranger and wife leased to George W. Bucher by deed of Oct. 1, 1866 (Balt. Co. J.H.L. 52/250); north on the west side of Old York Road 68 ft 8 in to the centre of an alley 6 ft wide; west at right angles along the alley's centre 121 ft more or less to the east line of the lot George G. Hooper leased to Thomas Johnson on Aug. 12, 1872 (E.H.A. 76/578); south along that line, parallel with Old York Road, 68 ft 8 in; east in a straight line to the beginning. Being the lot John Myerson and wife deeded to Edward L. Raborg on Oct. 4, 1906 (R.O. 2277/117). No rent is reserved or recited, and the deed carries no warranty clause beyond the grant. The clerk's margin says 'Unlocated'. Witness Mary R. Rider; acknowledged June 30, 1922 by both trustees before Mary R. Rider, notary; recorded Sept. 8, 1922 at 9:30 A.M., Stephen C. Little, Clerk (grantee stamp Oct. 11, 1922). Esselmann's $5,000 purchase-money mortgage follows at folio 359. What it settles: the Rich trustees' lot is the south-east 68 ft 8 in by 121 ft of the 1866 Bucher lot, on Old York Road south of the 6-ft alley; with the 30 ft north of the alley (the Starr Lane lot, parcel FOURTH, deeded to the Williamses in 1919) it makes up the 98 2/3 ft the 1866 lease gave on the old road; it reached Raborg in 1906 and his trustees sold it after his death in 1920. Schwaab's 1925 lot took its south part, and parcel SECOND (1936) the 18 ft 10 in left between Schwaab's line and the alley. What it does not settle: how Myerson held (fee or the Bucher leasehold) and when the 1866 rent ended; the next pull is R.O. 2277/117 (1906).

summary: Purchase-money mortgage and release, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 3904, folios 359 to 362 (MSA CE 168-3912; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 358 to 362, at 130 and 260 dpi). Dated June 30, 1922. George Esselmann and Virginia M. Esselmann his wife, of Baltimore City, to Charles S. Rich and Edward N. Rich, trustees under the will of Edward L. Raborg (Wills H.W.J. 135/27): $5,000, part of the purchase money for the lot, due one year from date with interest at 6 percent payable semi-annually, principal and interest in gold coin, prepayable before default in sums of not less than $1,000. The same lot as the deed just before it: 68 ft 8 in on the west side of Old York Road from the south-east corner of the 1866 Bucher lot (J.H.L. 52/250) north to the centre of the 6-ft alley, and 121 ft back along the alley to the Hooper-Johnson line (E.H.A. 76/578), being the lot in the Rich trustees' deed of even date. Assent to a decree; power of sale to Charles S. Rich as attorney; receiver, insurance and tax covenants; special warranty. Witness Holt Wooddell; acknowledged June 30, 1922 in Webster County, West Virginia, before Amos Cogar, notary public for Webster County (commission expires Feb. 28, 1926); Charles S. Rich swore to the consideration on Sept. 6, 1922 before Mary R. Rider, notary; recorded Sept. 8, 1922 at 9:31 A.M., Stephen C. Little, Clerk. Short release by Charles S. Rich and Edward N. Rich, trustees, dated June 30, 1923 (test Mary R. Rider), recorded July 6, 1923 at 3 P.M. What it settles: Esselmann paid $3,000 down on the $8,000 lot and paid off the $5,000 balance in a year; his wife was Virginia M. Esselmann (the Virginia Esselmann, widow, of the 1925 recital); the couple signed in Webster County, West Virginia, which fits his calling as a lumberman (Polk 1922). What it does not settle: anything about the lot's title before 1906.

The Title Holding Company, a Maryland corporation, by Chas. H. Buck, president, to Alvin J. Irvin and Alma R. Irvin his wife and Irving J. Orem and Carolyn W. Orem his wife, of Baltimore City, for $5 and other good and valuable considerations ($3 in revenue stamps, about $3,000; the mortgage that follows is for $3,000 'comprising the purchase price'), in fee simple, with special warranty. This is parcel SECOND: beginning on the west side of Old York Road 79 ft 8 in more or less south of the corner of the west side of Old York Road and the south side of Venable Avenue, intended to be the beginning of the seventh line of the lot in the deed from Samuel H. Adams to The Title Holding Company (March 1, 1928, S.C.L. 4853/457); south on Old York Road 18 ft 10 in to the end of that seventh line; west along part of the eighth line 134 ft 5 1/2 in to the easternmost outline of the lot in the Title Holding deed to Alvin J. Irvin et al. (July 21, 1933, S.C.L. 5368/38); north along that outline 49 ft 2 in to where a westward prolongation of the Adams lot's fourth line would cross it; east along that prolongation 12 ft 10 in to a point 4 ft west of the end of the fourth line; south, parallel with the fifth line and 4 ft west of it, 30 ft 4 in to the westward prolongation of the sixth line; then east to and along the sixth line and the centre line of the 6-ft alley 125 ft to the beginning. Being part of the Adams deed. Together with the right of ingress, egress and regress, in common with the grantor, over a strip 6 ft wide running from the fourth line of this lot north to Venable Avenue, its west side on the easternmost outline of the 1933 Irvin lot. Witness Geo. C. Wiedersum; acknowledged June 10, 1936 before George C. Wiedersum, notary; recorded June 25, 1936 at 10:01 A.M., Stephen C. Little, Clerk (grantee stamp Aug. 3, 1936). Just before it (folio 18; it begins on folio 17, not on the scan) Maryland Title Securities Corporation (Del., 1930), by Chas. H. Buck, president, attested by Arthur M. Hoff, secretary, gave a partial release of 'the said mortgages' for this same lot and right of way, retaining their lien on the rest; acknowledged June 10 and recorded June 25, 1936 at 10 A.M. The margin of the 1928 Adams first mortgage points to it (Liber 5635 fol. 17). What it settles: parcel SECOND is read; it is the 18 ft 10 in of the Rich trustees' lot left between Schwaab's north line and the 6-ft alley, carried west 134 ft 5 1/2 in behind the 1933 garage lot, plus a strip 12 ft 10 in wide and 30 ft 4 in long running north beside the Starr Lane lot; the 79 ft 8 in agrees with the 2017 Exhibit A, so the 79 ft 11 in and 77 ft 8 in elsewhere are copying errors; the 6-ft way north to Venable is the one the 1941 Franklin Realty deed carries; the price was $3,000, all of it lent back by the seller; and the calls leave The Title Holding Company a 4-ft strip between this lot and the Starr Lane lot's west line, and the land under the 6-ft way [inference]. What it does not settle: whether that 4-ft strip and the way's land passed to Hudson Realty with the rest of Title Holding's ground in 1941 (probably in the Nov. 24, 1941 deed, M.L.P. 6244/542).

summary: Purchase-money mortgage and assignment, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 5635, folios 19 to 22 (MSA CE 168-5643; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 18 to 22, at 130 and 260 dpi). Dated June 10, 1936. Alvin J. Irvin and Alma R. Irvin his wife and Irving J. Orem and Carolyn W. Orem his wife, of Baltimore City, to The Title Holding Company: $3,000 'comprising the purchase price for the property hereinafter described', repayable $125 at six and at twelve months, $200 at eighteen and at twenty-four months, $100 every three months from twenty-seven to fifty-seven months (eleven payments), and the $1,250 balance at five years, with interest at 5 percent payable semi-annually. The whole debt falls due at the mortgagee's option if the mortgagors, 'who are at this time the owners of the lot of ground lying immediately to the west of the lot herein described fronting on Greenmount Avenue', the residue of their 1933 purchase (S.C.L. 5368/38), sell that property. The description and the 6-ft right of way to Venable Avenue are word for word the deed's (parcel SECOND, 18 ft 10 in on Old York Road, 79 ft 8 in south of Venable), 'Being the same property' as the Title Holding deed of even date. Assent to a decree, power of sale, receiver and insurance clauses; special warranty. Witness C. A. Diffenderfer; acknowledged June 10, 1936 before Thomas M. Kerr, notary, with Charles H. Buck, president of the mortgagee, swearing to the consideration. Assigned the same day by The Title Holding Company (Chas. H. Buck, president; witness Geo. C. Wiedersum) to Maryland Title Securities Corporation; recorded June 25, 1936 at 10:02 A.M., Stephen C. Little, Clerk (grantee stamp July 21, 1936). No release is noted on the folios read. What it settles: parcel SECOND cost $3,000, wholly financed by the seller, and the lender tied it to the Greenmount filling-station lot by a due-on-sale clause, so the two were meant to be held and sold together, as they were in 1941. What it does not settle: when the mortgage was paid; its release is not in hand.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 3478, folios 514 to 516 (MSA CE 168-3486; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the handwritten scan Jeff saved, folios 514 to 518, at 130 and 260 dpi; folio 518 begins an unrelated McCreary Paine deed). Dated Oct. 30, 1919. Minnie Gordon Gorter (widow), Sophie H. Baker and J. Paul Baker her husband, Susan V. Norris, unmarried, and Francis W. Elder, unmarried, all of Baltimore City; George H. Elder and Anna Elder his wife, of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania (Francis W. and George H. Elder 'being the only heirs at law of Francis [or Frances] Elder deceased'); and Jessie S. [?] Norris Lewis, unmarried, of the State of New York, to Carter Williams and Sarah Williams his wife, as tenants by the entireties, in fee simple, for $5 and other good and valuable considerations ($1.50 in revenue stamps, about $1,500). The lot: beginning on the line of the west side of Starr Lane, formerly the Old York Road, north of Gorsuch Avenue, Waverly, at the 'northwest' [sic; on the old road it is the north-east] corner of the whole lot Lewis L. Barrenger and Barbara his wife leased to George W. Bucher by deed of Oct. 1, 1866 (Balt. Co. J.H.L. 52/250); south on the west side of Starr Lane 30 ft more or less to the centre of a 6-ft alley there; west at right angles along the alley's centre 121 ft more or less to the east line of the lot leased by Hooper to Thomas Johnson on Aug. 12, 1872 (E.H.A. 76/578); north along that line, parallel with Starr Lane, 30 ft more or less to the north line of the whole Bucher lot; east 121 ft more or less to the beginning; 'Known as No 134 Starr Lane'. Being the lot Charles Handfield [?] Wyatt, trustee, conveyed to Minnie Gordon Gorter et al. by deed dated July 7 [?], 1904, recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber R.O. 2084 [?] folio 563. Special warranty; no ground rent is recited or reserved. Witnesses Albert H. Carroll [?] (to Gorter, the Bakers, Norris and the Elder brothers), B. J. McConnell (to Anna Elder) and C. S. J. McVicker [?] (to Jessie S. Norris Lewis). Acknowledged Oct. 30, 1919 in Baltimore City before Albert H. Carroll [?], notary (commission expires May 1, 1920), by six grantors; Oct. 16, 1919 in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, by Anna Elder before B. J. McConnell, notary; Oct. 27 [?], 1919 in New York County by Jessie S. Norris Lewis before Chas. S. Adams [?], notary of Kings County (certificate filed in New York County). Recorded Nov. 10, 1919 at 2:53 P.M., Stephen C. Little, Clerk (grantee stamp Aug. 6, 1920). Recorded the same minute, just before it, is a certified copy of a 1913 Baltimore County deed (Balt. Co. Liber W.P.C. 420 folio 577; copy certified Nov. 7, 1919 by William P. Cole, clerk of the Circuit Court for Baltimore County), acknowledged by Christopher Aline [?] Wyatt and Lillian Wyatt his wife at Quincy, Massachusetts (Oct. 25, 1913) and by Katherine L. Wyatt in Baltimore (July 7, 1913) and recorded in the County Nov. 8, 1913; its opening is on earlier folios. What it settles: parcel FOURTH, the Starr Lane lot, 'No. 134 Starr Lane', 30 by 121 ft north of the 6-ft alley, passed in fee in 1919 from the Gorter, Baker, Norris, Elder and Lewis group, who held under a 1904 Wyatt trustee's deed, to Carter and Sarah Williams, who in 1926 leased it out at $3; with the Rich trustees' 68 ft 8 in south of the alley it fills the 98 2/3 ft the 1866 lease gave on the old road; the Williamses bought with a $1,430 Waverly Building Association advance (next instrument). What it does not settle: the Wyatt trust and the 1904 deed; whether the 1913 Wyatt deed copied in alongside is a confirmatory deed for this lot, which its placement suggests [inference]; and when the 1866 Bucher rent was extinguished, since this deed already conveys a fee. Next pulls: R.O. 2084 [?]/563 (1904) and S.C.L. 3478, the folios before 514.

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 3478, folios 516 to 517 (MSA CE 168-3486; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the handwritten scan Jeff saved, at 130 and 260 dpi). Dated Nov. 10, 1919. Carter Williams and Sarah Williams his wife, of Baltimore City, members of The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County, to that association: an advance of $1,430 on eleven shares of stock, the sum 'being paid as part of the purchase money for the property'; weekly dues of 25 cents a share until the payments reach $130 a share, its par value, and weekly interest of 15 cents a share, reduced by 15 cents for each $130 of principal repaid; the usual covenant to pay 'all ground rent taxes water rent' and other charges, fines under the by-laws, and fire insurance; assent to a decree. The lot is the deed's: west side of Starr Lane (formerly the Old York Road) north of Gorsuch Avenue, Waverly, at the 'northwest' [sic] corner of the 1866 Bucher lot (J.H.L. 52/250); 30 ft south to the centre of the 6-ft alley; 121 ft west to the Hooper-Johnson line (E.H.A. 76/578); 30 ft north; 121 ft east; 'Known as No 134 Starr Lane'; being the lot granted by Minnie Gordon Gorter et al. to Carter Williams and wife by deed of Oct. 30, 1919. Test Blanche L. Gregory; acknowledged Nov. 10, 1919 before Blanche L. Gregory, notary, with George H. Taylor [?], president of the association, swearing to the consideration; recorded Nov. 10, 1919 at 3:57 P.M., Stephen C. Little, Clerk. Margin: 'For release of mtge, date 2/24/26, Liber 4533 fol. 215'. What it settles: the Williamses financed nearly all of their 1919 purchase with this advance, so the price was about $1,500, and they cleared it on Feb. 24, 1926 (S.C.L. 4533/215), the folio before their Feb. 23, 1926 ground lease of the lot to Levine and Rosenstein (S.C.L. 4533/216). summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber B.B. No. 1, folios 210 to 212 (MSA CE 66-26; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 210 to 214, at 130, 220 and 250 dpi). The book is a fair copy in one uniform later hand (inference from the script), so some spellings may be the copyist's. Headed 'Charles Ridgely to Aeshah Hollyday'. Dated Dec. 27, 1753, between Charles Ridgely of Baltimore County, gentleman, and Achsah Hollyday, 'Daughter of the said Charles Ridgely' (no husband named). The consideration is 'the Naturall Love and affection which he hath & beareth' for her and five shillings sterling, receipted the same day as 'the consideration money': a deed of gift in the words of a bargain and sale. It conveys 'all the following several Tracts of Land lying in the County afsd and on the East side of Jones' Falls': 'Wilkinsons Lott containing Eighty nine acres'; 'Huntington containing fifty acres', named only, with no courses; part of 'Ridgely's Whim', beginning at the third bounded tree of Roberts Park, N 24 deg 15 min W 296 perches to a bound ash, S 28 W 140 perches to a white oak, the beginning tree of Roberts Park, SSE 26, S by W 68, S 53 E 72, S 42, SE by S 50, S 54 and N 56 W 28 perches to a Spanish oak of Durbin's land, N 25 W 83, N 31 W 214, N 24 E 86, N 22 W 44, N 5 W 20 and N 50 E 77 perches, then to a white oak, the fourth bounded tree of Merryman's Beginning, S 73 perches to a poplar, its third bounded tree, and back to the beginning, 'containing by estimation two hundred acres'; and two parts of 'Taylors Purchase lying in the fork of Gunpowder', bounded on Cox's Forrest, Blathynia Cambria, the World's End, 'Clemonara belonging to Charles Carroll Esquire' and Benjamin's Lott, 'in both the afsd parcels of Land six hundred acres'. Habendum to Achsah 'his [sic] heirs and assigns for ever', with a warranty against all claiming under Ridgely. Witnesses Nuxton Gay (so copied; very probably N. Ruxton Gay) and William Lyon, who took the acknowledgment the same day as justices of the peace; 'Received 28th April 1754 & then recorded' (Beale Bordley, Clerk). No alienation-fine receipt follows it, though the next deed in the book has one. The strike on folio 210: the upper three quarters of the folio is blank ruled paper, closed off by a horizontal rule and one diagonal stroke from upper right to lower left that ends at the Ridgely heading, and the same stroke closes the blank at the foot of folio 212 after this deed. It is the copying clerk's line through unused space so that nothing could be written in later. It is not a cancellation: no entry stands under it (the faint lines there are ink showing through from the other side of the leaf), and the deed has no marginal note or release. Folios 213 and 214 hold James Wells Jr. to Ulrich Ecklear (Nov. 21, 1753, 250 acres of Wells Care Enlarged, 75 pounds) and the start of John Robeson to Richard King Stevenson (Mar. 2, 1754); neither bears on Huntington. What it settles: the Onions' 1809 confirmatory deed (W.G. 102/33) cites this deed correctly as Charles Ridgely to Achsah Holliday, Dec. 27, 1753, B.B. 1/210. It is a gift in fee from father to daughter, and it names Huntington among her lands four years before the 1757 resurvey for John Carnan and Achsah his wife (475 acres, patented 1761). So on the 1688 to 1757 hand-off it shows that Charles Ridgely held a Huntington of fifty acres and gave it to Achsah in 1753. Taylors Purchase at 600 acres agrees with the 1768 settlement, which says her father conveyed Taylors Purchase and Ridgely's Whim to her. What it does not settle: Huntington has no courses here, so the deed does not place it on the ground or tie it to 3028. Fifty acres is less than the 135 acres of the 1688 survey, and the deed does not say 'part of', so how Ridgely came to hold it (from John Edwards or Tobias Stansbury) is not shown. The part of Ridgely's Whim here is 200 acres by estimation, against 500 acres in the 1768 deed. Whether Wilkinson's Lott and this part of Ridgely's Whim were taken into the 1757 resurvey is not shown.

summary: Index entry, Baltimore City Superior Court Grantee Index 1944 (January to June), H to O, page 151, 'Int' (MSA CE 166-315; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, at 130 and 300 dpi). The line reads 'Jan 11, Interrante Nicholas, Ida H, Charles T Leight &c, Deed, W S Greenmount Ave', M.L.P. 6549, folio 594. The folio is written plainly as 594. The '6549/554' recited in Nicholas Interrante's 1951 deed to Robert F. Podlich (M.L.P. 8386/70) miscopies 594 as 554, which is why folios 554 to 558 (MSA CE 168-6557), pulled October 14, held other deeds. It is the only Interrante line on the page. The other lines are Interstate Holding Corp. (Jan. 6), International Permanent Building and Loan Association (Jan. 15 and May 23), Interstate (Inter-State) Roofing Co. (assignments and mortgages, Jan. 25 to June 8) and International Harvester Co. of N.J. (June 10); none is on Greenmount Avenue. What it settles: the Leights' deed to the Interrantes of ground on the west side of Greenmount Avenue was recorded Jan. 11, 1944 at M.L.P. 6549/594 (MSA CE 168-6557, folio 594), and the grantees were Nicholas and Ida H. Interrante. Ida H. was very probably Nicholas's wife and had died by Mar. 14, 1951, when he conveyed as a widower (inference). What it does not settle: the index gives no consideration, no house number and no date of execution. Whether 6549/594 is the 1912 $66 reversion on 3030, as the 1951 recital implies, and how Charles T. and Ella B. Leight came to hold that rent from the Hooper trust, wait on the deed itself. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (late): the deed is read (726:mdlr-mlp6549-594-leight-interrante-3030-rent-1944), dated Jan. 7, 1944. It is not the 1912 reversion: the rent is the $66 of the Waverly Building Association's lease to Helen M. Bordley of Feb. 25, 1935 (S.C.L. 5518/171), whose reversion the Association deeded to the Leights that day (S.C.L. 5518/173).

summary: Index entry, Baltimore City Superior Court Grantor Index 1917, H to O, pages 130 to 132, 'Hoo' (MSA CE 167-162; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, at 130 and 300 dpi). Searched for Francis X. Hooper, F. X. Hooper, and his heirs, executors or trustees. The three pages run from Jan. 3 to Dec. 19, 1917 (page 132 is blank), and no line stands under Francis X. Hooper. The one line for the Hooper estate is the last on page 131: 'Dec 19, Hooper Florence W, Mercantile Trust & Deposit Co, Trs, Deed, Several Lots', S.C.L. 3177, with the folio column left blank. This is the widow's side of the Hooper division of Dec. 7, 1917, which the 1964 Mercantile-Safe deed of the 3032 rent recites at S.C.L. 3177/132 and which was read October 14 (MSA CE 168-3185): it put the four Aull rents (3026 to 3032) in the trustees' two-thirds. The other Hooper grantors on the pages (Timothy J.; Jenny M. and Arthur W.; Robert L. and Margaret A.; Thomas H., Gertrude C., Walter and Olivia C.; Adaline S.; Alcaeus Jr.; Anastatia; Charles A.; Walter C. and Lillian G.; John R.; Glen P. and Ida R.) deal in ground on Robinson, Carey, Madison, Kingsley, Stricker, Mount, Byrd, Chelsea and Baltimore Streets, Whitridge and East Avenues, Barrington Road and Derby Lane. None is on the York Road or Greenmount Avenue. What it settles: the division was recorded Dec. 19, 1917 in S.C.L. 3177, and no Hooper is indexed as grantor of any York Road ground in 1917, so none of the four Aull rents left the family by a Hooper's own deed that year. What it does not settle: the index leaves the folio blank and does not name the lots. The reciprocal half of the division would be indexed under Mercantile Trust and Deposit Co. (M). The trustees' later sale of the 3030 rent, the link to the Leights, would be in the grantor indexes under Mercantile Trust and Deposit Co., trustee, from 1918 to 1944. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (1929 and 1935 read): S.C.L. 5517/92 (MSA CE 168-5525, read; 726:mdlr-scl5517-92-hooper-trustees-waverly-bldg-redemption-3030-1935) is the deed of Feb. 18, 1935 by which Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore and William Jenkins, trustees under Francis X. Hooper's will, on the Waverly Building Association's statutory notice to redeem, conveyed it the 1912 $66 reversion on 3030 for $1,100, 'to the end and intent that the leasehold estate created by the lease aforesaid shall be merged with the fee'. So the trustees of the 1935 recitals are Hooper's, and the 1912 lease and rent on 3030 merged in the Association by that deed, not by inference. S.C.L. 5076/70 and /71 (MSA CE 168-5084, read) show how the leasehold reached the McCoys: Jacob H. Aull's executors deeded it to his widow Mary A. J. Aull on Oct. 11, 1922 (S.C.L. 3918/495, recited), she assigned it to David and Mary E. McCoy on Dec. 20, 1929, and they mortgaged it the same day to the Waverly Building Association for a $3,120 purchase-money advance on 24 shares, released only on Mar. 15, 1951 (M.L.P. 8386/69). Their 1932 assignment to that lender was very probably in lieu of foreclosure [inference].

The 6-ft right of way to Venable Avenue that the 1936 and July 1941 deeds grant with this lot is not repeated. Recital for both: 'Being the same two lots of ground described in a deed from the Franklin Realty & Finance Co Inc to the parties of the first part dated July 17 1941 and recorded among the land records of Baltimore City in Liber MLP No 6193 folio 218'. Third lot (parcel THIRD): beginning at the corner of the south side of Venable Avenue and the west side of Old York Road; south on Old York Road 49 ft 4 in to the fourth line of the lot Carter Williams and wife leased to Abraham H. Levine et al. (Feb. 23, 1926, S.C.L. 4533/216); west reversely along that line 121 ft to the lease lot's third line; south reversely along it 30 ft 4 in to the sixth line of the lot secondly described in the deed from Alvin J. Irvin et al. to Franklin Realty & Finance Co. Inc. (July 17, 1941, M.L.P. 6187/342); west reversely along part of that line 4 ft to its beginning; north reversely along that parcel's fifth line 30 ft 4 in to its fourth line; west reversely along it 12 ft 10 in to the third line of the lot firstly described in that deed; north reversely along part of that line to its beginning and on along the second line of the Siwinski lot (S.C.L. 5576/60), in all 49 ft, to the south side of Venable Avenue; and east on Venable 143 ft 5 in to the beginning. Recital: 'Being the same lot of ground described in a deed from the Title Holding Company to the parties of the first part herein dated September 30 1941 and recorded among the land records of Baltimore City in Liber MLP No 6222 folio 14'. No ground rent, lease or mortgage is excepted: neither the 1940 Metropolitan Savings Bank mortgage (M.L.P. 6071/98) that the July 1941 Franklin deed was subject to nor the 1926 Starr Lane lease is mentioned. Witness Fannie P. Gellman; acknowledged Nov. 24, 1941 by both grantors before Fannie P. Gellman, notary (commission expires May 3, 1943); recorded Nov. 24, 1941 at 12 o'clock noon, M. Luther Pittman, Clerk (grantee stamp Jan. 5, 1942). What it settles: the Chertkofs' deed to Hudson Realty is at M.L.P. 6244/542, as the grantee index said, not 524; the Chertkofs held FIRST and SECOND by a deed from Franklin Realty & Finance dated July 17, 1941, the same day Franklin took them from the Irvins and Orems (M.L.P. 6187/342), recorded at M.L.P. 6193/218, and held THIRD directly from The Title Holding Company by a deed of Sept. 30, 1941 (M.L.P. 6222/14), not through Siwinski; THIRD is the 49 ft 4 in Old York Road front of the 1922 Frederick lot carried west to the back line of parcel FIRST, plus the 4-ft strip between parcel SECOND and the Starr Lane lot, so it takes in the land under the 6-ft way north to Venable and answers the question the 1936 parcel SECOND deed left open [inference from the calls]; and Siwinski's 32-ft Greenmount corner lies outside all three lots, since THIRD binds on his lot's second line. What it does not settle: the terms of the two 1941 deeds to the Chertkofs (M.L.P. 6193/218 and 6222/14) and what they paid; whether the Metropolitan Savings Bank mortgage was released; and why this deed types the Schwaab line N 84 degrees 34 minutes W and the Siwinski line S 82 degrees 31 minutes E where the 1928 deeds have N 83 degrees 34 minutes W and S 82 degrees 55 minutes E.

Dated Feb. 27, 1928. Maude E. Shorey, widow, and Lillian K. Winbigler and Wilson W. Winbigler her husband, all of Baltimore City, to Samuel H. Adams of the same city and state, for $5 and other good and valuable considerations (no stamps are noted in the margin), 'all that lot of ground' in fee simple, with special warranty: beginning on the east side of Greenmount Avenue 101 ft 9 in north of the northeast corner of Greenmount Avenue and Thirty-third Street, at the end of the first line of the lot the same grantors deeded to Harry W. Schwaab and wife (Dec. 14, 1925, S.C.L. 4507/266, the folio blurred); north on Greenmount 101 ft 7 1/4 in to the first line of the lot thirdly described in the deed from Porter G. Wamsley and wife et al. to George Esselman (June 9, 1922, S.C.L. 3869/529); along that line and along the third line of the lot in the deed from Benedict J. Frederick and wife to Esselman (Sept. 8, 1922, S.C.L. 3905/14) S 82 degrees 55 minutes E 247 ft 4 in to the west side of Old York Road; south on it 49 ft 4 in to the beginning of the Frederick lot; west along that lot's first line 121 ft to the east or third line of the lot George G. Hooper leased to Thomas Johnson (Aug. 12, 1872, Balt. Co. E.H.A. 76/578); south reversely along part of that line 30 ft 4 in to the end of the second line of the lot in the deed from Charles S. Rich et al., trustees, to Esselman (June 30, 1922, S.C.L. 3904/358), in the centre of a 6-ft alley; east along the alley 121 ft to Old York Road; south 18 ft 10 in to the end of the second line of the Schwaab lot; and reversely along that line N 83 degrees 34 minutes W 238 ft 4 1/2 in to the beginning. The calls are those of Adams's two mortgages of March 1, 1928. Title recital, as typed: 'FOR TITLE of the said Maude E.Shorey and Lillian K.Winbigler to the aforesaid property see the following 1.Deed from Porter G.Wamsley et al to George Esselman dated June 9th 1922 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber S.C.L.No.3869 folio 529 2.Deed from Charles S.Rich et al Trustees to George Esselman dated June 20th 1922 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber S.C.L.No.3904 Folio 358 3. Deed from Benedict J.Frederick and wife to George Esselman dated September 8th 1922 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber S.C.L No.3905 folio 14 4.Deed from Charles W.Dames et al to George Esselman dated June 30th 1923 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber S.C.L.No.4039 folio 8[?]' (the folio is interlined and only its first figure can be read; the Rich deed itself is dated June 30, 1922). Then: 'The said George Esselman departed this life on or about December 28th 1923 intestate leaving as his only heirs at law his wife Virginia Esselman and daughter the said Maude E.Shorey The said Virginia Esselman departed this life on or about July 4th 1924 and by her last will and Testament of record in the office of the Register of Wills of Baltimore City and recorded in Wills Liber E.R.D.No.149 folio 438 devised all of her property to her daughter the said Lillian K.Winbigler'. Signed by Maude E. Shorey (witnesses Emma Hemel [?] and Amos S. Hebble [?]) and by Lillian K. and Wilson W. Winbigler (witness Harry Kuszmaul). Acknowledged by the Winbiglers on March 1, 1928 in Baltimore City before Harry Kuszmaul, notary, and by Maude E. Shorey on Feb. 27, 1928 in the Parish of Orleans, Louisiana, before Dorman C. Corkern, notary; recorded March 3, 1928 at 12:12 P.M., Stephen C. Little, Clerk (the grantee stamp reads 'APR 1 1936' as read; the mortgage below it is stamped Apr. 1, 1928). Folio 451 then opens Adams's first mortgage: dated March 1, 1928, Samuel H. Adams, unmarried, to The Mortgage Company of Maryland Incorporated, a Maryland corporation (in the margin 'of Del' is struck through), $25,000 'being a pary [sic] of the purchase money', due in two years at 6 percent payable quarterly in gold coin; so that mortgage begins at folio 451, not before 452 as filed earlier today. What it settles: the 'et al' were Lillian K. Winbigler, who held Virginia Esselman's share under her will, and her husband Wilson W. Winbigler; Esselman's only heirs were his widow and Maude, so Lillian, called Virginia's daughter, was probably Virginia's child by an earlier marriage [inference]; Maude signs as a widow and Miles C. Shorey, who joined the 1925 Schwaab deed, does not join, so he had died by February 1928 [inference]; Maude signed in New Orleans; the heirs' title rested on four Esselman deeds, not three, the fourth a deed of June 30, 1923 from Charles W. 'Dames' (Dawes [inference], the family of the 1866 partition) et al. at S.C.L. 4039, six months before Esselman died; and the deed states no price, so the $32,500 of purchase-money mortgages is the only measure of it. What it does not settle: what the 1923 Dawes deed conveyed (a strip, the 3-ft alley, or a release of old Dawes rights) and its folio; Virginia Esselman's will and any administration of George's estate; and what Adams paid.

Dated Sept. 8, 1922. Benedict J. Frederick and Mary D. Frederick his wife (she signs and acknowledges as Marie D. Frederick), of Baltimore City, to George Esselmann of the same city, for $5 and other good and valuable considerations (one $5 U.S. revenue stamp, about $5,000 at the 1922 rate of 50 cents per $500 [inference]), 'all that lot of ground' in fee simple, with special warranty: beginning on the west side of Old York Road at the northeast corner of lot No. 6 on a plat filed in the case of 'Dames vs Dames' in the Circuit Court of Baltimore County in Equity ('Vide judicial J B 37 folio 1'); west along the north line of lot 6, 120 ft; north, parallel with the York Turnpike Road, 50 ft to the south line of lot No. 4 on the plat; east along the south line of lot 4, 121 ft more or less to the west side of Old York Road; and south along the road 49 ft 4 in to the beginning, 'the improvements whereon are known as Nos 136-138 and 140 Old York Road or Starr Lane'. Title recital: 'BEING or intending to be the same lot of ground described in a Deed from The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County to Edward L Raborg and Benedict J Frederick dated September 24th 1915 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber S C L 3001 folio 545 etc SEE also Deed from Charles S Rich and Edward N Rich Trustees to the said Benedict J Frederick dated July 8th 1921 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber S C L 3757 folio 5' (the second figure of 3001 is blurred). Conveyed 'subject however to the legal operation and effect of a Mortgage from Benedict J Frederick to the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County dated July 8th 1921 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber S C L No 3757 folio 6'. No ground rent is reserved or recited. Witness Susie W. Marshall; acknowledged Sept. 8, 1922 by both grantors before Susie W. Marshall, notary; recorded Sept. 8, 1922 at 2:30 P.M., Stephen C. Little, Clerk, the same day as the Rich trustees' deed (9:30 A.M.); grantee stamp Oct. 11, 1922; the clerk's margin says 'Unlocated'. No Esselmann mortgage follows it. What it settles: 'Frederick' is Benedict J. Frederick, and his lot is the Venable Avenue and Old York Road corner, 49 ft 4 in on Old York Road by about 121 ft, the core of parcel THIRD, then improved as 136 to 140 Old York Road (Starr Lane), just north of the Starr Lane lot, No. 134; it lay between lots 4 and 6 of a Dawes partition plat, so it was presumably lot 5, and the northeast corner of lot 6 is the northeast corner of the 1866 Bucher lot, where the Starr Lane lot begins [inference]; the south line of lot 4 is the line the 1928 deeds run along to Old York Road, later the south side of Venable Avenue [inference]; Edward L. Raborg co-owned the lot with Frederick from 1915, and Raborg's trustees, the same Rich trustees who sold Esselmann the lot south of the alley, deeded his share to Frederick in 1921; Esselmann took subject to Frederick's 1921 building association mortgage; and the citation 'S.C.L. 2905/14' in the Title Holding deed is a slip for 3905/14. What it does not settle: the Waverly Building Association's own title in 1915 (S.C.L. 3001 [?]/545); the 1921 Rich trustees' deed and Frederick's mortgage (S.C.L. 3757/5 and /6) and the mortgage's release; the 'Dames vs Dames' plat itself; and the price beyond the stamp.

summary: Deed of assignment by a mortgagee (captioned 'David Stewart & Wife, Asst to John H. C. Legg'), Baltimore City land records, Liber J.B. No. 1289, folios 297 to 299 (MSA CE 168-1297; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, at 130, 260 and 300 dpi). Dated Apr. 23, 1890, between David Stewart and Alice Gerry Stewart his wife, mortgagee, and John H. C. Legg, all of Baltimore City. Recital, quoted: 'Whereas by virtue of a power of sale contained in a Mortgage from James E. Sinclair and Sarah C. Sinclair to David Stewart dated February 1st 1888 and recorded among the land records of Baltimore County in Liber J.W.S. No 135 folio 275 said Stewart having first entered a suit in the circuit Court of Baltimore City entitled David Stewart vs James E. Sinclair and Sarah C. Sinclair and filed said Mortgage with a plat and description of the property and having also duly advertised did on April 8th 1890 sell to John H. C. Legg the lots hereinafter described for an aggregate amount of $750.' The sale was reported to the court and 'ratified nisi', and Legg paid the $750. For the premises and $1, Stewart as mortgagee 'by virtue of all powers in him in any way vested', with his wife, grants, assigns and conveys to Legg 'all those six lots of ground lying at Waverly in Baltimore City'. (1) The apex at the corner of the northeast side of Merryman's Lane and the west side of the York Turnpike, 36 ft 1/2 in on the turnpike, 42 ft back through a division wall, 55 ft on the lane, held under Robert Riddell Brown's lease to Sinclair of June 14, 1887 (J.W.S. 162/71), rent $60 payable June 14 and December 14, redeemable after fifteen years at 4 1/2 percent. (2) A lot on the southwest side of the lane beginning 7 ft 8 1/2 in northwest of the turnpike, 102 ft 6 in on the lane, held under David Stewart's lease to Sarah C. Sinclair of May 28, 1887 (J.W.S. 160/403), rent figure blotted, payable March and September, redeemable after five years at 6 percent. (3) A lot on the west side of the turnpike from 96 ft 1/2 in to 132 ft 8 in north of the lane, 100 ft deep to the three-foot alley, bounding north on 'the lot leased by Alice P. Harris and husband', part of the ground Sinclair held in fee from Oliver P. Merryman and wife (Apr. 25, 1884, W.M.I. 141/404) and by a deed of Sept. 25, 1886 (J.W.S. 155/465). (4) A lot on the northeast side of the lane west of the alley, 72 ft 4 in on the lane to 'McAverney's [?] line', 55 by 63 ft 8 1/4 in at the back, part of the same Merryman ground in fee. (5) 'Beginning for the fifth at a point on the West side of the York Turnpike Road distant one hundred and thirty two feet and eight inches Northerly from the intersection of the Northeast side of Merryman's Lane and the West side of said Road and running thence Northerly sixty four feet and four inches by an even depth of one hundred feet to a three foot alley comprising all those four lots of ground leased by David Stewart to James E. Sinclair and Sarah C. Sinclair by deed dated February 1st 1888 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County in Liber J.W.S. No 167 folio 402 &c (Being subject to an aggregate rent of $252 per annum payable February and August and redeemable after fifteen years at six per cent).' (6) A lot on the southwest side of the lane west of the alley line, 97 ft by 75 ft 6 in to 'the Western outline of all of Sinclair's original property', 'intended to be leased' by Robert Riddell Brown to Sinclair by deed of Dec. 22, 1887 (J.W.S. 167/165), rent $50 payable June 22 and December 22, redeemable after fifteen years at 5 percent. The first four lots were also subject to 'a Mortgage for $3,500 [?] to Alice Gerry Stewart' (the first figure may be a 2). Habendum to Legg 'absolutely, subject only as to the leasehold lots to the payment of the annual rents created by said leases and as to the Mortgaged lots to the payment of said Mortgage'; special warranty and further assurances. Witness Robert A. Thursby [?], justice of the peace for Baltimore City, before whom 'David Stewart Mortgagee and Alice Gerry Stewart his wife' acknowledged on Apr. 23, 1890; received for record Apr. 24, 1890 at 12:35 P.M. and recorded the same day (Jas. Bond, Clerk). A pencilled sum at the head of folio 299, 132 plus 64 making 197, checks the fifth lot's footage. What it settles: 3224, the fourth lot of the 1888 sub-lease (181 to 197 ft north of the lane), lies inside the fifth lot here, so the Sinclairs' leasehold on 3224 passed to Legg by this deed. The 1888 sub-lease was cleared by foreclosure of the Sinclairs' own mortgage to Stewart, dated Feb. 1, 1888 like the sub-lease, under its power of sale, with the sale reported to and ratified nisi by the Circuit Court of Baltimore City. The deed names no insolvency trustee, so Sinclair's March 1890 insolvency was not the route, or not the recorded one. Legg paid $750 for all six equities, which remained subject to the ground rents (the $252 sub-rents on the four lots among them) and, on lots 1 to 4, the mortgage to Alice Gerry Stewart. What it does not settle: the mortgage itself (J.W.S. 135/275, not pulled), the court papers and the plat filed with them, the mortgage to Alice Gerry Stewart and its exact sum, the rent on the second lot, and whether Sinclair's insolvency trustee (Winfield J. Taylor) joined in or released the sale. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (batch 4): J.W.S. 135/275 read (768:mdlr-jws135-275-sinclair-stewart-mortgage-1000-1888). The mortgage of Feb. 1, 1888 (recorded Feb. 9) secures a $1,000 interest-free note at six months, extendable six months, on all the Sinclairs' property at or near Waverly, real, leasehold and personal, 'especially the premises on the South West corner of Merrymans Lane and the York Turnpike Road and the Machinery thereupon and the lots on the York Road North of Merrymans Lane and the lots on the North and South sides of Merrymans Lane West of the York Road', with no bounds; the power of sale runs to Stewart 'or Robert Riddell Brown his attorney or agent' on twenty days' notice in a Baltimore County newspaper. That is why a plat and description had to be filed with the 1890 suit [inference]. No release is noted. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (J.W.S. 162 read): the rent days the lease itself gives are June 1 and December 1 (J.W.S. 162/71, read: 'accounting from the first day of June'); the June 14 and December 14 in this deed are a slip that took the lease's date. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (J.B. 1292/384 read): the six lots' next step is read (768:mdlr-jb1292-384-legg-stewart-five-lots-1890): on Apr. 26, 1890 Legg conveyed lots 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 back to David Stewart, lot 3 enlarged by the three southern sub-lots of lot 5, keeping out only the Drechsler lot. The blotted rent on lot 2 is $80 (J.W.S. 160/403, payable March and September, redeemable after five years at 6 percent). The deed does not mention the mortgage to Alice Gerry Stewart.

summary: Deed in fee simple, Baltimore City land records, Liber J.B. No. 1289, folios 299 to 300 (MSA CE 168-1297; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, at 130, 260 and 300 dpi). Dated Apr. 23, 1890. For $4,200, David Stewart and Alice Gerry Stewart his wife 'do hereby grant and convey unto the said John H. C. Legg in fee simple All those four lots of ground adjoining each other and lying in Baltimore County (now Baltimore City) on the West side of the York Turnpike Road North of Merryman's Lane and particularly described in a lease from said Stewart and wife to Sarah C. Sinclair and husband dated February first A.D. 1888 and duly recorded among the land records of Baltimore County in Liber J.W.S. No 167 folio 402 &c the first of said lots having issuing from it a ground rent of thirty six dollars a year the second a ground rent of eighty seven dollars a year the third a ground rent of eighty one dollars a year and the fourth a ground rent of forty eight dollars a year all said rents being created by said lease all being payable February and August and all being redeemable at five per cent after February 1st 1893 and at six per cent between February 1st 1903 and February 1st 1904 (See deed from Alice P. Harris to David Stewart dated January 25th 1890 and recorded among the land records of Baltimore City in Liber J.B. No 1276 folio 42 &c)'. With the improvements, ways, alleys and privileges. Habendum to Legg, his heirs and assigns, 'absolutely in fee simple said Legg having prior hereto acquired title to the leasehold of said lots'. Special warranty and further assurances. Witness Robert A. Thursby [?], justice of the peace for Baltimore City, before whom both grantors acknowledged on Apr. 23, 1890; received for record Apr. 24, 1890 at 12:25 [?] P.M. and recorded the same day (Jas. Bond, Clerk). A margin note reads 'D Stewart, Sept 13 [?] 1890', probably the delivery of the recorded deed. The next deed on folios 300 and 301, Lucy C. and Benjamin R. George of Franklin County, Pennsylvania, to the same John H. C. Legg (Apr. 18, 1890, $1,200, recorded Apr. 24), is the reversion of the apex lot under the 1887 Brown lease, not 3224. What it settles: this is the fee deed for 3224, the fourth lot with its $48 rent. Stewart's title is recited: a deed from Alice P. Harris to him dated Jan. 25, 1890, recorded in Baltimore City at J.B. 1276/42, which closes the gap between the 1884 Harris lease and Stewart's 1890 sale. Legg had bought the Sinclairs' leasehold at the Apr. 8, 1890 foreclosure sale (J.B. 1289/297), so with this deed he held both the fee and the leasehold of the four lots, and the 1884 lease and 1888 sub-lease ended in his hands [inference; neither deed uses the word merger]. The price is exactly the four rents ($252 a year) capitalized at 6 percent, and Legg's $800 reversion deed of the $48 lot to Helen Stewart Ridgely, Stewart's sister (J.B. 1289/565), is the $48 rent at the same rate, which fits Legg acting as a conveyancing intermediary for the Stewart family when the rents were re-created on fresh leases such as the Drechsler lease (J.B. 1299/406) [inference]. Legg's initials are H. C. throughout this deed and the one before it. What it does not settle: the Harris deed itself (J.B. 1276/42, probably MSA CE 168-1284 by the offset of the J.B. libers in that series [inference]), why it names Alice P. Harris alone, and what Legg paid Stewart in fact if he was an intermediary. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (batch 3): J.B. 1276/42 read (768:mdlr-jb1276-42-harris-stewart-redemption-fee-two-lots-1890). The Harris deed of Jan. 25, 1890 is made by Alice Patterson Harris and W. Hall Harris her husband (the caption names Alice alone). It is a redemption: Stewart, holding the 1884 leasehold by the Sinclairs' assignment of Jan. 3, 1888 (J.W.S. 167/243), paid $2,680.66 and accrued rent, the $80 and $80.84 rents capitalized at 6 percent, for the fee of the two lots (132 ft 8 in to 197 ft north of Merryman's Lane) 'free and discharged from the operations of said Lease'. Recorded Jan. 25, 1890 at 12:55 P.M. and delivered to Stewart Jan. 27.

summary: Index lines, Baltimore County Circuit Court land records, Index 18 (surnames S, given names J), pages 57 to 59 (MSA CE 35-18; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, at 130 and 300 dpi). The pages run by date of record from Oct. 19, 1887 to Mar. 31, 1888. Page 57 (Oct. 19 to Dec. 20, 1887) and page 59 (Feb. 14 to Mar. 31, 1888) have no Sinclair line. Page 58 has seven lines for 'Sinclair, James E.': (1) Dec. 28, 1887, with wife, to Robert Riddell Brown, deed, 167/164; (2) Dec. 28, 1887, from Robert R. Brown, lease, 167/165; (3) Dec. 28, 1887, from Lennox [?] Birckhead, release, 117/372; (4) Jan. 4, 1888, with wife, to David Stewart, assignment, 167/243; (5) Jan. 23, 1888, from the Waverly Building Association, release, 136/94; (6) Feb. 2, 1888, with wife, from David Stewart, lease, 167/402; (7) Feb. 9, 1888, with wife, to David Stewart, mortgage, 135/275. Deeds, leases and assignments on these pages fall in the J.W.S. deed series (165 to 169); mortgages and releases in a separate series (78 to 136). Lines indexed under Sarah E. or Sarah C. Sinclair would be on other pages. What it settles: the Sinclair-to-Stewart assignment of the 1884 Harris leasehold, recited without a liber in the 1888 sub-lease, is J.W.S. 167/243, recorded Jan. 4, 1888 (the recital dates it about Jan. 3), and not at J.W.S. 167/397 to 401, where it was sought on Oct. 14. Line (6) is the sub-lease itself, recorded Feb. 2, 1888 as folio 407 says. Line (7) is the mortgage dated Feb. 1, 1888 that J.B. 1289/297 recites, whose foreclosure sale of Apr. 8, 1890 to John H. C. Legg cleared the sub-lease. Lines (1) and (2) are the sixth lot of that foreclosure: the Dec. 22, 1887 Brown lease (J.W.S. 167/165) on the southwest side of Merryman's Lane, which on its consecutive folio follows a Sinclair deed to Brown, a sale and lease-back [inference]. What it does not settle: the assignment (J.W.S. 167/243, MSA CE 62-167) and the mortgage (135/275) themselves, neither pulled, and the mortgage to Alice Gerry Stewart recited in 1890. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (batch 3): J.W.S. 167/243 read (768:mdlr-jws167-243-sinclair-stewart-assignment-harris-leasehold-1888). Line (4) is the assignment by Sarah C. and James E. Sinclair to David Stewart, dated Jan. 3 and recorded Jan. 4, 1888 at 8:30 a.m., for $1,500, of the two lots of the 1884 Harris lease (W.M.I. 141/407), 64 ft 4 in on the turnpike, subject to that lease and to a mortgage to the Waverly Building Association; line (5), the Waverly Building Association release of Jan. 23, 1888 (136/94), probably clears that mortgage [inference]. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (batch 4): J.W.S. 135/275 read (768:mdlr-jws135-275-sinclair-stewart-mortgage-1000-1888). Line (7) is the Sinclairs' $1,000 blanket mortgage to David Stewart, dated Feb. 1 and acknowledged Feb. 7, 1888, 'Recorded Feby 9th 1888 @ 8.30 A.M.', as indexed; it is in the County mortgage series (MSA CE 221-135), folios 275 to 278.

Treadway, deed, 39/499 (J.H.L.); (4) July 24, 1865, John alone to John G. Blum, sub-lease, 45/362 (J.H.L.); (5) Oct. 4, 1865, from O. P. Merryman and wife, deed, 46/149 (J.H.L.); (6) Nov. 25, 1865, John and wife to Jacob Aull, deed, 46/520 (J.H.L.); (7) May 14, 1866, John and wife to John H. White, lease, 48/502 (J.H.L.); (8) April 6, 1871, John and wife to Catherine E. Blum, deed, 70/80 (E.H.A.). No mortgage, release or assignment is indexed to or from him, and no line names his heirs, executors or administrators. Two damaged lines on page 276 (Nov. 1854, a John taking a deed from Benjamin A. Lavender and wife, No. 10/41, and a John and wife leasing to Lavender and wife, 10/44) have an illegible, shorter surname and are not counted. What it settles: these eight are John Litzinger's recorded dealings under his own name from December 1851 to May 20, 1874, all in the deed series. Lines 5 and 7 confirm by date and number the two citations already known, Merryman's 1865 deed of the fee of the 2 15/16-acre Huntington leasehold (J.H.L. 46/149) and the 1866 half-acre lease to John H. White (J.H.L. 48/502), which also fixes the clerk letters for the 1864 to 1866 numbers. The July 1865 sub-lease to John G. Blum shows he still held the Huntington leasehold between the York Turnpike and the Old York Road that summer and let part of it before he bought the fee. Seven weeks after buying the fee he and his wife deeded ground to Jacob Aull (J.H.L. 46/520), the likeliest root of the lots between the two roads that Jacob H. Aull conveyed to Augustus D. Clemens Jr. in 1898 (R.O. 1739/295), the 3011 lot among them [inference]; the 1871 deed to Catherine E. Blum likely passed the fee under the 1865 Blum sub-lease [inference]. He and his wife joined in a deed recorded April 6, 1871, so he was living at or shortly before that date, and no estate conveyance is indexed under his name through May 20, 1874. What it does not settle: the index gives no descriptions, so whether the 1852 Horne deed, the 1854 Bucher deed or the 1864 Treadway deed touch the fork wedge of Ensor's Inspection or the leasehold is unknown until H.M.F. 3/165, H.M.F. 7/347 and J.H.L. 39/499 are read, and the Aull and Blum instruments (J.H.L. 46/520, J.H.L. 45/362, E.H.A. 70/80) still have to be read to tie them to 3011-3013. Lines indexed under his wife Elizabeth alone would sit in the E given-name section of this volume, which these scans do not cover. The lot John Litzinger bought from Henry N. Bowerman, Walter T. Allender, Jacob Hoke and Henry Hammond, recited in E.H.A. 67/488 (1870), has no line here, so it was recorded before December 1851 or is indexed elsewhere. His death and any administration after May 1874 need the next index volume or the Orphans' Court records. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (Litzinger deeds): all six deeds are read. Horne 1852 (3/165) is 'Solomons Chance' near Hereford, not Waverly; Bucher 1853 (7/347) is the Ensor's Inspection lot beside St. John's Church; Treadway 1864 (G.H.C. 39/499) is the parent lot of 3011 to 3019 (the 1847 wedge plus the 1841 Stump land, T.K. 315/188); Aull 1865 (46/520) is the north 260 ft of the Huntington leasehold, merging his 1847 sub-lease (A.W.B. 388/79), so it is not the root of the 1898 Aull-to-Clemens lots (the inference above is superseded); the Blum sub-lease (45/362) and the 1871 deed to Catharine E. Blum (70/80) are the half-acre next north of 3117.

summary: Deed of assignment (margin 'Assgnt'), Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 2390, folios 331 to 332 (MSA CE 168-2398; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 331 to 335, at 130 and 300 dpi; the two mortgages of even date follow on folios 332 to 335 and are filed separately). Dated December 9, 1907. Augustus D. Clemens Junior of Baltimore City, for $5 and other valuable considerations, grants and conveys to John H. Dietrich of Baltimore City, his personal representatives and assigns, a lot (Block 4076) on the east side of the York Turnpike Road beginning 125 ft 6 in north of the beginning of the land Samuel H. Tagart, trustee, assigned to George C. H. Coffield by deed of January 31, 1865 (Balt. Co. J.H.L. 43/548), the beginning being 'designed to be' where a line drawn west from a point four feet north of the north side of the two-story house on the lot next south meets the turnpike; N 2 E 79 ft along the road to a post at the north-west corner of the whole Coffield tract, S 85 1/2 E 140 ft 6 in to a post on the west side of the Old York Road, S 19 1/2 W 78 ft 6 in along it to a post, N 86 1/4 W 119 ft to the beginning. Title recital: 'Being and comprising the same lot of ground and premises described and conveyed in a Deed dated March 15th 1898 recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber R.O. No 1725 folio 22 &c. from John S. Ensor to said Augustus D. Clemens Jr.' For the rest of the term with renewal forever, subject to the annual rent of $150, half-yearly on March 1 and September 1, 'Subject also to the operation of a Sub Lease from Charles Hamilton to Henry C. Zoll of the Northernmost thirty five feet of said lot dated March 17th 1891' and recorded in Liber J.B. No. 1338 folio 248, which reserved an annual sub-rent of $175, half-yearly on March 1 and September 1, 'but with the right to collect said Annual Sub rent'. Special warranty. Witness Lennox B. Clemens; acknowledged December 9, 1907 before Lennox B. Clemens, notary public for Baltimore County; recorded December 9, 1907 at 2:46 P.M. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). What it settles: Clemens Jr. held the whole 79 ft leasehold under the 1868 $150 rent by deed of John S. Ensor of March 15, 1898 (R.O. 1725/22), not through the 1904 Hershey trustee's sale. The '$175 ground rent' of the 1904 sale notice for the stable lot at 1027 York Road is the 1891 Hamilton-to-Zoll sub-rent on the northernmost 35 ft, which is 3117, so the 1904 sale was of Zoll's 35 ft sub-leasehold (an inference from the matching lot and rent), and Charles Hamilton still held the 79 ft leasehold in March 1891. Dietrich took the whole lot with the right to the $175 sub-rent; his building-association mortgage of the same day (S.C.L. 2390/332) shows he already held the 35 ft sub-leasehold by a deed of January 31, 1905 from W. Frank Tucker and others, receivers (R.O. 2123/235), and merged it here. So the Dietrichs were at 3117 from 1905, not about 1920. What it does not settle: how John S. Ensor came to hold the leasehold between Hamilton (1891) and 1898; whose receivers Tucker and the others were and whether their 1905 deed carries out the 1904 Hershey sale; and the price, since the deed states $5 (the two purchase-money mortgages of the same day total $4,100, so the price was very probably at least that; an inference).

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 2390, folios 332 to 334 (MSA CE 168-2398; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 331 to 335, at 130 and 300 dpi). Dated December 9, 1907. John H. Dietrich of Baltimore City, a member of the Loyola Perpetual Building Association of Baltimore City, having received an advance of $2,500 on twenty shares, mortgages to the association for $1 the 3117 lot (125 ft 6 in north of the beginning of the land Tagart, trustee, assigned to Coffield, J.H.L. 43/548; 79 ft on the turnpike; 140 ft 6 in east to the Old York Road; 78 ft 6 in on it; 119 ft back), 'Being the same lot described in a deed from Augustus D. Clemens Jr to said John H. Dietrich dated of even date herewith and intended to be recorded prior hereto See also deed from W. Frank Tucker et al Receivers to said John H. Dietrich dated 31 January 1905 and recorded among the land records of said City in liber R.O. No 2123 folio 235 &c. It being the intention of these presents to merge the Subleasehold interest and convey the same subject to the original ground rent of $150', the advance being 'in part the purchase money for said lot'. Leasehold for the rest of the term with renewal forever, subject to the $150 rent. Dues of 25 cents a share a week and 15 cents a share a week as interest until the shares mature; fire insurance of at least $2,500; possession until default; assent to a decree under Chapter 123, sections 720 to 732, of the Laws of 1898. Witness Lennox B. Clemens; acknowledged December 9, 1907 before Lennox B. Clemens, notary public for Baltimore County, William J. Donnelly, president, making oath to the consideration; recorded December 9, 1907 at 2:47 P.M. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Margin stamp: released January 13, 1928, Liber 4835 folio 513. What it settles: Dietrich already held a sub-leasehold in the lot by deed of January 31, 1905 from W. Frank Tucker and others, receivers (R.O. 2123/235), and the 1907 purchase was meant to merge it into the whole 79 ft leasehold, leaving only the $150 rent; read with the Clemens deed, which conveys the lot subject to the Hamilton-to-Zoll sub-lease of the north 35 ft, that sub-leasehold is very probably Zoll's 35 ft stable lot, 3117 (an inference). The release of January 13, 1928 cleared the lot seven weeks before Lula S. Dietrich's sub-lease to Miller Brothers (S.C.L. 4854/321). What it does not settle: whose receivers Tucker and the others were and what the 1905 deed recites; R.O. 2123/235 is not read. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 3): the 1905 deed is read (R.O. 2123/235, 742:mdlr-ro2123-235-equitable-receivers-dietrich-35ft-1905): W. Frank Tucker and Elmer J. Cook, receivers of the Equitable Building Loan and Investment Association of Baltimore City, sold John H. Dietrich Zoll's 35 ft for $300, subject to the $175 rent; Omer F. Hershey, trustee in their foreclosure suit against Henry C. Zoll (Circuit Court No. 2, 1903), had sold it to the receivers for $500 and deeded it Oct. 29, 1904. So the 1904 Hershey sale ends in this deed.

Dated December 9, 1907. John H. Dietrich of the City of Baltimore to Augustus D. Clemens Junior of Baltimore County, for $1, to secure $1,600 'being part purchase money for the property hereinafter described', by a promissory note of even date payable five years after date with interest at 6 percent half-yearly, prepayable at any time before default. summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 3311, folios 297 to 298 (MSA CE 168-3319; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 297 to 301, at 130 and 300 dpi; folio 297 opens with the end of an unrelated mortgage recorded at 12:43 P.M., and folios 298 to 301 hold Holmes's lease of five Limond Place lots to Helen M. Bordley and the opening of his deed to Joshua Ridgely and others). Dated February 7, 1919. Bertha F. Kiel and Samuel F. A. Kiel her husband, and Estella F. Himmelmann and Sigmund Himmelmann her husband, all of Baltimore City, for $5 and other good and valuable considerations, grant and convey to W. Harry Holmes of Baltimore City, his heirs and assigns, in fee simple, two lots. First: on the west side of Limond Place where it meets the N 89 1/4 E 240 1/2 ft line of the whole parcel, 69 ft more or less south of the south-west corner of Limond Place and Thirtieth Street; south 89 ft 2 1/2 in on Limond Place to the N 87 1/4 W 222 1/2 ft line of the whole parcel, west 71 ft on it to a 10-ft alley, north 78 ft 6 in on the alley, east 86 ft to the beginning. Second (3013): on the east side of Greenmount Avenue (formerly the York Turnpike Road) 190 ft 7 in south of the two-mile stone on the east side of the avenue 'in part of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot', and 267 ft 2 in south of the north side of a four-foot alley called Batemans Alley; south 14 ft on the avenue, east at right angles 42 ft 4 in to the westernmost side of the Old York Road, north-east 15 ft 2 1/2 in on it, west 48 ft 3 in by a straight line to the beginning. Title recital: 'For Title See Last Will and Testament of William L Fink dated February 2nd 1893 and recorded in the office of the Register of Wills in Wills Record S.R.M. No 82 folio 278 &c Also Deed from Mary K Fink to Estella F Himmelmann and husband dated May 1st 1917 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber S.C.L. No 3126 folio 290 &c Also Deed from Frederick Fink and wife to Mary C Fink Bertha F Kiel and Estella Fink dated February 9th 1910 and recorded among the aforesaid Land Records in Liber S.C.L. No 2559 folio 393 &c'. Special warranty. Signed Bertha F. Kiel, Saml. F. A. Kiel, Estella F. Himmelmann and Sigmund Himmelmann; witness Lennox B. Clemens; acknowledged February 7, 1919 before Lennox B. Clemens, notary public for Baltimore County; recorded February 8, 1919 at 12:50 P.M. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Revenue stamps of $7.50. The family name is spelled 'Kiel' throughout the deed, as in the index; Corridor has used 'Keil'. What it settles: the 'others' are Bertha's husband Samuel F. A. Kiel and Estella F. Himmelmann (born Fink, unmarried in 1910) with her husband Sigmund. The 3013 lot passed from William L. Fink by his will dated February 2, 1893 (Wills S.R.M. 82/278), so the grantee of the 1898 Clemens deed (R.O. 1729/241) was dead before February 1919 and is not the William L. Fink who died in 1946 (estate OLD45631); then by a 1910 deed of Frederick Fink and wife to Mary C. (written 'Mary K.' in the 1917 citation) Fink, Bertha F. Kiel and Estella Fink (S.C.L. 2559/393) and Mary K. Fink's 1917 deed to the Himmelmanns (S.C.L. 3126/290). 3013 was fee simple in 1919. At the stamp rate of 50 cents per $500, the stamps point to a price of about $7,000 to $7,500 for both lots (an inference). The other lot is on Limond Place: Holmes leased it in five lots to Helen M. Bordley the same day (S.C.L. 3311/298 to 301, read: 99 years renewable, $36 a year on each lot from February 1, 1919, 'a part of the first lot' of this deed) and she assigned the five leaseholds to Holmes and Lennox B. Clemens (S.C.L. 3311/309). What it does not settle: William L. Fink's date of death and the terms of the devise (the will is not read); what interest Frederick Fink conveyed in 1910; how Mary, Bertha, Estella and Frederick were related to William (very probably his widow and children; an inference; a Bertha Fink kept the 1005 York Road store from 1901 to 1904); and the folio order, since Holmes's deed of 3013 to James M. Sinclair is cited in Corridor at S.C.L. 3311/260, 37 folios before this deed, which was recorded at 12:50 P.M. on February 8, 1919 (check the recording time on 3311/260). Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Fink deeds S.C.L. 2559/393 and 3126/290 read): the 1910 and 1917 deeds behind this recital are read. Frederick Fink and wife conveyed all their interest in four lots (3013 the first) to Mary Catherine Fink, Bertha Kiel and Estella Fink as tenants in common on Feb. 9, 1910 (720:mdlr-scl2559-393-frederick-fink-mary-catherine-bertha-estella-four-lots-3013-1910), under William L. Fink's will of Feb. 2, 1893 (Wills S.R.M. 82/278), which left the residue to his wife Louisa for life or widowhood and then to his four children, Mary Catherine, Bertha, Frederick and Estella. So the grantors here are his daughters (Bertha and Estella and their husbands) and the 'Mary K Fink' of the 1917 recital is Mary Catherine Fink, who conveyed her undivided third of 3013 and five Limond Place lots (2922 to 2930) to the Himmelmanns on May 1, 1917 (S.C.L. 3126/290, 720:mdlr-scl3126-290-mary-catherine-fink-himmelmann-3013-and-five-limond-place-lots-1917); she is not a 1919 grantor because she had sold out. The 3013 lot was described in 1917 as '3013 York Road (formerly 1005)'. The 'first lot' of this deed is the Limond Place ground, which came by the County deed of 1887 (J.W.S. 167/484), not 3013's. Still open: William L. Fink's date of death and the will itself, and the 1914 division of the sisters' shares (S.C.L. 2883/370 and 371).

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. No. 6193, folios 218 to 220 (MSA CE 168-6201; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 218 to 222, at 130 and 300 dpi; folio 218 opens with the end of a Silberman deed and a 1918 Freeman-to-Freeman deed on St. Paul Street, and folios 220 to 222 go on to an O'Neill mortgage to the Kenwood Building Loan and Savings Association on 3111 Abell Avenue and the opening of Stella M. Levine's deed as administratrix to John Kaplan, M.L.P. 6193/222, read October 14; only the Franklin deed is about 3313). Dated July 17, 1941. Franklin Realty & Finance Co. Inc., a Maryland corporation, to David W. Chertkof and his wife, of Baltimore City, as tenants by the entireties, for $5 and other good and valuable considerations, 'all those two lots of ground' in fee simple, with special warranty. The wife's given name is left blank ('David W Chertkof and_Chertkof his wife'); the index line reads 'David W Chertkof &c'. Margin stamps '1-50¢1-5¢ USS Can' (55 cents) and '1-50¢ MdS Can' (50 cents), the same minimum stamps as the $500 Levine-to-Kaplan deed on folio 222, so the price was $500 or less [inference]. The deed is executed for Franklin 'by the hand of David W Chertkof its President', so Chertkof conveyed as the company's president to himself and his wife. First lot (parcel FIRST): beginning on the east side of Greenmount Avenue 101 ft 9 in north of the northeast corner of Greenmount Avenue and Thirty-third Street, at the end of the first line of the lot Maude E. Shorey widow et al. deeded to Harry W. Schwaab and wife (Dec. 14, 1925, S.C.L. 4507/266); north on Greenmount 69 ft 7 1/4 in to the end of the third line of the lot in the deed of Nov. 1, 1935 from Irving J. Orem et al. to George W. Siwinski (S.C.L. 5576/60); reversely along that line S 82 degrees 31 minutes E 103 ft 11 in to its end; S 0 degrees 28 minutes E, parallel to Greenmount, 68 ft 4 1/2 in to the second line of the Schwaab lot; and reversely along part of that line N 84 degrees 34 minutes W 103 ft 11 in to the beginning. Second lot (parcel SECOND): beginning on the west side of Old York Road 79 ft 8 in south of the corner of Old York Road and the south side of Venable Avenue, 'intended to be at the beginning of the seventh line' of the Adams-to-Title Holding lot (March 1, 1928, S.C.L. 4853/457); south on Old York Road 18 ft 10 in to the end of the seventh line; west along part of the eighth line 134 ft 5 1/2 in to the easternmost outline of the Title Holding-to-Irvin lot (July 21, 1933, S.C.L. 5368/38); north along it 49 ft 2 in to where the westward prolongation of the Adams lot's fourth line would cut it; east along that prolongation 12 ft 10 in to a point 4 ft west of the end of the fourth line; south, parallel with and 4 ft west of the fifth line, 30 ft 4 in to the prolongation of the sixth line; and east to and along the sixth line and 'the centre of an alley six feet wide' 125 ft to the beginning. Together with the right to use, in common with The Title Holding Company, its successors and assigns, a strip 6 ft wide from the fourth line of the second lot north to Venable Avenue, its west side on the easternmost outline of the 1933 Irvin lot. Title recital, for both lots: 'BEING the same two lots of ground described in a deed from Alvan J Irvin and wife et al to the party of the first part dated the _ day of July 1941 and recorded or intended to be recorded among the land records of Baltimore City prior hereto' (the day is left blank, no liber or folio is given, and 'Alvan' is underlined in the record). Conveyed 'subject however to the legal operation and effect of the mortgage from Alvan J Irvin and wife et al to the Metropolitan Savings Bank of Baltimore dated August 22 1940 and recorded among the land records of Baltimore City in Liber M L P No 6071 folio 98 which mortgage the grantees herein do not assume or covenant to pay or to perform any of the covenants and provisions therein' ('do not' interlined). Witness Fannie P. Gellman; corporate seal 'Franklin Realty & Finance Co Balto'; acknowledged July 17, 1941 by David W. Chertkof as President before Fannie P. Gellman, notary (commission expires May 3, 1943); recorded July 30, 1941 at 12 o'clock noon, M. Luther Pittman, Clerk; grantee stamp Sept. 19, 1941. What it settles: the deed by which the Chertkofs held FIRST and SECOND is at M.L.P. 6193/218, as the November 1941 Hudson Realty deed recites; it was made the same day as the Irvins' and Orems' deed to Franklin and cites that deed without a liber because it was not yet recorded; at the minimum stamps it moved the two lots from the family company to David W. and his wife for little or nothing, with Chertkof signing for the grantor [inference]; the lots passed still subject to the 1940 Metropolitan Savings Bank mortgage, which the couple did not assume; the 6-ft way north to Venable Avenue is granted again here, so the Hudson deed is the first to drop it; and the two bearings in the Hudson deed that differ from the 1928 deeds (S 82 degrees 31 minutes E and N 84 degrees 34 minutes W) already stand here, so the Hudson deed copied them from this deed. What it does not settle: whether the bearings began in the Irvin-to-Franklin deed (M.L.P. 6187/342); what, if anything, the couple paid Franklin beyond the stamps; whether and when the 1940 Metropolitan Savings Bank mortgage (M.L.P. 6071/98) was released, since the Hudson deed four months later does not mention it; and Mrs. Chertkof's name, which this deed leaves blank.

summary: Deed of reversion, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. No. 6549, folios 594 to 595 (MSA CE 168-6557; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 594 to 598 and the plat at 598a, at 130 and 300 dpi; folio 594 opens with the end of an instrument acknowledged before Ernest F. Tillson and a Baltimore Federal Savings and Loan release to John Schmidt of John, and folios 595 to 598a go on to an Isler mortgage on East Chase, Madison and Eager Street houses, a Garrison Lane Building and Savings Association release, a Logsdon-to-Gugerty rent deed on 3014 Abell Avenue and a Canton Company deed and plat for Poncabird Pass, none about 3030). Margin heading 'Charles T Leight &c, Deed of Reversion to Nicholas Interrante &c'. Dated Jan. 7, 1944 (recorded Jan. 11, the date in the grantee index). Charles T. Leight and Ella B. Leight his wife, of Baltimore City, to Nicholas Interrante and Ida H. Interrante his wife, of the same, as tenants by the entireties, 'in consideration of the sum of Eleven hundred dollars and accrued rent to the date hereof', in fee simple, with special warranty. Margin stamps '1-$1 1-40¢ 1-25¢ USS Can' ($1.65, three units of 55 cents) and '1-$1 1-10¢ MDS Can' ($1.10), both consistent with $1,100 [inference]. The lot: beginning on the west side of Greenmount Avenue 29 ft north of the corner of the west side of Greenmount Avenue and the north side of 'Vineyard Lane formerly Gilmor Lane', in line with the centre of the partition wall between this house and the house to the south; north on Greenmount 14 ft to the centre of the partition wall with the house to the north; west through that wall and on, in all 82 ft, to the east side of an alley 4 ft wide; south on the alley, with its use in common, 14 ft; and east 82 ft to the beginning, 'the improvements thereon being known as No 3030 Greenmount Avenue'. No other lot and no other rent is conveyed. Title recital: 'BEING the same lot of ground which by lease dated February 25th 1935 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber SCL No 5518 folio 171 was demised and leased by The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County to Helen M Bordley for the renewable term of ninety nine years at and under the annual rent of sixty six dollars and BEING the same lot of ground which by deed dated February 25th 1935 and recorded among said Land Records in Liber SCL No 5518 folio 173 was conveyed by The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County to the herein Grantors and BEING ALSO the same lot of ground which by assignment dated September 30th 1943 and recorded among said Land Records in Liber MLP No 6513 folio 139 was conveyed by Helen M Bordley to the herein Grantees'. Conveyed with 'especially the clear yearly rent of sixty six dollars issuing out of said lot of ground by virtue of the lease aforesaid', 'to the end and intent that the leasehold estate created by the lease aforesaid shall be merged with the fee and the annual rent issuing thereout shall be forever extinguished'. Witness Lennox B. Clemens; acknowledged Jan. 7, 1944 by both grantors before Lennox B. Clemens, notary; recorded Jan. 11, 1944 at 1:50 P.M., M. Luther Pittman, Clerk; grantee stamp Mar. 21, 1944. What it settles: this is the deed indexed at M.L.P. 6549/594 and recited in the 1951 Interrante-to-Podlich deed as '6549/554', a miscopy; the $66 rent the Leights sold was not the rent of Jacob H. Aull's 1912 lease to Alice M. Chapman but a new $66 rent created on Feb. 25, 1935, when The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County leased 3030 to Helen M. Bordley for 99 years renewable (S.C.L. 5518/171) and the same day deeded the reversion to the Leights (S.C.L. 5518/173); so by February 1935 the building association held 3030 in fee, with the 1912 leasehold and the Hooper reversion on this lot ended or united in it [inference], and the Leights never took anything from the Hooper trust; the Interrantes, who held the Bordley leasehold by her assignment of Sept. 30, 1943 (M.L.P. 6513/139), paid $1,100, the $66 rent capitalized at 6 percent [inference], merged the rent and held 3030 in fee from January 1944, which is why Nicholas Interrante could sell the fee to Robert F. Podlich in 1951 and Podlich could create the $90 rent. What it does not settle: how and when The Waverly Building Association came to own 3030, and what became of the 1912 Aull leasehold and the Hooper trustees' $66 reversion on it (most likely a foreclosure of a building association mortgage on the leasehold and a purchase of the reversion, but neither is read) [inference]; the 1935 lease and reversion deed themselves (S.C.L. 5518/171 and /173) and what the Leights paid; and the Bordley assignment (M.L.P. 6513/139). Update Oct. 16, 2026 (1935 read): the 1935 instruments are read (S.C.L. 5518/171 to 175, rows 47394 to 47396). The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County took the 3030 leasehold by assignment from David McCoy and wife, July 8, 1932 (S.C.L. 5312/27), and the reversion by a deed from 'the Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore et al Trustees', Feb. 18, 1935 (folio not given; very probably the Hooper trust selling the 1912 $66 rent, an inference), so the 1912 lease and rent met in the Association. On Feb. 25, 1935 it leased 3030 to Helen M. Bordley at $66, sold that new rent to Charles T. and Ella B. Leight for $1,100, and took the lease back from Bordley the same day (a straw, inference). Bordley's 1943 assignment to the Interrantes is M.L.P. 6513/139 (row 47397). Update Oct. 16, 2026 (5313/27 read): the McCoy assignment that the 1935 instruments cite as 'Liber S C L No 5312 folio 27' is recorded at S.C.L. 5313/27 (MSA CE 168-5321; Grantor Index 1932, row 47520), on a folio whose typed header reads '5312', corrected by hand to 5313. It is read (726:mdlr-scl5313-27-mccoy-waverly-bldg-assignment-3030-1932): David and Mary E. McCoy assigned the 3030 leasehold to The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County on July 8, 1932 (recorded July 12) for $5 and other valuable considerations, subject to the 1912 rent of $66 due June 1 and Dec. 1; they held it by Mary A. J. Aull's assignment of Dec. 20, 1929 (S.C.L. 5076/70). No mortgage or default is recited. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (1929 and 1935 read): S.C.L. 5517/92 (MSA CE 168-5525, read; 726:mdlr-scl5517-92-hooper-trustees-waverly-bldg-redemption-3030-1935) is the deed of Feb. 18, 1935 by which Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore and William Jenkins, trustees under Francis X. Hooper's will, on the Waverly Building Association's statutory notice to redeem, conveyed it the 1912 $66 reversion on 3030 for $1,100, 'to the end and intent that the leasehold estate created by the lease aforesaid shall be merged with the fee'. So the trustees of the 1935 recitals are Hooper's, and the 1912 lease and rent on 3030 merged in the Association by that deed, not by inference. S.C.L. 5076/70 and /71 (MSA CE 168-5084, read) show how the leasehold reached the McCoys: Jacob H. Aull's executors deeded it to his widow Mary A. J. Aull on Oct. 11, 1922 (S.C.L. 3918/495, recited), she assigned it to David and Mary E. McCoy on Dec. 20, 1929, and they mortgaged it the same day to the Waverly Building Association for a $3,120 purchase-money advance on 24 shares, released only on Mar. 15, 1951 (M.L.P. 8386/69). Their 1932 assignment to that lender was very probably in lieu of foreclosure [inference].
