summary: Deed in fee simple on the redemption of ground rents, Baltimore City land records, Liber J.B. No. 1276, folios 42 to 43 (MSA CE 168-1284; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, at 130 and 300 dpi). Captioned 'Alice P. Harris to Deed to David Stewart'. Dated Jan. 25, 1890, by Alice Patterson Harris and W. Hall Harris her husband to David Stewart. Recitals, quoted: 'Whereas by deed dated June 11th AD 1884 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County in Liber W M I No 141 folio 407 &c W Hall Harris and Alice P Harris leased to James E Sinclair the two lots hereinafter described And Whereas by mesne assignments and by deed dated January 3rd A.D. 1888 and recorded among said records in Liber J W S No 167 folio 243 &c from Sarah C Sinclair and James E Sinclair to David Stewart said Stewart became possessed of the leasehold interest in said lots created by said lease And Whereas by the terms of said lease the ground rents created thereby on said lots are redeemable and said Stewart now desires to redeem the same' (the day and the last digit of the year are cramped; the assignment itself is dated the third of January 1888). For 'twenty six hundred and eighty dollars and sixty six cents and accrued rent' the Harrises grant and convey to Stewart 'all those two lots of ground lying in Baltimore City (formerly County)'. The first begins on the westernmost side of the York turnpike road 164 ft 8 in northerly from the corner of the northeasternmost side of Merryman's Lane and the westernmost side of the turnpike, at the line drawn through the centre of 'the division wall between the house erected on the lot now being described and the house erected on the adjoining lot on the north thereof', and runs westerly through that wall 100 ft in all to an alley three feet wide communicating with Merryman's lane and laid out parallel with the turnpike, southerly on the east side of the alley 32 ft, easterly 100 ft to the road and northerly to the beginning (132 ft 8 in to 164 ft 8 in north of the lane). The second begins at the same point, at the centre of the division wall between its house and the house on the adjoining lot to the south, and runs westerly 100 ft to the alley, northerly on its east side 32 ft 4 in, easterly 100 ft to the road and southerly 32 ft 4 in to the beginning (164 ft 8 in to 197 ft north of the lane). '(Being the same two lots firstly and secondly particularly described in a Lease from W Hall Harris and Alice P Harris his wife to James E Sinclair mentioned aforesaid)'; a line runs under or through the words 'firstly and secondly particularly described'. With the improvements, rights, ways, alleys and privileges. Habendum 'unto the said David Stewart absolutely in fee simple free and discharged from the operations of said Lease'; special warranty and further assurances. Signed Alice Patterson Harris and W Hall Harris, witness Robert A. Thursby [?], justice of the peace for Baltimore City, before whom both acknowledged on Jan. 25, 1890. 'Recd for record Jan 25 1890 @ 12.55 o'clk P.M. same day recorded & exd per Jas Bond Clk.' Margin: 'Delivd Jan 27/90 to David Stewart'; a pencilled sum, 164 plus 32 making 196, stands beside the second lot. Folios 43 (foot) to 46 hold William L. Dallam's mortgage to the Merchants and Mechanics Permanent Building and Loan Company on Linden Avenue, not this ground. What it settles: the fee of the two lots passed from Alice P. Harris to David Stewart on Jan. 25, 1890 by redemption of the 1884 ground rents, not by an ordinary sale. Stewart already held the leasehold by the Sinclairs' assignment (J.W.S. 167/243), and the price is the two rents of the 1884 lease, $80 and $80.84 a year (recited in J.W.S. 167/404), capitalized at 6 percent ($160.84 divided by 0.06 is $2,680.67; the deed says $2,680.66), the rate at which the lease made them redeemable from June 11, 1889. The 1884 lease ended in Stewart's hands that day ('free and discharged from the operations of said Lease'). The 64 ft 4 in of the two lots is the same frontage as the four lots of Stewart's Feb. 1, 1888 lease to the Sinclairs (J.W.S. 167/402), so after this deed the 1888 rents ($36, $87, $81 and $48) issued out of Stewart's fee, which is why his Apr. 23, 1890 fee deed to John H. C. Legg (J.B. 1289/299) cites this deed and describes four rent-bearing lots [inference]. 3224, 181 to 197 ft north of the lane, is the northern 16 ft of the second lot. Both Harrises sign; the caption and the 1890 recital in J.B. 1289/299 name Alice alone, the holder of the fee under the 1884 deed to her. What it does not settle: it does not recite Harris's own title (the Sinclair deed to her of June 11, 1884, W.M.I. 141/405 is not cited, only the lease at 141/407); the 'mesne assignments' before the 1888 deed are not named (the 1884 lease ran to James E. Sinclair alone, and Sarah C. Sinclair is the first-named assignor in 1888); and the third lot of the 1884 Sinclair-to-Harris deed, beginning 36 ft 1/2 in north of the corner, is not in this deed. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (R.O. 1661, R.O. 1715 and S.C.L. 2610/548 read): the third lot of the 1884 deed to Harris, not in this redemption, stayed with the Harrises until Jan. 18, 1898, when they sold its fee to Alice Gerry Stewart for $2,500, the $150 rent at 6 percent (R.O. 1715/35, 768:mdlr-ro1715-35-harris-alice-gerry-stewart-third-lot-1898).

summary: Assignment of leasehold, Baltimore County land records, Liber J.W.S. No. 167, folios 243 to 244 (MSA CE 62-167; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, at 130 and 220 dpi). Captioned 'Sarah C. Sinclair et al Assgt to David Stewart'. Quoted: 'This Deed, made this Third day of January 1888 by Sarah C. Sinclair and James E. Sinclair her husband to David Stewart. Witnesseth that in consideration of fifteen hundred dollars the said Sinclair and husband hereby grant and assign to the said Stewart all those two lots of ground leased to said James E. Sinclair by W. Hall Harris and Alice P. Harris his wife by deed dated June 11th 1884 and duly recorded among the land records of Baltimore County in Liber W. M. I. No. 141 fol 407 &c said lots being the adjoining lots firstly and secondly described in said Lease, and being situate on the York Turnpike Road North of Merryman's Lane in Baltimore County aforesaid and fronting sixty four feet and four inches on said York Turnpike Road Together with the improvements thereupon and the rights, ways, and privileges thereunto belonging or in any way appertaining, subject to the operation of the aforesaid Lease and of a Mortgage to the Waverly Building Association.' Special warranty and further assurances. Signed Sarah C. Sinclair and Jas. E. Sinclair, witness John Willis [?], justice of the peace for Baltimore County, before whom both acknowledged on Jan. 3, 1888. 'Recorded Jany 4th 1888 at 8:30 Am & Exd Per John W. Shanklin Clerk.' Margin: ticket number 4874 and 'Delivered per [ticket?] June 8, 1888'. The instrument gives no metes and bounds, no rents and no term; it does not recite how Sarah C. Sinclair came to hold an interest in a lease made to her husband alone. Folio 243 above it ends an agreement between Henry C. Minor and Ogden A. Kirkland (recorded Jan. 3, 1888); folios 244 to 246 hold Samuel and Margaret C. Black's deed to Julian Henry Lee and the Sadtler trustees' lease to John P. Sadtler on Charles Street, neither for this ground. What it settles: this is the Sinclair-to-Stewart assignment that the Feb. 1, 1888 sub-lease (J.W.S. 167/404) recites without a liber, and the deed that the 1890 Harris deed (J.B. 1276/42) recites as J.W.S. 167/243. Dated Jan. 3, recorded Jan. 4, 1888, for $1,500. It carries the two lots described first and second in the 1884 Harris lease, 64 ft 4 in on the turnpike north of Merryman's Lane, which the 1890 Harris deed places at 132 ft 8 in to 197 ft north of the lane, so it includes 3224 (181 to 197 ft). Stewart took them subject to the 1884 rents and to a mortgage to the Waverly Building Association. The County index shows a release from the Waverly Building Association to James E. Sinclair recorded Jan. 23, 1888 (136/94), probably this mortgage cleared out of the $1,500 [inference]. Four weeks later Stewart leased the same 64 ft 4 in back to the Sinclairs as four lots (J.W.S. 167/402) and took their mortgage (J.W.S. 135/275), so the transaction worked as a sale and lease-back that turned one leasehold into four ground-rent lots [inference]. What it does not settle: the Waverly Building Association mortgage itself (date, amount, liber) and whether 136/94 is its release; the 'mesne assignments' of the 1890 recital (an assignment from James E. to Sarah C. Sinclair between 1884 and 1888 is possible but not found); and folio 409 of the 1884 lease. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (the mortgage released): the Waverly Building Association mortgage this assignment is subject to is the mortgage of Sept. 17, 1884 by James E. Sinclair and David H. Orr (W.M.I. 111) on two pieces, released to James E. Sinclair on Jan. 24, 1888, 21 days after this assignment (J.W.S. 136/94-95, 768:mdlr-jws136-94-waverly-bldg-assn-release-sinclair-1888). Orr's equity had been assigned to Sinclair in 1884 (W.M.I. 148/280, recited, not read). Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Orr's middle initial): where this row calls the 1884 co-mortgagor 'David H. Orr', read it as David F. Orr: the three instruments he is a party to, W.M.I. 142/124 (his assignment from Sinclair), W.M.I. 111/419 (the mortgage) and W.M.I. 148/280 (his assignment back to Sinclair, Oct. 28, 1885), all give 'David F. Orr' in the captions and the body; the hand in the 1888 release reads H or A (INFERRED F).

summary: Trustees' deed in fee simple, Baltimore County land records, Liber E.H.A. No. 72, folios 153 to 155 (MSA CE 62-72; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, at 130, 220 and 300 dpi). The deed begins at the foot of folio 153, continues on the leaf stamped 154 (MSA image p.155) and ends on the leaf stamped 155 (MSA image p.154); the clerk's notes 'Notice following page', 'Notice preceding page' and 'continues on preceding page' mark the reversed leaves. Captioned 'David S. Wilson &c Trustees &c Deed to Philip P Pendleton'. Made Sept. 1, 1871, between David S. Wilson, Thomas J. Wilson and Henry R. Wilson, 'Trustees as herein mentioned', of Baltimore County, and Philip P. Pendleton of Baltimore City. Recital, quoted: 'Whereas in pursuance of the power and authority vested by the Last Will and Testament of James Wilson dated 22 January 1848 and Codicil thereto dated 9th May 1848 recorded in the Orphans Court of Baltimore City in Liber N.H. No 26 folio 354 &c the said parties of the first part were authorised to sell and convey the parcels of ground herein described which they sold to said Philip P. Pendleton, and duly reported the same to the Circuit Court of Baltimore City which ratified said sales'. For $2,050 the trustees grant and convey to Pendleton 'his heirs and assigns in fee' two lots in Baltimore County 'being a part of the real estate of the late James Wilson and referred to in his Will aforesaid'. Description, quoted in part: 'Beginning for the said parcels on the west side of the York Turnpike Road at the end of the third line of a parcel of ground granted by said Wilson to a certain John H. Hartman and which place of beginning is southerly along the west side of said Turnpike Road distant eight hundred and sixty nine feet from the division line between the lands belonging to the said Wilsons and William McDonald's estate', then north 85 1/2 degrees west 200 ft along Hartman's third line reversed to a stake, south 3 1/2 degrees west parallel with the turnpike 100 ft to a stake, south 85 1/2 degrees east 200 ft to the turnpike, and north 3 1/2 degrees east 100 ft along the road to the beginning, 'subject however to the leaving open ten feet as the one half of an alley twenty feet wide along the second line of the above described parcel of ground, said parcel of ground comprises Lots numbers seven and eight (7 & 8) on the sales Plat of the Wilson property which plat is now filed in the case Wilson against Wilson and others in the Circuit Court of Baltimore City each of said lots being fifty feet front on said Turnpike Road by two hundred feet deep as subject aforesaid and is intended to begin southerly three hundred and seventy five feet from Wilson Street as laid down upon said Plat before referred to.' Habendum to Pendleton, his heirs and assigns, 'forever in fee'; the trustees covenant that they have done nothing to encumber the property, special warranty and further assurances. Signed D. S. Wilson, Thos. J. Wilson and Henry R. Wilson, each 'Trustee', witness Wm. H. Bayzand [?], justice of the peace for Baltimore City, before whom all three acknowledged on Sept. 1, 1871; certificate of Geo. Robinson, Clerk of the Superior Court of Baltimore City, Sept. 9, 1871. 'Recorded on the 12th day of September 1871 and Examined Per Edward H. Ady Clerk.' Margin: revenue stamps 'U.S.S. $2.50' and 'U.S.S. 5 cts', and 'Delivered June 21/1873 [?] G. S. Kepler [?] per Receipt'. Folio 153 above it ends John and Mary E. Wise's deed to Thomas Lytle (96 acres, Ensor ground); folios 156 and 157 hold James Manderson's lease to Joseph J. Mailhouse on Gough Street. What it settles: the trustees held the Wilson frontage on the York turnpike in fee as part of James Wilson's real estate, with a power of sale under his will of Jan. 22, 1848 and codicil of May 9, 1848 (Baltimore City wills, N.H. 26/354), and sold under ratification of the Circuit Court of Baltimore City; the deed mentions no ground rent and no Brown lease. The Wilson land along the turnpike was laid out in numbered lots, 50 ft front by 200 ft deep, on a sales plat filed in the equity case Wilson against Wilson and others. Lots 7 and 8 together run from 375 to 475 ft south of Wilson Street, and their northeast corner lies 869 ft south of the line between the Wilsons' land and William McDonald's estate, so Wilson Street lay about 494 ft south of that line. The Oct. 1, 1872 lease to Sinclair (E.H.A. 77/361) begins 475 ft south of Wilson Street at the southeast corner of 'lot number Seven as conveyed ... to P. P. Pendleton', so Lot 7 is the southern of the two, 425 to 475 ft south of Wilson Street [inference], and the 3224 ground is the Wilson land immediately south of Pendleton's Lot 7. The 20 ft rear alley, half of it taken from each side, is the 20 ft alley at the back of the 1872 lease. John H. Hartman's parcel lay immediately north of Lot 8; the trustees' deed to John H. Hartman and wife indexed Feb. 12, 1872 at 74/235 is probably its reversion [inference]. What it does not settle: the sales plat itself and the court papers in Wilson against Wilson and others (which would show whether the ground south of Lot 7 was a numbered lot, and where Wilson Street and Merryman's Lane fall on it); the will at N.H. 26/354 and the trustees' identity as James Wilson's sons or others; how James Wilson acquired the land; and the distance from Wilson Street to Merryman's Lane, so the placement of 3224 inside the 1872 Wilson lot still rests on the reading of Huff's 10 perches along the road. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (two citations of one will): the Jan. 14, 1871 Bolgiano deed (E.H.A. 70/115, row 18777) and the 1886 Clemens deed (J.W.S. 153/52) cite the same 1848 will at the Register of Wills, D.M.P. 24/154, not at N.H. 26/354 and without the May 9 codicil. Not reconciled; ask the Register of Wills for both volumes. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Hartman lease read): the trustees' lease to John H. Hartman and wife, Feb. 27, 1872 (E.H.A. 74/235-237, 768:mdlr-eha74-235-wilson-trustees-hartman-lease-1872), is of a 50 by 200 ft lot with the stone house, north of the Pendleton lots; it cites no plat, lot number or Wilson Street, and recites the will only as 'of record in the office of the Register of Wills for Baltimore City' under the power the will gave the trustees. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Archives finding aids): the Wilson equity records, from the Archives' catalog: the Baltimore City Circuit Court Equity Record book 'JRB 18' is T466-84, 1869 to 1870, shelf 03/04/06/039, no description and NO images listed online (so 'J.R.B. 18/536' is a recorded-proceedings volume of 1869 to 1870, at the Archives only); the equity docket is T55-9, T55-10 and T55-11 (1868 to 1869, 1869 to 1870, 1871; the series says units 1 to 20 are accessioned into C185); the defendant index is CM1295 (1853 to 1982, by defendant, giving book and page of the docket), volume CM1295-36 'WEY-WN' for Wilson, with a multipage PDF of 98 MB and page images online; equity plats are in C3026 ('Plats from Equity', findable by case number, name and date). None of these was opened. The case number and the docket page are not yet known; the next step is the Wilson entries in CM1295-36. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (CM1295-36 case located): the Archives' defendant index CM1295-36 lists the suit: defendants David S., Thomas J. and Henry R. Wilson, complainant 'William C. Wilson &c', equity docket 9, page 314, 1869 (no case number in the index; identification by the three trustees' names, the complainant and the year, INFERRED). Row 776:index-cm1295-36-wilson-v-wilson-1869-equity-docket-9-p314. The docket page, the papers and the sales plat are still to be requested from the Archives. Update Oct. 18, 2026 (N.H. 26/354 looked at): the Archives' viewer for CM219-3 (Baltimore City Register of Wills, 'NH 26', 1853 to 1855, 323 images) was opened to the folio this deed cites: folio 354 (image 198, with folios 346 to 355 on its ten PDF pages) carries the will of Eleanor Waters (signed Feb. 6, 1855, proved Feb. 24, 1855), NOT James Wilson's will, so 'Liber N.H. No 26 folio 354' does not lead to Wilson's will. Wilson died in 1848 (row 776:mdlr-wg179-639-union-bank-wilson-1826) and the book is dated 1853 to 1855, so the cite is either a mistake in the deeds (a different book or folio) or points to a later Orphans' Court recording, not the will's probate. Wilson's will is therefore still unread; the next tries are the probate year 1848 and the City will indexes. Only the folio was looked at; no other page of the book was read.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.B. 1289, folios 300 to 301 (MSA CE 168-1297; read 2026-10-16 by Claude from the scan Jeff saved for 3224, folios 297 to 301: 297 to 299 the Stewart foreclosure deed to Legg, 299 to 300 Stewart's fee deed of the four 3224 lots, then this deed; a release by the East Monument Street Permanent Building and Savings Association to George L. Ott, Apr. 24, 1890, begins at the foot of 301). Made Apr. 18, 1890. Lucy C. George and Benjamin R. George her husband, of Franklin County, Pennsylvania, for $1,200 grant John H. C. Legg of Baltimore City, in fee, the lot 'Beginning for the same at the corner formed by the intersection of the West side of the York Turnpike Road and the Northeast side of Merryman's Lane', north on the turnpike 36 ft 1 1/2 in, west at right angles 42 ft to the lane, and south-east on the lane 55 ft to the beginning. Recital: 'Being the same piece or parcel of ground which by lease dated June 14th 1887 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County was leased by Robert Riddell Brown to James E Sinclair at and under the yearly rent of sixty dollars payable in two equal instalments on June 1st and December 1st in every year and being the same piece or parcel of ground which was conveyed by Robert Riddell Brown to Lucy C George by deed dated 22nd [?] day of June 1887 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County in Liber J.W.S. No 162 folio 132 &c'. It passes 'especially and particularly the yearly rent reserved by the lease aforesaid', subject to the lessee's estate; special warranty. Witnesses J. R. Keenan [?] and D. K. Wunderlich; acknowledged Apr. 18, 1890 in Franklin County before Wunderlich, notary public (seal reads Chambersburg); received for record Apr. 24, 1890 at 12:35 P.M. and recorded the same day (Jas. Bond, Clerk). The day of the 1887 deed is written '12nd' or '22nd'; 22nd fits the ordinal and falls after the June 14 lease [inference]. What it settles: (1) how the Georges took Brown's reversion: Brown leased the apex to Sinclair on June 14, 1887 at $60 and sold the rent to Lucy C. George within days (J.W.S. 162/132), so the 1887 to 1890 owners of the 3200 fee are Brown, then Lucy C. George, then Legg. (2) Legg bought the rent six days before he took the Sinclair leasehold of the same lot at the foreclosure sale (J.B. 1289/297, lot 1, row 47359), and both deeds were received for record at 12:35 P.M. on Apr. 24, 1890 (the figure on this one is cramped), so he held fee and lease together from that day [inference that the lease merged; the deed does not say so]. (3) $1,200 for a $60 rent is 20 years' purchase (5 percent), below the 4 1/2 percent redemption figure the foreclosure deed gives (about $1,333) [arithmetic]. What it does not settle: the 1887 lease itself (J.W.S. 162/71) and Brown's deed to George (J.W.S. 162/132), not pulled; the rent days, which this deed gives as June 1 and December 1 and the foreclosure deed as June 14 and December 14; and Robert Riddell Brown's own title to the apex. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (J.W.S. 162 read): Brown's deed to Lucy C. George is read (J.W.S. 162/132, 752:mdlr-jws162-132-brown-george-apex-rent-reversion-1887): dated and acknowledged June 22, 1887, recorded June 23, $1,200; it recites the June 14, 1887 lease with the rent due June 1 and December 1, which settles the rent days. The 36 ft 1 1/2 in frontage and 'at right angles' begin in this deed. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (J.B. 1292/384 read): the apex left Legg on Apr. 26, 1890 (752:mdlr-jb1292-384-legg-stewart-five-lots-1890): his deed to David Stewart, recorded May 14, conveys it as 'the lot the Leasehold in which vested in said Legg by a deed from David Stewart and the fee by a deed from Lucy C. George', so both estates passed to Stewart together.

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore County land records, mortgage series, Liber J.W.S. No. 135, folios 275 to 278 (MSA CE 221-135; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, at 130 and 220 dpi). Captioned 'James E Sinclair et al Mortgage to David Stewart'. Made Feb. 1, 1888 by James E. Sinclair and Sarah C. Sinclair, husband and wife, of Baltimore County, to David Stewart of Baltimore City. Recital, quoted: 'Whereas the said Mortgagors are justly indebted to the said mortgagee in the sum of one thousand dollars for which sum they have passed to said mortgagee their joint and several promissory note of even date herewith payable six months after date with the agreement that said note shall be extended for a further period of six months without interest which note and indebtedness it was previously agreed should be secured by a mortgage upon the real and lease hold property and chattels of the mortgagors'. For the premises and $1 the Sinclairs 'grant convey assign and set over to the said David Stewart All the property and estate of said mortgagors real personal and mixed situated at or near Waverly in Baltimore County and especially the premises on the South West corner of Merrymans Lane and the York Turnpike Road and the Machinery thereupon and the lots on the York Road North of Merrymans Lane and the lots on the North and South sides of Merrymans Lane West of the York Road now owned by said Mortgagors or one of them subject to certain ground rents and a certain mortgage', with the improvements, rights, ways, alleys and privileges. No metes and bounds, no liber and no lessor is recited. Void on payment of 'said loan of $1000 at maturity'; the Sinclairs keep possession until default and pay all taxes, assessments, public dues and charges on the property and on the mortgage debt. On default the whole debt is due, and 'it shall be lawful for the said David Stewart his heirs personal representatives and assigns or Robert Riddell Brown his attorney or agent at any time after such default to sell the property hereby mortgaged or so much thereof as may be necessary', on twenty days' notice of the time, place, manner and terms of sale in a newspaper printed in Baltimore County; proceeds to the expenses of sale, including a commission of four percent to the party making it, then to the mortgagee's claims, then the surplus to the mortgagors. Signed 'Sarah E [?] Sinclair' (the clerk's initial looks like an E, perhaps over a C; the body and the acknowledgment say Sarah C.) and 'Jas E Sinclair', witness John Willis, justice of the peace for Baltimore County, before whom both acknowledged on Feb. 7, 1888. Stewart made the consideration oath the same day before Robert A. Thursby, justice of the peace for Baltimore City, with the certificate of Jas. Bond, Clerk of the Superior Court of Baltimore City (Feb. 7, 1888). 'Recorded Feby 9th 1888 @ 8.30 A.M. & Exd per John W Shanklin Clerk.' Horne and Pamelia A. Horne his wife, of Baltimore County, for $2,000, convey John Litzinger of the same place, in fee, 'All that piece or parcel of land situate and lying in Baltimore County aforesaid and near the village of Hereford called Solomons Chance': beginning at a stone on the east side of the Old Baltimore and York Road, also on the road to Fosters Meeting House and the road to John Wise's paper mills and Monkton Mills; S 14 1/2 E 28 perches, N 60 E 9, S 42 E 10, S 81 1/2 E 9, S 68 1/2 E 12 to two marked chestnut trees, S 66 1/2 E 8, S 56 1/4 E 39 9/10 to a stone, S 58 3/4 E 25 to a stone, N 42 1/2 W 70 1/2 (as written) to a stone, N 50 1/2 W 14 to a stone, about N 40 W about 100 perches to a stone on the south side of the road, and with the road to the beginning; no acreage is stated. Recital: 'being the same land that by Indenture bearing even date herewith ... was granted and conveyed by Mordecai Maddock and wife to the said David R. Horne'. Witnesses and justices John B. Kidd and Edward B. Freeland; acknowledged Oct. 11, 1852, Pamelia examined apart; $1 received in lieu of stamp Oct. 13; recorded Oct. 13, 1852 (Henry M. Fitzhugh, Clerk); margin 'Deld grantee 2 May 1853'. What it settles: line (1) of the 1851-1874 index (row 47363) is a farm near Hereford in the north of the county, not Waverly ground; it has nothing to do with 3011, 3013 or the fork. Horne bought it from the Maddocks and sold it to Litzinger the same day for $550 more. Edward B. Freeland, J.P., who took this acknowledgment, also took the Litzingers' acknowledgments of the 1864 Treadway deed (G.H.C. 39/499), the 1865 Blum sub-lease (J.H.L. 45/362) and the 1866 White lease (J.H.L. 48/502), so the Hereford buyer and the Waverly John Litzinger are very probably the same man, and he very probably lived up the county after 1852 (an inference from the justice). Bucher of the same, in fee, 'all that part of a tract of land called Ensors Inspection' beginning at the north-west corner of the lot Henry N. Bowerman, Walter T. Allender and others conveyed to the Vestry of St. Johns Church by deed of Sept. 27, 1844, and running on the east side of the old York road N 32 1/2 E 8 2/10 perches, S 81 1/4 E 10 4/10 perches, S 17 W 6 3/10 perches to the north-east corner of the Church lot, and on that lot N 87 1/2 W 12 6/10 perches to the beginning: 77 1/2 square perches (the courses close within 0.3 perch and compute to 79 square perches). Margin: 'Delivered to Rev W. T. Johnston Rector of St Johns Church Huntingdon May 20 1870' (the initials are uncertain). What it settles: the second parcel of the Bowerman deed to Litzinger (A.W.B. 381/477, row 46151) went, course for course, to Abraham H. Bucher in 1853. It lies east of the Old York Road between St. John's acre on the south (A.W.B. 349/45) and Jacob Aull's 2 acres 29 perches of 1848 on the north (A.W.B. 409/275, row 46158). It is not between the two roads and is not 3011, 3013 or any Greenmount frontage: the old road separates it from the fork. The recorded deed was handed to the rector of St. John's in 1870, so the lot very probably passed to the parish by then (an inference: no deed from Bucher to the Vestry is read). Abraham H. Bucher (1814 to 1893) is buried in St. John's churchyard (row 18255); a George W. Bucher (1843 to 1921) is buried there too (row 18260), and whether he is Abraham's son and the George W. Bucher of 3313 is not shown. What it does not settle: how and when the lot reached the Vestry, and where it lies in today's St. John's ground (the parish held church, cemetery and rectory as separate pieces in 2023).

Longnecker clk', and the index row 47363 inferred J.H.L.; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, pages 499 to 503, at 110 dpi, a clear transcribed hand; the top of 499 is the end of Peter B. and Elizabeth Wilhelm's deed to Charles Gore, acknowledged Dec. 24, 1863, and 501 to 503 hold Chauncey Brooks and wife's deed of Jan. 12, 1864 to the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore of 40 3/4 acres on Jones Falls by Druid Hill Park and the proposed lake, $23,453.75, margin 'Deld A. J. Bouldin June 1st 1864'). Dated Feb. 10, 1864. John Litzinger of Baltimore County and Elizabeth Litzinger his wife, for $900, convey John W. Treadway of the same place, his heirs and assigns, in fee simple: beginning on the east side of the York Turnpike Road at the south-west corner of 'a lot belonging to William Baden'; S 6 W 214 ft along the turnpike; N 89 E 8 1/2 ft to the west side of the old York Road; along it N 31 1/2 E 99 ft to a post and N 20 1/2 E 95 ft to a post at the south-east corner of William Baden's lot; N 61 W 82 ft along that lot to the beginning (closes within 0.8 ft; about 9,640 sq ft). Recital: 'Comprising the first described parcel of land in the Deed from Henry Bowerman and wife and others to John Litzinger bearing date tenth day of June Eighteen hundred and forty seven ... Liber A.W.B. No. 381 folio 477 and also comprising the same land described in a deed from John W. Stump and others to John Litzinger bearing date the 25th day of October A.D. 1841 ... Liber T.K. No. 315 folio 188', with the improvements; general warranty. Witness and justice Edward B. Freeland; acknowledged Feb. 10, 1864; a $1 U.S. stamp noted in the margin; recorded Feb. 11, 1864. What it settles: (1) these are, course for course, the courses of the 1896 trustee's sale (Sun 1896-07-18; Bayless to Miller, R.O. 1637/49) and of Miller's 1897 deed to Clemens Jr. (R.O. 1710/153): the parent ground of 3011, 3013, 3015, 3017 and 3019 is the lot Litzinger sold Treadway in 1864, and the lead from the 'Miss Tredway' lettered on Thompson's 1889 plat is confirmed in the County record. The ground north of 3019 to Baden's line (the later 3021 to 3025, lots 5 to 7 of the 1915 block) very probably lay in it too (an inference from the frontages). (2) The lot is two older pieces: the 8 1/2-perch Ensor's Inspection wedge of 1847 at the tip (90 ft 9 in on the turnpike; row 46151), on which Bouldin saw a two-story brick house in April 1847 (row 46681), and north of it the land Litzinger had from John W. Stump and others on Oct. 25, 1841 (T.K. 315/188, not read), by difference about 123 ft on the turnpike and 51 to 82 ft between the roads. That 1841 land is the 'parcel of land now owned by the said Letzinger' at whose south-west corner the 1847 wedge begins, not the Huntington leasehold (row 46153), so the probable match of the wedge to 3011 and 3013 (row 46167) is joined to the City chain by a deed. (3) The north neighbour in 1864 was William Baden's lot, nine years after William D. Baden's death: the Coffield tract of 3101 to 3117 (chapters 13 and 14), sold by Tagart's decree that summer. What it does not settle: the 1841 Stump deed and its tract; who John W. Treadway was; how the lot passed from him to the ward 'Miss Tredway' (John T. Ensor, guardian, 1889) and to Alice M. and N. Waldo Harrison, defendants in the 1896 decree (Alice M. Harrison may be the former Miss Tredway, an inference to test).

summary: Sub-lease, Baltimore County land records, Liber J.H.L. 45, folios 362 to 364 (MSA CE 62-45; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, pages 362 to 366, photographs of the bound book with the facing page in view, at 110 and 220 dpi; the top of 362 is the end of Jacob and Emily L. Wisner's deed to Philip Hare of 145 1/4 acres and 12 perches clear of a mill race, and 364 to 366 hold the executors of William H. Stinson's lease to George Henry Bramer of a lot on the Garrison Forest Road by the Frederick Turnpike). Dated March 1, 1865. John Litzinger of Baltimore County leases John G. Blum of the same place: beginning at a stone to be set up on the east side of the Baltimore and Yorktown Turnpike Road marked 1, 'it being also the beginning of John W Whites lot', with the first line of that lot S 84 1/2 E 9 23/25 perches to a stone marked 2, a corner of White's lot; on the western limits of the old York road S 10 3/4 W 8 13/25 perches to a stone marked 5; N 84 3/4 W 8 13/25 perches to a stone marked 6 on the east side of the turnpike; and by a straight line to the beginning; 'one half acre more or less' (computed 78 square perches, about 141 ft on the turnpike). 'Being a part of the land described in a deed of assignment from Walter T Allender trustee to John Litzinger' of June 10, 1847, A.W.B. 381/475: the Huntington leasehold under the 1798 lease to Jesse Brown. Term: 'all the rest and residue save one year of the term for years yet to come and unexpired', at $120 a year, half-yearly from March 1, 1865, over taxes; distress for any arrear, re-entry after sixty days, forfeiture after a year; renewal on a $10 fine by a new sub-lease reserving a reversion of one day, with a covenant for perpetual renewal; after five years Blum may pay $2,000 (the rent at 6 percent) for a deed of Litzinger's reversionary interest for the whole unexpired term, 'subject to the payment of no greater annual rent than one cent'. Witnesses Edward B. Freeland and a justice whose name reads like Jas. H. Stran; Litzinger acknowledged April 1, 1865 before Freeland, Blum (who signs as John George Blum) April 24, 1865 before the second justice; recorded July 24, 1865 (Jno. H. Longnecker, Clerk); margin 'Delivered to Grantee April 25th', the year unclear. What it settles: (1) Litzinger was still a leaseholder in March 1865 and let half an acre at a full rent before Oliver P. Merryman sold him the fee in June (J.H.L. 46/149, row 46585); on redemption a one-cent rent would remain, the same one-cent tenure on which William D. Baden's lot, the Coffield tract, was sold in 1864 (an observation; the source of Baden's tenure is not shown). (2) Place: the lot lies directly south of John W. White's lot, whose 1866 lease from Litzinger (J.H.L. 48/502, row 46310) begins at the same stone 1 and runs the same first line (written there 9 21/25 perches). Its south line, N 84 3/4 W 8 13/25 perches, is 140 ft 7 in; the north line of the 79-ft Coffield lot of 3113 to 3117 is 140 ft 6 in in six instruments (chapter 14); the 1908 Bradley deed puts that lot 'immediately to the south of No 4 Baltimore City Engine House', the house at 3123 that Baltimore County built in 1878 on a York Road lot near the toll-gate 'to be purchased of Mrs. Blum' (row 17881). So the Blum half-acre is probably the ground next north of 3117, with the 3123 engine-house lot inside it (probable, not proved: no deed out of the Blum lot is read). Along the turnpike the Blum lot (about 141 ft), White's lot (about 189 ft) and Jacob Aull's 260 ft at the north end (J.H.L. 46/520) add to about 590 ft against the 574 ft of the Brown lease parcel's closing line, so the three very probably fill the leasehold from its foot to its first line (an inference). (3) It is not 3011 to 3019: those lie in the Ensor's Inspection lot Litzinger sold Treadway in 1864 (G.H.C. 39/499), south of the Coffield tract. What it does not settle: John G. Blum's dates, the 1878 County deed from Mrs. Blum, and why the foot of the 1798 parcel (11.7 perches to the middle of the turnpike) is wider than this lot's 8 13/25 perches to its east side.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County land records, Liber J.H.L. 46, folios 520 to 521 (MSA CE 62-46; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, pages 520 to 524, at 110 and 200 dpi; the top of 520 is the end of a Baltimore City certificate of July 10, 1865 for another deed, and 521 to 524 hold James Curley, trustee, and the McCurley heirs' deed to Mary C. Start of a lot on the Frederick Road subject to a $40 rent). Dated Sept. 5, 1865. John Litzinger (written Litzsinger) and Elizabeth his wife, of Baltimore County, for $100, grant Jacob Aull of the same, in fee simple: beginning in the centre of the York Turnpike Road at the commencement of the first line of the lot Walter T. Allender, trustee under a decree of the Baltimore County Court sitting in equity, assigned Litzinger by deed of June 10, 1847 (A.W.B. 381/475); easterly on that first line to a stone on the west side of the Old York Road at its end; southerly on the Old York Road 260 ft to a stone marked A; westerly across the lot through a stone marked B, planted on the east side of the turnpike 260 ft from the first corner of the lot as enclosed, to the centre of the turnpike; and straight to the beginning. Recital: 'being the same ground which by deed dated the third day of November 1847 and recorded ... in Liber A.W.B. No. 388 folio 79 &c was conveyed by the said John Litzsinger to the said Jacob Aull subject to the payment of the yearly rent of five dollars eighty seven and a half cents', and 'especially and particularly' that rent, so that it 'shall be henceforth merged and forever extinguished'. Witness and justice P. T. Wilson, J.P. of Baltimore City (certified by Alfred Mace, clerk of the Superior Court, Sept. 5, 1865); 50 cents in stamps; recorded Nov. 25, 1865 (Jno. H. Longnecker, Clerk); margin 'Delivered to Mr. George Read May 17th 1866' (the name is a reading). What it settles: (1) Jacob Aull had held the north 260 ft of the Huntington leasehold between the roads since Nov. 3, 1847, under a sub-lease at $5.87 1/2 a year (A.W.B. 388/79, not read); in 1865, after Litzinger bought the fee from Oliver P. Merryman (J.H.L. 46/149), Aull bought the rent for $100, about its value at 6 percent ($97.92). (2) It is the north end of the 2 15/16-acre Brown lease parcel, beyond White's lot (J.H.L. 48/502) and the Blum half-acre (J.H.L. 45/362), which lie north of the Coffield tract of 3101 to 3117 (an inference from the lots' lengths along the turnpike): it is not 3011 or 3013, which lie in the Ensor's Inspection lot Litzinger sold Treadway in 1864 (G.H.C. 39/499). (3) So it is not the root of the Aull dealings on the study parcels: Jacob H. Aull's 1898 leases of 3011 and 3019 from Clemens Jr. were straws deeded back within three weeks (R.O. 1739/295), 3015's Aull deed is a straw too, and the 3026 to 3032 lots of his 1912 leases are on the west side of Greenmount, on the Wilson ground (E.H.A. 65/410). The inference in the index row (row 47363) that this deed was the likeliest root of the 3011 lot is withdrawn. What it does not settle: the modern lots inside the 260 ft (north of 3123, not shown), the 1847 sub-lease itself, and whether this Jacob Aull is the father of Jacob H. Aull, the Waverly builder.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County land records, Liber E.H.A. 70, folios 80 to 81 (MSA CE 62-70; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, pages 80 to 84, at 110 and 220 dpi; the deed opens at the head of 80, and 81 to 84 hold John S. Selby's assignment to William George Read of 81 acres of Wells Manor for $10,000). Dated April 1, 1871. It recites that John G. Blum, late of Baltimore County, died seised of the leasehold of the lot, and that Catharine Elizabeth Blum, his widow, holds it as residuary legatee and devisee under his will, probated in the Baltimore County Register of Wills. John Litzinger and Elizabeth his wife, of Baltimore County, for $2,000, convey Catharine Elizabeth Blum, her heirs and assigns, in fee, the half-acre of the 1865 sub-lease by the same courses: stone 1 on the east side of the Baltimore and Yorktown Turnpike at the beginning of John W. White's lot; S 84 1/2 E 9 23/25 perches to stone 2; S 10 3/4 W 8 13/25 perches on the western limits of the old York Road to stone 5; N 84 3/4 W 8 13/25 perches to stone 6; straight to the beginning. Recitals: part of the land in Allender's deed of assignment of June 10, 1847 (A.W.B. 381/475); 'also a part of the lot or parcel of ground the fee or reversionary interest in which was conveyed to said Litzinger by Oliver P. Merryman and wife by deed dated June 27, 1865' (J.H.L. 46/149); and the same lot that by deed of March 1, 1865 (J.H.L. 45/362) 'was leased by said Litzinger to said John G. Blum ... under the yearly rent of one hundred and twenty dollars'. With the buildings and improvements, 'Free, clear and released' from the $120 rent and from 'the original ground rent reserved on the land whereof the lot herein described is a part', that rent 'having been extinguished and forever released'; special warranty. Witness and justice Geo. Litzinger, J.P.; acknowledged April 1, 1871; $2 in stamps; recorded April 6, 1871 (Edward H. Ady, Clerk); margin 'Delivered to Grantee per ticket Oct. 27th 1874'. What it settles: (1) the 1865 sub-lease was redeemed at its $2,000 price six years on, by the widow, so the Blum half-acre was fee simple from April 1871, and the deed confirms that the 1798 Brown lease rent was extinguished by the 1865 Merryman deed. (2) The 'Mrs. Blum' from whom Baltimore County was to buy the 1878 engine-house lot on the York Road near the toll-gate (row 17881) is very probably Catharine E. Blum, and the engine house at 3123 stood immediately north of the 79-ft lot of 3113 to 3117, whose north line (140 ft 6 in) matches this lot's south line (8 13/25 perches, 140 ft 7 in): the half-acre is probably the ground next north of 3117, with 3123 inside it (probable, not proved). (3) A George Litzinger was a Baltimore County justice in 1871 and took the Litzingers' acknowledgment; the relationship is not stated. John Litzinger was alive on April 1, 1871. What it does not settle: the County's 1878 deed from Mrs. Blum, John G. Blum's dates and will, and what became of the rest of the half-acre.

Selby's assignment to William George Read of 81 acres of Wells Manor for $10,000). Dated April 1, 1871. It recites that John G. Blum, late of Baltimore County, died seised of the leasehold of the lot, and that Catharine Elizabeth Blum, his widow, holds it as residuary legatee and devisee under his will, probated in the Baltimore County Register of Wills. John Litzinger and Elizabeth his wife, of Baltimore County, for $2,000, convey Catharine Elizabeth Blum, her heirs and assigns, in fee, the half-acre of the 1865 sub-lease by the same courses: stone 1 on the east side of the Baltimore and Yorktown Turnpike at the beginning of John W. White's lot; S 84 1/2 E 9 23/25 perches to stone 2; S 10 3/4 W 8 13/25 perches on the western limits of the old York Road to stone 5; N 84 3/4 W 8 13/25 perches to stone 6; straight to the beginning. Recitals: part of the land in Allender's deed of assignment of June 10, 1847 (A.W.B. 381/475); 'also a part of the lot or parcel of ground the fee or reversionary interest in which was conveyed to said Litzinger by Oliver P. Merryman and wife by deed dated June 27, 1865' (J.H.L. 46/149); and the same lot that by deed of March 1, 1865 (J.H.L. 45/362) 'was leased by said Litzinger to said John G. Blum ... under the yearly rent of one hundred and twenty dollars'. With the buildings and improvements, 'Free, clear and released' from the $120 rent and from 'the original ground rent reserved on the land whereof the lot herein described is a part', that rent 'having been extinguished and forever released'; special warranty. Witness and justice Geo. Litzinger, J.P.; acknowledged April 1, 1871; $2 in stamps; recorded April 6, 1871 (Edward H. Ady, Clerk); margin 'Delivered to Grantee per ticket Oct. 27th 1874'. What it settles: (1) the 1865 sub-lease was redeemed at its $2,000 price six years on, by the widow, so the Blum half-acre was fee simple from April 1871, and the deed confirms that the 1798 Brown lease rent was extinguished by the 1865 Merryman deed. (2) The 'Mrs. Blum' from whom Baltimore County was to buy the 1878 engine-house lot on the York Road near the toll-gate (row 17881) is very probably Catharine E. Blum, and the engine house at 3123 stood immediately north of the 79-ft lot of 3113 to 3117, whose north line (140 ft 6 in) matches this lot's south line (8 13/25 perches, 140 ft 7 in): the half-acre is probably the ground next north of 3117, with 3123 inside it (probable, not proved). (3) A George Litzinger was a Baltimore County justice in 1871 and took the Litzingers' acknowledgment; the relationship is not stated. John Litzinger was alive on April 1, 1871. What it does not settle: the County's 1878 deed from Mrs. Blum, John G. Blum's dates and will, and what became of the rest of the half-acre.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Circuit Court land records, Liber J.W.S. 162, folios 70 to 71 (MSA CE 62-162; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 68 to 75, at 150 and 300 dpi). The scan holds, in order: the end of the Academy of the Visitation B.V.M. of Mount de Sales's power of attorney to Daniel J. Foley, trustee under Emily Mactavish's will (dated June 1, 1887, also recorded in City J.B. 1145/2; entry 3638, folios 68 to 70); this deed (entry 3639, foot of 70 to 71); Brown's lease back to Sinclair (entry 3640, 71 to 73); Gottlieb H. and Doratty C. Erdman's deed to Ruth A. Fischmyer [?], widow, of a lot at the Harford Road and Montebello Avenue (June 2, 1887, $1,200, entry 3641, 73 to 75); and the start of Francis S. and Mary F. Erdman's deed to Leonhard Lang (June 16, 1887, $200, entry 3642). Made June 13, 1887. James E. Sinclair and Sarah C. Sinclair his wife, of Baltimore County, for $1,200 'do hereby grant and convey to the said Robert Riddell Brown in fee simple', Brown being of Baltimore City, 'all that lot of ground lying on the York Turnpike in Waverly in Baltimore County': 'Beginning for the same at the corner formed by the intersection of the Northeasternmost side of Merryman's Lane with the Westernmost side of the York Turnpike road', north on the turnpike 'thirty six [feet, interlined] and one half of an inch to the centre of a division wall between the house on the lot now being described and the house on the adjoining lot to the North', west 'through the centre of said wall and continuing in the same direction in all forty two feet' to the north-east side of the lane, and south-east on the lane 55 ft to the beginning, with the improvements. Title recital: '(For title see deed from Eliz. Huff to J. E. Sinclair recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County in Liber E.H.A. No 74 fol 321, a deed from T. J. Wilson & others to J. E. Sinclair recorded as aforesaid in Liber J.B. No 84 fol 381 &c. and a deed from O. P. Merryman to J. E. Sinclair recorded as aforesaid in Liber W.M.I. No 141 fol 404 &c)'. Special warranty and further assurances. No tract is named. Witness John Willis, justice of the peace for Baltimore County, before whom both Sinclairs acknowledged on June 14, 1887; recorded June 17, 1887 at 8:30 a.m. (John W. Shanklin, Clerk); margin 'Mailed Oct. 21 1887 per Fischer [?]'. What it settles: (1) the folio and the dates: the sale is J.W.S. 162/70, the folio before the lease, made June 13, acknowledged June 14 and recorded June 17, 1887, the transfer day the Sun printed (row 5185). (2) The lot is the apex, 36 ft 1/2 in on the road, with a house on it and a division wall on its north line, the line of the third Harris lot of 1884 (W.M.I. 141/405). (3) Sinclair recites his title: the Huff assignment of 1872 and the Merryman release of 1884, both read, and a deed from the Wilson trustees. The Wilson folio is written 381, but the Wilson trustees' deed to Sinclair read in Corridor begins at J.B. 84/387 (row 46239), so 381 is a slip or a second Wilson deed (unsettled). The Wilson lot lies north of Brown's ten perches, so its citation here is Sinclair's general title carried over, not a sign that the apex is Wilson ground (inference). (4) Brown sold the rent and reversion for the same $1,200 nine days later (J.W.S. 162/132), so the sale and lease back was a ground-rent financing for Sinclair with Brown as the go-between (inference). What it does not settle: why Sinclair, who held the fee from 1884, raised $1,200 this way (his 1888 mortgage and the 1890 foreclosure suggest he was short of money, inference); and what folio 381 of J.B. 84 holds.

summary: Lease, Baltimore County Circuit Court land records, Liber J.W.S. 162, folios 71 to 73 (MSA CE 62-162; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 68 to 75, at 150 and 300 dpi; the scan's other contents are listed on the deed before it, 752:mdlr-jws162-70-sinclair-brown-apex-fee-1200-1887). Entry 3640. Made June 14, 1887 between Robert Riddell Brown, 'bachelor, of Baltimore City', and James E. Sinclair of Baltimore County. Brown leases Sinclair, his executors, administrators and assigns, the apex: from the corner of the north-east side of Merryman's Lane and the west side of the York Turnpike road, north on the road 'thirty six feet and one half of an inch, to the centre of the division wall between the house on the lot now being described and the house on the lot next adjoining to the north', west through the wall and on in all 42 ft to the lane, and south-east along the lane 55 ft to the beginning, '(Being the same lot of ground conveyed by said Sinclair and wife to said Brown by a deed dated June 13, 1887 and duly heretofore recorded.)'. Term 99 years from the date; rent 'the rent or yearly sum of sixty Dollars and that in even and equal half-yearly instalments, accounting from the first day of June One thousand eight hundred and eighty seven', clear of all taxes and assessments. Distress for any arrears; re-entry until paid after sixty days in arrear; re-entry 'as if this lease had never been made' after six months. Sinclair covenants to pay the rent, taxes and assessments; Brown warrants specially and, on a $10 renewal fine, will grant a new lease for another 99 years 'so that the demise hereby created may be renewable and renewed from time to time, forever'. Redemption: 'after the expiration of fifteen years accounting from the day of the date of these presents, on the payment of a sum of money equal to the capitalization of the rent hereby reserved at the rate of 4 1/2 per cent, in gold coin of the United States or its equivalent', with rent accrued and a pro-rata part of the current half-year's rent, the lot is released from the rent and the lessee's covenants. Witness John Willis, J.P. for Baltimore County, before whom Sinclair and Brown each acknowledged on June 14, 1887; recorded June 17, 1887 at 8:30 a.m. (John W. Shanklin, Clerk); margin 'Mailed per Fischer [?] Oct. 21 1887'. What it settles: (1) the lease is read: J.W.S. 162/71 to 73, made and acknowledged June 14, 1887 and recorded June 17, as the 1890 foreclosure deed cites it (J.B. 1289/297). (2) The rent days: the half-years run 'accounting from the first day of June' 1887, so the rent fell due December 1 and June 1, as Brown's deed to Lucy C. George (J.W.S. 162/132) and the 1890 George deed (J.B. 1289/300) state; the foreclosure deed's June 14 and December 14 took the lease's date for the rent days (inference from the wording). (3) The redemption sum at 4 1/2 percent is about $1,333, available after June 14, 1902 (arithmetic). (4) A house stood on the apex, with a division wall on its north line, by June 1887. What it does not settle: whether the rent was ever redeemed; it very probably merged when Legg took the reversion and the leasehold in April 1890 (inference; no deed says so).

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Circuit Court land records, Liber J.W.S. 162, folios 132 to 133 (MSA CE 62-162; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 132 to 136, at 150 and 300 dpi). The scan holds: the end of an instrument acknowledged before Robert A. Thursby [?], J.P., with the Superior Court clerk's certificate of March 4, 1887, recorded June 22, 1887 at 10 a.m.; this deed (entry 3683, 132 to 133); John W. Quick, executor of Annie Disney, to Andrew H. Schwabeland [?], seven-ninths of an acre of 'Constitution Hills' on the Baltimore and Reisterstown Turnpike (June 20, 1887, entry 3684, 133 to 135); and Benjamin H. Classen, committee of Frederick W. Classen, a lunatic, to Schwabeland, the other two-ninths (June 20, 1887, entry 3685, 135 to 136). Made 'this twenty second day of June' 1887. Robert Riddell Brown of Baltimore City, for $1,200, grants Lucy C. George, 'wife of Benjamin R. George of Franklin County in the State of Pennsylvania', her heirs and assigns, in fee, the lot 'Beginning for the same at the corner formed by the intersection of the West side of the York Turnpike Road and the North-east side of Merryman's Lane', north on the turnpike 'thirty six feet one and one half inches', 'thence westerly at right angles with the said Turnpike Road forty two feet' to the lane, and south-east on the lane 55 ft to the beginning. Recital: 'Being the same piece or parcel of ground which by Lease dated June 14, 1887 and recorded among the land records of Baltimore County was leased by Robert Riddell Brown to James E. Sinclair, at and under the yearly rent of sixty dollars, payable in two equal instalments on June 1 and December 1 in every year'. It passes 'especially and particularly the yearly rent reserved by the Lease aforesaid', to George in fee 'subject however to the estate of the said Lessee his personal representatives and assigns created by the Lease aforesaid'; special warranty and further assurances. Witness Robert A. Thursby [?], J.P. of Baltimore City, before whom Brown acknowledged on June 22, 1887 (clerk's certificate the same day, Jas. Bond); recorded June 23, 1887 at 8:30 a.m. (John W. Shanklin, Clerk); margin 'Mailed Nov. 12 1887 per Fichel [?]'. What it settles: (1) the day is the 22nd, written in words in the deed and in the acknowledgment, so the '12nd' or '22nd' of the 1890 recital (J.B. 1289/300) is the 22nd. (2) The deed names the lease, its date and the $60 rent, with rent days June 1 and December 1, which agree with the lease (J.W.S. 162/71); it cites no liber for the lease and does not recite Brown's own deed from Sinclair. (3) Brown sold the rent and reversion for the $1,200 he had paid Sinclair nine days before (J.W.S. 162/70), so he was a go-between and Lucy C. George the investor, at 5 percent (inference). (4) The variants in the 1890 George deed, 36 ft 1 1/2 in and 'at right angles' in place of the division wall, begin here; the deed to Brown and the lease say 36 ft 1/2 in. What it does not settle: who Lucy C. and Benjamin R. George were and why a Franklin County couple bought a Waverly rent. Justice Thursby also took the Stewarts' acknowledgments of the 1890 foreclosure deed (J.B. 1289/297), and Brown was David Stewart's named agent in the 1888 Sinclair mortgage (J.W.S. 135/275), which may put the Georges in Stewart's circle (inference). Frederick H. Samstag, who took the leasehold in 1911, had married the widow Mrs. Elizabeth George in 1909 (row 42322); nothing read links her to Lucy C. or Benjamin R. George (open lead).

summary: Lease, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 5518, folios 171 to 173 (MSA CE 168-5526; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 171 to 175, at 150 and 300 dpi). Folio 171 opens with the end of Peter and Annie Scherrer's mortgage (her mark; a decree-for-sale clause under Sections 720 to 732 of Chapter 123 of the Acts of 1898; Robert N. Baer, agent of a mortgagee not named on the folio; acknowledged before Kathleen Meehan and recorded Mar. 4, 1935 at 2:20 P.M.). Then come this lease (171 to 173), the Association's deed of the reversion to the Leights (173 to 174) and Helen M. Bordley's assignment of the lease back to the Association (174 to 175), all three about 3030; folio 175 goes on to Sarah H. Folick (formerly Sarah Harris) and Rebecca Harris to James L. and Laura Dowlin, Feb. 27, 1935, 434 South Parrish Street, not about 3030. Margin heading 'The Waverly Bldg Asso of Balto Co Lease to Helen M Bordley' (clerk's number 150). Dated Feb. 25, 1935. The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County, 'a body corporate of the State of Maryland', 'in consideration of the rent hereinafter expressed', leases to Helen M. Bordley of Baltimore City (spelled 'Bordly' once in the body) the lot beginning on the west side of Greenmount Avenue 29 ft north of the corner of its west side and the north side of 'Vineyard Lane formerly Gilmor Lane', in line with the centre of the partition wall between this house and the house to the south; north on Greenmount 14 ft to the centre of the partition wall with the house to the north; west through that wall and on, in all 82 ft, to the east side of an alley 4 ft wide; south on the alley, with its use in common, 14 ft; and east 82 ft to the beginning, 'the improvements thereon being known as No 3030 Greenmount Avenue'. Term 99 years from the date; rent $66 a year in even half-yearly instalments 'accounting from the twenty fifth day of February' 1935, over and above all taxes; distress for any arrears, re-entry until paid after sixty days in arrear, and re-entry 'as if this lease had never been made' after six months; the lessee pays the taxes; the lessor warrants against claims under it and will grant a new 99-year lease on payment of a $10 renewal fine, so that the lease is 'renewable and renewed from time to time forever'. Title recital: 'BEING the same lot of ground to which The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County acquired title by the following Assignment dated July 8th 1932 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber S C L No 5312 folio 27 from David McCoy and wife and Deed of Reversion Dated the 18th day of February 1935 and intended to be recorded among the Land Records of said City prior hereto from the Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore et al Trustees'. Signed for the Association by John G. Maier, its President, under a seal copied as '(Waverly Bldg Asso (Balto County Inc 1832)', and by Helen M. Bordley; witness Lennox B. Clemens; acknowledged Feb. 25, 1935 by Maier and by Bordley before Lennox B. Clemens, notary; recorded Mar. 4, 1935 at 2:30 P.M., Stephen C. Little, Clerk. What it settles: where the Association's title came from. It held the 3030 leasehold by the assignment of David McCoy and his wife of July 8, 1932 (S.C.L. 5312/27), and it bought the reversion from 'the Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore et al Trustees' by a deed of Feb. 18, 1935, recorded just before this lease. Those trustees are very probably Francis X. Hooper's testamentary trustees (Mercantile Trust and Deposit Company of Baltimore and William Jenkins in the 1917 division, S.C.L. 3177/132; 'Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore, surviving trustee' in 1945), and the reversion the 1912 $66 Aull rent the division gave them [inference: the recital names no testator and no earlier lease]. So the 1912 leasehold and the Hooper rent on 3030 met in the Association in February 1935 and merged [inference: no merger clause is on these folios], and the Association at once made a new $66 lease, the one whose rent the Leights sold the Interrantes in 1944 (M.L.P. 6549/594, read). What it does not settle: how David McCoy and his wife came to hold the 1912 leasehold (Aull took all four back from Alice M. Chapman in 1916 and sold 3032 and 3028 in 1918; no 3030 sale is found) and why they assigned it to a building association in 1932 (a defaulted building-association loan given up in lieu of foreclosure is a guess, not read); and the Mercantile deed of Feb. 18, 1935 itself, its folio and its price, which are not on these folios. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (5313/27 read): the McCoy assignment that the 1935 instruments cite as 'Liber S C L No 5312 folio 27' is recorded at S.C.L. 5313/27 (MSA CE 168-5321; Grantor Index 1932, row 47520), on a folio whose typed header reads '5312', corrected by hand to 5313. It is read (726:mdlr-scl5313-27-mccoy-waverly-bldg-assignment-3030-1932): David and Mary E. McCoy assigned the 3030 leasehold to The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County on July 8, 1932 (recorded July 12) for $5 and other valuable considerations, subject to the 1912 rent of $66 due June 1 and Dec. 1; they held it by Mary A. J. Aull's assignment of Dec. 20, 1929 (S.C.L. 5076/70). No mortgage or default is recited. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (1929 and 1935 read): S.C.L. 5517/92 (MSA CE 168-5525, read; 726:mdlr-scl5517-92-hooper-trustees-waverly-bldg-redemption-3030-1935) is the deed of Feb. 18, 1935 by which Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore and William Jenkins, trustees under Francis X. Hooper's will, on the Waverly Building Association's statutory notice to redeem, conveyed it the 1912 $66 reversion on 3030 for $1,100, 'to the end and intent that the leasehold estate created by the lease aforesaid shall be merged with the fee'. So the trustees of the 1935 recitals are Hooper's, and the 1912 lease and rent on 3030 merged in the Association by that deed, not by inference. S.C.L. 5076/70 and /71 (MSA CE 168-5084, read) show how the leasehold reached the McCoys: Jacob H. Aull's executors deeded it to his widow Mary A. J. Aull on Oct. 11, 1922 (S.C.L. 3918/495, recited), she assigned it to David and Mary E. McCoy on Dec. 20, 1929, and they mortgaged it the same day to the Waverly Building Association for a $3,120 purchase-money advance on 24 shares, released only on Mar. 15, 1951 (M.L.P. 8386/69). Their 1932 assignment to that lender was very probably in lieu of foreclosure [inference].

summary: Assignment of a leasehold, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 5518, folios 174 to 175 (MSA CE 168-5526; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 171 to 175, at 150 and 300 dpi; the other instruments on the folios are listed in the row for the lease, 726:mdlr-scl5518-171-waverly-bldg-bordley-lease-3030-1935). Margin heading 'Helen M Bordley Asst to The Waverly Building Asso of Balto Co' (clerk's number 152). Dated Feb. 25, 1935. Helen M. Bordley of Baltimore City, 'in consideration of the sum of five dollars and other valuable considerations', grants and conveys to The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County the 3030 lot in the words of the lease, 'BEING the same lot of ground which by lease of even date herewith and intended to be recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County prior hereto was demised and leased by The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County to the herein grantor for the renewable term of ninety nine years' (the lease is in the City records, so 'Baltimore County' is a slip), to hold 'for all the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein with the benefit of renewal forever subject to the payment of the annual rent of Sixty six dollars payable in equal half yearly instalments on the 25th days of February and August'; she covenants that she has not encumbered it and warrants specially. Signed Helen M. Bordley; witness Lennox B. Clemens; acknowledged Feb. 25, 1935 before Lennox B. Clemens, notary; recorded Mar. 4, 1935 at 2:32 P.M., Stephen C. Little, Clerk. What it settles: Helen M. Bordley was a straw lessee. The lease to her, the deed of the rent to the Leights and her assignment back were dated and acknowledged the same day and recorded a minute apart, so that the Association could create a new ground rent, sell it for $1,100 and keep the house as a leasehold under it [inference from the sequence; the papers do not say so]. She plays the same part on 3030 in 1943 (M.L.P. 6513/139, read) and on 3040 in 1944 (M.L.P. 6612/428, recited), each time before Lennox B. Clemens, the notary who took the Association's acknowledgments (the 1934 Sinclair mortgage, S.C.L. 5419/571). From Feb. 25, 1935 the Association held the 3030 leasehold and the Leights the rent. What it does not settle: when and how the Association parted with the leasehold before Nicholas Interrante held it in 1943 (an instrument in M.L.P. 6410, glimpsed on the facing page of the 1943 scan; see 726:mdlr-mlp6513-139-bordley-interrante-assignment-3030-1943). Ida H. Interrante, formerly Ida H. Caples, assigned 506 McCabe Avenue to Bordley the same day (M.L.P. 6513/137). Update Oct. 17, 2026 (M.L.P. 6410/265 read): the Association's assignment of 3030 to Nicholas Interrante, Dec. 29, 1942 (M.L.P. 6410/265, read; 726:mdlr-mlp6410-265-waverly-bldg-interrante-assignment-3030-1942) recites 'assignment dated the 25th day of February 1935 ... summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber T.K. 315, folios 188 to 189 (MSA CE 66-365; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 188 to 192, at 150, 280 and 400 dpi). The top of 188 is the end of Robert Forsyth's $400 instrument to David T. and John S. McKim, due in December 1844 and acknowledged Dec. 22, 1841; this deed follows under the margin heading 'John W. Stump & others Deed to John Litzinger' and ends on 189, where John Penn's deed to John Buckley of July 20, 1841 begins (part of 'Hopes Lot', 18 3/4 acres on the old Frederick road, $375; it ends on 190); 190 to 192 hold Samuel Mass and Francis Meyer's assignment to Francis A. De Mangin of Dec. 18, 1841 (a Ross Street leasehold in the City, $875). Dated Oct. 25, 1841, between John W. Stump, Sarah Biays, Jacob Hoke and Ann B. Hoke, Henry Hammond and Frances J. Hammond, Henry N. Bowerman and Elizabeth Bowerman, and W. T. Allender and Hannah J. Allender, of the first part, all of Maryland, and 'Jno. Litzinger of the second part same state'. For $300 they grant, bargain and sell to Litzinger, his heirs and assigns, 'all their right title and interest claim and demand to a piece of land adjoining or belonging to a tract called "Ensors Inspection" (and embraced in a deed of trust from John McFadon to Jno. W. Stump and Philip G. Biays for the use of the first named parties and recorded in Liber W.G. No. 165 folio 492 land records Baltimore County) and lying between the old and New York roads. Beginning at a stone at the south west corner of a lot belonging to Wm. Baden and running parallel with the present York road forty yards, thence seventeen yards in an easterly direction to the old road thence thirty one yards along the old road to Badens Lot and from thence twenty six yards to the place of beginning. Containing about the one sixth of an acre more or less'. No buildings are named and there is no warranty, only a covenant to make, at Litzinger's cost, any conveyance 'necessary further to convey the estate which they the said parties now have in the premises'. Signed Jno. W. Stump, S. Biays, J. Hoke, Ann B. Hoke, Henry Hammond, Fanny Hammond, Henry W. [sic] Bowerman, Elizabeth Bowerman, Walter T. Allender and Hannah J. Allender, before George W. King and Jesse Cloud, who took the acknowledgment the same day in Baltimore City, the four wives (the certificate calls the first 'Nancy B. Hoke') examined apart from their husbands; received to be recorded Dec. 22, 1841 at a quarter past 11 A.M. and recorded the same day (Thos. Kell, clerk); margin 'D. grantee 8th Oct 1842' (delivered, as read). Philip G. Biays, the co-trustee, is not a party, though he joined the 1844 Mumma deed (A.W.B. 354/374, row 46070). What it settles: (1) the deed recited in Litzinger's 1864 deed to John W. Treadway (G.H.C. 39/499, row 47383) is read, and it is the north piece of that lot. Its calls are 40 yards (120 ft) down the turnpike from Baden's south-west corner, 17 yards (51 ft) east to the old road, 31 yards (93 ft) up it (1864: N 20 1/2 E 95 ft) and 26 yards (78 ft) back along Baden's line (1864: N 61 W 82 ft). Laid on the 1864 courses, the line from 120 ft down the turnpike to the post where the old road bends (the end of the N 31 1/2 E 99 ft course) measures 51 ft 2 in and encloses about 6,880 sq ft (0.16 acre, against 'about the one sixth'); the other 94 ft of turnpike to the fork is the 1847 wedge (A.W.B. 381/477, row 46151), whose north line of 3 1/10 perches (51 ft 2 in) is this deed's 17-yard line. So this lot is the 'parcel ... now owned by the said Letzinger' at whose south-west corner the wedge begins, by measure as well as by the 1864 recital. (2) Stump's title is the McFadon deed of trust of April 11, 1822 (W.G. 165/492, row 46094) and nothing else is recited: the grantors are one of its two trustees, its life tenant, Sarah Biays, and the four Biays daughters who held the remainder, with their husbands; the same couples sold the wedge in 1847 after Stump's trustee's deed of 1845 (A.W.B. 359/136, row 46130). (3) The tract is named, but hedged: 'adjoining or belonging to' Ensor's Inspection. (4) By the City frontages (3015, 15 ft; 3017, 19 ft 2 in; 3019 and 3021, the 33-ft Aull lot of 1898; 3023, 28 ft; 3025, 33 ft; 128 ft 2 in in all, against 120) and the 1915 depths (46 ft 3 in at 3015 rising to 75 ft at 3025, against 51 ft at this lot's south line and about 75 ft square to the turnpike at Baden's line), this lot carries 3015 to 3025 and the wedge 3011 and 3013 (72 ft 4 in): an inference from the measures, good to about 8 ft. What it does not settle: whether the strip lies in Ensor's Inspection or in Huntington, whose leasehold of 1809 lay on the same strip north of Baden's lot (row 46153); how it came into McFadon's 1822 ground (no course or Moale lot is given; that it is the front of Moale's Lot 3 of 1819, sold 'subject to a County road' through its front, with buildings on the road let for 22 years (as read there) from May 26, 1819, W.G. 160/582, row 46129, is a lead, not shown); why Philip G. Biays did not join, which may explain the quitclaim form; the lessor and date of William Baden's lot, already there in 1841 (chapters 12 and 13); and what stood on the lot.

Stump & others Deed to John Litzinger' and ends on 189, where John Penn's deed to John Buckley of July 20, 1841 begins (part of 'Hopes Lot', 18 3/4 acres on the old Frederick road, $375; it ends on 190); 190 to 192 hold Samuel Mass and Francis Meyer's assignment to Francis A. De Mangin of Dec. 18, 1841 (a Ross Street leasehold in the City, $875). Dated Oct. 25, 1841, between John W. Stump, Sarah Biays, Jacob Hoke and Ann B. Hoke, Henry Hammond and Frances J. Hammond, Henry N. Bowerman and Elizabeth Bowerman, and W. T. Allender and Hannah J. Allender, of the first part, all of Maryland, and 'Jno. Litzinger of the second part same state'. For $300 they grant, bargain and sell to Litzinger, his heirs and assigns, 'all their right title and interest claim and demand to a piece of land adjoining or belonging to a tract called "Ensors Inspection" (and embraced in a deed of trust from John McFadon to Jno. W. Stump and Philip G. Biays for the use of the first named parties and recorded in Liber W.G. No. 165 folio 492 land records Baltimore County) and lying between the old and New York roads. Beginning at a stone at the south west corner of a lot belonging to Wm. Baden and running parallel with the present York road forty yards, thence seventeen yards in an easterly direction to the old road thence thirty one yards along the old road to Badens Lot and from thence twenty six yards to the place of beginning. Containing about the one sixth of an acre more or less'. No buildings are named and there is no warranty, only a covenant to make, at Litzinger's cost, any conveyance 'necessary further to convey the estate which they the said parties now have in the premises'. Signed Jno. W. Stump, S. Biays, J. Hoke, Ann B. Hoke, Henry Hammond, Fanny Hammond, Henry W. [sic] Bowerman, Elizabeth Bowerman, Walter T. Allender and Hannah J. Allender, before George W. King and Jesse Cloud, who took the acknowledgment the same day in Baltimore City, the four wives (the certificate calls the first 'Nancy B. Hoke') examined apart from their husbands; received to be recorded Dec. 22, 1841 at a quarter past 11 A.M. and recorded the same day (Thos. Kell, clerk); margin 'D. grantee 8th Oct 1842' (delivered, as read). Philip G. Biays, the co-trustee, is not a party, though he joined the 1844 Mumma deed (A.W.B. 354/374, row 46070). What it settles: (1) the deed recited in Litzinger's 1864 deed to John W. Treadway (G.H.C. 39/499, row 47383) is read, and it is the north piece of that lot. Its calls are 40 yards (120 ft) down the turnpike from Baden's south-west corner, 17 yards (51 ft) east to the old road, 31 yards (93 ft) up it (1864: N 20 1/2 E 95 ft) and 26 yards (78 ft) back along Baden's line (1864: N 61 W 82 ft). Laid on the 1864 courses, the line from 120 ft down the turnpike to the post where the old road bends (the end of the N 31 1/2 E 99 ft course) measures 51 ft 2 in and encloses about 6,880 sq ft (0.16 acre, against 'about the one sixth'); the other 94 ft of turnpike to the fork is the 1847 wedge (A.W.B. 381/477, row 46151), whose north line of 3 1/10 perches (51 ft 2 in) is this deed's 17-yard line. So this lot is the 'parcel ... now owned by the said Letzinger' at whose south-west corner the wedge begins, by measure as well as by the 1864 recital. (2) Stump's title is the McFadon deed of trust of April 11, 1822 (W.G. 165/492, row 46094) and nothing else is recited: the grantors are one of its two trustees, its life tenant, Sarah Biays, and the four Biays daughters who held the remainder, with their husbands; the same couples sold the wedge in 1847 after Stump's trustee's deed of 1845 (A.W.B. 359/136, row 46130). (3) The tract is named, but hedged: 'adjoining or belonging to' Ensor's Inspection. (4) By the City frontages (3015, 15 ft; 3017, 19 ft 2 in; 3019 and 3021, the 33-ft Aull lot of 1898; 3023, 28 ft; 3025, 33 ft; 128 ft 2 in in all, against 120) and the 1915 depths (46 ft 3 in at 3015 rising to 75 ft at 3025, against 51 ft at this lot's south line and about 75 ft square to the turnpike at Baden's line), this lot carries 3015 to 3025 and the wedge 3011 and 3013 (72 ft 4 in): an inference from the measures, good to about 8 ft. What it does not settle: whether the strip lies in Ensor's Inspection or in Huntington, whose leasehold of 1809 lay on the same strip north of Baden's lot (row 46153); how it came into McFadon's 1822 ground (no course or Moale lot is given; that it is the front of Moale's Lot 3 of 1819, sold 'subject to a County road' through its front, with buildings on the road let for 22 years (as read there) from May 26, 1819, W.G. 160/582, row 46129, is a lead, not shown); why Philip G. Biays did not join, which may explain the quitclaim form; the lessor and date of William Baden's lot, already there in 1841 (chapters 12 and 13); and what stood on the lot.
