summary: Sub-lease, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.B. No. 1338, folios 248 to 250 (MSA CE 168-1346; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 248 to 252, at 150 and 300 dpi). The scan pages hold, in order: the end of John T. Ensor's release to Henry C. Zoll (top of 248; its opening, and the mortgage it recites, are on 247, not saved); this sub-lease (248 to 250); Zoll's mortgage of the same 35 ft to the Loyola Perpetual Building Association (250 to 252); and, on the facing edge of 253, the start of an unrelated assignment. Dated March 17, 1891. Charles Hamilton of Baltimore City sub-leases to Henry C. Zoll of the same place a lot on the east side of the York Turnpike Road 'at the distance of two hundred and four feet and six inches northerly from the beginning of the Land assigned by Samuel H Tagart Trustee to George C H Coffield' (January 31, 1865, Balt. Co. J.H.L. 43/548), the beginning 'designed to be at a post standing at the northwest corner of said whole tract'; S 2 W 35 ft along the turnpike, S 85 1/2 E 126 ft more or less to the west side of the Old York road, N 19 1/2 E 35 ft more or less to a post at the north-east corner of the whole ground, N 85 1/2 W 140 ft 6 in to the beginning. Title: 'Being a part of the ground conveyed by Martin Kratt to said Charles Hamilton by deed of Assignment dated July 2nd 1870 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County in liber E H A No 67 folio 41'. Term: 'all the rest and residue save one day of the term of years yet to come'. Rent $175 a year in half-yearly instalments from March 1, 1891, over and above all taxes and assessments; distress for arrears; re-entry after 60 days until paid, and after six months as if the sub-lease had never been made. Hamilton warrants against claims under himself and for 'any other or greater rent', and on a $10 renewal fine will give a new sub-lease reserving one day, with 'a covenant for perpetual renewment'. No building covenant and no buyout. Witnessed by John Willis and acknowledged by both parties the same day before him as justice of the peace; recorded April 10, 1891 at 4:45 p.m. (Jas. Bond, Clerk). The release above it (John T. Ensor, $1, acknowledged March 26, 1891) frees 'the sub lease hold interest' from 'the mortgage above recited', 'leaving said mortgage however as to the other lot and the portion of the lot described in the deed from Kratt aforesaid not embraced in said sublease to Zoll in full force', and also as to the sub-reversion. Zoll's mortgage (March 20, 1891: an advance of $1,250 on ten shares, weekly dues of 25 cents and interest of 17 cents a share, consent to a decree under Article 4, sections 692 to 704 of the Public Local Laws; acknowledged before John J. Dunn, J.P., with Philip Walsh Jr., the association's president) puts the corner post 'about four hundred and sixteen feet northerly from the intersection of the York Turnpike and the Old York road'. All three were recorded April 10, 1891 at 4:45 p.m. What it settles: (1) how Hamilton held the 79 ft lot: by assignment from Martin Kratt on July 2, 1870, so the leasehold gap after George Vandyke Smith (1868) narrows to Smith to Kratt, 1868 to 1870; (2) the courses and terms of the $175 sub-rent that the 1898, 1904, 1905 and 1907 papers carry; (3) John T. Ensor already held a mortgage on the Kratt lot in March 1891, which makes his 1898 decree sale as trustee probably a foreclosure of it (inference: the mortgage's maker is named on 247, not saved, and that it was Hamilton is an inference from his title); (4) the 416 ft figure is about the 1896 wedge's 214 ft on the turnpike plus the Coffield frontage (198 ft by the 1865 courses, 204 ft 6 in to the corner post by these), so the fee-simple wedge at 3011 to 3019 and the Coffield tract very probably meet at Baden's south line with nothing between them (inference). What it does not settle: the mortgage's maker, date and liber, what 'the other lot' was, how Kratt took the lot from Smith, and whether a stable stood on the 35 ft in 1891. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 4): two open points are read. The mortgage was Hamilton's and was foreclosed: John T. Ensor, 'Assignee of Mortgage', sued Charles Hamilton in Circuit Court No. 2 and took a decree on June 1, 1895, and as trustee sold the 79 ft leasehold to John S. Ensor on about August 8, 1895 for $4,600 (R.O. 1725/20; 742:mdlr-ro1725-20-ensor-trustee-john-s-ensor-1898). Kratt held the lot jointly with Joseph M. Cone from May 1869 (E.H.A. 62/262), took Cone's interest in July 1869 (E.H.A. 63/71) and assigned to Hamilton in 1870 (E.H.A. 67/41, read; 742:mdlr-eha67-41-kratt-hamilton-79ft-leasehold-1870). The mortgage's date, first mortgagee and liber are still only on J.B. 1338/247. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 5): folios 246 to 247 are read. The mortgage recited is Charles Hamilton and wife to John T. Ensor, Apr. 21, 1886, $1,000, Baltimore County mortgage records J.W.S. 121/373, on the Kratt lot and 'another lot' not described (742:mdlr-jb1338-247-ensor-partial-release-zoll-1891). A second release to Zoll, the same day, from the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County, frees the 35 ft from Hamilton's mortgage to it of Oct. 19, 1889 (J.B. 1263/413), 'for the sole accommodation of said Hamilton' (742:mdlr-jb1338-246-waverly-bldg-assn-release-zoll-1891). Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 6): the 'another lot' of Ensor's 1886 mortgage is Margaret Hamilton's 1874 west-side lease (J.B. 86/487, row 46255), read in J.W.S. 121/373 (742:mdlr-jws121-373-hamilton-ensor-mortgage-1000-1886).

summary: Deed of assignment, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. No. 1725, folios 22 to 24 (MSA CE 168-1733; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 22 to 26, at 150 and 300 dpi). The scan pages hold, in order: the end of John T. Ensor, Trustee's deed to John S. Ensor (top of 22; its opening, with the case, the decree and the price, is on the folio or folios before, not saved); this assignment (22 to 24); Augustus D. Clemens Jr.'s mortgage of the same lot to the Loyola Perpetual Building Association (24 to 26); and John and Eliza Savage's mortgage of a Bartlett Street lot to the same association (26, unrelated). Dated March 15, 1898. John S. Ensor of Baltimore County, 'in consideration of Four Thousand dollars', assigns Augustus D. Clemens Jr. 'of said County and State' the lot beginning on the east side of the York Turnpike Road 125 ft 6 in north of the beginning of the land Samuel H. Tagart, trustee, assigned to George C. H. Coffield (January 31, 1865, J.H.L. 43/548), the beginning 'designed to be at a point or place where a line drawn westerly from a point four feet northerly from the north side of the two story house erected on the lot next adjoining on the south would intersect the east side of said Turnpike Road'; N 2 E 79 ft to a post at the north-west corner of the whole Coffield tract, S 85 1/2 E 140 ft 6 in to a post on the west side of the Old York Road, S 19 1/2 W 78 ft 6 in along it, N 86 1/4 W 119 ft to the beginning. Title: 'Being the same lot of ground described in a deed from John T. Ensor, Trustee to said John S. Ensor dated February 26th, 1898 and recorded among the Land Records of said City immediately prior hereto'. For the rest of the term, renewable forever, subject to the $150 rent (March and September) and 'to the operation of a sub-lease from Charles Hamilton to Henry C. Zoll of the northernmost thirty-five feet of said lot dated March 17th 1891' (J.B. 1338/248), reserving $175, 'but with the right to collect said annual sub-rent'. Special warranty. Witnessed by Geo. McCaffray and acknowledged before him as justice of the peace on March 15; recorded March 22, 1898 at 12 noon (Robt. Ogle, Clerk); a margin note records delivery to the grantee on April 6, 1898. The trustee's deed above it, made under a decree of Circuit Court No. 2 of Baltimore City (the sale 'duly reported to and ratified and confirmed', the purchase money paid), conveys for $5 'all the aforesaid leasehold property' and 'all the right title interest and estate of the parties to the aforesaid decree', 'and especially the annual sub-rent of One Hundred and seventy-five dollars above mentioned', subject to the annual rent and 'to the estate term and interest of the Sub-Lessee as to the part thereof above mentioned'; signed John T. Ensor, Trustee, witnessed by McCaffray, acknowledged February 26, 1898, recorded with this deed on March 22. Clemens's mortgage (March 15, 1898) secures an advance of $3,000 on 24 shares (weekly dues of 25 cents and interest of 15 cents a share; fire insurance of at least $2,000; consent to a decree), describes the lot by reference to this deed, 'Subject to the annual rent of $150. but with the right to collect an annual sub-rent of $175'; acknowledged before John J. Dunn, J.P., with Francis P. K. Walsh, the association's president; recorded March 22, 1898. What it settles: (1) how John S. Ensor held: by a trustee's deed under a Circuit Court No. 2 decree, made three weeks before he assigned to Clemens and recorded with that assignment; (2) John T. Ensor held a mortgage on the Kratt lot in 1891 (his release, top of J.B. 1338/248), so the decree was probably the foreclosure of that mortgage, and the mortgage very probably Hamilton's (both inferences), which closes the Hamilton-to-Ensor gap in outline; (3) Clemens paid $4,000, three-quarters of it advanced by the Loyola association, for the 79 ft lot with the $175 sub-rent. What it does not settle: the case name, the decree's date, the sale price and the trustee's own description (all on the folio before 22), what 'the other lot' in the 1891 mortgage was, and whether the 1898 Loyola mortgage was paid before Clemens sold to Dietrich in 1907. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 4): the trustee's deed's opening is read (R.O. 1725/20 to 21; 742:mdlr-ro1725-20-ensor-trustee-john-s-ensor-1898). The case was John T. Ensor, Assignee of Mortgage v. Charles Hamilton, Circuit Court No. 2 of Baltimore City, decree of June 1, 1895; the sale to John S. Ensor was on or about August 8, 1895 for $4,600; the trustee's description is the 79 ft lot only, 'the same lot' Kratt assigned to Hamilton in 1870 (E.H.A. 67/41). So the decree was a mortgage foreclosure against Hamilton, no longer an inference, and John S. Ensor resold to Clemens for $600 less than his bid.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. No. 2123, folios 235 to 237 (MSA CE 168-2131; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 235 to 239, at 150 and 300 dpi). The scan pages hold, in order: the end of an unrelated deed by Charles Nitze, trustee, Alice W. and Robert Garrett, and John W. Garrett by attorney (top of 235); this deed (235 to 237); Benjamin and Fannie Strouse's deed to Samuel S. Weinberg of 117 West Lombard Street, $15,500 (237 to 238); and the Assurance Permanent Loan and Savings Association's release to the administrators of Mary C. Miller, with their deed to Mary T. White of a Patterson Park Avenue leasehold (239); all unrelated. Dated January 31, 1905. W. Frank Tucker and Elmer J. Cook, Receivers, convey to John H. Dietrich of Baltimore City, for $300, Zoll's 35 ft leasehold. Recitals: a decree of Circuit Court No. 2 of Baltimore City of February 9, 1903, 'in a cause in said Court between James T Lynch et al Complainants and the Equitable Building Loan and Investment Association of Baltimore City Defendant', appointed Tucker, Cook and William A. Casler receivers of the association; a decree of March 5, 1903 confirmed Tucker and Cook and discharged Casler; an order of April 16, 1903 authorized them to foreclose the association's mortgages in default; they did so 'in the case of W Frank Tucker and Elmer J Cook Receivers vs. Henry C Zoll for the sale of the property hereinafter described' (Docket 12 B, folio 158, 1903; the last digit is uncertain); by a decree in that case 'Omer F Hershey was appointed Trustee to sell said property', and he 'sold said property to said W Frank Tucker and Elmer J Cook Receivers of said Equitable Building Loan and Investment Association of Baltimore City at and for the sum of five hundred dollars', the sale ratified and the property conveyed to them 'by deed dated October 29th 1904 and duly recorded' (no liber given); a decree in the Lynch case dated May 1 (the year is crossed by a scan artifact) let them sell at private sale; and on or about December 5, 1904 they sold to Dietrich. The lot: 204 ft 6 in north of the Coffield beginning (J.H.L. 43/548), at the post at the north-west corner of the whole tract; S 2 W 35 ft along the turnpike, S 85 1/2 E 126 ft more or less to the Old York Road, N 19 1/2 E 35 ft more or less to a post at the north-east corner of the whole lot, N 85 1/2 W 140 ft 6 in. To hold for the rest of the term, renewable forever, 'subject however to the payment of the annual rent of $175' (March and September). Witnessed by H. L. Drake and acknowledged January 31, 1905 before Harry L. Drake, notary; recorded February 4, 1905 at 11:50 a.m. (Robt. Ogle, Clerk). A margin stamp reads 'Grantee T APR 27 1927': the deed was taken out of the office nine days before C. Reese Dietrich's deed of May 6, 1927 (S.C.L. 4735/61), probably for that conveyance (inference). What it settles: (1) the receivers were those of the Equitable Building Loan and Investment Association of Baltimore City, in receivership from February 1903; (2) the 1904 Hershey sale of the stable lot at 1027 York Road was their foreclosure against Zoll: they bought the 35 ft in for $500, took Hershey's deed on October 29, 1904, and sold it to Dietrich for $300, so this deed completes the 1904 sale in two steps; (3) by 1903 Zoll's sub-leasehold carried a mortgage to the Equitable, so his 1891 Loyola mortgage had presumably been paid off or refinanced (inference). What it does not settle: the date, amount and liber of Zoll's mortgage to the Equitable, the liber of Hershey's 1904 deed, and the date of the auction at which the receivers bought (probably the March 14, 1904 sale the Sun advertised, inference).

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Circuit Court land records, Liber J.B. 84, folios 381 to 382 (MSA CE 62-84; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 381 to 386, at 150 and 300 dpi). The deed opens at the head of folio 381 under the caption 'James E. Sinclair & wife Deed to Mrs. Mary F. Ridgely'; the rest of the scan holds John T. Ensor and E. Beatty Graff, trustees, to Sarah A. Gross, about four acres near the Belair Road (Oct. 3, 1873, 382 to 384), George S. Clogg's assignment to Louis H. Reitz of a lot on Oak Street (Nov. 7, 1873, 384 to 386) and John N. Foss to Bauer and Bushe, a third of a water main in Canton (Dec. 26, 1873, 386). Made Oct. 31, 1873. James E. Sinclair and Sarah C. Sinclair his wife, of Baltimore County, for $600 'grant and convey unto the said Mary F. Ridgely her heirs and assigns in fee', she being 'wife of Dr Aquila S. [?] Ridgely of the same place', 'All that Lot or parcel of ground situate in said County, adjacent to the Village of Waverly': 'Beginning for the same on the west side of the York Turnpike Road at the distance of one hundred and fifty feet southwardly from a point where a line drawn along the Northernmost end wall of a stone house standing on the Lot of ground lately leased by David S. Wilson and others Trustees to J. H. Hartman' meets the turnpike, also 475 ft south of Wilson Street, '& being the south east corner of Lot No 7 as conveyed by said Wilson &c Trustees to P. P. Pendleton'; west along Pendleton's south line 190 ft 'to the East side of an alley, twenty feet wide to be kept open for the common use of the Lot hereby conveyed & other Lots bounding thereon'; south along the alley 30 ft more or less; east 190 ft to the turnpike; and north 30 ft on the turnpike to the beginning. Recital: '(Being part of the Lot described in a Lease from said Wilson &c Trustees to said James E. Sinclair dated the 1st October 1872, and Recorded in Liber E.H.A. No 77 folio 361 &c, and also in a Deed in fee from said Wilson &c Trustees to said James E. Sinclair dated the 24th day of October 1873 & duly recorded)'. With the improvements; special warranty and further assurances. Witness Frank C. Lewis [?], justice of the peace for Baltimore County, before whom both Sinclairs acknowledged on Oct. 31, 1873; recorded Dec. 31, 1873 (John Bacon, Clerk); margin 'Delivered to [J. H. ?] Ridgely per ticket July 28th 1874'. What it settles: (1) the Wilson lot was split a week after Sinclair bought its fee: he sold its north 30 ft, the 30 by 190 ft strip against Pendleton's Lot 7, to Mary F. Ridgely for $600, and kept the south 14 1/2 ft on the turnpike with the wedge back to Merryman's Lane. (2) The deed was recorded ahead of the Wilson trustees' deed it recites (J.B. 84/387, the same day), which is how the 1887 Sinclair deed to Brown (J.W.S. 162/70) came to cite the Wilson deed as 'J.B. No 84 fol 381': the folio is a slip for 387, as the 1884 Harris recital has it (inference that the conveyancer took the first Sinclair entry of Dec. 31, 1873). (3) It moves the Brown-Wilson line. Sinclair still owned the frontage from 132 ft 8 in to 197 ft north of the lane when he sold it to Alice P. Harris in 1884 (W.M.I. 141/405), so unless he bought the Ridgely strip back (no deed seen), the strip lies at or north of 197 ft, and the old division fence met the turnpike at or north of about 182 1/2 ft, not at Huff's 165 ft. If Sinclair's ground ended at the Ridgely line, 3224 (181 ft 4 in to 197 ft) is all but the whole 14 1/2 ft Sinclair kept, still Wilson-estate ground (inference from the measurements; no plat seen). What it does not settle: where the Ridgely strip went later (the Baker Block, 3226 to 3240, bought in 1925 a 33 by 191 ft 2 in lot from Edward N. Rich, trustee, and others, row 23946; whether that is this strip is untested), who Mary F. and Dr. Aquila Ridgely were, and the position of the Brown-Wilson line on a plat.

summary: Deed of assignment, Baltimore County land records, Liber E.H.A. No. 67, folios 41 to 42 (MSA CE 62-67; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 41 to 45, at 150 and 300 dpi). The scan pages hold, in order: this assignment (41 to 42); Bernhard Hlading's assignment to Louis Muth of a Bel Air Road lot, July 2, 1870, $1,700 (42 to 43); Jane Cecilia Broadbent, widow, to her daughter Cecilia Estelle Stambaugh, wife of John P. Stambaugh, dated March 12, 1870 and recorded July 5, 1870, of a lot on the west side of the York Turnpike Road, part of the ground Townsend Scott and others conveyed to James Bryan in trust for her in 1846 (A.W.B. 373/240), 125 ft on the turnpike (44 to 45); and the start of William J. Wilkinson Jr.'s deed to Stephen J. Bond (45). Only the first concerns 3117. Dated July 2, 1870. Recitals: 'Whereas the said Martin Kratt was heretofore jointly interested in a term of years in the property hereinafter described with a certain Joseph M. Cone' (the surname could be read McCone), by a deed dated on or about May 8, 1869 (the day word is probably 'eighth') and recorded in E.H.A. No. 62, folio 262; and Cone, by a deed dated on or about July 30, 1869 and recorded in E.H.A. No. 63, folio 71 (the folio is not certain), 'assigned his interest in said property to said Martin Kratt'. For 'five hundred dollars', Martin Kratt of Baltimore County grants Charles Hamilton of Baltimore County the lot beginning on the east side of the York Turnpike Road 125 ft 6 in north of the beginning of the land Samuel H. Tagart, trustee, assigned to George C. H. Coffield (January 31, 1865, J.H.L. 43/548), the beginning 'designed to be at the point or place where a line drawn westerly from a point four feet northerly from the north side of the two story house erected on the lot next adjoining on the south would intersect' the turnpike; N 2 E 79 ft to a post at the north-west corner of the whole Coffield tract, S 85 1/2 E 140 ft 6 in to a post on the west side of the Old York Road, S 19 1/2 W 78 ft 6 in along it, N 86 1/4 W 119 ft to the beginning. 'Together with the buildings thereupon'; for the residue of the term with the benefit of renewal forever, 'subject to the payment of the annual rent of one hundred and fifty dollars payable semi-annually on the first day of March and September'. Special warranty. Witnessed by A. Robinson and acknowledged before him as justice of the peace for Baltimore City on July 2, 1870, with George Robinson's clerk's certificate; recorded July 2, 1870 (Edward H. Ady, Clerk). The margins carry a delivery note and revenue-stamp entries. What it settles: (1) how Hamilton held: Kratt's assignment of July 2, 1870 for $500, the deed the 1891 sub-lease and the 1898 trustee's deed both cite; (2) after George Vandyke Smith's 1868 sub-lease the term was held jointly by Kratt and Joseph M. Cone under a deed of May 1869 (E.H.A. 62/262), and Cone assigned his share to Kratt in July 1869 (E.H.A. 63/71), so the leasehold gap after Smith is now that one deed, whose grantor is not named here (probably Smith, inference); (3) the lot is the 79 ft by the 1868 courses and nothing more, so the 1891 release's 'lot described in the deed from Kratt' is this lot; (4) the price, $500 for a lot under a $150 rent, fits ground with little on it, and Hamilton opened 'the new Waverly Hotel' in December 1873 at a place Polk later numbers 1025 York Road (3113, inside this lot), so he probably built the hotel here after 1870 (inference). What it does not settle: the grantor and price in E.H.A. 62/262 (whether Smith assigned directly), who Joseph M. Cone was, and what the 'buildings' were in 1870. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 5): E.H.A. 62/262 is read (742:mdlr-eha62-262-treadway-bruns-heise-cone-kratt-1869). It is dated May 6, 1869 (so the recital's day word is very probably 'sixth', not 'eighth'), recorded May 7; John W. Treadway, John Bruns and William Heise assigned the lot to Joseph M. Cone and Martin Kratt for $800, holding it from 'John C Smith' by a deed of Oct. 14, 1868 (E.H.A. 59/471). So the grantor was not Smith directly, and Kratt and Cone paid $800 for what Kratt sold to Hamilton for $500. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 6): E.H.A. 59/471 is read: Treadway, Bruns and Heise took the lot from George Vandyke Smith himself (Oct. 14, 1868, $325), so the batch 5 note's 'not Smith directly' is superseded; the chain is Smith, Treadway and partners, Cone and Kratt, Kratt, Hamilton. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 7): E.H.A. 63, folios 71 to 78, is read (742:mdlr-eha63-71-78-cone-kratt-assignment-not-on-folios-1869-negative): Cone's assignment to Kratt is not there. Those folios were recorded June 26 to 29, 1869, a month before the recited date, so the recital's folio is probably misread (171, 271 or 371; inference). Update Oct. 17, 2026 (3117 index 1869 Cone): the County index puts Cone's assignment to Kratt at E.H.A. 63/271, recorded August 3, 1869 (742:index-1851-1874-v2-cone-joseph-m-1869-1870), so this deed's '63, folio 71' dropped a '2'. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (3117 E.H.A. 63/271 read): Cone's assignment is read (E.H.A. 63/271 to 273, July 30, 1869; 742:mdlr-eha63-271-cone-kratt-half-79ft-leasehold-1869): $50 and Kratt's payment of three purchase-money notes given to Treadway and others. Every transfer from Coffield's 1868 sub-lease to this deed is now read.

summary: Trustee's deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. No. 1725, folios 20 to 22 (MSA CE 168-1733; read 2026-10-16 from two scans Jeff saved: folios 18 to 21, which hold the opening (MSA CE 168-1733 p.00018 to p.00021.pdf), and folios 22 to 26, which hold the end (MSA CE 168-1733 p.00022 to p.00026.pdf); at 150 and 300 dpi). Folios 18 to 20 above it hold, unrelated: the end of Shepard G. Miller's deed to William W. Oster of an Aisquith Street ground rent; the Locust Point Building Association's release to Anna C. Weaver; and Carl and Lisette Peine's deed to Fredericke Glindmeier of a Bel Air Road leasehold, all March 22, 1898. Dated February 26, 1898. John T. Ensor of Baltimore County, Trustee, to John S. Ensor of the same county. Recital: 'by a decree of the Circuit Court No. 2 of Baltimore City dated on the first day of June in the year one thousand eight hundred and ninety-five and passed in a Cause in said Court between John T. Ensor Assignee of Mortgage, Complainant and Charles Hamilton, Defendant', Ensor 'was appointed Trustee with Authority to Sell the Leasehold property', and 'did on or about the eighth day of August' 1895 'sell unto the said John S. Ensor at and for the sum of Forty-six Hundred ($4600.00) Dollars current money' the leasehold: the 79 ft lot by the 1868 courses (125 ft 6 in north of the Coffield beginning, J.H.L. 43/548; N 2 E 79 ft to the tract's north-west corner post; S 85 1/2 E 140 ft 6 in; S 19 1/2 W 78 ft 6 in; N 86 1/4 W 119 ft), 'Being the same lot or parcel of ground which by Deed dated the second day of July in the year one thousand eight hundred and Seventy and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County in Liber E.H.A. No. 67 folio 41 &c. was assigned by Martin Kratt to the said Charles Hamilton', subject to the $150 rent, 'The northernmost thirty-five feet of which said lot was demised and subleased by said Charles Hamilton to Henry C. Zoll' on March 17, 1891 (J.B. 1338/248) at $175. The rest is on folio 22 (read earlier the same day for row 47404): the sale 'duly reported to and ratified and confirmed' and the price paid, Ensor for $5 grants the leasehold 'and especially the annual sub-rent of One Hundred and seventy-five dollars', subject to the rent and to Zoll's term; witnessed by Geo. McCaffray and acknowledged before him February 26, 1898; recorded March 22, 1898 at noon (Robt. Ogle, Clerk), immediately before John S. Ensor's assignment to Augustus D. Clemens Jr. (R.O. 1725/22). A margin note records delivery to J. S. Ensor on April 6, 1898. What it settles: (1) the Hamilton-to-Ensor link: a mortgage foreclosure in equity by John T. Ensor, assignee of the mortgage, against Charles Hamilton, decree of June 1, 1895, so the mortgagor was Hamilton (he is the defendant); that the decree enforced the mortgage John T. Ensor released in part to Zoll in March 1891 is very probable (inference); (2) the sale was on or about August 8, 1895 at $4,600, two and a half years before the deed, and John S. Ensor resold to Clemens three weeks after the deed for $4,000; (3) the deed conveys the 79 ft lot only, so the mortgage's 'other lot' was not part of this sale. What it does not settle: the mortgage itself (its date, first mortgagee and liber, recited on J.B. 1338/247, not saved), when John T. Ensor took the assignment of it, and why the deed waited until 1898. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 5): the 1891 releases (J.B. 1338/246 to 248, read) show two mortgages by Hamilton on the lot: $1,000 to John T. Ensor himself, Apr. 21, 1886 (J.W.S. 121/373), and one to the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County, Oct. 19, 1889 (J.B. 1263/413). Because Ensor was the original mortgagee of the first, his style in this case, 'Assignee of Mortgage', fits the association's mortgage assigned to him at least as well (inference); which one the 1895 decree enforced is not shown. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 6): both mortgages are read. The 1886 one (J.W.S. 121/373) covers the 79 ft lot and Margaret Hamilton's west-side lease and has only a power of sale; the 1889 association mortgage (J.B. 1263/413, $2,080) covers the 79 ft lot only, has an assent to a decree, and was made first by Ensor's postponement. This deed conveys the 79 ft lot only, so the decree probably enforced the 1889 mortgage, assigned to Ensor (inference; the assignment is not yet found).

summary: Index entry, Baltimore City Superior Court Grantor Index 1932 (July to December), H to O, pages 483 to 486, 'McB' and 'McC' (MSA CE 167-252; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, at 150 and 300 dpi). Searched for David McCoy and his wife, and for any McCoy with the Waverly Building Association as grantee. Page 483 ('McB') has one line (Aug. 9, Margaret M. McBride to William T. Tippett Jr., assignment, south side of Gorsuch Avenue, S.C.L. 5317/414); pages 484 to 486 ('McC') run from July 6 to Dec. 31, 1932. The line for 3030 is the sixth on page 484: 'July 12, McCoy David, Mary E, Waverly Bldg Asso of Balto Co, Asst, W S Greenmount Ave', S.C.L. 5313, folio 27. The digits read 5313 and 27 plainly at 300 dpi. It is the only McCoy line on the pages and the only line on Greenmount Avenue. Three lines stand under H. Kent McCay (read 'McCay', not McCoy): a deed to Carolyn McC. Ames, July 15, south side of Mount Royal Avenue (5313/313); a deed to the same, Aug. 16, 'Real and Personal' (5318/597); and a mortgage to the Maryland Title Securities Corp. of Delaware, Dec. 6, south side of Mount Royal Avenue (5337/395). None is about 3030. What it settles: the true cite of David and Mary E. McCoy's assignment of the 3030 leasehold to The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County is S.C.L. 5313/27, indexed July 12, 1932, four days after the date the 1935 recital gives it (July 8). The 1935 lease and deed (S.C.L. 5518/171 and /173, rows 47394 and 47395) cite 'Liber S C L No 5312 folio 27': the folio is right and the liber is one too low, which is why 5312/27 held other deeds (row 47406). It also gives the wife's name, Mary E. The index line names no house, only 'W S Greenmount Ave'; that it is 3030 rests on the 1935 recital, the date and the grantee [inference, strong]. What it does not settle: how the McCoys held the 1912 Aull leasehold, whether a building-association mortgage or default stood behind the assignment, and the price; the index carries none of them. Next: S.C.L. 5313/27 (MSA CE 168-5321). Update Oct. 16, 2026 (5313/27 read): the McCoy assignment that the 1935 instruments cite as 'Liber S C L No 5312 folio 27' is recorded at S.C.L. 5313/27 (MSA CE 168-5321; Grantor Index 1932, row 47520), on a folio whose typed header reads '5312', corrected by hand to 5313. It is read (726:mdlr-scl5313-27-mccoy-waverly-bldg-assignment-3030-1932): David and Mary E. McCoy assigned the 3030 leasehold to The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County on July 8, 1932 (recorded July 12) for $5 and other valuable considerations, subject to the 1912 rent of $66 due June 1 and Dec. 1; they held it by Mary A. J. Aull's assignment of Dec. 20, 1929 (S.C.L. 5076/70). No mortgage or default is recited.

The 'Le' section runs from Jan. 9 to Dec. 23, 1890 in recording order (J.B. libers 1274 to 1324); page 224 is blank. Four lines are under 'Legg, John H. C.', on pages 217 and 219, and there is no other Legg line in 1890: (1) Apr. 3, to 'Joseph M. Cone', Deed, '2 lot S.s Lexington st.', J.B. 1286 (by ditto) folio 324 [?]; (2) Apr. 26 (by ditto), to 'Helen S. Ridgely', Deed, 'W.s York Rd.', J.B. 1289 (by ditto), folio not entered; (3) May 14, to 'David Stewart', Deed, '5 Lots', no location, J.B. 1292 (by ditto) folio 384 [?]; (4) June 30, to 'George T. Drechsler', Lease, 'W.s York Tp. Rd.', J.B. 1299 (by ditto), folio not entered. The grantor names on page 217 sit about a line below their grantees, so line (3) was matched by the order of the three entries for May 9 to 14 (Leland, Leonhardt, Legg) against the three grantees and three instruments on the right. What it settles: (a) lines (2) and (4) are the two 3224 instruments already read, Legg's reversion deed of the $48 lot to Helen Stewart Ridgely (J.B. 1289/565), recorded Apr. 26, and his $48 lease to Drechsler (J.B. 1299/406), which is dated Apr. 24, 1890 but was recorded only on June 30 (inference from the recording-order column). (b) Line (3) is Legg's only other 1890 deed, and its five lots are very probably the five foreclosure lots he had not otherwise dealt with, lots 1 to 4 and 6 of J.B. 1289/297, the 3200 apex first (inference: the count fits, and Legg acted for the Stewarts on 3224 in the same weeks). If so, the apex went back to David Stewart about May 14, 1890, three weeks after Legg took both its estates, which fits the David Stewart at 1100 York road in 1908 and the Stewart-Gerry rents of 1910 and 1911. (c) Line (1), two Lexington Street lots recorded before the foreclosure sale, is not corridor ground. What it does not settle: the May 14 deed itself (J.B. 1292/384, probably MSA CE 168-1300 by the offset of the J.B. libers, inference): which five lots, whether it carries the apex fee Legg bought from the Georges (J.B. 1289/300) as well as the leasehold, and the consideration; nor any Legg line after 1890, which would be in later index volumes. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (J.B. 1292/384 read): the deed is read (752:mdlr-jb1292-384-legg-stewart-five-lots-1890). Dated Apr. 26 and recorded May 14, 1890, it conveys foreclosure lots 1, 2, 4 and 6 and a lot 3 enlarged to 181 ft by the three southern 1888 sub-lots; lot 1 is the apex, with both the Sinclair leasehold and the George fee. Everything Legg took on Apr. 24 went back to David Stewart except the Drechsler lot (3224). The figure reads '$1100' [?].

What it does not settle: the May 14 deed itself (J.B. 1292/384, probably MSA CE 168-1300 by the offset of the J.B. libers, inference): which five lots, whether it carries the apex fee Legg bought from the Georges (J.B. 1289/300) as well as the leasehold, and the consideration; nor any Legg line after 1890, which would be in later index volumes. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (J.B. 1292/384 read): the deed is read (768:mdlr-jb1292-384-legg-stewart-five-lots-1890). Dated Apr. 26 and recorded May 14, 1890, it conveys foreclosure lots 1, 2, 4 and 6 and a lot 3 running 96 ft 1/2 in to 181 ft north of the lane, bounded north by 'the lot leased by said Legg to Drechsler', so the three southern 1888 sub-lots went back to David Stewart in fee and only 3224 stayed out. The figure reads '$1100' [?].

summary: Deed of assignment, Baltimore County land records, Liber E.H.A. No. 62, folios 262 to 264 (MSA CE 62-62; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 262 to 266, at 150 and 300 dpi with the contrast raised; the hand is faint). The scan pages hold, in order: the end of a deed by Wm. T. and Angeline A. Foster, John H. and Augusta A. Walsh (reading uncertain) and Henry and Mary A. Taylor to two copartners, Horace M. Hanman (reading uncertain) and William H. Shryock, acknowledged April 30 and recorded May 6, 1869 (top of 262); this deed (262 to 264); Sarah Hart (wife of Francis Hart Jr.) to Alice C. Sapp, May 5, 1869, $900, a lot by the Northern Central Railroad (264 to 265); and Ross and Elizabeth K. Winans to Alfred J. Ulman, March 8, 1869, $1,200 (265 to 266); none of the others concerns 3117. Dated May 6, 1869. John W. Treadway, John Bruns and William Heise, of the City of Baltimore, 'in consideration of the sum of Eight hundred dollars', 'grant and assign unto Joseph M. Cone and Martin Kratt their personal representatives and assigns' the lot on the east side of the York Turnpike Road 125 ft 6 in north of the beginning of the land Samuel H. Tagart, trustee, assigned to George C. H. Coffield (January 31, 1865, J.H.L. 43/548), by the 1868 courses: N 2 E 79 ft to a post at the north-west corner of the whole tract, S 85 1/2 E 140 ft 6 in to a post on the west side of the old York road, S 19 1/2 W 78 ft 6 in, N 86 1/4 W 119 ft. Title: 'Being the same ground which by deed dated the 14th October 1868 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County in Liber E.H.A. No. 59 folio 471 &c was assigned by John C Smith to said John W. Treadway &c subject to the annual rent of $150', payable March and September. 'Together with the improvements thereon'; for the residue of the term with renewal forever, subject to the $150 rent 'to whomever the same may be payable'. Special warranty against claims under the grantors. Signed John W. Treadway, John Bruns and Wilhelm Heise, witnessed by D. Hagerty, acknowledged before him as justice of the peace for Baltimore City on May 6, 1869 (George Robinson's clerk's certificate the same day); recorded May 7, 1869 (Edward H. Ady, Clerk). A margin note records delivery on July 28, 1869 (the name is unclear), two days before Cone's assignment to Kratt. What it settles: (1) the grantors of the 1869 deed that Kratt's 1870 assignment recites (E.H.A. 67/41): Treadway, Bruns and Heise, for $800; (2) they held by an assignment of October 14, 1868 from 'John C Smith' (E.H.A. 59/471), seven months after Coffield's sub-lease to George Vandyke Smith (E.H.A. 59/86, same liber), so the leasehold chain runs Smith (1868), Treadway, Bruns and Heise (1868), Cone and Kratt (1869), Kratt (1869), Hamilton (1870); (3) John W. Treadway is very probably the man who bought the 214 ft fee-simple lot south of Baden's lot, 3011 to 3019, from John Litzinger in 1864 (G.H.C. 39/499; an inference from the name and the place), so for a few months he held ground at both ends of the Coffield tract; (4) the price fell from $800 (1869) to $500 (1870, Kratt to Hamilton). What it does not settle: whether 'John C Smith' is a copying slip for George Vandyke Smith or a second holder between them (E.H.A. 59/471 will say), the price in 1868, who Bruns and Heise were, and what the improvements were. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 6): E.H.A. 59/471 is read (742:mdlr-eha59-471-george-vandyke-smith-treadway-bruns-heise-1868). The grantor is 'George Vandyke Smith of Baltimore County', for $325; the index heading reads 'John V. Smith', the probable source of 'John C Smith' here (inference). It names no improvements, so the rise to $800 by May 1869 suggests building in between (inference). Update Oct. 17, 2026 (3117 E.H.A. 63/271 read): Cone's assignment to Kratt (E.H.A. 63/271, read; 742:mdlr-eha63-271-cone-kratt-half-79ft-leasehold-1869) says Cone and Kratt gave Treadway and others 'three notes ... for the purchase money', so this $800 was at least partly on credit (inference).

summary: Release, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.B. No. 1338, folios 246 to 247 (MSA CE 168-1346; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 245 to 247, at 150 and 300 dpi). The scan pages hold, in order: the end of Oliver W. Audoun's sub-lease to Ann Binyon (top of 245; readings uncertain); Frederick W. and Catherine Schnaufer's assignment to Jacob Daniel and Mary E. Ortel of a Gough Street leasehold, April 10, 1891, $295 and a mortgage assumed (245 to 246); this release (246 to 247); and the opening of John T. Ensor's partial release to Zoll (247, filed separately); the first two are unrelated. Dated March 26, 1891. The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County recites that 'by a mortgage dated the 19th day of October AD 1889 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in liber J.B. No. 1263 folio 413 &c Charles Hamilton mortgaged to said body corporate the whole ground therein described and premises to secure the sums of money therein mentioned'; that Hamilton has sub-leased 'the northernmost thirty five feet of said whole ground fronting on the east side of the York Turnpike Road by a parallel depth to the Old York Road to Henry C Zoll at the yearly rent of One hundred and seventy five dollars'; and that 'for the sole accommodation of said Hamilton' it has agreed to release Zoll's leasehold, 'said mortgage to remain a lien against the balance of said whole ground and the reversion and ground rent in and to said portion'. For $1 it releases to Zoll the leasehold created by the sub-lease of March 17, 1891, 'it being agreed at the time said sub lease was delivered that this release should be executed', as fully as if the mortgage had never been made. Corporate seal (incorporated 1882), signed by Henry Joesting, President, attested by S. Seevers; acknowledged March 26, 1891 by the association's attorney (Henry W. Fox, reading uncertain) before John J. Dunn, J.P.; recorded April 10, 1891 at 4:45 p.m. (Jas. Bond, Clerk), with the sub-lease and Zoll's mortgage. What it settles: (1) Hamilton had a second mortgage on the 79 ft lot, to the Waverly Building Association, dated October 19, 1889 and recorded in the City (J.B. 1263/413), after the 1888 annexation; (2) both of Hamilton's mortgagees released Zoll's 35 ft on the same day so that Zoll could mortgage it to the Loyola association, and both kept their liens on the rest of the lot and on the $175 sub-rent. What it does not settle: the sum of the 1889 mortgage, whether it was paid before 1895, and whether it is the mortgage that John T. Ensor, styled 'Assignee of Mortgage', foreclosed against Hamilton in 1895 (R.O. 1725/20; that title fits an assigned mortgage better than his own 1886 one, an inference). Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 6): J.B. 1263/413 is read (742:mdlr-jb1263-413-hamilton-ensor-waverly-bldg-assn-mortgage-2080-1889): $2,080 on sixteen shares, on the 79 ft lot only, made a first mortgage by John T. Ensor's postponement of his 1886 mortgage, with an assent to a decree under Article 4, sections 692 to 704; it replaced Hamilton's 1885 association mortgage (W.M.I. 116/300), released the same day. It is probably the mortgage Ensor foreclosed as 'Assignee of Mortgage' in 1895 (inference; no assignment is noted on the folios).

summary: Partial release of mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.B. No. 1338, folios 247 to 248 (MSA CE 168-1346; read 2026-10-16 from two scans Jeff saved: folios 245 to 247, which hold the opening (MSA CE 168-1346 p.00245 to p.00247.pdf), and folios 248 to 252, which hold the end (MSA CE 168-1346 p.00248 to p.00252.pdf), at 150 and 300 dpi). The Waverly Building Association's release to Zoll precedes it on 246 to 247 and is filed separately. Dated March 26, 1891. John T. Ensor of Baltimore County recites: 'Whereas Charles Hamilton and wife by deed of Mortgage dated April 21st 1886 and recorded among the mortgage records of Baltimore County in liber J.W.S. No. 121 folio 373 &c conveyed to the said John T Ensor together with another lot the lot of ground particularly described in a deed from Martin Kratt to the said Charles Hamilton dated July 2nd 1870 and recorded among the Land records of said County in liber E.H.A. No 67 folio 41 &c to secure the payment of One thousand dollars with interest'; and that Hamilton, by a sub-lease of March 17, 1891 'intended to be recorded simultaneously herewith', sub-leased Zoll the portion beginning 'at a post standing at the northwest corner of the whole lot conveyed by Tagart Trustee to George C H Coffield which point of beginning is on the east side of the York Turnpike Road about 416 feet northerly from the intersection of the York Turnpike and the Old York Road', S 2 W 35 ft, S 85 1/2 E 126 ft more or less to the Old York Road, and so on. The end (folio 248, read earlier the same day for row 47403): for $1 Ensor releases 'the sub lease hold interest' to Zoll, 'leaving said mortgage however as to the other lot and the portion of the lot described in the deed from Kratt aforesaid not embraced in said sublease to Zoll in full force', and also as to the sub-reversion; acknowledged March 26, 1891; recorded April 10, 1891 at 4:45 p.m. What it settles: (1) the mortgage the release recites: Charles Hamilton and his wife to John T. Ensor, April 21, 1886, $1,000 with interest, Baltimore County mortgage records J.W.S. 121/373, on the Kratt lot (the 79 ft) and 'another lot' not described here; (2) Ensor was the original mortgagee, not an assignee, so whether his 1895 suit as 'Assignee of Mortgage' (R.O. 1725/20) enforced this mortgage or the Waverly Building Association's of 1889 (J.B. 1263/413), assigned to him, is open (inference either way); (3) Hamilton carried two mortgages on the lot by 1889, $1,000 to Ensor and the association's. What it does not settle: what 'the other lot' was (probably Hamilton's ground elsewhere in Waverly, inference), and which mortgage the 1895 decree enforced. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 6): the 1886 mortgage is read (J.W.S. 121/373; 742:mdlr-jws121-373-hamilton-ensor-mortgage-1000-1886). 'The other lot' is Margaret Hamilton's lease of Apr. 16, 1874 from William Thomas Wilson (J.B. 86/487, row 46255 on 2958 Greenmount), 100 ft on the west side of the turnpike south of A. G. Mott's lot. That mortgage has a power of sale only; the association's 1889 mortgage (J.B. 1263/413, read), on the 79 ft lot only, has an assent to a decree and was made first by Ensor's postponement, so the 1895 decree probably enforced it, assigned to Ensor (inference).

summary: Assignment of a leasehold, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5313, folios 27 to 28 (MSA CE 168-5321; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 27 to 31, at 150 and 300 dpi). The odd-numbered folios carry a typed header '5312' with a '3' written over the last digit by hand, which very probably explains why the 1935 lease and deed cite this instrument as 'Liber S C L No 5312 folio 27' [inference]. Folio 27 opens with the end of Mary A. Slatter's deed of assignment of another leasehold (acknowledged July 12, 1932 before Edwin M. Klitch; recorded at 2:31 P.M.). Folios 28 to 31 hold the Lanvale Building and Loan Association's release to Elwood L. Bowman; Stephen F. and Pauline F. Schwartz's assignment of 2415 Fait Avenue to Jakub Zborzynski and his $1,000 mortgage to the Polish American Building Association; and Charles H. and Martha E. Bradenbaugh's deed of four lots (2741 W. Fairmount Avenue and others) to Charles L. Bradenbaugh, all recorded July 12, 1932; none is about 3030. Margin heading 'David McCoy &c Asst to Waverly Bldg Asso of Balto Co' (clerk's number 20), with the stamp note '1-50¢ US S Canld'. Dated July 8, 1932. David McCoy and Mary E. McCoy his wife, of Baltimore City, 'in consideration of the sum of five dollars and other valuable considerations', grant and convey to The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County, a body corporate, the lot on the west side of 'Greenmount Avenue formerly the York Turnpike Road' 29 ft north of the north side of 'Vineyard Lane formerly Gilmor Lane', 14 by 82 ft to a 4-ft alley, between partition walls, 'Known as No 3030 Greenmount Avenue'. Title recital: 'BEING the same lot of ground which by Assignment dated the 20th day of December 1929 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber SCL No 5076 folio 70 was conveyed by Mary A J Aull to the said Grantors'. To hold 'for all the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein with the benefit of renewal forever subject to the payment of the annual rent of Sixty six($66.00)Dollars payable half yearly on the first days of June and December'; special warranty and further assurances. Signed David McCoy and Mary E. McCoy; witness Elisebeth H. Yearley; acknowledged July 8, 1932 before Elisebeth H. Yearley, notary; recorded July 12, 1932 at 2:20 P.M., Stephen C. Little, Clerk. What it settles: (1) the McCoys held the 1912 Aull leasehold, by the assignment of Mary A. J. Aull, Jacob H. Aull's widow (he died Oct. 12, 1921), of Dec. 20, 1929 (S.C.L. 5076/70); the Aulls had kept 3030 since Alice M. Chapman's assignment back to Jacob in 1916. (2) The rent on it was the 1912 rent, $66 due June 1 and Dec. 1, the same days as on 3028 (S.C.L. 3770/255), so the reversion was the one the Hooper trustees held; the Association held the 1912 leasehold from July 1932 and bought that reversion on Feb. 18, 1935, and the two merged in it [inference: no merger clause is read]. (3) The true cite of the assignment is S.C.L. 5313/27 (Grantor Index 1932, row 47520), not 5312/27 (row 47406). What it does not settle: why the McCoys assigned 3030 to a building association. No mortgage, debt or default is recited and no price is stated; the single 50-cent stamp points to a consideration of $500 or less [inference], far under the $1,932 the 1915 City roll put on the lot and house, which fits a deed in lieu of foreclosure on a building-association loan [inference, not read]. How Mary A. J. Aull held the leasehold (by Jacob's will or a deed from him) is not stated. Next: S.C.L. 5076/70 (MSA CE 168-5084) and the folios after it, where a McCoy purchase-money mortgage would be recorded. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (1929 and 1935 read): S.C.L. 5517/92 (MSA CE 168-5525, read; 726:mdlr-scl5517-92-hooper-trustees-waverly-bldg-redemption-3030-1935) is the deed of Feb. 18, 1935 by which Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore and William Jenkins, trustees under Francis X. Hooper's will, on the Waverly Building Association's statutory notice to redeem, conveyed it the 1912 $66 reversion on 3030 for $1,100, 'to the end and intent that the leasehold estate created by the lease aforesaid shall be merged with the fee'. So the trustees of the 1935 recitals are Hooper's, and the 1912 lease and rent on 3030 merged in the Association by that deed, not by inference. S.C.L. 5076/70 and /71 (MSA CE 168-5084, read) show how the leasehold reached the McCoys: Jacob H. Aull's executors deeded it to his widow Mary A. J. Aull on Oct. 11, 1922 (S.C.L. 3918/495, recited), she assigned it to David and Mary E. McCoy on Dec. 20, 1929, and they mortgaged it the same day to the Waverly Building Association for a $3,120 purchase-money advance on 24 shares, released only on Mar. 15, 1951 (M.L.P. 8386/69). Their 1932 assignment to that lender was very probably in lieu of foreclosure [inference].

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.B. 1292, folios 384 to 386 (MSA CE 168-1300; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 384 to 388, at 150 and 300 dpi). The scan also holds the end of H. Kent McCay, trustee, to Narcissa McCay, a lot on the west side of North Charles Street south of Eager Street (acknowledged in Jefferson County, Alabama, Apr. 28, 1890); the Mount Royal Land, Loan and Improvement Company of Baltimore County's release to Noble H. Creager of Erastus B. Tucker's mortgage (J.B. 1252/212), signed by Lennox Birckhead, president (May 13, 1890, 386 to 387); and Valentine and Anna Diller's assignment of a lot on Shuter Street to the Bohemian Permanent Building and Savings Association 'Slovanstvo' (May 14, 1890, 388). Entry 223. Made Apr. 26, 1890 'by John H. C. Legg to David Stewart both of Baltimore City'. For '$1100' (a raised mark follows the figure; $1,100 is the likely reading) Legg 'doth hereby grant assign and convey unto the said David Stewart All those five lots of ground lying in Baltimore City (formerly in Waverly Baltimore County)'. (1) The apex: from the corner of the north-east side of Merryman's Lane and the west side of the York Turnpike, 36 ft 1/2 in north 'to the centre of the division wall between the house on the lot now being described and the house on the adjoining lot on the North', west through the wall 42 ft in all to the lane, and south-east 55 ft on the lane, '(Being the lot the Leasehold in which vested in said Legg by a deed from David Stewart and the fee by a deed from Lucy C. George both deeds having been recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City on April 24th AD 1890)'. (2) On the south-west side of the lane from 7 ft 8 1/2 in north-west of the turnpike, 102 ft 6 in on the lane, 66 ft 7 in south and 78 ft 1 1/2 in east to the beginning: the lot David Stewart leased to Sarah C. Sinclair on May 28, 1887 (J.W.S. 160/403), 'subject to a ground rent of $80 redeemable after five years at six per cent payable March and September', assigned to Legg by Stewart. (3) On the west side of the turnpike from 96 ft 1/2 in north of the lane, 84 ft 11 1/2 in north, then west 'at right angles with said turnpike or nearly so bounding on the lot leased by said Legg to Drechsler' 100 ft to a three-foot alley, back down the alley and 100 ft east: '(For title see two deeds from David Stewart and wife to said Legg dated April 23rd 1890 and recorded prior hereto said deeds vesting this lot in said Legg in fee)'. (4) On the north-east side of the lane from 134 ft 7 in north-west of the turnpike, at the corner of a three-foot alley 100 ft west of the road, 72 ft 4 in on the lane, 63 ft 8 1/4 in north, 55 ft east to the alley and 110 ft 1 in down it, held in fee from Stewart. (5) On the south-west side of the lane west of the alley, 97 ft west 'to the Western outline of all Sinclair's original property', 75 ft 6 in north to the lane and about 125 ft back along it: 'the same lot intended to be leased by Robert Riddell Brown to James E. Sinclair by deed dated December 22nd 1887' (J.W.S. 167/165), 'subject to an annual rent of $50 payable December 22 and June 22 and redeemable after fifteen years at five percent'. 'It being intended to comprise in this deed all the property heretofore granted to said Legg by said David Stewart and wife and by Lucy C. George and husband by deeds recorded April 24th 1890 excepting the lot leased by said Legg to George T. Drechsler.' With the buildings; to Stewart 'absolutely subject however as to the leasehold lots to the aforesaid ground rents'; special warranty and further assurances. Witness Robert A. Thursby, J.P. for Baltimore City, before whom Legg acknowledged on Apr. 26, 1890; received for record May 14, 1890 at 9:55 a.m. and recorded the same day (Jas. Bond, Clerk); margin 'Grantee Nov 11 [?] 90'. What it settles: (a) the apex left Legg two days after he took it. Lot 1 is the apex, and both estates passed, the Sinclair leasehold from the foreclosure deed (J.B. 1289/297) and the fee carrying the $60 rent from the Georges (J.B. 1289/300), so from Apr. 26, 1890 David Stewart held the apex whole (that the lease merged is an inference; the deed does not use the word). (b) The five lots are foreclosure lots 1, 2, 4 and 6 and a third lot running from 96 ft 1/2 in to 181 ft north of the lane: foreclosure lot 3 (96 ft 1/2 in to 132 ft 8 in) joined to the three southern lots of the 1888 sub-lease (132 ft 8 in to 181 ft), which Legg held in fee and lease by the two Stewart deeds. Everything Legg took on Apr. 24 went back to Stewart except 3224, the lot leased to Drechsler, whose reversion Legg sold to Helen Stewart Ridgely (J.B. 1289/565); the round trip, Stewart to Legg on Apr. 23 and Legg back to Stewart on Apr. 26, shows Legg acting as Stewart's conveyancing intermediary, as was inferred on 3224. (c) The rent on lot 2, blotted in the foreclosure deed, is $80; lot 5 is under Brown's December 1887 lease at $50. (d) The deed names no mortgage: the 'Mortgage for $3,500 [?] to Alice Gerry Stewart' that the foreclosure deed laid on lots 1 to 4 is neither excepted nor released here (whether it was already satisfied is unsettled). What it does not settle: how David Stewart, holding the apex in fee from 1890, came to the Auxiliary Realty transfer of 1910 and the $120 lease the Samstags took in 1911; the Alice Gerry Stewart mortgage and its release; and the exact consideration. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (S.C.L. 2610/401 read): the next step is read (752:mdlr-scl2610-401-stewart-pangiris-auxiliary-five-lots-1910): David Stewart's title went to his wife Alice Gerry Stewart by a deed of Feb. 8, 1897 (R.O. 1661/69 [?], recited, not read), and on June 30, 1910 the Stewarts and Elizabeth Pangiris deeded the apex and four houses to the Auxiliary Realty Company, of which David Stewart was Treasurer. The 1910 deed names no mortgage to Alice Gerry Stewart and conveys 'free and discharged of any ground rent or of any mortgage'. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (R.O. 1661, R.O. 1715 and S.C.L. 2610/548 read): the next step is read (752:mdlr-ro1661-69-david-stewart-alice-gerry-stewart-waverly-property-1897): on Feb. 8, 1897 David Stewart conveyed 'all his Waverly property' to his wife Alice Gerry Stewart, 'seven lots of ground five of which' are in this deed, the apex in fee, for $2,500 subject to an unrecorded $10,000 mortgage and equitable lien of May 1, 1890 to Annah St. Clair Gerry, dated five days after this deed was made.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.B. 1292, folios 384 to 386 (MSA CE 168-1300; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 384 to 388, at 150 and 300 dpi). The scan also holds the end of H. Kent McCay, trustee, to Narcissa McCay, a lot on the west side of North Charles Street south of Eager Street (acknowledged in Jefferson County, Alabama, Apr. 28, 1890); the Mount Royal Land, Loan and Improvement Company of Baltimore County's release to Noble H. Creager of Erastus B. Tucker's mortgage (J.B. 1252/212), signed by Lennox Birckhead, president (May 13, 1890, 386 to 387); and Valentine and Anna Diller's assignment of a lot on Shuter Street to the Bohemian Permanent Building and Savings Association 'Slovanstvo' (May 14, 1890, 388). Entry 223. Made Apr. 26, 1890 'by John H. C. Legg to David Stewart both of Baltimore City'. For '$1100' (a raised mark follows the figure; $1,100 is the likely reading) Legg 'doth hereby grant assign and convey unto the said David Stewart All those five lots of ground lying in Baltimore City (formerly in Waverly Baltimore County)'. (1) The apex: from the corner of the north-east side of Merryman's Lane and the west side of the York Turnpike, 36 ft 1/2 in north 'to the centre of the division wall between the house on the lot now being described and the house on the adjoining lot on the North', west through the wall 42 ft in all to the lane, and south-east 55 ft on the lane, '(Being the lot the Leasehold in which vested in said Legg by a deed from David Stewart and the fee by a deed from Lucy C. George both deeds having been recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City on April 24th AD 1890)'. (2) On the south-west side of the lane from 7 ft 8 1/2 in north-west of the turnpike, 102 ft 6 in on the lane, 66 ft 7 in south and 78 ft 1 1/2 in east to the beginning: the lot David Stewart leased to Sarah C. Sinclair on May 28, 1887 (J.W.S. 160/403), 'subject to a ground rent of $80 redeemable after five years at six per cent payable March and September', assigned to Legg by Stewart. (3) On the west side of the turnpike from 96 ft 1/2 in north of the lane, 84 ft 11 1/2 in north, then west 'at right angles with said turnpike or nearly so bounding on the lot leased by said Legg to Drechsler' 100 ft to a three-foot alley, back down the alley and 100 ft east: '(For title see two deeds from David Stewart and wife to said Legg dated April 23rd 1890 and recorded prior hereto said deeds vesting this lot in said Legg in fee)'. (4) On the north-east side of the lane from 134 ft 7 in north-west of the turnpike, at the corner of a three-foot alley 100 ft west of the road, 72 ft 4 in on the lane, 63 ft 8 1/4 in north, 55 ft east to the alley and 110 ft 1 in down it, held in fee from Stewart. (5) On the south-west side of the lane west of the alley, 97 ft west 'to the Western outline of all Sinclair's original property', 75 ft 6 in north to the lane and about 125 ft back along it: 'the same lot intended to be leased by Robert Riddell Brown to James E. Sinclair by deed dated December 22nd 1887' (J.W.S. 167/165), 'subject to an annual rent of $50 payable December 22 and June 22 and redeemable after fifteen years at five percent'. 'It being intended to comprise in this deed all the property heretofore granted to said Legg by said David Stewart and wife and by Lucy C. George and husband by deeds recorded April 24th 1890 excepting the lot leased by said Legg to George T. Drechsler.' With the buildings; to Stewart 'absolutely subject however as to the leasehold lots to the aforesaid ground rents'; special warranty and further assurances. Witness Robert A. Thursby, J.P. for Baltimore City, before whom Legg acknowledged on Apr. 26, 1890; received for record May 14, 1890 at 9:55 a.m. and recorded the same day (Jas. Bond, Clerk); margin 'Grantee Nov 11 [?] 90'. What it settles: (a) the apex left Legg two days after he took it. Lot 1 is the apex, and both estates passed, the Sinclair leasehold from the foreclosure deed (J.B. 1289/297) and the fee carrying the $60 rent from the Georges (J.B. 1289/300), so from Apr. 26, 1890 David Stewart held the apex whole (that the lease merged is an inference; the deed does not use the word). (b) The five lots are foreclosure lots 1, 2, 4 and 6 and a third lot running from 96 ft 1/2 in to 181 ft north of the lane: foreclosure lot 3 (96 ft 1/2 in to 132 ft 8 in) joined to the three southern lots of the 1888 sub-lease (132 ft 8 in to 181 ft), which Legg held in fee and lease by the two Stewart deeds. Everything Legg took on Apr. 24 went back to Stewart except 3224, the lot leased to Drechsler, whose reversion Legg sold to Helen Stewart Ridgely (J.B. 1289/565); the round trip, Stewart to Legg on Apr. 23 and Legg back to Stewart on Apr. 26, shows Legg acting as Stewart's conveyancing intermediary, as was inferred on 3224. (c) The rent on lot 2, blotted in the foreclosure deed, is $80; lot 5 is under Brown's December 1887 lease at $50. (d) The deed names no mortgage: the 'Mortgage for $3,500 [?] to Alice Gerry Stewart' that the foreclosure deed laid on lots 1 to 4 is neither excepted nor released here (whether it was already satisfied is unsettled). What it does not settle: how David Stewart, holding the apex in fee from 1890, came to the Auxiliary Realty transfer of 1910 and the $120 lease the Samstags took in 1911; the Alice Gerry Stewart mortgage and its release; and the exact consideration. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (R.O. 1661, R.O. 1715 and S.C.L. 2610/548 read): the next step is read (752:mdlr-ro1661-69-david-stewart-alice-gerry-stewart-waverly-property-1897): on Feb. 8, 1897 David Stewart conveyed 'all his Waverly property', 'seven lots of ground five of which' are in this deed, to his wife Alice Gerry Stewart for $2,500, subject to an unrecorded $10,000 mortgage of May 1, 1890 to Annah St. Clair Gerry. 3224 is not in it: this deed excepted the Drechsler lot.

summary: Assignment of a sub-lease, Baltimore County land records, Liber E.H.A. No. 59, folios 471 to 473 (MSA CE 62-59; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 471 to 475, at 150 and 300 dpi with the contrast raised). The scan pages hold, in order: the end of John Lee Carroll, Trustee's deed to Charles A. Gambrill and Richard G. and Patrick H. Macgill, acknowledged Nov. 21, 1868 and recorded here Dec. 2, 1868 after Howard County (top of 471); this assignment (471 to 473); Walter and Valaria Virginia Wilson's deed to Richard P. Pindell, Oct. 12, 1868, $1,500, ten acres of 'Gays Inspection' on the Harford Turnpike (473 to 474); and James A. and Mary G. Appold's deed to Andrew Appold, Oct. 14, 1868, $1,000, lots 45 and 46 of 'Friendship' on Matthews and Townsend Avenues (474 to 475); none of the others concerns 3117. The margin index heading reads 'John V. Smith', with a later mark above 'John' (perhaps 'Geo'). Dated October 14, 1868. 'George Vandyke Smith of Baltimore County', 'in consideration of the sum of Three hundred and twenty-five dollars', grants John W. Treadway, John Bruns and William Heise the lot on the east side of the York Turnpike Road 125 ft 6 in north of the beginning of the land 'assigned' (written over a struck word) by Samuel H. Tagart, trustee, to George C. H. Coffield (January 31, 1865, J.H.L. 43/548), by the 1868 courses: N 2 E 79 ft to a post at the north-west corner of the whole tract, S 85 1/2 E 140 ft 6 in to the Old York Road, S 19 1/2 W 78 ft 6 in, N 86 1/4 W 119 ft. Title: 'Being the same lot piece or parcel of ground which was leased or subleased to the said George Vandyke Smith by George C. H. Coffield by lease dated the second day of March in the year one thousand eight hundred and sixty eight and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County in Liber E. H. A. No 59 folio 86 &c.', part of the parcel Tagart assigned to Coffield, and 'the same lot of ground which was leased for all the rest and residue save one year of the term of years yet to come' to Smith 'at the yearly rent of one hundred and fifty dollars payable in equal half yearly instalments accounting from the first day of March'. To hold for the remainder of the term 'by virtue of the original lease or assignment'. Smith covenants that he has the right to convey, special warranty and further assurances. No buildings or improvements are mentioned. Signed 'George V. Smith', witnessed by Gideon Herbert and acknowledged before him as justice of the peace for Baltimore County on October 14, 1868 (Herbert also took Tagart's 1865 acknowledgment); recorded October 14, 1868 (Edward H. Ady, Clerk); margin 'Delivered to Jno. W. Treadway Mch 17/1869'. What it settles: (1) Treadway's grantor is George Vandyke Smith himself, so the 'John C Smith' of E.H.A. 62/262 is a miscopy (very probably of this index heading, 'John V. Smith'; inference), and there is no holder between Smith and Treadway; (2) the leasehold side now runs deed by deed: Coffield to Smith (Mar. 2, 1868), Smith to Treadway, Bruns and Heise (Oct. 14, 1868, $325), they to Cone and Kratt (May 6, 1869, $800), Cone to Kratt (July 1869, recited), Kratt to Hamilton (July 2, 1870, $500); (3) the price more than doubled in seven months, and the 1869 deed adds 'the improvements thereon' where this one names none, so Treadway and his partners probably built on the lot (inference). What it does not settle: who Smith, Bruns and Heise were, what was built, and Cone's assignment (E.H.A. 63/71, not read). Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 7): E.H.A. 63/71 to 78 is read: Cone's assignment is not there (742:mdlr-eha63-71-78-cone-kratt-assignment-not-on-folios-1869-negative). Those folios do hold a deed of June 11, 1869 to 'William Heise and John Burns' of lot 147 on the Frisby estate's 'Oxford' plat, west side of Barkley Street, $1,800 from Charles Peach: very probably the same Heise and Bruns, buying suburban lots in 1868 and 1869 (inference).

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore County mortgage records, Liber J.W.S. No. 121, folios 373 to 374 (MSA CE 221-121; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 373 to 377, at 150 and 300 dpi). The scan pages hold, in order: a clerk's line ending the instrument before (top of 373); this mortgage (373 to 374); and Annie T. K. Condon and her husband Edwin M. Condon's mortgage to Margaret M. Royston, July 3, 1886, $500 (375 to 377), unrelated. Dated April 21, 1886. Charles Hamilton and Margaret Hamilton his wife, of Baltimore County. Recital: 'Charles Hamilton above named is justly indebted unto John T. Ensor in the full sum of one thousand dollars current money and has this day passed to him his promissory note for that amount of money payable in one year after date with interest thereon payable semi annually'. For $1 they grant Ensor (1) the ground 'particularly described in a deed of assignment from Martin Kratt to the said Charles Hamilton dated the second day of July A.D. 1870' (E.H.A. 67/41), and (2) 'also all that piece or parcel of ground situated & lying in Waverly Baltimore County and particularly described in a certain other deed of assignment from William T. Wilson to the said Margaret Hamilton dated the sixteenth day of April in the year A.D. 1874 and duly recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County in Liber J.B. No 86 folio 487 &c' (the surname is hard to read; the J.B. 86/487 lease, already read, names William Thomas Wilson: row 714:mdlr-jb86-487-wilson-margaret-hamilton-lease-1874). Both for the rest of their terms with renewal, subject to 'the clear yearly rent as particularly mentioned in said deeds of assignments respectively'. Terms: void on payment of the $1,000 and interest; the mortgagors hold until default, paying the ground rents, taxes and the mortgage tax; on default the whole debt is due and the deed is 'made in trust', Ensor 'his Executors administrators and assigns' being empowered to sell on at least twenty days' notice in a Baltimore County newspaper, with commissions as on sales under a decree; fire insurance of at least $1,000. A power of sale only: there is no assent to a decree. Witnessed by Wm. D. Wright and acknowledged before him as justice of the peace for Baltimore County on April 21, 1886, with Ensor's oath that the consideration is bona fide; recorded July 3, 1886 at 9 a.m.; margin 'Delivered Jan 4-1887'. No release or assignment is noted in the margins of 373 and 374. What it settles: (1) the 'other lot' of the 1891 releases: Margaret Hamilton's lease of April 16, 1874 from William Thomas Wilson, 100 ft on the west side of the York Turnpike immediately south of A. G. Mott's lot, at $325 a year (row 46255 on 2958 Greenmount), the west-side 'Chas. Hamilton' lot with glass houses on the 1877 Hopkins plate; so the Hamiltons pledged the hotel lot and the florist ground together; (2) the terms: $1,000 at one year, half-yearly interest, a power of sale. What it does not settle: whether it was ever paid or released, and why the 1895 suit styles Ensor 'Assignee of Mortgage' (the 1889 mortgage, J.B. 1263/413, read the same day, bears on it).

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.B. No. 1263, folios 413 to 415 (MSA CE 168-1271; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 413 to 417, at 150 and 300 dpi). The scan pages hold, in order: the end of Amanda J. Brown and John D. Brown's deed, recorded Oct. 19, 1889 (top of 413); the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County's release to Charles Hamilton (413); this mortgage (413 to 415); James J. and Catherine Monahan's mortgage to the Loyola Perpetual Building Association, Oct. 18, 1889, of a Townsend Avenue lot (415 to 417); and the Sycamore Permanent Building and Savings Society No. 1's release to Henry C. and Katie E. Schaub, Oct. 16, 1889 (417); the last two unrelated. The release, dated October 19, 1889: 'in consideration of the re-payment of the whole loan & interest thereon secured by a Mortgage executed by Charles Hamilton to said Body Corporate dated the 20th day of September A.D. 1885 & recorded among the Mortgage Records of Baltimore County in Liber W.M.I. No 116 folio 300 &c' (folio reading uncertain), the association releases to Hamilton 'all that lot of ground described in said Mortgage' (not described here); Henry Joesting, President; Henry W. Fox, attorney; acknowledged before Hugh O'Brien, J.P.; recorded October 19, 1889. The mortgage, the same day, is made 'by & between Charles Hamilton of Baltimore City party of the first part John T. Ensor of Baltimore County in the State of Maryland party of the second part & the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County' of the third part. Recitals: Hamilton, a member, 'has received therefrom an advance of Two Thousand & Eighty Dollars on Sixteen Shares of its Stock standing in his name'; 'said John T. Ensor holds a Mortgage upon the hereinafter described property dated April 21st 1886 & recorded among the Mortgage Records of Baltimore County in Liber J.W.S. No 121 folio 373 &c to secure the sum of 1000'; and 'at the request of said Charles Hamilton & for his sole accommodation' Ensor, for $1, joins 'for the sole purpose of postponing his right of priority under his said Mortgage so that this Indenture shall be and become a first Mortgage upon said premises' as if recorded before 'said Ensor's Mortgage'. Hamilton and Ensor grant the association the lot 'in said Baltimore City (the annex) in the Village of Waverly', the 79 ft by the 1868 courses (125 ft 6 in north of the Coffield beginning, J.H.L. 43/548; N 2 E 79 ft; S 85 1/2 E 140 ft 6 in; S 19 1/2 W 78 ft 6 in; N 86 1/4 W 119 ft), 'Being the same ground conveyed by Martin Kratt to the said Charles Hamilton by Deed of Assignment dated July 2nd 1870' (E.H.A. 67/41), subject to the $150 rent: the 79 ft lot only, not Margaret Hamilton's west-side lot. Terms: weekly dues of 25 cents a share until they reach $130 a share (sixteen shares, $2,080) and weekly interest of 15 cents a share, reduced by 15 cents for each $130 repaid; ground rent, taxes, fines and fire insurance; six weeks' default makes the whole debt due, and the trustee named in a decree, the association's assigns or Henry W. Fox may sell; and 'said Charles Hamilton & John T. Ensor assent to the passing of a decree by any Court of competent jurisdiction for a sale of said property in accordance with Article 4 Sections 692 to 704 inclusive of the Maryland Code Public Local Laws'. Signed by Hamilton and Ensor, witnessed by Hugh O'Brien and acknowledged before him October 19, 1889, with Joesting's oath; recorded October 19, 1889 (Jas. Bond, Clerk). The margins of 413 to 415 hold only index numbers: no assignment is noted. What it settles: (1) the sum and the lot: $2,080 on the 79 ft lot only, made the first mortgage by Ensor's postponement of his own, and taken out the day Hamilton's 1885 association loan was paid off and released (a refinance; that the 1885 mortgage was on the same lot is probable, inference); (2) which mortgage the 1895 decree enforced, probably this one, assigned to Ensor: John T. Ensor, 'Assignee of Mortgage', v. Charles Hamilton was decreed in Circuit Court No. 2 under the assent-to-decree procedure this mortgage contains and the 1886 mortgage lacks (it has only a power of sale); Ensor was the original mortgagee of the 1886 mortgage, not an assignee; and the trustee's deed (R.O. 1725/20) conveys the 79 ft lot only, this mortgage's lot, not the 1886 mortgage's two lots (all inferences; no assignment to Ensor is on these folios). What it does not settle: the assignment itself (date and liber), how much of the $2,080 was unpaid by 1895, and whether the 1886 mortgage was ever paid or released.

summary: Negative search, Baltimore County land records, Liber E.H.A. No. 63, folios 71 to 78 (MSA CE 62-63; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, page by page at 100 dpi with the contrast raised). Joseph M. Cone's assignment to Martin Kratt of his half of the 79 ft leasehold, which Kratt's 1870 deed to Charles Hamilton (E.H.A. 67/41) recites as dated on or about July 30, 1869 and recorded in 'E.H.A. No. 63, folio 71' (the folio was hard to read there), is not on these folios. They hold: the end of a deed between Charles Dennison and James G. McPheeters, acknowledged May 26, 1869 (71); Thomas M. Lanahan's bonds of conveyance of June 25, 1869 to John A. Needles and to Edward M. Needles, each in a $10,000 penalty for a lot sold at $5,000 on Denmead Street and Falls Alley, 336 ft north of the city's northern boundary (71 to 76), recorded June 26, 1869; the deed to Heise and Bruns described below (76 to 78), recorded June 29, 1869; and George W. and Jane Gordon's deed to Elizabeth G. Powell, June 26, 1869, $3,339.85, part of 'Young Man's Adventure' by the Northern Central Railroad (78). These folios were recorded June 26 to 29, 1869, a month before the date the recital gives Cone's assignment, so it very probably lies later in the liber, and the recital's '71' may be a misreading of 171, 271 or 371 (inference). One connection on these folios: Horatio L. Whitridge and Robert A. Dobbin, trustees under a decree of the Circuit Court for Baltimore County of January 23, 1864 in Parkhurst et al. v. Frisby et al., with Horatio and Mary Lloyd and Charles and Elizabeth Peach, convey to 'William Heise and John Burns' (the deed's spelling; Bruns in 1868 and 1869), June 11, 1869, lot 147 on 'the plat of Oxford' (the Frisby estate), 100 ft on the west side of Barkley Street, back 318 to 384 ft to the outline of the Frisby ground, beside lot 146 sold to Charles Gerber. Lloyd bought it at the trustees' private sale on June 17, 1867 for $1,365, sold his interest to Peach on October 7, 1868 for $1,900, and Peach 'has since sold the said property unto William Heise and John Burns for the sum of Eighteen hundred Dollars'; margin 'Delivered Grantee September 1st 1874'. What it settles: (1) Cone's assignment is not at E.H.A. 63/71 to 78; (2) William Heise and John Bruns, two of the three who took the 79 ft lot from George Vandyke Smith in October 1868, were also buying suburban lots elsewhere in Baltimore County in 1868 and 1869 (that they are the same men is an inference from the names and dates; the Barkley Street lot lay outside the 1869 city line, so north of North Avenue, also inference). What it does not settle: Cone's assignment itself (its folio, price, and whether a wife joined), or who Cone was. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (3117 index 1869 Cone): the County index (vol. 2, Ce-Fj, p. 63; 742:index-1851-1874-v2-cone-joseph-m-1869-1870) gives the place: 'Cone, Joseph M, to Martin Kratt, Assgt, 63, 271', recorded August 3, 1869. Kratt's recital dropped the '2'; the assignment is at E.H.A. 63/271 (MSA CE 62-63), not yet read. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (3117 E.H.A. 63/271 read): the assignment is read at E.H.A. 63/271 to 273 (742:mdlr-eha63-271-cone-kratt-half-79ft-leasehold-1869): dated July 30, 1869, recorded August 3, 1869.
