summary: Assignment of a leasehold, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5076, folios 70 to 71 (MSA CE 168-5084; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 70 to 74, at 150 and 300 dpi). Folio 70 opens with the end of a mortgage to the Harford Belmont Building and Loan Association of Baltimore City (recorded Dec. 20, 1929 at 1:08 P.M.; released Sept. 13, 1933) and the Progressive Building Company's release to Viola W. Eney (recorded at 1:40 P.M.). Then come this assignment (70 to 71) and the McCoys' mortgage to the Waverly Building Association (71 to 73, the next row), both about 3030; folios 73 to 74 hold Charles S. and Laura V. Dell's deed of 2504 N. Calvert Street to Edna M. Hammond, widow, and her $3,380 mortgage to the same Association, not about 3030. Margin heading 'Mary A J Aull Asst to David McCoy &c' (clerk's number 54). Dated Dec. 20, 1929. Mary A. J. Aull of Baltimore City, 'in consideration of the sum of five dollars and other valuable considerations', grants and conveys to David McCoy and Mary E. McCoy his wife, as tenants by the entireties, the lot on the west side of 'Greenmount Avenue formerly the York Turnpike Road' 29 ft north of the north side of 'Vineyard Lane formerly Gilmor Lane', 14 by 82 ft to a 4-ft alley, between partition walls, 'known as No 3030 Greenmount Avenue'. Title recital: 'BEING the firstly described lot of ground which by Deed dated October 11th 1922 and recorded among the land records of Baltimore City in Liber SCL No 3918 folio 495 &c was conveyed by Mary A J Aull et al Executors to the said Mary A J Aull'. To hold 'for all the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein with the benefit of renewal forever subject to the payment of the annual rent of sixty six dollars payable half yearly on the first days of June and December'; special warranty. Signed Mary A. J. Aull; witness Lennox B. Clemens; acknowledged Dec. 20, 1929 before Lennox B. Clemens, notary; recorded Dec. 20, 1929 at 1:35 P.M., Stephen C. Little, Clerk. What it settles: how the widow held 3030 after Jacob H. Aull's death (Oct. 12, 1921): by a deed of Oct. 11, 1922 from his executors, herself among them, to herself (S.C.L. 3918/495), in which 3030 is the first of several lots [inference from 'firstly described' and 'et al']. So the 1912 leasehold on 3030 stayed in the Aull family from Alice M. Chapman's assignment back in 1916 until December 1929, when the McCoys bought it on a building-association loan (the next row). What it does not settle: the price (no stamp note is copied; the $3,120 loan was 'part of the purchase money', so it was more than $3,120 [inference]); the executors' deed itself and Jacob H. Aull's will. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (S.C.L. 3918/495 read): the executors' deed is read (726:mdlr-scl3918-495-aull-executors-widow-3030-1922). On Oct. 11, 1922, under an order of the Orphans' Court of Baltimore City of Oct. 6, 1922 (Article 93, Section 139), Mary A. J. Aull and W. Harry Holmes, executors of Jacob H. Aull, conveyed to Mary A. J. Aull for $5 two leaseholds: 3030 Greenmount Avenue ($66, June 1 and Dec. 1), 'the same lot of ground which by deed dated August 27th 1916 ... Liber S C L No 3109 folio 328 &c was conveyed by Alice M Chapman to Jacob H Aull', and the Aull home at 510 Rossiter Avenue ($90). No will liber or folio is cited. The 1912 leasehold on 3030 is now read link by link from 1912 to its merger in 1935.

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5076, folios 71 to 73 (MSA CE 168-5084; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 70 to 74, at 150 and 300 dpi; the other instruments on the folios are listed in the row for the assignment, 726:mdlr-scl5076-70-aull-mccoy-assignment-3030-1929). Margin heading 'David McCoy &c Mtge to Waverly Bldg Asso of Balto Co' (clerk's number 55), and on folio 72 the stamp 'FOR RELEASE OF MTGE. DATE 3/15/51 LIBER 8386 FOL. 69' (the date and numbers written in by hand). Dated Dec. 20, 1929. David McCoy and Mary E. McCoy his wife, of Baltimore City, '(members of said body corporate) have received therefrom an advance of thirty one hundred and twenty ($3120.00) dollars on twenty four (24) shares of stock standing in their names', the mortgage being a condition of the loan, 'said sum so loaned being paid as part of the purchase money for the property hereinafter described'; for that and $1 they convey to The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County the lot on the west side of 'Greenmount Avenue formerly the York Turnpike Road' 29 ft north of the north side of 'Vineyard Lane formerly Gilmor Lane', 14 by 82 ft to a 4-ft alley, between partition walls, 'known as No 3030 Greenmount Avenue', 'BEING the same lot of ground which by Assignment of even date herewith and intended to be recorded among the land records of Baltimore City immediately prior hereto was conveyed by Mary A J Aull to the said mortgagors subject to the payment of the annual rent of sixty six dollars payable in equal half yearly instalments on the first days of June and December', for the residue of the term with renewal forever. Terms: 25 cents a week dues on each share until the dues reach $130 a share, its par, and 15 cents a week on each share as interest, cut by 15 cents for each $130 repaid; the mortgagors pay ground rent, taxes, water rent and fines and keep the house insured; assent to a decree for sale under Sections 720 to 732 of Chapter 123 of the Acts of 1898; on six weeks' default the whole debt falls due, and the Association's assigns or Lennox B. Clemens, as attorney, may sell under Article 66, Sections 6 to 10, of the Code of 1904. Signed David McCoy and Mary E. McCoy; witness Lennox B. Clemens; acknowledged Dec. 20, 1929 before Lennox B. Clemens, notary, with John G. Maier, President of the Association, swearing to the consideration; recorded Dec. 20, 1929 at 1:36 P.M., a minute after the assignment, Stephen C. Little, Clerk. What it settles: (1) the McCoys bought 3030 on a building-association loan of $3,120 from the same Association to which they assigned the leasehold on July 8, 1932 (S.C.L. 5313/27, row 47526) for $5 and other considerations. Payments came to $9.60 a week ($6 dues and $3.60 interest on 24 shares). An assignment by borrowers to their own lender two and a half years later, with no price and one 50-cent stamp, very probably was a deed in lieu of foreclosure [inference; neither instrument says so]. (2) The mortgage was not released when the Association took the leasehold: the margin dates the release Mar. 15, 1951, Liber 8386 folio 69, the folio just before Nicholas Interrante's deed of 3030 to Robert F. Podlich (M.L.P. 8386/70, recorded that day), so it was cleared for that sale [inference]. What it does not settle: whether the McCoys defaulted, and what the release at M.L.P. 8386/69 says.

summary: Deed of reversion, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5517, folios 92 to 94 (MSA CE 168-5525; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 92 to 96, at 150 and 300 dpi). Folio 92 opens with the end of Raymond A. Egner's deed of a leasehold to Edward R. Kinstler for life, remainder to Helen L. Betz, at $84 (acknowledged Feb. 23, 1935 before Beatrice M. Bussey; recorded Feb. 25, 1935 at 2:15 P.M.); folios 94 to 96 hold George A. Knipp and Enoch Harlan's deed as executors of Margaret Knipp of 4008 and 4010 Pennington Avenue to Arthur R. Knipp ($1,450) and Francis S. and Leonora L. Biggs's deed of the rent on 1700 N. Broadway to Caroline, Katherine and Frieda Speer; none is about 3030. Margin heading 'Mercantile Trust Co &c Trustees Deed of Reversion to Waverly Bldg Assn of Balto Co.' (clerk's number 68), stamps '1-$1-1-$.50-USS Cancelled'. Dated Feb. 18, 1935. Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore, 'formerly Mercantile Trust and Deposit Company of Baltimore', and William Jenkins of the City of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, trustees, to The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County. Recitals: 'WHEREAS Francis X Hooper by his Last Will and Testament admitted to probate in the Orphans Court of Baltimore County and of record in the office of the Register of Wills of said County in Wills Liber WJP No 19 folio 182' left his estate a third to Florence W. Hooper, his widow, and two-thirds to the trustees in trust with power to sell; the widow and trustees divided the real estate 'by deed dated December 7th 1917 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber SCL No 3177 folio 132'; 'WHEREAS the party hereto of the second part is the owner of the leasehold estate in the hereinafter described lot of ground to which it acquired title by deed of assignment dated the 8th day of July 1932 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber SCL No 5312 folio 27 from David McCoy and wife and has given to the herein parties of the first part the legally required notice to redeem the reversion and annual ground rent issuing out of said lot'. For 'the sum of eleven hundred dollars', in the exercise of the will's powers, the trustees grant the lot on the west side of 'Greenmount Avenue formerly the York Turnpike Road' 29 ft north of the north side of 'Vineyard Lane formerly Gilmor Lane', 14 by 82 ft to a 4-ft alley, between partition walls, 'known as No 3030 Greenmount Avenue', 'BEING the thirdly described lot of ground which by lease dated December 6th 1912 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber SCL No 2797 folio 374 was demised and leased by Jacob H Aull and wife to Alice M Chapman for the renewable term of ninety nine years at and under the annual rent of of sixty six dollars AND BEING the thirdly described lot of ground described in the deed from Florence W Hooper et al to the herein parties of the first part', 'and especially the clear yearly rent of sixty six dollars', to the Association in fee simple 'to the end and intent that the leasehold estate created by the lease aforesaid shall be merged with the fee and the annual rent issuing thereout shall be forever extinguished'. Signed for Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore by J. H. Miller, Vice President, attested by F. A. La Porte, Assistant Secretary, and by William Jenkins, 'Trustees under the Last Will and Testament of Francis X Hooper Deceased'; acknowledged by Miller ('Millar') in Baltimore on Feb. 20, 1935 before Charles H. Schanze, and by Jenkins on Feb. 18, 1935 in Pinellas County, Florida, before W. A. Bogert; recorded Feb. 25, 1935 at 2:15 P.M., Stephen C. Little, Clerk. What it settles: (1) the 'Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore et al Trustees' of the 1935 lease and deed (rows 47394, 47395) are Francis X. Hooper's testamentary trustees, Mercantile and William Jenkins, still both serving in 1935. (2) The rent they sold was the 1912 Aull rent on 3030, 'thirdly described' in the 1912 lease and the 1917 division. (3) It was a redemption, not a sale by choice: the Association, as leaseholder, gave the statutory notice to redeem, and $1,100 is the $66 capitalized at 6 percent [inference], as in the trustee's 1950 redemption of the 3026 rent for $1,200 (row 46282). (4) The deed itself merges the 1912 lease in the fee and extinguishes the rent: from Feb. 18, 1935 the Association held 3030 in fee. A week later it created a new $66 lease (S.C.L. 5518/171) and sold that rent to the Leights for the same $1,100. (5) The deed carries both miscopies: the 1912 lease as 2797/374 (it is 2787/374) and the McCoy assignment as 5312/27 (it is 5313/27). What it does not settle: the date of the notice to redeem, and why the Association redeemed one $66 rent only to sell another at the same price (a fresh 99-year term, new rent days, or a buyer the trust would not deal with are guesses).

summary: Baltimore County Circuit Court Land Records Index 1851-1874, vol. 2 (Ce-Fj), MSA CE 35-2, pages 62 to 64: the section for surnames beginning C with given names beginning J, in order of recording from February 19, 1869 to May 4, 1870 (read 2026-10-17 from the scan Jeff saved, at 150 and 300 dpi). Columns are date of record, surname, given name, course ('to' grantor, 'from' grantee), other party, instrument, and liber and folio; the index prints liber numbers only, with deeds, leases and assignments in one series (Nos. 60 to 66 here, E.H.A. by the recording dates) and mortgages and their releases and assignments in a lower-numbered series (Nos. 24, 26 and 32 to 36). There are five lines for Joseph M. Cone and no other Cone: (1) May 7, 1869, 'Cone, Joseph M &c, from John W Treadway &c, Deed, 62, 262'; (2) May 27, 1869, 'Cone, Joseph M, to Lanvale Bldg asso, Mort, 33, 77' (the association's name is a probable reading); (3) August 3, 1869, 'Cone, Joseph M, to Martin Kratt, Assgt, 63, 271'; (4) March 24, 1870, 'Cone, Joseph M, from Lanvale Bldg asso, Rel mtg, 36, 51' (with a tick mark after the folio); (5) March 24, 1870, 'Cone, Joseph M, to Harrison Bldg asso no 6, Mort, 36, 56'. Other Cones would sit under other given-name letters, which these pages do not cover. Also on the pages: June 22, 1869, 'Cross, John C, to Waverly Mutual Bldg asso, Mort, 33, 232' (very probably the John C. Cross whose wife Elenor took the 1874 Wilson lease beside Margaret Hamilton's, J.B. 86/483; inference); and February 18, 1870, 'Carlisle, James H, from Augustus D Clemens &wf, Deed, 65, 235' (an Augustus D. Clemens, not necessarily the Jr. who bought the 79 ft lot in 1898). What it settles: (1) line 1 confirms E.H.A. 62/262, read, recorded May 7, 1869; (2) line 3 gives the true place of Cone's assignment to Kratt: E.H.A. 63, folio 271, recorded August 3, 1869, a few days after the 'on or about July 30, 1869' of Kratt's 1870 recital, which gives folio 71 (a dropped '2'; the scan of 63/71 to 78, read, holds June 1869 deeds); it is indexed as an assignment, in the deed series; (3) Cone mortgaged something to the Lanvale building association twenty days after taking the 79 ft lot jointly with Kratt, had the mortgage released on March 24, 1870, and the same day mortgaged to the Harrison Building Association No. 6. What it does not settle: what Cone's two mortgages covered (the index gives no descriptions; that the May 1869 one was on his half of the 79 ft lot is possible, since its release in March 1870 came three months before Kratt sold the whole lot to Hamilton, but the same-day remortgage suggests other ground, inference either way), the price and terms of the assignment, and whether a wife joined (the index line shows no '&wf'). Update Oct. 17, 2026 (3117 E.H.A. 63/271 read): line 3 is read (E.H.A. 63/271 to 273; 742:mdlr-eha63-271-cone-kratt-half-79ft-leasehold-1869). Cone signs alone, for $50 and Kratt's payment of three notes given to Treadway and others, and covenants that he has not encumbered the lot, which suggests the Lanvale mortgage of line 2 was on other ground (inference).

summary: Executors' deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 3918, folios 495 to 496 (MSA CE 168-3926; read 2026-10-17 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 495 to 499, at 150 and 300 dpi). Folio 495 opens with the end of a deed by Marie L. Patterson (acknowledged Oct. 10, 1922 before Dorothea Jacob; recorded Oct. 13, 1922 at 9:30 A.M.); folios 497 to 499 hold Clinton J. and Helen Douty Ogle's assignment of 1644 N. Fulton Avenue to James Bernard and Catharine L. Griffin and the Griffins' $3,380 mortgage to the Rekab Building Association (recorded Oct. 13, 1922 at 9:10 A.M. and 2:51 P.M.), and the start of Charles Gensler's deed as trustee in bankruptcy of Amelia Puepke to Frances A. Milosh; none is about 3030. Margin heading 'Mary A J Aull &c Executors Deed to Mary A J Aull' (clerk's number 350), the typed note 'Block No 3656' beside the 3030 lot (the City block is 3856; very probably a typing slip [inference]) and 'New Annex' beside the second lot; grantee stamp 'Grantee T NOV 3 1922'. Dated Oct. 11, 1922. Mary A. J. Aull and W. Harry Holmes, 'Executors of the Estate of Jacob H Aull late of Baltimore City deceased', to Mary A. J. Aull. Recital: 'WHEREAS by an order of the Orphans Court of Baltimore City passed on the sixth day of October in the year one thousand nine hundred and twenty two in the matter of the estate of Jacob H Aull deceased the said Mary A J Aull and W Harry Holmes Executors were authorized and directed to convey unto the said Mary A J Aull the hereinafter described lots of ground in accordance with Article 93 Section 139 Code of Public General Laws of Maryland'. For $5 and under that order they convey 'all those two lots of ground'. First: the lot on the west side of 'Greenmount Avenue formerly the York Turnpike Road' 29 ft north of the north side of 'Vineyard Lane formerly Gilmor Lane', 14 by 82 ft to a 4-ft alley, between partition walls, 'Knonw as No 3030 Greenmount Avenue BEING the same lot of ground which by deed dated August 27th 1916 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber S C L No 3109 folio 328 &c was conveyed by Alice M Chapman to Jacob H Aull'. Second: on the north side of Rossiter Avenue 317 ft 5 in east of the east side of the York Turnpike Road, 63 ft 3 in along Rossiter Avenue to the westernmost outline of the first lot of a lease from Jacob H. Aull and wife to Alice M. Chapman of Nov. 2, 1910 (Balt. Co. W.P.C. 368/502), north 115 ft 9 in more or less to the northernmost outline of 'the whole tract of land belonging to said Jacob H Aull', N 87 50 W 59 ft more or less to lot No. 8 of a plat not otherwise named, and south 104 ft 10 in to the beginning, 'Known as No 510 Rossiter Avenue For reference See deed dated June 6th 1913 Balto Co W P C No 413 folio 446 &c'. For the residue of the terms with renewal forever, 'subject to the payment of the annual rent of $66.00 on the firstly described lot of ground payable in equal half yearly installments on the 1st days of June and December and ninety dollars on the secondly described lot of ground payable in equal half yearly installments on the first days of April and October'. Signed Mary A. J. Aull and W. Harry Holmes, Executors; witness Cora A. Du Laney; acknowledged Oct. 11, 1922 before Cora A. Du Laney, 'a Notary Public of the State of Maryland in and for Anne Arundel County', under a 'Baltimore City' venue heading; recording line typed 'October 11th 1922 at 2.51 o'clk PM', though the instruments on either side were recorded Oct. 13 and the Griffin mortgage at the same minute that day, so the date is very probably a slip for Oct. 13 [inference]. What it settles: (1) how the widow held 3030: Jacob H. Aull (d. Oct. 12, 1921) held the 1912 leasehold by Alice M. Chapman's assignment back of Aug. 27, 1916 (S.C.L. 3109/328, row 46607) until his death; his executors, his widow and W. Harry Holmes, conveyed it to her on Oct. 11, 1922 for $5 under an Orphans' Court of Baltimore City order of Oct. 6, 1922. With the 1912 lease, the 1916 assignment, the 1929 sale to the McCoys, their 1932 assignment and the 1935 merger, the 1912 leasehold on 3030 is now read link by link from 1912 to 1935. (2) The order covers only two lots: 3030, the one Aull house of the 1912 row still in his hands (3026 went to the Spellmans in 1917, 3028 and 3032 in 1918), and 510 Rossiter Avenue in the New Annex, the Aull home where he died, also a leasehold, at $90, out of his own tract and next to a 1910 lease to Chapman. No other corridor lot is named. What it does not settle: the will (the deed calls them executors but cites no will liber or folio) and the terms of the Oct. 6, 1922 order; whether Aull held other leaseholds or fees that passed by other instruments.

summary: Grantee index lines, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Grantee Indexes 1908, 1909 and 1910, A to G volumes, the 'Au' pages (MSA CE 166-128 p.49 to 51, MSA CE 166-131 p.53 to 57 and MSA CE 166-134 p.53 to 56; read 2026-10-17 by a helper agent from the scans Jeff saved, at 150 and 300 dpi). Each year's pages run in recording order; 1908 p.51, 1909 p.56 and 1910 p.56 are blank, and 1909 p.57 begins 'Av'. On these pages the grantor and the right-hand columns run about half a line below the grantee, so lines were matched in order. There are 60 lines for 'Auxiliary Realty Co.' (9 in 1908, 27 in 1909, 24 in 1910), and the first is the first line of 1908 (Jan. 3, Edwin C. Conklin and wife, deed, N.E.S. Cathedral St, S.C.L. 2395/113), so the company was already buying when the 1908 volume opens (formed in 1907 or earlier, inference). Only one pair is on the York road, both recorded Sept. 30, 1910 (1910 p.54): 'Cityco Realty Co', 'Mtge', '5 Lots W S York Road', S.C.L. 2610 folio 403; and 'Alice G Stewart &c', 'Deed &c', '5 Lots W S York Road', S.C.L. 2610 (by ditto) folio 401. Other lines with Stewart, Gerry-family or corridor-chain names: Apr. 16, 1908, 'David Stewart Trustee', Deed, location 'S.C.L. 2409.138', S.C.L. 2416/60, the property of the Mar. 17, 1908 deed from 'Indiana Rehan &c' ('Real & Personal', S.C.L. 2409/138); Mar. 4, 1909, grantee 'Auxiliary Realty Co &c' from 'Mary A. Legg &c', Deed, 'E S Hargrove alley', S.C.L. 2484/52; Jan. 25, 1910, 'David Stewart', Deed, 'N S Preston St', S.C.L. 2556/16; Feb. 1, 1910, 'Elizabeth Pangoris' [Pangiris], Deed, 'S.W.S. Ostend St', S.C.L. 2557/431; Apr. 29, 1910, 'Real Estate Pooling Co', Asst, 'E S Charles St', S.C.L. 2576/326. No Gerry or Griswold line. The rest are deeds of single lots and rows across the city (Cathedral, Madison, Woodyear, Mount Royal, Calhoun, Lexington, Preston, Ostend, Division and other streets), mortgages and assignments of mortgages (several on 'Interest in Estate' from the Baugher family and the Hoods), and one partial release; none is on the York road, Greenmount or Merryman's Lane. No line in November or December 1910 is from Cityco Realty Co.: the Nov. 10, 1910 sale of 1100 and 1102 York road from Cityco back to Auxiliary that the Sun reported is not in the 1910 grantee pages (recorded in 1911, or under another name, inference). What it settles: (a) the apex reached Auxiliary Realty from Alice G. Stewart and others, very probably her husband David Stewart, who held it whole from Apr. 26, 1890 (J.B. 1292/384), by the deed at S.C.L. 2610/401, recorded Sept. 30, 1910 (that the five lots are the apex at 1100 and 1102 and the houses at 1104, 1112 and 1114 York road is an inference from the Sun of Oct. 1, 1910, which reported those five transferred by Auxiliary to Cityco in fee). (b) The same day Auxiliary sold the five to Cityco (the deed would be at about S.C.L. 2610/402, inference) and took back a purchase-money mortgage (2610/403). (c) The Stewart rents were moving into Auxiliary in 1908 to 1910 (David Stewart as trustee in 1908, in his own name in January 1910, Elizabeth Pangiris in February 1910), which fits Auxiliary as the vehicle for the Gerry daughters' ground rents (inference). What it does not settle: the deeds themselves (S.C.L. 2610/401 to 403, MSA CE 168-2618), whether 401 conveys the fee, a leasehold or both, the lease behind the $120 rent of 1911, and how the apex passed from Auxiliary to Elizabeth Pangiris and the Real Estate Pooling Co. in 1911. summary: Assignment, Baltimore County land records, Liber E.H.A. No. 63, folios 271 to 273 (MSA CE 62-63; read 2026-10-17 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 271 to 275, at 150 and 300 dpi). The scan pages hold, in order: the end of the Farmers National Bank of Annapolis's extension to Robert Wilson of a lease of lots in Baltimore County to June 30, 1890, at $50 a year (George Wells, president; James Mackubin, attorney; acknowledged July 31, 1869 before Jesse McKenzie, J.P.) (top of 271); this assignment (271 to 273); Sophia C. Read, widow, to William L. Garitee, August 2, 1869, $8,000 ($400 in cash and a mortgage for the rest), 151 acres of 'The Hope' on the Patapsco (273 to 274); and Joshua and Elizabeth Zimmerman to William B. Kemper, July 20, 1869, $100, 25 ft on the Franklin Turnpike Road (274 to 275); all recorded August 3, 1869, and none of the others concerns 3117. 'This Deed made this thirtieth day of July in the year One thousand eight hundred and Sixty nine by Joseph M Cone of the City of Baltimore'. Consideration: 'the sum of fifty dollars and the payment by Martin Kratt of three notes given by Cone & Kratt to Treadway and others for the purchase money of the property hereinafter described'. Cone grants and assigns to Kratt 'all the said Joseph M Cone's right title & interest and claim (it being one undivided moiety or half part) in unto and out of' the lot on the east side of the York Turnpike Road 125 ft 6 in north of the beginning of the land assigned by 'Saml H Taggart Trustee to G H Coffield by deed dated the 21st January 1865' (J.H.L. 43/548; the deed is dated the 31st), by the 1868 courses: N 2 E 79 ft to a post at the north-west corner of 'said whole tract or lot assigned to said Coffield', S 85 1/2 E 140 ft 6 in to a post on the west side of the Old York Road, S 19 1/2 W 78 ft 6 in, N 86 1/4 W 119 ft. Title: 'Being the same ground which by deed dated the 6th day of May AD 1869 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County in Liber E H A No 62 folio 262 &c was assigned by John W Treadway and others to said Joseph M Cone et al subject to the annual rent of one hundred and fifty dollars payable semi annually on the first day of March and September in every year'. 'Together with the improvements thereon'; for the residue of the term with renewal forever, subject to the $150 rent 'to whoever the same may be payable'. Cone covenants that he 'has not done or suffered to be done any act matter or thing whatsoever to charge or encumber the property hereby conveyed', special warranty and further assurances. Signed by Joseph M. Cone alone, witnessed by D. Hagerty; acknowledged July 30, 1869 by Cone alone before Daniel Hagerty, J.P. for Baltimore City (who also took the May 1869 Treadway deed's acknowledgment), with George Robinson's clerk's certificate the same day; recorded August 3, 1869 (Edw. H. Ady, Clerk); margin 'Delivered Nov 24/69 to L H Robinson Jr per Recpt' and a $1 revenue stamp. What it settles: (1) the last unread link on the leasehold side: Cone's half passed to Kratt on July 30, 1869, so the chain from Coffield's 1868 sub-lease to Hamilton's 1870 assignment is now read deed by deed; (2) the price: Cone took $50 and Kratt assumed three notes that Cone and Kratt had given Treadway and his partners, so the $800 of May 1869 was at least partly on credit (inference from the notes; their amounts are not stated); (3) no wife joins: Cone signs and acknowledges alone, as a city resident; (4) the covenant against Cone's own encumbrances suggests that his mortgage to the Lanvale building association of May 27, 1869 (mortgage No. 33/77, indexed) was not on this lot (inference). What it does not settle: the amounts and due dates of the three notes and whether Kratt paid them before selling to Hamilton for $500 in 1870, what the improvements were, and who Joseph M. Cone was.

summary: Assignment of a leasehold, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. 6513, folio 138 (MSA CE 168-6521; read 2026-10-17 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 136 to 138, at 150 and 300 dpi; folio 139 onward was read Oct. 16, row 47397). Folio 136 holds the end of Mary Matthews's mortgage (John Lettner, president of the mortgagee, which is not named on the folio; Harry A. Kohlerman or John O. Dumler, attorneys; acknowledged Oct. 5, 1943 before Edith L. Lindsay; recorded Oct. 6, 1943 at 2:02 P.M.), not about 3030. Folio 137: Ida H. Interrante, 'formerly Ida H Caples', to Helen M. Bordley, Sept. 30, 1943, for $5 and other valuable considerations, the leasehold of 506 McCabe Avenue, Lot No. 15 on the plat of Lawrence B. McCabe's property (Balt. Co. Plat Book 2/384), subject to $75 a year (Jan. 1 and July 1), being the lot assigned by James C. Fields and wife to Ida H. Caples on June 16, 1943 (M.L.P. 6469/394), 'the said Ida H Caples having since married Nicholas Interrante'; witness and notary Lennox B. Clemens; recorded Oct. 6, 1943 at 2 P.M.; clerk's number 94, with the later margin note 'ORDER FILED 12-4-67'. Folio 138, this instrument: margin heading 'Nicholas Interrante Asst to Helen M Bordley' (clerk's number 95). Dated Sept. 30, 1943. Nicholas Interrante of Baltimore City, 'in consideration of the sum of Five dollars and other valuable considerations', assigns to Helen M. Bordley the lot on the west side of Greenmount Avenue 29 ft north of the north side of 'Vineyard Lane formerly Gilmor Lane', 14 by 82 ft to a 4-ft alley, between partition walls, 'The improvements thereon being known as No 3030 Greenmount Avenue BEING the same lot of ground which by Assignment dated the 29th day of December 1942 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber M L P No 6410 folio 265 was conveyed by The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County to the herein Grantor', for the residue of the term with renewal forever, 'subject to the payment of the annual rent of Sixty six dollars payable in equal half yearly installments on the 25th days of February and August'; special covenants. Signed Nicholas Interrante; witness Lennox B. Clemens; acknowledged Sept. 30, 1943 before Lennox B. Clemens, notary; recorded Oct. 6, 1943 at 2:01 P.M., M. Luther Pittman, Clerk. What it settles: (1) how Nicholas Interrante held 3030: by the Waverly Building Association's assignment of the 1935 leasehold to him alone, dated Dec. 29, 1942 (M.L.P. 6410/265), six months before he married Mrs. Ida H. Caples (June 26, 1943, row 39349). So the Association held the 3030 leasehold from Helen M. Bordley's assignment back of Feb. 25, 1935 (S.C.L. 5518/174, row 47396) until Dec. 29, 1942. (2) The round trip of Sept. 30, 1943 is now read whole: Ida assigned 506 McCabe Avenue (folio 137) and Nicholas 3030 (folio 138) to Bordley, who the same day assigned both back to them by the entireties (folio 139, row 47397), recorded at 2:00, 2:01 and 2:02 P.M., all witnessed by Lennox B. Clemens; its purpose was to put each spouse's leasehold into a tenancy by the entireties [inference]. With this, 3030 is read link by link from 1912 to 1951, the 1942 assignment itself recited only. What it does not settle: the 1942 assignment's price and terms, and whether Interrante mortgaged 3030 to the Association. Next: M.L.P. 6410/265 (MSA CE 168-6418). Update Oct. 17, 2026 (M.L.P. 6410/265 read): the Association's assignment of 3030 to Nicholas Interrante, Dec. 29, 1942 (M.L.P. 6410/265, read; 726:mdlr-mlp6410-265-waverly-bldg-interrante-assignment-3030-1942) recites 'assignment dated the 25th day of February 1935 ... Liber SCL No 5518 folio 174 ... by Helen M Bordley to the herein grantor' and, for $5 and other considerations (stamps pointing to about $3,500), sells him the leasehold the Association had held since 1932 or 1935, subject to the $66 due Feb. 25 and Aug. 25. The Association lent him $3,250 of the price on 25 shares the next minute (726:mdlr-mlp6410-266-interrante-waverly-bldg-mortgage-3030-1942); the margin dates its release Sept. 19, 1945 (M.L.P. 6797/529).

summary: Assignment of a leasehold, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. 6410, folios 265 to 266 (MSA CE 168-6418; read 2026-10-17 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 265 to 269, at 150 and 300 dpi). Folio 265 opens with the end of a J. Ford Miller deed (acknowledged Dec. 29, 1942 before Dietrich F. Brettschneider; recorded Dec. 30, 1942 at 1:40 P.M.), not about 3030. Then come this assignment (265 to 266) and Interrante's mortgage back to the Association (266 to 268, the next row); folio 268 goes on to William and Flora Karmiol's deed of 3530 W. Virginia Avenue to Benjamin B. Cooper and Cooper's deed of it to Flora Karmiol (recorded 2:05 and 2:06 P.M.), and folio 269 to the start of the Maroon Building Company's assignment of ground on Sixth Street to Antonio and Mary R. Manales, none about 3030. Margin heading 'Waverly Bldg Assn of Balto Co Asst to Nicholas Interrante' (clerk's number 179), stamps read as '1-$3 1-80c 1-5c USS Canld' ($3.85) and '1-$2 1-$1 1-50c MDS Canld' ($3.50), and 'GRANTEE MAR 4' with the year smudged (1943 [inference]). Dated Dec. 29, 1942; the body is headed 'THIS DEED', the margin and recitals call it an assignment. The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County, 'a body corporate of the State of Maryland', by Henry Joesting Jr., its President, 'in consideration of the sum of five dollars and other valuable considerations', grants and assigns to Nicholas Interrante, of Baltimore City, the lot on the west side of 'Greenmount Avenue' 29 ft north of the north side of 'Vineyard Lane formerly Gilmor Lane', 14 by 82 ft to a 4-ft alley, between partition walls, 'known as No 3030 Greenmount Avenue'. Title recital: 'BEING the same lot of ground which by assignment dated the 25th day of February 1935 and recorded among the land records of Baltimore City in Liber SCL No 5518 folio 174 was conveyed by Helen M Bordley to the herein grantor'. To hold 'for all the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein with the benefit of renewal forever subject to the payment of the annual rent of sixty six dollars payable in equal half yearly instalments on the 25th day of February and August'; the grantor covenants it has not encumbered the lot and will warrant specially. Signed under the seal 'Waverly Bldg Assn of Balto Co Inc 1882' by Henry Joesting Jr., President; witness Lennox B. Clemens; acknowledged Dec. 29, 1942 before Lennox B. Clemens, notary; recorded Dec. 30, 1942 at 1:50 P.M., M. Luther Pittman, Clerk. What it settles: (1) how Nicholas Interrante held 3030: the Association sold him the leasehold it had held since Bordley's assignment back of Feb. 25, 1935 (S.C.L. 5518/174, row 47396), and before that since the McCoys' assignment of July 8, 1932 (S.C.L. 5313/27, row 47526), so the Association held it ten years. (2) The deed recites $5, but both stamps (U.S. $3.85 at 55 cents per $500, Maryland $3.50 at 10 cents per $100) fit a price of about $3,500 [inference]; the Association lent him $3,250 of it the next minute (next row). (3) The Association's recital stops at the 1935 straw assignment: it does not cite the 1935 lease (S.C.L. 5518/171) or its 1932 and 1935 titles. What it does not settle: why the Association sold in December 1942 (nothing is stated; a lender selling, on its own loan, a house it took back in 1932 is the likeliest reading [inference]); what Nicholas Interrante paid in words.

DATE 9/19/45 LIBER 6797 FOL. 529' (the date and numbers written in by hand). Dated Dec. 29, 1942. Nicholas Interrante, of Baltimore City, 'being a member of the said body corporate has received therefrom an advance of thirty two hundred and fifty ($3250.00) dollars on twenty five shares of stock', the mortgage being a condition of the loan, 'said sum so loaned being a part of the purchase money for the hereinafter described property'; for that and $1 he conveys the Association the lot on the west side of 'Greenmount Avenue' 29 ft north of the north side of 'Vineyard Lane formerly Gilmor Lane', 14 by 82 ft to a 4-ft alley, between partition walls, 'known as No 3030 Greenmount Avenue', 'BEING the same lot of ground which by assignment of even date herewith and intended to be recorded among the land records of Baltimore City prior hereto was conveyed by the herein mortgagee to the herein mortgagor', for the residue of the term with renewal forever, subject to the rent of $66 due Feb. 25 and Aug. 25. Terms: 25 cents a week dues on each of the 25 shares until the dues reach $130 a share, its par, and 15 cents a week on each share as interest, dropping off as each $130 is paid in; $3.30 a week more for taxes, water rent, ground rent and insurance, which the Association pays out; he keeps the house insured; assent to a decree for sale under Sections 720 to 732 of Chapter 123 of the Acts of 1898 on six weeks' default. Those weekly sums come to $13.30 in all [arithmetic]. Signed Nicholas Interrante; witness Lennox B. Clemens; acknowledged Dec. 29, 1942 before Lennox B. Clemens, notary, with Henry Joesting Jr., President of the Association, swearing to the consideration; recorded Dec. 30, 1942 at 1:51 P.M., M. Luther Pittman, Clerk. What it settles: (1) the $3,250 loan was most of the price (about $3,500 by the stamps on the assignment [inference]), on a leasehold the Association itself had sold him. (2) The margin dates the release Sept. 19, 1945, Liber 6797 folio 529, so he repaid it in under three years, after the Leights' deed of reversion of Jan. 7, 1944 (M.L.P. 6549/594) and six years before the sale to Podlich in 1951; no default is recorded here [inference from a release stamp, not read]. What it does not settle: the release itself (M.L.P. 6797/529) and how he paid it off.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 2610, folios 401 to 402 (MSA CE 168-2618; read 2026-10-17 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 401 to 405, at 150 and 300 dpi. The scan holds, in order: the Stewarts' deed to the Auxiliary Realty Company (folios 401 to 402), the Auxiliary Realty Company's deed to the Cityco Realty Company (402 to 403), Cityco's purchase-money mortgage back to Auxiliary (403 to 405), and at the foot of 405 the City Block Building Association No. 4's release to George S. Laumann and wife and the head of William E. Hooton [?] and wife's deed to Laumann, neither on the corridor). Entry 264, indexed 'Alice Gerry Stewart &c, Deed to Auxiliary Realty Co' (the City grantee index of 1910, row 47720, has it at 2610/401). Dated June 30, 1910 and recorded Sept. 30, 1910: 'This Deed made this 30th day of June 1910 by Alice Gerry Stewart and David Stewart her husband of Baltimore City and State of Maryland and Elizabeth Pangiris Widow a Citizen of the United States now temporarily residing abroad to The Auxiliary Realty Company of Baltimore City a corporation'. For 'Five Dollars ($5) and other good and valuable considerations' they 'do hereby grant assign and convey unto the said The Auxiliary Realty Company of Baltimore City its successors and assigns in fee simple All those lots or parcels of ground comprised within the following boundaries to wit' 'Beginning for the same at the intersection of the Northeasternmost side of Merryman's Lane and the West side of the York Road and running thence along the West side of the York Road Northerly about 181 feet to a lot formerly leased to one Drechsler and known as No. 1116 York Road thence Westerly at right angles with the York Road 100 feet to a 3 foot alley thence Southerly about 96 feet and 7 1/2 inches to Merryman's Lane and thence South-easterly along Merryman's Lane about 121 feet and 7 inches to the place of beginning being the property known as 1100 1102 1104 1112 and 1114 York Road'. Title recital: '(For title see deed from David Stewart to Alice Gerry Stewart dated February 8, 1897 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber R.O. No. 1661 fol 69 [?] and deed from Alice Gerry Stewart and David Stewart to Elizabeth Pangiris dated October 24, 1899 and recorded in Liber R.O. No. 2174 [?] fol 196 [?] and deed from Alice Patterson Harris and husband to Alice Gerry Stewart dated January 13 [?], 1898 and recorded in Liber R.O. 1715 fol 35 [?])', with the improvements, ways and alleys. Habendum: 'in fee simple free and discharged of any ground rent or of any mortgage'. Special warranty and further assurances. Signed (with seals) Alice Gerry Stewart, David Stewart and Elizabeth Pangiris, each with a witness. Acknowledged by Alice Gerry Stewart before Edward D. Winslow, U.S. Consul General, Stockholm, Sweden, July 22 [?], 1910; by Elizabeth Pangiris before Julius Hartman, U.S. Consular Agent, Lucerne, Switzerland, July 18, 1910; and by David Stewart before Beverly W. Smith, notary public, Baltimore, June 30, 1910. Received for record Sept. 30, 1910 at about 3 P.M. and recorded the same day (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). What it settles: (1) how the apex left David Stewart: with the houses beside it, from the Gerry-Stewart family to Auxiliary Realty in fee, by the Stewarts and Elizabeth Pangiris together. The recited chain is David Stewart to his wife (1897, probably the step that took the 1890 Legg lots out of his name, inference), Alice Patterson Harris and husband to Alice Gerry Stewart (1898, probably the Harris fee in the lots north of the apex from the 1884 deed, W.M.I. 141/405, inference) and Alice and David to Elizabeth Pangiris (1899, a share for her, inference). The recital does not say which deed carries which lot. (2) The five lots are 1100, 1102, 1104, 1112 and 1114 York Road, the west-side frontage from Merryman's Lane north about 181 ft to 3224's south line (so 3224, '1116 York Road', is expressly out), 100 ft deep to the three-foot alley. The apex is in them: the beginning is the corner of the lane and the road, and 1100 and 1102 are the apex's two numbers (inference). The block is described once, so the apex is not drawn separately (36 ft 1/2 in, 42 ft, 55 ft) and the deed does not say which lot is which. (3) It is all fee simple, 'free and discharged of any ground rent or of any mortgage': nothing here names the $60 Brown rent or the Georges, which fits the rent having merged in Legg in 1890 (inference). (4) No price: $5 and other considerations; the $9,000 purchase-money mortgage Auxiliary took from Cityco the day before it conveyed (2610/403) puts the sale above $9,000 (inference). (5) Alice Gerry Stewart's 1890 mortgage on the apex is not mentioned. The clause 'free and discharged of any ground rent or of any mortgage' and her being the mortgagee and a grantor suggest it was satisfied or merged by 1910 (inference; no release is located). What it does not settle: which recited deed carried the apex (R.O. 1661/69 [?], the 1897 deed to Alice, is the likely one); the R.O. libers, which are hard to read, and the 1899 figure looks too high for October 1899 (R.O. 1759 is Nov. 1898, R.O. 2123 is Jan. 1905); whether the three houses between 1104 and 1112 (old 1106 to 1110, inside the 181 ft) are in the five; why the deed was dated June 30 but signed abroad in July and recorded only on Sept. 30; and the $120 lease of 1911, which this deed and the deed to Cityco show was not yet made. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (R.O. 1661, R.O. 1715 and S.C.L. 2610/548 read): the two recited steps are read. R.O. 1661/69 is David Stewart's deed to Alice Gerry Stewart of Feb. 8, 1897 (752:mdlr-ro1661-69-david-stewart-alice-gerry-stewart-waverly-property-1897): all his Waverly lots, 'seven lots, five of which' in Legg's deed of 1890 (J.B. 1292/384), so the apex in fee, for $2,500, subject to an unrecorded $10,000 mortgage of May 1, 1890 to Annah St. Clair Gerry; the 'R.O. 1661 fol 69 [?]' is confirmed. R.O. 1715/35 is dated Jan. 18, 1898, not the 13th, and recorded Jan. 19 (752:mdlr-ro1715-35-harris-alice-gerry-stewart-third-lot-1898): the Harrises' fee in the 60-ft lot north of the apex, $2,500. The 1899 deed to Pangiris is not read; its recited liber (R.O. 2174 [?]) is too high for October 1899 (R.O. 1759 is Nov. 1898, R.O. 2123 Jan. 1905).

Special warranty and further assurances. Signed 'The Auxiliary Realty Company of Baltimore City by Talbott Denmead President' under the corporate seal (its date may read 1892 [?]), attested by Webster Le Tall [?], Secretary, and Peter Sahm [?]; acknowledged Sept. 30, 1910 before Peter Sahm [?], justice of the peace, by Talbott Denmead, president. Received for record Sept. 30, 1910, about 3 P.M., and recorded the same day. What it settles: (1) the Oct. 1, 1910 Sun report of five houses 'transferred by the Auxiliary Realty Company to the Cityco Realty Company, in fee' is this deed (row 4651). The Stewarts' deed to Auxiliary and Auxiliary's deed to Cityco were received for record the same afternoon, minutes apart (the mortgage back at 3:04 P.M.), so Auxiliary took title only to pass it on, one step in a prearranged sale (inference). (2) The grant repeats the Stewarts' description and the five numbers, in fee, with no rent or mortgage named; Cityco held the apex and the four houses in fee from Sept. 30, 1910 until the sale back of 1100 and 1102 to Auxiliary that the Sun reported on Nov. 10, 1910 (rows 42319 and 5188). What it does not settle: the price; the Nov. 10 sale back (a deed not yet found, and whether 1104, 1112 and 1114 stayed with Cityco); or who stood behind Cityco. The scan holds, in order: the Stewarts' deed to the Auxiliary Realty Company (folios 401 to 402), the Auxiliary Realty Company's deed to the Cityco Realty Company (402 to 403), Cityco's purchase-money mortgage back to Auxiliary (403 to 405), and at the foot of 405 the City Block Building Association No. 4's release to George S. Laumann and wife and the head of William E. Hooton [?] and wife's deed to Laumann, neither on the corridor). Entry 266, indexed 'Cityco Realty Co, Mtge to Auxiliary Realty Co'. Made Sept. 29, 1910, the day before the deed it secures, 'by and between the Cityco Realty Company of Baltimore City of the first part and The Auxiliary Realty Company of Baltimore City of the second part both corporations duly incorporated under the laws of the State of Maryland'. Recital: 'Whereas The Mortgagee has sold to the Mortgagor certain property hereinafter described under the understanding that it should take a purchase money mortgage for Nine thousand ($9000.) Dollars of the purchase money payable one year after date with interest at six per cent per annum payable semi-annually'. For $1 Cityco 'does hereby grant and assign to The Auxiliary Realty Company of Baltimore City its successors and assigns in fee simple all those lots or parcels of ground' of the same description, '(being the property known as 1100 1102 1104 1112 and 1114 York Road)', defeasible on payment of the $9,000 and the interest. Power of sale on default by a decree of the Circuit Court or Circuit Court No. 2 of Baltimore City under the 1898 act (Chapter 123, sections 720 to 732), or by the mortgagee, or by 'David Stewart so constituted Attorney or Agent' under Article 66 of the 1888 Code; proceeds to the sale expenses and a commission, then the mortgagee's claim, then the surplus to Cityco; Cityco to pay taxes and to insure the improvements for at least $9,000 for the mortgagee's benefit. Signed 'Cityco Realty Company of Baltimore City, Per John J. Hurst [?], President' under its corporate seal, attested by Peter Sahm [?]. Acknowledged Sept. 29, 1910 before a justice of the peace by 'Talbott Denmead President of the Mortgag[...] named in the foregoing Mortgage' (the word is cut at the page edge; the signer is Hurst [?], so this is probably a clerk's slip, inference); at the same time David Stewart, Treasurer of the Auxiliary Realty Company, made oath that the consideration was true and bona fide (Peter Sahm [?], J.P., folio 405). Received for record Sept. 30, 1910 at 3:04 P.M. A marginal note under the recording line reads 'For Sht Rel & Sht Asst on folio 548', that is a short release and short assignment, which I take to refer to this mortgage (inference). What it settles: (1) the structure of the Sept. 1910 sale: Auxiliary took a $9,000 purchase-money mortgage on the five lots, payable in a year, from Cityco, so the price is above $9,000 (inference); (2) David Stewart was Treasurer of the Auxiliary Realty Company, so the 1910 deeds are the Stewarts conveying to their own company; (3) the note points to S.C.L. 2610/548, a short release and assignment of this mortgage, perhaps the paper that cleared 1100 and 1102 when Cityco sold them back to Auxiliary on Nov. 10, 1910 (inference). What it does not settle: folio 548 itself, who owned Cityco, and what became of the mortgage. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (R.O. 1661, R.O. 1715 and S.C.L. 2610/548 read): the 'Sht Rel & Sht Asst on folio 548' are read (752:mdlr-scl2610-548-auxiliary-hurst-short-assignment-cityco-mortgage-1912 and 752:mdlr-scl2610-548-hurst-cityco-short-release-1912): Auxiliary assigned this mortgage without recourse to John J. Hurst (dated Jan. 28 [?], 1912, recorded Mar. 12, 1912), the name Cityco's president signs here, and Hurst released it to Cityco on Mar. 12, 1912, so the $9,000 was paid by early 1912. The assignment's forwarding line reads 'folio 415', probably a slip for 405.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 2559, folios 393 to 395 (MSA CE 168-2567; read 2026-10-17 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 393 to 397, a faded high-contrast copy of a clerk's hand, at 110 to 450 dpi; the top of 393 is the end of the sisters' deed back to Frederick Fink, this deed opens at the foot of 393 under the index heading 'Frederick Fink &c Deed to Mary Catherine Fink &c' and ends on 395, and the rest of 395 to 397 is Mary K. Fink's mortgage to the Central Savings Bank, both filed as their own rows). Dated Feb. 9, 1910 (the numeral before 'th' prints like a 4 in this hand; the 1917 and 1919 recitals both read 'February 9th 1910', so the 9th is taken) and acknowledged the same day before William D. Gould, J.P.; recorded Feb. 10, 1910, about 1 P.M. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Frederick Fink and Pansy V. Fink his wife, of Baltimore City, for 'five dollars ($5.00) in hand paid', grant Mary Catherine Fink, Bertha Kiel wife of Samuel F. A. Kiel and Estella Fink, 'their heirs and assigns in fee simple all their right title and interest in and to all those four parcels of ground' in Baltimore City 'which are fully described in the deeds following'. First: the lot of the deed from Augustus D. Clemens Jr. and Mary Clemens his wife to William L. Fink of April 18, 1898, Liber R.O. No. 1729 folio 241 (the 3013 lot, row 46109). Second: the lot of the deed from Eugenia D. Gabler and Louis H. Gabler her husband, Sarah Pennington, Edward W. Mumma and wife, David T. Mumma and wife and Margaret M. Matthews, Nov. 10, 1894, J.B. 1530/115. Third: the lot of the deed to William L. Fink from Matilda W. Sanger and Charles W. Sanger her husband of April 1897 (the liber and folio read like 'No. 1347, folio 44' and are not safe to cite). Fourth: the lot of the County deed from the Gablers, Sarah and Ross J. Pennington, the Mummas, Julia and Nathan A. Clowes and Margaret M. Matthews to William Louis (as read) Fink of Dec. 30, 1887, Baltimore County 'now City', Liber J.W.S. No. 167 folio 484. No courses are given for any of them; each is described by its deed. Recital: the four lots are 'part of the rest residue and remainder of the estate of which William L. Fink late of Baltimore City aforesaid deceased died seized and possessed', which he 'by his last will and testament dated the 2nd day of February in the year 1893 duly admitted to probate by the Orphans Court of Baltimore City ... and recorded in the office of the Register of Wills of the said City in Wills Liber S.R.M. No. 82 folio 278 &c gave bequeathed and devised unto his wife Louisa Fink for life or for such time as she continued to remain a widow and from and after her death or marriage whichever should first happen to his four children the said Mary Catherine Fink, Bertha Fink who since intermarried with the said Samuel F. A. Kiel, Frederick Fink and Estella Fink as tenants in common share and share alike per stirpes and not per capita', her tenancy ending 'by her death on the 26th day of July 1907' (the numerals as read; the year cannot be right, see below). To hold to the three sisters 'as tenants in common in fee simple'; special warranty and further assurances. Witness Wm. D. Gould; signed Frederick Fink and Pansy V. Fink (seals). What it settles: (1) The step from William L. Fink to the Kiels and Himmelmanns is a family succession, not a sale. Fink, grantee of the 14-ft lot in 1898, left the residue of his estate by will to his wife Louisa for life or widowhood and then to his four children, Mary Catherine, Bertha, Frederick and Estella, as tenants in common; the deed says he 'died seized and possessed' of the 1898 lot, so he died after April 18, 1898, and the deed reads the lot as part of the residue of a will made five years before he bought it. (2) On Feb. 9, 1910 Frederick and his wife conveyed all their interest in the four lots to his three sisters; the same day, in the deed that ends at the top of folio 393, the sisters released Frederick a lot their mother Louisa had bought in 1907 (row 720:mdlr-scl2559-392-mary-bertha-estella-to-frederick-fink-louisa-fink-lot-1910-negative): a division of the two estates between the brother and the sisters (an inference from the pair). Each sister held an undivided share of 3013 from then, probably a third (an inference: no shares are stated). (3) Louisa Fink was the mother of Frederick, Bertha and Estella only ('her three children'), so Mary Catherine was very probably William L. Fink's daughter by an earlier marriage (an inference). Mary K. Fink of the 1915 roll and of the 1919 recital is Mary Catherine Fink: the 1919 deed cites as 'Mary K Fink to Estella F Himmelmann' the 1917 deed that is signed Mary Catherine Fink. (4) The 1917 deed (row 720:mdlr-scl3126-290-mary-catherine-fink-himmelmann-3013-and-five-limond-place-lots-1917) names the first lot of this deed '3013 York Road (formerly 1005)' and puts the County deed of 1887 behind five Limond Place lots, not behind 3013. What it does not settle: William L. Fink's date of death and the will itself (Wills S.R.M. 82/278, not read); the year of Louisa Fink's death: the recital reads 1907, yet the other deed on folio 393 recites her buying a lot from Frank D. Watkins on Sept. 26, 1907, so she lived past July 1907 and a numeral is misread (probably 1908 or 1909, an inference); the second and third parcels (Matilda W. Sanger was the ground-rent owner of the 3201 Greenmount block and leased William L. Fink ground there in 1889, J.B. 1244/245, row 17768, so the third parcel may lie there, an inference); the 1914 deeds that divided the sisters' shares (S.C.L. 2883/370 and 371, recited in 1917, not read); and whether the will, made in 1893, reached a lot bought in 1898 as the deed assumes.

summary: Deed (the tail only), Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 2559, ending on folio 393 (MSA CE 168-2567; read 2026-10-17; only the last page, 393, is on the scan, and it opens in the middle of the description, so the heading, the price and the lot's courses are on folio 392 or earlier and are not seen). It is the deed that stands directly before the Frederick Fink deed of 3013 (row 720:mdlr-scl2559-393-frederick-fink-mary-catherine-bertha-estella-four-lots-3013-1910) and is made the same day, Feb. 9, 1910 (the numeral reads like a 4, as there). Mary Catherine Fink, Bertha Kiel and Samuel F. A. Kiel her husband, and Estella Fink grant Frederick Fink, in fee simple, 'all the right title and interest of the said grantors' in a lot that Louisa Fink took 'by virtue of two deeds', one from Charles J. Murphy of Jan. 26, 1907 (Liber R.O. 2305, folio 824, as read; the writer's 2 prints like a 4) and one from Frank D. Watkins, widower, of Sept. 26, 1907 (R.O. 2371, folio 290, as read), 'and title to which said lot of ground descended in fee simple on the death of the said Louisa Fink their mother intestate to her three children the said Frederick Fink, Bertha Kiel born Fink and Estella Fink as her only heirs at law and being also the same lot of ground in and to which the said Mary Catherine Fink acquired a one fourth right title and interest by virtue of a deed bearing even date herewith ... from the said Frederick Fink and Pansy V. Fink his wife, Bertha Kiel and Samuel F. A. Kiel her husband and Estella Fink to the said Mary Catherine Fink'. Witness Wm. D. Gould; signed by the four; acknowledged before William D. Gould, J.P.; recorded Feb. 10, 1910, about 1 P.M. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). What it settles: this is not 3013's ground. It is Louisa Fink's own purchase of 1907, which her three children first gave Mary Catherine a quarter of and then, with her, all released to Frederick, on the day Frederick gave his three sisters his share of their father's four lots. It fixes the family: Louisa was the mother of Frederick, Bertha (Kiel) and Estella only, and Mary Catherine was the fourth child of William L. Fink (the will, recited in the next deed). The Murphy and Watkins libers fit the City series (R.O. 2298 was Dec. 26, 1906; R.O. 2358 Aug. 3, 1907; R.O. 2369 Sept. 17, 1907), so the dates are right and Louisa Fink was alive on Sept. 26, 1907. What it does not settle: where the lot lies, its price, and the deed of even date that gave Mary Catherine her quarter (not on these folios).

summary: Mortgage (negative: not 3013), Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 2559, folios 395 to 397 and on (MSA CE 168-2567; read 2026-10-17; the index heading on 395 is 'Mary K. Fink Mtge to Central Savings Bank of Balto', and the scan ends in the covenants on 397). Dated Feb. 10, 1910, the day after the Fink family deeds (row 720:mdlr-scl2559-393-frederick-fink-mary-catherine-bertha-estella-four-lots-3013-1910). Mary K. Fink, unmarried, borrows $1,500 from the Central Savings Bank of Baltimore, repayable with interest at 5 percent half-yearly on seven negotiable notes (one of $1,500 at three years and six of $37.50 at 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 and 36 months), and mortgages 'all that lot or parcel of ground situate in Baltimore City', beginning 'on the East side of the York Turnpike Road' at the north-west corner of a lot John Hussman (as read) and wife conveyed George Folts by deed of April 5, 1880 (J.B. 116/433), a beginning 422 ft 9 1/2 in northerly from the south-east corner of the York Turnpike Road and Eleventh Street: 20 ft on the turnpike, east about 196 ft, 20 ft south and straight back about 173 ft; the lot Edward Schleigh and wife deeded her on April 27, 1906 (R.O. 2230, folio 233, as read), with the privilege to prepay $300 or more at a time and a power of sale. What it settles: it is another lot of Mary K. Fink's, measured from Eleventh Street, nowhere near the two-mile stone, and has nothing to do with 3013. It shows she was already an investor in ground in 1906 and borrowed $1,500 on one of her own lots the day after she took her third of her father's four lots. What it does not settle: where the Eleventh Street lot is, or whether this mortgage was ever released.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 3126, folios 290 to 291 (MSA CE 168-3134; read 2026-10-17 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 290 to 294, in a clear clerk's hand at 110 and 170 dpi; the top of 290 is the end of a building association's release of a mortgage of Feb. 2, 1916 (S.C.L. 3026/457), recorded May 3, 1917, and 291 to 294 carry the next deed (row below) and three unrelated instruments: a Permanent Building Association release to Albin R. Windsor, Michael W. Ganzhorn's lease of an Augusta Avenue lot to Francis M. Ganzhorn and a York Road Building Association release to Norman P. Dewey). Index heading 'Mary Catherine Fink, Deed to Estella F. Himmelmann &c' (item 183; margin 'Grantee 7/12/17'). Dated and acknowledged May 1, 1917 before John G. Schilpp, Notary Public for Baltimore City, who is the witness; recorded May 3, 1917, about 1:17 P.M. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Mary Catherine Fink, unmarried, of Baltimore City, for 'five dollars' and 'other good and valuable considerations', grants Estella F. Himmelmann and Sigmund Himmelmann her husband 'as tenants by entireties their assigns the survivor of them and the heirs and assigns of such survivor in fee simple all her right title interest and estate in and to all those six lots or parcels of ground' in Baltimore City: 'The first thereof being the same lot or parcel which by deed dated April 18, 1898 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber R.O. No. 1729 folio 241 etc was granted and conveyed by Augustus D. Clemens and wife to William L. Fink and being also the same lot of ground which is first described in the deed from Frederick Fink and wife to the said party of the first part and Bertha F. Kiel and Estella Fink (now Himmelmann) dated February 9th 1910 and recorded as aforesaid in Liber S.C.L. No. 2559 folio 393 etc the improvements being 3013 York Road (formerly 1005)'; 'The Second, third, fourth, fifth and Sixth of said lots being and comprising Nos. 2922-2924-2926-2928 and 2930 Limond or Lamont Place', meant to carry 'all the land (with the improvements thereon) east of the westernmost [side] of the few foot alley laid out on the plat hereinafter referred to and extending over to the west side of Limond or Lamont Place together with the use of the alleys shown on said plat'. 'For title see' the deed from Eugenia D. Gabler etc. to William L. Fink of Dec. 30, 1887, Baltimore County, J.W.S. 167/484 (folio 484 in the 1910 deed; the first numeral reads like a 2 in this hand); the deed from Frederick Fink and wife 'above referred to'; the deed from Estella F. Himmelmann etc. to Bertha F. Kiel and the grantor, March 10, 1914, S.C.L. 2883/371, 'and plat of S. J. Martenet & Co. filed with said deed'. To hold 'as one undivided third interest in and to the said described lots of ground and premises'; the grantor covenants she has encumbered nothing and warrants specially. Signed Mary Catherine Fink (seal); witness John G. Schilpp. What it settles: (1) 3013 York Road, formerly 1005, is the 14-ft lot of the 1898 Clemens deed (R.O. 1729/241): the first deed to join that lot to the street numbers, so the Polk tenants of the 1005 store after 1898 (Bertha Fink 1901 to 1904, Rosa Vicary, Harry Peiser) are on 3013. (2) Mary Catherine Fink held an undivided third of 3013 in 1917 and sold it to her sister Estella and Sigmund Himmelmann, who with Bertha Kiel and her husband are the grantors of the 1919 deed to Holmes (row 47367): Mary Catherine is not a 1919 grantor because she had sold out two years earlier. (3) The Fink title in 3013 runs 1898 Clemens to William L. Fink, then by his will to his four children (S.C.L. 2559/393, Feb. 9, 1910), then the sisters' shares are rearranged on March 10, 1914 (S.C.L. 2883/370 and 371), May 1, 1917 and Feb. 7, 1919. (4) The five lots 2922 to 2930 Limond or Lamont Place are the Limond Place houses of the 1919 deed (S.C.L. 3311/297 and 309, rows 47367 and 47368) and come from the 1887 County deed (J.W.S. 167/484), not from 3013's ground; the 1887 deed does not need chasing for 3013. What it does not settle: the shares after 1914 (the 1917 deed says 'one undivided third', yet the 1914 deed from Estella to Bertha and Mary Catherine is recited as a division, so S.C.L. 2883/370 and 371 must be read), the price (the 1919 stamps point to about $7,000 to $7,500 for 3013 and one Limond Place parcel), and William L. Fink's date of death (the will, S.R.M. 82/278).

Hilberg and wife, deed, 50/477 (J.H.L.); (4) Oct. 14, 1868, from George V. Smith, John W. and others, assignment, 59/471 (E.H.A.); (5) Apr. 23, 1869, to William Courtenay, John W. and wife, lease, 62/110 (E.H.A.); (6) May 7, 1869, to Joseph M. Cone and others, John W. and others, deed, 62/262 (E.H.A.); (7) Jan. 18, 1870, from George W. Belt, assignment, 64/420 (E.H.A.). What it settles: (1) Line 1 is the Litzinger deed of Feb. 10, 1864, recorded Feb. 11 (row 47383): the index agrees with the scan on date, parties and numbers. (2) John W. Treadway was a dealer in lots, not the holder of one: seven lines in six years, four ways in (a deed from Litzinger, a deed from Hilberg, assignments from Smith and Belt) and three ways out (a deed to Pilson, a lease to Courtenay, a deed to Cone). Lines 4 and 6 are the Coffield 79-ft leasehold he held with John Bruns and William Heise in 1868 and 1869 (E.H.A. 59/471 and 62/262, read, rows 47529 and 47523, chapter 14), filed under the same John W. Treadway, and no second John W. Treadway is indexed in these eleven years, so the buyer of the 214-ft lot south of Baden's lot and the partner of Bruns and Heise are very probably one man (inference). (3) What became of the 214-ft lot (3011 to 3019): only line 2 can touch it, a deed from Treadway and wife to Ann Pilson a year after he bought (J.H.L. 44/25; the index gives no description). The ground sold at the 1896 decree sale and deeded to Miller and Clemens is the whole 214 ft by the 1864 courses, so if Pilson's lot was a piece of it, it came back before 1896 by a deed this index does not show; more probably line 2 is other ground of his (inference). After Jan. 18, 1870 there is no line of any kind for John W. Treadway through May 29, 1874, and the scan of the next volume shows none from April 1877 to August 1885 (720:index-1874-1895-v18-treadway-john-no-line-1877-1885): no deed, lease or mortgage out of him of the whole lot, and no mortgage or release under his name in any year read. (4) If he died owning the lot, it passed by will or descent and not by deed (an inference from the silence, to be tested against his estate papers): the 'Miss Tredway' of Thompson's 1889 plat, under John T. Ensor as guardian, would then be a minor heir, and the Harrisons of the 1896 decree her successors (both inferences). A deed or lease with his wife joining (lines 2 and 5) suggests ground of his own in fee, so J.H.L. 44/25 and E.H.A. 62/110 are the two to read first. What it does not settle: what the Pilson, Courtenay, Hilberg and Belt instruments describe (the index locates none of them); who Ann Pilson and William Courtenay were; whether and when John W. Treadway died; any Treadway under another given name (a widow, Alice, Mary or a trustee would be in the other given-name sections of the T surnames, before page 124 or after page 139, which these scans do not hold); and the record from June 1874 to April 1877.

summary: Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records (R.O. series), Liber R.O. 1661, folios 69 to 72 (MSA CE 168-1669; read 2026-10-17 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 69 to 73, at 150 and 300 dpi. The scan holds: the end of Eben B. Hunting's lease assignment to Wertie M. Reister of five Sherwood Avenue lots (acknowledged Feb. 1, 1897, recorded Feb. 10 at 9:30 a.m.; head of folio 69); this deed (foot of 69 to 72); the Light Street Savings and Building Association's release to Jacob Durm (Feb. 10, 1897; 72 to 73); and the head of Luther W. Hopkins's deed to the Remington Machine Company (Jan. 20, 1897; 73)). Captioned 'David Stewart, Deed to Alice Gerry Stewart'. Made Feb. 8, 1897: 'This Deed made this eighth day of February A D 1897 by David Stewart of Baltimore City and State of Maryland to Alice Gerry Stewart his wife'. The recitals are a family balance sheet. (a) Albert L. Gorter conveyed the premises 1005 N. Charles Street, 'the Colonial', to Stewart on Feb. 28, 1896 (R.O. 1607/306), Gorter being insolvent and the liens 'far in excess of its value'; to pay them and buy the furniture Stewart borrowed $6,000 from Elizabeth J. Pangiris (note of May 1, 1896, three years at 6 percent); on Oct. 1, 1896 (R.O. 1641/507) Alice Gerry Stewart guaranteed the ground rent on it and was to have it for $1,000 more, which she paid. (b) 'David Stewart being possessed of certain property at Waverly in Baltimore City formerly County did on May 1st A D 1890 borrow from Annah St. Clair Gerry ten thousand dollars for three years at six per cent interest per annum payable semi annually and did execute a Mortgage upon said Waverly property to said Gerry to secure the same which Mortgage was dated May 1st 1890 but by an oversight was never recorded'; and Alice 'has bought from said David Stewart all his Waverly property for $2500. Subject to said lien of ten thousand dollars and has paid said $2500'. (c) Stewart sold her his residence, 1301 N. Charles Street, and stable, 1302 Morton Alley, for $5,000 and other considerations, subject to a mortgage to Charles C. Harrison. Then, for the premises and five dollars, Stewart 'doth hereby grant convey and assign to said Alice Gerry Stewart all the following properties lying in Baltimore City', in three groups; the second is 'the Waverly property being all those seven lots of ground five of which are particularly described in a Deed from John H. C. Legg to David Stewart dated April 26th A D 1890 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber J B No 1292 folio 384 &c one of which is particularly described in a Deed from Lucy C George and husband to David Stewart dated July 18th A D 1890 and recorded as aforesaid in Liber J B No 1303 folio 206 &c and the last of which is particularly described in a Deed from Milton Heathcote to David Stewart dated October 13th A D 1891 and recorded as aforesaid in Liber J B No 1363 folio 585 &c the lot described in the second mentioned Deed being the reversion in the lot fifthly described in the first mentioned Deed the lot at the southwest corner of Merrymans Lane and York Road being subject to an eighty dollar ground rent payable March and September and the Heathcote lot to a $150 ground rent payable December 11th and June 11th and the other lots being in fee', 'subject however as to said two lots to said ground rents subject also to the operation and effect of an unrecorded Mortgage and equitable lien made by David Stewart to Annah St. Clair Gerry to secure the payment of a note drawn by him in her favor for $10,000 dated May 1st 1890'. No bounds are given for the Waverly lots. The habendum runs to 'the said two lots (Residence and stable)', 'in fee simple subject to the operation and effect of a five year Mortgage dated February 19th 1897 [as written; its liber, J.B. 1488, belongs to about 1894] and recorded in Liber J B No 1488 folio 370 from said David Stewart to said Charles C Harrison'; special warranty. Witness Peter Sahm, justice of the peace, before whom Stewart acknowledged and Alice Gerry Stewart swore the consideration true on Feb. 8, 1897; received for record Feb. 10, 1897 at 10:35 a.m. (Robt. Ogle, Clerk). The Charles Street recitals also show Robert R. Brown as Stewart's conduit (Alice Gerry Patterson's leasehold to Brown and Brown's deed back to Stewart, both May 19, 1886, J.B. 1096/257; Brown to Stewart, Feb. 11, 1891, J.B. 1330/127). What it settles: (1) the apex went from David Stewart to his wife on Feb. 8, 1897: it is lot 1 of the five lots of Legg's deed (J.B. 1292/384), conveyed by that reference, so the 1910 recital 'R.O. 1661 fol 69' is confirmed. The deed does not single the apex out and gives no bounds. (2) The estate is fee simple: only two Waverly lots carry rents, the $80 lot at the south-west corner of the lane (reversion bought from the Georges on July 18, 1890) and the $150 'Heathcote lot', and 'the other lots' are 'in fee', so the apex stands free of the $60 Brown rent (which merged in Legg, inference). (3) The price of the Waverly lots is $2,500, 'subject to said lien of ten thousand dollars', so about $12,500 in all (arithmetic, inference). (4) The only mortgage named on them is the unrecorded $10,000 mortgage of May 1, 1890 to Annah St. Clair Gerry, whom earlier rows take for Alice's mother (inference): five days after Legg's deed back to Stewart (Apr. 26) and thirteen before it was recorded (May 14), so the Gerry money very probably paid for Stewart's recovery of Sinclair's lots (inference). The note ran three years, to May 1, 1893; how the lien ended is not shown, and by 1910 the lots are conveyed 'free and discharged of any ground rent or of any mortgage' (S.C.L. 2610/401). No mortgage to Alice Gerry Stewart herself is named. (5) Robert R. Brown, the apex's lessor of 1887, appears as Stewart's go-between in 1886 and 1891 too, so the 1887 sale and lease back was a Stewart pattern (inference). summary: Deed in fee simple, Baltimore City Superior Court land records (R.O. series), Liber R.O. 1715, folios 35 to 36 (MSA CE 168-1723; read 2026-10-17 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 35 to 39, at 150 and 300 dpi. The scan holds: the end of Patrick H. Philbin's deed (acknowledged and recorded Jan. 20, 1898; head of folio 35); this deed (35 to 36); George A. Dubreuil's deed to William W. Snouffer of a Potter Avenue leasehold at $52 a year (Jan. 19, 1898; 36 to 37); and Snouffer's $400 mortgage to the Baltimore Fidelity Building and Savings Association (Jan. 19, 1898; 37 to 39), none on the corridor). Captioned 'Alice P Harris &c, Deed to Alice G Stewart'. Made Jan. 18, 1898: 'This Deed made this eighteenth day of January 1898 by Alice Patterson Harris and William Hall Harris her husband to Alice Gerry Stewart Witnesseth that in consideration of $2500' they 'do hereby grant and convey unto the said Alice Gerry Stewart all that lot piece or parcel of ground lying and situated in Baltimore City', 'Beginning for the same on the westernmost side of the York Turnpike Road at the distance of thirty six feet and one half of an inch northerly from the corner formed by the intersection of the northeast side of Merryman's Lane and the westernmost side of said York Turnpike Road which place of beginning is designed to be at the centre of the division wall between the house on the lot now being described and the house on the adjoining lot on the south': west through the wall 42 ft more or less to the lane, north-west 76 ft 7 in along the lane to the east side of a three-foot alley, north 11 ft 8 in on the alley to a line drawn west from a point on the turnpike 60 ft north of the beginning, east on that line 100 ft to the turnpike, and south on the turnpike 60 ft to the beginning. Recital: 'Being the same lot of ground thirdly described in a lease from W. Hall Harris and Alice P. Harris his wife to James E. Sinclair dated June 11, 1884 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County in Liber W.M.I. No 141 folio 407 said lease creating a redeemable ground rent of one hundred and fifty dollars ($150.) per annum'. 'To Have and To Hold unto the said Alice Gerry Stewart her heirs and assigns forever in fee simple'; special warranty and further assurances. Signed Alice P. Harris and W. Hall Harris, witness and justice of the peace Wm. Merriken, before whom both acknowledged on Jan. 18, 1898; received for record Jan. 19, 1898 at 3:25 P.M. (Robt. Ogle, Clerk). What it settles: (1) the 1884 lease had a third lot: 60 ft of frontage from 36 ft 1/2 in to 96 ft 1/2 in north of the lane corner, the lot just north of the apex (its south line is the apex's north wall; the houses are the old 1104 and its neighbours, probably today's 3204 to 3210, inference), let at $150 a year. The 1888 assignment to Stewart took only the first two lots (3224's), so this third leasehold stayed with Sinclair until it reached Stewart, probably as the 'Heathcote lot' of Oct. 13, 1891 (J.B. 1363/585), which the 1897 deed calls subject to a '$150 ground rent payable December 11th and June 11th': the same rent and the same days (inference). (2) The Harris fee did not come back to Stewart; the Harrises held the reversion in this lot from 1884 to 1898 and sold it, with the rent, to Alice Gerry Stewart for $2,500, which is the $150 rent at 6 percent exactly. The deed does not recite their own 1884 title (W.M.I. 141/405). (3) The estate is fee simple, to Alice alone; with the leasehold already in her by her husband's deed of Feb. 8, 1897, lease and rent met in her in January 1898 (inference). (4) No mortgage is named. (5) This is not the apex and not 3224's lot. It is one of the five lots of the 1910 deed to Auxiliary, whose recital cites it as 'dated January 13 [?], 1898 ... R.O. 1715 fol 35': the date is the 18th and the liber and folio are confirmed. What it does not settle: the Heathcote deed; why the Harrises, who let 3224's two lots go to Stewart on redemption in 1890 (J.B. 1276/42), kept this third lot to 1898; and who Alice Patterson Harris was (the name suggests kinship with Alice Gerry Stewart, once Alice Gerry Patterson, inference).

summary: Short assignment, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 2610, folio 548 (MSA CE 168-2618; read 2026-10-17 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 546 to 550, at 150 and 300 dpi. Folios 546 and 547 hold two deeds recorded Oct. 1, 1910 (Amelia A. List and husband to D. Meredith Reese and wife, a $45 rent and reversion on Hollins Street; Rudolph J. Motz to Geo. J. Steinmann, two Vincent Alley leaseholds at $30). Folio 548 is the back of the book, where short releases and assignments of earlier mortgages were entered later under 'Forwarded from folio N' headings: Isaac N. Cooper's release of lien to Conrad Jordan (Dec. 4, 1910); the pair filed here; and the Real Estate and Improvement Company's short release to George W. Abrams (Jan. 23, 1913, recorded April 1913). Folio 549 holds three more short releases (Levy, 1914; Johns, 1916; Spencer, 1920) and folio 550 is blank). Headed 'Auxiliary Realty Co, Sht Asst to, John J. Hurst', 'Forwarded from folio 415' (as read; the note on folio 405 sends the reader to this pair, so the figure is probably a slip for 405). 'The Auxiliary Realty Company of Baltimore City for value received doth hereby assign without recourse the within Mortgage to John J. Hurst. Witness the hand of its President and its corporate seal attested by its secretary this 28th [?] day of January 1912.' Edith H. Davis [?], secretary; the corporate seal reads 'The Auxiliary Realty Company of Baltimore City, Incorporated 1897'; signed 'The Auxiliary Realty Company of Baltimore City, Talbot Denmead, President'. Recorded March 12, 1912 (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). What it settles: (1) the 'Sht Rel & Sht Asst on folio 548' of the note on folio 405 are this pair: Cityco's $9,000 purchase-money mortgage (S.C.L. 2610/403) was assigned by Auxiliary, without recourse, to John J. Hurst, the name Cityco's president signed on the mortgage. (2) The seal answers the date of the Auxiliary Realty Company: 1897, the year David Stewart conveyed his Waverly lots to his wife (R.O. 1661/69) and, by earlier rows, Mrs. Gerry's rents were divided between her daughters. (3) Nothing on folio 548 shows a release or partial release of the mortgage in 1910 or 1911: if Cityco sold 1100 and 1102 back to Auxiliary on Nov. 10, 1910, as the Sun reported, the mortgage stayed of record on the five lots until March 1912 (inference). What it does not settle: the folio figure (415 or 405); who paid the $9,000; the Nov. 10, 1910 deed; and the date's day (28th [?]).
