summary: Index pages, Baltimore County Court Grantor Index A-Z, 1810 to 1813, pages 164 to 168 (MSA CE 33-6), the 'Go' surnames; read 2026-10-17 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved (five pages, each rendered at 130 dpi, every grantor, grantee and location line enlarged and read). Columns are date (a year only, written at the head of the page or in the margin), grantor, grantee, instrument, location of property, and liber and folio (W.G. numbering). The pages hold: p. 164 'Go cont'd' (1811 and 1812, W.G. 115/29 to 120/257); p. 165 'Go cont'd' (1813, W.G. 120/268 to 125/464); p. 166 'Go cont'd' (1813, W.G. 125/465 to 126/65, then blank to the foot of the page); p. 167 'Gr' (1810 and 1811, W.G. 105/216 to 112/481); and p. 168 'Gr cont'd' (1811, W.G. 112/572 to 115/291). The grantor surnames on the three Go pages are Goodwin, Gorsuch, Gouldsmith (Goldsmith), Gore, Gott, Goodfellow, Gordon, Golder and Gorman. There is NO line for Harry Dorsey Gough, Prudence Gough, Gough's executors, or Gough and wife on any of the five pages (confidence high: the grantor column was read line by line), no grantee named Trustees, and no location text that names a school or a school house. Three lines touch the Huntington ground without being Gough's: (1) 1811, Gorsuch Robert to John E. Taylor, lease, 'pt Merryman's Lot & Huntington', 115/410; (2) 1812, Gorsuch Joshua to John Wilson, lease, 'Lot No 30 York Turnpike road', 117/575; (3) 1813, Gordon James to John Maxfield, assignment, 'Lot No 4 on York Turnpike road', 125/580 (all three readings clear). A Joshua Gorsuch took a 1 1/4 acre Huntington lease from Prudence Gough as executrix in 1808 (W.G. 100/478, row 46655), so line 2 is possibly a sub-lease of a numbered lot of Gough's Huntington plan by the same man (INFERRED: the index names no lessor and the name is common); these are leads, not links. What it settles: (1) Under Go, from W.G. 115/29 (1811) to the end of the run at W.G. 126/65 (1813), there is no instrument by Gough, Prudence Gough or Gough's executors, and none to trustees or for a school under any grantor's name. (2) The Go run of this volume ends on p. 166 (the rest of that page is blank and p. 167 is already Gr), so no Gough line hides on pp. 167 and 168. What it does not settle: (1) W.G. 105 to 115/28 (1810 to mid-1811). p. 164 is already headed 'Go cont'd' and begins at 115/29, while the Gr run on p. 167 begins in 1810 at 105/216, so the first pages of the Go run, about two or three pages by line density (INFERRED: probably pp. 161 to 163), are not in the scan; Prudence Gough's first deeds after the last Gough line in CE 33-5 (105/40, 1809), if any, would be there. (2) A deed entered under another first-named grantor. Gough's will made James Carroll and Prudence Gough his executors (recital in W.G. 102/33, row 46100) and the index files a deed under its first-named grantor, so a school deed by the executors with Carroll named first would sit under Ca, not Go (INFERRED). (3) Whether the school house lot was ever deeded of record. Next: p. 163 and the one or two pages before it in CE 33-6 (the first Go pages, 1810 to mid-1811), then the Ca run for Carroll James, executor, in CE 33-5 to 33-8, and the grantee index under Trustees.

summary: Index pages, Baltimore County Court Grantor Index A-Z, 1814 to 1818, pages 193 to 197 (MSA CE 33-7), the 'Go' surnames; read 2026-10-17 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved (five pages, each rendered at 130 dpi, every line enlarged and read). Columns as in CE 33-6 (the year is written at the head of the page or in the margin; liber and folio are W.G.). The pages hold: p. 193 'Go cont'd' (1816 and 1817, W.G. 137/595 to 142/561); p. 194 'Go cont'd' (1817 and 1818, W.G. 142/562 to 146/689); p. 195 'Go cont'd' (1818, W.G. 147/140 to 147/621, then blank to the foot of the page); p. 196 'Go cont'd' (a ruled page with no entry); and p. 197 'Gr' (1814 and 1815, W.G. 126/126 to 130/268). The Gough lines are all on p. 195, all 1818, all entered 'Gough Prudence &c' as grantor, all Deeds, all W.G. 147, and all of 'Pt Ridgely's Whim', which is a different tract from Huntington: (1) to John Gambrill, 10 3/4 a 23 p, 147/140; (2) to Matilda Waters &c, 12 1/2 a 1 1/2 p, 147/141; (3) to Isaac Green, 7 3/4 a 24 p, 147/149; (4) to Solomon Moonier (surname reading uncertain, Moonier or Mooner), 1/2 acre, 147/151; (5) to Ann Cutler, 1/2 acre, 147/169; (6) to Robert Sinclair, 12 3/4 a 18 p, 147/234; (7) to Robert G. Harper, 18 3/4 a 34 p, 147/286; (8) to Richard Price, 12 a, 147/578. Confidence: grantor, grantees, tract and instrument high; the folios of lines 3 and 5 medium (a 9 that could be a 4). The '&c' after Prudence is not explained by the index; Gough's will made James Carroll and Prudence Gough his executors with a power to sell Huntington and Ridgely's Whim (recital in W.G. 102/33, row 46100), so these are very probably sales by the executors (INFERRED). No Gough line names Huntington, a turnpike, Gough's road, a trustee or a school. The only other line on the five pages that names Huntington is on p. 193: 1816, 'Gooding John' to the President and Directors of the Union Bank of Md, mortgage, 'Lot W.S. Harrison St &c + pts Huntingdon and Huntingdon Resurveyd', 137/595 (the surname is Gooding, not Gough; high confidence). Gooding's other lines are a release to William H. Winder (1818, 145/276) and a deed to John Donnell (1818, 147/317 and 318, 'Jacks Double Purchase' and personal property). No grantee is named Trustees and no location text names a school or a school house. What it settles: (1) Under Go, from W.G. 137/595 (1816) to the end of the run at W.G. 147/621 (1818), the only Gough entries are the eight 1818 Ridgely's Whim deeds: no Huntington deed, no lease, and no deed to trustees or for a school by Gough or Prudence Gough. (2) The Go run of this volume ends on p. 195 and p. 196 is blank, so no later Gough line hides before p. 197. (3) Prudence Gough was alive and conveying in 1818. What it does not settle: (1) W.G. 126 to 137/594 (1814 to 1816). p. 193 is already headed 'Go cont'd', so the first pages of the run, about two by line density (INFERRED: probably pp. 191 and 192), are not in the scan. (2) Executor deeds entered under Carroll (Ca) rather than Gough. (3) What the two half-acre Ridgely's Whim lots (Moonier, Cutler) were: the index gives no road or purpose; the 1823 deed excepts the school house from a Huntington lot, so a Ridgely's Whim lot is not the candidate (INFERRED). (4) Whether Gooding's mortgaged 'pts Huntingdon and Huntingdon Resurveyd' came from the Gough executors or lie near the turnpike; the Union Bank of Maryland later deeded a part of Huntington (W.G. 179/639, row 46037), but the two parcels are not shown to be the same (a lead only). Next: pp. 191 and 192 of CE 33-7 (the first Go pages, 1814 to 1816), then the Ca run for Carroll James, executor, and the grantee index under Trustees.

summary: Index pages, Baltimore County Court Grantor Index A-Z, 1787 to 1797, pages 151 to 160 (MSA CE 33-3), the 'Go' surnames, read for every Gorsuch line on 2026-10-17 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved (ten pages, each rendered at 130 dpi, every grantor, grantee, instrument, location and liber and folio line enlarged and read). It is the scan already filed for Gough's lines (725:index-ce33-3-p151-gough-1787-1797, row 46653); this row is the Gorsuch reading of it. Columns: date (a year in the margin), grantor, grantee, instrument, location of property, W.G. liber and folio, with ditto marks carrying the liber down; lines run in order of recording, not alphabetically. The Go run is pp. 151 to 157 (p. 151 headed 'Go', then 'Go cont'd'); p. 158 is a ruled page with no entry, and pp. 159 and 160 are 'Gr' pages, which hold no Gorsuch line. John Gorsuch as grantor, in page order (the index tags only some lines 'of Thos'): (1) p. 151, 1787: 'Gorsuch John of Thos' to James Edwards, Convey, 'Pt Ensors Inspection', W.G. A.A. 205 (no acreage, road or neighbour; every word high confidence). It stands directly under Harry D. Gough's sale to the same James Edwards ('Pt Huntington Lot No 34 6a', Z/544), and A.A. 205 comes twelve folios after the Maidwell mortgage to Gorsuch (A.A. 193, recorded May 16, 1787, row 46640), so it was recorded soon after that. (2) p. 152, 1792: 'Gorsuch John' to Charles Peregoy, Convey, 'Lot Land 131 Acres', H.H. 178 (no tract name; medium-high). (3) p. 153, 1793: 'Gorsuch Thomas' and 'Gorsuch John &c' (braced) to Joseph McClung, Convey, 'Pt My Lady's Manor, Lot No 52', K.K. 541; and 'Gorsuch John' to Nicholas Gorsuch, Convey, 'Lot No 284 Balto City', M.M. 617. (4) p. 154, 1794: 'Gorsuch John &c' to David McMechin, Convey, 'Jeopardy & Lord Crandals on the Hill' (the second name is hard to read), N.N. 333; and 'Gorsuch John' to Thomas Beasman, Convey, 'Deer Park & Trouting Stream', O.O. 232. (5) p. 155, 1795: 'Gorsuch John' to James Maidwell, 'Release &c', 'Pt Ensors Inspection 9 A. &c', S.S. 231 (the release of the 1787 mortgage, read, row 46630). (6) p. 156, 1796: 'Gorsuch John' to Elijah Merryman, Convey, 'Contrivance to Coles Chance 6 1/4 acres', X.X. 80; and 'Gorsuch John' with 'Gorsuch Sarah' (braced) to William Stone, Convey, 'Pt Friendship 117 Acres', X.X. 118. (7) p. 157, 1797: 'Gorsuch Robert' and 'Gorsuch John' (braced) to Samuel Smith, Convey, 'Pt Ensors Choice & Loveless' Addition 34 3/4 a', Y.Y. 236. Ensor's Choice is a different tract from Ensor's Inspection: it is the Gorsuch family land (the line above it on p. 151, 1787, Nathan and Loveless Gorsuch to Robert Gorsuch, 'Ensors Choice & Loveless' Addition', A.A. 196, is the deed that follows the Maidwell mortgage in the liber, row 46640), and this John is possibly John of Thomas, Robert's brother (INFERRED). Apart from line (5), which is his own release, the index does not say which John Gorsuch lines (2), (3), (4), (6) and (7) are; the other John of the pages is 'Gorsuch John of Wm' (1792, to Benjamin Parks, 'Pt Matthews Meadow 40a', J.J. 326), a different man. No Gorsuch line on pp. 151 to 157 names the York road or turnpike, Huntington, Merryman's Lot, Hailes, Speagle, or Baltimore Town lots 28 and 29; the other Gorsuch lines (Robert, Thomas, Benjamin, Nicholas, Joshua, David, Richard, William, Charles) are Baltimore Town lots and other tracts. Incidental, and not a Gorsuch line: p. 159 ('Gr'), 1787, 'Griffith Nathan' to James Maidwell, Convey, 'Lot No 15 Green St' (folio 387) and 'Lots No 28 & 29' (folio 389), the liber carried by ditto marks (read as A.A.; medium confidence): these are the two Baltimore Town lots Maidwell had mortgaged to Gorsuch in February 1787 (row 46640), so his deed from Griffith was recorded after his mortgage (INFERRED: the index gives the order of recording, not the date of the deed). What it settles: (1) In the 1787 to 1797 Go run the only John Gorsuch lines that name Ensor's Inspection are the 1787 deed to James Edwards (A.A. 205) and the 1795 release to Maidwell (S.S. 231). There is no Gorsuch deed to James Biays, Christopher Walker, Richard Dick, Thomas Cole Speagle or Job Garretson in these pages, and no Gorsuch line names Huntington, the York road, Merryman's Lot or Hailes. (2) If the 5 1/4 acres that Speagle and Carter sold John Gorsuch of Thomas on Sept. 13, 1778 (W.G. C/19, row 47038) left his hands by a recorded deed after the mortgage of 1787, A.A. 205 is the only candidate in this volume (INFERRED: the index gives no acreage, no road and no neighbour, so it could be another part of Ensor's Inspection, for example Richard Dick's part, which Edwards held by 1804). (3) James Edwards fits the ground: Maidwell sold him 2 1/2 acres of Ensor's Inspection in 1801 (W.G. 66/123) and 3 acres in 1804 (82/206), both in the Tract Index (row 46122), and Edwards sold James Biays the piece next to Maidwell's on Nov. 3, 1804 (W.G. 83/371, row 46194), a piece that computes to only about 1 1/2 acres from its calls (rough, the calls do not quite close; INFERRED), so if A.A. 205 was the 5 1/4 acres, Edwards sold Biays only part of it. What it does not settle: (1) What A.A. 205 conveys: it is not read, and the scan on disk (MSA CE 66-76 p.00193 to p.00197) stops at folio 197, so folio 205 has to be pulled. (2) Whether the 'lot ... which formerly belonged to John Gorsuch now the property of the said James Biays' (surveyed Sept. 17, 1799, drawn on the Biays plat, rows 46678 and 46679; named in the 1801 Spear deeds, rows 46180 and 46685) is this ground: the 1803 trust describes it as the 3 acres of Harkin's Rest, which Gorsuch bought of John Harkin in 1771 (row 46253), not the Speagle land. (3) The stretch W.G. 52/402 to 53/196: CE 33-3's Go run ends at 52/401 on p. 157 (p. 158 is blank) and CE 33-4 begins at 53/197 (the next row), so a Gorsuch line recorded in that stretch is in neither scan. (4) A deed indexed under another first-named grantor (a trustee, an executor or a co-grantor) or under another spelling (the 1803 deed writes 'Gosuch'; no 'Gosuch' line appears in the run). Next: W.G. A.A. 205 (MSA CE 66-76, folio 205), read against the 1778 deed's courses (row 47038) and the Edwards deeds W.G. 66/123 and 82/206; and the Grantee Index under Edwards, James, 1787, which gives the same entry from the other side.

(2) So the grantor index shows no John Gorsuch deed to James Biays at all before the 1803 trust, although the 1801 Spear deeds (May 30 and Oct. 24, 1801, rows 46180 and 46685) already call the Gorsuch lot 'now the property of the said James Biays': that ownership rests on a bond, contract or deed that is not indexed under Gorsuch or was never recorded, the 1803 deed to Biays's trustees then putting the legal title into the trust (INFERRED). (3) With the previous row (CE 33-3), the recorded Gorsuch conveyances of Ensor's Inspection in the County index from 1787 to 1803 come to three: A.A. 205 (1787, to James Edwards), S.S. 231 (1795, release to Maidwell) and 76/243 (1803, the trust). The Speagle 5 1/4 acres either went by A.A. 205 (INFERRED, not read) or by no deed in these two volumes. (4) The nearest figure to 5 1/4 acres in the run is 'Lot No 1, 5 a. 58 p.' from 'John Sr.' to Charles Gorsuch (73/72, 1802): 5 a 58 p is 5.36 acres, 18 perches over 5 a 40 p (5 1/4 acres). It is one of the deeds of a family division (lots to Charles, Micajah and John, with Jemima's 'Pt Matthews Meadows' beside it), and 'John Sr.' is probably the John Gorsuch who sold Benjamin Parks 'Pt Matthews Meadow 40a' in 1792 (CE 33-3 p. 152, 'John of Wm'; INFERRED), not John of Thomas. A coincidence of figures, not a match; not used. What it does not settle: (1) What A.A. 205 is (the previous row). (2) Which John Gorsuch 'John Sr.' is. (3) The stretch W.G. 52/402 to 53/196 between the two volumes, which appears on neither p. 158 of CE 33-3 (blank) nor p. 163 here. (4) John Gorsuch of Thomas after 1803, when and how he died, and whether an executor or heir conveyed anything: CE 33-5 (1804 to 1809, MSA CE 33-5 p.00181 to p.00190) was not read for Gorsuch lines (the Gough row for it, 46655, lists only Joshua Gorsuch's 1808 lease). (5) A deed indexed under another first-named grantor or another spelling. Next: W.G. A.A. 205, the one pull that can name the 1787 land and its neighbours; then the Go pages of CE 33-5 for John Gorsuch of Thomas, 1804 to 1809.

(2) Whether a Richard Dick is one of the unnamed '&c' in the James Dick lines of 1759 and 1765; those lines are of other ground (Joseph's Favor, Caledonia), so it is unlikely to matter (INFERRED). John Gorsuch is the GRANTOR on one line only: 1778, Gorsuch John, no grantee, 'Stray', W.G. B/290 (p. 135; an estray notice, not a conveyance; high). The ten more: 1778, Gorsuch David to Magdalane Dyne, lease, 'Ground on Charles St', A/525; 1780, Gorsuch Nathan to William Goodwin, conveyance, 'Lot No 39 Charles St', E/174; 1784, Gorsuch Elizabeth &c to John Winchester, lease, 'Ground on Charles St', T/315, to Joseph Southerlin, lease, 'pt of Lot No 39', T/505, and to Thomas Cooper, conveyance, 'pt Same', T/573; 1784, Gorsuch Charles Sr and Gorsuch Charles Jr &c to Rebecca Young, conveyance, 'Francis Freedom + Youngs Escape', U/449; 1785, Gorsuch Elizabeth &c to James Dugan, assignment, 'Lot no 39', V/236, to Matthias Benns, lease, 'pt of Lot no 39', V/239, to James Dugan, lease, same, V/242, and to Cleary and Peter Dular, lease, same, V/245. Confidence: names, instruments and locations high; the liber letters T, U, V medium (ditto marks); the folios of the Elizabeth lines medium-high. No Gorsuch line names Ensor's Inspection, the York or any main road, Huntington, Speagle, Maidwell, Baltimore Town lots 28 and 29 or Merryman's Lot. One line names Hailes: 1781, p. 133, Gist Mordecai &c to John McLure, conveyance, 'Hailes Folly 50 Acres of Land', W.G. G/108 (a Gist line, not Gorsuch); Hales Folly is the tract whose Ensor half went to Griffith and Gist in 1774 (A.L. L/307, rows 47035 and 47036), so this is very probably their half going on to McLure (INFERRED). C/19, row 47038) are not shown sold by him before 1787, consistent with his holding the lot south of Maidwell when he took Maidwell's mortgage on Feb. 26, 1787 (row 46640) (INFERRED: an unrecorded deed would not show). C/231, filed under Harkin), not from Speagle, so the fate of the Speagle 5 1/4 acres after 1787 is still open. (2) What 'Matthews Meadows' is. (3) The William Gorsuch who deeded it, and whether he and the Charles Street Gorsuches are the family of Thomas Gorsuch. summary: Plate, 7th Precinct, Section 3, p. 147 of the 1889 Thompson atlas of the 21st and 22nd Wards (JHU digital collections), west side of the York Road, the north end of the block between Wilson Street and Calvin Avenue; read 2026-10-17 by a helper agent from the 2000 px page image Jeff supplied. South of Calvin Avenue's corner lot (J. M. Russell Agt, 23.9 on the avenue, 90 on the road) the plate draws a narrow gap and then, going south along the road: a lot of 16 ft, 155 deep, coloured, with no name and no building; S. Phillips 17 (2S.B. Store & D., 1 1/2 S.F. Stab.); Mrs. W. Gards 16 (2S.B. Store & D., 1S.F. Stable); A. D. Clemens 16 (1S.B. Store); Wm. Gutman 25. Measured from the south line of Calvin Avenue the corner lot and the alley bring the first lot to 100 ft, so the plate's lots run 100 to 116, 116 to 133, 133 to 149 and 149 to 165 ft south of the avenue (INFERRED, the alley is not lettered). The Calvin Avenue lots round it out: the south side has sixteen lots from Barclay Street to the turnpike corner, the first fifteen totalling 375.1 ft, and the north side sixteen lots, the five nearest Barclay Street (B. L. Wright 24.1, A. Storck & Son twice, A. D. Clemens, H. Briele) totalling 124.1 ft. J. M. Russell Agt holds five south-side and two north-side lots, A. D. Clemens three and one; Agt is lettered after Russell, Boehm, Buchbaum & Co. and H. Smith & Co. on both sides. The sheet carries no plat lot numbers. Against the deeds: (1) The Oliver lease (J.W.S. 158/447, row 42101) and the Fuller deed (J.W.S. 162/110, row 46625) put the first lot, 17 ft ($51, now 3360), at the south-west corner of the turnpike and a 10-ft alley, 100 ft south of Calvin Avenue, and the second, 16 ft ($48), at 117 ft: together the span 100 to 133 ft, 33 ft, which is exactly the span of the plate's blank 16-ft lot and S. Phillips's 17 ft. The widths come in the opposite order, 17 then 16 in the deeds and 16 then 17 on the plate, and the plate letters Phillips only on the southern lot of the two. (2) The paper takes 3360 to be the plate's S. Phillips because of the 17 ft and Phillips's lease; by position 3360 is the lot at the alley, which on the plate is the one with no name (the 1905 ledger puts Laura V. Phillips at 1214 York Rd, the old number of 3360, row 47624). The readings that would reconcile them: (a) Phillips held both Oliver lots and the plate letters only the one with the store; (b) the plate's draftsman swapped the two widths and the names; (c) 3360 was the plate's blank lot and stood empty in 1889, which would be hard to square with the assignment of 1887 "with the buildings thereupon" (J.W.S. 164/231) unless those stood on the second lot. None is shown; do not force one. (3) Frontage tests only (parcel layer, used as a length test, not to place anything): the three plate lots below the blank one total 17 + 16 + 16 = 49 ft, and today's tax lot 3354 (the three-store row 3354 to 3358 of the 1940 permit) is 49.3 ft; today's 3360 is 18.3 ft against the deeds' 17. (4) The Brune lease (J.W.S. 153/55 to 64, row 46624) puts Lots 11 to 26 on the south side with the 15th at 375 ft east of Barclay Street and the 16th, the corner, 25 ft: the plate's south side has sixteen lots, the first fifteen totalling 375.1 and the corner 23.9, the corner depth 90 as the lease says. Its Lots 38 to 42 on the north side, five lots of 25 ft at the Barclay Street end, are the plate's five (124.1 ft), and the north side's sixteen lots would be numbers 27 to 42 counted from the turnpike (INFERRED). Agt after a name on these lots may mark an agent for the owner of the ground rent or for the lessee (INFERRED); the plate does not say whose. What it settles: (1) The 10-ft alley and the 90-ft corner lot north of it are on the plate where the deeds put them, and the Calvin Avenue layout of the Brune lease (sixteen south-side lots, 375 ft to the corner lot, five at the Barclay end of the north side) is confirmed by count and width. (2) The plate puts S. Phillips's 17 ft one lot south of the alley lot; the deeds do not. (3) The plate shows no plat lot numbers, so it cannot say which are Clemens's plat Lots 3 and 4. What it does not settle: (1) Whether 3360 is the plate's blank lot or S. Phillips's lot. (2) What stood on the blank lot in 1889. (3) Whether Laura A. Phillips held one Oliver lot or both. Next: J.W.S. 164/231 (Oliver to Laura A. summary: Plate, Sixth Precinct overview, p. 128 of the 1889 Thompson atlas of the 21st and 22nd Wards (JHU digital collections), the lower half (the York Road along the foot of the sheet); read Oct. 17, 2026 from the 4200 px image made from the original JP2 that Jeff supplied, enlarged. The sheet's upper half is a larger-scale inset of the Waverly block between Barclay Street and the York Road (Waverly Avenue to Merryman Lane, west side); the lower half shows, above the York Road: Section 2 (the pink block at the right), Gilmor Lane and Sumwalt Lane as diagonals, and between them the 'Estate Samuel Brady, 28 1/2 Acres' (2 S. & G. Roughcast D., 1 1/2 S.B.B.B., 1 1/2 S. & Basement B.B., 2 S. Stone Stable, 1 1/2 S.F.B., 2 S.F.D., 1 S.F.B.B.), with the small 'Est. H. L. Whitridge' lots (5 3/10 acres, Vacant) on its south side and, at the York Road, 'Est. Samuel Brady, Oriole Base Ball Park, 4 3/4 Acres': 518 ft on the road, 383 and 363 on its sides. To the park's right (north) the Brady ground keeps a strip of frontage lettered 369 ft, then comes the pink block lettered SEC 2 whose left (south) edge is lettered 455 and whose right edge is Gilmor Lane. The York Road is at the foot of the sheet and the ground described is above it, on the same side as the Waverly inset; with south to the left along the road the side is the west side (the 3100 to 3198 even numbers, INFERRED from the inset's Merryman Lane end). Against the deeds: (1) The Brady trustees' deed of 1906 (R.O. 2290/225, row 46168) sold 'the whole remaining Brady tract between the York Road, Guilford Avenue and Gilmor Lane' (the 3028 chapter's reading of that deed), and the 1848 Allender-to-Brady deed (A.W.B. 404/533, row 46149) ends its north line 'south 81 degrees east 27 perches to the Baltimore and York Turnpike Road': the plate puts the Brady estate between those two lanes and the road, on the side the Waverly inset is on, which Corridor's deeds put west of the turnpike (A.W.B. 404/533, R.O. 2319/497). (2) The block lettered SEC 2 with the 455-ft south edge is the block of p.132's Section 2 (Wilson 119, Cashmyer 35, Hamilton 100, Mott 64, Leichty 36.4: 354.4 ft on the road), whose Wilson lot has 455 ft on its south line; so the Keelty ground's south neighbour in 1889 is the Brady estate, the 369-ft strip, and the Oriole Base Ball Park lies beyond it to the south (INFERRED from the two sheets' lettering; the 369 against 354.4 on the other sheet is 14.6 ft more, which the width of Gilmor Lane may account for). (3) This contradicts the sentence in Edition 3 (the 'which blocks sit on which patent' page) that Ensor's Inspection is the Brady estate 'east of the York Road at about 26th to 29th': the plate puts the Brady estate and the ballpark west of the road. What it settles: the Brady estate and the Oriole ballpark are on the west side of the York Road, and the Brady frontage runs up to the block that holds the Keelty ground. What it does not settle: whether every acre of the 28 1/2 is Ensor's Inspection; which modern block the 369-ft strip is (the plate has no 1889 numbers); the ballpark's modern address. Next: p.131 and p.135 at full resolution (Sumwalt Lane, the Whitridge lots); the 1896 and 1905 Annex ledgers for the Brady strip.

summary: Index pages, Baltimore County Court Grantor Index A-Z, 1770 to 1786, pages 136 and 137 (MSA CE 33-2), the 'Go' surnames; read 2026-10-17 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved (the whole pages, 120 dpi). Columns as in the other index rows; the lettered books are my reading and medium confidence, the lot numbers and folios are clearer. The Huntington lines of 1783 to 1785, entered under 'Gough H. D. & Onion', 'Gough Harry D. &c' or 'Gough and Onion', all leases unless noted, 'Lot No.' of 'Huntingdon': 1783 to Joab Clark, Lot 91, fol. 488; to Hopkin Hopkins, Lot 90, fol. 492; to Thomas Burk, Lots 83, 84, 85 and 86, fol. 495, and again Lots 74 and 75 (book Q, fol. 228); to William Moody, Lot 82 (262); to Cornelius Hagerty, Lot 20 (274; the numeral could be 2 or 20); to Frederick Betz, 'part of Huntington' (363); to John Funk, part of Huntington, Lot 2 or 21 (214; the numeral is cramped); to John and Robert Casey, Lot 24 (435); 1784 to John Orrich, Lots 31 and 32 (467); to Charles Carbline, Lot 78 (book S, fol. 65), Lot 56 (69) and Lots 72 and 73 (72); to Robert Desilver, part of Lots 27, 28, 29, 40, 41 and 42 (326); to Lavalin Barry, Lots 76 and 77 (453) and Lot 59 (456); 1785 to Josias Pennington and others, Lot 24, 14 acres (688; Gough and Onion 'Extors', the same Lot 24 as Casey's, so one of the two readings is wrong, INFERRED); to Gerrard Hopkins, part of Lots 54, 55, 64 and 65, 16 acres 64 perches (279); to John Farner, part of Lots 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8, 14 acres 30 perches (book X, fol. 226); and a conveyance to Daniel Carroll, part of Lot 26 (670). A bond of conveyance from Gough to George Mathews (580) names no tract. The other Gough lines on the two pages are Baltimore Town ground (Baltimore, Paul's and Chatham Streets) and are not Huntington. What it settles: (1) By 1783 the Huntington ground was laid out in numbered lots, at least Nos. 2 to 91, of about 6 to 16 acres each (Lot 34 is 6 acres in Edwards's 1787 deed, row 46653), and Gough with Thomas Bond Onion was leasing them; Onion's 1790 deed to Gough (row 46068) therefore passed his half of lots already let, and 'Gough, 1790 to 1808' in the paper's chains starts at least seven years late for the lots. (2) The later numbered lots in the record are on the same plan: Lots 95 to 98 to Wilmans in 1794 (QQ/164, the 3326 to 3332 ground) and the 'Lot No. 74' of Bouldin's 1821 draft, which is Thomas Burk's 1783 lease of Lots 74 and 75 (INFERRED from the number; the draft's lot 2 is the second lot of the 1823 Carroll deed, row 46582). (3) The 1983 National Register nomination's 'about 1790' for the break-up of Huntington is late. What it does not settle: which numbered lot any study parcel is (the deeds, not the index, say), who Onion's co-lessor capacity was (Gough and Onion as co-owners or as Prudence Gough's trustees), or whether the plan survives as a plat. Next: the deeds themselves, starting with Burk's Lots 74 and 75 (book Q, fol. 228) and Desilver's Lots 27 to 42 (book S, fol. 326), and the 1783 to 1785 grantee index (CE 32-2) under the lessees.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. A.A., folios 205 to 206 (MSA CE 66-76; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 205 to 208 of the volume; the deed opens at the foot of 205, below the end of an Etienne Zacharie, Anne, Philip and Jas. Waters indenture, runs onto 206, and Nathan Bowen to Solomon Bowen begins below it). Indenture of May 16, 1787 between John Gorsuch son of Thomas, of Baltimore County, and James Edwards of the same: for 50 pounds, Gorsuch sells Edwards in fee 'all that part of a tract or parcel of land called Ensors Inspection lying on the west of the main road that leads from Baltimore Town to George Hailes', beginning at a bounded black oak of Mrs. Achsah Carnan's and running with her land S 52 E 22 perches 'to the main road', up the road N 14 E 29 1/2 perches to a black oak marked with six notches, bounding on the road N 41 E 6 perches to a bounded red oak marked with six notches, N 81 1/2 W 39 perches to a forked white oak marked with six notches, S 50 W 4 perches till it intersects Carnan's line, and with it to the first black oak, 'five acres and one quarter of an acre more or less', with the improvements and appurtenances; covenant of warranty against Gorsuch and his heirs. Witnesses Hez. Waters and Jon. Rutter, who also witnessed Gorsuch's receipt for the 50 pounds on the same sheet; acknowledged May 16, 1787 before John Moale and Lyde Goodwin, justices of the peace, Elizabeth Gorsuch his wife privately examined and releasing her dower; received for record May 18, 1787 and recorded the same day (W. Gibson, Clerk). The five courses, walked from the black oak, enclose 5.21 acres with the closing line implicit (about 26 perches toward S 30 E) against the deed's 5 1/4 [arithmetic]. What it settles: (1) The index's 'Gorsuch John to Edwards James, Pt Ensors Inspection, A.A. 205' (1787) is the Speagle lot. The beginning oak, the S 52 E 22, N 14 E 29 1/2, N 41 E 6, N 81 1/2 W 39 and S 50 W 4 perch courses and the 5 1/4 acres are word for word those of Speigle, Speigle and Carter's 1778 deed to Gorsuch (W.G. C/19, row 47038), and of Joseph Ensor's 1767 deed to the Speigles before it (B P/470). The inference of the earlier row that A.A. 205 was the best candidate is now read. (2) Gorsuch held the lot nine years, 1778 to 1787, and sold it three months after Maidwell mortgaged him the adjoining nine acres (Feb. 26, 1787, row 46640): by May 1787 the ground south of Maidwell's was James Edwards's, not Gorsuch's. (3) Edwards then bought the neighbouring ground from Maidwell himself in 1801 and 1804 (rows below). (4) The road is 'the main road that leads from Baltimore Town to George Hailes', the line the York Turnpike followed from 1808. What it does not settle: (1) Where the lot went after Edwards. The 1801 Spear deeds and Biays's plat call a lot that 'formerly belonged to John Gorsuch' 'now the property of the said James Biays' (rows 46180, 46685, 46678), but Gorsuch still owned 3 acres of Ensor's Inspection in 1803 (the Harkin's Rest trust, row 46253), so that lot is probably a different one, and no Edwards to Biays deed before Nov. 3, 1804 is known (INFERRED). (2) Whether Edwards held the 5 1/4 acres together with Richard Dick's part of the road line (the 1804 Maidwell deed below calls another Edwards parcel). Next: the County grantor index under Edwards, James, 1787 to 1804 and 1805 on, for the sale of the 5 1/4 acres onward.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 66, folios 123 to 125 (MSA CE 66-116; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 123 to 126; the deed opens on 123 under the index heading 'James Maydwell Deed To James Edwards', below the end of a Walsh and Williamson lease, and ends on 125, where David Robinson's letter of attorney to Charles Halsey follows). Indenture of Mar. 25, 1801 between James Maydwell of Baltimore County, wheelwright, and James Edwards of the same place, merchant: for $875 Maydwell sells Edwards in fee 'all that part of a tract of land situate in Baltimore County called Ensors Inspection that is contained within the following metes and bounds': beginning at a white oak marked with three notches, 'the beginning of that part of said tract conveyed by Joseph Ensor to the said James Madwell by deed dated the seventh of July one thousand seven hundred and sixty eight', N 34 E 13 perches to a stake standing one foot north of a stone, S 80 E 24 1/2 perches to a stake, S 12 1/2 E 4 perches, S 82 1/2 E 12 perches to a stake 'in the south thirty five degrees west line of the said part conveyed by Joseph Ensor to said Madwell', then bounding on that line S 35 W 9 perches to the end of it, and on 'the given line of said part' to the beginning tree; 'two and a half acres of land', with the benefits and appurtenances. Warranty; Maydwell signed 'James Maydwell', witnesses John Moale and Josias Penington; receipt for $875 the same day; acknowledged Mar. 25, 1801 before Moale and Penington, Temperance his wife privately examined and releasing her dower; received for record Apr. 2, 1801 and recorded the same day (William Gibson, Clerk). The courses, walked from the oak, enclose 2.57 acres and close by a line of about 39 1/2 perches toward N 81 W, the direction of the N 80 1/2 W closing line of Maidwell's own nine acres [arithmetic]. What it settles: (1) Maidwell sold the south end of his nine acres, along the first line (13 of its 35 perches), the closing line and the S 35 W road line (9 of its 14), to James Edwards in March 1801 for $875, six months after he sold the north 2 1/4 acres to James Biays (W.G. 67/62, row 46277, dated Sept. 26, 1800 as recorded). (2) The deed names Ensor's 1768 deed to Maidwell by its date, so this is the same Maidwell as the 1768 grantee and the 1787 mortgagor; he is a wheelwright, Edwards a merchant. (3) The piece's S 80 E 24 1/2, S 12 1/2 E 4 and S 82 1/2 E 12 courses are the north line of the 1804 piece (next row). What it does not settle: how Edwards came by the 'other parcel' that the 1804 deed names, or whether this 2 1/2 acres touches the modern 2958 lot. Next: W.G. 82/206 (next row) and the Edwards to Biays deed of Nov. 3, 1804 (W.G. 83/371, row 46194) laid on this one.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 82, folios 206 to 208 (MSA CE 66-132; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 206 to 209; the deed opens at the foot of 206 under the index heading 'James Maydwell Deed To James Edwards', after an Anthony Kimmel to August Schwatke lease assignment, and ends on 208, where Henry S. Keatinge to Robert Walsh follows). Indenture of Sept. 11, 1804 between James Maidwell of Baltimore County and James Edwards of the same: for $2,000, Maidwell sells Edwards in fee 'all that part of a tract of land called Ensors inspection situate in Baltimore County which is contained within the following metes and bounds': beginning at a stone marked J B 'standing on the west side and near to the York Turnpike road at the south east corner of a part of said tract conveyed by said James Maidwell to James Biays', S 84 W 34 perches along that part to another stone marked J B, S 34 W 8 1/2 perches 'to the north west corner of a part of said tract heretofore sold by said James Maidwell to said James Edwards' (the 2 1/2 acres of Mar. 25, 1801), then bounding on it S 80 E 24 1/2 perches, S 12 1/2 E 4 perches (the words 'and a half perch still bounding on said Edwards part south twelve and a half east four perches' interlined between the 22nd and 23rd lines of the first page) and S 82 1/2 E 12 perches 'until it intersects the out line of another parcel of land belonging to said James Edwards', and thence on that line to the beginning; 'three acres of land more or less together with all and singular the buildings and improvements thereon'. Warranty; the name of Charles A. Pindell stands under the note of the interlineation; acknowledged Sept. 11, 1804 before two justices, Temperance his wife privately examined and releasing her dower (the justices' names at the foot are Rob. Gorsuch and Geo. Gouldsmith Presbury); received for record Sept. 15, 1804 and recorded the same day (William Gibson, Clerk). The courses, walked from the J B stone, enclose 2.98 acres with the east side implicit [arithmetic]. What it settles: (1) Maidwell's nine acres were divided among Biays (the north 2 1/4 acres, 1800), Edwards (the south 2 1/2 acres, 1801) and Edwards again (the middle 3 acres, 1804), so by Sept. 15, 1804 Edwards held about 5 1/2 of the nine acres (2.57 and 2.98 computed) and Maidwell at most the remainder, about an acre on the deed's nine or half an acre on the computed 8.17 (INFERRED). (2) The 3 acres carry 'buildings and improvements' and sold for $2,000, against $875 for the 2 1/2 acres of 1801, whose deed names none: the buildings stood on this middle piece (INFERRED from the price and the words). (3) On Sept. 11, 1804 Edwards already owned 'another parcel of land' on the east of this piece, along the road: Richard Dick's part, 'now owned by the said James Edwards' in Edwards's deed to Biays of Nov. 3, 1804 (W.G. 83/371, row 46194), is the likely parcel (INFERRED; neither deed names the vendor). (4) The J B stones, James Biays's, at the south-east corner of his 2 1/4 acres and on its south line fix where Biays's ground ends. What it does not settle: when and from whom Edwards bought Dick's part, which of the three pieces is the ground of 2958 or its neighbours, and how the 5 1/4 acres of A.A. 205 (row above) lie against these. Next: the County grantor index under Edwards, 1804 to 1805; the Dick grantee entries in 1770 to 1786 (CE 32-2, Di) for the deed to Edwards.

summary: Index pages, Baltimore County Court Grantee Index A-Z, 1655 to 1769, pages 88 to 91 (MSA CE 32-1); read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved (pages 88 and 89 read; pages 90 and 91 are the 'Do' pages and were not read). Columns are date, grantee, grantor, instrument, location of property, and liber and folio. Page 88 is 'De cont'd' (1767 and 1768: Deaver, Deyer, Deal, Decker (Rudolph, from William Winchester), Deye, Dimmitt); page 89 is 'Di', the whole of it (1664 to 1769) and blank below 1767: Dixon and Dickson (John, 1664 and 1665, Daniel Jones); Dimmit and Diggs (the Darnall, Fasher, Gadd and Shey lines); Thomas Dick (1758, from Thomas Sligh, 'Coles Harbour' 6 acres; 1759, from Thomas Harrison, Lots 72 and 73; 1762, from Edward Fell, Lot 55, from William Askew, Lot 110, and from Thomas Sligh, Lot 116; 1764, from Benjamin Rogers, 'Rogers Inspection' 3/4 acre; the Baltimore Town and Fells Point lots); James Dick (1764, power of attorney from Thomas Dick; 1765, with others, from Samuel Owings Jr. and, in 1767, from William Ogg, 'William's Delight'; 1767, from Mary McCulloh and others, Lot 118 in Jonestown); and Dillon and Dill (1769). There is NO Richard Dick on either page, and no grantee of 'Ensors Inspection' under any Di name. What it settles: (1) The deed by which Joseph Ensor conveyed what the 1768 Maidwell deed calls 'the part of Ensor's Inspection sold to Richard Dick' is not in the County Grantee Index under Dick (or Dix, Dyck or any Di spelling) before the end of 1769; with the grantor index under Ensor (CE 33-1, which found Garretson, Speagle and Maidwell but not Dick) that is two indexes that do not find it. (2) The 'Rogers Inspection' lot of 3/4 acre to Thomas Dick in 1764 is another tract, not Ensor's. What it does not settle: whether Ensor's deed to Richard Dick was never recorded, was recorded under a miscopied name (Dicks, Deck, Dyke), or came after 1769 although the 1768 deed already calls it sold (the index years run about a year early, INFERRED); or whether Richard Dick was Ensor's tenant or heir. Next: the Grantee Index for 1770 to 1786 (MSA CE 32-2, 'Di' about p. 85 to 90); W.G. 83/371 (the 1804 Edwards to Biays deed) read for its recital; Edwards's own grantee entries, 1795 to 1804.

summary: Index pages, Baltimore County Court Grantor Index A-Z, 1844 to 1845, pages 531 to 534 (MSA CE 33-15), the 'U' surnames; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved. The question is the United States's sale of 'the Barracks' in front of St. John's, Waverly, which the St. John's nomination says the Gibson family bought from the federal government in 1844 (row 39495), distinct from the vestry's $1,200 Church Lot deed of Sept. 27, 1844 (A.W.B. 349/45, row 46157). The pages hold: p. 531 'Uh' (1844 and 1845: Uhler Erasmus R. &c to Jonathan S. Eastman, lease, Lot E. S. Hanover St., T.K. 342/77, June 1844; Uhrig John to Henry Miller, assignment, Lots on Mulberry and Chatsworth Streets, 348/224, Jan. 1845; Uhlhorn Clemens A. A. to John Christian Lehman (the surname is uncertain), mortgage, Lot S. Saratoga St., 359/41, Oct. 1845); p. 532 'Ul', blank; p. 533 'Up' (Upton William and wife to Emanuel Marriott, deed, part of 'Airey's Desire' resurveyed 14 3/4 acres 20 perches, 345/226, Sept. 1844); and p. 534 'Ut' (Utermohle George Wm. and wife to William Baker, deed, Lot 47 and part of 45 on S. S. Pratt St., A.W.B. 350/415, Mar. 1845). There is no 'Un' or 'Um' page in the scan, and the 'Ul' page, the nearest, is empty for the year. There is NO line for the United States, the War Department, the Ordnance Department, the Secretary of War, a barracks or the Gibsons. What it settles: no conveyance by the United States of land in Baltimore County is indexed under U in the pages held for 1844 and 1845. What it does not settle: (1) whether a U.S. grantor would be filed under 'Un' or 'Us' on a page the scan does not include (the volume's U pages run Uh, Ul, Up, Ut, so 'United' would fall in 'Ul', which is blank; INFERRED); (2) whether the federal sale was recorded in the County at all (a land-office or War Department sale may not have been, or may be indexed under an officer's name); (3) whether the Barracks lay in the County in 1844 (it stood at the York Road and Old York Road at Waverly, then County ground) or in the City. Next: the Grantee Index (CE 32) under Gibson, 1844, and the paper's sources for the Gibson purchase (the St. John's nomination and Scharf p. 888).

summary: Plate, 7th Precinct, Section 3, p. 147 of the 1889 Thompson atlas of the 21st and 22nd Wards (JHU digital collections), the south end of the west side of the York Road, where Merryman's Lane meets it; read Oct. 17, 2026 from the close-up Jeff supplied (the crop is about 1500 px across the apex, against the page image's 2000 px for the whole sheet). The lot at the point is lettered 'J. E. Sinclair', in smaller hand '2 S.B. Store & D.' and '1 S.F.B.B.'; the figure along the lane is cramped against the lane's edge and is not read, and on the road side three digits read 2, 8 and 5 with a point between the 8 and the 5: 28.5 ft. The lot above it is 'M. Heathcote', 3 S. & Mans. B. Store & D., 2 1/2 S.F.B.B., 2 S.F.B.B. and 1 1/2 S.F. Stab., 60.9 ft on the road (the figure reads 609, written upward), 72.3 ft along the lane, and 97 ft along its north side where it meets the next lot (the Sinclair 68-ft lot). Against the deeds: the 1884 Sinclair deeds put the apex's turnpike front at 36 ft 1/2 in and the two George deeds (1887, 1890) at 36 ft 1 1/2 in (rows on 752); the 1915 roll has 36 ft 1 in front. The plate's 28.5 is 7 to 8 ft less, as the earlier reading (28.8) already was, so the plate's lettering does not match the deeds' frontage; the difference could be a corner splay or plain lettering, but nothing in the deeds says so (INFERRED, not shown). What it settles: the digit that the 2000 px image left open is 5, not 8: the apex lettered on the plate is 28.5 ft, not 28.8. J. E. Sinclair held the apex in 1889 with a two-story brick store and dwelling (Edition 3's reading of his name stands). What it does not settle: the 7 to 8 ft gap against 36 ft 1/2 in; which of the two numbers (28.5 or 28.8) the c.1921 plat copied. Next: the close-up's source file, the whole JHU 'P 147' page at full resolution, if the lane figure matters; the 1921 plat laid beside this.

summary: Lease, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.M.I. 141, folios 409 and 410 (MSA CE 62-141; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 409 to 412; the lease opens at 407 and pages 407 and 408 were read earlier, rows 23724 and 47010 to 47017; pp. 411 and 412 hold the rest of an unrelated deed of John T. Morris and Charles E. Kendall, receivers, to Milton W. Offutt and others, and were not read). Folio 409 finishes the description of the third lot: from the beginning on the north-east side of Merryman's Lane, north-westerly on that side 76 ft 7 in more or less to the east side of an alley three feet wide laid out parallel with the York turnpike 100 ft west of it and running north from the lane; north on the east side of the alley 11 ft 8 in more or less to meet a line drawn west from a point on the west side of the turnpike 60 ft north of the beginning of the lot; then east, reversing that line, 100 ft to the turnpike; then south on it 60 ft to the beginning. A parenthesis says the three parcels are the same three that James E. Sinclair and his wife had conveyed to Alice P. Harris in fee by a deed 'perfected immediately before the execution hereof' (row 47016). Habendum to Sinclair, his executors, administrators and assigns for 99 years from the date, rendering to Alice P. Harris 'the rent or yearly sum of eighty dollars for the lot of ground first above described, the rent or yearly sum of eighty dollars and eighty four cents for the lot of ground secondly above described, and the rent or yearly sum of one hundred and fifty dollars for the lot of ground thirdly above described', in equal half-yearly instalments, counted from June 11, 1884, free of deductions for taxes and assessments, 'in such manner as that each of the aforesaid lots of ground shall be liable for its own rent only'. Distress for arrears; re-entry after 60 days' arrears of rent, and again after one year's arrears; Sinclair covenants to pay the rents, taxes and assessments. Folio 410: the Harrises covenant to warrant specially; on payment of one dollar as a renewal fine the lessor will give a new 99-year lease of each lot on the same rent and terms, so that the demise is 'renewable and renewed from time to time forever'; the rents are redeemable at any time after five years from the date at the tenant's option for the capitalisation of the rent at six per cent in gold coin, with rent in arrear and a pro rata share of the accruing rent paid first. Signed W. Hall Harris, Alice P. Harris and James E. Sinclair (seals), witness Wm. D. Wright; acknowledged June 11, 1884 before Wm. D. Wright, J.P.; recorded June 11, 1884 at 4:10 P.M. (Wm. M. Isaac, Clerk). The rents are $80, $80.84 and $150, together $310.84 a year; capitalised at 6 percent the first two redeem for $1,333.33 and $1,347.33 and the third for $2,500. What it settles: (1) The lease has three lots with three separate rents, each secured on its own lot only, so a lot's rent could be bought out alone; the 1884 rents were later redeemed (the Stewart redemption deed of 1890, J.B. 1276/42, is described in the 3224 chapter). (2) The third lot's courses and its 60 by 100 ft shape complete the description that the earlier rows begin. (3) The lease was recorded the day it was made, at 4:10 P.M., the same day as Harris's fee deed. What it does not settle: which of the three is 3224 (the paper reads the second, 164 ft 8 in to 197 ft north of the lane);  the end of the first two lots' descriptions (folios 407 and 408, earlier rows). Next: nothing on this lease; the Sinclair mortgage of Sept. 17, 1884 (next row) is the lien on it.

summary: Lease, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber E.H.A. 74, folios 235 to 237 (MSA CE 62-74; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 233 to 237; pp. 233 and 234 are the end of the previous instrument and were not read). Index heading 'David S. Wilson &c Trustees, Lease to John H. Hartman & wf' (margin: 'delivered March 31/77 per Rec't'). Lease made Feb. 27, 1872 between David S. Wilson, Thomas J. Wilson and Henry R. Wilson, trustees under the last will and testament of James Wilson late of Baltimore City, deceased, 'which will bears date the twenty second day of January A.D. 1848, has been duly proven and is now of record in the office of the Register of Wills for Baltimore City', and John H. Hartman and Catharine his wife, of Baltimore County. The trustees, 'acting under the powers conferred on them by said Will', for $700 and the rent reserved lease 'all that lot of ground situate in Baltimore County aforesaid (near to and north of the first toll gate at Waverly on which the Stone House stands which is now occupied by said Hartman' and which is thus described: beginning at a point on the York Turnpike Road where a line drawn along the north wall of the Stone House intersects the west side of the road, west reversing that line 200 ft, south parallel with the road 50 ft, east parallel with the first line 200 ft, and north along the westernmost side of the road 50 ft to the beginning; the trustees may, if they wish, use the westernmost ten feet of the lot to open an alley. With the improvements. Term 99 years from the day before the date, at $100 a year from May 1 (the year reads 18 and a word that looks like 'twenty'; 1872 is the only fit, INFERRED) in half-yearly instalments on Nov. 1 and May 1; distress for arrears; re-entry after 60 days (a second clause says six months' arrears allow the trustees to renew and annul the lease, so the two clauses disagree on the period, as they appear on the page); renewable forever on the lessees' request and proper cost; and the trustees will at any time 'on or before the first day of May A.D. 1875' on payment of $1,666.66 over and above the rent in arrear and the accruing rent, convey the lot in fee simple free of rent. Signed D. S. Wilson, Thos. J. Wilson and Henry R. Wilson, trustees, John H. Hartman and Catharine Hartman (she appears to sign in German script), witness Wm. H. Bayzand; acknowledged Feb. 29, 1872 before Bayzand, J.P., Baltimore City; George Robinson, clerk of the Superior Court of Baltimore City, certified his authority Feb. 29, 1872; recorded Mar. 12, 1872 (Edwd. H. Ady, Clk.). What it settles: (1) The lot just north of Pendleton's Lot 8 is a 50 ft by 200 ft lot with a stone house, leased to Hartman in February 1872 at $100 a year, redeemable for the capitalisation at 6 percent ($1,666.66) until May 1, 1875; it fits the plate of 1889 (J. H. Hartman 50 ft, 2 S. and attic stone dwelling, 375 ft south of Wilson Street, p. 147) in width, in the stone house and in position; the plate gives 190 ft deep against the lease's 200. (2) The trustees recite that the will was 'of record in the office of the Register of Wills for Baltimore City' and that they act under its powers, with no liber; the paper's two citations of the same will (D.M.P. 24/154 and N.H. 26/354) are therefore not settled by this deed. (3) The lease does not cite the Wilson plat, a lot number or Wilson Street: the lot is described from the stone house's north wall, so it does not restate the measurements from Wilson Street that the Pendleton deed gives (E.H.A. 72/153). What it does not settle: where Wilson Street and the lanes fall against 3224; whether Hartman bought the fee before 1875; why 'the first toll gate' is the reference (the Gate House lot of 1871 is at Gilmor Lane, far south, so the phrase may mean a gate near Wilson Street or loosely the toll-gate district, INFERRED either way). Next: the Wilson sales plat (the Circuit Court equity papers); a deed of the fee to Hartman, 1872 to 1875.

summary: Index pages, Baltimore County Court Grantor Index A-Z, 1829 to 1832 (MSA CE 33-10): pp. 437 to 441, the 'Pa' surnames (1829 to 1832), and p. 644, 'Yo' (1829 to 1832); read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scans Jeff saved. The question is Frederick Parks's administrators' assignment of the fork lot to John Litzinger on Apr. 7, 1831, which Litzinger's 1834 deed (T.K. 237/457, rows 46247 and 46248) cites with no liber. The 'Pa' pages hold no Frederick Parks and no administrators: the Parks lines are Ruth Parks, guardian of Mary Ann Jarman, to Charles Grover (1830, W.G. 203/66), Abraham Parks, a surrender of a lot on Gough Street (205/69) and Peter Parks, a mortgage to Wm. Bosley of part of John's Forest and Merriman's Adventure (1829, W.G. 201/455, the number is carried by ditto marks), none of them Huntington. The deed is on p. 644 under the first-named administrator, in the 1831 group: 'Young, McClintock &c., admrs of Fredk. Parks' to 'John Litzinger', 'Asst' (assignment), 'Pt of Huntington', W.G. 210, folio 583. Confidence: grantor, grantee, instrument and 'Pt of Huntington' high; the liber and folio 210/583 medium-high (the folio's last digit could be 5 or 8; the index's own neighbours, 209/305 above and 210/636 below, support 583). The same line group has 'Young, McClintock &c, trustee of Peter Diven &c' to Patrick J. Diven, a Jones Street lot (210/636), which is a different matter. What it settles: (1) The assignment is indexed as W.G. 210/583, so MSA CE 66-260 (liber plus 50), page 583, is the deed Litzinger's 1834 deed leaves without a liber; it is a conveyance of part of Huntington by Frederick Parks's administrators, McClintock Young and James Buchanan (the index prints 'Young, McClintock &c'). (2) Parks's administrators are filed under Young, so an index search under Parks never finds it, the reason the 'Pa' run was blank. (3) The 'Pt of Huntington' puts the fork lot on Huntington and not on Ensor's Inspection, as the paper reads it (the lot between the roads, W.G. 54/156, the Gough 1798 Brown lease). What it does not settle: the deed's courses and parties' wording; Parks's own title (the 1798 Brown lease, Brown's assignment of 1801 or a later one); whether the figures are 210/583 or 210/588. Next: W.G. 210/583 itself (MSA CE 66-260, pp. 583 to 587) for the lot and the recitals of Parks's title.

summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 69, folios 163 to 164 (MSA CE 66-119; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 163 to 166; the deed opens at the FOOT of 163, under the index heading 'James Barry Deed To James Edwards and Andrew Van Bibber', below the end of Edward Hall Spicer's deed to Amos Scott, and ends on 164, where William Asquith's lease to Samuel French follows). Indenture of April 13, 1801 between James Barry 'of the Territory of Columbia' and James Edwards and Abraham Van Bibber of Baltimore County (the index heading writes Andrew): for 'one Cent' Barry sells them, 'as Tenants in common but not as Joint Tenants', all that piece or parcel of ground in Baltimore County: 'Beginning at a Stone set up in the first line of Merryman's lot for a Corner between Merryman and Hall and running thence with said line South forty Degrees West two poles fifteen Links, then North forty nine and three quarters degrees West Eleven poles fifteen Links, thence North forty degrees East two poles fifteen Links, thence with a straight line to the Beginning containing thirty Square perches of Ground more or less', with all of Barry's right, title, interest, property, claim and demand. Signed James Barry; witness Owen Dorsey; acknowledged April 13, 1801 before Owen Dorsey and Geo. Gould Presbury, justices of the peace; received for record Oct. 12, 1801 and recorded and examined the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk); a pencil '30' stands in the margin. Arithmetic (a link is 1/25 of a pole): 2 poles 15 links is 2.6 perches (42.9 ft) and 11 poles 15 links is 11.6 perches (191.4 ft); a figure with sides of those two lengths (the first and third calls are parallel, 2.6 by 11.6 perches) holds 30.2 square perches (about 8,200 square feet, 0.19 acre), which is the deed's thirty [arithmetic]. The long side runs N 49 3/4 W, the bearing of Merryman's Lane in the 1802 Wilson deed (S 49 E closing line), and the short sides run S 40 W and N 40 E, the bearing of the first line of Merryman's Lot. What it settles: (1) The cite in the 1802 Wilson deed is right: 'W.G. 69 folio 163' is Barry's deed, not an unrelated one. The earlier negative pull (this project read only the top of the page, which is Spicer to Scott) and every sentence that called the cite 'unplaced' are corrected. (2) The Barry piece is a 30-perch strip, about 43 by 191 feet, not a tract. (3) It cannot be the source of Lots 16 and 17: those two lots are 100 by 200 feet, about 73.5 square perches, against its 30 (41 percent), and a 43-foot strip would have to be laid across the 100-foot frontage. (4) It cannot account for the 3 3/8 acres of the Hackett ground that the acreage ledger left over (row 47831): the gap is 3 3/8 acres, 540 perches, against 30. (5) The deed begins 'in the first line of Merryman's lot' at a corner 'between Merryman and Hall', so it lay on or beside the Merryman's Lot ground that Hackett's trustees had also sold Edwards and Van Bibber (half an acre, rows 46015 and 46016), and Barry, who sold Hugh Thompson an undivided half of two Merryman's Lot parcels on Feb. 12, 1801 (W.G. 66/150, row 46322), held a small piece of the same lot. What it does not settle: (1) Where the stone stood. The deed names no road, lane or street, and 'Hall' is not identified (the Spicer deed above it is Edward Hall Spicer's, a different page, no connection shown). (2) Whether the strip is inside or beside the 1802 Wilson parcel; the 1802 deed's own first call is N 40 E 1 1/2 perches and its closing line runs S 49 E, the bearings of this strip's sides, which is a fit of bearings only (INFERRED, not shown). (3) Why Barry sold for one cent: the deed says only that the cent was paid, so the real price may be a trust, a quitclaim of a doubtful claim or a settlement (not shown). summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 69, folios 163 to 164 (MSA CE 66-119; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 163 to 166; the deed opens at the FOOT of 163, under the index heading 'James Barry Deed To James Edwards and Andrew Van Bibber', below the end of Edward Hall Spicer's deed to Amos Scott, and ends on 164, where William Asquith's lease to Samuel French follows). Indenture of April 13, 1801 between James Barry 'of the Territory of Columbia' and James Edwards and Abraham Van Bibber of Baltimore County (the index heading writes Andrew): for 'one Cent' Barry sells them, 'as Tenants in common but not as Joint Tenants', all that piece or parcel of ground in Baltimore County: 'Beginning at a Stone set up in the first line of Merryman's lot for a Corner between Merryman and Hall and running thence with said line South forty Degrees West two poles fifteen Links, then North forty nine and three quarters degrees West Eleven poles fifteen Links, thence North forty degrees East two poles fifteen Links, thence with a straight line to the Beginning containing thirty Square perches of Ground more or less', with all of Barry's right, title, interest, property, claim and demand. Signed James Barry; witness Owen Dorsey; acknowledged April 13, 1801 before Owen Dorsey and Geo. Gould Presbury, justices of the peace; received for record Oct. 12, 1801 and recorded and examined the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk); a pencil '30' stands in the margin. Arithmetic (a link is 1/25 of a pole): 2 poles 15 links is 2.6 perches (42.9 ft) and 11 poles 15 links is 11.6 perches (191.4 ft); a figure with sides of those two lengths (the first and third calls are parallel, 2.6 by 11.6 perches) holds 30.2 square perches (about 8,200 square feet, 0.19 acre), which is the deed's thirty [arithmetic]. The long side runs N 49 3/4 W, the bearing of Merryman's Lane in the 1802 Wilson deed (S 49 E closing line), and the short sides run S 40 W and N 40 E, the bearing of the first line of Merryman's Lot. What it settles: (1) The cite in the 1802 Wilson deed is right: 'W.G. 69 folio 163' is Barry's deed, not an unrelated one. The earlier negative pull (this project read only the top of the page, which is Spicer to Scott) and every sentence that called the cite 'unplaced' are corrected. (2) The Barry piece is a 30-perch strip, about 43 by 191 feet, not a tract. (3) It cannot be the source of Lots 16 and 17: those two lots are 100 by 200 feet, about 73.5 square perches, against its 30 (41 percent), and a 43-foot strip would have to be laid across the 100-foot frontage. (4) It cannot account for the 3 3/8 acres of the Hackett ground that the acreage ledger left over (row 47831): the gap is 3 3/8 acres, 540 perches, against 30. (5) The deed begins 'in the first line of Merryman's lot' at a corner 'between Merryman and Hall', so it lay on or beside the Merryman's Lot ground that Hackett's trustees had also sold Edwards and Van Bibber (half an acre, rows 46015 and 46016), and Barry, who sold Hugh Thompson an undivided half of two Merryman's Lot parcels on Feb. 12, 1801 (W.G. 66/150, row 46322), held a small piece of the same lot. What it does not settle: (1) Where the stone stood. The deed names no road, lane or street, and 'Hall' is not identified (the Spicer deed above it is Edward Hall Spicer's, a different page, no connection shown). (2) Whether the strip is inside or beside the 1802 Wilson parcel; the 1802 deed's own first call is N 40 E 1 1/2 perches and its closing line runs S 49 E, the bearings of this strip's sides, which is a fit of bearings only (INFERRED, not shown). (3) Why Barry sold for one cent: the deed says only that the cent was paid, so the real price may be a trust, a quitclaim of a doubtful claim or a settlement (not shown). summary: Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 72, folios 60 to 62 (MSA CE 66-122; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 60 to 63; the deed opens in the middle of 60, under the index heading 'James Edwards and Abraham Van Bibber Deed To Ludwick Herring', and ends on 62, where Daniel Harner's assignment to Herring of Jan. 8, 1802 follows). Indenture of Jan. 2, 1802 between James Edwards and Abraham Van Bibber of Baltimore County and Ludwick Herring of the City of Baltimore. It recites that Daniel Grant and Samuel Moale by their indenture of bargain and sale (W.G. 65/444) conveyed to Edwards and Van Bibber the part of Huntington 'distinguished on a plat thereof by the numbers ninety eight, ninety seven, ninety five and ninety six' containing 'by estimation fourteen acres one quarter and twenty square perches', and that John Hackett and Jane his wife released their dower in it (W.G. 65/442). For $646.87 they sell Herring, in fee, a piece of that tract: 'Beginning for the same at a stone marked L Herring 1801 standing on the east side of the York turnpike road, and running and bounding on said road north twenty three perches and seven tenths of a perch to a stone marked L H D M 1801, it being the beginning of a lot conveyed to David Mumma, and running thence south eighty two degrees east fifteen perches and eight tenths of a perch to a stone standing on the west side of the old road, thence bounding on said old road south four and a half degrees west twenty three perches and three tenths of a perch to another stone, and thence by a straight line to the beginning, containing two acres and twenty five square perches of land more or less', with the buildings and improvements; a pencil '2.25' stands in the margin. Warranty; signed Jas. Edwards and Abm. Van Bibber; witnesses Geo. Gould Presbury and Tho. B. Hodgkin; receipt for the $646.87 the same day; acknowledged Jan. 2, 1802 before Presbury and Hodgkin, Ruth wife of James Edwards and Mary wife of Abraham Van Bibber privately examined and releasing dower; received for record Jan. 8, 1802 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). What it settles: (1) The Herring lot is on the EAST side of the York turnpike, between the turnpike and the 'old road' (the old York road), not on the west side where the Wilson ground and Lots 16 and 17 lie: the Hackett ground (Gough's plat lots 95 to 98) lay on both sides of the road, and Edwards and Van Bibber sold the east side first. (2) It is one of the lots the Tract Index listed ('to Herring, 2 acres 25 perches, 72/60'): 2 acres 25 perches is the deed's figure, 2.16 acres. (3) The stone marked 'L H D M 1801' fixes Herring's north end as the south end of the Mumma lot sold the same day (next row). (4) The road is called the York turnpike road in a deed of January 1802. What it does not settle: (1) Where along the road the lot stands; no street, neighbour or tract other than Mumma is named. (2) The 2 acres 25 perches is the deed's own figure; its sides (23.7 perches on the turnpike, 15.8 across the north, 23.3 on the old road) were not checked by arithmetic. (3) Which later address it is (not shown). Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Herring sold to Constable): the Tract Index (MSA CE 15-1 p. 518, 1813, read) lists 'Huntington pt, 2 a 25 Pr, Deed, Herring to Constable, W.G. 124/367': Ludwick Herring's 2 acres 25 perches of this deed appears to have been sold to Constable in 1813 (INFERRED from the identical 2 a 25 p and the name; W.G. 124/367 not read).

summary: Lease, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 73, folios 605 to 607 (MSA CE 66-123; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 605 to 608; the lease opens at the foot of 605, under the index heading 'James Edwards Lease To Samuel Sargent', below the end of Armacost's deed to Joseph Cole, and ends on 607, where Abraham Stevens's deed to Henry Ebaugh follows). Indenture of Aug. 20, 1802 between James Edwards of Baltimore County, gentleman, and Samuel Serjeant of the same County (signed Saml. Sargent): Edwards leases 'all those two parts of tracts or parcels of land hereinafter particularly described, being part of the tract of land called Huntington'. First parcel: 'Beginning for one of the said parcels ... on the York Turnpike road at the distance of sixty feet southward from a lot heretofore leased on said road by the said James Edwards to a certain William Weeks, then running to the end of the south line of a parcel of land purchased by the said James Edwards of Harry Dorsey Gough and Prudence his wife by deed bearing date the seventh day of February in the year seventeen hundred and ninety five, thence south twenty two degrees west thirteen perches and half a perch, then north forty nine degrees west to the said Turnpike road and then bounding on said road to the beginning', 'subject nevertheless to any future correction of the north line of Darley Hall'. Second parcel: 'Beginning at the distance of four hundred and eighty feet north from the above described place of beginning of the first parcel ... on the said Turnpike road, thence running with said road north one hundred and twenty feet, then east to the north line of Darley Hall, then with said line reversely one hundred and twenty feet, and then to the place of beginning', subject to any correction of that north line. Term 99 years, 'renewable and renewed forever' on payment of $52 for a new lease; yearly rent fifty two dollars. A closing clause releases and voids a deed of demise from Edwards to Serjeant of June 9, 1798. Signed Jas. Edwards and Saml. Sargent; witness Joseph Rocke; acknowledged Aug. 20, 1802 before Geo. Gould Presbury and Rob. Gorsuch, justices of the peace; received for record Oct. 30, 1802 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). What it settles: (1) Edwards personally (not with Van Bibber) held and leased lots on the York turnpike in 1798 to 1802: a lot leased to William Weeks, the 1798 Serjeant lease it replaces, and these two parcels, 480 feet apart along the road. (2) It names Darley Hall's north line as a boundary and says it may need correction, so the lots lay against Darley Hall on the turnpike (the lease places the parcels, it does not locate them on today's blocks). (3) It names a Gough deed to Edwards dated Feb. 7, 1795, the same day as Gough's deed to Wilmans (W.G. Q.Q. 164, row 46043); the index lines of Feb. 7, 1795 under Gough were not read for an Edwards line (a lead, not shown). (4) The Tract Index's 'lease to Sargent (73/605)' is this instrument. What it does not settle: which side of the turnpike the parcels lie on (the call 'north forty nine degrees west to the said Turnpike road' suggests the east side, INFERRED); their areas (the second is 120 feet along the road by an unstated depth); the lessee's later history; and where Darley Hall's north line runs.

summary: Assignment of a ground-rent lease, Baltimore County Circuit Court land records, Liber W.M.I. 148, folios 280 to 282 (MSA CE 62-148; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 280 to 283; the deed opens at the foot of 280, under the heading 'David F. Orr Assgt to James E. Sinclair', below the end of a Canton Company deed to Lewis H. Robinson Jr., and ends at the top of 282, where Henry Hertel's assignment to Francis P. K. Walsh follows). Deed made Oct. 28, 1885 by David F. Orr of Baltimore City to James E. Sinclair of Baltimore County: for 'one dollar and other good and valuable considerations' Orr grants Sinclair, his personal representatives and assigns, 'all that lot, piece or parcel of ground situate and lying in Baltimore County, in the Village of Waverly': 'Beginning for the same on the Westernmost side of the York Turnpike Road, at the distance of one hundred and sixty four (164) feet and eight (8) inches Northerly from the corner formed by the intersection of the Northeasternmost side of Merryman's Lane and the Westernmost side of the York Turnpike Road, which place of beginning is designed to be at a point on the West side of said Turnpike Road which would be intersected by a line drawn Easterly from the centre of the division wall between the house on the lot now being described and the house erected on the adjoining lot on the South thereof, and continuing in the same direction to the said Turnpike Road, thence running Westerly reversing the line so drawn and bounding thereon, passing through the centre of said division wall at right angles or nearly so to said Turnpike Road, and continuing in the same direction in all one hundred (100) feet to an alley three (3) feet wide communicating with Merryman's Lane and laid out parallel with said Turnpike Road, thence Northerly on the East side of said alley thirty two (32) feet and four (4) inches, thence Easterly parallel with the first line of this description one hundred (100) feet to the West side of said Turnpike Road, and thence Southerly bounding thereon thirty two (32) feet and six (6) inches to the place of beginning.' 'Being the same lot of ground conveyed by said James E. Sinclair to said David F. Orr by Deed of Assignment dated September 17th 1884 and recorded among the Land Records of said Baltimore County, in Liber W.M.I. No. 142 folio 124 &c.' Held 'for all the residue of the term yet to come and unexpired therein with the benefit of renewal forever', subject to the annual rent of $80.84 payable in equal half-yearly instalments on June 11 and December 11, and subject to the effect of 'a Mortgage from said David F. Orr and James E. Sinclair to the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County, a body corporate, dated September 17th 1884 and recorded among the Mortgage Records of said Baltimore County, in Liber W.M.I. No. 111 folio 419 &c.' Orr covenants special warranty except as to the mortgage. Signed David F. Orr, witness Jno. T. Maddox; acknowledged Oct. 28, 1885 before Maddox, a justice of the peace of Baltimore City (the Superior Court clerk, James Bond, certifies his signature Oct. 30, 1885); recorded Oct. 31, 1885 at 8.30 a.m. (per William M. Isaac, Clerk). What it settles: (1) The 1884 mortgage the Waverly Building Association held on Orr's and Sinclair's lots, released in 1888 to Sinclair alone (J.W.S. 136/94, row on 768), is at W.M.I. 111 folio 419 (the earlier lead 'W.M.I. 111' has a folio). (2) Orr's name enters this chain only as an intermediary: Sinclair assigned him the lot on Sept. 17, 1884 (W.M.I. 142/124) and he assigned it back on Oct. 28, 1885, (the reason is not stated). (3) A new dimension: the lot is 32 ft 6 in on the turnpike and 100 ft deep, with a 3-foot alley at the rear 'communicating with Merryman's Lane' (the deed says the alley communicates with the lane). (4) The yearly rent is $80.84, the same figure the 1884 Harris lease's end (W.M.I. 141/409, row on 768) gives for one of three lots. What it does not settle: (1) Which lot of the 1884 Harris lease this is, and which address it became: its front starts 164 ft 8 in from the lane corner and ends 197 ft 2 in from it, so 164 ft 8 in of other ground lies between it and the lane corner, which this deed does not identify. (2) The reason for the Orr assignment back; the Sinclair to Orr assignment and the mortgage themselves (W.M.I. 142/124 and 111/419), which are the next pulls (CE 62-142 p.124, CE 221-111 p.419). Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Harris lots, Tharp and Jenkins read): the 1885 Orr to Sinclair deed's lot is 'the secondly described lot' of the Harris lease of June 11, 1884 (W.M.I. 142/124, Sinclair to Orr, Sept. 17, 1884, $1,000, rows 768:mdlr-wmi142-124-sinclair-orr-second-harris-lot-1884 and the mortgage 768:mdlr-wmi111-419-orr-sinclair-mortgage-waverly-bldg-assn-first-and-second-lots-1884): a FIRST lot (rent $80) lies directly south of it. The 1885 deed's 32 ft 6 in on the turnpike side is 32 ft 4 in in the 1884 assignment and mortgage (a 2-inch slip, INFERRED). The lot's span, 164 ft 8 in to 197 ft 0 in north of the lane corner, falls on today's 3222 and 3224 (analysis row 768:analysis-harris-lots-1884-distances-against-2026-parcels-3218-3224).

summary: Assignment of a ground-rent lease, Baltimore County Circuit Court land records, Liber W.M.I. 148, folios 280 to 282 (MSA CE 62-148; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 280 to 283; the deed opens at the foot of 280, under the heading 'David F. Orr Assgt to James E. Sinclair', below the end of a Canton Company deed to Lewis H. Robinson Jr., and ends at the top of 282, where Henry Hertel's assignment to Francis P. K. Walsh follows). Deed made Oct. 28, 1885 by David F. Orr of Baltimore City to James E. Sinclair of Baltimore County: for 'one dollar and other good and valuable considerations' Orr grants Sinclair, his personal representatives and assigns, 'all that lot, piece or parcel of ground situate and lying in Baltimore County, in the Village of Waverly': 'Beginning for the same on the Westernmost side of the York Turnpike Road, at the distance of one hundred and sixty four (164) feet and eight (8) inches Northerly from the corner formed by the intersection of the Northeasternmost side of Merryman's Lane and the Westernmost side of the York Turnpike Road, which place of beginning is designed to be at a point on the West side of said Turnpike Road which would be intersected by a line drawn Easterly from the centre of the division wall between the house on the lot now being described and the house erected on the adjoining lot on the South thereof, and continuing in the same direction to the said Turnpike Road, thence running Westerly reversing the line so drawn and bounding thereon, passing through the centre of said division wall at right angles or nearly so to said Turnpike Road, and continuing in the same direction in all one hundred (100) feet to an alley three (3) feet wide communicating with Merryman's Lane and laid out parallel with said Turnpike Road, thence Northerly on the East side of said alley thirty two (32) feet and four (4) inches, thence Easterly parallel with the first line of this description one hundred (100) feet to the West side of said Turnpike Road, and thence Southerly bounding thereon thirty two (32) feet and six (6) inches to the place of beginning.' 'Being the same lot of ground conveyed by said James E. Sinclair to said David F. Orr by Deed of Assignment dated September 17th 1884 and recorded among the Land Records of said Baltimore County, in Liber W.M.I. No. 142 folio 124 &c.' Held 'for all the residue of the term yet to come and unexpired therein with the benefit of renewal forever', subject to the annual rent of $80.84 payable in equal half-yearly instalments on June 11 and December 11, and subject to the effect of 'a Mortgage from said David F. Orr and James E. Sinclair to the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County, a body corporate, dated September 17th 1884 and recorded among the Mortgage Records of said Baltimore County, in Liber W.M.I. No. 111 folio 419 &c.' Orr covenants special warranty except as to the mortgage. Signed David F. Orr, witness Jno. T. Maddox; acknowledged Oct. 28, 1885 before Maddox, a justice of the peace of Baltimore City (the Superior Court clerk, James Bond, certifies his signature Oct. 30, 1885); recorded Oct. 31, 1885 at 8.30 a.m. (per William M. Isaac, Clerk). What it settles: (1) The 1884 mortgage the Waverly Building Association held on Orr's and Sinclair's lots, released in 1888 to Sinclair alone (J.W.S. 136/94, row on 768), is at W.M.I. 111 folio 419 (the earlier lead 'W.M.I. 111' has a folio). (2) Orr's name enters this chain only as an intermediary: Sinclair assigned him the lot on Sept. 17, 1884 (W.M.I. 142/124) and he assigned it back on Oct. 28, 1885, (the reason is not stated). (3) A new dimension: the lot is 32 ft 6 in on the turnpike and 100 ft deep, with a 3-foot alley at the rear 'communicating with Merryman's Lane' (the deed says the alley communicates with the lane). (4) The yearly rent is $80.84, the same figure the 1884 Harris lease's end (W.M.I. 141/409, row on 768) gives for one of three lots. What it does not settle: (1) Which lot of the 1884 Harris lease this is, and which address it became: its front starts 164 ft 8 in from the lane corner and ends 197 ft 2 in from it, so 164 ft 8 in of other ground lies between it and the lane corner, which this deed does not identify. (2) The reason for the Orr assignment back; the Sinclair to Orr assignment and the mortgage themselves (W.M.I. 142/124 and 111/419), which are the next pulls (CE 62-142 p.124, CE 221-111 p.419). Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Harris lots, Tharp and Jenkins read): the 1885 Orr to Sinclair deed's lot is 'the secondly described lot' of the Harris lease of June 11, 1884 (W.M.I. 142/124, Sinclair to Orr, Sept. 17, 1884, $1,000, rows 752:mdlr-wmi142-124-sinclair-orr-second-harris-lot-1884 and the mortgage 768:mdlr-wmi111-419-orr-sinclair-mortgage-waverly-bldg-assn-first-and-second-lots-1884): a FIRST lot (rent $80) lies directly south of it. The 1885 deed's 32 ft 6 in on the turnpike side is 32 ft 4 in in the 1884 assignment and mortgage (a 2-inch slip, INFERRED). The lot's span, 164 ft 8 in to 197 ft 0 in north of the lane corner, falls on today's 3222 and 3224 (analysis row 768:analysis-harris-lots-1884-distances-against-2026-parcels-3218-3224).
