summary: Assignment of a lease, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 210, folios 583 to 585 (MSA CE 66-260; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 583 to 586; the deed opens on 583 under the index heading 'McClintock Young & James M. Buchanan admrs of Fre. Parks Assignment to John Litzinger', below the recording note of a preceding deed, and ends on 585, where the Baltimore Improving Company's deed to John Glenn follows). Indenture of Apr. 7, 1831 between McClintock Young and James M. Buchanan, both of the City of Baltimore, administrators de bonis non with the will annexed of Frederick Parks, late of Baltimore County, deceased, and John Litzinger of the City. It recites an assignment of about Mar. 28, 1825 from Edward Jenkins to Frederick Parks (W.G. 176/711 &c) of 'all that lot, piece or parcel of ground, being part of a tract of land called Huntington, situate in Baltimore County in the State of Maryland, near Christopher Walker's': 'Beginning for the same at the intersection of the York Turnpike road (agreeable to Baker's survey) and the road leading to Van Bibber's Mill, and running up the said York road ten perches, thence running square with the said road down to a road leading to said Van Bibber's Mill'; reference to that assignment for more. For $426 the administrators assign Litzinger, his executors, administrators and assigns, that lot and the buildings and improvements, 'all the rest residue and remainder yet to come and unexpired of the term of years in and by the original Lease thereof granted, with the benefit of renewal forever', subject to the rent and covenants of the original lease (the lease, its date and its lessor are not named in this deed). Signed McClintock Young and James M. Buchanan 'adm. of F. Parks', John Litzinger; witness Ja. B. Latimer; acknowledged Apr. 7, 1831 before Ja. B. Latimer and Tho. W. Griffith, justices of the peace; received for record Apr. 7, 1831 at 25 minutes past 3 o'clock P.M. and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). What it settles: (1) The 1829 to 1832 County index line 'Parks admrs to Litzinger, Pt of Huntington, W.G. 210/583' (row on 768) is this deed. (2) The lot at the fork of the York turnpike and the road to Van Bibber's Mill, 10 perches (165 ft) up the turnpike, was a LEASEHOLD, passed Edward Jenkins (1825) to Frederick Parks to his administrators (1831) to John Litzinger. (3) The road to Van Bibber's Mill is called a road in 1831, the way the 1802 Wilson deed does (the lane of the later names). What it does not settle: (1) The date and lessor of the 'original Lease' and the rent, which sit in the Jenkins assignment W.G. 176/711 (the next pull, CE 66-226 p.711) and further back. (2) Which side of the turnpike (the call is 'running up the said York road'; not shown) and where Christopher Walker's land lies. (3) Whether 'ten perches' is the whole frontage of the later triangle and lots or only the first lot. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (Harris lots, Tharp and Jenkins read): the Parks assignment's own source is read: Edward Jenkins to Frederick Parks, Mar. 28, 1825, $500, W.G. 176/711 (row 768:mdlr-wg176-711-jenkins-parks-fork-lot-1825), which recites George Tharp's assignment to Jenkins of about Jan. 25, 1825; the original lease is not named (next: Tharp's assignment and the grantor index under Tharp, 1824 to 1828, CE 33-9).

summary: Mortgage, Baltimore County Circuit Court mortgage record, Liber W.M.I. 111, folios 419 onward (MSA CE 221-111; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 419 to 422; the mortgage opens at the foot of 419 under the heading 'David F. Orr et al Mort. to The Waverly Bldg. Asso. of Baltimore County', below the end of the Green release of Sept. 5, 1884, and runs on past 422 to a page not saved (the signatures, the acknowledgement and the recording note are on 423 or after). Mortgage made Sept. 17, 1884 by and between David F. Orr (the preamble writes 'Daniel F. Orr') and James E. Sinclair, both of Baltimore County, mortgagors, and The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County, a body corporate. Orr, a member, has received an advance of $1,040 on eight shares of its stock; for that and one dollar Orr and Sinclair grant the association 'all those lots, pieces or parcels of ground and premises situate lying and being in Baltimore County in the Village of Waverly', two lots. FIRST lot: beginning on the Westernmost side of the York Turnpike Road 164 ft 8 in Northerly from the corner of the Northeasternmost side of Merryman's Lane and the Westernmost side of the turnpike, at the point a line drawn Eastwardly through the centre of the division wall between the house on the lot and the house on the adjoining lot on the NORTH would meet the road; thence Westerly 100 feet to a 3-foot alley communicating with Merryman's Lane; thence SOUTHERLY on the East side of the alley 32 feet; thence Easterly 100 feet; thence Northerly on the turnpike to the beginning. SECOND lot: the same beginning, the line drawn through the division wall to the lot on the SOUTH; 100 feet Westerly to the alley; thence NORTHERLY 32 feet 4 inches; Easterly 100 feet; Southerly on the turnpike 32 feet 4 inches to the beginning. 'Being the first and second lots described in a Lease from W. Hall Harris and wife to said James E. Sinclair dated June 11th 1884 and recorded among the Land Records of said Baltimore County in Liber W.M.I. No. 141', the first lot subject to the yearly rent of $80 and the second to $80.84, both payable half-yearly on June 11 and December 11; the second lot 'was conveyed by said Sinclair to said David F. To Frederick Parks', below the end of Philip Euler's deed, and ends on 712, where William Robeson's deed to Jacob Timanus follows). Indenture of Mar. 28, 1825 between Edward Jenkins of the City of Baltimore and Frederick Parks of Baltimore County. It recites that George Tharp by an assignment of about Jan. 25, 1825 granted Jenkins 'all that lot piece or parcel of ground being part of a tract of land called Huntington situate in Baltimore County ... near Christopher Walkers. Beginning for the same at the intersection of the York turnpike road (agreeably to Baker's survey) and the road leading to Van Bibbers Mill and running up the said York road ten perches, thence running square with the said road down to a road leading to said Van Bibbers Mill', with the buildings and 'all the estate right title interest term of years yet to come and unexpired in the original lease', and that Jenkins has sold the leasehold to Parks. For $500 Jenkins assigns Parks, his executors, administrators and assigns, the lot, the buildings and the residue of the term 'in and by the original lease thereof granted with the benefit of renewment forever', subject to the yearly rent and covenants of the original lease (not named). Signed Edw. Jenkins; witnesses James Mercer and A. J. Bouldin; acknowledged Mar. 28, 1825 before Ja. B. Latimer and Felder Israel; received for record Aug. 8, 1825 (the page reads 1826, but the volume is 1825 and the deed above is Aug. 8, 1825) and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk); a margin note reads 'delivered 21 Aug 1827'. What it settles: (1) The fork lot's leasehold chain is George Tharp (Jan. 1825) to Edward Jenkins to Frederick Parks (Mar. 28, 1825, $500) to his administrators (W.G. 210/583) to John Litzinger (Apr. 7, 1831, $426): the price fell from $500 to $426 in six years. (2) The assignment recites the same call as the 1831 deed, so the Litzinger lot is the Tharp lot. What it does not settle: (1) The original lease: its lessor, date and rent (Tharp's assignment, about Jan. 25, 1825, is the next pull, probably W.G. 172 to 175; the Grantor Index 1824 to 1828, CE 33-9, under Tharp, would give it). (2) Who George Tharp was and whether he was the original lessee. (3) Which side of the turnpike the lot is on (the call is 'up the said York road', not shown).

Indenture of Jan. 25, 1825 between George Tharp of Washington County in the District of Columbia and Edward Jenkins of Baltimore County. It recites that Joseph Eaverson (the hand reads Eaverson or Caverson), administrator of Thomas Eaverson late of Baltimore County, by an indenture of assignment of about Jan. 15, 1819, recorded 'in Liber W.G. No. 148 folio 693', assigned Tharp, his executors, administrators and assigns, 'all that lot piece or parcel of ground being part of a tract of land called Huntington situate in Baltimore County ... near Christopher Walkers. Beginning for the same at the intersection of the York turnpike road (agreeably to Bakers survey) and the road leading to Mr. Van Bibbers Mill and running up the said York road ten perches, thence running square with the said York road down to a road leading to said Van Bibbers Mill', with the buildings and 'all the estate right title interest term of years yet to come and unexpired in the original lease'. Tharp having sold the leasehold to Jenkins, for $700 he assigns it to Jenkins, his executors, administrators and assigns, for the residue of the term 'in and by the original lease thereof granted with the benefit of renewment forever', subject to the yearly rent and covenants of the original lease (not named). Tharp appoints Joseph D. Paul of Baltimore County his attorney to acknowledge the deed. Signed George Tharp; witnesses Chas. Polkinhorn and Rich. H. Polkinhorn, who swore at Baltimore City on Apr. 11, 1825 that they saw Tharp sign in Washington County, D.C.; Paul acknowledged it for Tharp on Apr. 14, 1825 before Fielder Israel and John F. Harris, justices of the peace; received for record Apr. 14, 1825 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). What it settles: (1) The assignment the 1825 Jenkins to Parks deed (W.G. 176/711) recites 'about the 25th of January 1825' is this deed: the Tharp assignment, W.G. 175/449, $700, Jan. 25, 1825 (Tharp's assignment was recorded Apr. 14, 1825, after Jenkins had already assigned the lot to Parks on Mar. 28; Jenkins's assignment to Parks was recorded Aug. 8, 1825). (2) The leasehold came to Tharp from the Eaverson estate by an assignment of about Jan. 15, 1819 (W.G. 148/693), so the original lessee was Thomas Eaverson or an earlier holder, not Tharp (INFERRED). (3) The $700 is within $5 of the $704.33 Tharp owed Jenkins on the 1823 mortgage of the same lot (next row), so the 1825 assignment looks like a transfer in satisfaction of that debt (INFERRED from the figures; the deed does not say so). What it does not settle: the original lease: its lessor, date and rent (the Eaverson assignment W.G. 148/693, CE 66-198 p.693, is the next pull); where the lot lies on the turnpike (the call is 'up the said York road'); and which side of the road.

Indenture of Apr. 26, 1823 between George Tharp 'of ___ County and State of Maryland' (the county is blank) and Edward Jenkins of the City of Baltimore: Tharp is indebted to Jenkins in 'seven hundred and four dollars and thirty three cents'; to secure it, for one dollar, Tharp grants Jenkins, his executors, administrators and assigns, 'all that lot piece or parcel of ground being part of a tract of land called Huntington situated in Baltimore County and beginning for the same at the intersection of the York Turnpike road (agreeably to Baker's survey) and the road leading to Mr. Vanbibbers Mill and running up the said York road ten perches thence running square with the said York road down to a road leading to said Vanbibbers Mill', with the privileges and appurtenances, for the residue of the term 'by virtue of the original lease thereof' with renewal forever; the mortgage void if Tharp pays Jenkins the $704.33 with interest on or before Nov. 1, 1824. Signed George Tharp; witnesses Cha. Winchester and Ja. B. Latimer; acknowledged Apr. 26, 1823 before Winchester and Latimer, justices of the peace; received for record Apr. 26, 1823 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). What it settles: (1) Tharp held the fork lot's leasehold by April 1823 and mortgaged it to Jenkins for $704.33 due Nov. 1, 1824. (2) The 1825 assignment from Tharp to Jenkins (W.G. 175/449, $700) is for the same lot and almost the same sum, so Jenkins took the leasehold in place of the debt (INFERRED, not stated). (3) The mortgage cites the same call as the 1825 and 1831 deeds, so the Litzinger lot is the Tharp lot. What it does not settle: the original lease; Tharp's own source (the Eaverson assignment); where the lot lies.

summary: Assignment of a lease, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 148, folios 693 to 695 (MSA CE 66-198; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 693 to 696; the deed opens at the foot of 693, under the index heading 'Joseph Eaverson admr of Thomas Eaverson Assignment To George Tharp', below the end of Isaac Gardner's deed to Moses Wells, and ends at the top of 695, where Philip Gore's deed to William Gore follows). Indenture of Jan. 15, 1819 between Joseph Eaverson, administrator of the goods, chattels, rights and credits of Thomas Eaverson of Baltimore County, deceased, and George Tharp of the City of Baltimore. It recites that Thomas Eaverson in his life and at his death was possessed of 'a lot or piece of ground part of a tract of land called Huntington situate in Baltimore County near Christopher Walkers. Beginning for the same at the intersection of the York turnpike road (agreeable to Bakers survey) and the road leading to Mr. Vanbibbers Mill and running up the said York road ten perches thence running square with the said York road down to a road leading to said Vanbibbers Mill', for the residue of the term of years 'originally leased'; that letters of administration were granted to Joseph Eaverson; and that at an orphan court held at the City of Baltimore 'some time the year 1815' it was ordered that he set up and expose to public sale the leasehold estate; he did so, 'subject to the payment of the yearly rent therein contained to such person or persons legally authorized to receive the same on the days and times mentioned in the original lease', and George Tharp was the highest bidder at 'one thousand and one dollars'. For that sum Eaverson assigns Tharp, his executors, administrators and assigns, the lot, the buildings and all the term of years yet to come in the original lease, subject to the yearly rent in the original lease. Signed Joseph Eaverson; witness Geo. Gould Presbury; acknowledged Jan. 15, 1819 before Presbury and Rob. Gorsuch, justices of the peace; received for record Feb. 16, 1819 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). What it settles: (1) The leasehold of the fork lot began, in this chain, with Thomas Eaverson, who died before about 1815; his administrator sold it by court order (Baltimore County Orphans' Court, about 1815) and George Tharp bought it, taking the assignment on Jan. 15, 1819 (the sale and the assignment are four years apart; the deed does not say why). (2) So the chain of the lot is now: Thomas Eaverson (lessee) to Joseph Eaverson, administrator, to Tharp (W.G. 148/693, 1819, $1,001) to Edward Jenkins (W.G. 175/449, Jan. 25, 1825, $700; mortgage W.G. 167/456, 1823) to Frederick Parks (W.G. 176/711, Mar. 28, 1825, $500) to his administrators and John Litzinger (W.G. 210/583, Apr. 7, 1831, $426). The price fell from $1,001 to $426 over twelve years; the assignments say nothing about improvements. What it does not settle: (1) The ORIGINAL LEASE: its lessor, date and rent are not named here (nor in the 1823, 1825 and 1831 papers), so the lessor of the fork lot's lease is still unknown; the Orphans' Court sale proceedings of about 1815 (Archives, not on MDLandRec) may name it. (2) Which side of the turnpike the lot lies on (the call is 'up the said York road'; not shown). (3) Which road is meant: 'the road leading to Mr. Vanbibbers Mill' is the road the 1802 deeds call the road to Van Bibber's Mill (the later Merryman's Lane, INFERRED).
